## Critical Notes

**Page 240. line 16. (IV. 55, 2.)** **"The removers of pains"** <note>original: "duḥkhānāmamiyayitāraḥ"</note> in Manuscript Ca. **"The drivers away of pains"** <note>original: "duḥkhānāmaprayitāraḥ"</note> in Manuscripts A and B.

**Page 241. line 1. (IV. 55, 3.)** **"Just as"** <note>original: "yathā"</note> is missing in Manuscripts A, B, and C.

**Page 241. line 2. (IV. 55, 3.)** **"So || indeed so"** in Manuscripts A, B, and C2. **"Just as"** in Manuscript B by a second hand and Manuscript Ca. Manuscript Ca. omits the entire passage.

**Page 241. line 19. (IV. 55, 5.)** **"Of the friend of Indra"** <note>original: "indrasakhasya"</note> in Manuscript Ca. **"Of the friend of the mountain"** <note>original: "adrasakhasya"</note> in Manuscript A. **"The mountain is of the friend"** in Manuscript B.

**Page 243. line 12. (IV. 56, 1.)** **Áśvalāyana** <note>An ancient teacher and author of ritual manuals (Sutras).</note> adds **"here in the eldest"** <note>original: "iha jyeṣṭhe"</note> after **"great heaven and earth."**

**Page 243. line 19. (IV. 56, 1.)** **"In this sacrifice"** <note>original: "iha yajñe"</note> is missing in Manuscripts A and C.

**Page 245. line 13. (IV. 56, 6.)** **"Of the kingdom; belonging to the Lord"** in Manuscript Ca.

**Page 245. line 13. (IV. 56, 6.)** **"With a part of the body"** <note>original: "śarīrekadeśena"</note> in Manuscript Ca. **"With a single part of the body"** in Manuscript A. **"By the unity of the body, etc."** in Manuscript B.

**Page 245. line 14. (IV. 56, 6.)** **"Heaven [sustains] the earth with its own immortal power, and she [the earth] with her own effect"** in Manuscript Ca. **"Heaven [sustains] the earth with its own power, and she with her own effect"** in Manuscript A2 and A3. **"With its own power/moisture"** in Manuscript A3 by a second hand. **"Heaven [sustains] the earth with its own essence, and she with her own effect"** in Manuscript B. **"Those two [sustain] the earth with their own essence, and he with his own effect"** in Manuscript C2. **"Heaven [sustains] the earth with its own power, and she with her own effect"**—found in **Sāyaṇa's Commentary to the Sama-veda.**

**Page 247. line 2. (IV. 57, 2.)** **"Dripping with sweetness, well-purified"** <note>original: "madhusrāvi supūtaṃ"</note> || **"Caused to drip sweetness, well-purified"** in Manuscript Ca. **"Caused to drip sweetness"** in Manuscript A. **"That which drips sweetness"** in Manuscript B. Manuscript B places **"well-purified, cleansed"** after the words **"carrying, performing."**

**Page 248. line 8. (IV. 57, 5.)** **"O Shunasira"** <note>original: "śunāsīrā"</note> stands before **"truth, Shuna is Indra"** in Manuscripts A and B. In the quotation from **Yāska** <note>The ancient author of the Nirukta, a treatise on Vedic etymology.</note>, the phrase **"Shuna is Vayu"** is left out in Manuscripts A, B, and C. **Sāyaṇa** takes the <term>Shunasira<note>Agricultural deities; literally 'Plough and Share'.</note></term> to be either Indra and Vāyu, or, according to the **Etymologists** <note>original: "Nairuktás"</note>, as Vāyu and the Sun <note>original: "Āditya"</note>. This is shown in verse 8. Manuscript Ca. reads: **"Shuna-deva, 'those whose deity is Shuna,' says Shaunaka. Truth: Shuna is Indra, Sira is Vayu—they are Indra and Vayu. O Shunasira, you two are Indra and Vayu. The Etymologists say they are Vayu and the Sun. Shuna is Vayu, 'Shu' refers to the atmosphere, etc."** **Shadguruśishya**, in his Commentary on the Nirukta, writes: **"The name 'Shuna' refers to Vayu [the Wind]. So say the knowers of the Brihaddevata. Vayu is Shuna, and Sira is the Sun; they call Vayu and the Sun 'Shunasira'. But Yaska considered Shunasira to be Indra; Parashara says Shakapurni thinks they are the Sun and Indra."**

**Page 248. line 8. (IV. 57, 5.)** **"Shu"** in Manuscript A3 by the first hand and Manuscript Ca. by the first hand. **"Shuna"** in Manuscript A by the second hand and Manuscript Ca. by the second hand. **"Shuna"** in Manuscript A2. **"Shu"** in Manuscripts B and C. **"Shu"** in the **Nirukta**.

**Page 249. line 9. (IV. 57, 8.)** **"Our earth, the ploughshares are the woods that cleave the earth"** || **"Those ploughshares are the woods that cleave the earth"** in Manuscript B. **"Those earth-ploughshares are the cleaving woods"** in Manuscript A. **"Our earth, the ploughshares are the cleaving woods"** in Manuscript Ca.

**Page 249. line 25. (IV. 58, 1.)** **"Thus, or the Ocean is the earthly Fire"** in Manuscript Ca. **"Thus, or earthly [fire]"** in Manuscript A. **"Thus, or earthly [fires]"** in Manuscript Ca. **"Thus, the earthly [fire]"** in Manuscript B.

**Page 250. line 2. (IV. 58, 1.)** **"Generator of beings"** <note>original: "janmyutpātakaḥ"</note> in Manuscript A. **"Producer of beings"** <note>original: "janmyutpādakaḥ"</note> in Manuscript Ca. **"Generator of beings"** <note>original: "janmyutpātṛko"</note> in Manuscript B.

**Page 250. line 3. (IV. 58, 1.)** **"Moving in the ocean"** <note>original: "samudravaṇā"</note> in Manuscripts B and Ca. **"Walking in the ocean"** <note>original: "samudracaraṇā"</note> in Manuscripts A and C2.

**Page 250. line 17. (IV. 58, 2.)** **"We shall praise"** <note>original: "stavāma"</note> || **"We praise"** <note>original: "stuvāmo"</note> in Manuscript B. **"We praise"** <note>original: "stumo"</note> in Manuscripts A and C.

**Page 250. line 19. (IV. 58, 2.)** **"The horns are the forms of the directions, or the forms of the four Vedas"** in Manuscript Ca.

**Page 251. line 4. (IV. 58, 3.)** **"He [belongs] to the three castes through the three Vedas"** in Manuscript Ca. In **Ápastamba's Ritual Definitions** <note>original: "Paribhāshā-sūtras"</note> we have: **"1. We shall explain the sacrifice. 2. It belongs to the three castes: the Brahmin, the Noble [Kshatriya], and the Merchant [Vaishya]. 3. It is ordained by the three Vedas."** See the **Journal of the German Oriental Society** <note>original: "Zeitschrift der Deutschen Morgenländischen Gesellschaft"</note>, volume 9, page 43, in the article **"On the Funeral Rites among the Brahmins by Max Müller."**

**Page 251. line 11. (IV. 58, 3.)** **"The Great God: this soul of the sacrifice, the god of great power"** in Manuscript Ca.

**Page 251. line 14. (IV. 58, 3.)** **"Indeed, because of being for the purpose of hearing"** in Manuscript A. Same in Manuscript C and Manuscript Aa by the first hand. Same in Manuscript Aa by the second hand. Same in Manuscript A. **"Indeed, because of being worthy of being heard"** in Manuscript Ca.

<summary>This page lists scholarly variant readings for Rig Veda hymns concerning agricultural deities and the nature of sacrifice, notably debating whether the "Shunasira" refers to Indra, Vayu, or the Sun. It also cites the ritual specialist Apastamba regarding the social classes eligible to perform Vedic sacrifices.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the critical apparatus for the Rig Veda commentary. It concludes the variant readings for the final hymn of Mandala IV (Hymn 58, dedicated to Ghee or Agni) and begins the variants for Mandala V, specifically the first few hymns dedicated to Agni. The translator notes that manuscript "Ca" often provides more expansive or corrective readings compared to the older "A" and "B" manuscripts.</meta>

<page-num>xxiii</page-num>

->**VARIANT READINGS**<-

## Critical Notes

**Page 251. line 20. (IV. 58, 3.)** **"Connected by being of the nature of Agni and others"** <note>original: "agnyādyātmakatvena sambaddhaḥ"</note> in Manuscript Ca. **"Connected by mutual nature"** <note>original: "anyonyātmakatvena saṃbandhaḥ"</note> in Manuscripts A and B.

**Page 252. line 16. (IV. 58, 5.)** **"Born from water"** <note>original: "apsambhavo"</note> in Manuscript Ca. **"From the water, the birth"** <note>original: "apaḥ sambhavo"</note> in Manuscripts A and B.

**Page 252. line 25. (IV. 58, 6.)** **"Above this fire || above"** is missing in Manuscripts A and B.

**Page 253. line 19. (IV. 58, 7.)** **"He, like one splitting wood"** <note>original: "sa yathā kāṣṭhā bhindan"</note> in Manuscript Ca.

**Page 254. lines 11 and 13. (IV. 58, 9.)** **"Manifesting"** <note>original: "vyañjantyaḥ"</note> instead of the grammatically correct **"causing to manifest"** <note>original: "vyañjayantyaḥ"</note>, a mistake of frequent occurrence in Sāyana <note>Sāyana is the primary medieval commentator on the Vedas</note>.

**Page 255. line 2. (IV. 58, 11.)** **"At the end of that, thus the verse"** in Manuscript C. **"At the end of that, thus the extent"** in Manuscript A. **"At the end of that, the ladle"** <note>original: "ghṛtācī"</note> in Manuscript B.

**Page 255. line 8. (IV. 58, 11.)** **"Resting upon the whole world"** in Manuscript B. **"Resting upon the whole world, upon the entire collection of beings. And even that is called the abode, the family, the origins || so it is said"** in Manuscript Ca; missing in Manuscripts A and C2.

**Page 255. line 8. (IV. 58, 11.)** **"Within the ocean in the form of the submarine fire"** <note>original: "vaḍavāgnitvena"</note> in Manuscript B. **"Within the ocean of the atmosphere, in the form of the solar sphere"** in Manuscript Ca; missing in Manuscripts A and C2.

->**Mandala V**<-

**Page 257. line 13. (V. 1, 3.)** **"Then"** <note>original: "tadā"</note> in Manuscript B. **"Exactly when"** <note>original: "yadaiva"</note> in Manuscript C. **"When"** <note>original: "yadava"</note> in Manuscript A.

**Page 257. line 26. (V. 1, 4.)** **"Multiform, of various shapes"** <note>original: "virūpe nānārūpe"</note> in Manuscript Ca.

**Page 260. line 4. (V. 1, 9.)** **"For which sacrifice"** in Manuscript B.

**Page 260. line 6. (V. 1, 9.)** **"Of the human [women], who take the form of the sacrificer"** in Manuscript Ca.

**Page 260. line 15. (V. 1, 10.)** The word **"Great"** <note>original: "mahi"</note> from the text is left unexplained in Manuscripts A and C. **"Large, great, broad, auspicious, great, and worthy of praise"** in Manuscript B.

**Page 261. line 23. (V. 2, 1.)** **"Ikshvaku"** <note>A legendary king</note> in Manuscripts A and B. **"The descendant of Ikshvaku"** <note>original: "aikṣvākaḥ"</note> in Manuscript C.

**Page 262. line 5. (V. 2, 1.)** **"Through passion"** in Manuscript C. **"Through speed"** in Manuscripts A and B.

**Page 262. line 9. (V. 2, 1.)** **"Thus singing, that Rishi [found] a wife born of the sin of killing a Brahmin"** in Manuscript C. **"Thus singing, the Rishi [found] his wife born of the sin of killing a Brahmin"** in Manuscript A. **"Thus singing, that Rishi [found] a wife born of the sin of killing a Brahmin"** <note>A slight grammatical variation</note> in Manuscript B.

**Page 262. line 11. (V. 2, 1.)** **"Having properly satisfied that [Brahmin]"** in Manuscript C. **"Having satisfied Sakastare"** in Manuscript A. **"Having satisfied on a ritual seat"** <note>original: "saṃstare"</note> in Manuscript B.

**Page 262. line 13. (V. 2, 1.)** **"Running"** or **"Washing"** in Manuscripts A and C. **"Holding"** in Manuscript B.

**Page 262. line 21. (V. 2, 1.)** **"Placed, standing"** in Manuscript B. **"Standing"** in Manuscript C; missing in Manuscript A.

**Page 262. line 21. (V. 2, 1.)** **"In front, in the forward region"** in Manuscript Ca. **"In front"** in Manuscript B; missing in Manuscript A.

**Page 263. line 4. (V. 2, 1.)** **"Covered by a cushion"** in Manuscript B and Manuscript Ca (by the first hand). **"Split by a cushion"** in Manuscript A and Manuscript Ca (by the second hand).

**Page 263. line 9. (V. 2, 2.)** **"The birth of the boy"** in Manuscripts A and B. **"The birth of the boy"** <note>different spelling</note> in Manuscript B (first hand). **"The killing of the boy"** <note>original: "hananam", likely a scribal error for "jananam" (birth)</note> in Manuscript B (second hand). **"The mother of the boy"** in Manuscript C.

**Page 264. line 2. (V. 2, 4.)** **"In the fire-wood"** <note>original: "araṇyāṃ"</note> in Manuscript C. **"Belonging to the forest"** in Manuscripts A and B.

**Page 264. line 22. (V. 2, 6.)** **"Among mortals; in their respective worlds"** in Manuscript Ca.

**Page 264. line 26. (V. 2, 6.)** **"In the sacred truths"** <note>original: "ṛte brahmāṇi"</note> || **"Sacred truths"** in Manuscripts A and C. **"Truth, sacred truths"** in Manuscript B.

**Page 265. line 1. (V. 2, 6.)** **"Tip of the branch"** <note>original: "prākhāmayaṃ"</note> || **"Cloud of the branch"** in Manuscripts Aa, B, and C. **"Branch of the cloud"** <note>original: "śākhāṃ tegaṃ"</note> in Manuscript A.

**Page 265. line 11. (V. 2, 7.)** **"From various sacrificial posts"** in Manuscript Ca. **"From many posts"** in Manuscripts A and B.

**Page 265. line 14. (V. 2, 7.)** **"This is an act of praise"** || **"This is an act of praise"** in Manuscript Ca (first hand). **"Because it is an act of praise"** in Manuscripts A, B, and C.

**Page 266. line 20. (V. 2, 10.)** **"Destruction"** <note>original: "bhaṅgaṃ"</note> in Manuscript B. **"Which two"** <note>original: "yāvāṃ"</note> in Manuscript A. **"Which two"** <note>slight variation</note> in Manuscript C.

**Page 268. line 21. (V. 3, 3.)** **"Waters"** <note>original: "apo"</note> taken from Manuscript B; missing in Manuscripts A and C.

**Page 268. line 22. (V. 3, 3.)** **"O Agni, producer [of things]"** in Manuscript C. **"O Agni, increased by Rudra"** <note>original: "rudrāvardhitaragne"</note> in Manuscript A. **"O Agni, increased by Rudra"** <note>standard spelling</note> in Manuscript B.

## Critical Notes

->**VARIANT READINGS.**<-

**"Absence of dropping (of a letter)"** <note>original: "pābhāvaḥ"</note> in **Manuscript C 2**: compare **Pāṇini's Grammar 6.4.136** and **Rig Veda 6.15.6.** It may be meant for **"the absence of dropping (of a letter) due to the rule of 'diversity of usage';"** <note>original: "bahulavacanācca-lopābhāvaḥ"</note> compare **Pāṇini 3.3.1.**

**Page 305. line 2. (V. 11, 2.)** **"Middle-accented"** <note>original: "madhyodāttaḥ"</note> versus **"End-accented"** <note>original: "antodāttaḥ"</note> in **Manuscripts A and Ca.**

**Page 308. line 4. (V. 12, 3.)** **"Knowing"** <note>original: "navedāḥ"</note> is explained as **"one who knows"** <note>original: "jñātā"</note>; and **"you should be"** <note>original: "bhuvaḥ"</note> as **"may you become"** <note>original: "bhaveḥ"</note> in **Manuscript C 2.** **"Knowing, you should be"** <note>original: "navedāḥ bhuvaḥ"</note> in **Manuscript Ca.** **"Knowing, you should be, may you become"** <note>original: "navedāḥ bhuvaḥ bhaveḥ"</note> in **Manuscript A.** **"Knowing, you should be, not knowing"** <note>original: "navedāḥ bhuvaḥ na vennāsi"</note> in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 308. line 5. (V. 12, 3.)** **"Protector of the seasons"** <note>original: "ṛtūnāmṛtupā"</note> means **"protector of the seasons like Spring etc."** <note>original: "vasantādīnāṃ pālakaḥ"</note> in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 313. line 25. (V. 15, 2.)** **"Those sacrificers"** <note>original: "te yajamānāḥ"</note> versus **"Which sacrificers"** <note>original: "ye yajamānāḥ"</note> in **Manuscripts A, B, and Ca.**

**Page 315. line 3. (V. 15, 6.)** **"'Tayu' is a name for a thief."** <note>original: "tāyuriti stenanāma"</note> **"Like a footstep, one's own path, placing it in a cave—in a secret place; hiding one's own light from enemies"** <note>original: "padamiva ātmīyaṃ mārgamiva guhā guhāyāṃ dadhānaḥ ātmanaḥ śatrūṇāṃ prakāśaṃ nidadhānaḥ"</note> in **Manuscript A (in the margin)** and **Manuscript C 2**, which leaves out **"one's own;"** <note>original: "ātmanaḥ"</note> **Manuscripts Ca and Aa** omit the whole passage. **"Like a thief, just as one holds and protects property in a cave, so he holds it"** <note>original: "tāyurna taskaro yathā guhāyāṃ padaṃ dravyaṃ dadhānaḥ dhārayan rakṣati tadvat"</note> in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 333. line 16. (V. 25, 9.)** **"Practicing our strength"** <note>original: "asmākaṃ balamācarantaṃ"</note> in **Manuscript A.** **"Destroyer of enemies"** <note>original: "śatrunāśakaṃ"</note> in **Manuscript B**; omitted in **Manuscript Ca.**

**Page 341. line 16. (V. 29, 1.)** The passage from **"they are"** <note>original: "santi"</note> to **"splendors"** <note>original: "tejāṃsi"</note> is from **Manuscript B.** **"The shining ones are bright, glowing, consisting of the sky, fire, and sun; celestial, divine, existing in the atmosphere; those are the splendors"** <note>original: "santi rocanaṃ rocanā rocamānāni dyuagni-sūryātmakāni divyā divyāni antarikṣe bhavāni tāni tejāṃsi"</note> in **Manuscript Ca**; omitted in **Manuscript A.**

**Page 341. line 18. (V. 29, 1.)** **"Pure in strength"** <note>original: "śuddhabalā"</note> in **Manuscripts A and Ca.** **"Auspicious in strength"** <note>original: "bhadrabalā"</note> in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 341. line 26. (V. 29, 2.)** **"From that"** <note>original: "tato"</note> in **Manuscript A.** **"In that way"** <note>original: "tathā"</note> in **Manuscript B.** **"Of those two"** <note>original: "tayoḥ"</note> in **Manuscript Ca.**

**Page 342. line 21. (V. 29, 4.)** **"They two go away"** <note>original: "vyetevau"</note>. **"They two go"** <note>original: "yetevau"</note> in **Manuscript A.** **"They two go away"** <note>original: "vyetevau"</note> in **Manuscript Ca.**

**Page 343. line 7. (V. 29, 5.)** **"Those who have the thunderbolt as their foot, etc."** <note>original: "vajrapādayaḥ"</note> in **Manuscripts A and Ca.** **"Agni and the others"** <note>original: "agnyādayaḥ"</note> in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 356. line 17. (V. 31, 5.)** **"Stones for overcoming"** <note>original: "abhibhavapāṣāṇāḥ"</note> in **Manuscripts Ca and B.** **"Stones of the act of overcoming"** <note>original: "abhibhavaṇapāṣāṇāḥ"</note> in **Manuscript A.**

**Page 357. line 14. (V. 31, 7.)** **"The young women, the winds"** <note>original: "yuvatīḥ pavanāḥ"</note> in **Manuscript A.** **"The Yavanas"** <note>original: "yavanāḥ"</note> in **Manuscript Ca**; omitted in **Manuscript B.** **"The Kapardins (those with braided hair)?"** <note>original: "kapadān?"</note>

**Page 357. line 15. (V. 31, 7.)** **"Or near"** <note>original: "samīpaṃ vā"</note>. **"Near"** <note>original: "samīpa"</note> in **Manuscripts A and Ca**; omitted in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 357. line 22. (V. 31, 8.)** **"On the further shore"** <note>original: "pāre"</note> in **Manuscript A.** **"Shore"** <note>original: "pāra"</note> in **Manuscript Ca.** **"The shore"** <note>original: "pāraḥ"</note> in **Manuscript B**; omitted in **Manuscript C 2.** Sāyaṇa mistook **"shore"** <note>original: "pāra"</note> in the Samhita text for a locative case.

**Page 366. line 17. (V. 33, 2.)** **"Season"** <note>original: "ṛtu"</note> after **"pleasure"** <note>original: "prītiṃ"</note> is omitted in **Manuscripts A and Ca.** **Manuscript B** puts it after **"forth."** <note>original: "pra"</note>

**Page 366. line 25. (V. 33, 3.)** **"That (which). Dropping of the case ending. Those."** <note>original: "yat | supo lopaḥ | ye"</note> in **Manuscript Ca.**

**Page 367. line 9. (V. 33, 4.)** **"O Indra, you are the showerer, the one who rains down desires; for Surya, the Sun, you have made a place in his own home, his own place. Furthermore, when there are many various hymns of praise belonging to you, then, fighting for the cow—the water of the rain—in the fertile lands endowed with crops, you establish [it] against the obstructor of waters; may it be equal"** <note>original: "he indra vṛṣā kāmānāṃ varṣakस्त्वं sūryāya citsūrya ca sva okasi svasthāne cakrartha kṛtavānasi | kiñca te tava yadyadā svabhūtāni puru purūṇi bahūnyukyokthāni śastrāṇi santi tadovarāsu śasyopetāsu bhūmiṣu gave vṛṣṭyudakāya yudhyan jalapratibandhakāt tattasthe saṃpādayāsi samāstu"</note> in **Manuscript B.** From **"collecting"** <note>original: "saṃharan"</note> to **"having been increased"** <note>original: "vardhitā san"</note> is omitted in **Manuscript Ca.**

**Page 367. line 20. (V. 33, 5.)** Instead of **"what kind of people are we,"** <note>original: "kīdṛśā vayaṃ"</note> **Manuscript B** has **"those living beings, we."** <note>original: "te satvā prāṇino vayaṃ"</note>

**Page 368. line 20. (V. 33, 7.)** **"By the described characteristic"** <note>original: "uktalakṣaṇena"</note>. **"By the characteristic of the hymn"** <note>original: "sūktalakṣaṇena"</note> in **Manuscripts A and Ca**; omitted in **Manuscript B.**

## Critical Notes

**Page 393. line 26. (Verse 41, 9.)** **"In praise; eight; seeking all around"** <note>original: "abhiṣṭau aṣṭau abhitaḥ eṣaṇe"</note> in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 394. line 10. (Verse 41, 10.)** **"Agni; and further, Agni in the world, Agni in the other"** <note>Agni is the god of fire; this likely refers to the different ritual or cosmic forms of fire</note> in **Manuscript A.** **"Agni in the other"** in **Manuscripts B and Ca.**

**Page 395. line 19. (Verse 41, 13.)** **"Carrying around, they cause to come"** <note>original: "pariharannāyayanti"</note> in **Manuscripts A and B.** **"Carrying around, they select"** <note>original: "pariharantro varyanti"</note> in **Manuscript Ca.**

**Page 398. line 11. (Verse 41, 19.)** The word **"or"** after **"of the water"** is added by conjecture. Yāska <note>the ancient author of the Nirukta, a treatise on Vedic etymology</note> does not use the word **"of light/energy"** <note>original: "tejaso"</note>, but rather **"of the brilliance/heavenly light"** <note>original: "jyotiṣo"</note>. Compare with the **Paris Manuscript** and the **East India House manuscript.**

**Page 400. line 5. (Verse 42, 3.)** **"Gold ornaments"** <note>original: "hiraṇyāni"</note> in **Manuscripts A and Ca.** **"Things easily sacrificed"** <note>original: "suyagāṇi"</note> in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 419. line 21. (Verse 44, 12.)** **"It is"** in **Manuscript A.** **"It shines"** in **Manuscripts B and Ca.**

**Page 420. line 2. (Verse 44, 13.)** The section from **"And he"** to **"Milch-cow"** <term>Dhenu: a milch-cow, often symbolizing the rewards of sacrifice or the earth</term> is left out in **Manuscript Ca.** **"He who is the place of all prayers and praises, who serves the assembly of gods, he is the sustainer of my son [the priest Sutambhara], the performer of the sacrifice of me, the seer Avatsara; he is the protector and giver of the fruits belonging to those who exist. Such is the meaning. The cow,"** etc. in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 420. line 5. (Verse 44, 13.)** **"And by the power of this"** in **Manuscript A.** **"Or by the power"** in **Manuscript Ca.** **"By the power"** in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 420. line 5. (Verse 44, 13.)** **"Thoroughly proclaiming"** in **Manuscript A.** **"Proclaiming"** in **Manuscripts B and Ca.**

**Page 420. line 6. (Verse 44, 13.)** **"The sustainer of the son is of such a kind"** in **Manuscript A.** **"The sustainer of the son is of such a kind"** <note>slightly different spelling</note> in **Manuscript Ca.** **"The term 'Sutambhara' [sustainer of the son] is a Vedic usage"** in **Manuscript B.**

**Page 420. line 21. (Verse 44, 15.)** The Samhita manuscripts (S. 1, 2, 3) add after verse 15 the following verse, which does not exist in the Word-for-Word texts (Padas), is not counted in the Index (Anukramaniká), and is not explained by the commentator Sáyana:

---

## Hymn Text

->You are awake in the world, O Knower of all Beings;<-
->You are awake when the one possessing the oblation sacrifices.<-
->I offer this oblation, placing it in the fire;<-
->By that, protect the secret name of the cows.<-
<note>This verse is an interpolation addressed to Jātavedas, an epithet of Agni (the Fire God).</note>

---

**Page 421. line 7. (Verse 45, 1.)** **"The connection is 'to the cows'; hidden"** in **Manuscripts A and Ca.** **"The connection is 'to the cows'"** in **Manuscript B.**

(Verse 51, 15.)** At the end of the hymn the Saṃhitā manuscripts give the following <term>Khila: a supplementary or "apocryphal" hymn not found in the standard Rig Veda padapāṭha</term>; **Manuscript S. 1.** and **S. ---

## Hymn Text

-> For a safe journey, let us mount Tārkṣya, whose wheels are unhurt, the great being, the bird of the deities, <-
-> the slayer of demons, the friend of Indra in battles; like a ship, may we ascend his great glory. || 1 || <-
-> To the one who delivers from distress, the descendant of Angiras and Gaya, and to Tārkṣya of the Atri family, with the mind, <-
-> with hands restrained in prayer, I take refuge. May there be safety for us; let there be fearlessness in times of narrow difficulty. || 2 || <-

## Critical Notes

->**VARIANT READINGS.**<-

**Page 450. line 21. (Verse 52, 12.)** **"Which Maruts"** <note>original: "yāmmarutaḥ" - here in a feminine or variant form</note> in **A. and Ca.** **"Those Maruts"** <note>original: "ye marutaḥ" - masculine</note> in **B.**

**Page 451. line 8. (Verse 52, 13.)** **"The visible great one... who..."** <note>original: "darśanīyāṃ mahatīṃ hrāto yā"</note> in **Ca.**, which is meant to be **"Visible or great."** <note>original: "darśanīyā mahatī vā"</note>

**Page 451. line 9. (Verse 52, 13.)** **"Creators of all"** <note>original: "sarvata vidhātāraḥ"</note> in **A.** **"Of all..."** <note>original: "sarvasya ci..."</note> in **Ca.** **"All-knowing creators"** <note>original: "sarvavidhātāraḥ"</note> in **B.**

**Page 451. line 10. (Verse 52, 13.)** **"Now, 'worship,' 'delight,' 'stand'; because it follows, it is unaccented. In both places, there is a Samhitic lengthening of the vowel."** <note>original: "atha namasya ramaya tiṣṭha uttaratvadanudāttaḥ | ubhayatra sāṃhitiko dīrghaḥ ||"</note> in **Ca.** after the word **"praise."** <note>original: "stuhi"</note> As **"delight"** <note>original: "ramayā"</note> has been explained as an adjective, this addition was probably a marginal gloss.

**Page 451. line 17. (Verse 52, 14.)** **"And thus 'toward' [accha], meaning 'come' is the implied remainder. From the root cyu..."** <note>original: "tathā cāccha āgaccheti śeṣaḥ | cyuperu..."</note> followed by: **"And thus 'toward', he comes, from the root cyu..."** in **Ca.** **"And thus 'toward', meaning 'go toward' is the implied remainder."** in **A.** **"He comes, from the root cyu..."** in **B.**

**Page 452. line 2. (Verse 52, 15.)** **"Or else, the word 'na' is in the sense of 'now'. The praise to be spoken says 'he carries the gods'. Thus, 'thinking of these divine Maruts, pressing [the Soma], praising'..."** <note>original: "yadvā neti saṃpratyarthe | vahati devāniti vakṣyamāṇā stutiḥ | tathā eṣāṃ etāndevyānmaruto'ccha manvānaḥ sunvan abhiṣṭuvan iti"</note> in **Ca.** after the word **"he thinks."** <note>original: "manute"</note>

**Page 452. line 3. (Verse 52, 15.)** **"By the wise ones, the stimulators"** <note>original: "medhāvibhiḥ prerayitṛbhiḥ"</note> in **A.**

**Page 452. line 13. (Verse 52, 16.)** **"Of the two narratives"** <note>original: "ākhyānayoḥ"</note> in **Ca.** **"Of the two grave accents"** <note>original: "nighātayoḥ" - a technical term for the unaccented Vedic pitch</note> in **A.**

**Page 453. line 18. (Verse 53, 1.)** **"In pleasures"** <note>original: "sukhepu"</note> in **A.** **"In the sacrifices"** <note>original: "makheṣu"</note> in **B. and Ca.**

**Page 453. line 18. (Verse 53, 1.)** **"The expanding ones"** <note>original: "pṛthatīḥ"</note> in **B.** **"Expanding"** <note>original: "pṛthataḥ"</note> in **Ca.** **"Expanding ones"** <note>original: "pṛthatyaḥ"</note> in **A.**

**Page 454. line 1. (Verse 53, 2.)** **"The sound of a shout"** <note>original: "ākrośadhvaniṃ"</note> in **Ca.**

**Page 454. line 2. (Verse 53, 2.)** **"How? In what manner? Those who previously desired."** <note>original: "kathā kathaṃ yaḥ pūrvamicchaṃti"</note> in **B.**

**Page 454. line 4. (Verse 53, 2.)** **"Rain and so forth"** <note>original: "vṛṣṭyādīni"</note> added in **A.** after the word **"they might descend."** <note>original: "avatareyuḥ"</note>

**Page 454. line 10. (Verse 53, 3.)** **"He might produce"** <note>original: "janayāt"</note> in **A. and Ca.**; **B.** omits the whole passage.

**Page 454. line 11. (Verse 53, 3.)** **"They say to me: 'He speaks thus'."** <note>original: "itthaṃ lapate mahyamāhuḥ"</note> in **A.** **"They say to me of the one speaking thus."** <note>original: "itthaṃ me mahyaṃ lapaṃtamāhuḥ"</note> in **B.** **"They say to me: 'Speaking thus'."** <note>original: "ittha mahya lapaṃtamāhuḥ"</note> in **Ca.**

**Page 454. line 13. (Verse 53, 3.)** **"Stainless ones"** <note>original: "alepāḥ"</note> in **A. and Ca.** **"Sinless ones"** <note>original: "apāpāḥ"</note> in **B.**

**Page 454. line 14. (Verse 53, 3.)** **"Standing thus"** <note>original: "tathā sthitān"</note> in **B. and Ca.** **"Standing as they were"** <note>original: "yathāsthitān"</note> in **A.**

**Page 454. line 25. (Verse 53, 4.)** **"In the desert regions"** <note>original: "dhanyasu nisṛdakapradeśeṣu" - likely for 'dhanvasu', waterless lands</note> in **B.**

**Page 455. line 9. (Verse 53, 5.)** **"Your chariots"** <note>original: "yuṣmākaṃ rathān"</note> in **A.** **"Your... you"** <note>original: "yuṣmākaṃ yuṣmān"</note> in **B.** **"You"** <note>original: "yuṣmān"</note> in **Ca.**

**Page 455. line 9. (Verse 53, 5.)** **"For joy"** <note>original: "modāya"</note> in **A.** **"For exhilaration"** <note>original: "madāya" - often referring to the effects of Soma</note> in **B. and Ca.**

**Page 455. line 11. (Verse 53, 5.)** **"Splendor"** <note>original: "dīptiḥ"</note> in **A., B., and Ca.**

**Page 455. line 11. (Verse 53, 5.)** **"In the rain... the rains"** <note>original: "vṛṣṭyāṃ || vṛṣṭyaḥ"</note> in **A., B., and C.**

**Page 456. line 6. (Verse 53, 7.)** **"Cleaving from the cloud"** <note>original: "nirbhiṃdaṃto meghāt"</note> in **B. and Ca.** **"Finding/cleaving?"** <note>original: "vittiraṃto"</note> in **A.**

**Page 456. line 7. (Verse 53, 7.)** **"A newly delivered [mother/cow]"** <note>original: "navaprasūtikā"</note> in **A.**

**Page 456. line 9. (Verse 53, 7.)** **"The rivers turn toward release in various ways..."** <note>original: "nadyo vimokāya vartaṃte vividhaṃ"</note> etc. in **A.**

**Page 456. line 10. (Verse 53, 7.)** **"Having turned back"** <note>original: "pratinivṛtya"</note> in **Ca.** **"Having turned toward"** <note>original: "prativṛtya"</note> in **A.**

**Page 456. line 18. (Verse 53, 8.)** **"From the far distance, in a remote land, here and there in the heavenly world, etc."** <note>original: "parāvato dūradeśe tatra tatra dyulokādau"</note> in **A.** **"From the far distance... there, in various remote lands, etc."** <note>original: "parāvato dū tatra tatra dūradeśādau"</note> in **Ca.**

**Page 457. line 2. (Verse 53, 9.)** **"Not"** <note>original: "mā"</note> before **"debased"** <note>original: "nikṛṣṭaṃ"</note> from **B.**

**Page 457. line 12. (Verse 53, 10.)** **B.** has only the second explanation: **"O Maruts, of the chariots that are gliding, most new, of you who possess the dregs [of Soma], I praise the host of Maruts which is overpowering, brilliant, and radiant."** <note>original: "he marutaḥ rathānāṃ rahaṇaśīlānāṃ navyasīnāṃ ajīṣīṇāṃ vaḥ yuṣmākaṃ śardhaṃ yeṣāmabhibhāvukaṃ tveṣaṃ dīptaṃ taṃ mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ staumi |"</note> etc.

**Page 457. line 22. (Verse 53, 11.)** **"Desired to be distinguished"** <note>original: "vivikṣita..."</note> in **Ca.** **"Intended"** <note>original: "vivakṣita"</note> in **A.** **"A troop whose number is not specifically intended"** <note>original: "avivakṣitagaṇo vrātaḥ"</note> inserted by **Ca.** in the commentary of the preceding verse, instead of **"Now, [the verse] addressed in the third person."** <note>original: "atha parokṣakṛtaḥ"</note>

**Page 459. line 2. (Verse 53, 14.)** **"All that"** <note>original: "tatsarve"</note> in **A.** **"By all"** <note>original: "sarveṇa"</note> in **B. and Ca.**

**Page 459. line 12. (Verse 53, 15.)** **"It becomes thus"** <note>original: "evaṃ bhavati"</note> in **A.** **"It becomes thus"** <note>original: "evaṃ bhavati"</note> in **B.** **"Those who become thus"** <note>original: "ya evaṃ bhavaṃti"</note> in **Ca.**

## Critical Notes

**Page 461. line 10. (Verse 54, 3.)** **"Risen up"** <note>original: "udgataṃ"</note> in **B.** and **Ca.** **"Elevated"** <note>original: "unnataṃ"</note> in **A.**

**Page 461. line 20. (Verse 54, 4.)** **"Regions, the worlds"** <note>original: "rajāṃsi lokān"</note> in **B.**

**Page 461. line 20. (Verse 54, 4.)** From **"O shakers"** <note>original: "he dhūtayaḥ"</note> to **"O Maruts"** <note>original: "he marutaḥ"</note> is omitted in **Ca.** The same gap <note>lacuna</note> seems to have existed in the manuscript from which **B.** was copied, because **B.** provides a completely different explanation: **"O shakers, O Maruts who cause things to tremble, you have conquered the unknown paths; you do not harm us. The comparison is to ships: just as they protect those who have taken refuge in them, so do you."** <note>original: "ajñānmārgān vyajaya he dhūtayaḥ kaṃpayitāro marutaḥ yūyaṃ īṃ asmān nāha riṣyatha na hiṃsatha dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ nāvaḥ yathā āśritānāṃ rakṣanti tadvat"</note>

**Page 461. line 21. (Verse 54, 4.)** **"Conquered"** <note>original: "vivyajaya"</note> || **"Trembled"** <note>original: "vivyatha"</note> in **A.**

**Page 462. line 8. (Verse 54, 5.)** **"Those who struck down"** <note>original: "nihatavantaḥ"</note> in **A.** **"Those who placed/fixed"** <note>original: "nihitavantaḥ"</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 462. line 15. (Verse 54, 6.)** **"From the rain"** <note>original: "vṛṣṭeḥ"</note> in **A.** **"Variously"** <note>original: "vividhaṃ"</note> in **B.**

**Page 462. line 15. (Verse 54, 6.)** In **Ca.** there is a gap <note>lacuna</note> from **"from the rain"** <note>original: "vṛṣṭeḥ"</note> to **"tree"** <note>original: "vṛkṣo"</note>. Again, **B.** has unique readings: **"O wise ones, O Maruts the various disposers, when you strike the watery cloud, then that host shone brilliantly, etc."** <note>original: "he vedhasaḥ vividhaṃ vidhātāraḥ marutaḥ yat arṇasaṃ meghaṃ moṣatha tāḍayatha tat śardhaḥ abhrāji aśobhata etc."</note>

**Page 462. line 15. (Verse 54, 6.)** **"Troop"** <note>original: "gaṇaṃ"</note> in **A.** and the **C. Mill** manuscript. **"Strength?"** <note>original: "balaṃ?"</note>

**Page 463. line 14. (Verse 54, 8.)** **"Seizing that, the Maruts are the separators of the mass of matter; 'men' refers to those in human form or the leaders"** <note>original: "tadgraṃto marutaḥ saṃghātakasya padārtha(sya marg.) viśleṣayitāraḥ naro narākārā netāro vā"</note> in **A.** **"Seizing that, the Maruts, the men, are the conquerors of communities, the separators of the mass of matter; 'men' refers to the leaders"** <note>original: "tadgraṃto marutaḥ naro saṃghātakasya padārthasya grāmajitaḥ viśleṣayitāraḥ naro nakārā netāro vā"</note> in **Ca.** **"Seizing that, the Maruts, the men, the leaders of the mass of matter, the conquerors of communities, the separators, the Maruts"** <note>original: "tadgraṃto marutaḥ naraḥ saṃghātakasya padārthasya netāraḥ grāmajitaḥ viśleṣayitāraḥ marutaḥ"</note> in **B.**

**Page 463. line 15. (Verse 54, 8.)** **"The word 'svayaṃ'"** <note>oneself</note> in **A.** **"The word 'niyut'"** <note>team of horses</note> in **Ca.**

**Page 463. line 16. (Verse 54, 8.)** **"Like men"** <note>original: "nara iva" (for "naro yathā")</note> in **A.** and **Ca.**; missing in **B.**

**Page 463. line 17. (Verse 54, 8.)** **"Splendid"** <note>original: "dīmrā"</note> in **A.** **"Shining/Blazing"** <note>original: "dīptāra"</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 463. line 19. (Verse 54, 8.)** **"When they flowed"** <note>original: "yadākṣaran"</note> in **Ca.** **"When they sounded"** <note>original: "yadāsvaran"</note> in **A.**; missing in **B.**

**Page 464. line 2. (Verse 54, 9.)** **"Maruts, make them move"** <note>original: "marutsāraya"</note> in **A.** **"Maruts, beyond"** <note>original: "marutparā"</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 464. line 5. (Verse 54, 9.)** **"Possessing food"** <note>original: "kṣumatayaḥ"</note> in **Ca.** **"Offerings"** <note>original: "sutayaḥ"</note> in **A.** **"Thoughts"** <note>original: "matayaḥ"</note> in **B.**

**Page 468. line 19. (Verse 55, 5.)** **"From the means of the sea"** <note>original: "samudravatsādhanāt"</note> in **Ca.** **"From the means of the color of the sea"** <note>original: "samudravaṛṇasādhanāt"</note> in **A.**

**Page 475. line 21. **Page 476. line 8. (Hymn 57, Verse 4.)** **"Of like form"** <note>original: sarūpāḥ</note> in **A.** **"Similar"** <note>original: sadṛśāḥ</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 477. line 4. (Hymn 57, Verse 6.)** **"To be dug around"** <note>original: viparikhātavyāḥ</note> || **"To be dug around"** <note>original: viparikhōtavyāḥ</note> <note>These are minor spelling variations of the same Sanskrit verbal adjective</note> in **A.** and **Ca.**

**Page 477. line 7. (Hymn 57, Verse 6.)** **"Likewise, whatever all-encompassing beauty is fixed upon the bodies or limbs"** <note>original: tathā yaḥ tanūṣu avayaveṣu viśvā śrī sarvā kāntiḥ pipiśe āśritā</note> in **B.** In **Ca.** this passage and the beginning of the next verse are given only in the margin. **B.** has supplied the missing text independently, as was done in Hymn 55, Verse 9.

**Page 477. line 14. (Hymn 60, Verse 6.)** **"You are in the highest, the most excellent, the furthest heaven"** <note>original: yūyaṃ ut utkṛṣṭe uttame carame divi</note> in **A.** and **Ca.** **"You are in the most excellent, highest heaven"** <note>original: yūyaṃ uttame utkṛṣṭe divi</note> in **B.**

**Page 488. line 3. (Hymn 60, Verse 6.)** **"From knowing"** <note>original: vijñāddhi</note> in **Ca.**; the rest, which should follow on the next page, is left out. **"From knowing, you know"** <note>original: vijñāt vettha</note> in **B.** **"From knowing, know thou; 'know' is the remaining word to be supplied."** <note>original: vijñāt viddhi jānīhīti śeṣaḥ</note> in **Aa.**

**Page 488. line 24. (Hymn 60, Verse 8.)** **"With those who possess good life (the long-lived)"** <note>original: svāyubhirāyuṣmadbhiḥ</note> from **B.**

**Page 489. line 2. (Hymn 61, Verse 1.)** **"To be tamed"** <note>original: dābhyaṃ</note> according to the *Anukramaṇī* <note>Vedic index of poets and meters</note>.

**Page 489. line 11. (Hymn 61, Verse 1.)** **"The daughter"** <note>original: sutāṃ</note> in **A.** **"The king"** <note>original: nṛpaṃ</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 489. line 12. (Hymn 61, Verse 1.)** **"You will give"** <note>original: pradāsyasi</note> in **A.** **"I will give"** <note>original: pradāsyahaṃ</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 489. line 23. (Hymn 61, Verse 1.)** **"By those who know the delighted Self"** <note>original: muditātmavidbhiḥ</note> in **B.** and **Ca.** by the same error.

**Page 489. line 24. (Hymn 61, Verse 1.)** **"Afterward, having gone back to the house, having obtained a hundred cows again; then..."** <note>original: paścā tpunargṛhaṃ gatvā bhūyo labdhvā gavāṃ śataṃ । tato</note> in **A.** **"Having gone to the house of Purumīḷha; afterward, having gone back to the house; having obtained a hundred cows again, to be tamed..."** <note>original: purumīḷhgṛhaṃ paścāt gatvā paścātpunargṛhaṃ । gatvā bhūyo labdhvā gavāṃ śataṃ dābhyo</note> in **Ca.** **"Having gone to the house of Purumīḷha; afterward, having gone back to the house to obtain a hundred cows again, to be tamed..."** <note>original: purumīḷhgṛhaṃ paścāt gatvā paścātpunargṛhaṃ gatvā bhūyo labdhuṃ gavāṃ śataṃ dābhyo</note> in **B.**

## Critical Notes

**Page 489. line 24. (Hymn 61, Verse 1.)** **"And urged by the teacher"** <note>original: cābhyācoditaḥ</note> in **A.** **"And urged by the king's command"** <note>original: cājñāvoditaḥ</note> in **Ca.** **"Beautifully urged"** <note>original: cārucoditaḥ</note> in **B.** **"By the king"** <note>original: rājñā</note> is a scholarly conjecture <note>a researcher's educated guess to correct a likely error in the manuscripts</note>.

**Page 490. line 16. (Hymn 61, Verse 3.)** **"Striking continuously, this is the meaning"** <note>original: tāḍayanvanta ata ityarthaḥ</note> by conjecture. This reading is found in **Ca.** Manuscript **A.** reads **"Striking..."** <note>original: tāḍayanvata</note> followed by "this is the meaning."

**Page 490. line 17. (Hymn 61, Verse 3.)** **"Having thoroughly separated"** <note>original: vi vivicya</note> || **"He separated"** <note>original: viveca</note> in **Ca.** **"Having separated"** <note>original: vivicya</note> in **A.** **"They restrain or control"** <note>original: viyamuḥ niyacchanti</note> in **B.**

**Page 490. line 21. (Hymn 61, Verse 4.)** **"Go ye"** <note>original: itana</note> in the <term>Pada Manuscript<gloss>A version of the Veda where every word is separated and analyzed</gloss></term> P. 1. 2. **"Go ye"** <note>original: etana</note> in the <term>Sanhita Manuscript<gloss>The version of the Veda where words are joined together in continuous recitation</gloss></term> S. 1. 2. 3.

**Page 490. line 25. (Hymn 61, Verse 4.)** **"Sons of Rudra"** <note>original: rudraputrā</note> in **B.** and **Ca.** **"Having Rudra as a husband"** <note>original: rudrapatikā</note> in **A.**

**Page 490. line 25. (Hymn 61, Verse 4.)** **"Like the stars, etc., are shining"** <note>original: tānnādayo yathā dīptāḥ</note> from **A.**

**Page 490. line 26. (Hymn 61, Verse 4.)** The explanation of **"Go ye"** <note>original: etana; called 'itana' in the Pada manuscripts</note> is left out in **A.** and **Ca.** Manuscript **B.** reads: **"Burnt by the fire of asceticism, as you might be, in that manner you are brilliant beyond that."** <note>original: agnitapaḥ-agninā taptāḥ yathā asatha tadvat parā tena pradīptā bhavathaḥ</note>

**Page 491. line 15. (Hymn 61, Verse 6.)** **"O Self"** or **"O Soul"** <note>original: he ātman</note> in **B.** after the phrase **"and also."**

**Page 491. line 15. (Hymn 61, Verse 6.)** **"Or rather, this very one [is used] in the sense of 'only'. Among women, she is the same."** <note>original: yadvā utaitayamevakārārthe। strīṣu saiva</note> in **A.** **"Or rather, the word 'uto' or 'va' is used in the sense of 'only'. Among women, there is only one."** <note>original: yadvā uto vetyevamevakārārthe strīṣu ekaiva</note> in **Ca.** This is not present in **B.**

**Page 491. line 18. (Hymn 61, Verse 6.)** **"A deity is one who is extended/pleased by praise and the like."** <note>original: deva yena tāyante stutyādinā sa devataḥ</note> in **A.** by a second hand <note>added by a later scribe</note>. The first hand in **A.** and manuscript **Ca.** read **"By the way of the deities, they are extended..."** A sentence is missing, which should be **"The opposite is a non-deity"** or **"Another is a non-deity."** Manuscript **B.** reads: **"The gods are not extended by those of praise, etc. (instead of 'by praise, etc., by which'); he is a non-deity."**

**Page 491. line 24. (Hymn 61, Verse 7.)** **"Likewise, he recognizes the one who is satisfied"** <note>original: tathā tṛpyantaṃ vijānāti</note> is omitted in **Ca.** Therefore, **B.** has a peculiar explanation: **"He recognizes the thirsty one as the satisfied one."**

**Page 492. line 18. (Hymn 61, Verse 9.)** **"For the wise one"** <note>original: viprāya</note>, left out in **A.** and **Ca.**, is inserted in **B.** after **"for one who has an abundant house."**

**Page 492. line 20. (Hymn 61, Verse 9.)** **"They two restrained; they two specially restrained,"** <note>original: viyematuḥ। viśeṣeṇa yamayatuḥ</note> etc., in **A.**

**Page 493. line 2. (Hymn 61, Verse 10.)** **"I praise him"** <note>original: taṃ stuve</note> in **B.** **"Praise ye!"** <note>original: stuvata</note> in **A.** and **Ca.**

**Page 493. line 7. (Hymn 61, Verse 11.)** **"By those famous among people"** <note>original: janaprasiddhaiḥ</note> || **"By those famous among women"** <note>original: janīprasiddhaiḥ</note> in **A.** **"By those famous"** <note>original: prasiddhaiḥ</note> in **Ca.**

**Page 494. line 23. (Hymn 61, Verse 17.)** The introductory verses are wanting in **B.**

**Page 494. line 23. (Hymn 61, Verse 17.)** After the word **"Racyi-"**, at the beginning of the third <term>Śloka<gloss>a specific meter of Sanskrit verse</gloss></term>, three leaves are missing in **Ca.** These have been replaced by others written by a modern hand. This omission extends as far as the words **"Abna vya-"** in Hymn 62, Verse 7. It can be proven that these leaves were copied from Manuscript **A.** because there are no variant readings between **A.** and **Ca.** in this section, and they share the same errors; for example, in 62, 6, they both read **"be thou"** <note>original: bhavayeti</note> where **B.** reads **"be thou"** <note>original: bhavaya iti</note> with proper word separation. They also share **"supporting many, golden-formed,"** etc.

**Page 495. line 5. (Hymn 61, Verse 17.)** **"O Blessed One"** <note>original: bhagavan</note> in **A. C.** **"The Lord"** or **"The Blessed One"** <note>original: bhagavān</note> in **A.** and **Ca.**

**Page 496. line 17. (Hymn 62, Verse 1.)** **"According to the custom"** <note>original: manvarya°</note> || **"According to the custom"** <note>original: anvarya°</note> in **A.** and **Ca.** (compare Rig Veda 1. 118, 5).

**Page 496. line 18. (Hymn 62, Verse 1.)** **"The best, the singular, the chief, the praiseworthy"** <note>original: śreṣṭhaṃ ekaṃ mukhyaṃ praśasyaṃ</note> in **B.**

**Page 497. line 5. (Hymn 62, Verse 2.)** **"Due to the impossibility of returning"** <note>original: āvarttanāyogāt</note> || **"Due to the impossibility of one who is returning"** <note>original: āvarttamānāyogāt</note> in **A.** and **Ca.**

**Page 497. line 12. (Hymn 62, Verse 3.)** **"Those two from whose presence"** <note>original: yayoḥ sakāśāttau</note> in **A.** and **Ca.** **"By which two, those two"** <note>original: yābhyāṃ tau</note> in **B.**

**Page 498. line 12. (Hymn 62, Verse 5.)** **"Whose strength is command"** <note>original: ājñabalau</note> in **A.** and **Ca.** **"Whose strength is dependent"** <note>original: āyattabalau</note> in **B.**

**Page 498. line 26. (Hymn 62, Verse 6.)** **"Possessing many supporting pillars, beautiful..."** <note>original: anekāvaṣṭabhakastambhopetaṃ sau°</note> in **A.** and **Ca.** **"Possessing many pillars, beautiful..."** <note>original: anekastambhopetaṃ sau</note> in **B.**

**Page 499. line 9. (Hymn 62, Verse 7.)** **"Made of iron"** <note>original: ayovikārā</note> in **A.** and **Ca.** **"Made of gold"** <note>original: hiraṇyavikārā</note> in **B.**

**Page 499. line 11. (Hymn 62, Verse 7.)** **"The lightning, and she shines in the sky"** <note>original: vidyut sā ca divibhrājate</note> in **A.** **"The lightning, and she shines in the sky"** <note>original: vidyut sā ca divi bhrājate</note> in **Ca.** **"The lightning, like that"** <note>original: vidyut tadvat</note> in **B.**

**Page 499. line 12. (Hymn 62, Verse 7.)** **"Or it grew bright. The word 'va' is used in the sense of 'like'."** <note>original: titvile vā। vāśabda ivārthe</note> in **Ca.**

## Critical Notes

**Page 499. line 14. (Hymn 62, Verse 7.)** **"The post, the sacrificial pillar, is constructed and stands in place."** <note>original: nirmitā sthūṇo yūpayaṣṭiravasthitaḥ</note> Manuscript **Ca.** reads: **"The cause, the post, the sacrificial pillar, stands in place."** <note>original: nimittā sthūṇo yūpayaṣṭiravasthitaṃ</note> Manuscript **A.** reads: **"A pillar for the cause, it stands."** <note>original: nimittāyayaṣṭiḥ avasthitaḥ</note> The word for **"post"** <note>original: sthūṇo</note> might be a dual <note>a grammatical form referring to exactly two items</note>.

**Page 499. line 15. (Hymn 62, Verse 7.)** Instead of **"Of that which has been attained,"** <note>original: adhigatasya</note> Sāyaṇa explains it as two words: **"over"** and **"attained."** <note>original: adhi gatasya</note> Manuscript **B.** only has **"attained, gone."** <note>original: gatasya gataṃ</note>

**Page 499. line 25. (Hymn 62, Verse 8.)** **"Consisting of offspring and others"** <note>original: prajādikā</note> in **B.** **"To the one consisting of offspring"** <note>original: prājādikāṃ</note> in **Ca.** **"To the one consisting of the wise"** <note>original: prājñādikāṃ</note> in **A.**

**Page 501. line 6. (Hymn 63, Verse 1.)** **"The protector of the water of truth/order"** <note>original: ṛtasyodakasya gopī</note> in **A.** **"The protector of the water of the sacrificial truth"** <note>original: ṛtasya yajñasyodakasya gopī</note> in **Ca.** **"The protector of the truth, the two guardians of the sacrifice"** <note>original: ṛtasya gopī yajñasya rakṣitārau</note> in **B.**

**Page 502. line 12. (Hymn 63, Verse 4.)** The text from **"it is said"** <note>original: ucyate</note> to **"the falling drops"** <note>original: maṃto drupsā</note> is left out in Manuscripts **A.** and **Aa.** The **Mill MS.** <note>A manuscript from the collection of W.H. Mill, now in the Bodleian Library</note> has no such omission, which shows that in this part it was not copied directly from the manuscript used by **Colebrooke** (Manuscript A). That it is, however, a copy from an **A.** type manuscript is indicated by the fact that it has, like **A.**, the phrase **"because of being a killer of enemies,"** <note>original: śatrumārukatvāt</note> while **B.** and **Ca.** read **"because of being the killer of the enemies."** <note>original: śatrūṇāṃ mārakatvāt</note>

**Page 502. line 14. (Hymn 63, Verse 4.)** **"They come, touching you"** <note>original: tvatspṛśau āgacchanti</note> in **B.**

**Page 502. line 20. (Hymn 63, Verse 5.)** **"For the sake of water"** <note>original: udakārthaṃ</note> in **A.** **"For the sake of auspicious work"** <note>original: śubhakāryārthaṃ</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 502. line 20. (Hymn 63, Verse 5.)** **"Having a gate of beautiful eyes"** <note>original: śobhanākṣadvāraṃ</note> in **A.** **"Having beautiful eyes"** <note>original: śobhanākṣaṃ</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 502. line 23. (Hymn 63, Verse 5.)** **"The bodies, the increasers, then those Maruts..."** <note>original: tanvayaḥ vardhayitāraḥ tataste maruto</note> in **B.** **"The bodies, then those Maruts..."** <note>original: tanvayastataste maruto</note> in **Ca.**

**Page 503. line 16. (Hymn 63, Verse 7.)** **A.** has: **"O Mitra and Varuna, you both, by the law that sustains the world, with the wise one—meaning with the one who is praised. By the vow, by the action. Or, with the wise one—this is a name for the singer/sacrificer. The sacrificer is also a cause of protecting the world through rain, for rain is produced by the offering made by him. By the vow, by your action, of the demon..."** <note>original: he mitrāvaruṇā yuvāṃ dharmaṇā jagadvārakeṇa vipaścitā stutenetyarthaḥ | vratā vratena karmaṇā | athavā vipaścitā | stotṛnāmetat | yajamānena vṛṣṭyā jagadrakṣaṇasya yajamāno’pi kāraṇaṃ | tatkṛtayāhutyā vṛṣṭyutpatteḥ | vratā vratena yuvayoḥ karmaṇā asurasya.</note> **B.** and **Ca.** agree in: **"O Mitra and Varuna (the dual form is added in B.), you two wise ones, protect the sacrificial rites through the law that sustains the world, characterized by rain and so forth, by the vow (by the action in Ca.). Of the demon etc."** <note>original: he mitrāvaruṇā (mitrāvaruṇau added in B.) vipaścitā prājñau yuvāṃ dharmaṇā jagadvārakeṇa vṛṣṭyādilakṣaṇena karmaṇā vratā (vratena Ca.) yajñādikarmāṇi rakṣāye pālayethaḥ | asurasya etc.</note>

**Page 503. line 17. (Hymn 63, Verse 7.)** **"Protect the sacrificial rites; you two protect"** <note>original: yajñādikarmāṇi rakṣāye | pālayethaḥ |</note> is added from **B.** and **Ca.** After **"the production of rain,"** **A.** repeats **"by the vow, by your action."**

**Page 503. line 19. (Hymn 63, Verse 7.)** **"This is the meaning: for protection"** <note>original: rakṣāye ityarthaḥ</note> in **A.** **"This is the meaning: illumine"** <note>original: vidīpaya ityarthaḥ</note> in **Ca.** **"You two illumine"** <note>original: dīpayathaḥ</note> in **B.**

**Page 504. line 8. (Hymn 64, Verse 1.)** **"Then it is said by the young woman"** <note>original: athāyuvatyocyate</note> in **A.** **"Then it is said by the one who does not move"** <note>original: adhāvayatyocyate</note> in **Ca.**; not present in **B.** We might expect **"Then it is said by joining together."** <note>original: atha saṃyujyocyate</note>

**Page 505. line 14. (Hymn 64, Verse 4.)** **B.** and **Ca.** have **"for the one who is competing"** <note>original: spardhamānāya</note> instead of **"for the competition"** <note>original: spardhanāya</note> in **A.**

**Page 506. line 2. (Hymn 64, Verse 6.)** Both <term>Pada Manuscripts<gloss>The version of the Veda where each word is written separately</gloss></term> read **"Varuna"** <note>original: varuṇā</note> (with a long 'a'); the <term>Sanhitas<gloss>The version where words are joined in continuous recitation</gloss></term> read **"Varuna"** <note>original: varuṇa</note> (short 'a'); Sāyaṇa reads **"Varuna"** <note>original: varuṇā</note>. The same occurs in Hymn 66, Verse 6, where **"mivā"** is in the Sanhita and **"Mitra"** <note>original: mitrā</note> is in the Pada.

**Page 506. line 16. (Hymn 64, Verse 7.)** **"In the sacrifice"** <note>original: yajñe</note> in **B.** and **Ca.** **"In the house"** <note>original: gṛhe</note> in **A.** The explanation of the word **"kshata"** as **"sacrifice"** is very common.

**Page 506. line 19. (Hymn 64, Verse 7.)** **"Bearing Archānan; you two, holding the hunger of Archānan"** <note>original: arcanānasaṃ bibhratau arcanānasaṃ kṣudhiṃ dhārayantau yuvāṃ</note> in **B.** at the end.

**Page 507. line 3. (Hymn 65, Verse 1.)** **"The singer who perceives, knows the praise"** <note>original: ya stotā ciketa jānāti stutiṃ</note> in **A.** **"Who extends the praise"** <note>original: yastatoti stutiṃ</note> in **Ca.** and **B.**

**Page 507. line 4. (Hymn 65, Verse 1.)** **"The deity among the gods, in the midst of the singers || or rather, in the midst of the gods"** <note>original: devatā deveṣu stotṛmadhye || yadvā deveṣu madhye</note> in **A.** **"The deity in the midst of the gods"** <note>original: devatā deveṣu madhye</note> in **Ca.** and **B.**

**Page 507. line 5. (Hymn 65, Verse 1.)** **"Whose || sacrifice"** <note>original: yasya || yajña</note> in **A., B.,** and **Ca.**

**Page 507. line 7. (Hymn 65, Verse 1.)** **"He enjoys"** <note>original: saṃbhajate</note> in **A.** **"He obtains"** <note>original: sa labhate</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 508. line 6. (Hymn 65, Verse 4.)** **"Even from the distressed"** <note>original: aṃhasvato’pi</note> in **A.** and **Ca.** **"Even from the sin of the sinner"** <note>original: aṃhasaḥ pāpino’pi</note> in **B.**

**Page 508. line 7. (Hymn 65, Verse 4.)** The word **"for"** <note>original: hi</note> is explained twice in **A., B.,** and **Ca.**, but **"for what is measured"** <note>original: mitasya hi</note> is left out in **Ca.**

**Page 509. line 15. (Hymn 66, Verse 1.)** **"With the offering of the oblation, 'thou', thus it is his"** <note>original: rātahavye tvamiti tasyaivaṃ</note> in **A.** **"Only of the one who offers the oblation"** <note>original: rātahavyasyaiva</note> in **Ca.**

## Critical Notes

**Page 509. line 16. (Hymn 66, Verse 1.)** **"Bring near, cause to come"** <note>original: ā ākāraya</note> in Manuscript **A.** **"Invoke, cause to come"** <note>original: āhvayākāraya</note> in **Ca.** **"Invoke"** <note>original: āhvaya</note> in **B.**

**Page 509. line 18. (Hymn 66, Verse 1.)** The word **"for Varuna"** <note>original: varuṇāya</note> is taken from **B.**

**Page 509. line 26. (Hymn 66, Verse 2.)** **"Possessing the destruction of demons; the meaning is, in order to kill [them]."** <note>original: asuravighātimaṃtaṃ haṃtumityarthaḥ</note> in **A.** **"O you who destroy the demons"** <note>original: asuravighātimahan he</note> in **Ca.**

**Page 510. line 11. (Hymn 66, Verse 3.)** **"With relatives"** <note>original: saṃvaṃdhibhiḥ</note> in **B.** **"Relatives"** <note>original: saṃbaṃdhinaḥ</note> in **A.** and **Ca.**

**Page 511. line 3. (Hymn 66, Verse 5.)** The phrase **"It also comes from the root *kṣi* [to dwell or possess]"** <note>original: kṣayaterapi bhavati</note> is from **Ca.**

**Page 511. line 26. (Hymn 67, Verse 1.)** **"Or rather, you two [Mitra and Varuna] hope for the sacrifice from me, the Seer, who am wounded. 'Wounded' means 'exhausted'. Make [it] known. Make [it] pervade; that is the meaning."** <note>original: yadvā yajataṃ māmṛpiṃ kṣatamāśāthe । kṣataṃgālityarthaḥ । jñāyayataṃ । vyāpayataṃmityarthaḥ</note> in **Ca.** after the phrase **"should be made plural."** <note>original: bahuvacanīkartavyaṃ</note>

**Page 512. line 22. (Hymn 67, Verse 4.)** **"The makers of water"** <note>original: udakasya kartāraḥ</note> in **B.** and **Ca.** **"The makers of the state of touching the water"** <note>original: udakaspṛśatvasya kartāraḥ</note> in **A.**

**Page 513. line 4. (Hymn 67, Verse 4.)** The Manuscripts of the **Pada** <note>the word-for-word analysis of the Vedic text</note> have the word **"measured"** <note>original: mita</note> (masculine), not the feminine form **"measured"** <note>original: mitā</note>.

**Page 513. line 6. (Hymn 67, Verse 5.)** **"Being praised by all"** <note>original: sarvaiḥ stūyamānaḥ</note> in **A.** **"Praised by all"** <note>original: sarvaiḥ stutaḥ</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 514. line 7. (Hymn 68, Verse 2.)** **"Sing with praise"** <note>original: stutyā gāyata</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 514. line 18. (Hymn 68, Verse 4.)** **"The two oblations"** <note>original: havirvau</note> in **B.** and **Ca.** **"The two sacrificial grass-seats"** <note>original: barhiṣī</note> in **A.**

**Page 514. line 24. (Hymn 68, Verse 5.)** **"Showering"** <note>original: vṛṣyathī</note> in **A.** **"Increase"** <note>original: vardhā</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 515. line 2. (Hymn 68, Verse 5.)** Variants for the word **"possessing gifts"** <note>original: dānumatyāḥ</note>: **"From the one possessing gifts, the one giving, the one for whom giving is proper."** <note>original: dānumatyā dānavatyā dātṛbhūcitāyā</note> **A.** also repeats: **"From the one possessing gifts; the one giving; the one for whom giving is proper."** Manuscript **B.** reads: **"From the one possessing gifts; the one for whom giving is proper."** Manuscript **Ca.** reads: **"From the one possessing gifts; the one possessing giving; for the thought among the givers."** <note>original: dānumatyāḥ dānamatyāḥ ॥ dātṛṣu ciṃtāyā</note>

**Page 515. line 18. (Hymn 69, Verse 1.)** **"Uninterrupted"** <note>original: avirataṃ</note> in **A.** **"Not of long duration, not continuous"** <note>original: aciṃratanaṃ asaṃtataṃ</note> in **Ca.**

**Page 515. line 24. (Hymn 69, Verse 2.)** **"Possessing food; food characterized as milk, those having that"** <note>original: irāvatīḥ irāḥ kṣīralakṣaṇāṃ tadvatyo</note> in **A.** and **Ca.** **"Possessing food; those having milk"** <note>original: irāvatī kṣīravatyaḥ</note> in **B.**

**Page 515. line 25. (Hymn 69, Verse 2.)** The section from **"similarly the rivers"** <note>original: tathā siṃdhavaḥ</note> to **"similarly they"** <note>original: tathā tayaḥ</note> is left out in **Ca.** Manuscript **B.** reads: **"Similarly for you two, the rivers, the streams, milk the honeyed essence."** <note>original: tathā vāṃ siṃdhavaḥ nadyaḥ madhumat rasaṃ duduhre duhaṃti</note>

**Page 516. line 2. (Hymn 69, Verse 2.)** **"Of the worlds of earth, atmosphere, and heaven"** <note>original: pṛthivyaṃtarikṣadyulokānāṃ</note> from **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 516. line 20. (Hymn 69, Verse 4.)** **"Of the earthly realm, which two..."** <note>original: pārthivasya rajaso yā yau</note> in **A.** and **Ca.** **"Of the earthly, of the world of earth"** <note>original: pārthivasya bhūlokasya</note> in **B.**

**Page 517. line 8. (Hymn 70, Verse 1.)** **"Even from before, many, wide, very much"** <note>original: purorapi bahu urū bahutaṃra</note> in **A.** and **Ca.**; missing in **B.** We should expect: **"Even among the many, even from much, wide, very much."** <note>original: purūṣvo'pi bahuto'pyuru bahutaṃraṃ</note>

**Page 517. line 17. (Hymn 70, Verse 2.)** **"By those crying"** <note>original: rudadbhiḥ</note> and **"By those shining"** <note>original: rudbhiḥ</note> in **A.** **"By those shining"** <note>original: rukṣadbhiḥ</note> (variant spelling) in **Ca.**

**Page 517. line 23. (Hymn 70, Verse 3.)** **"With a beautiful vehicle"** <note>original: śobhanena vākhanena</note> in **A.** **"With the beautiful"** <note>original: śobhanena</note> in **Ca.** **"The beautiful protector"** <note>original: śobhanapālako</note> in **B.**

**Page 518. line 6. (Hymn 70, Verse 4.)** **"Prosperous we, by the wealth of another [we] do not perform nourishment of the body; that is the meaning. Similarly the remainder consisting of the seasons..."** <note>original: samṛddhā vayaṃ anyayā [vayaṃ kasya] cit dhanena śarīrapoṣaṃ na kurma ityarthaḥ । tathā śeṣa ṛtūcātmakaṃ</note> etc. Manuscript **B.** has: **"Prosperous we, similarly with the remainder, let us not perform nourishment of the body with the wealth of another; similarly with the offspring, with wealth consisting of another self, let us not perform nourishment of the body. Prosperous we, by the wealth of another we do not perform nourishment of the body; that is the meaning. Similarly with the offspring, may we not enjoy [it] alone."** <note>A significant divergence in word order and phrasing between A and B regarding the maintenance of the body and family lineage.</note>

**Page 518. line 17. (Hymn 71, Verse 1.)** **"To be practiced"** <note>original: caraṇīyaṃ</note> in **A.** **"Delightful"** <note>original: ramaṇīyaṃ</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 518. line 19. (Hymn 71, Verse 1.)** **"The destroyers, the killers of enemies"** <note>original: nibarhaṇau haṃtārau śatrūṇāṃ</note> from **Ca.** **"The destroyers, the killers of enemies"** <note>original: barhaṇau haṃtārau śatrūṇāṃ</note> in **B.**

**Page 518. line 25. (Hymn 71, Verse 2.)** **"With fruits"** <note>original: phalaiḥ</note> from **B.** and **Ca.**

**Page 519. line 16. (Hymn 72, Verse 1.)** **"Of the two who have gone"** <note>original: gatayoḥ</note> after **"of Mitra and Varuna"** <note>original: mitrāvaruṇayoḥ</note> in the margin of **Ca.**

**Page 521. line 16. (Hymn 73, Verse 3.)** **"Possessing splendor"** <note>original: tejovat</note> in **A.** **"Splendid"** <note>original: tejasvat</note> in **B.** and **Ca.**; compare the grammatical rule in Pāṇini I. 4, 18, 2.

**Page 521. line 16. (Hymn 73, Verse 3.)** The word **"wheel"** <note>original: cakraṃ</note> after **"possessing splendor"** is repeated in **A.**, **B.**, and **Ca.**

**Page 521. line 18. (Hymn 73, Verse 3.)** **"From the morning and other pressings"** <note>original: prātarādisavanāt</note> in **A.** and the second hand of **Ca.** **"The pressings"** <note>original: savanāni</note> in **B.** and the first hand of **Ca.**

**Page 522. line 2. (Hymn 73, Verse 4.)** Fragmentary reading in **A.**

**Page 522. line 4. (Hymn 73, Verse 4.)** **"You two cause to go"** <note>original: gamayathaḥ</note>. Variants: **"gamayadhuḥ"** in **A.** and **Ca.**; **"rayamadhuḥ"** in **B.** <note>These are likely scribal errors in the manuscript tradition.</note>

<summary>This page lists technical textual variants for the commentary on Rig Veda Mandala V, Suktas 66-73, showing differences in word choice and grammar between three primary manuscripts. It highlights the challenges of reconstructing the original text of Sāyaṇa's commentary due to scribal errors and divergent phrasing.</summary>

The notes document differences in wording and spelling between the primary manuscript (A), the Royal Asiatic Society manuscript (Ca), and others (B, C, and the Mill edition). These variations often involve Sayana's commentary on the Vedic verses.</meta>

-># VARIANT READINGS<-

## Critical Notes

**Page 522. line 22. (Hymn 73, Verse 6.)** **"The father with the seers"** <note>original: avismintpitā ṛṣibhiḥ</note> in Manuscripts **B** and **Ca** before the word **"being"** <note>original: sati</note>.

**Page 522. line 22. (Hymn 73, Verse 6.)** **"In the act of rising"** <note>original: udyatye</note> in **Aa.**; **"In the risen"** <note>original: udyate</note> in **A**; **"Risen"** <note>original: udyata</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 522. line 24. (Hymn 73, Verse 6.)** **"The burning fire"** <note>original: dahaṃtamagniṃ</note> in **B** and **Ca**; **"The burning demon"** <note>original: dahaṃta asu</note> in **A**.

**Page 524. line 10. (Hymn 73, Verse 10.)** **"Like chariots, the craftsman; in that same way, may those be"** <note>original: rathānīva śilpī tadvattathame tāni saṃtu</note> in **A**. **"Like chariots, the craftsman; in that same way, the truths"** <note>original: rathānīva śilpī tadvat tathyāma</note> in **Ca** by corrections. **"Like chariots, the craftsman; may those be most peaceful, most pleasant, and satisfied"** <note>original: rathān iva śilpī tāni śaṃtamā sukhatamāni saṃtuṣṭa</note> in **B**.

**Page 524. line 22. (Hymn 74, Verse 1.)** **"Who on the earth"** <note>original: ko bhūmau</note> is left out in **A**. **"In the two wells, who on the earth"** <note>original: kūpyau kī bhūmau</note> in **C** and the **Mill edition**.

**Page 524. line 22. (Hymn 74, Verse 1.)** **"You two hear"** <note>original: śuṇuthaḥ</note> from **B**, **Ca**, **C**, and the **Mill edition**.

**Page 524. line 24. (Hymn 74, Verse 1.)** **"Or rather"** <note>original: athavā</note> is missing in **A** and **C** (Mill edition).

**Page 525. line 6. (Hymn 74, Verse 2.)** **"The two stand"** <note>original: tiṣṭhataḥ</note>; read as **"standing"** <note>original: tiṣṭhayaḥ</note> in **A**, **B**, and **Ca**.

**Page 525. line 15. (Hymn 74, Verse 3.)** **"Having risen, you two go"** <note>original: udyaṃya yāthaḥ</note> in **Ca** and the **Mill edition**. **"Having risen-risen-risen"** <note>original: udyaṃyayayaḥ</note> <note>a scribal error or repetition</note> in **A**.

**Page 526. line 3. (Hymn 74, Verse 4.)** **"You two impel"** <note>original: prerayathaḥ</note> in **B**, **C**, and **Ca**; not in **A**.

**Page 526. line 3. (Hymn 74, Verse 4.)** **"Thus indeed the ancestors"** <note>original: haimiti pūravāḥ</note> in **A** and **Ca**. **"Indeed the ancestors"** <note>original: hi pūravāḥ</note> in **B**.

**Page 526. line 4. (Hymn 74, Verse 4.)** **"For the sake of seizing"** <note>original: gṛbhītātaye</note>; read as **"for the sake of taking"** <note>original: gṛhītātaye</note> in **Ca**.

**Page 526. line 5. (Hymn 74, Verse 4.)** **"The roaring lion"** <note>original: vaglaṃ siṃhaṃ</note> in **B**, **C**, and **Ca**; omitted in **A**.

**Page 526. line 14. (Hymn 74, Verse 5.)** **"Then"** <note>original: tadā</note> in **B** and **Ca**. **"In that way"** <note>original: tathā</note> in **A**.

**Page 526. line 15. (Hymn 74, Verse 5.)** **"To the desired, lovely form"** <note>original: kāmamā kamanīyaṃ rūpamṛkhe</note> in **A**.

**Page 526. line 22. (Hymn 74, Verse 6.)** **"Of you two here, in the meeting"** <note>original: vāṃ iha saṃdarśane</note> in **B**.

**Page 527. line 7. (Hymn 74, Verse 7.)** From **"from all sides, who is the sacrificer"** <note>original: sarvato to ko yajamāno</note> from **A**; **"Who? In the mound, in the mound, who is the sacrificer? With sacrifices, you two, who are the carriers of the wise/priests to the mound; of the wise sacrificer, you two are the bringers of what is desired; who is the wise one in the mound?"** <note>original: kaḥ avapre vapre kaḥ yajamānaḥ yajñaiḥ yuvāṃ vapre vipravāhasā viprasya yajñamānasya abhimataprāpayitārau yuvāṃ kaḥ vipraḥ vapre</note> in **B**.

**Page 527. line 7. (Hymn 74, Verse 7.)** **"To be carried"** <note>original: vahanīyau</note> by conjecture. **"The two carriers"** <note>original: vahanī</note> in **A**.

**Page 527. line 8. (Hymn 74, Verse 7.)** **"In the mound. That sacrificer who, with sacrifices, in the mound, dwelling..."** <note>original: vapre । yo yajamāno yajñairvapre kṣayaṃtaṃ</note> etc.

**Page 528. line 1. (Hymn 74, Verse 9.)** **"Full of sweetness, or desiring Soma"** <note>original: madhumaṃto somakāmo vā</note> in **Ca**.

**Page 528. line 4. (Hymn 74, Verse 9.)** **"With the Abrigus"** <note>original: abhrigubhiḥ</note> <note>a specific group of ritual assistants</note>; compare Rig-Veda I. 104, 1. **"Fly with the Abrigus"** <note>original: abhrigbhirdīyataṃ</note> in **A**; missing in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 528. line 10. (Hymn 74, Verse 10.)** **"Your"** <note>original: tava</note> in **A**. **"Even your, from anywhere"** <note>original: kutaścit-tavāpi</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 529. line 10. (Hymn 75, Verse 2.)** **"As"** <note>original: yathā</note> before **"vessel/portion"** <note>original: grahaṃ</note> from **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 529. line 23. (Hymn 75, Verse 3.)** **"Rich in swiftness/energy"** <note>original: vājinadhanī</note> in **A** and **Ca**. **"Rich in food"** <note>original: annadhanī</note> in **B**.

**Page 530. line 6. (Hymn 75, Verse 4.)** **"O you two who possess the wealth of showers, that of wealth"** <note>original: he vṛṣaṇavasū to vasūnāṃ</note> from **Ca**. **"O you two who possess the wealth of showers, who increase wealth"** <note>original: he vṛṣaṇavasū vardhadhanau</note> in **B**; left out in **A**.

**Page 530. line 8. (Hymn 75, Verse 4.)** **"The beast is the seeker, the goer is the traveler"** <note>original: mṛgo mṛgayitā yayirgantā</note> in **B** and **Ca**. **"The beast is the seeker"** is left out in **A**.

**Page 530. line 18. (Hymn 75, Verse 5.)** **"Free from illusion/deceit"** <note>original: māyārahitaṃ</note> from **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 530. line 18. (Hymn 75, Verse 5.)** **"On the path"** <note>original: pathi</note> in **Ca**. **"On the path"** <note>variant spelling: paṃthi</note> in **B**. **"In me"** <note>original: mayi</note> in **A**.

**Page 531. line 19. (Hymn 75, Verse 8.)** **"In this sacrifice"** <note>original: asminnyajñe</note> from **B**.

**Page 531. line 20. (Hymn 75, Verse 8.)** **"Approached the nectar/immortality"** <note>original: upaprāmṛtaṃ</note> in **A**. **"Attained"** <note>original: prābhūtaṃ</note> in **B** and **Ca**. **Ca** has at the end: **"The verbal root is 'bhū' in the sense of 'attainment.' Or rather, becoming near to those of tomorrow."** <note>original: bhū prāptau iti dhātuḥ । yadvā śvastayoḥ samīpe bhavaṃtaṃ ।</note>

**Page 532. line 1. (Hymn 75, Verse 9.)** **"The Ahavaniya fire; should be occurring; be present in the time of occurrence"** <note>original: agnirāhavanīyaḥ vṛttivyaḥ vṛttau kāle bhava</note> in **B** and **Ca** after the word **"studied."** <note>original: adhīyata</note>

**Page 532. line 1. (Hymn 75, Verse 9.)** **"Meaning: the oblation is illuminated."** <note>original: prakāśitahavirityarthaḥ</note> in **A** and **Ca**. Compare **"Good-sighted"** <note>original: sucakṣūḥ</note> in Böehtlingk’s edition, and **"Good-lighted"** <note>original: sujyotiḥ</note> in Benfey’s. **"Of white radiance"** <note>original: khitaśociḥ</note> in Rig-Veda VI. 10, 3; but **"O you of auspicious radiance"** <note>original: bhadraśoce</note> in Rig-Veda X. 45, 9.

**Page 532. line 23. (Hymn 76, Verse 1.)** From **"with one's own limbs"** to **"with the Vasativari waters"** <note>original: svāṃgaiḥ to vasatīvarībhiḥ</note> taken from **Ca**. **"Toward whom? The overflowing, the swollen, in the heat/offering, the dripping form..."** <note>original: kaṃ prati । pīpivāṃsaṃ ādhyāyitaṃ gharme kṣaradrupaṃ</note> in **A**. **"Toward whom? The overflowing, encompassed by one's own limbs, in the heat, the blazing sacrifice"** <note>original: kaṃ prati । pīpivāṃsaṃ svāṃgaiḥ parivṛḍhaṃ gharme pradīptayajñaṃ</note> in **B**.
