-># VARIANT READINGS<-

## Critical Notes

**Page 533. line 6. (Mandala V. Hymn 76, Verse 2.)** **"Violence"** <note>original: hiṃsāṃ</note> || **"Injurious"** <note>original: hiṃsraṃ</note> in Manuscripts **A**, **Ca**, and **B**.

**Page 533. line 7. (V. 76, 2.)** **"You two, the most frequent visitors"** <note>original: gaṃtṛtamau yuvāṃ</note> in **A**. **"The Ashvins, the most frequent visitors"** <note>original: gaṃtṛtamau aśvinau</note> in **Ca** and **B**.

**Page 533. line 8. (V. 76, 2.)** **"And with a horse"** <note>original: aśvena ca</note> after **"with protection"** <note>original: rakṣaṇena</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 533. line 8. (V. 76, 2.)** **"The two most frequent visitors, towards the horses"** <note>original: āgaṃtṛtamau arvān prati</note> in **A**. **"The two most frequent visitors, may they destroy [the poverty]—this is the implied remainder—or, towards the horse"** <note>original: āgaṃtṛtamau nāśayatāmiti śeṣaḥ athavā arvati prati</note> in **Ca**. **"The two most frequent visitors, may they destroy [the poverty]—this is the implied remainder. Having destroyed the poverty and lack of livelihood that arises by being a rival, for the donor..."** <note>original: āgaṃtṛtamau nāśayatāmiti śeṣaḥ | prati dvaṃdvibhū jāgatya vartiṃ ajīvanaṃ dāridryaṃ nāśayitvā dāśuṣe</note> in **B**.

**Page 533. line 11. (V. 76, 2.)** **"Let them be"** <note>original: bhavatāṃ</note>; missing in **A** and **B**.

**Page 533. line 17. (V. 76, 3.)** **"Fading"** <note>original: tamānā</note> in **A**; **"Moistened"** <note>original: timānā</note> in **Ca** after the word **"fifteen-fold"** <note>original: paṃcadaśadhā</note>.

**Page 533. line 23. (V. 76, 3.)** **"What then?"** <note>original: kiṃ tarhi</note> in **B** and **Ca**. In **A**, the reading is a corrupted string of syllables.

**Page 533. line 25. (V. 76, 3.)** **"The drinking of the Soma or the hot milk offering of the other gods"** <note>original: itaradevāṃnāṃ somasya dharmasya vā pānaṃ</note> in **Ca**. **"The drinking of the Soma of the other gods"** <note>original: itaradevāṃnāṃ somasya pānaṃ</note> in **B**. **"The drinking of the other gods"** <note>original: itaradevāṃnāṃ pānaṃ</note> in **A**.

**Page 533. line 25. (V. 76, 3.)** **"Did not extend, does not extend"** <note>original: nātatāna na tanoti</note> in **A**. **"Has extended, extends"** <note>original: tatāna tanoti</note> in **Ca**. **"Has extended, extends, without leaving the Ashvins—this is the implied remainder. Therefore, come here."** <note>original: ātatāna tanoti aśvinara aśvinau na vihāyeti śeṣaḥ | tasmādāgacchataṃ</note> in **B**.

**Page 534. line 9. (V. 76, 4.)** **"Night"** <note>original: kṣapā</note> || **"Nights"** <note>original: kṣapaḥ</note> in **A**, **B**, and **Ca**.

**Page 535. line 19. (V. 77, 2.)** **"Our [sacrifice] going to the gods"** <note>original: devagāmi no</note> in **A**. **"For us, going to the gods"** <note>original: devagāmi naḥ</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 535. line 23. (V. 77, 2.)** **"One to be shared with or honored among the gods"** <note>original: devānāṃ saṃbhajanīya saṃbhāvyo</note> in **A**. **"The enjoyer of the gods"** <note>original: devānābhokteti</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 536. line 19. (V. 77, 4.)** **"Action to be distinguished"** <note>original: karma viceya</note> in **A**. **"A distinction of action"** <note>original: karmaviśeṣaṃ</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 536. line 20. (V. 77, 4.)** **"Should protect"** <note>original: pālayet</note> || **"Protecting"** <note>original: pālayat</note> in **A**, **B**, and **Ca**.

**Page 537. line 4. (V. 78, 1.)** The <term>Anukramaṇī</term> <note>the traditional index or catalog of the Veda</note> has besides: **"The final five verses are an esoteric teaching regarding the delivery of the fetus."** <note>original: aṃtāḥ paṃca garbhāsāvitya upaniṣat</note>

**Page 537. line 7. (V. 78, 1.)** The second <term>Viniyoga</term> <note>the liturgical or ritual application of a verse</note> is left out in **Ca**.

**Page 537. line 17. (V. 78, 1.)** **"As they two..."** <note>original: tau yathā</note> after **"like"** <note>original: iva</note> added by conjecture.

**Page 537. line 24. (V. 78, 2.)** **"The grass, the fodder"** <note>original: yavasaṃ ghāsaṃ</note> in **Ca** and **B**. **"For the grass, for the fodder"** <note>original: yavase ghāsāya</note> in **A**.

**Page 538. line 17. (V. 78, 4.)** **"To protect him with the chariot"** <note>original: rathena taṃ rakṣituṃ</note> in **B** and **Ca**; not in **A**. **Ca** adds **"with the speedy [one]"** <note>original: javatā</note> before **"most beneficial."** <note>original: śaṃtamena</note>

**Page 538. line 20. (V. 78, 5.)** **"They uncover"** <note>original: avāvṛṇvaṃti</note> in **A**. **"They speak down [declare]"** <note>original: ava bruvaṃti</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 538. line 20. (V. 78, 5.)** **"Having thrown/placed into"** <note>original: prakṣipya</note> in **B** and **Ca**. **"To be thrown"** <note>original: prakṣepya</note> in **A**.

**Page 538. line 22. (V. 78, 5.)** **"They will fashion"** <note>original: nirmimiṣyaṃti</note> in **A**. **"They will create"** <note>original: nirmitiṣyaṃti</note> in **Ca**. **"The ocean-fire will fashion"** <note>original: samudrāgnirmimiṣyati</note> in **B**. **"They will fashion"** <note>original: nirmiṣyaṃti</note> in the Manuscript of the *Nītimanjarī*.

**Page 538. line 23. (V. 78, 5.)** **"Thin/Emaciated"** <note>original: kṛśaḥ</note> in **B** and **Ca**. **"Child/Infant"** <note>original: śiśuḥ</note> in **A**.

**Page 538. line 26. (V. 78, 5.)** **"Having caused to rest"** <note>original: ramayitvā</note> in **A**. **"Having rested"** <note>original: ramitvā</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 539. line 7. (V. 78, 5.)** **"Of one about to give birth"** <note>original: prasovonmukhyāḥ</note> in **A**. **"Of one who will deliver"** <note>original: prasoṣyamāṇāyāḥ</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 539. line 7. (V. 78, 5.)** After **"like the womb"** <note>original: yoniriva</note>, **Ca** adds a grammatical note: **"The root *sū* denotes the birth of living beings; this is the form in the future tense with the present participle suffix. Because the rules for established names are not permanent, there is an absence of vowel-strengthening [Guna]."** <note>original: sūṅ prāṇiprasave luṭi śatari rūpaṃ saṃjñāpūrvasya vidher anityatvāt guṇābhāvaḥ</note>

**Page 539. line 16. (V. 78, 6.)** The commentary is given according to **A** and **B**, with the exception that the phrase **"for the sake of my recitation"** <note>original: mama nigadārthaṃ</note> appears only in **B**. After the words **"to be addressed,"** <note>original: saṃ cācyaḥ</note> **Ca** has: **"When I have entered and then departed, to remove the doubt that I have not entered, explain it; cause it to depart, for the sake of my recitation..."** <note>original: praviṣṭe mayi nirgate cāpraviṣṭāśaṃkāpanodanāthaṃ vyacayasva vigamayataṃ mama nigadārthaṃ</note> etc. The same addition is found in the margin of **A** by a later hand. The **Mill** Manuscript does not contain it.

**Page 540. line 8. (V. 78, 8.)** **"Just as the ocean itself trembles with waves, so even so do you, O ten-month-old [fetus]..."** <note>original: yathā svayaṃ samudraḥ taraṃṅgaiḥ kaṃpati evaṃ evaṃ tvaṃ he daśamāsya</note> etc. in **B**.

**Page 540. line 10. (V. 78, 8.)** **"Born with a placenta"** <note>original: jarāyujaḥ</note> || **"With a placenta"** <note>original: jarāyutaḥ</note> in **A**. **"Endowed with a placenta"** <note>original: jarāyuktaḥ</note> in **Ca**.

**Page 541. line 5. (V. 79, 1.)** **"Awaken [us]! Make [us] know!"** <note>original: aśbodhayaḥ prajñāpayaḥ</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 542. line 21. (V. 79, 5.)** **"Fruit/Result"** <note>original: phalaṃ</note> || **"Strength"** <note>original: balaṃ</note> in **A**.

## Hymn Text

-> **Khila (a supplementary mantra found at the end of the 29th Varga <note>a small sub-section of the Vedic text</note>):** <-

> May the lightnings of the cloud of heaven rain for you, O radiant goddess! 
> May all seeds sprout; likewise, strike down the haters of the sacred word!
> <note>original: varṣantu te vibhavari divo abhrasya vidyutaḥ | rohantu sarvabījānyavaṃ brahmadvisho jahi ||</note>

## Critical Notes

**Page 543. line 3. (V. 79, 6.)** **"Among the praisers"** <note>original: stotṛṣu</note> left out in Manuscript **Ca**. **"Among the wise patrons who have offspring"** <note>original: sūriṣu prajāvatsu</note> in **B**.

**Page 544. line 3. (V. 79, 9.)** **"Shone forth"** <note>original: vibhātaṃ</note> in **A**. **"Illumination"** <note>original: vivāsaṃ</note> in **Ca**. **"The illumination of darkness"** <note>original: tamovivāsaṃ</note> in **B**.

**Page 544. line 11. (V. 79, 10.)** **"What is this much, O you who go, just this much"** <note>original: kimetāyat he yaditu etāvadeva</note> in **A**.

**Page 545. line 1. (V. 80, 1.)** **"Abounding in clarified butter, abounding in truth"** <note>original: ghṛtāyatī satyavatī</note> in **B**.

**Page 546. line 3. (V. 80, 4.)** **"She becomes white; specifically, she becomes white"** <note>original: śyenī bhavati | viśeṣeṇa śvetā bhavati</note> in **A**. **"She becomes white"** <note>original: śyenī bhavati</note> in **Ca**, with **"she becomes white"** <note>original: śvetā bhavati</note> in the <margin>margin</margin>. **"She becomes white, she becomes the one who illuminates"** <note>original: śyenī prakāśayatī bhavati</note> in **B**.

**Page 546. line 3. (V. 80, 4.)** After **"of the first and middle"** <note>original: prathamamadhyamayoḥ</note> we should expect **"places"** <note>original: sthānayoḥ</note>, as seen in Rig Veda I. 71, 6 and 114, 10.

**Page 546. line 5. (V. 80, 4.)** **"The path, the edge of Mount Meru, in order"** <note>original: paṃthānaṃ meroḥ prāṃtadeśaṃ anukrameṇa</note> in **B**. **Ca** omits all text from **"in the direction"** <note>original: diśi</note> to **"destroys"** <note>original: mināti</note>.

**Page 546. line 7. (V. 80, 4.)** **"And understanding"** <note>original: avagacchaṃtī ca</note> in **Ca** and **A**.

**Page 546. line 25. (V. 80, 6.)** **"Impels, reveals"** <note>original: prerayati vivṛṇoti</note> in **Ca**.

**Page 548. line 18. (V. 81, 3.)** **"Bright, being beautiful"** <note>original: śubhraḥ śobhamānaḥ san</note> in **A**, **B**, and **Ca**.

**Page 550. line 10. (V. 82, 2.)** **"Demons and others || Gods and others"** <note>original: asurādayo || surādayo</note> in **A**, **B**, and **Ca**.

**Page 550. line 23. (V. 82, 4.)** **"Offspring, cattle, houses, etc."** <note>original: prajāpaśugṛhādikaṃ</note> stood probably in the margin of the original Codex. **A** inserts it after **"impel"** <note>original: preraya</note>, while **B** and **Ca** have it in the right place in the following verse.

**Page 551. line 20. (V. 82, 7.)** **"Indeed him || Indeed he"** <note>original: taṃ hi || sa hi</note> in **A** and **Ca**.

**Page 551. line 20. (V. 82, 7.)** **"Because of being the soul of all"** <note>original: sarvātmatvāt</note> in **A**. **"Because of having the nature of the soul of all"** <note>original: sarvātmakatvāt</note> in **Ca**.

**Page 553. line 1. (V. 83, 1.)** **"The causer of decay"** <note>original: jarayitā</note> in **A** and **Ca**.

**Page 553. line 10. (V. 83, 2.)** **A** and **Ca** begin with **"Parjanya <note>the Rain God</note> is from the root 'tṛp' <note>to satisfy</note> with the first and last letters reversed"** <note>original: parjanyastṛperādyantaviparyayasya</note>. **B** has **"The sinless Parjanya strikes the trees etc."** <note>original: anāgāḥ niṣpāpaḥ parjanyaḥ vṛkṣān haṃti etc.</note>

**Page 555. line 2. (V. 83, 6.)** **"All things"** <note>original: sarvāṃi</note> in **B**. **"All limbs"** <note>original: sarvāṅga</note> in **A** and **Ca**.

**Page 556. line 16. (V. 83, 10.)** **"Watery regions"** <note>original: jalapradeśān</note> in **A** before **"deserts"** <note>original: dhanvāni</note>.

**Page 556. line 17. (V. 83, 10.)** **"You have made them watery"** <note>original: jalavataḥ kṛtavānasi</note> in **B** and **Ca**; not in **A**.

**Page 556. line 25. (V. 84, 1.)** **"And this in the hymn to the Earth || in the hymn to you"** <note>original: bhūmistome caiṣā || stome teyā</note> in **A** and **Ca**.

**Page 557. line 18. (V. 84, 2.)** **"Raised up"** <note>original: udvṛttaṃ</note> in **A**. **"Extracted"** <note>original: uddhṛtaṃ</note> in **Ca**.

**Page 558. line 3. (V. 84, 3.)** **"If of her || That of her"** <note>original: yadyasyāḥ || yat asyāḥ</note> in **A**. **"That, because"** <note>original: yat yasmāt</note> in **B** and **Ca**.

**Page 558. line 5. (V. 84, 3.)** **"Below the sky, in the atmosphere"** <note>original: divo nīcairamtari-</note> in **A**.

**Page 558. line 7. (V. 84, 3.)** At the end of the 29th Varga <note>section</note> the Sanhitas <note>collections of verses</note> give a supplementary verse:

**Page 558. line 15. (V. 85, 1.)** **"O white one"** <note>original: he śvate</note> in **B** and **Ca**. **"O knower of the white"**? <note>original: he śvatajña (śvettajña?)</note> in **A**.

**Page 558. line 20. (V. 85, 1.)** **"In the second, in the third"** <note>original: dvitīyasyāṃ tṛtīyasyāṃ</note> in **Ca**.

**Page 559. line 3. (V. 85, 2.)** A very similar but not identical passage is to be found in the **Satapatha-Brahmana** <note>a prose text describing Vedic rituals</note> III. 3, 1, 7. (p. 253.)

**Page 559. line 16. (V. 85, 3.)** **"That is feared || That is sung"** <note>original: taddrāyate || tadgīyate</note> in **B**. **"That is sung"** <note>original: tadgīyate</note> in **A** and **Ca**. See also the ancient linguist Yaska.

**Page 559. line 21. (V. 85, 3.)** **"Spreads out"** <note>original: prasārayati</note> in **A**, **Ca**, and **B**.

**Page 560. line 6. (V. 85, 4.)** **"Covers completely"** <note>original: samācchādayati</note> in **A**, **Ca**, and **B**.

## Critical Notes

**Page 561. line 3. (V. 85, 6.)** **"Many rivers"** <note>original: bahvyo nadyaḥ</note> only in Manuscript **A**.

**Page 561. line 5. (V. 85, 6.)** **"It should not be said 'fittingly of Varuna,' because of his existence in the form of Varuna and others"** <note>original: evocitaṃ na varuṇāsyeti na vācyaṃ tasya varuṇādirūpeṇāvasthānāt</note> in **Ca**. **"It is said 'as spoken by Varuna,' it should not be said [otherwise] because of his existence in the form of Varuna and others"** <note>original: evoditaṃ na varuṇāvācyaṃ tasya varuṇādirūpeṇāvasthānāt</note> in **A**.

**Page 561. line 13. (V. 85, 7.)** **"And the teacher from the meditation of the wanderer"** <note>original: īrikhānmananācca śāstrī</note> in **A**. **"He praises from the meditation of the self of the wanderer"** <note>original: irakhātmananā praśāstī°</note> in **Ca**.

**Page 561. line 16. (V. 85, 7.)** **"Soundless"** <note>original: aśabdāṃ</note> in the main text; **"Soundless"** <note>original: aśabdaṃ</note> in **A**. **"Powerless"** <note>original: aśakaṃ</note> in **Ca** and **B**.

**Page 561. line 24. (V. 85, 8.)** **"As in gambling, whatever the rival"** <note>original: dyūte yathā yadripuḥ</note> in **B** and **A**. **"As in gambling, the non-rival"** <note>original: dyūte yathā adripuḥ</note> in **Ca** by the first hand. **"In gambling, whatever the rival"** <note>original: dyūte yadripuḥ</note> in **Ca** by the second hand.

**Page 561. line 24. (V. 85, 8.)** **"Which in us"** <note>original: yadasmāsu</note>; **"In them"** <note>original: tasmāsu</note> in **Ca** by the first hand. **"Likewise in us"** <note>original: tathāsmāsu</note> in **Ca** by the second hand and **A**; missing in **B**.

**Page 562. line 24. (V. 86, 2.)** **"Or"** <note>original: vā</note> added by conjecture.

**Page 563. line 10. (V. 86, 3.)** **"They approach; they go toward."** <note>original: pratīpate | pratigacchataḥ</note> **"They go toward"** <note>original: pratigacchataḥ</note> in **B**. **"Approaches; he goes toward"** <note>original: pratipate pratigacchati</note> in **Ca**. **"It happens; he approaches; he goes toward"** <note>original: bhavati īpate abhigacchati</note> in **A**.

**Page 564. line 2. (V. 86, 5.)** **"Like a mortal, like two men, those two"** <note>original: martaiva manuṣyāviva tau</note> etc. in **A**. **"Like a mortal man, those two"** <note>original: martiya manuṣyāyiva tau</note> in **Ca**; **B** omits the entire passage. It seems that the commentator Sāyaṇa took the word **"martiya"** for **"martaiva"** <note>like a mortal</note>, perhaps misled by the following word **"aṃśeva"** <note>like two portions</note>.

**Page 564. line 15. (V. 86, 6.)** **"Wealth and riches"** <note>original: rayiṃ dhanaṃ ca</note> in **Ca** and **B**; missing in **A**. It ought to be **"Wealth, riches, among those who sing praises."** <note>original: rayiṃ dhanaṃ gṛṇatsu stuvatsu</note>

**Page 565. line 1. (V. 87, 1.)** **"In speech..."** <note>original: vāci ni°</note> changed to **"In the prize..."** <note>original: vājini°</note> in **A** and **Ca**. **"Speech is..."** <note>original: vāk ni</note> in **B**.

**Page 565. line 2. (V. 87, 1.)** **"For Vishnu the all-pervading, or for Indra-Vishnu"** <note>original: viṣṇuve vyāptāyendrāya viṣṇuve vā</note> in **A**. **"For Vishnu..."** <note>original: viṣṇuve pā</note> in **Ca**.

**Page 565. line 18. (V. 87, 2.)** **"He praises"** <note>original: stauti</note> from **B** and **Ca**. After **"he praises,"** **Ca** adds: **"because it is at the beginning of a sentence, there is no loss of accent."** <note>original: vākyāditvānan-nighātaḥ</note>

**Page 565. line 23. (V. 87, 2.)** **"You are powerful"** <note>original: vo yūyaṃ pravalāḥ</note> in **A**. **"The power, you are powerful"** <note>original: śavo yūyaṃ pravalāḥ</note> in **Ca**. **"And those of you who..."** <note>original: ye ca yūyaṃ</note> in **B**.

**Page 566. line 8. (V. 87, 3.)** **"They have heard those"** <note>original: tān śṛṇvire</note> repeated in **A** and **Ca** after **"he has praised."** <note>original: stutavān</note> Perhaps intended for **"He has heard him."** <note>original: taṃ śṛṇvire</note>

**Page 566. line 9. (V. 87, 3.)** The explanation of **"īrī"** <note>a rare word meaning a wanderer or wind</note> is omitted in **A**. **"Not desired... nor does it move"** <note>original: neṣṭ chā | neśate ca cāla°</note> in **A**. **Ca** has: **"For those remaining in the dwelling, the wanderer, the one sent, the one moved; it is not desired, it does not happen, and it moves..."** <note>original: nivāse tiṣṭhatāṃ īrī īritā preritā neṣṭ chā neśate bhavati ca cāla°</note>; **B** has: **"For those remaining in the dwelling, the one sent, the one moved; not desired, not a master, anyone becomes, moves..."** <note>original: nivāse tiṣṭhatāṃ īritā preritā neṣṭ anīśvaro kaścana bhavati cāla°</note>. The word **"īrī"** does not occur again in the Rig-veda.

**Page 569. line 12.** At the end of the 5th Maṇḍala <note>the fifth 'book' of the Rig Veda</note>, Manuscripts **S. 1**, **S. 2**, and the Colebrooke manuscript (where, however, the leaf containing it is bound after the 6th Adhyāya and no accents are marked) give the following **Appendix** <note>original: Pariśiṣṭa</note>:

---

## Hymn Text

-> **O Jātavedas <note>Agni, the knower of all births</note>, bring to me the goddess Lakṣmī, who is golden-hued, radiant like a doe, adorned with garlands of silver and gold, brilliant as the moon, and made of gold. || 1 ||** <-

-> **Bring that Lakṣmī to me, O Jātavedas, the one who does not go away; through whom I may obtain gold, cows, horses, and men. || 2 ||** <-

-> **I invoke the goddess of Fortune [Śrī], who is preceded by horses, centered in a chariot, and delighted by the trumpeting of elephants; may the goddess of Fortune be pleased with me. || 3 ||** <-

-> **I invoke here that goddess of Fortune who is brightly smiling, surrounded by a wall of gold, radiant, shining, satisfied and satisfying, seated on a lotus, and lotus-colored. || 4 ||** <-

---

<note>a</note> **"Radiant/Moist"** <note>original: mārdrāṃ</note> in Manuscript **S. 2**.

<summary>This page lists textual variants for the end of Mandala 5 and provides the opening verses of the Śrī Sūkta, an early Sanskrit hymn to the goddess of wealth, found as an appendix in certain manuscripts.</summary>
<keywords>Variant Readings, Sāyaṇa, Mandala 5, Śrī Sūkta, Lakṣmī, Jātavedas, Agni, manuscript discrepancies, Sanskrit philology</keywords>

--- Page 47 ---
<meta>This page continues the "Varietas Lectionis" (Variant Readings) section for the fifth book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda. Specifically, it provides the text and scholarly apparatus for the Śrī Sūkta, a famous "Khila" or supplemental hymn dedicated to the goddess Lakṣmī. The previous page concluded the standard hymns of Mandala 5 and began this appendix.</meta>

<page-num>xli</page-num>
<header>VARIANT READINGS.</header>

## Hymn Text

5. I take refuge in the Goddess of Fortune (Śrī), who is radiant like the moon, glowing with fame, cherished by the gods in this world, and noble. She is like a lotus-rimmed wheel. May my misfortune <note>original: alakṣmī</note> perish; I choose you. ^b (1)

6. O Sun-colored one! By your penance was born the king of the forest, the Bilva tree <note>A sacred fruit tree (Aegle marmelos) associated with Shiva and Lakshmi</note>. May its fruits drive away the delusions and the internal and external misfortunes through that penance. ^c

7. May the friend of the gods <note>Kubera, the god of wealth</note> and Fame come to me along with the jewel. I have manifested ^d in this kingdom; grant me fame and prosperity.

8. I destroy Misfortune <note>Alakṣmī, the personification of bad luck and the elder sister of Lakshmi</note>, who is stained by hunger and thirst. Drive away all lack of prosperity and growth from my home. ^f

9. I summon here the goddess Śrī (Fortune), who is perceived through her fragrance, who is difficult to overcome, ever-thriving, rich in cattle <note>original: kariṣiṇīm, literally 'abounding in manure,' indicating a wealth of livestock</note>, and the sovereign of all beings. ^l

10. May we attain the heart's desire and intent, and the truth of speech. May the form of cattle and the essence of food ^e abide in me. May Glory and Fortune (Śrī) dwell with me. (2)

11. Through Kardama <note>One of the sons of Lakshmi, personifying 'mud' or 'clay' in which lotuses grow</note> progeny was born. O Kardama, dwell in me. Establish the Mother, Fortune, who wears a lotus garland, in my family. ^f

12. May the waters produce ^g friendly things. O Ciklīta <note>Another son of Lakshmi, personifying 'moisture' or 'clinging'</note>, dwell in my house. And ^h establish the divine Mother, Fortune, in my family.

13. O Jātavedas <note>A title for Agni, the Fire God, meaning 'he who knows all births'</note>, bring to me the moist one, the lotus-dweller, the embodiment of nourishment ^i, the golden one, who wears a garland of gold ^k—the sun-like, golden Goddess of Fortune (Lakṣmī).

14. O Jātavedas, bring to me the moist one, the lotus-dweller, the slender one <note>original: yaṣṭīm, literally 'staff' or 'stalk'</note> ^m, the tawny one, who wears a garland of lotuses—the moon-like, golden Goddess of Fortune.

15. O Jātavedas, bring to me that Goddess of Fortune who never departs ^n, through whom I may obtain abundant ^o gold, cattle, female servants, horses, and men.

16. Whoever, being pure and self-restrained, offers clarified butter daily and constantly recites these fifteen verses of the Śrī Sūkta, desiring Fortune, shall obtain it. (3)

17. O Lotus-faced one, lotus-thighed ^p, lotus-eyed, born from a lotus! O lotus-eyed one, favor me ^q so that I may obtain happiness. (1)

18. Giver of horses ^r, giver of cattle, giver of wealth in great abundance—may the Goddess ^s take pleasure in my wealth and grant me all desires.

---

## Critical Notes

^b **"I take refuge"** <note>original: śaraṇamahaṃ pra</note> in manuscripts S. 2 and 3.

^c **"Delusions and obstacles"** <note>original: māyāntarā°</note> in S. 2 and 3.

^d **"Manifested... / Let there be"** <note>original: °bhūto suṃ</note> in S. 2; <note>original: °bhūto'stu</note> in S. 3.

^e **"Form of food"** <note>original: rūpamannasya</note> in S. 3.

^f **"In the house"** <note>original: gṛhe</note> in S. 1.

^g **"Produce"** <note>original: °jantu</note> in S. 1; **"May the waters produce"** <note>original: āpaḥ sṛjantu</note> in S. 3.

^h **"And indeed"** <note>original: ni ca</note> in S. 1 and 3.

^i **"Nourishment"** <note>original: puṣṭiṃ</note> in S. 3.

^k **"The tawny one, wearing a garland of lotuses"** <note>original: piṅgalāṃ padmamālinīṃ</note> in S. 1.

^l **"He who... abounding in manure"** <note>original: yaḥ kariṣī</note> in S. 2 and 3.

^m **"The staff"** <note>original: yaṣṭiṃ</note> in S. 3.

^n **"Unfailing"** <note>original: napa</note> (fragment of *anapāgāminīm*) in S. 3.

^o **"Abundant"** <note>original: prabhūtaṃ</note> in S. 2.

^p **"Thighs"** <note>original: ūrū</note> (variant spelling) in S. 3.

<summary>This page contains the concluding verses (5-18) of the Śrī Sūkta, a supplemental hymn to the goddess Lakṣmī, along with a critical apparatus comparing readings across three Sanskrit manuscripts (S. 1, S. 2, and S. 3).</summary>

<meta>This page continues the "Variant Readings" appendix from Max Müller's edition of the Rig Veda. It specifically focuses on the concluding verses of the Śrī Sūkta (a supplementary hymn to the Goddess of Fortune) and documents additional verses found in specific manuscripts, including prayers to Shiva and Vishnu that were often appended to this hymn in the medieval tradition.</meta>

<page-num>xlii</page-num>
<header>VARIANT READINGS.</header>

## Hymn Text

Children, grandchildren, wealth, grain, elephants, horses, cattle, and a chariot—you are the<sup>t</sup> mother of all beings. May she grant me<sup>u</sup> a long life. (19) (4)

Fire <note>Agni</note> is wealth, Wind <note>Vayu</note> is wealth, the Sun <note>Surya</note> is wealth, the Vasus <note>a group of elemental deities</note> are wealth; Indra, Brihaspati, and Varuna<sup>x</sup> provide wealth.<sup>y</sup> (20)

O son of Vinata <note>Garuda, the divine eagle and mount of Vishnu</note>, drink the Soma; let the slayer of Vritra <note>Indra</note> drink the Soma; may the Soma-sacrificer give the Soma of beautiful wealth to me.<sup>z</sup> (21)

Neither anger nor envy<sup>a</sup>, nor greed, nor impure thoughts exist for those who have performed meritorious deeds; for the devotees, one should recite the <term>Śrī Sūkta|A celebrated supplementary hymn of the Rig Veda dedicated to Lakshmi, the goddess of prosperity</term>.<sup>b</sup> (22)

O you who dwell in the lotus, holding a lotus in your hand, shining with the whitest and most auspicious fragrant garlands; O Goddess, beloved of Hari <note>Vishnu</note>, captivating, bringer of prosperity to the three worlds, be gracious to me. (23)

One is magnified by the splendor of Fortune <note>original: Śrī-varcasvam</note>, long life, health, and the purifying power<sup>c</sup>; wealth, grain<sup>d</sup>, cattle, the gain of many sons, and a long life of a hundred years. (24) (5)

---

## Commentary / Scholarly Notes

Manuscript S. 3 adds after verse 23 the following verses:

> O you seated on a lotus, lover of lotuses, having petals like a lotus, lover of the lotus, with eyes as wide as lotus petals; O you who are dear to the universe, favorable to the mind of the world, place your lotus-feet near to me.
> I bow to Lakshmi, the wife of Vishnu, the Goddess who is Patience, the consort of Madhava <note>Vishnu</note>, the beloved of Madhava, the dear friend of the gods, the beloved of Achyuta <note>the "Infallible One," an epithet of Vishnu</note>.
> We know the Great Lakshmi <note>Mahālakṣmī</note>, and we meditate upon the wife of Vishnu. May that Lakshmi inspire us.
> Ananda, Kardama, and the famous Chiklita <note>The three sons of Lakshmi, representing joy, mud/clay, and moisture, in which lotuses grow</note>... may debt, disease, poverty, sin, hunger, and accidental death, as well as sickness, grief, and mental anguish, be destroyed forever.

Then follows verse 24.

On the margin of the same leaf, manuscript S. 3 adds the following verses in red ink. The first three verses are addressed to Shiva, and followed by two addressed to Vishnu. Kulluka <note>A famous 13th-century commentator on Hindu law</note>, in his Commentary on the *Laws of Manu* (III. 233), explains the **supplementary hymns** <note>original: khilāni</note> as **the Śrī Sūkta, the Śiva-saṃkalpa, and others**; and it is not unlikely, therefore, that he knew the *Śrī Sūkta* as being followed by some verses addressed to Shiva.

> Lord of the Universe, Three-eyed One <note>original: Virūpākṣa</note>, Universal Form, Ever-Auspicious <note>Sadāśiva</note>; be my refuge, Lord of Beings, O Shambhu <note>Source of Happiness</note>, the Merciful One. (1)
> O Destroyer <note>Hara</note>, Shambhu, Great God <note>Mahādeva</note>, Lord of the Universe, beloved of the immortals; O Shiva, the Source of Happiness, the Soul of All, the Blue-throated One <note>Nīlakaṇṭha</note>, salutations to you! (2)

---

## Critical Notes

<sup>t</sup> "si" in S. 3.
<sup>u</sup> "I do" <note>original: karomyaham</note> in S. 1.
<sup>x</sup> "Varuna, you bestow wealth" in S. 1.
<sup>y</sup> "Wealth of the Ashvins" <note>The twin physicians of the gods</note> in S. 3.
<sup>z</sup> "to me" in S. 3; "here" in S. 1.
<sup>a</sup> "Envy" in S. 3.
<sup>b</sup> S. 1 inserts here the verse "O Lotus-faced one," and then repeats verse 16: "He who is pure."
<sup>c</sup> "purity/health" in S. 1 and 3.
<sup>d</sup> "Grain, wealth" in S. 3.

## Hymn Text

To the Conqueror of Death, to Rudra, to the Blue-Throated one, to the Source of Happiness <note>original: "Shambhu"</note>; to the Lord of the Nectar of Immortality, to the Archer <note>original: "Sharva"</note>, to the Great God—salutations to you. (3)
These are the names of Shiva; he who recites them regularly, even once, has no fear of death, nor of any disease born of sin.

O Lord of Sacrifice, O Infallible One, O Govinda <note>Guardian of Cattle</note>, O Madhava, O Infinite One, O Keshav; O Krishna, O Vishnu, O Lord of the Senses, O Vasudeva—salutations be to you. (1)
To Krishna, the Lord of the Gopis <note>cowherd women</note>, the wielder of the Discus, the enemy of the demon Mura; to the Lord of Nectar, the Protector, to Govinda—salutations again and again. (2)
One should always recite these infinite names at the end of a <term>Mandala|One of the ten "books" or "circles" that constitute the Rig Veda</term>.

---

(**VI. 5, 4.**) **most satisfied** <note>original: "tṛptatama"</note> A. **most heated** <note>original: "tapastitama"</note> Ca. **ascetic** <note>original: "tapasvin"</note> B.: compare <term>Nirukta|An ancient Sanskrit treatise on etymology and the interpretation of the Vedas</term> VI. 12.

P. 594. l. 15. (**VI. 6, 5.**) After **it falls forward; excessively**, Ca. leaves out all to the beginning of the next hymn. B. supplies this <term>lacuna|A gap or missing part in a manuscript</term> quite arbitrarily to verse 7, where it copies from A:
> **"It falls forward" means it falls with great force. An illustration: "like a cattle-fighter" means like a thunderbolt <note>original: "ashani"</note> that strikes because of water; as that falls, so does this. Furthermore, "of the one difficult to approach" <note>original: "durvarttuḥ"</note> refers to the fire existing with unbearable flames. "Fierce" <note>original: "bhīmaḥ"</note> means terrifying. "Burning" <note>original: "kṣātiḥ"</note> means pride; it burns the forests. An illustration: "like the onset of a hero"—just as a hero's obstructive valor is a killer of living beings, so is this. (6) "With the light"—O Agni, you who are great, ward off the earthly [beings] existing on the earth, the beings moving here and there for the sake of daily life, and the expanded obstruction; this is the meaning. Furthermore, with the light of the "striker" <note>original: "todasya"</note>, with the crushing radiance, ward off the affliction of living beings from all sides. Furthermore, with powers <note>original: "sahobhiḥ"</note>, O Fire who are angry at the envious <note>original: "vanuṣaḥ"</note>, performing anger, strike down and thoroughly conquer our enemies. (7)**

P. 594. l. 18. (**VI. 6, 5.**) **unbearable as if by steeds || unbearable as if by bad conduct** <note>original: "yathātyairduḥsahaṃ || yathānayai duḥsaha"</note> A.

# VARIANT READINGS.

## Commentary (Sāyaṇa)

**Manuscript B. contains an independent explanation of this passage:** 

> A "well-turned" <note>original: suvṛttiḥ</note> is a beautiful hymn of praise. It is praised; in some seat of the earth, in every house <note>original: sadma sadmani</note>, that is, in the house of the sacrificer, the sacrifice even now rests upon the sacrificer.

## Critical Notes

**P. 711. l. 9. (VI. 31, 3.)** **fighting** <note>original: "yudhyamānaṃ"</note> **B. Ca.** after **with Kutsa** <note>original: "kutisena"</note>.

**P. 713. l. 10. ## Critical Notes

**P. 742. l. 4. (VI. 44, 8.)** **being near** <note>original: "sānnītyaṃ"</note> **B.** **and being near** <note>original: "sānnītyaṃ ca"</note> **A.** **and being near** <note>original: "sānnītyaṃ ca"</note> **Ca.** From this verse **B.** gives again the complete commentary; agreeing, as formerly, more with **A.** than **Ca.** The <term>Viniyogas</term> <note>Viniyogas are the specific ritual instructions or applications for how a verse should be used in a sacrifice.</note>, however, are omitted.

**P. 749. l. 14. (VI. 44, 24.)** **knowing the internal motive** <note>original: "hetugarbhavit°"</note> **A.** **knowing the internal motive** <note>original: "hetugarbhavit°"</note> **B.** **the motive in the interior** <note>original: "garbheheturvi°"</note> **Ca.** : compare <note>original: "cf."</note> Sáyana's commentary on VIII. 2, 5 and 7.

**P. 749. l. 24.** The <term>Sanhitás</term> <note>The Sanhitás are the primary collections of the Vedic hymns themselves, as opposed to the commentaries.</note> contain at the end of the 44th hymn (Ashtaka IV. 7, 20.) the following <term>Khila</term> <note>A 'Khila' is a supplemental or 'additional' hymn not found in the standard Rig Veda canon but preserved in certain manuscript traditions.</note>:

---

## Hymn Text

-> [Supplemental Hymn] <-

The eye and the ear and the mind and the speech, the out-breath and the in-breath, the form, and this body. Two facing inward, two in the natural order, two emissions—this I think <note>variant "a": you think/consider</note>; let them reveal that fountain. ॥ 1 ॥
The chest and the back and the hips and the arms, the shanks and the thighs, the belly and the head. The hair, the flesh, the blood, the bone, and the marrow—this body is like a bubble on the water. ॥ 2 ॥
The eyebrows, the forehead, the nose and the ears, the jaws, the cheeks, and the chin likewise. The lips and the teeth and likewise the tongue—this body of mine is a jewel-box of the mouth. ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Critical Notes

In verse B., the word **he should impel** <note>original: "prerayeḥ"</note> is corrected to **you impel** <note>original: "prerayasi"</note>, and is written as **you impel** <note>original: "prerayasi"</note> the second time. Manuscript A. has **he should impel** and **you impel**; Ca. has **you impel yourself** <note>original: "prerayase"</note> and **you impel**.

**P. 875. l. 16. (VI. 68, 9.)** **Endowed with flame and splendor** <note>original: "śociṣā tejasā yuktaḥ"</note> in A. Paris and C. Mill. **P. 876. l. 18. (VI. 69, 1.)** **Relating to the deity Gaṇagāri** <note>original: "gāṇagāridevataṃ"</note> || Variants include: **Relating to the deity Gaṇagāre** in Calcutta; **Relating to the deity Gaṇāgāri** in A. Paris and C. Mill; **Relating to the deity Gaṇagāri** in the Áśvaláyana text; and **Relating to the deity Gaṇagāri [feminine form]** in B 1.

**P. 877. l. 4. (VI. 69, 1.)** **Of the ritual action** <note>original: "karmaṇo"</note> is omitted in B and Calcutta.

**P. 877. l. 4. (VI. 69, 1.)** **I should serve** <note>original: "seveyāṃ"</note> || **I should serve [variant spelling]** <note>original: "seveyyāṃ"</note> in A. Paris and C. Mill; omitted in B and Calcutta.

**P. 878. l. 19. (VI. 69, 5.)** **While striding** <note>original: "vicakramāṇe"</note> is not found in B or Calcutta.

**P. 879. l. 7. (VI. 69, 6.)** **The receptacle of Soma** <note>original: "somanidhānaḥ"</note> || **The name of Soma** <note>original: "somābhidhānaḥ"</note> in A. Paris and C. Mill. **The names of Soma** <note>original: "somābhidhānāḥ"</note> in B 1; missing <note>original Latin: "deest"</note> in B 4 and Calcutta.

**P. 879. l. 13. (VI. 69, 7.)** **The intoxicating Soma of this sweet juice, the Soma of the Soma [libation]** <note>original: "madhvo'sya madakaraṃ somaṃ somasya somaṃ"</note> in A. Paris and C. Mill. **Of this Soma, this Soma, the sweetness of the sweet juice** <note>original: "asya somasya imaṃ somaṃ madhvaḥ madhuraṃ"</note> in the margin <note>original Latin: "in marg."</note> of Calcutta. **The sweetness of the sweet juice, the sweetness of the sweet, of this Soma, this Soma** <note>original: "madhvaḥ madhurasya madhuraṃ asya somasya imaṃ somaṃ"</note> in B 4. The entire passage is omitted in B 1.

**P. 880. l. 13. (VI. 70, 1.)** This aphorism <note>term: Sūtra; a concise rule or statement in Sanskrit literature</note> is omitted in A. Paris, C. Mill, B 1, and Calcutta. It is found in the Áśvaláyana Śrauta-Sútra, IX. 5: **"The buttery ones [heaven and earth], for the glory of the worlds, Indra, with the waters like a churning stick..."** <note>original: "ghṛtavatī bhuvanānāmabhiśriyendraṃ kṣubhabhivajivādbhiḥ"</note> etc.

**P. 881. l. 1. (VI. 70, 1.)** **By the act of supporting** <note>original: "dhāraṇena"</note> in B and Calcutta. **By the supporter** <note>original: "dhārakeṇa"</note> in A. Paris and C. Mill.

**P. 881. l. 2. (VI. 70, 1.)** **Or those two are characterized by many actions** <note>original: "bahukārye vā bhavataḥ"</note> in B 1 and Calcutta. **The sense is "characterized by many actions"** <note>original: "bahukāryeti bhāvaḥ"</note> in A. Paris and C. Mill.

**P. 882. l. 14. (VI. 70, 4.)** **The sacrifice proceeds** <note>original: "yāgaḥ pravartate"</note> in A. Paris and C. Mill. **The sacrifices proceed [plural]** <note>original: "yāgāḥ pravartate"</note> in B and Calcutta.

## Critical Notes

**P. 882. l. 21. (VI. 70, 5.)** **Two actions for the purpose of water** <note>original: "udakārthakarmāṇau"</note> in Calcutta and B 4. **Actions in the work of water** <note>original: "udakakārye karmāṇī"</note> in Asiatic Society Paris and C. Mill. **Of the action for the purpose of water** <note>original: "udakārthe karmaṇo"</note> in B 1.

**P. 883. l. 10. (VI. 70, 6.)** **The two who cause all to be, the benefactors of all** <note>original: "viśvaśaṃbhuvā sarvasya bhāvayitryau"</note> from B 4.

**P. 883. l. 18. (VI. 71, 1.)** **Thus one should rise up after** <note>original: "ityanūttiṣṭhet"</note> is missing in the Áśvaláyana manuscript <note>A text detailing Vedic rituals and domestic ceremonies</note>.

**P. 884. l. 4. (VI. 71, 1.)** **For the libation, for the production** <note>original: "savanāya suvanāya"</note> etc. || **For the libation, for the libation, for the libation, or for giving** <note>original: "savanāya savanāya savanāya dānāya vā"</note> in Asiatic Society Paris. **For the libation, for the association, or for giving** <note>original: "savanāya sacanāya dānāya vā"</note> in C. Mill. **For the libation, or for giving** <note>original: "savanāya dānāya vā"</note> in B 1 and Calcutta. **For the libation, for giving** <note>original: "savanāya dānāya"</note> in B 4. It might have been **For the libation, for the production, for the impelling, or for giving** <note>original: "savanāya suvanāya preraṇāya dānāya vā"</note>.

**P. 884. l. 21. (VI. 71, 3.)** **By those creating happiness** <note>original: "sukhakāribhiḥ"</note> in Asiatic Society Paris. **By those who cause happiness** <note>original: "sukhakaraiḥ"</note> in B and Calcutta; omitted in C. Mill.

**P. 885. l. 2. (VI. 71, 3.)** **Enemy** <note>original: "śatruḥ"</note> taken from B and Calcutta. **Our** <note>original: "no’smākaṃ"</note> is repeated before **Let not** <note>original: "mākiḥ"</note> in Asiatic Society Paris, C. Mill, Calcutta, and B 1.

**P. 886. l. 4. (VI. 71, 6.)** **And what more by much speaking?** <note>original: "kiṃca bahuktyā"</note> in Calcutta, A, and B 1. **In short** <note>original: "kiṃ bahunā"</note> in B 4.

**P. 886. l. 18. (VI. 72, 1.)** **And you two made the people reach** <note>original: "alaṃbhayataṃ ca janān"</note> || **Either you two made the souls reach, or you two made the people reach from** <note>original: "alaṃbhayataṃ vā jānān alaṃbhayataṃ vā janāt"</note> in Calcutta. **You two made reach** <note>original: "alaṃbhayataṃ"</note> in B 4. **You two made the people reach** <note>original: "alaṃbhayata vā janān"</note> in B 1.

**P. 887. l. 1. (VI. 72, 2.)** **Shining forth** <note>original: "vyucchantī"</note> || **Shining forth and having shone forth** <note>original: "vyucchantī vyucchaṃ ca"</note> in Calcutta. **Shining forth, they shone forth** <note>original: "vyūchantī vyuchanta"</note> in B.

**P. 888. l. 8. (VI. 72, 5.)** **Overpowering the enemy's armies** <note>original: "śatrusainyābhibhāvukaṃ"</note> from B 4.

**P. 888. l. 15. (VI. 73, 1.)** Some words are left out after **Thus** <note>original: "iti"</note>, which are to be supplied in this manner: **The invitatory verse for the Svistakrit [Agni] <note>The Svistakrit is a specific offering to Agni 'the maker of good sacrifice'</note>. And it is indicated: Brihaspati conquered the riches.** Compare <note>original Latin: "Cf."</note> VII. 11, 2.

**P. 889. l. 23. (VI. 73, 3.)** **Desiring to share** <note>original: "saṃbhaktukāmaḥ"</note> || **Desiring shared things** <note>original: "saṃbhaktakāmaḥ"</note> in Asiatic Society Paris and C. Mill. **Wishing to share** <note>original: "saṃbhaktumicchan"</note> in Calcutta and B 4. **Wishing to share [variant form]** <note>original: "saṃbhaktamicchan"</note> in B 1.

**P. 891. l. 5. (VI. 74, 3.)** **The loose bond** <note>original: "śithilabandhaṃ"</note> || **The bond that is loose** <note>original: "śithilaṃ bandhaṃ"</note> in Asiatic Society Paris and C. Mill. **Bound loosely** <note>original: "śithilabaddhaṃ"</note> in B 1 and Calcutta.

**P. 892. l. 3. (VI. 75, 1.)** **Because of having the form of a praise of the arrow** <note>original: "iṣustutirūpatvāt"</note> etc. in Calcutta. **In the deity having the cause of the form of the praise of the arrow** <note>original: "iṣustutirūpanimittadevatāke"</note> in Asiatic Society Paris and C. Mill. **Because of having the form of the chariot [?] and praise of the arrow** <note>original: "iṣustutithurūpatvāt"</note> in B 1.

**P. 894. l. 1. (VI. 75, 4.)** **Like those having the same mind** <note>original: "samanaskeva"</note> from B and Calcutta. **Like** <note>original: "iva"</note> stands for **as** <note>original: "yathā"</note>, otherwise we might write **abandoning** <note>original: "tyajantī"</note>.

**P. 894. l. 4. (VI. 75, 4.)** **From the two powders** <note>original: "curṇibhyāṃ niḥ"</note> in Calcutta. **Away from the two powders** <note>original: "curṇibhyāṃ viḥ"</note> in Asiatic Society Paris and C. Mill; omitted in B 1. The Sutra <note>A concise aphorism or rule</note> is not to be found in the Uṇádi-sūtra <note>A collection of rules for deriving irregular nouns</note>, where **powder** <note>original: "cūrṇi"</note> and **fire** <note>original: "agni"</note> are formed by a different rule.

**P. 896. l. 24. (VI. 75, 10.)** **[Obscure form]** <note>original: "meṣṭa"</note> || **Do not be harmed** <note>original: "mā riṣṭā"</note> in Asiatic Society Paris and C. Mill. **[Obscure form]** <note>original: "māṣṭa"</note> in B 4. **Do not be harmed [variant]** <note>original: "mā iśiṣṭa"</note> in Calcutta and B 1.

**P. 897. l. 18. (VI. 75, 11.)** **May they grant peace and protection** <note>original: "śarma śaraṇaṃ prayacchantu"</note> in manuscript A. **May they grant peace** <note>original: "śarma yacchantu"</note> in Calcutta. **They grant peace** <note>original: "śarma yacchanti"</note> in B 1.

**P. 897. l. 25. (VI. 75, 12.)** **Firm** <note>original: "dṛḍhā"</note> from B and Calcutta.

**P. 900. l. 8. (VI. 75, 18.)** **Beyond/Wider** <note>original: "uruttaraṃ"</note> || **Wide for you** <note>original: "uru tubhyaṃ"</note> in Asiatic Society Paris, C. Mill, and Calcutta. **Wide** <note>original: "uru"</note> in B.

My copy of the Paris manuscript terminates with the sixth Maṇḍala.

## Critical Notes

**P. 926. l. 19. (VII. 5, 6.)** **They served** <note>original: "asevanta"</note> || **They serve** <note>original: "sevanta"</note> in manuscripts A. B. Ca., C. and Mill.

**P. 927. l. 6. (VII. 5, 7.)** **And the desires** <note>original: "kāmān ca"</note> || **Or the desires** <note>original: "kāmānvā"</note> in A. Ca., C. Mill, and B 1. **Desires** <note>original: "kāmān"</note> in B 4.

**P. 927. l. 15. (VII. 5, 8.)** **This food** <note>original: "iyamannaṃ"</note> in C. Mill and B 1. **This food, this...** <note>original: "iyamannamaiyaṃ"</note> in A. and Ca.

**P. 929. l. 8. (VII. 6, 3.)** **The vain leaders of time** <note>original: "vṛthā kālasya netṛn"</note> in A. and Ca. **The vain throwers-away of time** <note>original: "vṛthā kālasyotkṣeptṛn"</note> in B 4.

**P. 929. l. 9. (VII. 6, 3.)** The phrase from **Agni** to **made** <note>original: "agniḥ to cakāra"</note> is from C. Mill; it is missing in A. and Ca. **The former, ancient Agni made the other men, who were non-sacrificers and unfit for sacrifice, [as they are]** <note>original: "pūrvaḥ purātanaḥ agniḥ aparān puruṣān ayajyūn yāgānarhān cakāra"</note> in B 4.

--- Page 67 ---
<meta>This page transitions from the general front matter and the first Mandala of the Rig Veda to the beginning of the Fourth Mandala. It maintains the structure established by Max Müller, presenting the technical indices (Anukramani), the sacred verse in two traditional formats, and the opening of Sayanacharya’s scholarly commentary.</meta>

## Mandala Introduction

-> **Om** <note>The sacred syllable and traditional invocation of the divine.</note> <-
-> **Salutations to the Illustrious Lord Ganesha** <note>original: "Shri Ganeshaya Namah." Ganesha is the remover of obstacles, traditionally invoked at the start of new sections or books.</note> <-
-> **Now begins the Fourth Book** <note>original: "Atha Chaturtham Mandalam."</note> <-

In the Fourth Book, attributed to the lineage of Vamadeva, there are five sections <note>original: "Anuvakas."</note>. In the first section, there are ten hymns. Among these, the first hymn—beginning with the words "Thee, indeed, O Agni, always"—consists of twenty verses. Here is the descriptive index <note>original: "Anukramani," a traditional cataloging system for Vedic texts.</note>: The hymn "Thee, indeed, O Agni" contains twenty verses. The first is in the **Ashti** meter, the second in **Atijagati**, and the third in **Dhriti**. The last four verses may be addressed to the god Varuna. The Seer of this Book is the Sage Vamadeva. 

The first verse is in the <term>Ashti meter</term> (containing 64 syllables); the second is in the <term>Atijagati meter</term> (52 syllables); the third is in the <term>Dhriti meter</term> (72 syllables). From the fourth verse onwards, according to the general rule of undefined meters, the seventeen remaining verses are in the <term>Trishtubh meter</term> (44 syllables). By the general rule governing the start of a Book, the deity of the entire hymn is Agni (the Fire-god), though alternatively, the three verses starting from the second are addressed to the deity Varuna. The ritual application of the hymn is determined by its internal characteristics. It is used in the rituals at the commencement of the study of the first chapter and in the offerings at the start of the Book.

## Hymn Text

-> **This is the first verse of the hymn** <-

Thee indeed, O Agni, always with one mind, the gods, the divine messenger, have established; with wisdom they have established. The immortal one, worthy of worship among mortals, the god, the primordial god, they generated, the wise one; the universal primordial god they generated, the wise one. **1**

---

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:** <note>original: "Padapatha." This format removes the phonetic blending (Sandhi) between words to show each word in its original, isolated form for clarity of study.</note>

Thee | indeed | O Agni | always | indeed | with one mind | the gods | the divine | messenger | established | thus |
with wisdom | established | 
the immortal | worthy of worship | among mortals | [intensifier] | the god | the primordial god | they generated | the wise one | the universal | the primordial god |
they generated | the wise one. **1**

## Commentary (Sayana)

Vamadeva offers praise: O Agni, "with one mind" <note>original: "samanyavah."</note>. The word "manyu" refers to competitive zeal or spirit. Thus, the phrase means "possessing that spirit," or more specifically, those who act with a shared purpose or compete together against others. 

The "gods" <note>original: "devasah," referring to the shining ones like Indra and others</note>, who are by nature luminous, have established thee, who art a god, a radiant messenger <note>original: "aratim," interpreted here as a swift-goer or messenger</note> who moves quickly, always—"at all times." They truly impel you in the battle sparked by competition. The word "thus" <note>original: "iti"</note> here signifies cause: because the gods constantly impel you for the sake of war, therefore the sacrificers...

B
</margin>

<keywords>Mandala 4, Vamadeva, Agni, Ashti meter, Trishtubh meter, Padapatha, Sayanacharya, Vedic Commentary, Varuna</keywords>

--- Page 68 ---
<meta>This page continues the commentary on the first verse of the first hymn of the Fourth Mandala (Book) of the Rig Veda and provides the full text and commentary for the second verse. The previous page introduced the Vedic seer Vamadeva and the specific meters used in this section.</meta>

Through the act of praise, they have impelled you. In the sacrificial work, they truly and constantly urge you to bring the oblations to the gods and to summon the gods. O Agni, you who are worthy of worship, you are immortal <note>original: "amartyam," meaning free from the nature of death</note> and all-pervading, the shining one, the wise one <note>original: "pracetasam," one whose consciousness or knowledge is directed toward excellent deeds</note>. They have produced you among the mortals performing the sacrifice, you who come toward the gods. The gods produced you for the purpose of cooking the sacrificial offerings. Likewise, they have made you—the one who is wise, skilled in action, and the one who approaches the various sacrifices—to be all-pervasive, so that you may simultaneously bring oblations to sacrifices happening in different places at once. 

**Technical Analysis of the Text:**
The word "impelled" <note>original: "nyerire"</note> comes from the root *ir*, meaning "to go." In the perfect tense, it undergoes specific transformations. The term "through the act" <note>original: "ritva"</note> uses a Vedic variation where the standard ending is replaced.

---

## Hymn Text

->### Verse 2###<-

O Agni, bring back to us your brother Varuna, toward the gods with kind intent, he who loves the sacrifice, the Eldest who loves the sacrifice; the possessor of Truth, the son of Aditi, the supporter of the people, the King, the supporter of the people.

->**Word-by-Word Breakdown**<-

He; brother; Varuna; O Agni; bring back; gods; toward; kind intent; lover of sacrifice; eldest; lover of sacrifice; possessor of truth/order; son of Aditi; supporter of the people; King; supporter of the people.

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, as such a one, bring back your brother—called "brother" because he dwells in the same place—Varuna. He is called Varuna because "he covers or encloses the waters." Bring that god, who is the lover of sacrifice <note>original: "yajnavanasam," he who is to be enjoyed or honored through sacrificial offerings</note>, who is the enjoyer of the sacrifice, the eldest <note>meaning most excellent or praiseworthy</note>, the possessor of truth <note>original: "ritavanam," which can also mean "possessor of waters"</note>, and the son of the goddess Aditi. He is the supporter of the people, sustaining them by granting rain, and he is the King, the shining one, held in high regard by the wise. Turn this god Varuna, and the other gods who have the nature of light, toward the chanters of praise.

**Linguistic Notes for the Verse:**
- **Bring back** <note>original: "vavritsva"</note>: From the root *vrit* (to turn). In the imperative mood, it uses a Vedic form where the class sign is dropped.
- **Kind intent** <note>original: "sumati"</note>: This word uses a specific suffix (*ktin*) which carries a high accent on the first syllable.
- **Eldest** <note>original: "jyeshtham"</note>: A superlative form of "praiseworthy." Due to its grammatical markers, the accent falls on the first syllable.
- **Lover of sacrifice** <note>original: "yajnavanasam"</note>: Derived from the root *van*, meaning to help or share. It describes one who acts for the sake of the sacrifice.

---

## Critical Notes

In the ritual known as the <term>Pravargya</term> <note>an introductory ceremony to the Soma sacrifice involving the heating of milk in a clay pot</note>, during the subsequent recitation, the verse beginning with "O friend, to the friend" is used. This is indicated in the <term>Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra</term> (4.7): "O friend, bring back the friend to us, upright for our protection."

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ This is the third verse of the hymn ॥ <-

O friend, turn your friend toward us; like the two chariot horses <note>original: "rathyeva"</note> turn the swift wheel, O wonderful one, speed toward us.
O Agni, may you find favor in Varuna and among the Maruts <note>storm gods who accompany Indra</note> who possess all-pervading light.
O Shining One, create happiness for our children and our grandchildren; O wonderful one, create happiness for us. ॥ 3 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown**

O Friend; friend; toward; [bring] back; swift; like; wheel; chariot horses; speed; for us; O wonderful one; speed;
O Agni; favor/happiness; in Varuna; together; find; in the Maruts; in the all-shining ones;
for the child; for the grandchild; O Shining One; happiness; create; for us; O wonderful one; happiness; create. ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**O Friend**: You who are like a friend, **O Wonderful One** <note>original: "dasma," meaning one who is beautiful or visible to all</note>, O Agni, turn your friend Varuna toward us for our benefit. Make him face us. An illustration is given: **Like the two chariot horses** <note>original: "rathyeva"</note>, which are skilled in traveling, turn the **swift wheel** toward its destination, so should you act. 

O Agni, **together** with your companion Varuna, you have obtained the **favor** <note>original: "mṛḷīkaṃ," refers here to the pleasant sacrificial offering</note>. Likewise, you have obtained favor among the **Maruts**, whose light is all-pervading. The sense is that you have been worshiped through the specific rituals dedicated to Agni-Varuna and Agni-Marut.

**O Shining One**: O Agni, you who are blazing, create **happiness** for our **child** <note>original: "tokāya," literally "the one by whom the mother is pained through dwelling in the womb"</note> and for our **grandchild** <note>original: "tuje," literally "the one through whom the father goes beyond his debt to his ancestors"</note>. O wonderful one, O Agni, create happiness for us.

**Grammatical Note:** The word "rathyeva" means "these two belong to the chariot," using a specific Vedic suffix. The word "ranhyā" is derived from the root meaning "to speed" or "to go."

**Liturgical Application (Viniyoga):**
Beginning with the verse "O Agni, [turn] to us," this hymn and the subsequent hymns are utilized in the **Morning Litany** <note>original: "Prātaranuvāka"</note>, specifically in the section dedicated to Agni during the ritual of the three meters, and in the **Ashvina Litany** <note>a late-night or pre-dawn recitation</note>. This is indicated in the *Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra* (4.13): 
> "The four hymns starting with 'O Agni, you who know Varuna...'"

In the **Purificatory Rite** <note>original: "Avabhṛtheṣṭi," performed at the end of a Soma sacrifice</note>, for the sake of the **Final Offering** <note>original: "Sviṣṭakṛt"</note>, Agni and Varuna must be worshiped together. In that context, two specific verses are used as the **Invoking and Offering Formulas** <note>original: "Yājyānuvākyā"</note>. This is noted in the *Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra* (6.13): 
> "For the Final Offering to Agni and Varuna, use the two verses beginning 'O Agni, you who know Varuna...'"

Furthermore, if one performs the **Fire Sacrifice** <note>original: "Agnihotra"</note>, there is a specific offering to Agni and Varuna. In that rite, these same two verses serve as the invoking and offering formulas, as stated in the *Aitareya Brahmana* (7.9):
> "O Agni, you who know Varuna... and O Agni, be closest to us with your protection."

<summary>This page provides the text and commentary for the third verse of Rig Veda 4.1, emphasizing the friendship between Agni, Varuna, and the Maruts, and defining the specific ritual contexts in which these verses are recited.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Varuna, Maruts, offspring, ritual application, Viniyoga, Morning Litany, Aitareya Brahmana, Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the first hymn of the Fourth Mandala (Book) of the Rig Veda. ## Hymn Text

-> ॥ This is the fourth verse of the hymn ॥ <-

O Agni, you who are wise, turn away from us the wrath <note>original: "heḷas," meaning anger or disregard</note> of the god Varuna.
As the best of sacrificers, the greatest bearer of oblations, and shining brightly, release us from all that is hated <note>original: "dveṣāṃsi," which refers here to sins or spiritual obstructions</note>. ॥ 4 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown**

You; our; O Agni; of Varuna; the wise/knowing one; of the god; wrath; away; turn/remove;
best of sacrificers; greatest bearer; shining brightly; all; hatreds/sins; effectively; release; from us. ॥ 4 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, you are the **wise** one <note>original: "vidvān"</note>, meaning you know the means to achieve all human goals. As such, may you **turn away** the **wrath** <note>original: "heḷas"</note>—the anger—of the shining **god Varuna** from **us**. Specifically, remove those "nooses" <note>original: "pāśa-grahān," symbolic of Varuna’s judgment</note> that belong to us as a consequence of his will. You are the **best of sacrificers** <note>original: "yajiṣṭha," the most effective performer of rituals</note> and the **greatest bearer** <note>original: "vahnitaḥ," the one who most excellently carries the offerings to the gods</note>. You are **shining brightly** with intense light. Therefore, **release** us <note>original: "pra mumugdhi"</note>—liberate us effectively—from **all** **hatreds**, which refers to sins or the dark forces that oppose us.

<note>Grammatical note: Sayana explains that "heḷas" comes from a root meaning "disregard." The verb "yāsi" with the prefix "ava" is used here to mean destruction or removal of the divine anger. The form "mumugdhi" is a command for Agni to "release" the worshipper from the bonds of sin.</note>

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now, the fifth verse ॥ <-

O Agni, be the nearest to us with your protection, being our closest help at the breaking of this dawn.
Appease Varuna for us by your sacrifice; being gracious, enjoy the offering; be one who is easy for us to invoke. ॥ 5 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown**

That [same]; you; our; O Agni; nearest/lowest; be; with protection; closest; of this; of dawn; in the dawning;
away; sacrifice [away]; our; Varuna; being gracious; enjoy/eat; the happiness [oblation]; well-invoked; our; be. ॥ 5 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, **that** very same you, be **nearest** to us <note>original: "avama," literally "lowest" or most accessible</note> through your **protection**. At the **breaking of this dawn**—the early morning time when rituals like the Agnihotra are performed—**be** our **closest** helper so that our sacred work may be accomplished. In other words, stay very near to us.

Furthermore, **sacrifice away** for **us** the **Varuna** <note>the commentator explains this means "sacrifice away the disease of Varuna," such as dropsy, or the sins that cover us like a veil</note>. **Being gracious** <note>original: "rarāṇa," rejoicing in the offerings we provide</note> or acting as the one who grants great rewards to the sacrificers, **enjoy** this **happiness** <note>original: "mṛḷīkam," here referring to the pleasant sacrificial food</note>. Eat of it. Finally, O you who possess a beautiful call <note>original: "suhava," one who is easily and effectively invoked</note>, **be** present for **us**.

<note>Grammatical note: Sayana notes that "nediṣṭha" (closest) is derived from the word for "near." He also mentions that "rarāṇa" implies Agni is finding delight in the ritual acts of the priests.</note>

<summary>In these verses, Agni is petitioned to act as a divine mediator who pacifies the wrath of Varuna and removes the "nooses" of sin or disease from the worshippers, particularly during the morning sacrifice.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Varuna, wrath, protection, dawn, sacrifice, sin, purification, Sayana, Rig Veda</keywords>

...the deletion of the letter 'm' <note>original: "m-kāra-lopa"</note> is a Vedic peculiarity. Alternatively, the word "kānaci" comes from the root "rā" (to give) with a change in suffix. The initial syllable of reduplicated forms is accented. In the word "edhi" (be), the root "as" (to be) becomes "e" before the suffix "dhi," and the reduplicated syllable is dropped. Because this change is considered "not yet occurred" for certain rules, the suffix "hi" becomes "dhi." The accent is lowered.

## Hymn Text

->॥ Verse 6 ॥<-

The appearance of this fortunate god is most excellent and most wonderful among mortals. Like the pure, warm clarified butter of the cow that must not be slain, his presence is as desirable as the generous gift of a milking cow from a god. ॥ 6 ॥ <note>RV 4.1.6</note>

**Word-by-word breakdown**
Of this; most excellent; of the fortunate; appearance; of the god; most wonderful; among mortals;
pure; clarified butter <note>original: "ghṛtam"</note>; like; warm; of the cow that must not be slain <note>original: "aghnyāyāḥ"</note>; desirable; of the god; like a generous gift; of a milking cow. ॥ 6 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Of the **fortunate** <note>original: "subhagasya," meaning one who is highly worthy of being honored</note> **Agni**, the **appearance** <note>original: "saṃdṛk," his visual manifestation</note> is **most excellent**—highly praiseworthy—and **most wonderful** among **mortals**. It is exceedingly to be sought and worshipped. It is **desirable** <note>original: "spārhā"</note>, meaning everyone yearns for it.

An illustration is provided: Just as for a man desiring milk, the **pure**, radiant, and **warm clarified butter** <note>original: "ghṛtam," here implying the richness of the milk</note> of the **cow that must not be slain** <note>original: "aghnyāyāḥ"</note> is desirable, so is Agni. Another illustration: it is like the **generous gift** <note>original: "maṃhanā"</note> of a **milking cow** to a person who is begging for one. The term "maṃhati" refers to the act of giving; just as a gift brings joy, so does the sight of Agni.

<note>Grammatical note: "Subhaga" has the accent on the first syllable of the second part of the compound. "Spārhā" is formed with a suffix that puts the accent on the final syllable. "Deva" (god) comes from a root meaning "to shine" or "to play"; it refers here to beauty or light.</note>

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Verse 7 ॥<-

Threefold are his highest, true, and desirable births; they belong to the god Agni. Enveloped within the infinite, he has come to us—pure, bright, noble, and shining intensely. ॥ 7 ॥ <note>RV 4.1.7</note>

**Word-by-word breakdown**
Threefold; his; those; highest; are; true; desirable; of the god; births <note>original: "janimāni"</note>; of Agni;
in the infinite; within; enveloped; hither; he has come; pure; bright; noble; shining intensely. ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

There are **threefold**—three distinct—**births** of this **god Agni**. These represent his manifestations as Fire on earth, Wind/Lightning in the atmosphere, and the Sun in the sky. **Those** births are **highest**, meaning they are most excellent, and they are **true**, meaning they are real and effective. They are **desirable** to all. Alternatively, these could refer to three specific births of Agni himself, as mentioned in other verses:

> "Agni was first born from heaven..." <note>Rig Veda 10.45.1</note>

and

> "Three births encompass him..." <note>Rig Veda 1.95.3</note>

...famous among platforms and the like. Within the **infinite**, boundless **sky**, in the midst, he is **enveloped** <note>original: "parivītaḥ"</note> by his own light. He is **pure**—the purifier of everything—and **radiant**, possessing light. For this reason, he is **shining intensely**, the **Lord** <note>original: "aryaḥ"</note> and master. In the word "satyā," the suffix is dropped according to the Vedic rule that allows for frequent variations in endings. The word "enveloped" <note>original: "parivītaḥ"</note> comes from the root *vyeñ* (to cover or wrap) with the past participle suffix. It undergoes a linguistic process called "vowel extension" <note>original: "saṃprasāraṇa"</note> due to its root type. The word **Lord** <note>original: "aryaḥ"</note> is derived from the root *ṛ* (to go) and is a specific form used to denote either a master or a member of the merchant class; here, it carries the accent on the final syllable to signify its meaning as "master."

## Hymn Text
He, the messenger, desires all the dwellings; the invoker with the golden chariot and pleasant tongue. He with red horses, beautiful and resplendent, is always delightful, like a gathering where food is abundant. ॥ 8 ॥ <note>RV 4.1.8</note>

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
He; the messenger; all; indeed; toward; desires; the dwelling; the invoker; golden-charioted; pleasant-tongued; red-horsed; beautiful; resplendent; always; delightful; like a gathering full of food; the assembly. ॥ 8 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
Agni is the **messenger** <note>original: "dūta"</note> of the gods and the **invoker** <note>original: "hotā," the priest who calls the gods to the ritual</note>. He possesses a **golden chariot** and a **pleasant tongue**—meaning his flames are beautiful and pleasing to behold. Such a god **desires** <note>original: "vasti"</note> or loves all the **dwellings**, which are the places where gods are worshipped.

What else is he like? He is **red-horsed** <note>original: "rohidaśvaḥ"</note>, meaning his horses (his flames) are of a reddish hue. He is **beautiful** in form and **resplendent** with light; for this reason, he is always **delightful**. A comparison is provided: **like a gathering full of food**. Just as an assembly or a household that is prosperous and filled with food is pleasing to people, so is Agni's presence at the sacrifice.

Regarding the grammar: in "pleasant-tongued" <note>original: "raṃsujihvaḥ"</note>, the first part of the compound retains the original accent. The word for "beautiful" <note>original: "vapuṣyaḥ"</note> uses a suffix meaning "effective in that form." The word "resplendent" <note>original: "vibhāvā"</note> is formed with a Vedic suffix common in the hymns.

## Hymn Text
Making men conscious, he is the friend of sacrifice; they lead him with a great rope. He dwells in the houses of this mortal, performing his work; the god has attained fellowship with the mortal. ॥ 9 ॥ <note>RV 4.1.9</note>

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
He; making conscious; of the man; the friend of sacrifice; forward; him; with a great; rope; they lead; he; dwells; of this (mortal); in the houses; performing; the god; of the mortal; the state of having shared wealth (fellowship); has attained. ॥ 9 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
He is the **friend of sacrifice** <note>original: "yajñabandhuḥ"</note> because his connection or employment is firmly established in rituals like the *Agnihotra* (the daily fire offering). This Agni **makes men conscious** <note>original: "cetayan"</note>, meaning he recognizes and brings awareness to those humans who are engaged in sacred actions. They lead him with a **great rope**, which refers to a great hymn of praise...

## Commentary (Sayana)
[Continuation of commentary for verse 9]

The Adhvaryu priests and others lead forward that Agni, who is equipped with a beautiful rope. They cast him into the northern altar and other such ritual spaces. Within the **homes** <note>original: "duryāsu"</note> of the **mortal** <note>original: "martyasya"</note>, the sacrificer, that Agni **dwells** <note>original: "kṣeti"</note>, **accomplishing** <note>original: "sādhan"</note> their desired goals. That shining god, Agni, attains fellowship with the wealthy person in whose house he resides. This means that by causing abundant wealth to be given to the sacrificer, he becomes associated with that wealth. The word **accomplishing** <note>original: "sādhan"</note> is derived from the roots *rādh* or *sādh*, meaning "to achieve success"; it is a present participle form meaning "one who brings about results."

## Hymn Text
->॥ This is the tenth verse ॥<-

May that Agni, knowing all, lead us quickly toward the treasure assigned by the gods which belongs to him; that which all the immortals created through prayerful action, he whom Heaven, the Father and Procreator, truly sprinkles. ॥ 10 ॥ <note>RV 4.1.10</note>

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
He; indeed; us; Agni; may he lead; knowing well; toward; the treasure; assigned by the gods; which; of him;
by prayerful action; which; all; the immortals; they made; Heaven; Father; Procreator; truly; sprinkling. ॥ 10 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Knowing all** <note>original: "prajānan"</note>, may that Agni **lead** <note>original: "nayatu"</note> **us** <note>original: "naḥ"</note> **quickly** <note>original: "tu"</note> **toward** <note>original: "acchā"</note> the excellent **treasure** <note>original: "ratnam"</note> (wealth) which is **distributed by the gods** <note>original: "devabhaktam"</note>—meaning it is to be enjoyed by the gods or by the praising worshipers—and which is associated with this Agni. **All** <note>original: "viśve"</note> the **immortals** <note>original: "amṛtāḥ"</note> (those who do not die) **made** <note>original: "akṛṇvan"</note> **which** [Agni] through their **thought** <note>original: "dhiyā"</note> (referring to the sacrificial act) to be the conveyer of oblations. Of this Agni, **Heaven** <note>original: "dyauḥ"</note> is the **father** <note>original: "pitā"</note>, the protector, and also the **procreator** <note>original: "janitā"</note>. This is known from the scripture: "O Agni, you are the wise son of Heaven" (Rig Veda 3.25.1). Alternatively, Heaven refers to the shining Sun, the father and procreator, as tradition states that Agni is born from the Sun. The Adhvaryu priests **sprinkle** <note>original: "ukṣan"</note> that **true** <note>original: "satyam"</note> (real/existing) Agni with oblations like clarified butter.

The term **distributed by the gods** <note>original: "devabhaktam"</note> is formed from the root *bhaj* (to serve or distribute) with a passive suffix; the accent follows the rule for compounds where the first word retains its original tone. **Sprinkle** <note>original: "ukṣan"</note> comes from the root *ukṣ* (to moisten); it is a past tense form that lacks the usual prefix according to Vedic grammatical flexibility.

->॥ This ends the thirteenth varga in the fourth chapter of the third book (Ashtaka) ॥<-

## Hymn Text
->॥ This is the eleventh verse ॥<-

He was born first among the dwellings, at the foundation of the great space, in this womb. Without feet and without a head, hiding his ends, and constantly moving within the nest of the Bull. ॥ 11 ॥ <note>RV 4.1.11</note>

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
He; was born; first; in the dwellings; of the great; at the foundation; of space; of this; in the womb;
footless; headless; hiding; the ends; moving/joining; of the Bull; in the nest. ॥ 11 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
That Agni, being **first** <note>original: "prathamaḥ"</note> or most excellent in his forms such as the Ahavaniya (the primary sacrificial fire), was born among the **dwellings** <note>original: "pastyāsu"</note> (the houses of the sacrificers)...

<meta>The previous page's continuity note mentions Mandala 4, Sukta 1, whereas this page's header and content correspond to the end of Mandala 3, Sukta 54. This suggests a transition or a discrepancy in the provided manuscript sequence. [The verse begins by describing how Agni] was born. He comes into existence by being the foundation for the ritual oblation. Likewise, he is established at the base <note>original: "budhne"</note> of this great, vast firmament, upon the earth, and specifically in the "womb"—the place of the northern altar and other ritual sites. That Agni is "footless" <note>original: "apāt"</note> and "headless" <note>original: "aśīrṣā"</note>. The text explains this: he is hiding <note>original: "guhamānaḥ"</note> his feet and his head at the two ends. This means his head and feet cannot be distinguished. In the "nest" <note>original: "nīḷe"</note> or the abode of the Bull <note>the Bull refers to the cloud, which is capable of "showering" rain</note>, he remains in the sky, joining <note>original: "āyoyuvānaḥ"</note> himself to it in the form of smoke. 

Alternatively: That first lightning-fire which moves among the rivers, in the depths of the atmosphere, in the place of the great light or water; being without feet or head, he covers the surrounding regions with his own brilliance. Then, mingling those lights within himself, he moves in the sky—the place of the Bull—and has now been born due to his fitness for the ritual act. 

**Grammatical Note:** **Apat** (footless): The 'a' at the end is dropped according to the rules for compound words. **Guhamānaḥ** (hiding): Derived from the root *guh* (to cover), using the **śānac** <term>a present participle suffix</term> suffix. **Āyoyuvānaḥ** (joining/mingling): From the root *yu* (to mix/join), a frequentative form indicating repeated action.

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ This is the twelfth verse ॥<-

The first host has come forth through the inspired song, in the womb of Cosmic Order, in the nest of the Bull. Desirable, young, beautiful, and radiant, the seven dear ones have generated him for the Showerer. ॥ 12 ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Forth; the host/strength; has come; the first; through inspired song; of Cosmic Order; in the womb; of the Bull; in the nest; desirable; young; beautiful; radiant; seven; dear ones; they generated; for the Showerer. ॥ 12 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, through the **inspired song** <note>original: "vipanyā"</note>, which is your praise, your **host** <note>original: "śardhaḥ"</note> or strength first **went forth** <note>original: "pra-ārta"</note>. This occurred in the place of the immortal water, in the atmosphere which is the "nest" or dwelling-place of the Bull—the cloud capable of raining—where you exist in the form of lightning. Because Agni is **desirable** <note>original: "spārhaḥ"</note> to all, **eternally young** <note>original: "yuvā"</note>, **beautiful in form** <note>original: "vapuṣyaḥ"</note>, and **radiant** <note>original: "vibhāvā"</note>, the **seven dear** <note>original: "sapta priyāsaḥ"</note> officiating priests have **generated** <note>original: "ajanayanta"</note> him for that **Showerer** <note>original: "vṛṣṇe"</note> who bestows desired rewards. That is to say, they performed the hymn of praise.

**Grammatical Note:** **Ārta** (went): From the root *ṛ* (to go), imperfect tense. **Vipanyā** (through song): Derived from the root *pan* (to praise) with the *in* suffix. In the combination **vipanyãँ ṛtasya**, the text follows the *Shakalya* rule <note>a specific phonetic rule in Vedic chanting</note> where the vowel becomes short and nasalized.

| Term | Translation | Definition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **śardham** | host / strength | Refers to the collective force of the Maruts or Agni’s power. |
| **ṛtasya yonā** | in the womb of Order | In the place of Cosmic Truth or Natural Law. |
| **vṛṣabhasya nīḷe** | in the nest of the Bull | The location of Agni, often the rain-cloud or the altar. |
| **spārhaḥ** | desirable | Something to be longed for or sought after. |
| **vibhāva** | radiant | One who possesses great light or shines far and wide. |
| **vṛṣṇe** | for the showerer | A title for a deity (like Agni or Indra) who pours out blessings. |
| **śānac** | śānac suffix | A Sanskrit grammatical suffix used to form middle-voice participles. |
| **Pā. 6.1.127** | Panini 6.1.127 | A specific rule from Panini’s grammar regarding vowel shortening. |

म० ४. अ० १. सू० १. || तृतीयोऽष्टकः ||
<note>Mandala 4, Adhyaya 1, Sukta 1 | The Third Eighth (Ashtaka) subdivision</note>
