## Commentary (Sayana)

**Regarding the eighth verse —**
O Indra, you have performed **this** specific **manly strength** <note>original: *pauṃsyam*; refers to virile or masculine power</note> and **heroic power** <note>original: *vīryam*; the capacity to perform great deeds</note>. The particles *gha* and *it* are used here for poetic emphasis. Furthermore, you **struck down** <note>original: *vadhīḥ*; killed or destroyed</note> the **woman** named **Dawn** <note>Ushas</note>, the **daughter of the sky** who was born from the celestial realm, because she was **seeking to do harm** <note>original: *durhaṇāyuvam*; interpreted here as one desiring wicked destruction</note>.

**Regarding the ninth verse —**
O Indra, you are **the Great**. You **crushed** <note>original: *saṃ piṇak*; pulverized or shattered</note> the Goddess **Dawn**, the **daughter of the sky**, even as she was **being honored** or worshiped by others.

**Regarding the tenth verse —**
Indra, the **Bull** <note>original: *vṛṣā*; a common epithet for Indra as the "showerer" of benefits or the powerful male</note> who rains down desires, **struck down** or destroyed **this** cart belonging to the Dawn. Then **the Dawn**, the goddess of daybreak, **fled** and went away from her **cart** <note>original: *anas*; a heavy bullock cart or wagon</note> which had been **shattered** <note>original: *sampishṭād*; ground to pieces</note> by Indra, because she was **trembling in fear** of him. The word *aha* is a filler particle.

-> || This concludes the twentieth varga of the sixth chapter of the third book || <-

**Regarding the eleventh verse —**
**This cart** belonging to **this** Dawn, which was **well-crushed** <note>thoroughly pulverized</note> by Indra, **lies** on the **Vipasha** <note>term: *Vipaśyā*; the river Beas in modern Punjab</note>.

**Vocabulary Terms**
- **Indra:** The King of the Gods and god of storms.
- **Ushas:** The Goddess of the Dawn, usually depicted as a beautiful woman bringing light.
- **Anas:** A cart or wagon; in Vedic mythology, the Dawn travels in a cart.
- **Shakata:** A synonym for a cart used in the commentary.
- **Paumsya:** Manly strength or virility.
- **Vipashya:** Refers to the river Vipasha (Beas). The commentator notes the cart was broken and left on its banks.

152 || Rig Veda || [Book 3, Chapter 6, Verse 21] <note>The header follows the traditional division into Adhyayas (Chapters) and Vargas (Sections), though it belongs to the Fourth Mandala (Book) of the Samhita.</note>

The river named Vipasha <note>The modern Beas River in India</note>. Upon its bank, the cart lies. It lies there completely. This goddess Dawn, when her cart was broken, fled from that place to a far-off distance. She moved away.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here begins the twelfth verse ॥ <-

**And also the River <note>original: *Sindhu*; likely referring to the Indus River</note>, which was flowing in full youth, you established upon the earth, O Indra, by your creative power. ॥ 12 ॥**

> **Word-for-word analysis:** And | the River | in full youth | flowing in various places | upon | the earth | established | Indra | by creative power ॥ 12 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Indra, and also the River which has passed the stage of childhood <note>original: *vigata-bālya-avasthām*; meaning it is full of water and mature</note>, being full of water and flowing in various directions—you established her everywhere upon the earth by your creative power <note>original: *māyayā*; often meaning wisdom or miraculous power</note>. You have fixed her in place.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here begins the thirteenth verse ॥ <-

**And by your boldness, you have seized the wealth of Shushna when you crushed his cities. ॥ 13 ॥**

> **Word-for-word analysis:** And | of Shushna | through boldness | [particle] | you seized | [particle] | wealth | the cities | when | of him | you crushed ॥ 13 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

And also, O Indra, you who are the assailant <note>original: *dharṣakaḥ*; one who overpowers</note>, have through your boldness completely seized the wealth <note>original: *vedanam*; property or knowledge of possessions</note> belonging to the demon named Shushna from all sides. This seizure occurred at the time when you crushed the cities—the fortified towns—of this Shushna.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here begins the fourteenth verse ॥ <-

**And you struck down, O Indra, the Dasa Shambara, the son of Kulitara, from the great mountain. ॥ 14 ॥**

> **Word-for-word analysis:** And | the Dasa | son of Kulitara | from the great | mountain | from | [particle] | struck down | Indra | Shambara ॥ 14 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

And also, O Indra, you struck down the Dasa <note>term: *Dasa* (an enemy of the Vedic people, often described as a demon or a servant-class being)</note> named Shambara, who is the son of one named Kulitara and who is a destroyer of others. You hurled him down from the top of the great mountain and killed him.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here begins the fifteenth verse ॥ <-

**And you struck down the hundreds and thousands of the Dasa Varchin, like the felloes of a wheel. ॥ 15 ॥**

> **Word-for-word analysis:** And | of the Dasa | of Varchin | thousands | hundreds | you struck down | [particle] | five | like felloes ॥ 15 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

And also, O Indra, you struck down the thousands and five hundreds of the Dasa [Varchin]. ## Hymn Text
**And also that son of Amyua, the cast-aside one, Indra of a hundred powers <term>Shatakratu: an epithet for Indra meaning "one of a hundred sacrifices or powers"</term> made a participant in the hymns. ॥ 16 ॥**

**Word-for-word analysis:**
And | that | son | of Amyua | the cast-aside | of a hundred powers | in the hymns | Indra | [particle] | made a participant ॥ 16 ॥

## Commentary (Sayanacharya)
And also, Indra of a hundred powers made that well-known person named Paravrikta <note>literally "the cast-aside" or "the rejected"</note>, who was the son of a woman named Amyua, a participant in the hymns <note>Ukthas: a specific type of recited Vedic praise</note>. He made him a sharer in the benefits of the sacrifice. This story is further explained in the verse "The ants [brought out] the son of Amyua..." (Rig Veda 4.19.9).

## Hymn Text
**And also those two, Turvasha and Yadu, who were not yet anointed, the Lord of Power, the wise Indra, led across. ॥ 17 ॥**

**Word-for-word analysis:**
And | those two | Turvasha and Yadu | not yet anointed | the Lord of Power | Indra | the wise | led across ॥ 17 ॥

## Commentary (Sayanacharya)
And also, those two famous kings named Turvasha and Yadu—who were "not yet anointed" <note>original: *asnātārā*; meaning they had not received the ritual bath of kingship because of a curse from King Yayati</note>—were led across. Indra, who is the "Lord of Power" <note>Shachipati: can mean either the protector of ritual acts or the husband of Shachi, Indra's wife</note>, being wise and all-knowing, led them across the difficulties. He made them worthy of being consecrated as kings.

## Commentary (Sayanacharya)
And also, O Indra, you instantly killed two kings named Arna and Chitraratha, who lived on the far bank of the Sarayu River. You did this even though they were "Aryas" <note>meaning they belonged to the noble class or claimed the status of Aryans</note>, because they were devoid of devotion and faith toward you. You struck them down.

## Commentary (Sayana)
Indra shattered—meaning he threw down or destroyed—a hundred, or a great number, of cities <note>Sanskrit: *purām*; often referring to fortresses or fortified settlements</note> made of stone belonging to Shambara <note>a mountain-dwelling demon or enemy king</note> for the sake of the sacrificer named Divodasa, who had given oblations <note>Sanskrit: *dashushe*; one who serves the gods through offerings</note>.

## Commentary (Sayana)
Indra, through his own <term>Maya: illusory power or supernatural magic</term>, sent twenty thousand "Dasas"—referring to demons and others who cause decay or destruction to people—to sleep, which means he slew them. १५५

<header>Mandala 4. Hymn 31. Verse 1.] || Third Book || १५५</header>

## Commentary (Sayana) — Continued from previous page
Furthermore, O Indra, regarding that manly power of yours, that sensory strength endowed with capability which you have surely exercised—no one today can diminish or harm that strength.

->॥ Here begins the twenty-fourth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text (RV 4.30.24)
**May the god Aryaman grant us every desirable thing; may Pushan, may Bhaga, and may the toothless god grant us every desirable thing. ॥ २४ ॥**

**Padapatha:**
Every | desirable | thing. | To you. | O Breaker. | God. | May he grant. | Aryaman. |
Every | desirable | thing. | Pushan. | Every | desirable | thing. | Bhaga. | Every | desirable | thing. | God. | Toothless. ॥ २४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Breaker** <note>original: *ādure*; an epithet for Indra as one who "tears apart" enemies</note> of enemies, O Indra, may the **god** named **Aryaman**, who is the regulator of rivals, **grant** to **you** <note>referring here to the sacrificer</note> **every desirable thing**—whatever delightful and enjoyable wealth exists in the world. Likewise, may the nourishing **god Pushan**, who is **toothless** <note>original: *karūḷatī*; meaning "broken-toothed" or "gap-toothed"</note>, **grant** such **desirable** wealth. May **Bhaga** also grant wealth. 

In this verse, because the word "toothless" is placed near the name "Bhaga," one might think it refers to him. Or, it could potentially be an adjective for all three deities (Aryaman, etc.). One might ask: why should it specifically describe Pushan? We answer: No, even though there is proximity to Bhaga, a connection cannot be made without logical fitness. According to the sacred scriptures <note>Sanskrit: *shrutis*</note> which state, "Pushan is indeed toothless as he eats the ground-up portion of the offering," the quality of being toothless is well-known to belong to Pushan alone. Therefore, it is proper to apply this adjective to him, even if the words are separated in the sentence. The term "desirable" <note>original: *vāmam*</note> refers to that which is sought after, as explained in the *Nirukta* (Etymology) 6.31. This should be observed there.

->॥ Thus ends the twenty-third section of the sixth chapter of the third book ॥<-

---

## Hymn Introduction (RV 4.31)
The tenth hymn, beginning with "**With what [help]**," consists of fifteen verses. The Seer is Vamadeva, the deity is Indra, and the meter is Gayatri. The verse "**Directly toward us**" is a specific variation of the Gayatri meter called *Padanivrit*, characterized by having three lines of seven syllables each. As the *Anukramani* (Index) states: "**The hymn 'With what' has fifteen verses; the verse 'Directly toward us' is in the Padanivrit meter.**" 

The application of this hymn follows the ritual requirements. In the *Agnishtoma* sacrifice, on the twenty-fourth day, during the midday libation <note>Sanskrit: *madhyandina savana*</note>, the triplet beginning with "**With what help**" is used by the Maitra-Varuna priest as a chant of praise <note>Sanskrit: *stotriya*</note>. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "**For the assistant priests, the triplet 'With what help the wonderful one shall be present' is used**" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 7.4). Furthermore, in the *Varunapraghasa* rituals, this verse serves as the invitatory prayer <note>Sanskrit: *anuvakya*</note> for the oblation to Ka (Prajapati). It is indicated: "**'With what help the wonderful one shall be present' and 'The Golden Embryo evolved in the beginning'**" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.19).

->॥ Therein, the first verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text (RV 4.31.1)
**With what help will our wonderful, ever-prospering friend be present for us? With what most powerful troop? ॥ १ ॥**

**Padapatha:**
With what. | For us. | Wonderful. | [prefix] | Shall be. | Help. | Ever-prospering. | Friend. | With what. | Most powerful. | Troop. ॥ १ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana) - Verse 1 (continued)
May the **ever-increasing** <note>original: *sadāvṛdhaḥ*</note>, **venerable** <note>original: *cāyanīyaḥ*</note>, and **friend-like** <note>original: *sakha*</note> Indra turn toward us. By what **satisfaction** <note>original: *ūtyā*; specifically through the offering of the sacrifice</note> may he be present before us? With what **most wise** <note>original: *śaciṣṭhayā*</note> wisdom, and by what **conduct** <note>original: *vṛtā*; referring to the performance of the ritual</note> or sacred action, may he become favorably inclined toward us?

---

## Hymn Text - Verse 2
-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

**Which of the exhilarators, the most generous and true, shall intoxicate you from the Soma juice, O Indra, so that you may break through even the firmly-held wealth of the enemy? ॥ २ ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Which | you | true | of exhilarators | most generous | may intoxicate | of the Soma juice | firmly-held | even | to break through | wealth ॥ २ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Indra, which among the **exhilarating** <note>original: *madānām*</note> juices of the **Soma** <note>original: *andhasaḥ*</note>—which is **true** <note>original: *satyaḥ*</note> in its effects and **most generous** <note>original: *maṃhiṣṭhaḥ*; also meaning most worthy of worship</note>—shall **intoxicate** <note>original: *matsat*</note> **you** <note>original: *tvā*</note>? May that juice inspire you to **shatter** <note>original: *āruje*</note> on all sides even the **firmly-held** <note>original: *dṛḷhā*</note> **treasures** <note>original: *vasūni*</note> belonging to our enemies.

---

## Hymn Text - Verse 3
-> ॥ Now the third verse ॥ <-

**Be the protector of us, your friends and your singers; may you be present with a hundred protections. ॥ ३ ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Towards | well | us | of friends | protector | of singers | hundred | may you be | with protections ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Indra, you are the **protector** <note>original: *avitā*</note> of your **friends** <note>original: *sakhīnām*; those who share the same renown</note> and of your **singers** <note>original: *jaritṝṇām*; the chanters of your praise</note>. May you be present **well** <note>original: *su*</note> and favorably inclined toward **us** <note>original: *naḥ*</note> along with a **hundred** <note>original: *śatam*; implying many</note> **protections** <note>original: *ūtibhiḥ*</note>.

---

## Hymn Text - Verse 4
-> ॥ Now the fourth verse ॥ <-

**Turn toward us like a rotating wheel, O Indra, by the prayers of our people. ॥ ४ ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Towards | us | hither | turn | wheel | like | rotated | of a horse | with prayers | of people ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Indra, just **as a rotating wheel** <note>original: *vṛttaṃ cakraṃ na*</note> turns, please **turn toward** <note>original: *abhyāvavṛtsva*</note> us. Come near to **us** <note>original: *naḥ*</note> by the **prayers** <note>original: *niyudbhiḥ*; also can refer to Indra's team of horses, but interpreted here as the praises</note> of **our people** <note>original: *carṣaṇīnām*</note>.

---

## Hymn Text - Verse 5
-> ॥ Now the fifth verse ॥ <-

**For you come to the sloping paths of the sacrifices as if to your own places; I have worshipped alongside the Sun. ॥ ५ ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
By the sloping paths | indeed | of sacrifices | hither | indeed | like places | you go | I have worshipped | in the Sun | together ॥ ५ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Indra, you indeed **go** <note>original: *āgacchasi*</note> to the **sloping** <note>original: *pravatā*</note> regions or paths of the **sacrifices** <note>original: *kratūnām*</note> performed by the worshippers, just **as if** you were going to your own **places** <note>original: *padā-iva*</note> or stations. The particle *ha* is used for emphasis or to fill the meter. O Indra, I have **worshipped** <note>original: *abhaṃkṣi*</note> you **together** <note>original: *sacā*</note> with the **Sun** <note>original: *sūryeṇa*</note>.

-> ॥ Thus ends the twenty-fourth section of the sixth chapter of the third book ॥ <-

Andhas: Often refers to food or the Soma plant/juice itself.
Jaritṛ: A singer or chanter of Vedic hymns.
Kratu: A sacrifice, ritual action, or the mental power behind it.
</vocab>

## Hymn Text
When, O Indra, your **furies** are joined together, and your **wheels** are joined together, then they reside in you, and then in the **Sun**. ॥ ६ ॥
**Word-by-word breakdown:** Joined | when | your | Indra | furies | joined | wheels | are joined | then | they | then | in the Sun ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Indra, whenever the **praises** <note>original: *manyavaḥ*; while usually meaning "fury" or "zeal," Sayana interprets this here as hymns of praise offered by the worshippers</note> intended for you are joined together or accepted by us, and your **movements** <note>original: *cakrāṇi*; literally "wheels," referring to the movements or divine actions of the deity</note> are also joined, then in that moment those praises and those actions reside in you. Subsequently, they also reside in the **Sun** <note>original: *sūrye*; implying the solar nature of Indra or his influence over the heavenly bodies</note>.

-> ॥ The Seventh Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Lord of Power** <note>original: *śacīpate*; the protector of ritual acts or the husband of Shachi</note>, the protector of sacred work, they truly speak of you as the **Bountiful One** <note>original: *maghavānam*; the possessor of great wealth</note> and as the **Giver** <note>original: *dātāram*</note> who grants the desires of those who praise you. You are **ever-shining** <note>original: *avidīdhuyum*; Sayana explains this as "not un-shining," meaning eternally radiant or active</note>. The particles <term>hi</term> and <term>it</term> in the verse are used for poetic emphasis.

## Commentary (Sayana)
And further, O Indra, you immediately grant **abundant wealth** <note>original: *purū cit vasu*; many kinds of riches</note> from all sides to the sacrificer who is **laboring in praise** <note>original: *śaśamānāya*; according to the ancient etymologist Yaska, this refers to one who chants hymns</note> and to the one **pressing the Soma** <note>original: *sunvate*; the ritual extraction of the sacred juice</note>. You truly bestow these gifts.

-> ॥ The Ninth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Indeed, a hundred **devourers** cannot obstruct your **wealth**, nor can they stop your **mighty deeds** when you act. ॥ ९ ॥
**Word-by-word breakdown:** Not | indeed | your | hundred | even | wealth | obstruct | the devourers | nor | mighty deeds | of the one performing ॥ ९ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Indra, the **devourers** <note>original: *āmuraḥ*; obstructors such as the Rakshasas or demons</note> cannot hinder your **wealth** <note>original: *rādhaḥ*</note>, even if that wealth were a hundred-fold. Furthermore, when you are performing the destruction of your enemies, they cannot obstruct your **mighty deeds** <note>original: *cyautnāni*; your heroic strengths or powers</note>.

## Hymn Text

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra**, with your **new** <note>original: *navābhiḥ*; fresh or recent</note> **protections**, may you **open up** <note>original: *apā vṛdhi*; uncover or unlock</note> for **us** those well-known **cow-pens** <note>original: *vrajān*; enclosures where cattle are kept</note> which are **full of cows**. Do this like an **archer** <note>original: *asteva*; a hero or thrower of weapons</note> who clears the way or releases his force.

<summary>This page concludes Sukta 37 of the 3rd Mandala, featuring prayers to Indra for multifaceted protection, friendship, and the liberation of wealth symbolized by cattle enclosures.</summary>
<keywords>Indra, protections (utayaḥ), friendship (sakhyāya), wealth (rāye), cow-pens (vrajān), Sayana commentary, Rig Veda Mandala 3</keywords>

<header>Mandala 4. Chapter 3. Hymn 32.] || The Third Book (Ashtaka) ||</header>

-> ॥ Now the fourteenth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O Indra, let our **daring**, **radiant**, and **unfailing chariot**, seeking **cattle** and seeking **horses**, proceed forward. ॥ १४ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:** Our | daringly | chariot | radiant | Indra | unfailing | seeking cattle | seeking horses | proceeds. ॥ १४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Indra, may **our** <note>original: *asmākam*</note> **chariot** <note>original: *rathaḥ*</note> **proceed** <note>original: *īyate*; meaning it moves everywhere</note>. This chariot is **daring** <note>original: *dhṛṣṇuyā*; a term for that which overpowers enemies</note>, **radiant** <note>original: *dyumān*</note>, **unfailing** <note>original: *anapacyutaḥ*; free from destruction</note>, **seeking cattle** <note>original: *gavyuḥ*</note>, and **seeking horses** <note>original: *aśvayuḥ*</note>. Let it go everywhere. The implied meaning is: through that chariot, may you protect us.

With the verse "Make ours the highest," one should descend from a chariot while looking at the Sun. Thus it is instructed in the ritual manuals: "Having muttered the verse beginning with 'Make ours the highest' while gazing at the Sun, one should descend." <note>This refers to the Grihya Sutra 2.6, a text detailing domestic rituals and etiquette for chariot travel.</note> **Grihya Sutra 2. 6. ॥**

---

-> ॥ This is the fifteenth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O **Sun**, make our **fame** the **highest** among the **gods**, like the **most extensive heaven** above. ॥ १५ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:** Our | highest | make | fame | among gods | Sun | most extensive/highest | heaven-like | above. ॥ १५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Sun** <note>original: *sūrya*</note>, the impeller of all—or perhaps O Indra in the form of the Sun—**make** <note>original: *kṛdhi*</note> **our** <note>original: *asmākam*</note> **fame** <note>original: *śravaḥ*</note> (or glory) **highest** <note>original: *uttamam*</note> and most excellent **among the gods** <note>original: *deveṣu*</note>, that is, among the shining ones such as the fire-god Agni and others. He provides an illustration: **like the heaven** <note>original: *dyām-iva*</note> which is **most extensive** <note>original: *varṣiṣṭham*</note> (meaning exceedingly great or capable of pouring down blessings). Just as you made the celestial realm the most excellent and situated it above all worlds, do the same for our reputation.

-> ॥ Thus ends the twenty-sixth section in the sixth chapter of the third book. ॥ <-

---

The eleventh hymn, beginning with "Come to us, O Indra," consists of twenty-four verses. It was seen by the seer **Vamadeva** <note>Vamadeva is the primary sage-author of the 4th Mandala</note>, is set in the **Gayatri** meter, and is dedicated to **Indra**. In the final portion, the two verses beginning with "Like two young girls" (*kanīnakeva*) are specifically dedicated to Indra's horses. Thus it is recorded in the *Anukramani* <note>The ancient systematic index of the Rig Veda</note>: "The twenty-four verses beginning 'Come to us'; in the last two, Indra's horses are praised." The ritual application has already been mentioned.

-> ॥ There, the first verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Come** indeed to us, O **Indra**, **slayer of Vritra**; come to **our side**, O **Great One**, with your **great protections**. ॥ १ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:** Come | indeed | us | Indra | Vritra-slayer | our | side | come | Great | great (plural) | protections. ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **slayer of Vritra** <note>original: *vṛtrahan*; referring to Indra's defeat of the demon of drought and obstruction</note>, the destroyer of enemies, O Indra, **come** <note>original: *ā-gahi*</note> **indeed** <note>original: *tu*</note> quickly **to us** <note>original: *naḥ*</note>. O **Great One** <note>original: *mahān*</note>, you who are abundant, **come** to **our side** <note>original: *asmākam ardham*</note>—meaning near us—along **with great** <note>original: *mahībhiḥ*</note> **protections** <note>original: *ūtibhiḥ*</note> (or acts of favor).

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

**You are active, a winner of spoils; gather [wealth] for us. You perform wonderful deeds for our protection. ॥ २ ॥**

**Active | indeed | surely | you are | winner of spoils | gather | indeed | gather | wonderful | you perform | for protection. ॥ २ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O <note>original: *cicca*</note> worshipful and venerable Indra, although you are **active** <note>original: *bhūrmiṣidvat*; meaning one who is constantly moving or wandering</note>, you are also a **winner of spoils** <note>original: *tūrturirdhāsi*; meaning a provider of our desired objects</note>. The particle "ā" is used here in the sense of "and." Among our people who are **engaged in wonderful works** <note>original: *ciciṣīṣu*</note>, you **bring about** <note>original: *ā kṛṇoṣi*; perform or bestow from all sides</note> **wonderful** <note>original: *citraṃ*</note> and desirable wealth **for protection** <note>original: *ūtaye*</note>. The word **gha** is a filler particle used for poetic completion.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the third verse ॥ <-

**With even a few companions, you strike down the one who leaps high and grows mighty through your power, [joined] with those who are with you. ॥ ३ ॥**

**With few | indeed | the one who leaps high | you strike | the growing one | by might | with companions | who | in you | associated. ॥ ३ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Indra, **with even a few** <note>original: *dabhrebhiścit*</note> **companions** <note>original: *sakhibhiḥ*</note>—the sacrificers—you **strike** <note>original: *haṃsi*</note> or destroy the **growing** <note>original: *vṛdhantaṃ*</note> and great enemy who **leaps high** <note>original: *śaśīyāṃsaṃ*</note> <note>derived from the root *śaś*, meaning to move by leaping</note> through your own **might** <note>original: *ojasā*</note>. This refers to **those** <note>original: *ye*</note> sacrificers who are **associated** <note>original: *sacā*</note> **with you** <note>original: *tve*</note>. This last phrase connects back to the companions mentioned earlier.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the fourth verse ॥ <-

**O Indra, we are associated with you; we praise you repeatedly. Protect us, indeed, protect us! ॥ ४ ॥**

**We | Indra | you | associated | we | you | towards | praise repeatedly | us | us | indeed | and | protect. ॥ ४ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Indra, **we** the sacrificers are **associated** <note>original: *sacā*</note> with **you** <note>original: *tve*</note>. **We** **praise you repeatedly** <note>original: *abhinonumaḥ*; meaning to praise intensely or frequently</note>. O Indra, you **protect** <note>original: *udava*</note> **us, indeed, all of us** <note>original: *asmānasmanit*</note> with excellence.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the fifth verse ॥ <-

**O Wielder of the Stone, come to us with your wonderful, blameless, and unassailable protections. ॥ ५ ॥**

**He | us | with wonderful | O wielder of the stone | with blameless | with protections | with unassailable | come | come. ॥ ५ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Wielder of the Stone** <note>original: *adrivo*; referring to Indra as the holder of the thunderbolt or *Vajra*</note>, may **you** <note>original: *sa*</note> **come to** <note>original: *ā gahi*</note> **us** <note>original: *naḥ*</note> along with **protections** <note>original: *ūtibhiḥ*</note> that are **wonderful** <note>original: *citrābhiḥ*; meaning desirable</note>, **blameless** <note>original: *anavadyābhiḥ*; free from fault</note>, and **unassailable** <note>original: *anādhṛṣṭābhiḥ*</note> by any enemies.

-> ॥ Thus ends the twenty-seventh Varga in the sixth Chapter of the third Book ॥ <-

[Mandala 4. Hymn 32. Verses 15–18.] || Third Book (Ashtaka) || 163

## Hymn Text

-> **॥ Now the fifteenth verse ॥** <-
**May the hymn of our thoughts, O Indra, reach you. Bring your two bay horses hitherward. ॥ १५ ॥**
> **Our | you | of thoughts | [to reach] | hymn | Indra | may [it] reach | hitherward | [hither] | turn | the two bay horses. ॥ १५ ॥**

---

-> **॥ Now the sixteenth verse ॥** <-
**Eat our sacrificial cake and enjoy our songs, as a man desiring a bride [enjoys] a maiden. ॥ १६ ॥**
> **Sacrificial cake | and | our | eat | enjoy | songs | and | our | one desiring a bride-like | maiden. ॥ १६ ॥**

---

-> **॥ Now the seventeenth verse ॥** <-
**We beg of Indra a thousand trained, swift-moving horses and a hundred measures of Soma. ॥ १७ ॥**
> **A thousand | of swift ones | of the trained | Indra | we beg | a hundred | of Soma | measures. ॥ १७ ॥**

---

-> **॥ Now the eighteenth verse ॥** <-
**Thousands and hundreds of cows we draw toward us. May your wealth come to us. ॥ १८ ॥**
> **Thousands | your | hundreds | we | of cows | [hither] | draw | among us | wealth | let [it] come | your. ॥ १८ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

[...O] **Vasu** <note>original: *vaso* — one who dwells in the sacrifice or provides a dwelling</note>, O Indra, be **hitherward-facing** <note>original: *arvācīnaḥ*</note> toward us, the sacrificers. Likewise, O **drinker of Soma** <note>original: *somapāḥ*</note>, O Indra, **rejoice** <note>original: *matsva*</note> greatly with the food of the Soma juices.

**॥ Regarding the fifteenth verse ॥**
**Of thoughts** <note>original: *matīnām*</note> refers to the praisers; the word is derived from the root "to think." May the **hymn** <note>original: *stomaḥ*</note> or song of praise belonging to **us** <note>original: *asmākam*</note> **reach you** <note>original: *tvāmāyacchatu*</note>, O Indra. That is, may it fix you among us. You, in turn, **turn** <note>original: *āvartaya*</note> your two **bay horses** <note>original: *harī*</note> so that they face toward us.

**॥ Regarding the sixteenth verse ॥**
O Indra, **eat** <note>original: *ghasaḥ* / *addhi*</note> **our** <note>original: *naḥ*</note> **sacrificial cake** <note>original: *puroļāśam*</note>—which is food in the form of a baked grain-cake. Likewise, **enjoy** <note>original: *joṣayāse*</note> or accept **our songs** <note>original: *giraḥ*</note> consisting of words of praise. An example is given: **Like a man desiring a bride** <note>original: *vadhūyuriva*</note>. Just as a man seeking a wife enjoys the words of women, in that same way [accept our songs].

-> **॥ Thus ends the twenty-ninth section (Varga) of the sixth chapter (Adhyaya) of the third book (Ashtaka) ॥** <-

**॥ Regarding the seventeenth verse ॥**
**We** the praisers **beg** <note>original: *īmahe*</note> **Indra**, who possesses supreme sovereignty, for a **thousand** <note>original: *sahasram*</note> **swift-moving** <note>original: *vyatīnām*</note> and **trained** <note>original: *yuktānām*</note> horses. Likewise, we beg for a **hundred** <note>original: *śatam*</note> **measures** <note>original: *khāryaḥ*</note> of pressed Soma. Here, the word "measure" <term>Khari (a specific volume or vessel)</term> indicates the <term>Dronakalasha (a large wooden Soma-vat)</term>. The meaning is that we ask for many sacrifices involving countless ritual vessels.

<vocab>
- **Indra**: The king of the gods and the primary deity of this hymn.
- **Purodasha (Purōļāśa)**: A traditional sacrificial cake made from ground rice or barley, offered in the fire.
- **Stoma**: A technical term for a chanted hymn or a collection of praises.
- **Khari**: An ancient unit of measurement for grain or liquids; in this ritual context, it refers to the containers holding the Soma juice.
- **Dronakalasha**: A large trough or vessel used for collecting the Soma juice after it has been pressed and filtered.
- **Vadhuyu**: A poetic term for a suitor or a man seeking a bride, used here as a simile for Indra’s eagerness to hear the prayers.
</vocab>

<summary>This page contains the final verses of the 32nd hymn to Indra, where the worshippers offer sacrificial cakes and songs while requesting abundance in the form of horses, cows, and Soma. Sayana's commentary clarifies the ritual significance of these requests, framing the desire for "measures" of Soma as a request for more opportunities to perform the sacrifice.</summary>

## Commentary (Sayana)

The word **expanded** <note>original: *vidrudhe*</note> means manifested or well-placed. # Rig Veda: Ashtaka 4, Adhyaya 1, Varga 1

-> ॥ Salutation to Lord Ganesha ॥ <-

**I salute that Great Lord, the Holy Pilgrimage of Knowledge, whose breath is the Vedas and who created the entire universe from those very Vedas.**

In this fourth section <note>Anuvaka</note> there are thirteen hymns. Among them, the first hymn beginning with **"Toward the Rbhus"** <note>original: *Pra rbhubhyah*</note> consists of eleven verses. It was revealed to the seer Vamadeva and is composed in the *Trishtubh* meter. This group of five hymns is dedicated to the **Rbhus** <note>original: *Rbhu* — a group of three brothers, divine artisans known for their skill</note>. The Index <note>original: *Anukramanika*</note> states: **"Toward the Rbhus is an eleven-verse hymn to the Rbhus."** During the ten-day sacrifice <note>original: *vyudha dasharatra*</note>, on the fourth day, this hymn is recognized as part of the recitation for the All-Gods <note>original: *Vaishvadeva-shastra*</note>. As indicated in the ritual manuals: **"Toward the Rbhus, toward the pure"** <note>original: *Pra rbhubhyah pra shukretu*</note> is the hymn for the All-Gods (Aitareya Brahmana 9.4).

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the first verse ॥ <-

**Toward the Rbhus I send forth my speech like a messenger; at the ritual preparation I praise the white cow. They who, swift as the wind, with their rapid movements, instantly encompassed the heavens through their diligent works. ॥ १ ॥**

**Toward | the Rbhus | a messenger-like | speech | I send forth | at the preparation | the white | cow | I praise |**
**They who | wind-driven | with rapid | movements | around | the heavens | instantly | working | became (present) ॥ १ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Regarding the Rbhus: they were originally human beings who attained divinity through their ascetic penance. This is clearly recorded in the **Holy Explanation** <note>original: *Brahmana*</note>: **"The Rbhus were indeed among the gods"** <note>original: *Aitareya Brahmana 3.30*</note>. Some teachers claim that the "Rbhus" are actually the rays of the sun. 

I, the sacrificer, send forth my speech—consisting of this hymn of praise—toward these gods named Rbhus, who shine with great light. In what manner? **Like a messenger** <note>original: *dutam-iva*</note>. Just as people send a messenger to accomplish their specific tasks, I send this prayer to them. 

Furthermore, at the **preparation** <note>original: *upastare* — the ritual spreading of the grass or preparation for the Soma juice</note>, I **praise** <note>original: *ile*</note> the **white cow** <note>original: *shvaitarim dhenum* — literally "the daughter of Shvitara" or simply a very white cow</note> that provides milk. I seek this from the Rbhus. 

These Rbhus are **driven by the wind** <note>original: *vata-jutah*</note>, meaning their speed is equal to the wind. Being **diligent workers** <note>original: *apasa*</note> who perform deeds for the benefit of the world, they **encompassed** <note>original: *pari-babhu-vuh*</note> or pervaded the **heavens** <note>original: *dyam* — the sky or atmosphere</note> instantly with their **rapid** <note>original: *taranibhih*</note> **movements** <note>original: *evaih*</note>. 

If we follow the interpretation that the Rbhus are the rays of the sun, then this means the rays of the sun spread and encompass the entire atmosphere instantly.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

**When the Rbhus, with skillful hands and through their wondrous deeds, served their parents... ॥ २ ॥**

## Hymn Text

<note>Word-for-word breakdown of Verse 2, continued</note>
When | indeed | they performed | the Rbhus | for their parents | service | through application | with wondrous deeds | then | indeed | of the gods | near | friendship | they approached | the wise ones | nourishment | they brought | to the worshipper ॥ २ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

**When** <note>original: *yada*</note> at which time the **Rbhus** <note>the three divine brothers</note> through the **service** <note>original: *parivisti*</note> of attending to their **parents** <note>original: *pitrbhyam* — specifically their mother and father</note> were **occupied with the application** <note>original: *vesana*</note> of their skills. Alternatively, this refers to the "dress" or form they gave them—making their aged parents young again. Through their **wondrous deeds** <note>original: *damsanabhih* — such as the crafting of the divine horse and the chariot</note> they labored. **Immediately thereafter** <note>original: *at it*</note>, they **approached** the **friendship** <note>original: *sakhyam* — meaning a state of equality or alliance</note> of the **gods**, such as Indra and the others; they attained divinity. This reflects the idea that the gods granted them divinity as a reward for their craftsmanship, as noted in other verses (Rig Veda 1.161.3). Furthermore, being **wise** <note>original: *dhiraso* — intelligent</note>, they **brought** or sustained the **nourishment** <note>original: *pustim*</note> consisting of cattle and other wealth for the **worshipper** <note>original: *manaya*</note> who performs the ritual. Alternatively, they brought nourishment to the **mind** <note>original: *manayai*</note> to provide it with great clarity.

---

## Hymn Text

->|| Now the third verse ||<-

**They who made their parents young again, who were old and lying like withered posts; may Vaja, Vibhvan, and Rbhu, accompanied by Indra and tasting the sweetness of the ritual drink, protect our sacrifice. ॥ ३ ॥**

<note>Word-for-word breakdown of Verse 3</note>
Again | they | made | the parents | young | always | like posts | aged | lying | they | Vaja | Vibhvan | Rbhu | Indra-accompanied | sweetness-tasting | our | may protect | sacrifice ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Those **Rbhus** who **made** their **parents**—their mother and father—**young again**, who had been **aged** and **lying** still **like posts** <note>original: *yupeva* — like the stumps of sacrificial posts or weathered pillars</note>, making them eternally youthful. Those three—named **Vaja, Vibhvan, and Rbhu**, the sons of Sudhanvan from the lineage of Angiras—being **accompanied by Indra** <note>original: *indravantah*</note> as their follower, and being **tasters of the sweetness** <note>original: *madhupsaraso* — drinkers of the sweet Soma juice or possessing beautiful forms</note>, may they **protect** <note>original: *avantu*</note>, guard, or come to **our sacrifice**.

**Because for a year the Rbhus guarded the cow; because for a year the Rbhus fashioned the flesh; because for a year they sustained its light; through those labors they attained immortality. ॥ ४ ॥**

**A year** <note>original: *samvatsam*</note>: The word *samvatsa* refers to a year because all beings "dwell" <note>original: *sam-vasanti*</note> within it. For the duration of a full year, the Rbhus **the cow**... <note>the commentary breaks off here and continues on the next page</note>

# Rig Veda [Book 3, Chapter 7, Section 2]

## Commentary (Sayana)

...they protected the dead or dying <note>original: *mṛtāmarakṣan*</note> parents by their own power <note>original: *svasāmarthyāt*</note>. During the **year** <note>original: *saṃvatsam*</note>, they fashioned the flesh <note>original: *māṃsamapiṃśan*</note> of that same cow, meaning they reconstructed its limbs. Furthermore, for the duration of the year, they brought forth its radiance <note>original: *bhāso'bharan*</note>, providing beauty to the limbs. Through those **works** <note>original: *śamībhir*</note>—namely the actions concerning the renewal of the dead cow—they **attained immortality** <note>original: *amṛtatvamāpuḥ*</note>. That is, they reached the state of divinity. This was promised by the gods as a means to attain divinity: "Make the cow." Alternatively, the phrase "for a year" should be interpreted as concluding the previous description.

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥<-

The **eldest** said, "Let us make **two cups**"; the **middle one** said, "Let us make **three**"; the **youngest** said, "Make **four**." **Tvashtri**, O **Rbhus**, praised that **speech** of yours. ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-for-word Breakdown:**
The eldest | said | cups | two | let us make | <note>iti - marks the end of a quote</note> | the middle one | three | let us make | <note>iti</note> | said | the youngest | said | four | make | <note>iti</note> | Tvashtri | Rbhus | that | praised | speech | of yours ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

> **"Divide the one cup into four"** <note>Rig Veda 1.161.2</note>. When the divine messenger Agni spoke thus to the Rbhus as a condition for attaining divinity, the **eldest** among them, desiring divinity, spoke to the others. What did he say? **"Let us make two cups"** <note>original: *camasā dvā kara*</note>. That is, let us make two from the one that exists. The **middle one** <note>original: *kanīyān* — the second brother, Vibhu</note> then said, **"let us make three"** <note>original: *trīn kṛṇavāma*</note>. The one below him, the **youngest** <note>original: *kaniṣṭha* — the third brother, Vaja</note>, said, **"make four"** <note>original: *caturaḥ kara*</note>, meaning "divide it fourfold." That very act of fourfold division, O <term>Rbhus</term> <note>celestial artisans</note>, your teacher <term>Tvashtri</term> <note>the divine smith and architect of the gods</note> **praised** <note>original: *panayat*</note>. He lauded it; that is, he accepted and approved of it.

->॥ Thus ends the first section (varga) of the seventh chapter (adhyaya) of the third book (ashtaka) ॥<-

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥<-

The **men** spoke the **truth**, for they indeed **did so**; the **Rbhus** followed this **offering**. **Tvashtri**, having seen the **four cups** shining like **days**, gazed upon them with favor. ॥ ६ ॥

**Word-for-word Breakdown:**
The truth | they spoke | the men | indeed | for | they did | followed | the offering | the Rbhus | went to/attained | this | shining | cups | days | like | gazed upon with favor | Tvashtri | four | having seen ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **men** <note>original: *naro* — here referring to the Rbhus who were originally human</note> spoke the **truth**. They said only what was true. **For** <note>original: *hi*</note> because of this, **they indeed did so**; they made the four cups. The meaning is that they performed exactly as they had spoken. **Following** <note>original: *anu*</note> after the fourfold division, the Rbhus **approached** this **offering** <note>original: *svadhām* — the sacrificial nectar called <term>Soma</term></note> belonging to the third libation. For it is heard in the sacred texts: "Divide the one cup into four; then you shall be worthy of sacrifice along with the gods." Then the divine Tvashtri, seeing the four cups shining like days—

<summary>This page describes the Rbhus' transformation into gods through two main feats: rejuvenating a cow (representing nature or the parents) and dividing the single sacrificial cup of the god Tvashtri into four. Tvashtri, initially skeptical or testing them, ultimately praises their craftsmanship, allowing them to share in the Soma offerings.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the 33rd hymn of the fourth Mandala of the Rig Veda. The previous page concluded the discussion of the Rbhus—divine artisans—and their miraculous act of dividing a single sacrificial cup into four, which earned them immortality and divinity. This page explores their rest at the house of the Sun and their creative powers regarding the natural world.</meta>

...the shining cups, like days <note>original: *ahānīva*</note>, making them four, he [the divine architect Tvashtri] accepted and desired them. This means he agreed to their work.

->|| Now the Seventh Verse ||<-

## Hymn Text
When for twelve days, O **Rbhus**, you took your pleasure while resting in the hospitality of the **Unconcealable** <note>The Sun, referred to as *Agohya*, the one who cannot be hidden</note>, you made the fields fertile, you led the rivers on their way; plants occupied the dry land, and waters the valleys. ॥ ७ ॥

**Word-for-word Breakdown:**
Twelve | days | when | of the Unconcealable | in the hospitality | rejoicing | Rbhus | resting | good fields | they made | they led | the rivers | dry land | upon | they stood | the plants | the low ground | the waters ॥ ७ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
Since it has been stated that the **Rbhus** <note>The Rbhus are often interpreted as solar rays or seasonal deities</note> are indeed the rays of the sun, they are praised in 그 that form here. "When" <note>original: *yat*</note> for "twelve days" <note>original: *dvādaśa dyūn*</note>—this refers to the twelve days of the rainy constellations beginning with Ardra. They stayed "in the hospitality" <note>original: *ātithye*</note> of the "Unconcealable" <note>original: *agohyasya*</note>, meaning the Sun (*Aditya*), in his house. An **Atithi** <note>term: guest (someone who arrives without a fixed date)</note> is a guest who arrives unexpectedly; the honor and service appropriate for such a guest is called *Atithya*. For that purpose, "resting" <note>original: *sasantaḥ*</note> or dwelling there comfortably, the Rbhus "rejoiced" <note>original: *raṇan*</note>. It is said elsewhere: "When, O Rbhus, you slept in the house of the Unconcealable" <note>Rig Veda 1.161.11</note>.

At that time, they "made the fields fertile" <note>original: *sukṣetrā-akṛṇvan*</note>; they made the empty, barren fields rich with crops and abundance through rain. They "led the rivers" <note>original: *sindhūn-anayanta*</note>, meaning they impelled them to flow. At that time, the "plants" <note>original: *oṣadhayaḥ*</note> "occupied the dry land" <note>original: *dhanva*</note>, growing in places previously lacking water. The "waters occupied the low ground" <note>original: *nimnam*</note> or the valleys. It is said elsewhere: "You have made grass for the heights and water for the depths."

---

->|| Now the Eighth Verse ||<-

## Hymn Text
Those who made the **well-rolling chariot** that carries the hero; those who made the **cow** that is all-impelling and multiform—may those **Rbhus** fashion wealth for us, they who are well-horsed, skillful, and deft-handed. ॥ ८ ॥

**Word-for-word Breakdown:**
Chariot | who | made | well-rolling | carrying the hero | who | the cow | all-impelling | multiform | they | may [they] fashion | Rbhus | wealth | for us | having good horses | having good works | having good hands ॥ ८ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **Rbhus** made a "well-rolling" <note>original: *suvṛtam*</note> chariot, meaning one with excellent wheels or one that functions perfectly, which "carries the hero" <note>original: *nareṣṭhām*</note>, standing firm for the leader or driver. They also made the "cow" <note>original: *dhenum*</note>—either the specific cow named **Vishvarupa** <note>term: "Multiform," often representing the earth or the source of all nourishment</note> or a cow that is "all-impelling" <note>original: *viśvajuvam*</note> (the stimulator of all) and "multiform" <note>original: *viśvarūpām*</note> (appearing in many colors or shapes). It is said: "Brihaspati brought forth the multiform cow" <note>Rig Veda 1.161.6</note>.

May those great Rbhus "fashion" <note>original: *ā takṣantu*</note> or produce "wealth" <note>original: *rayim*</note> for us from all sides. What are these Rbhus like? They are "skillful" <note>original: *svapasaḥ*</note>, performing good deeds; "well-horsed" <note>original: *svaśvasaḥ*</note>, possessing beautiful horses; and "deft-handed" <note>original: *suhastāḥ*</note>, having skillful hands for their crafts.

<meta>This page continues the 33rd hymn of the fourth Mandala of the Rig Veda, focusing on the Rbhus—divine artisans who were once mortal men but achieved divinity through their extraordinary skill. The previous page discussed their twelve-day stay at the house of the Sun (Agohya) and their mastery over the natural elements. This page details their specific association with the major gods—Indra, Varuna, and the collective pantheon—and their role in the third daily sacrifice.</meta>

-> ॥ Now the Ninth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
For the gods enjoyed their work, meditating with purposeful wisdom in their minds; **Vaja** became the gods’ artisan, **Rbhukshan** was **Indra’s**, and **Vibhvan** belonged to **Varuna**. ॥ ९ ॥

**Word-for-word Breakdown:**
The work | indeed | of these | they enjoyed | the gods | towards | with wisdom | with the mind | meditating | Vaja | of the gods | became | the skillful worker | Indra’s | Rbhukshan | Varuna’s | Vibhvan ॥ ९ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The gods, led by **Indra**, enjoyed the "work" <note>original: *apas*</note> of these **Rbhus**, which consisted of the construction of the sacrifice and the sacred rites. This means they accepted their work in the manner described in other verses—such as the creation of Indra’s two bay horses and the **Ashvins’** chariot. What was the nature of these gods? They were "meditating" <note>original: *abhidīdhyānāḥ*</note>, meaning they were shining with a gracious mind and through the act of granting boons. 

The text then explains what was gained through the gods' grace: **Vaja**, the youngest brother and a "skillful worker" <note>original: *sukarmā*</note>, became associated with all the gods. Similarly, **Rbhukshan**, the eldest of the **Rbhus**, became associated with **Indra**. And **Vibhvan**, the middle brother, became associated with **Varuna**.

---

-> ॥ Now the Tenth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
They who made the two bay horses for **Indra**, rejoicing with wisdom and songs of praise—those horses which are easy to harness—may you, O **Rbhus**, grant us abundance of wealth and riches, protecting us like a friend. ॥ १० ॥

**Word-for-word Breakdown:**
Who | the two bay horses | with wisdom | worthy of praise | rejoicing | for Indra | made | easy to harness | who | horses | they | of wealth | nourishment | riches | to us | grant | Rbhus | desiring well-being | like | a friend ॥ १० ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **Rbhus** created the two "bay horses" <note>original: *harī*</note> through their "wisdom" <note>original: *medhayā*</note> and while "rejoicing" <note>original: *madantaḥ*</note> or gladdening the gods with "songs of praise" <note>original: *ukthyā*</note>. They fashioned those horses specifically for **Indra** so they would be "easy to harness" <note>original: *suyujā*</note>. 

O **Rbhus**, you who did this, "grant" <note>original: *dhatta*</note> or bestow upon us the "nourishment of wealth" <note>original: *rāyaspoṣam*</note>, which includes cattle and other riches that lead to happiness. Do this like a "friend" <note>original: *mitram na*</note> who "desires the well-being" <note>original: *kṣemayantaḥ*</note> of another. Here, although there is only one brother specifically named **Rbhu**, the plural "Rbhus" is used to refer to all three brothers through the **logic of the vital breath** <note>term: *Prāṇabhṛn-nyāya* — a rule of interpretation where a group is named after its most prominent member or a shared vital characteristic</note>.

---

-> ॥ Now the Eleventh Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
They have placed the drinking and the joy of the day [in the sacrifice]; for the gods do not offer their friendship except to one who has labored. Therefore, O **Rbhus**, grant us riches now during this third libation. ॥ ११ ॥

**Word-for-word Breakdown:**
Now | of the day | the drinking | and | your | joy | they placed | not | without | the one who has labored | for friendship | the gods | they | surely | to us | Rbhus | riches | third | in this | libation | grant ॥ ११ ॥

<meta>This page concludes the commentary for the 34th hymn of the fourth Mandala and introduces the 35th hymn. It continues the story of the Rbhus—mortal artisans who became divine—specifically focusing on their right to drink the ritual Soma nectar alongside the primary gods like Indra.</meta>

<header>Mandala 4, Chapter 4, Hymn 34. ] || Third Book (Ashtaka) || 971</header>

## Commentary (Sayana) - End of Hymn 34
Now, following the construction of the [Soma] cups and other ritual items, on the day of the sacrifice, the gods gave the **Rbhus** the drinking of the Soma nectar and the resulting joy during the **third pressing** <note>original: *tṛtīye savane*; the final of three daily ritual offerings</note>. The gods do not grant their friendship to those who are not "weary"—meaning those who have not performed the exhausting toil of ascetic heat <note>original: *tapas*</note>. Because these **Rbhus** were weary from their sacred labors, the gods gave them this share. O great **Rbhus**, surely grant and hold within us riches <note>original: *vasūni*</note> during this third pressing.

-> || This concludes the second section (Varga) of the seventh chapter in the third Book (Ashtaka) || <-

---

## Commentary (Sayana) - Introduction to Hymn 35
The second hymn of this section, beginning with the words "Rbhu, Vibhvan," contains eleven verses. It was revealed to the Sage **Vamadeva**, is composed in the **Trishtubh** meter, and is dedicated to the **Rbhus** <note>original: *ārbhavam*</note>. The Index of Verses <note>original: *Anukramani*</note> confirms this. In the "Ten-Night" ritual ceremony <note>the *Dasharatra*</note>, specifically on the fifth day, this hymn is to be recited during the ritual of the Universal Gods <note>original: *vaiśvadeva-śastra*</note>. This is indicated by the ritual manuals which state: "Rbhu, Vibhvan, I praise the person." <note>original: *Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 8.8*</note>.

-> || Here is the first verse || <-

## Hymn Text
**Rbhu**, **Vibhvan**, **Vaja**, and **Indra**! Come toward this sacrifice of ours to bestow jewels. For now the divine **Goddess of Speech** <note>original: *dhiṣaṇā*</note> has prepared the drink for the days of Soma-pressing; the joys of the nectar have met with you. ॥ १ ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown (Pada-patha):**
**Rbhu** | **Vibhvan** | **Vaja** | **Indra** | our | toward | this | sacrifice | for the bestowing of jewels | come | now | indeed | your | **Goddess of Speech** | divine | the days [of pressing] | has placed | the drinking | together | the joys | have met | you ॥ १ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
May the gods **Rbhu**, **Vibhvan**, **Vaja**, and **Indra** come toward our sacrifice for the purpose of "bestowing jewels" <note>original: *ratnadheyāya*</note>, or giving us wealth. One might ask: **Indra** is the master of the Soma, so he should naturally come, but how do the others gain a place at the sacrifice? The text explains: "For now," indeed, the divine **Goddess of Speech**—who is associated with the Creator **Prajapati**—has established the drinking of the Soma for the days of the ritual pressing. 

The sacred prose of the **Aitareya Brahmana** <note>3.30</note> explains this: "Prajapati said to the Sun God **Savitar**: 'These **Rbhus** were your pupils; you must drink the Soma with them.'" Because of this divine decree, the "joys" or intoxications of the ritual drink have met with you all. Alternatively, it means your joys have joined with those of the other gods.

---

-> || Now the second verse || <-

## Hymn Text
Knowing your origins, O **Rbhus**, take delight together with the seasons. The joys have met with you, and so has the **Goddess of Abundance** <note>original: *puramdhiḥ*</note>. Bring toward us wealth that includes brave sons. ॥ २ ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown (Pada-patha):**
Knowing | of your birth | for the sake of wealth-jewels | and | with the seasons | O **Rbhus** | take delight | together | your | joys | have met | together | the **Goddess of Abundance** | with good heroes | in us | wealth | bring toward [us] ॥ २ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Rbhus**, you who are "knowing of your birth"—meaning you are aware of your own divine origin—rejoice together with the "seasons" <note>original: *ṛtubhiḥ*</note> or the deities presiding over the seasons. The joys of the sacrifice have met with you, as has **Puramdhi**, the goddess of abundance or multifaceted wisdom. Therefore, bring toward us—establish within us—wealth <note>original: *rayim*</note> that is "accompanied by good heroes" <note>original: *suvīrām*</note>, meaning it includes sons and grandsons who are brave.

It highlights the ritual use of these hymns and the blessings of wealth and heroic progeny requested by the worshippers.</summary>

<header>|| Rig Veda || [Book 3, Chapter 1, Section 3] || Page 172</header>

## Commentary (Sayana)
<note>Continuation of the commentary on the previous verse, Rig Veda 4.35.2</note>

O **Vajaratnas** <note>original: *vājaratnāḥ*; those who shine with the "wealth" of the Soma food</note>, you **Rbhus**, knowing <note>original: *vidānāso*</note> the **birth** <note>original: *janmano*</note> that is the attainment of your divine nature. Or rather, knowing the attainment of the Soma, even though you formerly possessed a human birth. And—the word **uta** <note>meaning "and"</note>—rejoice together with the Seasons <note>the *Rtus*, who are also deities of the sacrifice</note>. The **intoxications** <note>original: *madāḥ*; the exhilarating effects of the Soma</note> have **met** <note>original: *samagmata*</note> **with you**. Even the **abundance** <note>original: *purandhiḥ*; often interpreted as the goddess of plenty or the spirit of prayer</note> has met with you. May you **send** <note>original: *airayadhvam*</note> to **us** <note>original: *asme*</note> wealth that is accompanied by noble and heroic sons.

---

## Hymn Text

-> || Now, the Third Verse || <-

O Rbhus, this sacrifice has been performed for you, which you hold within yourselves like Manu, anciently luminous. Toward you, the Soma juices, being enjoyed, have stood forth; O Vibhvan and Vaja, you have become the foremost.

**Word-for-Word Breakdown:**
**This** [sacrifice]; **for you**; **sacrifice**; **O Rbhus**; **has been performed**; **which**; [preposition: **unto**]; **like Manu**; **anciently luminous**; **you hold**;
**forward**; **for you**; [preposition: **towards**]; **being enjoyed**; **they have stood forth**; **it has become**; [for] **Vibhvan**; **foremost**; **and**; **Vajas**.

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Rbhus**, **this sacrifice has been performed** <note>original: *ayaṃ yajño’kāri*</note> **for you** <note>original: *vaḥ*</note>. **Which** sacrifice you **hold** <note>original: *ā dadhidhve*</note> in your bellies, being **anciently luminous** <note>original: *pradivaḥ*</note> **like Manu** <note>original: *manuvat*; referring to the first human to perform a sacrifice</note>. For that purpose, the Soma juices, **being enjoyed** <note>original: *jujuṣāṇāḥ*</note> by you, **stand forth** <note>original: *pra asthuḥ*</note>—meaning they are established—directly toward **you**. **And also** <note>original: *utāpi*</note>, having held this sacrifice, O **Vajas** <note>one of the three Rbhu brothers</note> and **Vibhvan** <note>the second brother</note>, you all **have become** <note>original: *abhūt*</note> **foremost** <note>original: *agriyāḥ*; those worthy of the first rank or highest status</note>.

---

## Hymn Text

-> || Now, the Fourth Verse || <-

O Leaders, the bestowing of wealth has now become yours for the worshipper, for the mortal who gives. Drink, O Vajas, O Rbhus; I have given to you the great third pressing for your joy.

**Word-for-Word Breakdown:**
**It has become**; [particle for emphasis]; **for you**; **for the worshipper**; **the bestowing of wealth**; **now**; **O Leaders**; **for the giver**; **for the mortal**;
**Drink**; **O Vajas**; **O Rbhus**; **I have given**; **to you**; **the great**; **third**; **pressing**; **for joy**.

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Leaders** <note>original: *naro*; meaning "men" or "guides"</note>, O **Rbhus**, by your grace **now** at this **third pressing**, may the **bestowing of wealth** <note>original: *ratnadheyam*; the gift of jewels or precious things</note> **be** <note>original: *abhūt*</note> for the **mortal** <note>original: *martyāya*</note> **worshipper** <note>original: *vidhate*; one who serves with praise</note> and **giver** <note>original: *dāśuṣe*; the one offering the oblation</note>, meaning for me, the sacrificer. For that purpose, O **Vajas**, O **Rbhus**—these names here represent all three brothers, including Vibhvan, as the plural is used for each individually to include the others—you all **drink**. For this, **I have given to you** <note>original: *vo dade*</note>. What? The **great** <note>original: *mahi*</note> **third pressing** <note>original: *tṛtīyaṃ savanam*; the final Soma ritual of the day</note>, meaning the Soma juice associated with it. For what purpose? For **joy** <note>original: *madāya*; meaning exhilaration or total satisfaction</note>.

<summary>This page details two verses of a hymn to the Rbhus, celestial artisans who transitioned from mortals to gods. The text emphasizes their right to the "third pressing" of Soma and asks them to bestow wealth upon the human sacrificer, following the ancient precedent of the first sacrificer, Manu.</summary>

<header>Ma. 4. Adh. 4. Su. 34.] || Third Ashtaka || 193</header>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now, the fifth verse ॥ <-

O Vajas, O Ribhukshan, come to us! O great leaders, you who are praised for your wealth. Toward you, these drinks have gone at the close of day <note>original: *abhipitve*; referring to the evening/third pressing</note>, just as newly-calved cows hasten to their stalls. ॥ 5 ॥

**O Vajas | come | toward | us | Ribhukshan | great | leaders | wealthy | being praised |**
**toward | you | the drinks | at the close | of days | these | the stall | like newly-calved cows | have gone ॥ 5 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Vajas** and **Ribhukshan**, you who are **leaders** <note>original: *naraḥ*; literally "men" or "heroes," used here for the divine Ribhus</note>, come toward us. Doing what? **Praised for your wealth** <note>original: *draviṇasaḥ*; wealth or possessions</note>, that is, being celebrated while possessing great riches. Furthermore, **at the close of day**—meaning at the completion or the falling of the days—which refers to the Third Soma Pressing <note>The Vedic day is divided into three ritual pressings of the Soma plant; the Ribhus are specifically invited to the final evening session</note>. These **drinks** <note>the Soma libations</note> have **gone** toward **you**. A comparison <note>original: *dṛṣṭānta*</note> is given: **to the stall** <note>original: *astam*; a name for the home or cow-pen</note>, just as **newly-calved cows** <note>original: *navasvaḥ*; cows that have recently given birth and are eager to return to their calves</note> hasten home.

-> ॥ Thus ends the third section (varga) in the seventh chapter of the third book ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now, the sixth verse ॥ <-

O Sons of Might, come toward this sacrifice, being summoned with reverence. You are wise ones, dwelling in harmony with Indra; you who are associated with him, drink the sweet Soma, O bestowers of jewels. ॥ 6 ॥

**come | O Sons | of Might | come | toward | this | sacrifice | with reverence | being summoned |**
**with harmony | wise ones | of whom | and | you are | the sweet juice | drink | bestowers of jewels | accompanied by Indra ॥ 6 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Sons of Might** <note>original: *shavaso napātaḥ*; "napāt" can mean sons or those who do not let strength fall</note>, meaning you who are powerful or the children of strength. You, being **summoned** or called by this **reverence** <note>the hymn of praise</note>, come toward this **sacrifice**. What kind of beings are you? You are **wise ones** <note>original: *sūrayaḥ*; enlightened or scholarly</note> who are **in harmony** or pleased along with Indra. The connection between Indra and the Ribhus is explained: **of whom you are associated** <note>original: *yasya ca stha*</note>. This means you belong to Indra and are fittingly his companions because of the miraculous works you performed for him <note>The Ribhus famously crafted Indra’s chariot and his two bay horses</note>. Because of this, being **accompanied by Indra** and being **bestowers of jewels** <note>givers of beautiful riches</note>, you must **drink** the **sweet** Soma juice.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now, the seventh verse ॥ <-

O Indra, in harmony with Varuna, drink the Soma; O lover of song <note>original: *girvaṇo*</note>, in harmony with the Maruts; in harmony with the Adityas, the protectors of the seasons; in harmony with the goddesses, the wives of the gods, the bestowers of wealth. ॥ 7 ॥

<note>The following list provides the technical definitions for the terms used in the verses above.</note>

*   **Vajas** <note>original: *Vājāḥ*</note>: The Vajas (deities, one of the three Ribhu brothers).
*   **Ribhukshan** <note>original: *Ṛbhukṣāḥ*</note>: The eldest of the Ribhus; also a title for their chief.
*   **Wealth** <note>original: *Draviṇasaḥ*</note>: Possessions or riches granted to the worshiper.
*   **At the close of day** <note>original: *Abhipitve*</note>: In the evening or the completion of the ritual day.
*   **Sons/Descendants** <note>original: *Napātaḥ*</note>: Literally "grandsons," often used to mean "offspring of [a quality]."
*   **Of Might** <note>original: *Shavaso*</note>: Of strength or spiritual power.
*   **Harmonious** <note>original: *Sajoṣāḥ*</note>: Being in agreement or associated with other gods.
*   **Bestowers of jewels** <note>original: *Ratnadhāḥ*</note>: Those who hold or give precious things.
*   **Soma** <note>original: *Somam*</note>: The sacred libation offered in the fire.

<meta>This page continues the Rig Veda, Mandala 4, Sukta 33, which is dedicated to the Ribhus—divine artisans who attained immortality through their skill. While the previous page (referenced as Sukta 34 in your notes, though this text is Sukta 33) discussed their invitation to the evening sacrifice, this page specifies the various deities they accompany and lists their miraculous transformations of the natural world. <header>|| Rig Veda || [Book 3, Chapter 7, Class 4]</header>

## Hymn Text

<note>Rig Veda 4.33.7 Word-for-word breakdown (Pada-patha)</note>
**In harmony | Indra | with Varuna | the Soma | in harmony | protect | O singer | with the Maruts |**
**with the fire-drinkers | with the season-drinkers | in harmony | with the wives of the gods | with the wealth-bestowers | in harmony ॥ 7 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra**, being **in harmony** <note>original: *sajoṣāḥ*; having equal pleasure or shared affection</note> with **Varuna**, the deity who presides over sovereignty, **protect the Soma**. That is, drink it. O **singer** <note>original: *girvaṇas*; Indra, who is to be praised and served with songs</note>, being united **in harmony with the Maruts** <note>the storm gods</note>, **protect the Soma**. Drink it. Furthermore, drink it along with the **fire-drinkers** <note>original: *agnepābhiḥ*; those who drink first or alongside Agni</note>, the **season-drinkers** <note>original: *ṛtupābhiḥ*; the deities of the seasonal sacrifices</note>, and the **wives of the gods** <note>original: *gnāḥ-patnībhiḥ*; the Gnas are divine females or protectors of women</note>. The *Nirukta* <note>an ancient Vedic dictionary/etymology text</note> states that "Mena" and "Gna" are names for women. Drink with them. Also, with the **wealth-bestowers** <note>original: *ratnadhābhiḥ*; bestowers of delightful riches</note>, which refers to the seasons. Or perhaps this "wealth-bestowers" is an adjective describing the wives of the gods. Being in harmony with them, drink the Soma.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now, the eighth verse ॥ <-

<note>Rig Veda 4.33.8 Full Verse (Samhita)</note>
**In harmony with the Adityas, rejoice; in harmony, O Ribhus, with the mountains.**
**In harmony with the divine Savitar; in harmony with the rivers, the bestowers of wealth. ॥ 8 ॥**

<note>Rig Veda 4.33.8 Word-for-word breakdown (Pada-patha)</note>
**In harmony | with the Adityas | rejoice | in harmony | O Ribhus | with the mountains |**
**in harmony | with the divine | Savitar | in harmony | with the rivers | with the wealth-bestowers ॥ 8 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Ribhus**, being united **in harmony with the Adityas** <note>the solar deities</note>, may you **rejoice**. Likewise, **rejoice in harmony with the mountains** <note>original: *parvatebhiḥ*; refers to the mountain-gods or specific deities worshipped at the 'nodes' (parva) or seasonal transitions</note>. Furthermore, **rejoice in harmony with the divine Savitar** <note>the solar Impeller</note>, who is beneficial to the gods, and with the **rivers** <note>original: *sindhubhiḥ*; the personified flowing waters</note> who are **bestowers of wealth** and are flowing by nature.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now, the ninth verse ॥ <-

<note>Rig Veda 4.33.9 Full Verse (Samhita)</note>
**Those who [fashioned] the Ashvins, those who the parents, those who with aid fashioned the cow, the Ribhus who [fashioned] the horses;**
**Those who [fashioned] the limbs, and those who separately [fashioned] the two worlds, they who as all-pervading leaders performed deeds of good offspring. ॥ 9 ॥**

<note>Rig Veda 4.33.9 Word-for-word breakdown (Pada-patha)</note>
**Those | the Ashvins | those | the parents | those | with aid | the cow | fashioned | the Ribhus | those | the horses |**
**those | the limbs | those | separately | the two worlds | those | all | leaders | good-offspring-deeds | performed ॥ 9 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Those** Ribhus who pleased the **Ashvins** <note>the divine twins</note> with their **aid** <note>original: *ūtī*; an act such as the construction of their chariot</note>. **And those who fashioned the parents**—meaning through the act of "carving" or reshaping, they **made** their aged parents young again with their **aid**. **And those who fashioned the cow** by making it new again after it had died. **And those who fashioned the horses**. It has been said elsewhere: "With their skills, they formed the cow from a hide, and they made the two who were old to be young again." And those who [fashioned] the limbs—

<note>The text breaks off here at the end of the page.</note>

<vocab>
Indra: King of the gods; Varuna: God of cosmic order; Ribhavas: The divine craftsmen (Ribhus); Maruts: Storm deities; Adityas: Solar deities; Savitar: The sun as the source of life/impulsion; Ashvins: Twin physicians of the gods; Ratnadha: Givers of wealth/jewels; Gna: Divine female/wives of gods; Soma: The sacred ritual drink; Rtupa: Deities who drink according to the seasons; Rodasi: Heaven and Earth.
</vocab>

<header>Mandala 4, Adhyaya 4, Sukta 35.] || Third Ashtaka || 175</header>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Tenth Verse ॥ <-

**Those who bestow wealth rich in cattle, rich in food, accompanied by noble heroes, possessing treasures, and full of much nourishment—those Rbhus, as the first-drinkers, being joyful, bestow wealth upon us and upon those who praise your gift. ॥ 10 ॥**

**Those | rich in cattle | rich in food | with noble heroes | wealth | you bestow | possessing treasures | full of nourishment |**
**Those | first-drinkers | O Rbhus | being joyful | upon us | bestow | who | and | the gift | praise ॥ 10 ॥**

-> ॥ The Eleventh Verse ॥ <-

**Do not be absent, O Rbhus; we have not let you remain thirsty. You are un-reproached at this sacrifice. Rejoice together with Indra, with the Maruts, and with the kings, O gods, for the bestowing of treasures. ॥ 11 ॥**

**Not | away | be | not | you | have we let be thirsty | un-reproached | O Rbhus | sacrifice | in this |**
**Together | with Indra | rejoice | together | with the Maruts | together | with the kings | for the bestowing of treasures | O gods ॥ 11 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

...They made armors <note>original: kavacāni</note> for the gods. And those who made the two worlds—heaven and earth—separate from each other. In this described manner, those Rbhus, who are the pervasive <note>original: vibhvaḥ</note> leaders <note>original: naraḥ</note>, performed deeds <note>original: karmāṇi</note> that were the means of their own success or the means of attaining that status. The phrase "those first-drinkers" connects to what follows. <note>This paragraph completes the commentary on the previous verse, verse 9.</note>

-> ॥ The Tenth Verse ॥ <-

O **Rbhus**, you who **hold** <note>original: dhattha</note> or possess for the purpose of giving to me **wealth** <note>original: rayim</note> that is **rich in cattle** <note>original: gomantaṃ</note>, **rich in food** <note>original: vājavantam</note>, **accompanied by noble heroes** <note>original: suvīram</note> (meaning excellent sons), **possessing treasures** <note>original: vasumantam</note> (such as houses and lands suitable for dwelling), and **full of much nourishment** <note>original: purukṣum</note> (abundant food)—O you **Rbhus**, being the **first-drinkers** <note>original: ayepāḥ</note> and **being joyful** <note>original: mandasānāḥ</note> or intoxicated with delight, **bestow** <note>original: dhatta</note>—give—that wealth **upon us** <note>original: asme</note>. Furthermore, bestow it upon those **who praise** <note>original: gṛṇanti</note> the **gift** <note>original: rātiṃ</note> given, or the Soma. Alternatively, bestow it upon the patrons <note>sacrificers</note> who praise the gift.

-> ॥ The Eleventh Verse ॥ <-

O **Rbhus**, you **do not be absent** <note>original: na apābhūta</note>. Do not go away; do not be those who are excluded. And **we** have **not let you remain thirsty** <note>original: na atītṛṣāma</note>; we have not made you excessively thirsty. Therefore, O **Rbhus**, you **gods**, being **un-reproached** <note>original: aniḥśastāḥ</note> or blameless, **rejoice together** <note>original: saṃ madatha</note> **in this sacrifice** with **Indra**. Rejoice with the **kings** <note>original: rājabhiḥ</note>, the other shining deities. Be satisfied. For what purpose? **For the bestowing of treasures** <note>original: ratnadheyāya</note>, which means the granting of delightful wealth.

-> ॥ Thus ends the fourth class (varga) in the seventh section (adhyaya) of the third book (ashtaka) ॥ <-

The third hymn beginning with "Come here" <note>original: iha upa yāta</note> has nine verses. Its seer <note>rsi</note> is Vamadeva, its meter is Trishtubh, and it is addressed to the Rbhus. This is the sequence according to the index <note>original: anukramaṇikā</note>. During the Third Pressing <note>original: tṛtīyasavane</note>, this hymn is to be recited by the Maitravaruna priest <note>one of the main officiating priests</note> when the Soma is being brought forward. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "Let the horses bring you... Come here," as per the sequence of the pressings <note>original: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 5. 5.</note>.

**Purukshu** (possessing much food or nourishment)
**Gomat** (rich in cattle/cows, a primary measure of Vedic wealth)
**Vajavat** (rich in food or strength)
**Mandasana** (rejoicing or delighted by the ritual drink)
**Yajna** (sacrifice or ritual ceremony)
</vocab>

->॥ Here is the First Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**Come here, O sons of power <note>original: śavaso napātaḥ</note>, sons of Sudhanvan, O Ribhus, do not be absent. Indeed, at this ritual libation <note>original: savana</note>, may the intoxications <note>original: madāsaḥ; referring to the Soma juice</note> that bestow wealth reach Indra following after you. ॥ 1 ॥**

**Here | Near | Come | Of power | Sons | Sons of Sudhanvan | O Ribhus | Not | Away | Be |**
**In this | Indeed | Your | Ritual libation | Bestowing of wealth | May they go | Indra | Following | Your | Intoxications ॥ 1 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **sons of power**, meaning sons of strength or those who do not let strength perish; O **sons of Sudhanvan** <note>the father of the Ribhus</note>; O **Ribhus**, you all **come here**. Approach this third **ritual libation** <note>original: savane; the Soma offerings are typically performed three times a day</note>. **Do not be absent**; do not be those who have gone away. At this ritual libation, following after Indra who is the giver of **the bestowing of wealth** <note>original: ratnadheyam</note> (delightful riches), may **your intoxications**—the exhilarating Soma juices—**go** <note>reach the goal</note>. Or, the word **following** <note>original: anu</note> may be connected to the action: the meaning being, "let them come after Indra and you." The word **indeed** <note>original: hi</note> is a rhythmic filler.

---

->॥ Now the Second Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**The bestowing of wealth by the Ribhus has come here; the drinking of the well-pressed Soma has taken place. For, with skillful work <note>original: sukṛtyayā</note> and with a desire for good craftsmanship <note>original: svapasyayā</note>, you made the one drinking vessel <note>original: camasam</note> into four. ॥ 2 ॥**

**Near | Has come | Of the Ribhus | Here | The bestowing of wealth | Has been | Of Soma | Of the well-pressed | The drinking |**
**By skillful work | Since | By good craftsmanship | And | The one | Being | Vessel | Fourfold ॥ 2 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **bestowing of wealth** by you **Ribhus**—the giving of jewels—**has come** to me here at the third ritual libation. Or, the wealth called Soma belonging to you has come. Because of this, the **drinking** of the **well-pressed Soma has taken place**; meaning, it was received by Prajapati <note>the Lord of Creatures</note>. If you ask how that happened, it is explained: **Since** by your **skillful work**—the beautiful movement of your hands—**and** by your **good craftsmanship**—the desire for deeds such as constructing the beautiful chariot—you **made** the **one vessel** that existed into **four**.

---

->॥ Now the Third Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**You made the drinking vessel fourfold; the friend <note>perhaps Agni or a fellow artisan</note> spoke, "Do teach us." Then, O Ribhus, O skilled-handed ones, you went to the path of immortality, the assembly of the gods. ॥ 3 ॥**

**Apart | You made | Vessel | Fourfold | Friend | Apart | Teach | So | He spoke |**
**Then | You went | O Vajas <note>the youngest of the three Ribhus, here used for all</note> | Of immortality | The path | The assembly | Of the gods | O Ribhus | Skilled-handed ॥ 3 ॥**

<meta>This page continues the commentary and text of Mandala 4, Sukta 35, dedicated to the Ribhus—divine artisans who attained immortality through their skill.
