[Page 197]

## Commentary (Sayana)
<note>Conclusion of Commentary on Rig Veda 4.41.1</note>

O **Indra**, O **Varuna**, O **Indra-Varuna**! <note>The commentator notes the use of the dual grammatical form to address both deities together.</note> For you two, what **hymn of praise** <note>original: "stoma"</note>, accompanied by **offerings** <note>original: "havishmana"</note>—that is, containing materials to be offered such as Soma-juice, clarified butter, and so on—has attained comfort or happiness? The meaning is: which hymn shall attain its goal? 

Alternatively, the word "possessing offerings" should be linked to the next part. Like the **Invoker-Fire** <note>original: "hota-agni"</note> who possesses offerings, who is immortal, and who is the means to reach heaven—likewise, O Indra-Varuna, may this hymn, which is wise, filled with respect, and arising from us, touch your heart. May it reach your heart. The question "which one?" is asked to praise the quality of the hymn.

---

## Hymn Text
->|| Now the Second ||<-

**Indra** and **Varuna**, the **mortal** who makes you his **kinsmen** for the sake of **friendship**, he who brings **offerings**; he destroys **sins** in the clash of **battles**, and he destroys **enemies**. Through your great **protections**, he becomes **renowned**. || 2 ||

**Word-for-word analysis:**
**Indra**; indeed; who; **Varuna**; has made; **kinsmen**; the two gods; **mortal**; for **friendship**; possessing **offerings**.
He; **slays**; **sins** <note>original: "vritra," often meaning obstacles or sins in this context</note>; in **battles**; **enemies**; with **protections**; or; **great**; he; is **heard of**. || 2 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra-Varuna**, the two gods! That **mortal** <note>original: "marta," one who is subject to death</note> who possesses food in the form of offerings, and who makes you two his **kinsmen** <note>original: "api"</note> for the sake of **friendship** <note>original: "sakhyaya"</note>—that mortal destroys **sins** <note>original: "papani"</note> which envelop or obstruct him. Likewise, he slays **enemies** in **battles** <note>original: "samitheshu"</note>. The word "or" <note>original: "va"</note> here acts as "and." Through your great **protections** <note>original: "avobhi," acts of guarding or help</note>, that man is "greatly heard of" <note>original: "pra shrutve"</note>. This means he becomes famous and distinguished.

---

## Hymn Text
->|| Now the Third ||<-

O **Indra** and **Varuna**, you two are the greatest **givers** of **wealth** to the **men** who **praise** you. When the two of you, as **friends**, are **delighted** by the **pressed Soma-juices** and fine **offerings** for the sake of **friendship**. || 3 ||

**Word-for-word analysis:**
**Indra**; indeed; **wealth**; **Varuna**; **greatest givers**; thus; to **men**; **praising**; those two.
If; **friends**; for **friendship**; with **Soma-juices**; **pressed**; with fine **offerings**; they are **delighted**. || 3 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra-Varuna**! You two are famous. Those two gods indeed, in this manner, are the **greatest givers** <note>original: "dheshtha"</note> of **lovely wealth** <note>original: "ratnam"</note> to us, the **men** who are **praising** <note>original: "shashamanebhya"</note> you. It is understood that "you become so." If you two, who are **friends** <note>original: "sakhaya"</note> to each other or to the worshiper, are **delighted** <note>original: "madayete"</note> with the **pressed Soma-juices** <note>original: "sutebhih somaih"</note> and excellent food for the purpose of the **act of friendship**, then you become the bestowers of treasures.

<note>
**Technical Terms:**
- **Indra-Varuna:** A dual deity representing both the kingly power of the storm and the cosmic order of the waters/heavens.
- **Soma:** A sacred ritual drink offered to the gods.
- **Ratna:** While literally "jewel," in the Rig Veda it often refers to any delightful treasure or spiritual gift.
</note>

# Rig Veda | Book 3, Chapter 7, Varga 16

-> ॥ Now the Fourth || <-

## Hymn Text
O **Indra** and **Varuna**, strike down upon this enemy with your most powerful, shining **thunderbolt**; O fierce ones, use your weapon! May your overcoming strength be directed against him who is **evil-minded**, **wolf-like** in his greed, and **harmful** to us. || 4 ||

**Word-for-word analysis:**
**Indra**; you two; **Varuna**; **shining weapon** <note>original: "didyu"</note>; against this (enemy); **most powerful** <note>original: "ojishtha"</note>; **fierce ones**; down; **strike**; **thunderbolt** <note>original: "vajra"</note>.
Who; our; **evil-acting**; **wolf-like/thief** <note>original: "vrikati"</note>; **harmer**; against him; **exercise**; **overcoming**; **strength** <note>original: "ojas"</note>. || 4 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Indra** <note>original: "Indrau"</note> and **Varuna** <note>original: "Varunau"</note>, O **fierce ones** <note>original: "ugrau"</note>. Here, the dual grammatical form is used throughout to address the two deities together, similar to the phrase "Before the two friends, Mitra and Varuna" <note>original: "pra mitrayorvarunayoh," Rig Veda 7.66.1</note>. Alternatively, the ending may be modified due to Vedic poetic license. Against **this** enemy, **strike down** <note>original: "ni vadhishtam"</note>—meaning, impel for the purpose of killing—the **shining** <note>original: "didyu"</note> and **most powerful** <note>original: "ojishtham"</note> or excessively brilliant **thunderbolt** weapon. **Against him**, the enemy who is **evil-minded** <note>original: "dureva"</note> or difficult to reach, who is **wolf-like** <note>original: "vrikati"</note> meaning one who takes excessively or a thief, and who is a **harmer** <note>original: "dabhiti"</note> or injurer of us—against such an enemy, **exercise** <note>original: "mimatham"</note>, meaning perform or create, your **overcoming strength** <note>original: "abhibhuti ojah"</note>.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fifth || <-

## Hymn Text
O **Indra** and **Varuna**, may you two be the **gratifiers** of this **prayer**, like two **bulls** toward a **cow**. May she, like a **great cow** with a **thousand streams** of milk, yield her bounty to us after having gone to the **pasture**. || 5 ||

**Word-for-word analysis:**
**Indra**; you two; **Varuna**; **be**; of this; **prayer/hymn**; **gratifiers**; like **bulls**; of a **cow**.
She; to us; **may she milk**; like to **grass/pasture**; **having gone**; **thousand-streamed**; with **milk**; **great**; **cow**. || 5 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Indra-Varuna**, may **you two** **be** <note>original: "bhutam"</note> the **gratifiers** <note>original: "pretara"</note> or pleasers **of this prayer** <note>original: "asya dhiyah"</note>—that is, this hymn of praise. Be like two **bulls** who are the fertilizers **of a cow**. May **she**, this prayer in the form of a cow, **milk** <note>original: "duhiyat"</note> for us; that is, may she fulfill our desires. Just as a **great cow**, having **gone** to the **pasture** <note>original: "yavasa"</note> to eat grass and other fodder, returns as a **thousand-streamed** vessel of **milk**, so may this prayer be for us.

-> ॥ Thus ends the fifteenth section (Varga) of the seventh chapter of the third Book (Ashtaka) ॥ <-

---

-> ॥ Now the Sixth || <-

## Hymn Text
When **offspring** is granted, when **progeny** is born, in the **fertile fields**, and for the **beholding of the sun**, and in the **manly deeds** of the **strong**; O **Indra** and **Varuna**, may you be **here** with your **protections** for us, O **skillful ones**, in the **approaching danger**. || 6 ||

**Word-for-word analysis:**
In **offspring** <note>original: "toka"</note>; **granted**; in **progeny** <note>original: "tanaya"</note>; in **fertile lands**; in the **sun**; in **beholding**; of the **strong/vigorous**; and; in **manly strength**; 
**Indra**; our; **here**; **Varuna**; **may you two be**; with **protections**; **skillful ones**; in the **approaching danger/battle** <note>original: "paritakmyayam"</note>. || 6 ||

<vocab>
<term>Indra-Varuna</term>: A dual deity (dvandva) combining the king of gods and the guardian of cosmic order.
<term>Vajra</term>: The thunderbolt weapon of Indra, representing divine power.
<term>Dhenu</term>: A cow; frequently used in the Vedas as a metaphor for a prayer that "milks" or yields blessings.
<term>Ojas</term>: Vital energy or overcoming strength.
<term>Dabhiti</term>: A term for a harmer or enemy; also the name of a specific king in some Vedic contexts.
<term>Yavasa</term>: Fresh grass or pastureland.
<term>Toka / Tanaya</term>: Terms referring to children and grandchildren, often translated as offspring and progeny.
</vocab>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Rig Veda, Mandala 4, Hymn 41, addressed to the dual deity Indra-Varuna. The previous page began the commentary on Verse 6; this page concludes that commentary and provides the full text, word-analysis, and Sayana’s explanation for Verses 7 and 8.</meta>

# Mandala 4, Hymn 4, Verse 41 | Book 3 | Page 199

...O Gods **Indra** and **Varuna**, for our benefit, regarding our offspring <note>original: "toke"</note>—our children and their children—and in our fertile, crop-rich lands, may you be present so that we may long behold the **Sun** <note>original: "sūraḥ"</note>, the impeller. This means grant us a long life. Likewise, for the virility and procreative strength of me, the sacrificer, may you two—as destroyers of enemies—be present with your protections during the night <note>original: "paritakmyāyām," interpreted as the time when dangers circulate</note> to slay those who would harm us in the dark.

---

->॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
We choose you two alone for our ancient protection, O seekers of cattle and **good kinsmen**. We seek your dear friendship; O heroes, most generous and beneficent, you are like **parents** to us. || 7 ||

**Padapatha:**
You two; alone; indeed; for protection; for the ancient; [around/fully]; the two powerful ones; seekers of cattle; **good kinsmen** <note>original: "su-āpī"</note>.
We choose; for friendship; for the dear; heroes; most generous; **like parents**; the two who cause happiness. || 7 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Indra** and **Varuna**, we who desire cattle <note>original: "gaviṣaḥ"</note> choose you two alone. The particle *hi* <note>meaning 'indeed'</note> is used here to complete the poetic meter. We choose you for that ancient protection which has been granted by you both. You are the two powerful ones and **good kinsmen** <note>original: "svāpī"</note>—the word *āpi* signifies a kinsman or relative. Alternatively, it means those who are well-pervading. You are heroes of great valor and most worshipful; we pray for your friendship and your dear company. You are the producers of happiness <note>original: "śambhū"</note>, just as **parents** are toward their son.

---

->॥ Now the Eighth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
O **bounteous givers**, those prayers of mine, desiring wealth and seeking you, have reached you for protection as if in a race. My praises have come to **Indra** and **Varuna** like cows approaching the **Soma** for the sake of beauty. || 8 ||

**Padapatha:**
Those; of you two; prayers; for protection; desiring wealth/strength; a race/battle; as if; they have gone; seeking you two; **bounteous givers** <note>original: "su-dānū"</note>.
For beauty; as if; cows; near; **Soma**; they stood; **Indra**; praises; **Varuna**; my; prayers. || 8 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **deities** who give excellent rewards <note>original: "sudānū"</note>, our prayers <note>original: "dhiyaḥ"</note>, which desire wealth <note>original: "vājayantīḥ"</note>, have reached you. These prayers seek you <note>original: "yuvayuḥ"</note> just as wives seek their husbands, or as competitors hasten toward a race <note>original: "ājim"</note>. Furthermore, my prayers <note>original: "manīṣāḥ"</note> and praises, which are the lords of the mind, stand before **Indra** and **Varuna** to please them. They approach the gods just as cows <note>original: "gāvaḥ"</note> approach the **Soma** juice to be mixed with it <note>Milk is traditionally mixed with Soma</note> for the sake of beauty or excellence <note>original: "śriye"</note>.

<summary>This page concludes the commentary on Verse 6 and presents Verses 7 and 8 of Rig Veda 4.41, emphasizing the protective, parental nature of Indra and Varuna and the way prayers reach them like racers or cattle.</summary>
<keywords>Indra-Varuna, protection, kinsmen, cattle (gaviṣaḥ), Soma, Sayana, Vedic sacrifice, parents (pitara), prayers (dhiyaḥ)</keywords>

# Mandala 4, Hymn 41 | Book 3 | Page 200

-> || Now the Ninth Verse || <-

## Hymn Text
These prayers of mine, desiring wealth, have approached **Indra** and **Varuna**. They have stood near them like devoted servants <note>original: "joṣṭāraḥ"</note> seeking riches from a master, or like swift ones <note>original: "raghvīḥ"</note> begging for fame and sustenance <note>original: "śravasaḥ"</note>. || 9 ||

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
These; to Indra; to Varuna; my; prayers; they have gone; near; wealth; desiring.
Near; indeed; they stood; like servants; of wealth; like swift ones; for fame/food; begging. || 9 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
My prayers or praises <note>original: "manīṣāḥ stutayaḥ"</note>, being seekers of wealth, have approached **Indra** and **Varuna**. They approach just as servants <note>original: "joṣṭāraḥ sevakāḥ"</note> approach a wealthy master to obtain riches <note>original: "vasvo dhanasya lābhāya dhanikaṃ svāminam-iva"</note>. Like swift ones <note>original: "raghvīr-iva"</note>—meaning light or quick-moving prayers—begging for food <note>original: "śravaso’nnasya"</note>, they stand near this Indra and Varuna to serve them.

---

## Hymn Text

-> || Now the Tenth Verse || <-
May we, by our own spirit <note>original: "tmanā"</note>, become masters of wealth consisting of horses, of chariots, of nourishment, and of eternal riches. May those two gods, performing deeds with newest protections, cause horses and wealth to be joined with us. || 10 ||

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Consisting of horses; by self/spirit; of chariots; of nourishment; of eternal; of wealth; masters; may we be.
Those two; performing; with protections; with newest; among us; riches; horses; may they join/serve. || 10 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
May we, by our own selves <note>original: "tmanātmandā"</note>—that is, naturally and without strenuous effort—become masters of wealth consisting of herds of horses <note>original: "aśvyāśva-samūhasya"</note>, of the form of chariots or suitable for chariots <note>original: "rathyasya"</note>, of the increase of nourishment, and of eternal or unwavering <note>original: "nityasyā-vicalitasya"</note> riches. May those two gods, who are the "goers" or active ones <note>original: "cakrāṇā"</note>, be present. With newest or most modern protections <note>original: "navyasībhir-ūtibhiḥ"</note>, let the horses <note>original: "niyutaḥ"</note> and the riches <note>original: "rāyo dhanāni"</note> serve or accompany us.

---

## Hymn Text

-> || Now the Eleventh Verse || <-
O Great Ones, come to us with great protections, O **Indra** and **Varuna**, in the winning of the prize <note>original: "vāja-sātau"</note>. Where the arrows <note>original: "didyavaḥ"</note> play in the midst of battles, may we be the winners of that prize in the conflict. || 11 ||

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
To; us; the two Great Ones; with great; protections; Indra; come; Varuna; in the winning of the prize.
Where; the arrows; in battles; play; of that; of you two; may we be; the winners; of the conflict. || 11 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Great Ones <note>original: "bṛhantā mahāntau"</note>, O **Indra**, O **Varuna**, come along with your great protections. In the winning of the prize <note>term: Vājasāti (a compound of 'vāja' meaning food/wealth and 'sāti' meaning gain; often refers to battle as the means of acquisition)</note>, which refers to a battle fought for the sake of obtaining sustenance, [come to us]. Where in this battle... <note>The commentary ends mid-sentence on this page.</note>

While Hymn 41 was a prayer to the dual deity Indra-Varuna for victory, Hymn 42 begins with a remarkable "Self-Praise" (Atma-stuti) by the King Trasadasyu, who speaks as an incarnation or representative of the divine sovereign Varuna.</meta>

# Mandala 4, Section 4, Hymn 42 | Book 3 | Page 201

## Commentary (Sayana) — Continued
...in battle <note>original: "saṃgrāme"</note>, among the ranks of armies <note>original: "pṛtanāsu"</note>, the missiles <note>original: "didyavaḥ"</note>—this is a name for weapons—the weapons belonging to the enemy play about. May we be the winners <note>original: "sanitāraḥ"</note> or enjoyers of such a struggle through the grace of you two [Indra and Varuna].

->**॥ Thus ends the sixteenth varga of the seventh adhyaya of the third book ॥**<-

The tenth hymn, beginning with "Mama dvita," consists of ten verses. The seer is the royal sage <term>Trasadasyu</term> <note>a famous king of the Puru dynasty</note>, son of Purukutsa. Because he praises himself in the first six verses, the "Self" <note>original: "ātmā"</note> is the deity. For the remaining four verses, **Indra** and **Varuna** are the deities. The meter is **Trishtubh**. So says the Index <note>original: "Anukramaṇikā"</note>: "Mama dvita, ten verses, Trasadasyu son of Purukutsa, the first six are self-praise." The ritual application <note>original: "viniyoga"</note> was mentioned in the previous hymn.

---

## Hymn Text

->**॥ Now the First Verse ॥**<-

Mine is the sovereignty <note>original: "rāṣṭram"</note> of the warrior <note>original: "kṣatriyasya"</note>, of the lord of all life, in two ways—just as all the immortals are ours. The gods follow the will <note>original: "kratum"</note> of Varuna; I rule over the people of the highest form. || 1 ||

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Mine; in two ways; sovereignty; of the warrior; of the lord of all life; all; immortals; as; ours.**
**The will/action; they follow; of Varuna; the gods; I rule; of the people; of the highest; of the form.** || 1 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Of the warrior <note>original: "kṣatriyasya"</note>—born of the warrior caste. Of the lord of all life <note>original: "viśvāyoḥ"</note>—the master of all human beings. The word "Mine" <note>original: "mama"</note> is a reference to the speaker's self. In two ways <note>original: "dvitā"</note>—meaning the sovereignty <note>original: "rāṣṭram"</note> has attained a double state, divided between earth and heaven. The meaning is: just as all the immortal gods belong to us, so too do the kingdom and the subjects belong to me, Trasadasyu. All the gods follow or serve the work <note>original: "kratum"</note> of the form <note>original: "vavreḥ"</note>—this is a word for "form" or "body"—of me, who possesses the nature of **Varuna** the Enveloper, and who is the closest <note>original: "upamasya"</note> to all. And I rule <note>original: "rājāmi"</note>—the root *rāj* implies lordship. I am the lord of all. Alternatively, it can be joined as: "I rule over the people of the highest form."

---

## Hymn Text

->**॥ Now the Second Verse ॥**<-

I am King **Varuna**; for me were these first lordly powers <note>original: "asuryāṇi"</note> established. The gods follow the will of Varuna; I rule over the people of the highest form. || 2 ||

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**I; King; Varuna; for me; those; lordly/divine powers; first; they established.**
**The will/action; they follow; of Varuna; the gods; I rule; of the people; of the highest; of the form.** || 2 ||

---

<summary>This page concludes the previous hymn's commentary and begins Hymn 42, where King Trasadasyu proclaims his divine sovereignty and identity with the god Varuna. The text establishes his rule over both heaven and earth, asserting that even the gods follow his will.</summary>

<keywords>Trasadasyu, Varuna, sovereignty (rashtra), warrior (kshatriya), divine power (asurya), self-praise (atma-stuti), Sayana, Rig Veda</keywords>

--- Page 268 ---
<meta>This page continues the "Self-Praise" (Atma-stuti) of King Trasadasyu, who identifies himself with the highest deities, Indra and Varuna. On the previous page, he asserted his royal sovereignty and his role as a lord of life. Here, he describes his role in the creation and maintenance of the cosmos, mirroring the acts of the gods.</meta>

I myself become the king <term>Varuna</term>. For me, and for my sake alone, the gods held those first, principal, and famous powers <note>original: "asuryāṇi"</note> which are capable of destroying the enemies of the gods <note>original: "asura-vighātakāni"</note>. The rest is as previously stated.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

I am **Indra**, I am **Varuna**; by my greatness, I [support] these two wide, deep, well-founded regions. Like the divine artisan **Tvashtri**, I, knowing all beings, have set in motion the two worlds and I support them. || 3 ||

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**I; Indra; Varuna; by [my] greatness; wide; deep; two regions; well-founded; like Tvashtri; all; beings; knowing; set in motion; the two worlds; and; support.**

## Commentary (Sayana)

I, King <term>Trasadasyu</term>, am also **Indra**. I am also **Varuna**. By my greatness <note>original: "mahitvā"</note>, I encompass the two regions <note>original: "rajasī"</note>, meaning Heaven and Earth, which are wide <note>original: "urvī"</note>, deep <note>original: "gambhīre"</note> or difficult to fathom, and well-formed <note>original: "sumeke"</note>. Knowing all, I, like the creator-artisan <term>Tvashtri</term> <note>the divine architect of the universe</note>, have set in motion <note>original: "samairayam"</note> or prompted all beings. I have also supported <note>original: "dhārayam"</note> the two worlds <note>original: "rodasī"</note> of Heaven and Earth. I have held them firm.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

I made the sprinkling waters swell; I support the sky in the seat of **Order**. By **Order**, the son of **Aditi**, the observer of **Order**, spread out the three-fold earth. || 4 ||

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**I; the waters; made swell; sprinkling; support; the sky; in the seat; of Order; by Order; the son; of Aditi; the observer of Order; and; three-fold; spread out; extensively; the earth.**

## Commentary (Sayana)

I alone caused the sprinkling or showering waters <note>original: "ukṣamāṇāḥ"</note> to swell <note>original: "apinvam"</note> or flow. Likewise, in the seat <note>original: "sadane"</note> or place of **Order** <note>original: "ṛtasya"</note>—which can mean water or the Sun—I support the sky. Alternatively, this means I hold the Sun in the sky, which is the source of water. By the cause of this Order, I became the son of **Aditi** <note>referring here to Varuna</note> and the observer of Order <note>original: "ṛtāvā"</note>. Furthermore, the pervasive expanse of the earth <note>original: "bhūma"</note> was spread out in a three-fold manner <note>original: "tridhātu"</note>. For my sake, the Supreme Lord created the three worlds, beginning with the Earth.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

Me the heroes with fine horses, seeking spoils, call upon; me do the warriors call when they are surrounded in battle. I, the bountiful **Indra**, create the contest; I, whose strength is overwhelming, stir up the dust. || 5 ||

<vocab>
- **Indra**: The King of the gods, associated with storms, war, and supreme vitality.
- **Varuna**: The guardian of cosmic law and the celestial waters; the judge of truth.
- **Trasadasyu**: A legendary king who, in this hymn, speaks as if he is the embodiment of the gods themselves.
- **Order (Rita)**: The fundamental truth or cosmic rhythm that governs the seasons, the gods, and human morality. It is often linked to the flow of water and the path of the sun.
- **Tvashtri**: The celestial craftsman who shapes the forms of all living beings.
- **Rodasi**: A common Vedic term for the pairing of Heaven and Earth.
- **Rajasi**: The "two regions" or spaces, typically referring to the atmosphere or the realms of earth and sky.
- **Ukshamanah**: Sprinkling or moistening, usually describing the life-giving rain or ritual waters.
- **Tridhatu**: "Three-fold," referring to the Vedic cosmology of three worlds (Earth, Atmosphere, and Heaven).
</vocab>

<summary>King Trasadasyu continues his divine self-identification, claiming the creative and supportive roles of Indra, Varuna, and Tvashtri. He describes his authority over the cosmic order (Rita), the waters, the three worlds, and his invocation by warriors in battle.</summary>
<keywords>Trasadasyu, Indra, Varuna, Tvashtri, Rita (Cosmic Order), Creation, Sovereignty, War, Vedic Cosmology</keywords>

## Commentary by Sayana

<note>On Verse 5</note>
"Me—even me—leaders and soldiers with excellent horses, desiring battle <note>original: "vājayantaḥ"</note>, follow [this is the implied meaning]. They call upon me alone when they are surrounded in the heat of battle <note>original: "samaraṇe"</note>. They summon me to aid them in war. Being the wealthy and bountiful <term>Maghavan</term>, I, as **Indra**, create the contest or the prize of the race. Possessing power that overcomes all enemies <note>original: "abhibhūtyojāḥ"</note>, I raise the dust of the battlefield."
->**|| Thus ends the seventeenth section of the seventh chapter of the third book ||**<-

->**|| Now the Sixth Verse ||**<-
<note>On Verse 6</note>
"I, King <term>Trasadasyu</term>, have performed all those well-known deeds. No divine power belonging to the gods <note>original: "daivyaṃ sahaḥ"</note> can check or ward me off, for I am irresistible. Because the **Soma** offerings have exhilarated me, and the recited hymns <note>original: "ukthā"</note> have also exhilarated me, therefore both the boundless <note>original: "apāre"</note> realms <note>the two "Rajasi," meaning Heaven and Earth</note> tremble or shake in fear of my might."

->**|| Now the Seventh Verse ||**<-
<note>On Verse 7</note>
From here onwards, the hymn shifts to the praise of **Indra** and **Varuna** together. "O **Varuna**, all beings—all created things—know those deeds of yours. O Worshipper <note>original: "Vedhas," here interpreted as a name for the singer or the wise one</note>, you proclaim these praises to **Varuna**. You praise **Varuna**. O **Indra**, you are famously known for having slain the obstacles <note>original: "vṛtrāṇi," referring to the demon **Vritra** or general blockages</note>; you have released the rivers that were held back."

<vocab>
- **Indra**: The king of the gods, associated with thunder, war, and the release of waters.
- **Varuna**: The deity of cosmic order, law, and the celestial ocean.
- **Maghavan**: A common title for Indra, meaning "the generous" or "the lord of riches."
- **Trasadasyu**: A famous king of the Puru dynasty who is the seer (Rishi) and speaker of this hymn.
- **Vritra**: The "Enveloper" or "Obstacle," a dragon-like being slain by Indra to release the waters of the world.
- **Vedhas**: A term meaning a wise person, a creator, or a ritual performer.
- **Rajasi**: Literally "the two dusty/dark spaces," used here to denote the vastness of the Earth and the Sky.
- **Soma**: A sacred ritual drink offered to the gods to grant them strength and exhilaration.
</vocab>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Rig Veda, Mandala 4, Hymn 42. The previous page detailed the self-praise of Trasadasyu as a manifestation of Indra and Varuna. Having struck and killed the enemies <note>original: "vairiṇo jaghanvān"</note>—this is what is meant by the phrase "having slain." Furthermore, O Indra, you caused the rivers—whose nature is to flow and which were obstructed or covered—to move forward.

-> || The Eighth Verse || <-

## Hymn Text
Our fathers were present here, those Seven Seers, when the son of Durgaha was being held in captivity. For her, they worshipped and obtained Trasadasyu, a slayer of enemies like Indra, a semi-divine hero. || 8 ||

**Padapatha (Word-by-word analysis):**
Our; here; fathers; they; were; seven; seers; in the case of the son of Durgaha; being bound; they; [prefix]; worshipped; Trasadasyu; for her; Indra; like; slayer of enemies; semi-divine. || 8 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)
While Purukutsa (the son of Durgaha) was held in captivity, his queen <note>the wife of King Purukutsa</note>, seeing the kingdom without a ruler and desiring a son for the sake of the nation, worshipped the Seven Seers <note>the *Saptarshis*, legendary sages of the Vedic era</note> who happened to arrive. Pleased by her devotion, they prayed fervently to the gods Indra and Varuna. After she had worshipped Indra and Varuna, she gave birth to Trasadasyu. Knowing this ancient history, the Seer <note>the poet of the hymn</note> speaks these two verses here.

"Now, in this kingless land—or perhaps on this earth—our fathers, the protectors and progenitors, were present. These famous Seven Seers, while Purukutsa (the son of Durgaha) was held fast in bonds, performed a sacrifice to grant Trasadasyu to her <note>the wife of Purukutsa</note> through the grace of Indra and Varuna." 

What was this son like? He was a slayer of enemies <note>original: "vṛtraturaṃ"</note> and one who stays in the presence of the gods <note>original: "ardha-devaṃ"</note>. Alternatively, they granted a son who was "half-god," like Indra himself. As the *Taittiriya* text says, "Indra is half of all [the gods]," meaning Indra is the most significant recipient of offerings among the deities.

---

-> || The Ninth Verse || <-

## Hymn Text
For Purukutsa's wife worshipped you both, O Indra and Varuna, with offerings and with homages. Then you two gave to her the king Trasadasyu, the slayer of enemies, the semi-divine hero. || 9 ||

**Padapatha (Word-by-word analysis):**
Purukutsa’s wife; indeed; for you two; worshipped; with offerings; O Indra and Varuna; with homages; then; the king; Trasadasyu; for her; slayer of enemies; you two gave; semi-divine. || 9 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Indra and Varuna, Purukutsani (the wife of Purukutsa), urged by the seers, worshipped you both. She indeed pleased you with oblations <term>original: "havyebhiḥ"; ritual food offerings</term> and with hymns of praise <term>original: "namobhiḥ"; respectful bows or prayers</term>. Then, you both gave the king Trasadasyu—the slayer of enemies and a "semi-divine" hero as described previously—to her, the wife of Purukutsa.

<vocab>
- Indra: The King of the gods and deity of storms and war.
- Varuna: The guardian of moral law (*Rta*) and the celestial waters.
- Purukutsa: A Vedic king of the Ikshvaku dynasty who was captured in battle.
- Trasadasyu: The son of Purukutsa, a famous king known for his piety and divine favor.
- Seven Seers (Saptarshi): A group of seven legendary sages who act as spiritual guides for humanity.
- Vritra-han: "Slayer of Vritra"; a title for a great conqueror, originally referring to Indra killing the demon of drought.
- Semi-divine (Ardha-deva): A term meaning "half-god," indicating a king who shares in divine power or nature.
</vocab>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Tenth Verse ॥ <-

May we, having obtained wealth, rejoice, as the gods rejoice with the oblation and cows with the pasture. O Indra and Varuna, grant us forever that "cow" <note>Here, "cow" is a metaphor for a source of abundance or the speech of prayer</note> which is unfailing and steady. || 10 ||

-> **Word-by-word Analysis** <-

By wealth; we; having obtained; may we rejoice; with the oblation; the gods; with pasture; the cows;
that; cow; O Indra and Varuna; you two; to us; always; grant; unfailing. || 10 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**By wealth** <note>original: "rāyā"</note>—meaning with riches—**may we rejoice**, having become **those who have obtained** <note>original: "sasavāṃso"</note> it from you two. Just as **the gods** rejoice **with the oblation**, and as **cows** rejoice **with the pasture**, so may we. O **Indra and Varuna**, you who are the destroyers of all enemies <note>Sayana interprets "viśvāhā" here as "destroyers of the universe's foes," though it usually means "always"</note>, **grant** to **us** **that cow** which is the source of delight and wealth. What kind of cow? One that is **unfailing** <note>original: "anapaspurantīm"</note>, meaning one that is not taken away or harmed. Alternatively, the word **always** <note>original: "viśvāhā"</note> is an indeclinable meaning "at all times."

-> ॥ This concludes the eighteenth group of the seventh chapter of the third book ॥ <-

---

The hymn beginning with **"Who indeed will hear"** <note>original: "ka u śravat"</note> consists of seven verses and is the eleventh hymn of this section. The Seers <note>the poet-composers</note> are Purumilha and Ajamilha, both sons of Suhotra. The meter is *Trishtubh* <note>a Vedic meter of 44 syllables</note>. The deities are the Ashvins <note>the divine twin physicians who herald the dawn</note>. Regarding this, the Index <note>the *Anukramani*, a traditional catalog of the Veda</note> states: "The seven verses beginning with *ka u śravat* belong to Purumilha and Ajamilha, the sons of Suhotra, and are addressed to the Ashvins." In the morning recitation and the ritual of the Ashvin cup, these two hymns—beginning with "The cow of the ancient one" <note>Hymn 43</note> and "Who indeed will hear" <note>Hymn 44</note>—are used during the Ashvin season in the *Trishtubh* meter. This is indicated by the ritual manuals: "The cow... of the ancient... who indeed will hear" (Asvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.15).

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The First Verse ॥ <-

Who indeed will hear? Which of the gods worthy of sacrifice? Which god will accept our adoring praise? In whose heart, among the immortals, shall we lodge this most dear and shining prayer, which is accompanied by excellent oblations? || 1 ||

-> **Word-by-word Analysis** <-

Who; indeed; will hear; which; of those worthy of sacrifice; adoring; god; which; will accept;
of whom; this; shining; among the immortals; most dear; in the heart; may we lodge; excellent praise; accompanied by good oblations. || 1 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Among the **gods worthy of sacrifice**, **who indeed is the god** who **will hear** our praise? **Which** god **will accept** the **adoring** hymn—that is, the praise characterized by bowing and worship? **In whose heart**, among the **immortals**, **shall we lodge**—meaning, cause to rest or take refuge—**this most dear**, most beloved, **shining** <note>original: "devīm"</note>, and **excellent praise** which is **accompanied by good oblations** or good food? The implication is: who else but the Ashvins could be the rightful master of such a hymn?

<vocab>
- <term>Wealth (Rāyā)</term>: Material prosperity or the spiritual reward of sacrifice.
- <term>Indra-Varuna (Indrāvaruṇā)</term>: A dual deity combining the power of the storm-king and the guardian of cosmic order.
- <term>Purumilha and Ajamilha</term>: Historical or legendary Seers credited with these hymns.
- <term>Ashvins (Aśvinau)</term>: Twin gods often associated with helping the distressed and bringing light.
- <term>Worthy of sacrifice (Yajñiyānām)</term>: Deities who are entitled to receive offerings in the Vedic fire ritual.
</vocab>

# ॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Book 3. Chapter 7. Section 19.]

-> ॥ The Second Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Who will be gracious? Which of the gods is the most frequent visitor? Which of the gods is the most superlative source of happiness? Of which chariot do they say that it is drawn by swift, galloping horses—the very one which the daughter of the Sun <note>original: "sūryasya duhitā"; in Vedic mythology, the daughter of the Sun god (often called Sūryā) chose the Ashvins as her husbands</note> chose? ॥ 2 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Who; will be gracious; which; most frequent visitor; of the gods; indeed; which; most superlative source of happiness;
the chariot; whom; they say; with galloping horses; swift; which; of the Sun; the daughter; chose. ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Who will be gracious?** Which god will gladden us? **Which of the gods is the most frequent visitor** <note>original: "āgamiṣṭha"</note> to our sacrifice? Among **the gods**, which one is the **most superlative source of happiness** <note>original: "śaṃbhaviṣṭha"</note>, the one who most brings about well-being? The implication is: who could possess these qualities other than the Ashvins? About **which chariot** do they **say** <note>original: "āhuḥ"</note> or speak of as having **swift, galloping horses**? About that chariot which the **daughter of the Sun**—here meaning the wife of the Sun—**chose** <note>original: "avṛṇīta"</note> or took for herself. They ask: which is that famous, rapid chariot?

---

-> ॥ The Third Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Come quickly, for you two proceed towards the days of sacrifice, just as Indra shows his power at the end of the night <note>original: "paritakmyāyām"; referring to the transition between night and dawn</note>. Born from heaven, divine, and beautiful-winged, by which of your powers do you two become the most powerful in ritual acts? ॥ 3 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Quickly; indeed; [filler]; you two go; of the coming; days; Indra; like; power; at the end of night;
from heaven; born; divine; beautiful-winged; by which; of powers; you two become; most powerful. ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Quickly** <note>original: "makṣu"</note> means speedily. The words "indeed" and "surely" are used here to complete the meter. You two **go** <note>original: "gacchathaḥ"</note> towards the **days** of the ritual that are approaching. Just as **Indra** shows his own **power** <note>original: "śaktim"</note> at the end of the night—meaning Indra arrives at the dawn of the day of sacrifice—likewise, you two should also arrive. You two are **born from heaven**, you reside in the divine realm, and you are **beautiful-winged** <note>original: "suparṇā"</note>, meaning you possess beautiful movement. Among **powers** or ritual acts, by which **power** do you two become the **most powerful** <note>original: "śaciṣṭhā"</note> or the most excellent performers of deeds?

-> ॥ The Fourth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
What has been your favor? By what means, O Ashvins, will you come to us when you are invoked? Who will deliver us from great abandonment <note>original: "tyajasaḥ"; often interpreted as danger, sin, or being left behind by the gods</note> in the moment of encounter? O sweet ones, O doers of wonders, protect us with your aid. ॥ 4 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
What; your; has been; favor; by what; us; [towards]; O Ashvins; you two come; being invoked;
who; your; of the great; [even]; abandonment; in the encounter; protect; O sweet ones; O doers of wonders; us; with aid. ॥ 4 ॥

---

<vocab>
- <term>Ashvin (अश्विन्)</term>: Twin deities associated with the dawn, healing, and traveling in a swift chariot.
- <term>Shambhavishtha (शंभविष्ठ)</term>: A superlative form meaning "the best at conferring happiness or peace."
- <term>Mridati (मृळाति)</term>: To be gracious or compassionate; to bestow joy.
- <term>Suryasya Duhita (सूर्यस्य दुहिता)</term>: The Daughter of the Sun, a figure who, in a famous myth, participated in a race where the Ashvins won the right to her hand in marriage.
- <term>Shachinam (शचीनाम्)</term>: Related to 'Shakti'; refers to divine powers, specifically those manifested through ritual skill.
- <term>Urushyatam (उरुष्यतम्)</term>: A plea for protection or to be led into "wide space" (freedom) away from restriction.
</vocab>

# म० ४. अ० ४. सू० ४३.] ॥ The Third Book ॥ २०७

## Commentary (Sayana)
[Continuation of Verse 4]
**Your** <note>original: "vām"</note>, of you two, what is the measure of your qualities? What kind of **praise** <note>original: "stutiḥ"</note>—which is the measurement or definition of qualities—can truly approach you? By what hymn, being called upon, would you **come to us**? Who could be the one to withstand the **wrath** <note>original: "tyajaḥ"</note>—meaning that which is abandoned or avoided by all—of your greatness in your presence? O **creators of sweet water** <note>original: "mādhvī"</note>, O **destroyers of enemies** <note>original: "dasrā"</note>, O Ashvins, favor us with your **protection** <note>original: "ūtyā"</note>. This refers to the act of guarding; protect us.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ The Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**Your vast chariot encompasses the heaven when it turns toward you from the ocean. O you of sweetness, let [the priests] sprinkle the sweet Soma with sweet milk, as the cooked offerings reach you everywhere.** ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Vast; your; chariot; encompasses; heaven; when; from the ocean; towards; turns; your; with sweetness; O you of sweetness; the sweet; your; sprinkling; when; everywhere; your; offerings; reach; cooked. ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Ashvins, **your chariot** encompasses or **travels** <note>original: "nakṣati"</note> extensively around **the heaven** <note>original: "dyām"</note>. It does so because it turns toward you from the **ocean** <note>original: "samudrāt"</note>—which here refers to the mid-air or atmosphere, the means of reaching you. O **you of sweetness** <note>original: "mādhvī"</note>, possessing the previously described characteristics, let the officiating priests **sprinkle** <note>original: "pruṣāyan"</note> the **sweet Soma juice** <note>original: "madhu"</note> with **sweet milk** <note>original: "madhvā"</note>. Because the **cooked parched barley** <note>original: "pakvā yavā"</note> and other **offerings** <note>original: "pṛkṣo"</note> reach you from all sides, the chariot turns toward you.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ The Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**The river [or cloud] has indeed sprinkled your horses with moisture; the bright, bird-like horses have gone around with radiant heat. That swift vehicle of yours is well known, by which you become the lords of Sūryā.** <note>The daughter of the Sun</note> ॥ ६ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
The river/cloud; indeed; your; with moisture; sprinkled; horses; with heat; bird-like/goers; bright; around; gone; that; indeed; well; your; swift; is known; vehicle; by which; lords; you become; of Sūryā. ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **river** <note>original: "sindhuḥ"</note>, meaning the flowing cloud or its water, **sprinkled** <note>original: "asiñcat"</note> **your horses** with **moisture** <note>original: "rasayā"</note>. With **radiant light** <note>original: "ghṛṇā"</note>, the **horses** <note>original: "vayaḥ"</note>—which are like birds or are the "goers"—becoming **bright** <note>original: "aruṣāsaḥ"</note> or shining, have **gone around** <note>original: "pari gman"</note>. **That vehicle** of yours, the famous chariot which is the means of your travel, is **well known** <note>original: "ceti"</note> to be **swift** <note>original: "ajiram"</note>. The chariot **is known** as the one by which you **become the lords** <note>original: "patī"</note>—the protectors or carriers—**of Sūryā** <note>The daughter of the Sun god</note>.

<vocab>
**Ashvinau** (अश्विनौ): The twin Vedic deities associated with dawn and healing.
**Ratha** (रथ): The celestial chariot used by the gods.
**Sindhu** (सिंधु): Literally "river," but often interpreted as "cloud" or "flowing atmosphere" in the Rig Veda.
**Sūryā** (सूर्या): The daughter of the Sun god, who travels on the Ashvins' chariot.
**Mādhvī** (माध्वी): An epithet meaning "possessors of sweetness" or "givers of honey."
**Dasra** (दस्र): An epithet for the Ashvins meaning "accomplishers of wonderful deeds" or "destroyers of diseases/enemies."
**Pṛkṣa** (पृक्ष): Offerings, often specifically Soma or sacrificial food.
**Ajira** (अजिर): A technical Vedic term meaning "fast" or "rapid."
</vocab>

# म० ४. अ० ४. सू० ४३.] ॥ The Third Book ॥ २०८

-> ॥ The Seventh Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Here and here, since I have joined you two together with praise, let this beautiful prayer of ours be rich in the jewels of sustenance. O you two, protect the singer, for our desire, O Nāsatyas, has rested, directed toward you.** ॥ ७ ॥

**Padapatha:**
Here—here; since; of you two; together; I have joined; that; this; in us; beautiful prayer; sustenance-jewels; protect; the singer; you two; indeed; rested; desire; Nāsatyas; directed-toward-you. ॥ ७ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Ashvins** <note>The twin divine physicians of the Vedas</note>, **since** <note>original: "yat"</note>, or by which beautiful prayer, **here and here**—meaning in this very sacrifice—I **join** <note>original: "papṛkṣe"</note> you two, who are **of the same mind** <note>original: "samana"; meaning identical in intent or form</note>, with this praise. May **this** <note>original: "sā iyam"</note> beautiful prayer being performed now **be fruitful for us** <note>original: "asme"</note>. O **you who possess the jewels of sustenance** <note>original: "vājaratnā"; those for whom delightful food is as wealth</note>. The sacred texts say, "Food is indeed *vāja*" <note>original: "annaṃ vai vāja iti śruteḥ"</note>. You two **protect** <note>original: "uruṣyatam"</note> or guard me, the **singer** <note>original: "jaritāram"; the one who chants the praises</note>. O **Nāsatyas** <note>original: "nāsatyā"; a common name for the Ashvins, often interpreted as "those in whom untruth is not"</note>, our **desire** <note>original: "kāmaḥ"</note> has **rested** <note>original: "śritaḥ"</note>, having reached you, being **directed toward you** <note>original: "yuvadrik"</note> alone.

-> ॥ This concludes the nineteenth section of the seventh chapter of the third book ॥ <-

The twelfth hymn, beginning with "That chariot of yours" <note>original: "taṃ vāṃ ratham"</note>, consists of seven verses. The seers are Purumīḷha and Ajamīḷha. The meter is Triṣṭubh. The deities are the Ashvins. The ritual application is as stated in the morning litany and the Ashvin-shastra <note>specific parts of the Soma sacrifice dedicated to the Ashvins</note>.

-> ॥ The First Verse of the New Hymn ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**That chariot of yours we would invoke today, O Ashvins—that chariot of vast speed, the bringer of light, which carries Sūryā, possessing the seat, borne by songs, most abundant, and seeking wealth.** ॥ १ ॥

**Padapatha:**
That; of you two; chariot; we; today; would invoke; vast-speed; Ashvins; bringer; of the cow (light); which; Sūryā; carries; possessing-the-seat; song-borne; most-abundant; wealth-seeking. ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Ashvins**, we the singers **invoke** <note>original: "huvema"</note> or call upon **your chariot today**, on this day of the Soma pressing. What is that chariot like? It has **vast speed** <note>original: "pṛthujrayam"</note> or a famous velocity, and it is the **bringer of the cow** <note>original: "goḥ saṃgatim"; here "cow" refers to the rays of light or the rewards of the sacrifice</note>. It is the chariot **which carries** or supports **Sūryā** <note>The daughter of the Sun god, who chose the Ashvins as her husbands</note> and is **possessing the seat** <note>original: "vandhurayuḥ"; *vandhura* refers to the wooden framework or seat within the chariot where the riders sit</note>. It is **borne by songs** <note>original: "gīrvāhasam"; carried toward the sacrifice by the power of the priests' praises</note>, **most abundant** <note>original: "purutamam"</note> in its gifts, and **seeking wealth** <note>original: "vasuyum"</note> or possessing great riches.

# [Mandala 4. Section 4. Hymn 44.] ॥ The Third Octave ॥ २०९

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**O Ashvins, you two divine beings, sons of heaven, you enjoy that glory through your wondrous deeds. Your forms are touched by the nourishing offerings, when your great horses carry you in your chariot.** ॥ २ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
You two; glory; O Ashvins; divine beings; that; of heaven; sons; you enjoy; through deeds/powers;
of you two; form; toward; nourishing offerings; they touch; they carry; when; the great ones (horses); in the chariot; of you two. ॥ २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Sons of Heaven** <note>original: "divo napātā"; meaning either the sons of the Sun or those who do not allow the heavenly realm to fall</note>, O **Ashvins** <note>The twin celestial physicians</note>, **you two divine beings** <note>original: "devatā"; the commentator notes a grammatical variation in the case ending here</note>, you **enjoy** <note>original: "vanathaḥ"</note> **that** famous **glory** through your **deeds** or your powers <note>original: "śacībhiḥ"</note>. Alternatively, the word for "enjoy" may mean "to bestow." The **nourishing offerings** <note>original: "pṛkṣaḥ"</note>, characterized by the Soma juice, **touch** or reach **your forms** <note>original: "vapuḥ"; your bodies</note> **when** the **great horses** <note>original: "kakuhāsaḥ"</note> **carry you** in your **chariot**. Alternatively, the "great ones" may refer to the hymns of praise that carry you to the sacrifice.

---
-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**Who today, having offered oblations, shall bring you here with hymns for protection or for the drinking of the pressed Soma? Who, performing salutations to the ancient friend of the sacred Law, shall turn you, O Ashvins, toward us?** ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Who; of you two; today; shall make; one who has offered oblations; for protection; or; for the drinking of the pressed (Soma); or; with hymns;
of the Law (or water); or; for the friend; the ancient; salutation; performing; O Ashvins; [hither]; shall turn. ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Who** among the sacrificers **today shall make** or perform a praise **of you two** with **hymns** <note>original: "arkaiḥ"; mantras</note>? This person is **one who has offered oblations** <note>original: "rātahavyaḥ"; one who has given the Soma</note> either **for protection** <note>original: "ūtaye"</note> **or for the drinking of the pressed Soma**. O **Ashvins**, who **performing salutations** <note>original: "namo yemānaḥ"</note> **shall turn** or bring the sacrifice toward us for the **friend** <note>original: "vanuṣe"</note>—the enjoyer—of the **ancient** <note>original: "pūrvyāya"</note> **sacred Law** <note>original: "ṛtasya"; referring to the sacrifice or the cosmic order</note>?

---
-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**O Nāsatyas, you who are present in many places, come to this sacrifice in your golden chariot. Drink of the honeyed Soma-juice, and bestow wealth upon the person who honors you.** ॥ ४ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
With the golden; present in many places; with the chariot; this; sacrifice; O Nāsatyas; [hither]; come;
you two drink; indeed; of the honeyed; of the Soma; you two bestow; wealth; for the honoring; person. ॥ ४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **you who are present in many places** <note>original: "purubhū"</note>, O **Nāsatyas** <note>An epithet of the Ashvins meaning "truthful" or "not untruthful"</note>, **come to this sacrifice with your golden chariot. Drink** of the **Soma**...

# ॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Book 4. Chapter 1. Section 20.] २१०

...of the sweet juice <note>original: "madhuno"</note> related to the Soma. <note>The commentator notes that the genitive case is used here for the object of the action.</note> You two drink the Soma juice. You bestow <note>original: "dhatthaḥ"</note> or hold delightful wealth <note>original: "ratnaṃ"</note> for me, the person who worships and attends to you. <note>The verb "dhatthaḥ" is explained as a form of "to give" in the Vedic subjunctive mood.</note>

---

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Come to us from heaven and from earth with your golden, well-rolling chariot. Let not other god-seeking worshippers detain you, for the ancient bond of praise connects us to you.** ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Come; to us; from heaven; toward; from earth; with the golden; with the well-rolling; with the chariot;
not; you two; others; let them detain; seeking the gods; since/when; it connects; the bond (navel); ancient; of you two. ॥ ५ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
**To us** <note>original: "no-achha"</note> means to reach us. Come from **heaven** <note>the celestial realm</note> and from **earth**. By what means? With the **golden** <note>original: "hiranyayena"; meaning beneficial and beautiful</note> and **well-rolling** <note>original: "suvṛtā"; meaning having a smooth or excellent motion</note> **chariot**. Let **other god-seeking** <note>original: "devayanto"</note> people—meaning other sacrificers who desire you two gods—**not detain** you. Do not let them restrain you or hold you back. **Since** <note>original: "yat"</note> the **ancient** <note>original: "pūrvyā"</note> **bond** <note>original: "nābhiḥ"; literally 'navel', signifying a central connection or a binding hymn of praise</note>, which existed even before the later morning sacrifices, **connects** <note>original: "saṃ dade"</note> us to you, therefore you must come.

---

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Now, O Wonder-workers, grant us great wealth consisting of many heroes for both of us. O Ashvins, when the leaders have brought the hymn to you, the descendants of Ajamidha have come with their collective praise.** ॥ ६ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Now; for us; wealth; abounding in heroes; great; O Wonder-workers; grant/create; among both; for us;
the leaders; when; of you two; O Ashvins; the hymn; they have brought/protected; with collective praise; the descendants of Ajamidha; they have come. ॥ ६ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Now** <note>original: "nu"; quickly</note> grant us **wealth** <note>original: "rayim"</note> that is **abounding in heroes** <note>original: "puruvīraṃ"; meaning accompanied by many sons</note> and is **great** or vast. O **Wonder-workers** <note>original: "dasrā"; an epithet of the Ashvins meaning those who perform miraculous deeds</note>, you two **grant** <note>original: "mimāthām"</note> or create this. **Among both** <note>meaning among the two groups of sacrificers, the Purumidhas and the Ajamidhas</note>, grant this **to us**. **When** <note>original: "yat"</note> the **leaders** <note>original: "naro"; the guiding officiating priests</note> belonging to the line of Purumidha **have brought** or attained **your hymn**, then likewise the **descendants of Ajamidha** <note>original: "ājamīḷhāso"</note> have also **come** together with them, offering **collective praise**.

---

-> ॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Here and there, where your common nourishment is sprinkled, may that grace of yours, rich in food, be with us. Protect your singer; for our desire, O Nasatyas, is directed toward you.** ॥ ७ ॥

| Term | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Ashvins** (Aśvinau) | The divine twins, physicians of the gods. |
| **Wealth** (Rayi) | Wealth, treasure, or spiritual abundance. |
| **Abounding in heroes** (Puruvīra) | Having many heroic sons or followers. |
| **Wonder-worker** (Dasra) | Accomplishing wonderful deeds; a title for the Ashvins. |
| **Descendants of Ajamidha** (Ājamīḷhāsaḥ) | The members of the Ajamidha family or clan. |
| **Well-rolling** (Suvṛt) | Rolling smoothly (describing the celestial chariot). |
| **Nasatyas** (Nāsatyā) | Another name for the Ashvins, meaning "truthful" or "not untrue". |

# म० ४. अ० ४. सू० ४५.] ॥ तृतीयोऽष्टकः ॥ २११

## Hymn Text

-> [Rig Veda 4.44.7 Word-by-word Analysis] <-

Right here; right here; what; of you two; with a common mind; has been mixed; that; this; in us; <note>original: "asme iti"</note>; good thought; rich in jewels of strength; protect; the singer; you two; indeed; directed; desire; O Nasatyas <note>name for the Ashvins</note>; toward you. ॥ ७ ॥

The phrase "**Right here, right here**" <note>original: "iheheti"</note> has been explained in previous sections.

-> ॥ Thus ends the twentieth section of the seventh chapter of the third book. ॥ <-

---

-> [Introduction to Hymn 45] <-

The thirteenth hymn, beginning with the words "**This very light**" <note>original: "eṣa sya bhānuḥ"</note>, consists of seven verses. The meter for the first six verses is **Jagati** <note>a 48-syllable meter</note>, while the seventh is **Trishtup** <note>a 44-syllable meter</note>. The seer <note>Rishi</note> of this Mandala is **Vamadeva**. The deities addressed are the **Ashvins**. The index confirms that this hymn ends with a Trishtup verse. This hymn is to be recited during the Jagati-meter portions of the Morning Litany and the Ashvin-shastra ritual. As indicated in the ritual manuals: "Agni has been awakened on the earth; this very light..." <note>referencing Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.15</note>.

-> ॥ Now the First Verse ॥ <-

This very light rises up; the all-encompassing chariot is yoked upon the ridge of this heaven. Within it are three pairs of foods; a fourth, a leather bag of honey, overflows with abundance. ॥ १ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
This; that; light; up; rises; is yoked; chariot; all-encompassing; of heaven; of this; on the ridge; foods; in this; pairs; upon; three; leather bag; fourth; of honey; intensely; overflows. ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**This** <note>original: "eṣa"</note>, the one visible before us, refers to **that** <note>original: "sya"</note> **radiant light of the Sun** <note>original: "bhānuḥ"</note> which **rises up** <note>original: "udiyarti"</note> or moves upward. Furthermore, the chariot belonging to you two, which is **all-encompassing** <note>original: "parijmā"</note>—meaning it travels everywhere—moves upon the **ridge** <note>original: "sānavi"</note>, the elevated region of **this heaven** <note>original: "divaḥ"</note>, the shining sky. In this chariot, **three** <note>original: "trayaḥ"</note> types of **pairs** <note>original: "mithunā"</note> of **foods** <note>original: "pṛkṣāsaḥ"</note> are placed. Food is traditionally categorized in three ways: that which is eaten, drunk, or chewed. The term "pair" or "union" <note>original: "mithuna"</note> is used in Taittiriya texts to describe all things: "Mother, father, and son—that itself is the union." The **fourth** <note>original: "turīyaḥ"</note> element is the **leather bag** <note>original: "dṛtiḥ"</note>, a term for a skin-vessel used to hold liquid substances. This bag, which belongs to the **honey** <note>original: "madhunaḥ"</note>—meaning it is filled with sweet Soma juice—**overflows with abundance** <note>original: "virapshate"</note> or shines forth in various ways.

---

## Hymn Text (continued)

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

At the flushings of the Dawn, your food-laden, honey-filled chariots and horses rise up, uncovering the encompassing darkness and spreading the bright light like the sun across the middle realm. ॥ २ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Up; of you two; foods; honey-laden; rise; chariots; horses; of the dawn; in the flushings; uncovering; darkness; hither; all-encompassing; light/heaven; like; bright; spreading; hither; the middle realm. ॥ २ ॥

<meta>This page continues the translation of Rig Veda Mandala 4, Hymn 45. The hymn is dedicated to the Ashvins, the twin physicians of the gods, associated with the dawn.</meta>

### Rig Veda | Book 3, Chapter 6, Section 21.

## Commentary (continued)
Your chariots, O Ashvins, are **filled with strength** <note>original: "pṛkṣāsaḥ"</note>, possessing the means of brilliance, and **full of honey** <note>original: "madhumantaḥ"</note>, meaning they are provided with Soma juice, and are drawn by horses. Alternatively, the honey-filled, powerful chariots and horses rise up during the **break of dawn** <note>original: "vyuṣṭiṣu"</note>. They move forward. What are they doing? They are **uncovering the darkness** <note>original: "tama apa-ūrṇuvantaḥ"</note> that is spread all around, and they are spreading the **bright light** <note>original: "śukraṃ rajaḥ"</note> like the sun <note>original: "svar-ṇa"</note>. The word "ca" <note>and</note> is implied here. Or, it means they are spreading the bright light through the **mid-air** <note>original: "rajas"</note>.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Now the Third Verse ॥<-

Drink the sweet juice with mouths that drink honey; and yoke the dear chariot for the sake of the honey. You satisfy the path with honey, O lords of the path; O Ashvins, you carry the leather bag full of honey. ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Of the honey-sweet** <note>original: "madhvaḥ"</note>; **Drink** <note>original: "pibatām"</note>; **With mouths that drink honey** <note>original: "madhu-pebhiḥ āsa-bhiḥ"</note>; **And** <note>original: "uta"</note>; **The dear** <note>original: "priyam"</note>; **For the sake of honey** <note>original: "madhune"</note>; **Yoke** <note>original: "yuñjāthām"</note>; **The chariot** <note>original: "ratham"</note>; **Unto** <note>original: "ā"</note>; **The path** <note>original: "vārtanim"</note>; **With honey** <note>original: "madhunā"</note>; **You satisfy** <note>original: "jinvathaḥ"</note>; **Of the path** <note>original: "pathaḥ"</note>; **The leather bag** <note>original: "dṛtim"</note>; **You two carry** <note>original: "vahethe"</note>; **Full of honey** <note>original: "madhu-mantam"</note>; **O Ashvins** <note>original: "aśvinā"</note>. ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Drink the sweet Soma juice with your **mouths** <note>original: "āsyaiḥ"</note> which are fit for drinking Soma. Moreover, **yoke** <note>original: "yuñjāthām"</note> the beloved chariot—meaning, equip it with horses—for the purpose of obtaining the honey-Soma. The phrase "unto the path" implies: "Come to the house of the sacrificer." You **satisfy** <note>original: "jinvathaḥ"</note> or please the traveling paths with honey. Alternatively, this is one sentence: You satisfy the path and the atmosphere. O Ashvins, you **carry** <note>original: "vahethe"</note> or hold the leather bag that is full of honey.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥<-

Your horses, like swans, honey-laden, non-harming, golden-winged, waking at dawn, splashing through water, joyous, touching the intoxicant—like flies to honey, you go to our ritual libations. ॥ ४ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Swans** <note>original: "haṃsāsaḥ"</note>; **Which** <note>original: "ye"</note>; **Of you two** <note>original: "vām"</note>; **Honey-laden** <note>original: "madhu-mantaḥ"</note>; **Non-harming** <note>original: "asridhaḥ"</note>; **Golden-winged** <note>original: "hiraṇya-parṇāḥ"</note>; **Carriers** <note>original: "uhuvaḥ"</note>; **Waking at dawn** <note>original: "uṣar-budhaḥ"</note>; **Splashing through water** <note>original: "ud-prutaḥ"</note>; **Joyous** <note>original: "madinaḥ"</note>; **Touching the intoxicant** <note>original: "madi-spṛśaḥ"</note>; **Of honey** <note>original: "madhvaḥ"</note>; **Like** <note>original: "na"</note>; **Flies** <note>original: "makṣaḥ"</note>; **To the libations** <note>original: "savanāni"</note>; **You go** <note>original: "gacchathaḥ"</note>. ॥ ४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **swans** <note>original: "haṃsāsaḥ"</note> here refer to the horses that travel quickly on the road. They are **honey-laden** <note>endowed with sweetness</note>, **non-harming** <note>original: "asridhaḥ"</note> (those who do not deceive or fail), **golden-winged** <note>having wings that are beneficial and beautiful</note>, **carriers** <note>original: "uhuvaḥ"</note> (those who bear the chariot), and **waking at dawn** <note>becoming active at daybreak</note>. They are **splashing through water** <note>causing water to flow</note>, **joyous** <note>original: "madinaḥ"</note> (causing delight), and **touching the intoxicant** <note>original: "madi-spṛśaḥ"</note> (touching the exhilarating Soma). With such horses, you go to our **ritual libations** <note>original: "savanāni"</note> just as **flies** <note>original: "makṣaḥ"</note> go toward **honey** <note>original: "madhu"</note>.

<vocab>Ashvins (Twin gods of the dawn and healing), Madhu (Honey or the sacred Soma juice), Soma (A ritual drink offered to gods), Hamsas (Literally 'swans', used here as a metaphor for the Ashvins' swift horses), Usarbudh (Awakening at the time of the dawn), Savana (The three daily ritual offerings of Soma)</vocab>

<summary>This page contains verses 3 and 4 of Hymn 45, where the poet invites the Ashvins to drink Soma and describes their magnificent, "golden-winged" horses that arrive at dawn. # Mandala 4, Chapter 4, Hymn 45. | The Third Book | Page 213

-> || Now the Fifth Verse || <-

## Hymn Text

The fires <note>original: "agnayaḥ"</note>, providing good sacrifice and possessing sweetness, greet the Ashvins <note>the twin gods of dawn</note> at the break of day; when the wise priest, the deliverer of the rite, with washed hands, has pressed the sweet Soma-juice with the stones. ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Providing good sacrifice** <note>original: "su-adhvarāsaḥ"</note>; **possessing sweetness** <note>original: "madhu-mantaḥ"</note>; **the fires** <note>original: "agnayaḥ"</note>; **at dawn** <note>original: "usrā"</note>; **they greet/praise** <note>original: "jarante"</note>; **towards** <note>original: "prati"</note>; **the day/dawn** <note>original: "vastoḥ"</note>; **O Ashvins** <note>original: "aśvinā"</note>; **when** <note>original: "yat"</note>; **with washed hands** <note>original: "nikta-hastaḥ"</note>; **the deliverer [of the rite]** <note>original: "taraṇiḥ"</note>; **the wise/all-seeing** <note>original: "vi-cakṣaṇaḥ"</note>; **the Soma** <note>original: "somam"</note>; **has pressed** <note>original: "suṣāva"</note>; **possessing sweetness** <note>original: "madhu-mantam"</note>; **with stones** <note>original: "adri-bhiḥ"</note>. ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Providing good sacrifice** means they are the instruments of a beautiful ritual. **Possessing sweetness** means they possess the Soma juice that is to be offered. **The fires**, referring to the household fire <note>original: "Gārhapatya"</note> and others, greet the **Ashvins**, who dwell together, **towards the day**, meaning daily at the time of dawn. They **greet**, or rather, they praise them. **When**—at which time—the **wise** Adhvaryu priest, who sees clearly and is the **deliverer** or completer of the ritual, **has pressed the sweet Soma with stones** <note>original: "gravabhiḥ"</note> after having his **hands washed** and purified with water, then those **fires** offer praise. The meaning is: "Therefore, O Ashvins, please come to the rite."

---

-> || Now the Sixth Verse || <-

## Hymn Text

The rays, falling nearby and dispersing the darkness throughout the days, spread the bright light like the sun; the Sun too proceeds, yoking his horses. You, O Ashvins, perceive all the paths through your own power. ॥ ६ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Falling nearby** <note>original: "āke-nipāsaḥ"</note>; **by the days** <note>original: "ahaḥ-bhiḥ"</note>; **dispersing/shaking** <note>original: "davidhataḥ"</note>; **the sun/heaven** <note>original: "svaḥ"</note>; **like** <note>original: "na"</note>; **the bright** <note>original: "śukram"</note>; **spreading** <note>original: "tanvantaḥ"</note>; **the mid-region/light** <note>original: "rajaḥ"</note>; **the Sun** <note>original: "sūraḥ"</note>; **indeed** <note>original: "cit"</note>; **the horses** <note>original: "aśvān"</note>; **yoking** <note>original: "yuyujānaḥ"</note>; **proceeds** <note>original: "īyate"</note>; **all** <note>original: "viśvān"</note>; **along** <note>original: "anu"</note>; **by power/food** <note>original: "svadhayā"</note>; **you two perceive/manifest** <note>original: "cetathaḥ"</note>; **the paths** <note>original: "pathaḥ"</note>. ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Falling nearby** <note>original: "ākenipāsaḥ"</note>: the word refers to the rays <note>original: "rashmayaḥ"</note> that fall in the vicinity. These rays, **dispersing** or destroying the darkness **by the days**, and **spreading the bright light** throughout the mid-region <note>original: "rajaḥ"</note> **like the sun**, are the horses of the Ashvins. **The Sun indeed**, yoking his own **horses, proceeds** onward. O Ashvins, you both **perceive**—meaning you manifest or make known—**all the paths** of your arrival in sequence, **by your own power**, which here refers to the food in the form of the Soma juice.

---

-> || Now the Seventh Verse || <-

## Hymn Text

I have uttered a prayer for you, O Ashvins; the chariot is well-horsed and ageless. With this chariot, you quickly traverse the worlds to reach the donor who possesses the oblation and who crosses over difficulties. ॥ ७ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Forth** <note>original: "pra"</note>; **for you two** <note>original: "vām"</note>; **I have spoken** <note>original: "avocam"</note>; **O Ashvins** <note>original: "aśvinā"</note>; **the prayer/thought-bearer** <note>original: "dhiyam-dhāḥ"</note>; **the chariot** <note>original: "rathaḥ"</note>; **well-horsed** <note>original: "su-aśvaḥ"</note>; **ageless** <note>original: "ajaraḥ"</note>; **which** <note>original: "yaḥ"</note>; **is** <note>original: "asti"</note>; **by which** <note>original: "yena"</note>; **instantly** <note>original: "sadyaḥ"</note>; **around** <note>original: "pari"</note>; **the worlds/spaces** <note>original: "rajāṃsi"</note>; **you two go** <note>original: "yāthaḥ"</note>; **possessing the oblation** <note>original: "haviṣmantam"</note>; **the deliverer** <note>original: "taraṇim"</note>; **the donor/enjoyer** <note>original: "bhojam"</note>; **towards** <note>original: "accha"</note>. ॥ ७ ॥

---

## Critical Notes
<note>Bottom of page identifies the volume and signature: VOL. III. 3 I</note>

<vocab>
**Ashvinau**: The twin Vedic deities associated with the dawn, healing, and speed.
**Agni**: The fire-god; in plural, refers to the various ritual fires in the sacrifice.
**Soma**: A sacred ritual drink made from a plant, central to Vedic offerings.
**Adhvaryu**: The priest responsible for the physical details of the sacrifice, such as preparing the Soma.
**Rajāṃsi**: Refers to the various regions of the world, often the mid-air or celestial spaces.
</vocab>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on the final verse of Hymn 45 (dedicated to the Ashvins) and begins the fifth sub-section (Anuvaka) of the Fourth Book. It introduces Hymn 46, shifting focus to the wind-god Vayu and the king of gods, Indra. This follows the previous discussion on the Soma rituals performed at dawn.</meta>

I, the sustainer of sacred works <note>original: "dhiyaṃdhāḥ"</note>, proclaim <note>original: "pra-vocaṃ"</note> these words to you, O Ashvins. I speak them forth; I praise you. There is a chariot which is well-horsed, ageless <note>original: "ajaro"</note>—meaning it never decays and is eternally new—a chariot that makes its riders ageless. With that chariot by which you instantly traverse the worlds <note>original: "rajāṃsi"</note>, come to our sacrifice <note>original: "ach-prāpnu-māgacchata"</note>. Come to the sacrificer who offers the Soma-oblation, the one who is swift and delivering <note>original: "taraṇiṃ"</note>, the enjoyer who provides food for the gods.

->॥ This concludes the nineteenth group of the seventh chapter of the third book. ॥<-
->॥ This concludes the fourth sub-section of the fourth Mandala. ॥<-

---

In the fifth sub-section <note>original: "anuvāka"</note>, there are thirteen hymns. Among these, the first hymn beginning with "Here, drink" <note>original: "ayaṃ piba"</note> has seven verses. It was revealed to the seer Vamadeva and is composed in the Gayatri meter. The entire hymn is dedicated to the dual deity Indra-Vayu, though the first verse is addressed solely to Vayu. As recorded in the Ancient Index <note>original: "Anukramaṇī"</note>: "This first verse is for Vayu, while the rest are for Indra-Vayu in the Gayatri meter." The ritual application of the hymn follows the nature of its verses. The first two verses are used as the offering-prayers <note>original: "yājyā"</note> for the cup dedicated to Indra and Vayu. As noted in the ritual manuals: "The two prayers starting with 'Here, drink of the sweets' are to be recited without a breath." <note>Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 5.5</note>

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ First Verse ॥<-
O Vayu, drink this pressed juice of the sweet liquids during the light-seeking rites; for you indeed are the first-drinker. ॥ १ ॥
<note>RV 4.46.1</note>
**This juice** <note>original: "ayam"</note>; **drink** <note>original: "piba"</note>; **of the sweet liquids** <note>original: "madhūnām"</note>; **pressed** <note>original: "sutam"</note>; **O Vayu** <note>original: "vāyo"</note>; **in the light-seeking rites** <note>original: "divi-iṣṭiṣu"</note>; **you** <note>original: "tvam"</note>; **indeed** <note>original: "hi"</note>; **the first-drinker** <note>original: "pūrva-pāḥ"</note>; **are** <note>original: "asi"</note>. ॥ १ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Vayu, drink this pressed juice belonging to the sweet juices—the Soma—before Indra and the other gods. Where should this be done? The text says: **In the light-seeking rites** <note>original: "diviṣṭiṣu"</note>, meaning in sacrifices that lead one to the light of heaven, or those performed for the sake of our desire for heaven. **For you are the first-drinker**: the word 'for' <note>original: "hi"</note> is used to highlight a well-known fact mentioned in other verses, such as "O God, you have held the first-drink" <note>Rig Veda 7.92.1</note>. The story of Vayu drinking first is clearly explained in the Brahmanas <note>prose commentaries on rituals</note>: "The gods indeed contended for the first drink of King Soma... I shall drink first, I shall drink first..." <note>Aitareya Brahmana 2.25</note>. In that story, Vayu won a race among the gods and thus earned the right to the first portion of the sacrifice.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Second Verse ॥<-
With a hundred protections, O Vayu, possessed of your teams of horses and having Indra as your charioteer, may both of you be satisfied with the pressed juice. ॥ २ ॥
<note>RV 4.46.2</note>
**With a hundred** <note>original: "śatena"</note>; **our** <note>original: "naḥ"</note>; **with protections** <note>original: "abhiṣṭi-bhiḥ"</note>; **possessed of teams** <note>original: "niyutvān"</note>; **having Indra as charioteer** <note>original: "indra-sārathiḥ"</note>; **O Vayu** <note>original: "vāyo"</note>; **of the pressed [juice]** <note>original: "sutasya"</note>; **be satisfied** <note>original: "tṛmpatam"</note>. ॥ २ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Vayu, being **possessed of teams** <note>original: "niyutvān"</note>—referring to the specific team of horses called 'Niyuts' that draw the wind's chariot—and being **Indra's charioteer** <note>meaning having Indra as your companion and helper</note>, come to us. Come with **a hundred**, meaning countless, **protections** <note>original: "abhiṣṭibhiḥ"</note> or desired blessings. Having arrived, **be satisfied** with the pressed Soma juice. This is a request for both you and Indra to drink. The companionship of Indra and Vayu is also detailed in the Brahmana texts.

| Term | Definition |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Ashvin** | Twin deities who represent the transition from darkness to light; physicians of the gods. |
| **Vayu** | The deity of the wind, celebrated as the first to receive the Soma drink. |
| **Indra** | The king of the gods and deity of storms and battle. |
| **Soma** | The sacred ritual drink pressed from a plant, central to Vedic sacrifice. |
| **Vamadeva** | The ancient seer <note>Rishi</note> to whom the hymns of the Fourth Book were revealed. |
| **Anuvaka** | A 'sub-section' or chapter within the larger books <note>Mandala</note> of the Rig Veda. |
| **Sukta** | A 'well-spoken' hymn or poem of the Veda. |
| **Gayatri** | A sacred three-line poetic meter used in many central Vedic verses. |
| **Aitareya Brahmana** | An ancient prose text that explains the myths and procedures behind the rituals. |
| **Niyutvan** | A title for Vayu, meaning 'he who possesses teams of horses.' |
