Mandala 5. Adhyaya 2. Hymn 18. || Fourth Ashtaka || 319

## Commentary (Sayana)
[Continuation of commentary on Rig Veda 5.17.5]

The word "Give" <note>original: *prayaccha*</note> is implied to complete the sense. **Protect** <note>original: *pāhi*</note>; guard us from calamities. For our **well-being** <note>original: *svastaye*</note>, meaning for security and the preservation of wealth—such as cattle—**be capable** <note>original: *śagdhi*</note>. I entreat you. <note>Note: The commentator mentions a grammatical shift to the middle voice here</note>. Or it means, "become powerful." O **Agni**, and **furthermore** <note>original: *uta*</note>, in **battles** <note>original: *pṛtsu*</note>, be there for our **growth** <note>original: *vṛdhe*</note> or prosperity. Be present.

-> ॥ This concludes the ninth section (Varga) of the first chapter (Adhyaya) of the fourth book (Ashtaka) ॥ <-

---

The fourth hymn of this section, beginning with "Agni at dawn" <note>original: *prātar agniḥ*</note>, consists of five verses. The *Anukramani* <note>an ancient index of the Rig Veda's authors and meters</note> states: "At morning... Dvita, the bearer of cleansed offerings." The seer (Rishi) of this hymn is Dvita, a descendant of Atri, who is distinguished by the epithet "bearer of cleansed offerings." Because of the technical rule "ending in a Pankti," the fifth verse of this hymn is in the **Pankti** meter <note>a meter of five 8-syllable lines</note>. Based on general definitions, the remaining verses are in the **Anushtubh** meter <note>the most common Vedic meter, 4 lines of 8 syllables</note>. Its ritual application is mentioned for the morning recitation and the recitations dedicated to the Ashvins <note>the twin physician gods of the dawn</note>.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the first verse ॥ <-

At dawn, let **Agni**, the much-beloved **guest** of the people, be praised;
He, the **immortal**, who among **mortals** delights in all the offerings. || 1 ||

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Pada Patha):**
At dawn; Agni; Much-beloved; The people (clans); Let him be praised; Guest;
All; Who; Immortal; Offerings; Among mortals; Delights. || 1 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Much-beloved** <note>original: *purupriyaḥ*</note> means dear to many. He is the **guest of the people** <note>original: *viśaḥ... atithiḥ*</note> because he establishes wealth in the house of the sacrificer. He is called a "guest" because he approaches the houses of the sacrificers just like a visitor. In this regard, the ancient etymologist Yaska says: "A guest <note>original: *atithi*</note> is one who comes to the home, or one who visits other families or houses on specific lunar dates <note>tithi</note>." 

Such an Agni should be **praised** at dawn. He is **immortal** <note>original: *amartyaḥ*</note>, possessing an undying nature. Among **mortals**, meaning human sacrificers, this Agni **delights in** <note>original: *raṇyati*</note> or desires **all** the various sacrificial **offerings** <note>original: *havyāni*</note> presented to him.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now, the second verse ॥ <-

For **Dvita**, the bearer of cleansed offerings, through the greatness of your own **skill**;
He holds the **Soma** continuously; even the **singer** [is recognized] by you, O Immortal. || 2 ||

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Pada Patha):**
For Dvita; Cleansed-offering-bearer; Own; Of skill (or strength); By greatness;
The Soma juice; He; Holds; Continuously; The singer; Even; Your/By you; O Immortal. || 2 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, for **Dvita**, the son of Dvita <note>or the seer named Dvita</note>, who is the **bearer of cleansed offerings** <note>original: *mṛkta-vāhase*</note>. He is called this because he carries or conveys the "cleansed" <note>original: *mṛktam*</note>—meaning pure—offering to the gods. For him, by the **greatness** <note>original: *maṃhanā*</note> of your own **skill** <note>original: *dakṣasya*</note>, which refers to your strength or wealth...

<vocab>
- **Agni**: The god of fire and the primary mediator between gods and humans.
- **Dvita**: The Vedic seer (Rishi) attributed with composing this hymn.
- **Atithi (Guest)**: A frequent title for Agni, reflecting how the sacrificial fire is "invited" into the home.
- **Havya**: The physical substance (like clarified butter) offered into the fire.
- **Mṛktavāhas**: A technical term for one who carries pure, ritualistically cleaned offerings.
- **Anushtubh**: A standard poetic meter used in Hindu scripture.
- **Maṃhanā**: A term for the abundant giving or inherent greatness of a deity.
</vocab>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on Hymn 18 of the 5th Mandala and begins Hymn 19. It transitions from the rewards given by patrons to Agni to the specific mystical experiences of the Seer Vavri.</meta>

...they gave fifty [rewards]. O **immortal Agni** <note>original: *amṛtāgne*</note>, for these **wealthy patrons** <note>original: *maghonāṃ*</note>, create **great** <note>original: *mahi*</note>, **glorious** <note>original: *dyumat*</note>, and **extensive** <note>original: *bṛhat*</note> **food** <note>original: *avaḥ*</note> accompanied by human attendants <note>original: *nṛvat*</note>. That is, please grant it to them.

->॥ Thus ends the tenth group <term>varga: a traditional subsection of a Vedic chapter</term> of the first chapter of the fourth book. ॥<-

The fifth hymn, beginning with "Conditions arise" <note>original: *abhyavasthāḥ*</note>, consists of five verses. The index of meters and authors <term>Anukramaṇikā</term> states: "The hymn starting with *abhyavasthā* is by Vavri; the first two are in the Gāyatrī meter, the next two in Anuṣṭubh, and the fifth is in the Virāṭ-rūpā meter." The Seer is **Vavri Ātreya** <note>descendant of Atri</note>. The first and second verses are **Gāyatrī** <term>a meter of 24 syllables</term>; the third and fourth are **Anuṣṭubh** <term>a meter of 32 syllables</term>; and the fifth is **Virāṭ-rūpā** <term>a specific variation of the Virāṭ meter</term> because it possesses the required characteristics, consisting of three lines of eleven syllables and one of eight.

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Here is the first verse ॥<-
Conditions arise one after another; from the cover, the Concealed One has understood. He gazes upon all things in the lap of the Mother. ॥ 1 ॥

> **Conditions** | **forth** | **are born** | **forth** | **from the cover** | **the Concealed One** | **has understood** | **in the lap** | **of the Mother** | **widely** | **he gazes** ॥ 1 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
Various unfavorable **conditions** <note>original: *avasthāḥ*</note> or stages of life arise for the Seer Vavri, one after the other. **Agni**—the "Concealed One" <note>original: *vavriḥ*</note> and the enjoyer of oblations—has **fully understood** <note>original: *praciketa*</note> these situations. The sense is: "May he know them and remove them." This refers to Agni who **gazes upon** <note>original: *vicaṣṭe*</note> or sees every object situated in the **lap** <note>original: *upasthe*</note> or proximity of the **Mother** <note>original: *mātuḥ*</note>, which is the Earth.

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the second verse ॥<-
The mindful ones have called him; they guard the strength without blinking. They have entered the firm city. ॥ 2 ॥

> **They called** | **widely** | **the mindful ones** | **without blinking** | **the strength** | **they guard** | **unto** | **the firm** | **city** | **they have entered** ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
Those **mindful people** <note>original: *vicitayantaḥ*</note> who know your power, O Agni, **call upon you** <note>original: *juhure*</note> for the sake of the sacrifice. Having called you, they **guard** <note>original: *pānti*</note> your **strength** <note>original: *nṛmṇam*</note> or power with oblations and hymns **without blinking** <note>original: *animiṣam*</note>—meaning constantly. Such people **enter** <note>original: *āvivisṣuḥ*</note> a **firm city** <note>original: *dṛḷhāṃ puram*</note> that is impossible for enemies to conquer. The scripture says elsewhere: "Protect us with a hundred iron cities" (Rig Veda 7.3.7).

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the third verse ॥<-
The people, the creatures of Shvaitreya, have increased in splendor. With a golden ornament on his neck, with great hymns, like one desiring spoils through this honey. ॥ 3 ॥

> **Unto** | **of Shvaitreya** | **the creatures** | **splendidly** | **they increased** | **the peoples** |
> **with a golden neck-ornament** | **with great hymns** | **by this** | **with honey** | **as if** | **desiring spoils** ॥ 3 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Creatures** <note>original: *jantavaḥ*</note> refers to those who are born. The **peoples** <note>original: *kṛṣṭayaḥ*</note>, specifically the human officiating priests, like those [seeking] **honey** <note>original: *madhvā*</note>, by this... <note>text breaks off</note>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on the third verse of the fifth hymn in the fourth book of the Rig Veda and continues with the translation and commentary of the fourth and fifth verses. ## Commentary (Sayana)
...with praise. Or, the word "na" functions as "and." And with the sweetness of the white sky. "White" <note>original: *shvityam*</note> refers to the atmosphere. And they increased the glorious, brilliant strength of the lightning-form **Agni** <term>Agni: the deified fire, central to Vedic ritual</term>. What kind of people? Those whose necks are adorned with **golden ornaments** <note>original: *niṣkagrīvāḥ*; from *niṣka* (gold ornament) and *grīvā* (neck)</note>. Here, the singular form is used in place of the plural. They are those who possess great hymns and desire food.
---
->॥ Here is the fourth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
Like desirable milk, let him hear our faultless, dear hymn along with the two sisters. Like the hot vessel, he has food in his belly; he is undeceived and the eternal destroyer of enemies. ॥ 4 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Dear** | **Milk** | **Like** | **Desirable** | **Faultless** | **Of the two sisters** | **Together** | 
**Hot vessel** | **Like** | **Food-bellied** | **Undeceived** | **Eternal** | **Destroyer** ॥ 4 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
May **Agni**, who is the companion of the "two sisters"—meaning Heaven and Earth—hear our dear, faultless, and desirable hymn, which is as pleasant as milk. What is the nature of Agni? He is like the **Gharma** <term>Gharma: a hot sacrificial vessel or the heated milk offering within it</term>, described as "having food in his belly" <note>original: *vājajaṭharaḥ*</note>. This means his belly contains the offerings. Just as the Gharma vessel is filled with oblations like clarified butter and milk, so is he filled with offerings. He is "undeceived," meaning he is not harmed by his enemies, and he is the eternal and constant destroyer of foes.
---
->॥ Here is the fifth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
O Radiant One, playing, be present for us, being recognized by your ashes and the wind. Let those fierce, well-sharpened flames of his, which reside in the fire-pit and carry the offering, not be too sharp for us. ॥ 5 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Playing** | **Our** | **O Radiant One** | **Towards** | **Be** | **With** | **Ashes** | **Wind** | **Being recognized** | 
**Those** | **His** | **Being** | **Overpowering** | **Like** | **Sharp** | **Well-sharpened** | **Flame-bearers** | **Residing in the fire-pit** ॥ 5 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Radiant Agni** <note>original: *raśme*</note>, playing in the forests and being perfectly recognized by your effect (the ashes) and by the wind (the **Maruts** <note>storm deities</note>) who impels you, please turn toward us. "Residing in the fire-pit" refers to staying within the sacrificial fire. The "flame-bearers" are the flames that carry the oblation to the gods. These flames are well-sharpened and capable of overpowering enemies. Let those flames of this sacrificer (me) not be too piercing or "sharp" <note>original: *tigmāḥ*</note> toward us. (The word *san* is a form of the verb "to be" in the **imperative mood** <term>loṭ: the grammatical mood used for commands or requests</term>).

->॥ Thus ends the eleventh group of the first chapter of the fourth book ॥<-

The sixth hymn, beginning with "This Agni" <note>original: *yam agne*</note>, consists of fourteen verses. It was revealed to the Seers of the **Angiras** <note>an ancient family of priests</note> family, specifically those known as the Prayasvats. It is dedicated to Agni. The final verse is in the **Pankti** meter <term>a meter consisting of five lines of eight syllables each</term>...

<summary>This page concludes the fifth hymn of the fourth book, focusing on Agni's role as a consumer of offerings and his relationship with the atmosphere and the wind. It emphasizes the priest's plea for Agni's powerful flames to remain beneficial and not destructive to the worshiper.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from the general introduction of Hymn 20 in the fifth Mandala (Book 5) of the Rig Veda to the specific details of its first three verses. It includes the ritual instructions, the poetic text, word-by-word breakdowns, and the traditional commentary by the scholar Sayana.</meta>

Book 5, Section 2, Hymn 20. || Fourth Book (Ashtaka) ||

The remaining verses are in the **Anushtubh** <term>Anushtubh: a common Vedic meter consisting of four quarters of eight syllables each</term> meter. This is confirmed by the index (Anukramani), which states: "O Agni, the group of four [verses] beginning with 'the winner of food' <note>original: *yam agne vājasātamam*</note> ends with the **Pankti** meter."

The ritual application (viniyoga) is mentioned in the "Morning Recitation" (Pratar-anuvaka) and the "Litany to the Ashvins" (Ashvina-shastra). In the multi-day sacrifice known as **Idhma-tuvira**, this hymn is used for the "Clarified Butter Litany" (Ajya-shastra) on the second day. As stated in the *Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra* (10. 2.): "On the second day, the 'Winner of Food' hymn is the Clarified Butter offering."

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The First Verse ॥ <-

O **Agni**, whichever wealth you consider to be the greatest winner of food, make that famous treasure of ours—joined with our songs—known among the gods. ॥ 1 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Which** | **O Agni** | **Best winner of food** | **You** | **Even** | **Consider** | **Wealth** | 
**That** | **Of us** | **By songs** | **Famous** | **Among the gods** | **Praise/Celebrate** | **Companion** ॥ 1 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, O **best winner of food** <note>original: *vājasātama*; from *vāja* (food/booty) and *sātama* (best giver/winner)</note>, whatever **wealth** <note>original: *rayim*</note>—specifically the wealth in the form of our sacrificial offerings—that **you consider** or recognize; the word "even" <note>original: *cit*</note> is used here to fill out the poetic meter. Make **that wealth of ours**—which is **famous** (worthy of being heard), praiseworthy, and **joined** with our **songs** of praise—reach **among the gods** <note>original: *devatra*</note>. This means you should make the gods accept our offering.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Second Verse ॥ <-

O **Agni**, those who do not offer [sacrifices] to you, though they are grown great with wealth, are deprived of their fierce strength. They fall into the hatred and the crooked violence of those who follow other laws. ॥ 2 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Those who** | **O Agni** | **Not** | **Offer** | **To you** | **Grown/Increased** | **Of the fierce** | **Strength** | 
**Away** | **Hatred** | **Away** | **Crookedness/Violence** | **Of another law** | **They encounter/reach** ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, those people who have **grown** rich with cattle and other treasures, but who **do not offer** <note>original: *nerayanti*; from *na* (not) and *irayanti* (send/offer)</note> oblations to **you**, are led away from **fierce strength** <note>original: *shavasaḥ*</note> or food. This means they become powerless. Furthermore, they encounter the **hatred** (opposition) and the **crooked violence** of **those who follow other laws** <note>original: *anyavratasya*</note>—meaning those whose ritual actions are separate from the Vedic path, such as the **Asuras** <term>Asuras: a class of powerful beings often depicted as the rivals or enemies of the Vedic gods</term>.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Third Verse ॥ <-

We choose you as our **Invoker priest**, O **Agni**, the achiever of skill. We, who possess sacrificial food, call upon you, the ancient one, with our song during the rituals. ॥ 3 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Invoker (Hotri)** | **You** | **We choose** | **O Agni** | **Of skill** | **Achiever** | 
**In sacrifices** | **Ancient/First** | **With song** | **Possessing food** | **We call** ॥ 3 ॥

<vocab>
- **Anushtubh**: A Vedic meter (32 syllables total).
- **Viniyoga**: The specific ritual use or application of a hymn.
- **Vajasatama**: "Best winner of booty or food," a title for Agni.
- **Rayi**: Wealth or treasure, often interpreted as the sacrificial offering itself.
- **Devatra**: Among the gods or in the presence of the divine.
- **Hotri**: The "Invoker" priest who recites the Rig Veda verses to call the gods.
- **Daksha**: Spiritual skill, mental strength, or will.
- **Yajna**: The sacred ritual or sacrifice.
</vocab>

It provides ritual instructions for its use in the Idhma-tuvira sacrifice and explains the first three verses, which focus on Agni's role in delivering offerings to the gods and the consequences for those who neglect the rituals.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Anushtubh meter, Vajasatama, Hotri, ritual offerings, Asuras, Vedic sacrifice, Sayana commentary</keywords>

324 || Rig Veda || [Book 4. Chapter 1. Varga 13.]

O Agni, we who possess food <note>original: *prayavantah*</note> and carry this name, choose you—the accomplisher of strength and the invoker <note>original: *hotāraṃ*</note> who calls the gods. Furthermore, in the sacrifices, we call upon you, the foremost one, with speech in the form of praise. We offer our hymns.

-> ॥ The Fourth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
In this way, so that we may be under your protection, O powerful one, day after day; for wealth and for the sacred Law, O wise one, may we rejoice together with cattle, and may we rejoice together with heroes. ॥ 4 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**In this way** | **So that** | **Your** | **For protection** | **O powerful one** | **Day by day** | 
**For wealth** | **For the sacred Law** | **O wise one** | **With cattle** | **May we be** | **Rejoicing together** | **With heroes** | **May we be** | **Rejoicing together** ॥ 4 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **powerful** <note>original: *sahasa-van*</note> Agni, **day by day**—meaning every single day—make it so that we **may be** recipients of **your protection**. O **wise one** <note>original: *sukrato*, one of good works</note>, act so that we may attain **wealth** and the **sacred Law** <note>original: *ṛtāya*, the sacrifice or the cosmic order</note>. Furthermore, **may we be rejoicing together** <note>original: *sadhamādaḥ*</note> alongside our **cattle**. And **may we be rejoicing together** with our **heroes**—meaning our sons and descendants. Please bring this to pass.

-> ॥ This concludes the twelfth Varga of the first chapter of the fourth Book ॥ <-

The seventh hymn, beginning with "Like Manu" <note>original: *manušvat-tvā*</note>, consists of four verses and is attributed to the seer Sasa of the Atri family. The index <note>original: *Anukramani*</note> states: "Like Manu" is the opening. As previously mentioned, the hymns ending in **Pankti** <term>Pankti: a Vedic meter consisting of five lines, usually of eight syllables each</term> include the three starting from this one. The remaining verses are in the **Anushtubh** <term>Anushtubh: a four-line meter with eight syllables per line</term> meter. Agni is the deity. The ritual application <note>original: *viniyoga*</note> is cited in the Morning Recitation and the Litany to the Ashvins.

-> ॥ Here is the first verse of that hymn ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Like Manu, we set you down; like Manu, we kindle you. O Agni, O Angiras, like Manu, sacrifice to the gods for the one who seeks the gods. ॥ 1 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**In the manner of Manu** | **You** | **Down** | **We set** | **In the manner of Manu** | **Well** | **We kindle** | 
**O Agni** | **In the manner of Manu** | **O Angiras** | **The gods** | **For the god-seeker** | **Sacrifice** ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, **we set you down**—we establish you—**like Manu** <note>original: *manušvat*; Manu is the archetypal first sacrificer</note>. The word *manušvan* is a variation of Manu. <note>Sayana provides a technical grammatical note here explaining that the word follows a specific rule where the "u" sound is treated specially in Vedic Sanskrit.</note> **Like Manu, we kindle you**—meaning we light the sacrificial fire. O **Angiras** <note>original: *aṅgiraḥ*; a title for Agni referring to his fiery essence or his connection to the ancient Angiras priests</note>, for the sake of the **god-seeker** <note>original: *devayate*, the patron of the sacrifice</note>, and **like Manu**—meaning for the sake of the descendants of Manu—**sacrifice to the gods**.

<vocab>
- Sahasāvan: Powerful/Mighty (epithet of Agni)
- Dive dive: Day by day / daily
- Sukrato: One of good works / wise (epithet of Agni)
- Sadhamādaḥ: Feasting together / rejoicing together
- Manuṣvat: Like Manu / in the manner of Manu (the ancestral human)
- Aṅgiraḥ: Angiras (a title for Agni)
- Devayate: For one who desires the gods (the patron or sacrificer)
</vocab>

## Hymn Text

**O Agni, you are indeed kindled among the human race, being well-pleased [by our hymns]. The sacrificial ladles reach you in a continuous stream, O you who are born of ghee, O you for whom melted butter is the offering. ॥ 2 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, being **well-pleased** <note>original: *suprītaḥ*</note> by the hymns of praise, **you are kindled**—you shine brightly—**among the human race** in the world of men. The **sacrificial ladles**, filled with oblations, **reach you**—they attain you—**continuously**, in an uninterrupted sequence. O **well-born** one <note>original: *sujāta*</note>, O **one to whom ghee is poured as food** <note>original: *sarpi rā sute*, referring to the melted butter offered into the fire</note>.

## Commentary (Sayana)

Being **pleased together** <note>original: *sajoṣasaḥ*</note>, **all the gods made you** their **messenger**. For this reason, O **Sage** <note>original: *kave*, interpreted here as *krāntadarśin* or "all-seeing"</note>, the sacrificers **serving**—attending to—**you**, the **shining god**, **praise you in the sacrifices**. They ask you to call the other gods to the ritual.

->sit upon ॥ 4 ॥<-

The **mortal** man—the human worshipper—should **worship** <note>original: *īḷīta*, to praise or invoke</note> the shining **Agni**, the leader, **for your sake** through the **sacrifice to the gods** <note>original: *devayajyayā*, for the purpose of a divine offering</note>. O **bright one** <note>original: *śukra*, meaning one who possesses pure light</note>, being **well-kindled** and increased by the offerings...

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on Verse 4 of the 21st Hymn (Sukta) and introduces the 22nd Hymn of the 5th Mandala. It marks the transition from Varga 13 to Varga 14 within the first Adhyaya of the fourth Ashtaka.</meta>

326 || Rig Veda || [Ashtaka 4. Adhyaya 1. Varga 14.]

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Shine.** Be radiant. May you **sit**—occupy as a deity—in the **place of sacrifice** <note>original: *yajñasthānam*</note>, which is the **womb** or source of **truth** <note>original: *ṛtasya*, referring to the cosmic order or the sacrifice itself</note>, and is the means for attaining heaven. The word is repeated to show great reverence.

->॥ Thus ends the thirteenth varga in the first adhyaya of the fourth ashtaka ॥<-

The eighth hymn, beginning with "**Forward, O Vishvasaman**" <note>original: *pra viśvasāman*</note>, consists of four verses. The Seer (Rishi) is Vishvasaman, a descendant of Atri. The fourth verse is in the *Pankti* meter, while the remaining three are in the *Anushtubh* meter. The deity addressed is **Agni**. As stated in the Index <note>original: *Anukramani*</note>: "Forward, O Vishvasaman, [the hymn] by Vishvasaman..." The ritual application has already been mentioned in the context of the Morning Litany and the *Ashvin Shastra* <note>specific parts of the Soma sacrifice</note>.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Here is the first verse ॥<-

**O Vishvasaman, offer a radiant word of praise to the one of purifying luster, who is to be praised in the sacrifices, the Invoker, the most delightful among the people. ॥ 1 ॥**

**Word-for-word analysis**
Forward | O Vishvasaman | radiant | word | to the one of purifying luster |
who | in sacrifices | to be praised | Invoker | most delightful | among the people ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Vishvasaman**! <note>This is an address to the Rishi/Seer of the hymn</note>. You must **offer praise** <note>original: *prārca*</note> with a **radiant word**—a hymn shining like a beam of light—to Agni, who possesses **purifying luster**. That Agni is **to be praised** by all the performers of the sacrifice **in the sacrifices**, he is the **Invoker** <note>original: *hotā*, the priest who calls the gods</note>, and is the **most delightful** or most praiseworthy **among the people**.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Now the second verse ॥<-

**Establish Agni, the knower of all births, the deity, the officiating priest. May the sacrifice, which most effectively reaches the gods, proceed today in a continuous stream. ॥ 2 ॥**

**Word-for-word analysis**
Down (establish) | Agni | knower of all births | establish | deity | officiating priest |
Forward | sacrifice | may it go | continuously | today | most reaching of the gods ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Sacrificers, **establish**—place firmly—**Agni**, the **knower of all births** <note>original: <term>Jatavedas</term>, an epithet for Agni meaning he who knows all created beings or possesses all wealth</note>, the **deity**, the shining one, the **officiating priest** <note>original: <term>Ritvij</term>, one who sacrifices according to the seasons</note>. Furthermore, may the **sacrifice**—the oblation being offered by us which is the means of the sacrifice—**proceed** toward that Agni **today**, on this very day, in a **continuous** or uninterrupted manner, being the **most reaching of the gods** <note>original: *devavyacastamaḥ*, the one that most effectively brings the gods to the ritual</note>.

---

**We mortals, seeking protection, have thought of you, the deity of conscious mind. We pray for your excellent favor. ॥ 3 ॥**

The tenth hymn in this section, beginning with "Agni, you are our..." <note>original: *agne tvaṃ naḥ*</note>, consists of four verses. According to the Index <note>the *Anukramanika*, a traditional catalog of Vedic hymns</note>: The seers of this hymn are the Gaupayanas or Laupayanas—specifically the brothers Bandhu, Subandhu, Shrutabandhu, and Viprabandhu. It is composed in the *Dvaipada* <note>a "two-footed" or two-line meter</note> form. This is because they are classified as twenty-syllable *Dvaipada-Viraj* meters. Agni is the deity being addressed.

**Ritual usage:** In the Great Sacrifice to the Fathers <note>original: *Maha-pitriyajna*; a ritual honoring ancestors</note>, the priests should mutter this entire hymn while they are walking toward the *Ahavaniya* <note>the eastern sacrificial fire</note>. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "Then they come together toward him <note>the fire</note>, muttering 'Let us not go away...' and 'Agni, you are our...'" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.19). 

Furthermore, during the Ten-Night ceremony <note>original: *Dasharatra*</note>, on the sixth day during the third pressing of Soma, the Maitravaruna priest recites two verses starting with "Agni, you..." and one starting with "You, O most brilliant..." <note>original: *taṃ tvā śociṣṭha*</note>. Together, these three two-line verses form the *Stotriya* <note>chant</note>. This is indicated in the manuals: "Agni, you are our nearest..." and "Agni, be well-kindled..." (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 8.2).

->॥ Here are the first and second verses ॥<-

Agni, the dweller, famous for wealth—reach out to us; give us the most splendid riches. ॥ 1 ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, you are the **provider of shelter** <note>original: *varūthyaḥ*</note>, meaning one who is to be chosen or served. Alternatively, it means one surrounded by "shelters" <note>the protective wooden fences around the altar</note>. Be **nearest** <note>original: *antamaḥ*</note> to **us**, meaning our most intimate relation. **And also** <note>original: *utāpi*</note> be our **protector** and **gracious** <note>original: *śivaḥ*</note>, meaning a bringer of happiness. **Agni** is the **dweller** <note>original: *vasuḥ*</note>—the one who causes everyone to dwell, the leader of all. You are **famous for wealth** <note>original: *vasuśravāḥ*</note>, meaning your food and riches are pervasive. **Reach out** <note>original: *nakṣi*</note> toward us; come to us. **Give** <note>original: *dāḥ*</note> us **riches** <note>original: *rayiṃ*</note>, consisting of cattle and other wealth, which are **most splendid** <note>original: *dyumattaman*</note> or exceedingly bright.

**"Unto you, Agni..."** <note>original: *acchā vo agnim*</note> is the eleventh hymn, consisting of nine verses. According to the Index <note>the *Anukramanika*, a traditional catalog of Vedic hymns</note>: "Unto you... nine [verses], the Vasuyus, Anushtubh." The seers of this hymn are the descendants of Atri named Vasuyu. The meter is *Anushtubh* <note>a four-line stanza with eight syllables per line</note>. According to the general definitions for this book, Agni is the deity. 

The ritual application <note>original: *viniyoga*</note> is stated to be in the Morning Litany and the Litany to the Ashvins <note>original: *prātar-anuvāka* and *āśvina-śastra*; specific collections of hymns recited at dawn</note>. During the morning Soma-pressing ceremony, when the priest is commanded, "O Invoker <note>original: *acchāvāka*</note>, speak!", he should recite the verse "Unto you, Agni, for protection..." This is indicated in the ritual manual: **"He recites the verse 'Unto you, Agni, for protection...' (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 5.7)."**

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the first verse ॥ <-
Sing toward your divine Agni for protection; he is our benefactor.
The son of the powerful ones, the possessor of truth, shall grant [our wishes] and carry us past our enemies. ॥ 1 ॥

**[Word-for-word analysis]**
Unto. Your. Agni. For protection. Divine. Sing. He. Our. Benefactor.
Shall grant. Son. Of the powerful ones. Possessing truth. Carries across. Enemies. ॥ 1 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **seekers of wealth** <note>original: *vasuyavaḥ*</note>, you all **sing** <note>original: *gāsi* / *abhipragāyata*</note> **toward** <note>original: *acchā*</note> the **divine Agni for protection**. Agni is the benefactor who causes the sacrificers to dwell <note>original: *vāsayitā*</note> in their houses for the sake of the fire-sacrifice; **may that Agni grant** to us our desires. He is the **son of the powerful ones** <note>original: *ṛṣūṇām*</note>. He is figuratively called a "son" because he is produced by the sages through the churning of the fire-sticks. **Possessing truth** <note>original: *ṛtāvā*</note>—meaning one who is truthful or one who possesses the sacrificial waters—may **that Agni carry us across our enemies**, meaning may he help us overcome our foes. ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Even the ancients**, the great seers of old, [kindled him]. He is the **Invoker** <note>original: *hotṛ*</note>, the one who calls the gods to the sacrifice. He is **delightful-tongued** <note>original: *mandra-jihvam*</note>. This means he possesses a tongue that delights the gods through the offering of oblations. Or, it means a tongue that is itself delightful. As the ancient etymologist Yaska says: "**Mandra-jihvam** means a tongue that praises or a tongue that delights" (Nirukta 6.23). **With beautiful flames** <note>original: *sudītibhiḥ*</note>—with love-

- Agni: The fire god, central to Vedic ritual as the messenger between humans and gods.
- Vasuyu: "Seeking wealth"; here it refers both to the family of the poets and the intent of the worshipers.
- Rita: The cosmic order or truth that governs the universe and the sacrifice.
- Hotri: The "Invoker" priest who recites the Rig Vedic hymns.
- Mandrajihva: A compound meaning "having a pleasant or praising tongue," referring to the crackling and "consuming" action of the sacrificial fire.

...associated with his splendors, the one whose wealth is light, that Agni whom they kindled—whom they have fully ignited. Even the gods themselves kindled this Agni; they fully ignited him. For that Agni is "true" <note>original: *satya*</note>; he is true to his promise. The word *it* <note>a particle found in the original Sanskrit</note> is used merely to fill the meter.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the third verse ॥ <-

**May he, with the most excellent thought, with the best and most favorable mind,**
**O Agni, shine riches upon us through our hymns, O adorable one. ॥ 3 ॥**

**May he . us . with thought . with the most excellent . with the best . and . with a favorable mind .**
**O Agni . riches . shine . upon us . through hymns . O adorable one. ॥ 3 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Through hymns** <note>original: *suvṛktibhiḥ*</note> means by the songs of praise being recited. **O Adorable one** <note>original: *vareṇya*</note> means O you who are worthy of being chosen, O **Agni**. **May he**, that is you, through the **most excellent** <note>original: *variṣṭhayā*</note>—the very best—and **best** <note>original: *śreṣṭhayā*</note>—the exceedingly praiseworthy—**thought** <note>original: *no dhītī*</note>, meaning through our action characterized by service, and with a **favorable mind**. The term "favorable mind" <note>original: *sumati*</note> here refers to the *Shastra* <note>a specific type of recited liturgical hymn</note>. Being pleased by this hymn, **shine riches** <note>original: *rāyo dīdīhi*</note>—that is, grant wealth—**to us**.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the fourth verse ॥ <-

**Agni rules among the gods; Agni enters among mortals.**
**Agni is our carrier of oblations; honor Agni with your thoughts. ॥ 4 ॥**

**Agni . among the gods . rules . Agni . among mortals . entering .**
**Agni . our . carrier of oblations . Agni . with thoughts . honor. ॥ 4 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

That **Agni** who **rules among the gods** <note>original: *deveṣu rājati*</note> shines in the form of a deity in their midst. That **Agni** who **enters among mortals** <note>original: *marteṣu āviśan*</note> enters into humans in the form of the sacrificial fires, such as the *Ahavaniya* <note>the consecrated fire used for offerings to the gods</note>. That **Agni** who is **our carrier of oblations** <note>original: *havyavāhana*</note> is the one who bears the offerings meant for the gods in our sacrifices. Therefore, O sacrificers, **honor** <note>original: *saparyata*</note>—that is, serve—**that Agni with thoughts** <note>original: *dhībhiḥ*</note>, which means with hymns of praise.

## Critical Notes

In the sacrifice for those desiring a son <note>original: *Putrakāmeṣṭi*</note>, the two verses beginning with "Agni, the most famous" are the invitation and offering verses <note>original: *yājyānuvākyā*</note> for the *Svishtakrit* <note>an offering to Agni at the end of a ritual to ensure its success</note>. It is also indicated in the ritual manual: <note>Rig Veda 5.25.5</note> "Agni, the most famous..." these two are the concluding verses <note>original: *saṃyājye*</note>. <note>Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.10.</note>

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the fifth verse ॥ <-

**Agni gives a son to the giver: a son who is most famous, possessing much sacred knowledge,**
**the most excellent, unvanquished, and making his lord famous. ॥ 5 ॥**

<note>Glossary of key terms used in this section:</note>
- **Agni**: The Fire deity, the central focus of these hymns.
- **Adorable (Vareṇya)**: Choice, worthy of being sought after.
- **Carrier of oblations (Havyavāhana)**: A title for Agni describing his role in transporting the essence of burnt offerings to the heavens.
- **Praise (Stuti)**: A hymn or prayer intended to please the deity.
- **Sacrifice for a son (Putrakāmeṣṭi)**: A specific Vedic ritual performed by those wishing for male progeny.
- **Concluding verses (Saṃyājye)**: Two specific mantras recited during the final stage of a sacrifice.

## Rig Veda | Book 4, Chapter 1, Section 18

## Hymn Text

<note>Word-by-word breakdown (Pada-patha) for Rig Veda 5.6.5</note>
**Agni . the one who is most possessed of great fame . the one who is most possessed of great prayers . the highest . the uninjured . the lord who makes [his fathers] heard . a son . he gives . to the giver [of oblations]. ॥ 5 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Agni** gives a **son** to the **giver** <note>original: *dāśuṣe*</note>, the sacrificer who has offered oblations. This son is described as **the one who is most possessed of great fame** <note>original: *tuviśravastamam*</note>, meaning one who possesses an abundance of food or renown; **the one who is most possessed of great prayers** <note>original: *tuvibrahmāṇam*</note>, meaning one who has many hymns; **the highest** <note>original: *uttamam*</note> or most excellent; **the uninjured** <note>original: *atūrtam*</note>, one who is not harmed by enemies; and **the lord who makes [his fathers] heard** <note>original: *śrāvayatpatim*</note>. This last term means he is one who makes his fathers, the protectors, well-known and famous through his own righteous deeds. Such is the son he gives—or rather, may he give.

->॥ Thus ends the seventeenth section (Varga) of the first chapter (Adhyaya) of the fourth book ॥<-

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the sixth verse ॥<-

**Agni gives a protector of the virtuous, a conqueror who overcomes [enemies] in battle with his men;**
**Agni gives a horse, swift-moving, a victor, and one who is never defeated. ॥ 6 ॥**

<note>Word-by-word breakdown (Pada-patha)</note>
**Agni . gives . a protector of the virtuous . a conqueror . who . through battle . with men .**
**Agni . a horse . swift-moving . a victor . one who is never defeated. ॥ 6 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Agni gives** a son who is a **protector of the virtuous** <note>original: *satpatim*</note>, a guardian of good men. This son is a **conqueror** <note>original: *sasāham*</note> **who** overcomes his enemies **through battle** along **with his men** <note>original: *nṛbhiḥ*</note>, meaning his attendants or followers. May he give us such a son. Furthermore, Agni gives a **horse** <note>original: *atyam*</note>. The word *atya* refers to a horse because "it goes constantly" <note>original: *atati satataṃ gacchatītyatyo*</note>. This horse is **swift-moving** <note>original: *raghuṣyadam*</note>—where *raghu* means light or fast and *syada* means speed—and is a **victor** over enemies, remaining **undefeated** by them. May he give such a horse.

In the context of the **Horse Sacrifice** <term>Ashvamedha; a royal ritual to assert sovereignty</term>, during the offerings to the goddess Pushan, the verse beginning with "That which is most effective" is used as the concluding prayer <term>sviṣṭakṛt; the "maker of the right sacrifice"</term>. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "The two concluding prayers to Agni are 'that which is most effective' and 'that to Agni'" <note>original reference: Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 10. 6.</note>.

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the seventh verse ॥<-

**O Agni, whatever song is most effective at carrying [our prayer], sing that loudly,**
**O you whose wealth is light; like a queen, riches and strengths rise up from you. ॥ 7 ॥**

<note>Word-by-word breakdown (Pada-patha)</note>
**Whatever . is most effective at carrying . that . for Agni . loudly . sing . O you whose wealth is light .**
**Like a queen . from you . riches . from you . strengths . upwards . rise. ॥ 7 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Whatever** hymn is **most effective at carrying** <note>original: *vāhiṣṭham*</note> our intent, that is performed **for Agni**. Therefore, **O you whose wealth is light** <note>original: *vibhāvaso*</note>—O Agni, you whose treasure is your radiance—grant us **loud** <note>original: *bṛhat*</note> or great food and wealth, or speech. If one asks how Agni can be the giver of the wealth belonging to others, the text replies:

Mandala 5. Chapter 2. Hymn 26.] || Fourth Book || 333

...because from you, the Great Wealth <note>original: mahiṣī ratiḥ</note>—meaning great riches—arises and goes upward. Foods <note>original: vājāḥ</note> also arise from you. The word "like" <note>original: iva</note> here is used as a poetic filler.

## Hymn Text

->॥ The Eighth Verse ॥<-

<note>Rig Veda 5.26.8</note>
Your brilliant flames are spoken of as great, like the pressing-stone <note>used to crush the Soma plant</note>. And may your own sound come from the sky like thunder. ॥ 8 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Your . brilliant . flames . like-the-pressing-stone . is-spoken-of . great .
And-also . your . thunder . like . sound . let-it-come . by-its-own-power . from-the-sky ॥ 8 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O <term>Agni (Deity of fire)</term>, your rays or flames are brilliant and radiant. You, being great and mighty, are praised like the pressing-stone <note>original: grāveva</note> used in the sacrifice. Furthermore, by your own power, the sound of you—the shining one—arises from the sky like the rumbling of clouds or thunder <note>original: tanyatur-yathā</note>.

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ The Ninth Verse ॥<-

<note>Rig Veda 5.26.9</note>
Thus have we, desiring wealth, praised Agni who is full of power. May he, of excellent wisdom, carry us across all those who hate us, like a boat [across water]. ॥ 9 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Thus . Agni . desiring-wealth . the-powerful-one . we-have-praised .
He . us . all . enemies . may-he-carry-across . like-a-boat . of-excellent-wisdom ॥ 9 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

We, the <term>Vasuyavah (the seers who desire wealth)</term>, have praised <note>original: vavandima</note> Agni in this manner—Agni, who acts with a strength that overcomes others. May that Agni of righteous action carry us past all our enemies. How? Like one crossing a river by means of a <term>Nava (boat)</term>.

->**॥ Thus ends the eighteenth section of the first chapter of the fourth book ॥**<-

---

## Ritual Notes / Introduction (Hymn 27)

The twelfth hymn of this section, beginning "O Agni, O Purifier," consists of nine verses. The seers are the **Vasuyus**. The poetic meter is <term>Gayatri (a specific three-line meter)</term>. The deity is **Agni**. The index <note>Anukramani</note> states: "Agni is in Gayatri." This hymn is used in the morning recitation <note>original: prātaranuvāka</note> during the fire-ritual, specifically in the Gayatri portion, and also in the litany for the Ashvins <note>original: āśvina-śastra</note>. This is indicated in the manual: "In the two hymns 'O Agni, O Purifier' and 'Your messenger...'" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.13). Additionally, in the second offering of the fire-establishment ritual, this verse is the sacrificial prayer for the first oblation. This is recorded as: "May he be our purifier, O shining one... O Agni, purifier with your radiance" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.1).

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The First Verse ॥ <-

O <term>Agni</term> <note>the deity of fire</note>, the Purifier, with your radiant and joyful tongue, O God, bring the gods here and sacrifice to them. ॥ 1 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Agni . Purifier . with-radiance . joyful . O-God . with-tongue . hither . the-gods . bring . sacrifice . and ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Purifier** <note>original: pāvaka</note>, you who cleanse, with your own light (radiance), and with a **joyful** tongue that gladdens the gods, O **God**, the shining Agni, **bring** the gods here for the sake of the sacrifice. **And sacrifice** to them; that is, perform the ritual for them.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Second Verse ॥ <-

We call upon you, who drips with clarified butter, O you of variegated luster, you who see the light of heaven; bring the gods for their enjoyment. ॥ 2 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
That . you . dripping-with-ghee (clarified butter) . we-call-upon . of-variegated-luster . heaven-seeing . the-gods . hither . for-enjoyment . bring ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Dripper of Ghee** <note>original: ghṛtasno</note>, you who send forth the clarified butter, or perhaps you who are produced by it; O **Variegated Luster** <note>original: citrabhanu</note>, you who possess various kinds of rays—this is an address to him. We **call upon** you—**you** who are **heaven-seeing** <note>original: svardṛśaṃ</note>, the witness of all things. Therefore, **bring** the gods for their **enjoyment**, to consume the sacrificial offerings.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Third Verse ॥ <-

O Seer, we kindle you, the one who receives the sacrificial offering, the radiant and great one, O Agni, at the sacrifice. ॥ 3 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Receiving-the-offering . you . O-Seer . radiant . well . we-kindle . O-Agni . great . at-the-sacrifice ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Seer** <note>original: kave</note>, O Agni who possesses visionary wisdom, we **kindle** <note>original: samidhīmahi</note> you—meaning we light you up brightly—at the **sacrifice**. We kindle **you**, who are the **one who receives the offering**, the **radiant** one, and the **great** or mighty one.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Fourth Verse ॥ <-

O Agni, come with all the gods for the giving of the oblation; we choose you as the invoking priest. ॥ 4 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Agni . with-all . hither . come . with-the-gods . for-the-giving-of-oblation . the-invoker . you . we-choose ॥ 4 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, **come** to the sacrifice together **with all** the other **gods** for the sake of the **giving of the oblation**—that is, for the benefit of the patron who gives the offerings. For **we choose** you, we pray to **you**, as the **Invoker** <note>original: hotāraṃ</note> who calls the gods to the ritual.

## Hymn Text

-> **॥ The Fifth Verse ॥** <-

O **Agni**, bring great strength to the <term>sacrificial patron</term> <note>original: yajamāna; the one who sponsors the ritual</note> who presses the soma juice. Sit upon the **sacred grass** <note>original: barhis; the grass mat prepared for the gods</note> along with the gods. ॥ 5 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
For-the-patron . for-the-one-pressing-soma . hither . O-Agni . great-strength . bring . with-the-gods . hither . sit . on-the-sacred-grass ॥ 5 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, for the **sacrificial patron** who is performing the pressing of the soma juice, **bring**—that is, cause him to obtain—**great strength** or excellent might. Furthermore, **sit** upon the **sacred grass** at this sacrifice along with the other **gods**.

-> ॥ Thus ends the nineteenth section of the first chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> **॥ The Sixth Verse ॥** <-

O **Agni**, conqueror of thousands, being kindled, you nourish the **sacred laws** <note>original: dharmani; the cosmic and ritual order</note>. You are the praiseworthy messenger of the gods. ॥ 6 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Being-kindled . conqueror-of-thousands . O-Agni . sacred-laws . you-nourish . of-the-gods . messenger . praiseworthy ॥ 6 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **conqueror of thousands**, O **Agni**, who conquers a thousand enemies, you who are **being kindled** and made to shine by our oblations; you are **praiseworthy** and commendable. Being the **messenger of the gods**, you **nourish**—that is, you foster and complete—our **sacred laws**, which are our ritual actions and sacrifices.

---

## Hymn Text

-> **॥ The Seventh Verse ॥** <-

Establish **Agni**, the **Knower of All Beings** <note>original: jātavedas</note>, the carrier of the sacrifice, the most youthful god, the priest. ॥ 7 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Down . Agni . knower-of-all-beings . sacrifice-carrier . most-youthful . establish . the-god . the-priest ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O sacrificial patrons, **establish** or place down the **Agni** who is the **Knower of All Beings** <note>Sayana explains the original 'jatavedas' as: he who knows all beings that have been born</note>. Establish him who is the **carrier of the sacrifice** <note>original: hotravaham</note>, who bears the ritual to the heavens; the **most youthful** <note>original: yavisthyam; implying the most vigorous and newly kindled</note> god, the shining one; and the **priest** <note>original: rtvijam</note>, the one who sacrifices at the proper time.

---

## Hymn Text

-> **॥ The Eighth Verse ॥** <-

May the **sacrifice** go forward continuously today, filling the space for the gods; spread the **sacred grass** for Agni to sit upon. ॥ 8 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Forward . the-sacrifice . let-it-go . continuously . today . filling-the-space-for-gods . spread . sacred-grass . for-sitting-upon ॥ 8 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Today**, on this day, may the **sacrifice**—meaning the oblation which is the means of the ritual—**go forward** toward the gods so that it becomes **continuous** or uninterrupted. This sacrifice is **filling the space for the gods** <note>original: devavyacastamaḥ</note>, meaning it is most widely occupied by the gods and the radiant chanters. O priests, **spread the sacred grass** for the sake of **sitting**—that is, to provide a seat for Agni.

---

## Hymn Text

-> **॥ The Ninth Verse ॥** <-

May the <term>Maruts</term> <note>storm deities</note>, the <term>Ashvins</term> <note>twin physician gods of the dawn</note>, **Mitra**, and **Varuna** sit here—the gods with all their folk. ॥ 9 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Hither . this . the-Maruts . the-two-Ashvins . Mitra . let-them-sit . Varuna . the-gods . with-all . folk ॥ 9 ॥

<meta>This page concludes the 20th section (Varga) of the 1st Chapter (Adhyaya) of the 4th Book (Ashtaka) and begins Hymn 27 of the 5th Mandala. It transitions from a general invocation of the gods to a "praise of gifts" (danastuti), where the seer acknowledges the generosity of royal patrons like King Tryaruna.</meta>

May the **Maruts** (the storm-god host), the **Ashvins** (the twin physicians of the gods), **Mitra** (the sun-god), and **Varuna**—all these gods—sit upon this **sacred grass** <note>original: barhis; the ceremonial seating for deities</note> along with their entire kin and followers.

-> ॥ Thus ends the twentieth section of the first chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-

The thirteenth hymn <note>this refers to its position within the current chapter of the commentary; in the Rig Veda it is Mandala 5, Hymn 27</note> begins with the words "With a wagon" <note>original: anasvantā</note> and consists of six verses. According to the **Index** <note>original: anukramaṇikā; a traditional catalog of Vedic hymns</note>: "The hymn 'With a wagon' has six verses. Two are the kings **Tryaruna**, son of Trivrishna, and **Trasadasyu**, son of Purukutsa; the third is **Ashvamedha**, son of Bharata. These three kings together are the seers of this hymn. Alternatively, the seer is **Atri**. The first three verses are in the **Trishtubh** meter, and the last three are in the **Anushtubh** meter. The sixth verse is dedicated to the gods **Indra** and **Agni**, while the remaining five are dedicated to **Agni**." The application of these verses is determined by their specific technical characteristics.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Here is the first verse ॥ <-

The <term>Lord of the Good</term> <note>original: satpatiḥ; a protector of the righteous</note>, the most wise and powerful among the wealthy, **Tryaruna**, descendant of Trivrishna, has bestowed upon me two oxen with a **wagon**. O **Agni**, O **Vaishvanara** <note>original: vaiśvānara; a title of Agni meaning "Belonging to all men"</note>, Tryaruna is renowned for his gifts of ten thousand. ॥ 1 ॥

> With-a-wagon . Lord-of-the-good . has-bestowed . me . two-oxen . most-wise . powerful . among-the-wealthy .
> Descendant-of-Trivrishna . O-Agni . with-ten . thousands . O-Vaishvanara . Tryaruna . is-renowned ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

With this hymn, the <term>Royal Seer</term> <note>original: rājarṣi; a king who is also a spiritual poet</note> describes the gifts given by kings in the presence of the fire. O **Vaishvanara**, you who are **Agni**, the leader of all men! The **Lord of the Good**—meaning the protector of virtuous people—who is **most wise** (the best knower), **powerful**, and **wealthy** <note>the grammar here indicates the wealth of the patron</note>. This **Tryaruna**, the descendant of Trivrishna and a Royal Seer, has **bestowed** upon me—that is, he has given to me—two **oxen** harnessed to a **wagon**, along with ten thousand pieces of gold and other wealth. The word *mame* means "he gave." That Royal Seer is **renowned**; he is known by all people because of this great act of giving.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

He who gives me a hundred and twenty cows, and two bay horses harnessed to a good yoke. O **Vaishvanara**, well-praised and growing in strength, O **Agni**, grant protection to **Tryaruna**. ॥ 2 ॥

> Who . me . hundred . and . twenty . and . of-cows . two-bay-horses . and . harnessed . to-a-good-yoke . gives .
> O-Vaishvanara . well-praised . growing-in-strength . O-Agni . grant . to-Tryaruna . protection ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana) — Continued from Verse 2
He, **Tryaruna**, who gives to me a hundred and hundreds of gold pieces, and twenty cows joined to a wagon, and two well-yoked, strong-shouldered <note>original: sudhurā; refers to horses that pull the yoke well</note> horses <note>original: harī</note>—O **Agni**, the Universal One <note>original: vaiśvānarāgne</note>, who has been well-praised by us and is strengthened by our offerings, grant happiness <note>original: śarma; protection or peace</note> to that Tryaruna.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the third verse ॥ <-

Thus, O **Agni**, desiring your favor, **Trasadasyu** <note>a famous king of the Puru dynasty</note> has offered a new song of praise to you, the most praiseworthy. **Tryaruna**, who listens to my many songs of praise, he who is born of many, speaks to me with a focused mind. ॥ 3 ॥

### Word-by-Word Analysis
Thus | your | O Agni | favor | desiring | to the most praiseworthy | newest [praise] | Trasadasyu | who | my | songs | born of many | many | with a focused [mind] | toward | Tryaruna | speaks ॥ 3 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
That **Tryaruna**, having heard the many songs and praises of me, who has many children <note>original: tuvijātasya; Sayana interprets this here as "having many offspring"</note>, and being pleased, speaks to me with an attentive mind, saying, "Take this, take that." Thus, O **Agni**, **Trasadasyu** also, desiring your newest and best favor for you who are most worthy of praise, has requested me [to accept gifts] saying, "Take this, take that."

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the fourth verse ॥ <-

He who says to me, "Give to **Ashvamedha** <note>here a proper name of a royal patron, not the sacrifice itself</note>, the patron"; he, Ashvamedha, giving wealth with a sacred hymn to the one who approaches him, and giving wisdom to the one who seeks the divine law <note>original: ṛtāyate; one who acts according to truth or performs sacrifice</note>. ॥ 4 ॥

### Word-by-Word Analysis
Who | to me | [speech marker] | speaks | for Ashvamedha | for the patron | giving | with a hymn | wealth | to the one who goes | giving | wisdom | to the one who desires the rite ॥ 4 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
Whoever is a seeker or a beggar speaks to the patron <note>original: sūraye; the one who impels others or gives wealth</note>, the royal sage **Ashvamedha**, saying to me, "Give to him!" This means he begs wealth from Ashvamedha. To that seeker who approaches him with a hymn of praise for **Agni**, Ashvamedha gives wealth <note>original: sanim</note>. O Agni, give sacrificial wisdom to that Ashvamedha who desires the sacrifice.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the fifth verse ॥ <-

Whose hundred spotted <note>original: paruṣāḥ</note> oxen excite me with joy, the gifts of **Ashvamedha**, like **Soma** <note>the sacred ritual drink</note> mixed with milk <note>original: vyāśiraḥ</note>. ॥ 5 ॥

<note>
**Technical Vocabulary:**
- **Universal One (Vaishvanara):** A form of Agni representing the fire that dwells in all humans.
- **Trasadasyu:** A prominent king often mentioned in the Rig Veda as a generous patron of the Seers.
- **Ashvamedha:** While usually the name of a horse sacrifice, here it refers to a specific individual, likely a prince or king, known for his generosity.
- **Soma mixed with milk:** In Vedic ritual, the pressed Soma juice was often mixed with milk (āśir) to mellow its flavor and prepare it for offering.
</note>

## Hymn Text (RV 5.27.5-6)

**Word-by-word Analysis (Verse 5):**
Whose | me | spotted <note>original: paruṣāḥ; Sayana interprets this as "fulfillers of desires"</note> | hundred | up | gladden | bulls | of Ashvamedha <note>The name of the king/patron</note> | gifts | like Somas | mixed with three ingredients <note>original: tri-āśiraḥ; refers to Soma mixed with milk, curd, and grain</note> ॥ 5 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The hundred bulls <note>original: ukṣāṇaḥ; literally oxen or strong bulls</note> given by the king **Ashvamedha**, who is the fulfiller of desires <note>original: paruṣāḥ</note>, gladden me—they lift my spirits greatly. O **Agni**, may those bulls be as pleasing to you as the **Soma** juices mixed with the three additives <note>original: tri-āśiraḥ; the three additives are curd, parched grain, and milk</note> used for your satisfaction.

---

-> ।। Now follows the sixth verse ।। <-

**Complete Verse (Verse 6):**
O **Indra** and **Agni**, maintain great, undying power and heroic strength in **Ashvamedha**, the giver of hundreds, like the sun remains in the sky. ॥ 6 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis (Verse 6):**
O Indra and Agni | O giver of hundreds | in Ashvamedha | excellent heroism | power | maintain | great | in the sky | like the sun | undying ॥ 6 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Indra** and **Agni**, in this King **Ashvamedha**, who is a "giver of hundreds" <note>original: śatadāvi; one who gives unlimited wealth to those who ask</note>, maintain <note>original: dhārayatam; preserve or establish</note> a power and wealth <note>original: kṣatram</note> that is accompanied by excellent heroism, is great, and is undying <note>original: ajaram; literally "without decay"</note>. How should it be maintained? Like the sun is held in the atmosphere of the sky.

-> ।। This concludes the twenty-first section of the first lesson of the fourth book ।। <-

## Hymn Text (RV 5.28.1)

**Introductory Note:**
The fourteenth hymn, beginning with "The kindled Agni," consists of six verses. The index <note>original: Anukramani</note> states: **"The kindled [Agni] is by Vishvavara of the Atri clan; it uses the Trishtubh, Jagati, Trishtubh, Anushtubh, and two Gayatri meters."** The seer <note>term: Rishi (sage-poet)</note> of this hymn is a woman named **Vishvavara**, born into the lineage of Atri. The first and third verses are in the *Trishtubh* meter, the second in *Jagati*, the fourth in *Anushtubh*, and the final two are in *Gayatri*. The deity addressed is **Agni**. The application of the hymn follows the nature of its verses.

-> ।। Here is the first verse ।। <-

**Complete Verse (Verse 1):**
The kindled **Agni** has reached his light to the heavens; he shines widely facing the dawn. **Vishvavara**, bearing the ladle of ghee <note>original: ghṛtācī; the sacrificial spoon filled with clarified butter</note>, goes eastward with bows, praising the gods with the oblation. ॥ 1 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis (Verse 1):**
Kindled | Agni | in the sky | light | has reached | facing | the dawn | widely | shines | goes | eastward | Vishvavara | with bows [reverence] | the gods | praising | with oblation | bearing the ghee-ladle ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The well-kindled and brightly blazing **Agni** has extended his light into the shining atmosphere. He rests there.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the 28th Hymn of the 5th Mandala. This hymn is significant because its seer (Rishi) is Vishvavara, a woman of the Atri family, and it focuses on the domestic fire and marriage.</meta>

[Header: Mandala 5, Chapter 2, Hymn 28] || Fourth Book || 339

Facing the Dawn <note>original: uṣasam; the goddess of daybreak</note>, Agni shines forth extensively. He shines with particular brilliance. With songs of praise <note>original: namobhiḥ</note> honoring the gods such as Indra, and possessing the sacrificial offering <note>original: haviṣā</note> like the rice-cake, the seer named Vishvavara—carrying the ghee-dripping ladle <note>original: ghṛtācī; a ritual spoon used to pour clarified butter into the fire</note> and capable of warding off all evil enemies—being East-facing, approaches such an Agni.

->॥ Now follows the second verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

Being kindled, you rule over immortality; you attend to the one making the offering for his well-being. That person whom you visit gains all wealth; he places the hospitality-offering before you, O Agni. ॥ 2 ॥

---

**Word-by-word Analysis (Pada-patha):**
Being kindled | of immortality | you rule | the offering | making | you attend / serve | for well-being | all | he | holds | wealth | whom | you visit | hospitality-offering | O Agni | down | and | he places | indeed | before ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni, being kindled**, being thoroughly set ablaze, you **rule** over **immortality** <note>original: amṛtasya; Sayana also glosses this as "water," referring to the rain produced by sacrifice</note>. Likewise, you **attend to** or protect the **sacrificer** <note>original: haviṣ-kṛṇvantaṃ; literally "one making the offering"</note> for his **well-being** or non-destruction. Furthermore, whichever sacrificer you **visit** or go toward, that sacrificer **holds** or possesses **all wealth** such as cattle and other riches. Moreover, O Agni, he **places** the **hospitality-offering** <note>original: ātithyam; an offering fit for a guest, as Agni is the divine guest of the home</note> **indeed before** you.

In the *Pavicestya* sacrifice <note>a specific ritual ritual for purification</note>, this verse serves as the sacrificial chant for Agni Svishtakrit <note>the aspect of Agni that "makes the offering correct"</note>. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "The two concluding prayers are *Juṣo damūnā* and *Agne śardha mahate saubhagāya*..." <note>quoting the Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.12</note>. Also, in the *Sakamedha* rites <note>seasonal sacrifices</note> dedicated to the "Sporting Maruts" <note>storm gods</note>, where a rice-cake on seven potsherds is offered, this same verse is used for the Svishtakrit offering, as cited: "The two concluding prayers are *Juṣo damūnā* and *Agne śardha mahate saubhagāya*..." <note>quoting Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.14</note>.

->॥ Now follows the third verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

O Agni, be strong for our great fortune; let your glories be supreme. Establish well-ordered domestic harmony; overcome the powers of those who act as enemies. ॥ 3 ॥

---

**Word-by-word Analysis (Pada-patha):**
O Agni | be strong / overcome | for great | for good fortune | your | glories / riches | supreme | let them be | together | domestic harmony | well-regulated | establish | those acting as enemies | overcome | the powers ॥ 3 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, you must **be strong** and overcome our enemies for our **great** and abundant **good fortune** <note>original: saubhagāya; referring to excellent wealth or prosperity</note>. Likewise, let the **glories**—either the riches or the splendors—pertaining to **you** be **supreme** or excellent. Furthermore, O Agni, **establish** or create **domestic harmony** <note>original: jāspatyam; the relationship between the wife (jāyā) and husband (pati)</note> that is **well-regulated**. Between those two...

<vocab>
**Agni**: The god of fire.
**Being kindled (samidhyamāna)**: The act of lighting the ritual fire.
**Immortality/Water (amṛta)**: That which does not die; often linked to rain in Vedic thought.
**Performing oblation (haviṣkṛṇvat)**: The person carrying out the ritual sacrifice.
**Sacrificer (yajamāna)**: The patron who sponsors the ritual.
**Well-being (svasti)**: Peace, health, and prosperity.
**Wealth (draviṇa)**: Material riches, often specifically livestock.
**Hospitality/Offering (ātithya)**: Ritual treatment of Agni as an honored guest.
**Overcome/Strength (śardha)**: To show power or to defeat opposition.
**Good fortune (saubhagya)**: Luck or blessed prosperity.
**Glory/Wealth (dyumna)**: Radiance or the fame that comes from riches.
**Domesticity (jāspatya)**: The bond and shared life of a husband and wife.
</vocab>

...domestic duties <note>original: jāspatyaṃ; pertaining to the master and mistress of the house</note>. Make that well-governed <note>original: susuyamaṃ</note>, meaning properly joined together or harmonious. Make it complete. Furthermore, trample upon <note>original: abhitistha</note> the might <note>original: mahāṃsi</note> of those acting as enemies <note>original: śatrūyatāṃ</note> who desire to harm us.

## Hymn Text

-> || Now the fourth verse || <-

**I praise your splendor, O Agni, of you who are kindled and of great might.**
**You are the bull, possessing wealth; you are kindled at the sacrifices. ॥ 4 ॥**

**Kindled | of great might | O Agni | I praise | your | splendor |**
**The bull | possessing wealth | you are | well | in sacrifices | you are kindled ॥ 4 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, I **praise** the **splendor** or brilliance belonging to you who are **kindled**, meaning fully grown or set ablaze, and of **great might** <note>original: pramahasaḥ; possessing excellent light</note>. I, the sacrificer, offer this song of praise. You are the **bull** <note>original: vṛṣabhaḥ; a common metaphor for Agni as the "showerer" of rewards and benefits</note> and you **possess wealth** or riches. **In sacrifices** <note>original: adhareṣu</note>, you are **kindled** or thoroughly illuminated.

Regarding the New and Full Moon sacrifices <note>original: darśapūrṇamāsayoh</note>, there are two kindling verses <note>original: sāmidhenya-mantras</note> beginning with **"O Agni, being kindled, to whom the offering is made."** This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "The two verses starting 'O Agni, being kindled, to whom the offering is made' [are used]." <note>Reference to Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 1.2</note>

## Hymn Text

-> || Here is the fifth verse || <-

**O Agni, being kindled and invoked, sacrifice to the gods, O you of the good sacrifice! For you are the carrier of the offerings. ॥ 5 ॥**

**Kindled | O Agni | invoked | the gods | sacrifice | O one of good sacrifice | you | for | carrier of offerings | are ॥ 5 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **invoked** one—you who are called from all sides by the sacrificers—O **one of good sacrifice** <note>original: svadhvara; one associated with an excellent ritual</note>, O **Agni**, being **kindled** or properly set ablaze, **sacrifice** to the **gods**, the shining ones such as Indra and others. **For** <note>original: hi</note> the reason that you, O Agni, **are the carrier of the offerings** <note>original: havyavāṭ; the one who conveys the sacrificial food to the heavens</note>, for this reason, the instruction is "sacrifice to the gods."

---

## Hymn Text

-> || Now the sixth verse || <-

**Offer the oblation, serve Agni as the sacrifice proceeds. Choose the carrier of the offerings. ॥ 6 ॥**

**Offer | serve | Agni | proceeding | in the sacrifice | choose | the carrier of offerings ॥ 6 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O priests <note>original: ṛtvijaḥ</note>, while our **sacrifice** is **proceeding** or has commenced, **offer the oblation** <note>original: ā juhota; pour the clarified butter</note> from all sides to this Agni, and likewise **serve** him or attend to him. And **choose** or resort to this **carrier of offerings** <note>original: havyavāhana</note>. The fact that Agni, in his role as "Carrier of Offerings," is the one associated with the gods and the one to be chosen by the sacrificers is clearly stated in the Taittiriya scripture: **"There are indeed three fires: the Carrier of Offerings [Havyavahana] of the gods..."** <note>RV 5.6.6; text continues on next page</note>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on a previous section regarding the different forms of Agni (Kavyavahana and Saharaksha) and introduces the 29th Hymn (Sukta) of the 5th Book (Mandala) of the Rigveda. This hymn is dedicated to Indra and was seen by the sage Gaurivīti.</meta>

...Kavyavāhana <note>original: kavyavāhanaḥ; the form of fire that carries offerings to the ancestors</note> belongs to the ancestors, while Saharakṣa belongs to the demons <note>original: asurāṇām</note>. They ask regarding this sacrifice, "Whom will he choose for me?" and the answer is given: "Choose Havyavāhana," <note>original: havyavāhanam; the form of fire that carries offerings to the gods</note> for he is the one who belongs to the gods. -> ॥ Thus ends the twenty-second section (Varga) of the first chapter of the fourth book (Ashtaka) ॥ <-

The fifteenth hymn begins with the words "Three Aryamans" <note>original: tryaryamā</note> and consists of fifteen verses. The Index <note>original: anukramaṇikā</note> states: **"The hymn beginning 'Tryaryamā' has fifteen verses; the seer is Gaurivīti, son of Śakti; the deity is Indra; the meter is Trishtubh."** The sage is Gaurivīti, born in the lineage of Śakti. Since no other meter is mentioned, it is Trishtubh <note>a meter of 4 lines with 11 syllables each</note>. Indra is the deity because the general definition at the start of the book applies. The phrase "When Ushanā with the bold ones" in a later verse indicates it may be related to the sage Ushanā. This hymn is used during the third day of the Abhiplava ritual <note>a six-day Vedic sacrifice</note> during the ceremony for the Maruts. It is noted in the ritual manuals: "The noon ceremony of the third day begins with 'Three Aryamans' and 'He who was born'." (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 7.7).

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the first verse ॥ <-

**The three Aryamans, in the sacrifice of Manu, upheld the three heavenly lights.**
**The Maruts of pure strength praise you; O wise Indra, you are their Seer. ॥ 1 ॥**

**Pada-patha:**
Three | Aryamans | of Manu | in the sacrifice | three | lights | heavenly | they upheld |
They praise | you | the Maruts | of pure strength | You | of these | the Seer | Indra | are | wise ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**In the sacrifice** <note>original: devatātā</note> belonging to **Manu**, the **three Aryamans**—referring to the three forms of solar or divine energy—as well as the **three heavenly lights** <note>original: rocanā divyā</note> which exist in the atmosphere and consist of Wind, Fire, and the Sun <note>Vayu, Agni, and Surya</note>, were **upheld** or supported by the Maruts. The **Maruts**, who possess **pure strength**, **praise you**, Indra. O **Indra**, you who are **wise**, you are the **Seer** <note>original: ṛṣiḥ; the one who envisions or sees the truth</note> of these Maruts.

**When the Maruts praised Indra as he was delighted, having drunk the pressed Soma,**
**He took up the thunderbolt; when he struck the serpent, he released the great waters to flow. ॥ 2 ॥**

**Pada-patha:**
After | when | indeed | the Maruts | being delighted | they praised | Indra | having drunk | of the pressed [Soma] |
Took up | the thunderbolt | against | when | the serpent | he struck | the waters | great | he released | to flow | indeed ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**When** the Maruts **praised Indra** while he was **being delighted** after **having drunk** the **pressed Soma** juice, **Indra took up** the **thunderbolt** <note>original: vajram</note>. Then, when he **struck the serpent** <note>original: ahim; referring to the demon Vritra who held back the rains</note>—

...struck down <note>original: abhyahan</note>, having struck down. At that time, when the great waters that had been held back by Vritra <note>original: vṛtreṇa niruddhānyudakāni</note> were released to flow <note>original: sartavai</note> according to their own nature; he released them from their confinement.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the third verse ॥ <-

**And may the Great Ones, and Indra, drink of this well-pressed Soma of mine. For that oblation found the cows for mankind, when Indra, having drunk of this, slew the Serpent.** ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
And. Great ones. Maruts. My. Of this. Indra. Of the Soma. Well-pressed. May [you] drink.
That. Indeed. Oblation. For the man. The cows. Found. He slew. The Serpent. Having drunk. Indra. Of this. ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

"And also, O Great ones <note>original: brahmāṇo; here interpreted as 'the great ones,' referring to the Maruts</note>, O Maruts, may you and Indra drink this Soma of mine, which is well-prepared and well-extracted. <note>The commentator notes that the genitive case 'of this Soma' is used here to mean the object: 'drink this Soma'</note>. The word 'drink' <note>original: peyāḥ</note> is a prayerful request in the plural. That oblation of Soma, once drunk by you, truly obtained for the man <note>meaning the sacrificer</note> the cows <note>original: gāḥ; which can mean literal cattle or the waters of the rain</note>. In other words, it causes the sacrificer to attain them. Furthermore, Indra, having drunk <note>original: papivān</note> of this Soma, slew the Serpent Vritra."

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the fourth verse ॥ <-

**He propped apart the two worlds even wider; pervading all, he made the beast a thing of terror. Indra, casting off the shroud, struck down the snorting son of Danu.** ॥ ४ ॥

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Indeed. The two worlds [Heaven and Earth]. Wider. Apart. He propped. Pervading. Even. For fear. The beast. He made.
The swallower. Indra. Casting off the shroud. Against. Snorting. Down. The son of Danu. He struck. ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

"Indra, possessed of supreme power, after drinking the Soma, propped apart <note>original: viṣkabhāyat</note> the two worlds—Heaven and Earth <note>original: rodasī</note>—making them even more extensive and rendering them unmoving. The word 'pervading' <note>original: saṃvivyānaḥ; which can mean 'shrouding' or 'moving'</note> refers to Indra's action. He made the 'beast' <note>original: mṛgam</note>—referring to Vritra who was fleeing like a wild animal—into an object of terror. Indra, who is the swallower <note>original: jigartim; one who consumes or covers his enemies</note>, struck down the son of Danu <note>original: dānuvam; Vritra</note> who was snorting in fear. He did this while casting off the concealment <note>original: apajagurāṇaḥ</note> and attacking him directly."

<term>Indra</term>: The king of the gods and deity of rain and war.
<term>Maruts</term>: Storm deities and companions of Indra.
<term>Soma</term>: A sacred ritual drink offered to the gods.
<term>Vritra</term>: The dragon or serpent demon who held back the waters.
<term>Heaven and Earth</term>: (Sanskrit: Rodasī) The two halves of the world propped apart by Indra.
<term>Ahi</term>: (The Serpent) Another name for the demon Vritra.
<term>Danu</term>: The mother of the Danavas (a class of demons), including Vritra.
<term>Brahmanas</term>: (In this context) The 'Great' Marut deities.
<term>Oblation</term>: (Sanskrit: Havya) A religious offering made into a consecrated fire.
</vocab>
