<meta>This page continues the commentary on Rig Veda, Mandala 5, Hymn 64. The previous page introduced the hymn with an invocation to Mitra and Varuna as protectors and leaders to the light. This page concludes the commentary on Verse 3 and provides the full text and explanation for Verses 4 and 5, focusing on the rewards of sacrifice—wealth and prosperity for both the patrons and the singers.</meta>

## Commentary (Sayana)
If and when I truly attain <note>original: 'āśyāṃ' - from the root 'aś', to reach or obtain</note> the path or the going... because of the grammatical link to the word 'if' <note>original: 'yat'</note>, there is no loss of accent in the verb. At that time, may I go by the path of Mitra, who is a friend, a path that leads one to the friend. The fact that Mitra is the one who leads us to this region or state is well known from passages such as, "May the wise Mitra lead us" <note>RV 1.90.1</note>. It is not only I alone who am the traveler, but everyone else has gone there as well; thus the text says: **of this beloved**, meaning of Mitra. **Of the one who does not harm** <note>original: 'ahiṃsānasya'</note>, because this beloved deity does not cause injury. **In his peace**, meaning in his happiness, his house, or his place, **they have gathered**, or come together.

---
-> ॥ The Fourth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**O Mitra and Varuna, may I offer a most excellent tribute to you both with a hymn; that which indeed leads to competition in the dwelling of the wealthy patrons and the chanters.** ॥ 4 ॥

-> **Word-by-Word Analysis** <-
**To you two . O Mitra-Varuna . Most excellent / Near . May I place . With a hymn .**
**Which . Indeed . In the dwelling . Of the wealthy patrons . Of the chanters . And . For competition.** ॥ 4 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Mitra and Varuna, **to you two**, **may I place** or hold <note>original: 'dheyām'</note> a **most excellent** <note>original: 'upamam' - glossed as wealth measured out or brought near</note> wealth by means of a **hymn** or praise. **That which indeed** <note>original: 'yaddha'</note> is the wealth obtained from you both, which **in the dwelling** or house **of the wealthy patrons** <note>original: 'maghonām' - the 'Maghavans' or generous givers who fund the sacrifice</note> **and the chanters**, becomes a cause **for competition**. This means a friendly rivalry arises between the rich patrons and the singers regarding who possesses the greatest abundance of wealth. The implication is that the wealth bestowed by the gods becomes immeasurable.

---
-> ॥ The Fifth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**O Mitra, come to us with your bright rays, and Varuna, to the place of gathering; in your own dwelling, for the prosperity of the wealthy patrons and our friends.** ॥ 5 ॥

-> **Word-by-Word Analysis** <-
**Come . To us . O Mitra . With bright rays . Varuna . And . In the place of gathering . Come .**
**In own . Dwelling . Of the wealthy patrons . Of the friends . And . For prosperity.** ॥ 5 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Mitra**, you **and Varuna**, both endowed **with bright rays**, **come** to **us** at the **place of gathering**, which is the place of sacrifice. The second use of the word **'come'** <note>original: 'ā' - repeated in the verse</note> is either redundant or used for the sake of emphasis or respect. For what purpose should you come? It is said: **for the prosperity** or growth of the **wealthy patrons** (those who provide the offerings) **and the friends** (meaning us, the priests and singers who have become your friends), **in your own dwelling** or house.

---

<vocab>
- **Mitra-Varuna:** A dual deity representing the social and moral order of the cosmos.
- **Maghavan:** A term for a "bounteous" person, usually the patron who pays for the Vedic sacrifice.
- **Sadhastha:** A "place of sitting together," specifically the sacrificial ground where gods and men meet.
- **Vṛdhase:** A dative form meaning "for the purpose of increasing" or for prosperity.
- **Ṛcā:** By means of a verse from the Rig Veda.
- **Dheyām:** A prayerful wish ("May I place") often used when offering prayers or oblations.
- **Kṣaya:** A place of rest, a dwelling, or a home.
- **Sasmire:** A perfect tense verb meaning "they have met" or "they have come together."
</vocab>

<meta>This page continues the translation of the Rig Veda, Mandala 5, Sukta 66, specifically concluding the hymn with verses 6 and 7. It then transitions into the ninth hymn of the cycle (Sukta 67), dedicated to Mitra and Varuna, composed by the seer Ratahavya of the Atri family. -> ॥ The Sixth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**O Varuna and Mitra, among those singers for whom you maintain great power and abundance; make wide the way for us to gain wealth, for riches, and for our well-being.** ॥ 6 ॥

**You two . for us . among whom . O Varuna <note>Original: 'varuṇā' - used here as a dual address for both Mitra and Varuna</note> . power . great . and . you maintain .**
**Wide . for us . for the gaining of wealth . make . for riches . for well-being.** ॥ 6 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Varuna** (meaning both Mitra and Varuna), **you two**, on account of **those** hymns of praise we offer, **maintain** or uphold for **us** a **power** <note>original: 'kṣatram' - strength or dominion</note> that is **great** and includes vast nourishment. This food and strength held by you, **make** it **wide** <note>original: 'uru' - meaning spacious or expanded</note> for **us**; that is, make it extensive for the **gaining of wealth** or for the sake of the sacrifice, for the sake of **riches**, and for **well-being** or security.

---

-> ॥ The Seventh Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**At the dawning of the light, O adorable ones, in the divine dominion when the rays are shining; come running to my pressed Soma like horses with swift feet, O leaders, you who support the sage Archananas.** ॥ 7 ॥

**At the dawning . my . O adorable ones . in the divine dominion . in the shining rays .**
**Pressed . Soma . indeed <note>original: 'na' - here used in the sense of 'now' or 'indeed'</note> . with hands <note>original: 'hastibhiḥ' - interpreted here as swift limbs</note> . [come] . with feet . run . O leaders . supporting . Archananas.** ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**At the dawning** refers to the time of the Dawn (Ushas). The phrase **my Soma** indicates the connection to the offering. You two are **adorable** <note>original: 'yajatā' - those worthy of being worshipped with sacrifice</note> in the **shining rays** <note>original: 'ruśadgavi' - where 'go' (cow) refers to the rays of light</note> of the morning libation, and in the **divine dominion** <note>original: 'devakṣatre'</note>, which is the sacrifice where the power (kshatra) of the gods is present. To **my pressed Soma**, come **now** <note>original: 'na' - used as 'sampratyarthe', meaning 'now'</note>. Come **running** with **hands**—meaning those possessing hands or limbs—and with **feet** <note>original: 'padbhiḥ'</note>, referring to horses endowed with four feet. O **leaders** <note>original: 'narā'</note>, you two guides, Mitra and Varuna, who support the seer **Archananas**.

-> ॥ Thus ends the second Varga of the fourth Adhyaya in the fourth Ashtaka ॥ <-

---

The ninth hymn of this section, beginning with "He who understands" <note>original: 'yaściketa'</note>, consists of six verses. The Seer (Rishi) is Ratahavya, a descendant of Atri. The deities are Mitra and Varuna. The Index (Anukramani) states: "He who understands is a six-verse hymn by Ratahavya." Because it is said that the hymn ends in a Pankti metre, by the rules of definition, the first five verses are in the Anustubh metre and the **final is in Pankti**. The ritual application follows the characteristic signs of the verses.

-> ॥ The First Verse of the Ninth Hymn ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**He who understands, who is of good wisdom, who is dedicated to the gods—let him speak to us. Varuna, who is visible, or Mitra, who favors our songs.** ॥ 1 ॥

## Hymn Text

**[Mandala 5, Adhyaya 5, Sukta 65, Verse 1]**

-> (Word-by-word Analysis) <-
He who | perceives | he | of good wisdom | directed toward the gods | he | let him speak | to us | Varuna | whose | visible/beautiful | Mitra | or | accepts | songs ॥ 1 ॥

---

**॥ The Second Verse ॥**
For those two are of the highest luster, the two sovereign kings, the most far-hearing; those two are the lords of the pious, the nourishers of the cosmic order, and the possessors of truth among all people. ॥ 2 ॥

-> (Word-by-word Analysis) <-
Those two | indeed | of excellent luster | the two kings | most far-hearing | those two | lords of the pious | nourishers of the Truth | possessors of the Truth | in person after person ॥ 2 ॥

---

**॥ The Third Verse ॥**
Approaching you two for protection, I invoke the ancient ones together; with good horses and with good wisdom, we pray for the granting of strengths. ॥ 3 ॥

-> (Word-by-word Analysis) <-
Those two | you two | approaching | for protection | the ancient [praises] | near | I speak | together | having good horses | with good wisdom | strengths | toward | forth | for the sake of giving ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**He who** <note>original: 'yaḥ'</note>, the worshiper, **perceives** <note>original: 'ciketa'</note> or knows the praise of you two, **he is of good wisdom** <note>original: 'sukratuḥ'</note>; he alone is the performer of beautiful sacrificial acts **among the gods** <note>original: 'devacā'</note> or among the circle of worshipers. Alternatively, he who knows the praise of you two among the gods is the one of good wisdom. Let **him**, the one of good deeds, **speak to us** <note>original: 'no bravītu'</note>; let him instruct us further in this praise. **Varuna**, whose appearance is **visible** <note>original: 'darśataḥ'</note> or beautiful, **or Mitra** <note>original: 'mitro vā'</note> (where 'or' is used in the sense of 'and')—these two **accept** <note>original: 'vanate'</note> or enjoy **our songs** <note>original: 'giraḥ'</note> of praise. ॥ 1 ॥

**For those two** <note>original: 'tā hi'</note>, indeed Mitra and Varuna, are **of the highest luster** <note>original: 'śreṣṭhavarcasā'</note> or most excellent splendor. They are the **sovereign kings** <note>original: 'rājānā'</note> or lords, and the **most far-hearing** <note>original: 'dīrghaśruttamā'</note>, meaning they are the best at hearing calls from distant lands. **Those two** are the **lords of the pious** <note>original: 'satpatī'</note>, the masters of the virtuous sacrificers. They are the **nourishers of the cosmic order** <note>original: 'ṛtāvṛdhā'</note>, meaning they increase the power of the sacrifice or the celestial waters. **Among all people** <note>original: 'jane jane'</note> or on behalf of all worshipers, they are the **possessors of truth** <note>original: 'ṛtāvānā'</note> who come to the rite. ॥ 2 ॥

**Approaching** <note>original: 'iyānaḥ'</note> or going toward **those two** ancient ones, I **invoke** <note>original: 'upa bruve'</note> or praise **you two** <note>original: 'vām'</note> **together** <note>original: 'sacā'</note> **for protection** <note>original: 'avase'</note>. We, the descendants of Atri <note>original: 'ātreyāḥ'</note>, possessing **good horses** <note>original: 'svaśvāsaḥ'</note>, address you who have **good wisdom** <note>original: 'sucetunā'</note> or excellent perception. We praise you **for the sake of giving** <note>original: 'dāvane'</note> or bestowing **strengths** <note>original: 'vājān'</note> and food. Alternatively, "having good horses" refers to the two gods themselves; in this grammatical interpretation, it functions as a description of those we invoke. ॥ 3 ॥

<term>Varuna</term>: The Vedic deity of the cosmic moral law and the night sky.
<term>Mitra</term>: The Vedic deity of friendship, contracts, and the morning light, often paired with Varuna.
<term>Sukratu</term>: One who possesses 'kratu' (will, wisdom, or sacrificial power).
<term>Rta</term>: The fundamental cosmic order or truth that governs the universe and the sacrifice.
<term>Atreya</term>: A descendant of the sage Atri; the family credited with composing the fifth book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda.

## Hymn Text
Mitra, even from distress, surely provides a broad path for dwelling. For the benevolence of Mitra, the powerful, is with the one who serves him. ॥ 4 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Mitra | from distress | even | surely | broad | for dwelling | a path | provides |
of Mitra | indeed | of the powerful | benevolence | is | of the one who serves ॥ 4 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Mitra, the god <note>original: 'mitro devo'</note>, even for a singer who is in **distress** <note>original: 'anhasvataḥ'</note>, immediately provides a **path** <note>original: 'gātum'</note>—a means or way—to a **broad** <note>original: 'uruve'</note> **dwelling** <note>original: 'kṣayāya'</note> or home. Indeed, the **benevolence** <note>original: 'sumatiḥ'</note> or beautiful intellect of the god Mitra remains with the one who **serves** <note>original: 'vidhataḥ'</note> or performs attendance, even if that worshiper is currently struggling <note>original: 'pratūrvataḥ'</note> or being overpowered. This truly comes to pass.

---
---

-> || The Fifth Verse || <-

## Hymn Text
May we remain in the most extensive protection of Mitra. May we be sinless, protected by you, and blessed with the offspring of Varuna together. ॥ 5 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
We | of Mitra | in the protection | may we be | in the most extensive |
sinless | protected by you | together | having Varuna’s offspring ॥ 5 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
May we, the worshipers, abide in the **protection** <note>original: 'avasi'</note> of the god Mitra, who is the remover of sorrow. May we be in that protection which is **most extensive** <note>original: 'saprathastame'</note> or widest in all directions. Furthermore, may we be **sinless** <note>original: 'anehasaḥ'</note> or free from fault, **protected by you** <note>original: 'tvotayaḥ'</note>, and **possessing the offspring of Varuna** <note>original: 'varuṇasheshasaḥ'</note>. The word <term>shesha</term> is a name for offspring; therefore, these are people who possess sons who ward off evil. May we all be like this **together** <note>original: 'sacā'</note>.

do not | the wealthy patrons | overlook | and not | our | of the seers | in the protection of cattle | us | protect ॥ 6 ॥

O **Mitra** <note>original: 'mitra'</note>—meaning the two gods Mitra and Varuna—**you two** <note>original: 'yuvam'</note> approach **this person** <note>original: 'imam janam'</note>, the singer, who is myself. Having arrived, you **lead them well** <note>original: 'sam ca nayathaḥ'</note>; that is, you bring them to the fulfillment of their desires. <meta>This page concludes the commentary on the final verse of Sukta 65 and begins Sukta 66 of the 5th Mandala. The previous page ended mid-commentary on verse 6 of Sukta 65, which is a prayer to Mitra and Varuna for protection and the preservation of offspring.</meta>

Its meaning is as follows: In the day, you both **cause [others] to exert** <note>original: 'yatathaḥ'</note> themselves; you lead them toward their various activities. And in the night, you **bring them together** <note>original: 'sannayathaḥ'</note>; you cause them to be without activity. Do not **abandon** <note>original: 'parikhyataṃ'</note> us, who possess wealth in the form of sacrificial oblations. Do not—never—**abandon** our sons, the descendants of us seers. Rather, **protect** <note>original: 'uruṣyataṃ'</note> us in the **Soma-drinking sacrifice** <note>original: 'gopīthe'</note>. "Go" refers to the Soma juice; that sacrifice in which its drinking <note>original: 'pānaṃ'</note> occurs is the "Go-pitha." Protect us there.

->॥ Thus ends the third Varga of the fourth Adhyaya of the fourth Ashtaka ॥<-

**"O wise one"** <note>original: 'ā cikitāna'</note> is the tenth hymn of six verses. The seer <note>term: 'Rishi' - the inspired poet-sage to whom the hymn was revealed</note> is Ratahavya. The meter is Anushtubh. The deities are Mitra and Varuna. Regarding this, the Ancient Index <note>original: 'Anukramaṇikā'</note> states: **"O wise one is Anushtubh, six [verses]."** The first three verses are used in the Prauga-shastra <note>term: 'shastra' - a recited litany</note> of the priest representing Mitra and Varuna on the fourth day of the ten-night ritual <note>original: 'Dasharatra'</note>. It is also indicated in the ritual manuals: **"O wise one, you of good deeds... that one for you who is not to be abandoned" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 7.11).**

->॥ Here follows the first verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
O wise one, [invoke] the two gods of good deeds and destroyers of enemies for the mortal. For Varuna, whose form is clarity, may he offer the great oblation for enjoyment. ॥ 1 ॥

> O | wise one | of good deeds | the two gods | for the mortal | destroyers of enemies |
> for Varuna | whose form is clarity | may he offer | for enjoyment | the great ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **wise one** <note>original: 'cikitāna'</note>, you who know the praise; O **mortal** <note>original: 'marte'</note> man, Ratahavya—this is an address to the seer himself. Invoke the **two gods** <note>original: 'devau'</note> who are **of good deeds** <note>original: 'sukratū'</note>—those who perform beautiful actions—and are **destroyers of enemies** <note>original: 'riśādasā'</note>, the killers of those who cause harm. This is the implied completion of the sentence. And having called them, **may he offer** <note>original: 'dadhīta'</note>—meaning "you should give"—the oblation <note>implied</note> to the **great** <note>original: 'mahe'</note>, worshipful, and **mighty** Varuna, for the sake of **enjoyment** <note>original: 'prayase'</note>. "Enjoyment" here refers to the food characterized by the oblation <note>the possessive suffix is dropped in the original Sanskrit</note>. He is described as **having clarity as his form** <note>original: 'ghṛtapeśase'</note>; the word "peshas" is a name for "form," and "ghrita" here refers to "water." Thus, he whose form is water itself. Alternatively, the dative case <note>for Varuna</note> is used in place of the second case <note>accusative</note>: "one should offer the great oblation." Or it can be joined as: "for the sake of obtaining great food."

->॥ Here follows the second verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
For they two truly possess an unharmed dominion and a divine power that is perfect. Then, like sacred laws, for the human, a visible light is established. ॥ 2 ॥

> They two | indeed | dominion | unharmed | perfectly | divine power | possess |
> then | like sacred laws | for the human | heaven/light | like | is established | visible ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**For they two** <note>original: 'tā hi'</note>. The word "hi" indicates a reason. Because those two **possess** <note>original: 'āśāte'</note> a **dominion** <note>original: 'kṣatraṃ'</note> or strength that is **unharmed** <note>original: 'avihutam'</note>, not to be injured, and a **divine power** <note>original: 'asuryam'</note> belonging to the spirits—

## Hymn Text
**To those two of yours, for the movement of these chariots, we seek a wide pasture-land.**
**With the beautiful praises of Ratahavya, we honor you firmly with hymns. ॥ ३ ॥**

### Pada-patha
To those two; of you two; for moving; of chariots; wide; pasture; of these;
of Ratahavya; beautiful-praise; firmly; with hymns; we honor. ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Mitra and Varuna**, we honor those two famous ones—you two—so that these chariots of ours, standing here before us, may travel <note>original: 'eṣe'</note> along a wide, abundant pasture <note>term: 'gavyūti' - traditionally a measure of distance, here referring to a wide, safe path or grazing ground</note>. This means for the protection of the path. For that purpose, we honor and praise you both with the "beautiful praises" <note>original: 'suṣṭuti'</note> of the seer Ratahavya, using hymns <note>term: 'stoma' - a formal collection of chanted praises</note> which are instruments of beautiful worship, addressing you two who are firm and overpowering.

## Hymn Text
**For then, through the protections of the skillful one, you two wonderful ones [endowed with] poetic wisdom,**
**perceive the [praises] of the people with your intellect, O you of purified strength. ॥ ४ ॥**

### Pada-patha
Then; indeed; poetic-wisdoms; you two; of the skillful; with-protections; wonderful;
down; with-intellect; of people; you two perceive; O you of purified strength. ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
And furthermore: you two are famous. You two, who are worthy of praise through poetic wisdom <note>original: 'kāvyā'</note>, being wonderful, great, and marvelous through the "protections"—that is, the filling hymns—of me, the empowered worshiper <note>original: 'dakṣasya'</note>, you both completely perceive <note>original: 'ni cikethe'</note> the praise of the people—meaning the sacrificers—with your intellect <note>original: 'ketunā'</note> and favorable mind. O you of **purified strength** <note>term: 'pūtadakṣasā' - those whose power or mental acuity is clean and bright</note>!

## Hymn Text
**That is the Great Truth, O Earth; this is the seeking of fame by the seers.**
**Being victors, they flow abundantly and widely toward the goal through their ritual journeys. ॥ ५ ॥**

### Pada-patha
That; Truth; Earth; Great; seeking fame; of the seers;
the two victors; fitly; wide; goal; they flow; with journeys. ॥ ५ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
<note>This is the conclusion of the commentary for Verse 5</note>

O Goddess Earth, in you, that which is famous for being sought by all—the great, abundant, and immortal water—goes to the two who are moving <note>original: 'jñayasānau'</note> when there is a desire for food among us, the sages and praisers. <note>Sayana provides a technical grammatical explanation here: the suffix '-asanac' is applied to the root 'jñā' (to know/go) following Vedic rules.</note> Because of the accent on the final syllable, it is "fully" or "excessively" broad. In this way, they flow beyond by their movements; they rain excessively. <note>Note: There is a grammatical variation here where the plural is used instead of the dual.</note>

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**Since we and the wise praisers call upon you two, O Mitra and Varuna of all-pervading vision, may we strive for self-rule in that most extensive [realm] which is guarded by many. ॥ ६ ॥**

**Padapatha:**

## Commentary (Sayana)
O you two of all-encompassing vision <note>original: 'īyacaksasā'</note>, O **Mitra and Varuna**, since we and the **wise ones** (the praisers) call upon **you two**, may we reach—may we strive for—**self-rule** <note>term: 'Svarajya' - referring to independent celestial sovereignty or spiritual autonomy</note>. May we attain a kingdom of this kind, which is **most extensive** and which is either to be approached by many or **guarded by many**.

## Hymn Text
The eleventh hymn, beginning with **"Truly, in this manner, O Gods"** <note>original: 'Balittha deva'</note>, consists of five verses. Here is the Index <note>term: 'Anukramani' - a traditional register of a hymn's details</note>: **"Balittha, five [verses], Yajata."** The Seer (Rishi) is named Yajata Atreya. The deities are Mitra and Varuna. As it was stated "the rest are Anushtubh," this hymn is also in the **Anushtubh** meter <note>a poetic meter of four quarters with eight syllables each</note>. Its ritual application is determined by its internal markers.

-> ॥ There, the First Verse ॥ <-

**Truly, O shining Adityas, you have attained the prepared, venerable, and great dominion, O Varuna, Mitra, and Aryaman, that most excellent power. ॥ १ ॥**

**Padapatha:**
Truly; in this manner; O Gods; prepared; O Adityas; venerable; great;
O Varuna; O Mitra; O Aryaman; most excellent; power; you two have attained. ॥ १ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **shining gods**, O **Adityas** <note>original: 'Adityas' - the sons of the goddess Aditi, representing solar and moral qualities</note>, O **Varuna**, O **Aryaman** (the restrainer of enemies), O **Mitra**—you [two] have attained <note>original: 'āśāthe'</note> **power** <note>term: 'Kshatra' - dominion, strength, or martial authority</note>. This power is **truly** <note>original: 'bat'</note> real and unassailable; it is **venerable** (worthy of sacrifice), **great** (fully expanded), and **most excellent**. <note>Note: Sayana remarks that although Aryaman is mentioned separately as a third deity, the verb remains in the dual form, implying that Aryaman is included in the pair of Mitra-Varuna.</note>

<vocab>
- Adityas: A group of solar deities, primarily Mitra, Varuna, and Aryaman, who uphold the cosmic order.
- Svarajya: Sovereign independence; the state of being a self-ruler (Svarat).
- Kshatra: The vital force of ruling or protection; temporal and spiritual power.
- Yajata: "Worthy of worship" or "Venerable"; here, also the name of the Sage (Rishi) of this hymn.
- Iyachakshasa: Possessing vision that spans the entire universe.
- Balittha: An adverb meaning "truly," "certainly," or "in this very way."
- Varshishtham: The highest, oldest, or most abundant state of excellence.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

**O Varuna and Mitra, when you sit upon the golden seat, you who are the supporters of all people and destroyers of enemies, grant us happiness. ॥ २ ॥**

**Padapatha:**
To; when; seat; golden; Varuna; Mitra; you two sit;
supporters; of people; grant; happiness; O destroyers of enemies. ॥ २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

When—for the reason that—you two, O **Varuna** and **Mitra**, come to the **golden** seat—meaning the sacrificial ground which is beneficial and beautiful—and because you are the **supporters** of all **people** (human beings), O **destroyers of enemies** <note>original: 'riśādasā' - those who cast down or destroy those who cause harm</note>, you two should **grant** us **happiness**. The sense is: "Please create favor for us." <note>Sayana notes the term 'sumram' is a variant for 'sumnam,' meaning happiness or divine favor.</note>

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

**For all of them are all-knowing—Varuna, Mitra, and Aryaman. They follow our sacred laws like footsteps; they protect the mortal from harm. ॥ ३ ॥**

**Padapatha:**
All; indeed; all-knowing; Varuna; Mitra; Aryaman;
sacred laws; like footsteps; they follow; they protect; the mortal; from harm. ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**For all** <note>original: 'viśve'</note> of them indeed—the "indeed" functioning as a connective—are **all-knowing** (possessing all knowledge or all wealth). These three—**Varuna, Mitra, and Aryaman**—all **follow** our **sacred laws** (our sacrificial acts) just as one follows **footsteps** or specific locations. Having arrived, they **protect** me, the **mortal** worshiper, from **harm**—meaning from any attacker or injurer.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

**For they are true, they touch the Truth, they are righteous in every person; they are good leaders, generous givers, and they make a wide path even from distress. ॥ ४ ॥**

**Padapatha:**
They; indeed; true; truth-touching; righteous; in person and person;
good leaders; generous givers; from distress; even; wide-path makers. ॥ ४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**They** are **indeed** (certainly) **true**—meaning they are the essence of truth or they produce true results. They are **touchers of Truth** <note>original: 'ṛtaspṛśaḥ'</note>, meaning those who perform the touching of water or are in contact with the cosmic order. They are **righteous** <note>term: 'Ṛta' - the fundamental principle of cosmic order, truth, and sacrifice in Vedic thought</note>, possessing the sacrifice **in every person** (among all the different sacrificers). They are **good leaders** (those with excellent guidance) and **generous givers**. The word "indeed" used here indicates their well-known qualities and should be applied throughout the description. Such great beings as Varuna and the others are **wide-path makers** <note>original: 'urucakrayaḥ'</note>—meaning they create abundant wealth—**even from distress** <note>original: 'aṃhas'</note> or sin, for the sake of their praisers.

<meta>This page concludes the 68th hymn and begins the 69th hymn of the 5th Mandala of the Rig Veda. It continues the focus on the dual deities Mitra and Varuna, shifting from a rhetorical question about their universal praise to a formal call for the priests to begin their ritual singing.</meta>

Mandala 5, Section 5, Hymn 68. | The Fourth Book | 513

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

### Hymn Text
Who among you, O **Mitra**, or you **Varuna**, is left **unpraised** by these **bodies**? To you, our **thought** surely **hastens**; from the **Archi** singers, our **thought hastens**. ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Padapatha):**
Who; indeed; of you two; O Mitra; unpraised; Varuna; or; of bodies;
That; well; to you two; toward; hastens; thought; from the Archi singers; toward; hastens; thought. ॥ ५ ॥

---

### Commentary (Sayana)
O **Mitra**, between the two of you, who indeed—you or **Varuna**—is **unpraised**? The meaning is that both are equally worthy of praise; there is no one who does not praise you. The word **of bodies** <note>original: 'tanūnām'</note> uses the possessive case to mean "by means of," referring to the physical bodies or voices of the singers. 

In this verse, only Mitra is addressed by name, yet Varuna is included in the address. This is similar to other Vedic passages <note>original reference: Rig Veda 5.62.6</note> where, even when many are present, a speaker addresses one individual to signify "this belongs to both of you." 

Therefore, because everyone praises you, our **thought** (or our hymn of praise) **hastens** toward you. Even though the word "bodies" appeared earlier, it connects here: the thought of us, who possess these small bodies/minds, reaches you. Our thought hastens from the **Archi** <note>the 'Archi' refers to a specific lineage or clan of singers descended from the sage Archi</note>. The repetition of "thought hastens" is for the sake of showing great respect or emphasis.

-> ॥ Thus ends the fifth section of the fourth chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-

---

The twelfth hymn, beginning with "Sing forth for Mitra" (*Pra vo mitrāya*), consists of five verses. It is attributed to the seer **Yajata Atreya**; it is composed in the **Gayatri** meter <note>a sacred poetic meter consisting of three lines of eight syllables each</note> and is dedicated to **Mitra and Varuna**. The Index (*Anukramani*) confirms this, stating: "Sing forth... is Gayatri." 

In the **Agnistoma** sacrifice <note>the most essential of the seven Soma sacrifices</note>, during the morning libation (**Pratah-savana**), this hymn is used by the **Maitra-varuna** priest. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "Sing forth for Mitra... for Mitra and Varuna" <note>original reference: Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 5.10</note>. Furthermore, during the six-day ritual cycles (Abhiplava and Pṛṣṭhya), these four hymns—starting with this one but excluding the second—are used to fill the ritual requirements. This is also noted in the manuals: "Of the four starting with 'Sing forth for Mitra,' one should omit the second." <note>original reference: Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 7.5</note>.

-> ॥ Now the First Verse ॥ <-

### Hymn Text
**Sing** forth with a **vibrant voice** to your **Mitra** and to **Varuna**, you who possess **great power**, for the **mighty cosmic order**. ॥ १ ॥

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Padapatha):**
Forth; for you; for Mitra; sing; for Varuna; with vibrant; voice; great power; cosmic order; mighty. ॥ १ ॥

---

### Commentary (Sayana)
O my officiating priests, you (**vo**) should **sing forth** a praise with a **vibrant** or all-pervading **voice** (song) for **Mitra** and **Varuna**. To "sing a song" is used here as a common expression, much like saying "to cook a meal." 

O you two deities of **great power** (possessing abundant strength), [come to] the **mighty**, great, and highly praiseworthy **cosmic order** <note>original: 'ṛtam' - here referring to the sacrifice itself as an expression of the divine order</note>. Or, alternatively, the meaning could be: "Listen to this great and abundant hymn of praise."

---

## Rig Veda | [Book 4, Chapter 4, Section 6]

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

### Hymn Text

**O universal sovereigns, you two who dwell in the source of clarity—both Mitra and Varuna—you are the gods who are highly praised among all divine beings. ॥ २ ॥**

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Padapatha):**
Universal-sovereigns; who; clarity-source; thus; clarity-source; Mitra; and; both; Varuna; and; gods; among the gods; highly-praised. ॥ २ ॥

---

### Commentary (Sayana)

The two who are **Mitra and Varuna**. The word **and** <note>original: 'ca'</note> is used to show their mutual relationship. Both are **universal sovereigns** <note>original: 'samrājā', meaning lords of all</note> and **dwell in the source of clarity** <note>original: 'ghṛtayonī', which refers to them being the producers or sources of water/rain</note>. You are the two shining **gods** who are **highly praised** <note>original: 'praśastā'</note> or exceptionally worthy of hymns among the **gods**. The instruction to "sing to them" is carried over from the previous verse.

---

### Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

**May those two empower us with the great wealth of the earth and of heaven; for your great sovereignty, O you two, is renowned among the gods. ॥ ३ ॥**

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Padapatha):**
Those two; us; empower; of the earthly; great; of wealth; of the heavenly; great; your; sovereignty; among the gods. ॥ ३ ॥

---

### Commentary (Sayana)

May **those two** gods **empower us** <note>original: 'śaktaṃ', meaning to make capable or to bestow</note> for the sake of obtaining **great wealth** <note>original: 'maho rāyo'</note> that belongs to the **earth** and that which exists in **heaven**. The phrase "to give" is implied here. O gods, we praise your **great** and worshipful **sovereignty** <note>original: 'kṣatram', meaning power or strength</note> which is **renowned among the gods**. The phrase "we praise" is implied to complete the thought.

---

### Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

**Upholding the sacred law by means of the water, they reach the energetic and skillful sacrificer. The two guileless gods increase in strength. ॥ ४ ॥**

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Padapatha):**
Sacred-law; by-the-water; reaching; energetic; skillful; they-attain; thus; guileless; gods; they-increase; thus. ॥ ४ ॥

---

### Commentary (Sayana)

By means of the **water** <note>original: 'ṛtena'</note>, they are **reaching** or touching the **sacred law** <note>original: 'ṛtaṃ'</note>, which here refers to the sacrifice. They **attain** <note>original: 'āśāte', meaning to pervade or reach</note> the **energetic** <note>original: 'iṣiram', meaning full of desire or effort</note> and **skillful** <note>original: 'dakṣam'</note> sacrificer or the sacrificial offering itself. O **Mitra and Varuna**, you **two gods** who are **guileless** <note>original: 'adruhā', meaning those who do not deceive or harm</note>, you **increase** <note>original: 'vardhete'</note> or become great.

---

### Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**They who cause the heavens to rain, who obtain the flowing waters, the lords of nourishment and of the gift-bearing cloud; they occupy their vast, high seat. ॥ ५ ॥**

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Padapatha):**
Rain-heaven; flow-water; of-nourishment; lords; thus; gift-possessing; vast; high-seat; they-attain; thus. ॥ ५ ॥

---

### Commentary (Sayana)

**They who cause the heavens to rain** <note>original: 'vṛṣṭidyāvā'</note>. This refers to those for whom the heaven (or the sky) exists for the purpose of rain. Alternatively, it means the two through whom the heaven/mid-air becomes a rain-giver. **Who obtain the flowing waters** <note>original: 'rītyāpa'</note>. The root *ri* means to go or to desire; thus *riti* means the attainment or movement of waters. <unclear>illegible fragment regarding the specific grammatical derivation</unclear>

<note>Translator's note: The commentary here emphasizes the role of Mitra and Varuna as "Lords of the Order" (Rita) who manifest that order through the physical world as rain and wealth.</note>

**Technical Vocabulary:**
- **Mitra-Varuna:** The dual deity representing cosmic order, friendship, and the celestial laws.
- **Universal Sovereigns:** <term>Samraja</term>; a title indicating absolute or supreme rulership over the entire universe.
- **Sacred Law / Truth:** <term>Rita</term>; a central Vedic concept meaning the natural and moral order of the cosmos, often associated with the cycle of water and the performance of sacrifice.
- **Clarity-source:** <term>Ghrita-yoni</term>; literally "the womb of ghee," metaphorically referring to the source of life-giving rain or the clarity of the ritual.
- **Sovereignty:** <term>Kshatram</term>; the divine power and authority held by the gods to maintain the world.
- **Rain-heavens:** <term>Vrishti-dyava</term>; a compound describing the gods' ability to manifest moisture from the sky.

## Hymn Text

**O Varuna, you uphold the three shining realms and also the three heavens; O Mitra, you uphold the three earthly worlds. You two, increasing in strength, guard the unaging law of the sovereign. ॥ १ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Varuna**, O **Mitra**, the connection is that you two **uphold** <note>original: 'dhārayatha'</note> the **three** <note>original: 'trī'</note> **shining realms** <note>original: 'rocanā', referring to the celestial worlds</note>. **And also** <note>original: 'utāpi'</note> you uphold the **three heavens** <note>original: 'trīn dyūn'</note>, which are the shining intermediate realms or atmospheres. Likewise, you uphold the **three earthly worlds** <note>original: 'trīṇi rajāṃsi'</note>. What is your nature? You are **increasing in strength** <note>original: 'vāvṛdhānā'</note>. You are **guarding** <note>original: 'rakṣamāṇā'</note> the **form** <note>original: 'amati'</note>—this word refers to both form and name—and the **law** <note>original: 'vratam'</note> or ritual action, which is **unaging** <note>original: 'ajuryam'</note>, meaning it is either never-decaying or continuous. This law belongs to the **sovereign** <note>original: 'kṣatriyasya'</note>, which refers either to Indra (who possesses power) or to the patron of the sacrifice who belongs to the warrior class.

The **shining ones** <note>original: 'dyumanto'</note>—referring to the deities Agni (Fire), Vayu (Wind), and Aditya (Sun)—are the masters of the **three places** <note>original: 'tisṛṇāṃ... dhiṣaṇānāṃ'</note>, namely the earth, the mid-air atmosphere, and the heavens. ## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-
**In the morning I repeatedly call upon the divine Aditi; I call her at midday when the sun has risen. O Mitra and Varuna, I praise you for wealth, for total well-being, for children, for progeny, and for peace and safety. ॥ ३ ॥**

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Padapatha):**
In-the-morning; the-goddess; **Aditi** <term>Aditi: the mother of the gods, representing the infinite and boundless</term>; I-call-repeatedly; at-midday; at-the-rising; of-the-sun; for-wealth; Mitra-and-Varuna; in-the-total-extension-of-the-sacrifice; I-praise; for-children; for-progeny; peace; safety. ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

I, the Seer, call upon **Aditi**—the indestructible mother of the gods and the shining goddess—at the time of dawn. I also **call her repeatedly** <note>original: 'johavīmi'</note> at midday, the time of the sun's full ascent during the midday **libation** <term>Savana: the ritual pressing and offering of the Soma juice, performed three times a day</term>. O Mitra and Varuna, I **praise** <note>original: 'īle'</note> you both for the sake of obtaining wealth during this sacrifice. Furthermore, I pray for the sake of my **children** <note>original: 'tokāya'</note> and their **descendants** <note>original: 'tanayāya'</note>, seeking **peace** <note>original: 'śam'</note> from all afflictions and the **granting** <note>original: 'yoḥ'</note> of happiness.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-
**O you two who are the upholders of the shining realm and also of the heavenly and earthly regions; O Adityas, the immortal gods do not violate your firm laws, O Mitra and Varuna. ॥ ४ ॥**

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Padapatha):**
Who; the-two-upholders; of-the-region; of-the-shining; and; Adityas; of-the-heaven; of-the-earth; not; your; gods; the-immortal-ones; violate; laws; Mitra-and-Varuna; firm. ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

You two are the **upholders** <note>original: 'dhartārā'</note> of the **shining region** <note>original: 'rocanasya rajaso'</note>, which refers to the heavenly world. Furthermore, you are the sustainers of the earthly **region** <term>Rajas: often translated as 'atmosphere' or 'space,' it refers here to the various layers of the inhabited universe</term>. You two are the **Adityas** <note>original: 'ādityā'</note>, the sons of Aditi, and you reside in the heavens. The connection to the previous verse is: "I praise you both." O Mitra and Varuna, other **immortal** <note>original: 'amṛtā'</note> gods—such as Indra and the rest—do not **violate** <note>original: 'ā minanti'</note> or hinder your **firm laws** <note>original: 'dhruvaṇi vratāni'</note> or sacred actions. This is because your laws are established and unshakeable.

-> ॥ Thus ends the seventh section (varga) of the fourth chapter of the fourth book (Ashtaka) ॥ <-

The fourteenth hymn, beginning with the words **"In many places"** <note>original: 'pururūṇā'</note>, consists of four verses. The Seer is **Urucakri**, a descendant of Atri. The meter is **Gayatri**, and the deities are **Mitra and Varuna**. The **Index** <term>Anukramani: the ancient systematic tables of contents for the Veda</term> states: "The hymn 'Pururūṇā' is in the Gayatri meter." In the six-day ritual cycles (Pristhya and Abhiplava), this hymn is used as an additional recitation during the morning libation <unclear>...</unclear>

<meta>This page transitions from the general praises of the deities in the previous section to the specific invocation of Hymn 70 in the Fifth Mandala. It introduces a new sequence of prayers addressed to the dual deity Mitra-Varuna, focusing on their vast protection and their role in removing suffering. This page contains the ritual instructions, the first three verses (the "triplet"), their word-by-word breakdown, and the scholarly commentary by Sayana.</meta>

[Mandala 5, Anuvaka 5, Hymn 70.]  ॥ Fourth Ashtaka ॥ 517

Regarding this hymn, as with the previous one, it is stated: "**Towards you, O Mitra**" <note>original: 'pra vo mitrāya'</note>—this refers to the ritual sequence where the second of the four hymns should be extracted. During the "Chaturvimsha" day <term>Chaturvimsha: a specific twenty-four-day ritual period in the Vedic calendar</term>, at the morning libation, the Maitra-Varuna priest recites the first triplet (three verses) known as the "Stotriya." This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "Even for the many, that which exists..." <note>original: 'pururṇā cid yasti'</note> as seen in Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 7.2.

---

-> ॥ Now the First Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O Varuna and Mitra, truly your protection is exceedingly vast; surely now, may I enjoy your benevolence. ॥ 1 ॥
<note>Rig Veda 5.70.1</note>

**Exceedingly vast; truly; for; exists; protection; surely; of you two; O Varuna; O Mitra; I enjoy; of you two; benevolence. ॥ 1 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Mitra and Varuna**, the protection of **you two** is **exceedingly vast** <note>original: 'purūruṇā cit'</note>. 
<note>Grammatical note: In the word 'purūruṇā', the final 'ā' reflects an archaic Vedic case ending.</note> 
The word 'puru' means many or great, and 'uru' means wide or extensive; thus, it means "extremely vast." Such **protection** <note>original: 'arvaḥ'</note> **surely exists** <note>original: 'nūnamasti'</note>. The word **for** <note>original: 'hi'</note> indicates a well-known truth, and **truly** <note>original: 'cit'</note> is used for emphasis. O Varuna, O Mitra, I **enjoy** <note>original: 'vaṃsi'</note>—meaning I partake in or associate with—the **benevolence** <term>sumati: a gracious or favorable state of mind; the gods' goodwill toward the worshipper</term> of you both. The sense is: "Because your protection exists, therefore I enjoy your favor."

---

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O non-deceiving ones, may we perfectly attain that food for our nourishment; O Rudras, may we be yours. ॥ 2 ॥
<note>Rig Veda 5.70.2</note>

**That; of you two; perfectly; O non-deceiving ones; food; may we attain; for nourishment; we; your; Rudras; may we be. ॥ 2 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **non-deceivers** <note>original: 'adruhvṇā'</note>—those who do not harbor malice—we **perfectly** <note>original: 'samyak'</note> praise **you two** <note>original: 'tā vāṃ'</note> (this verb is implied). May we, the singers, **attain** <note>original: 'aśyāma'</note> **food** <note>original: 'iṣam'</note> for the sake of **nourishment** <note>original: 'dhāyase'</note>, both for eating and drinking. O **Rudras** <term>Rudra: though usually a specific god, here it is used as an epithet for Mitra and Varuna meaning 'those who drive away (drāvayitārau) suffering'</term>, **we** who are your praisers, **may we be** <note>original: 'syāma'</note> yours. This means we should be prosperous, or perhaps, we should become your own people.

---

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Protect us, O Rudras, with your protections, and guard us with your good vision; may we overcome the destroyers with our bodies. ॥ 3 ॥
<note>Rig Veda 5.70.3</note>

**Protect; us; O Rudras; with protections; and; may you guard; with good vision; may we overcome; the destroyers; with bodies. ॥ 3 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
O gods of the **form described as Rudras**, may **you two** **protect** <note>original: 'pātam'</note> **us** <note>original: 'naḥ'</note> with your **guardianships** <note>original: 'pāyubhiḥ'</note>. **And also** <note>original: 'uta'</note>, may you **guard** <note>original: 'cāyethām'</note> us with **good vision** <note>original: 'sucācā'</note> (or beautiful speech). The distinction here lies between attaining what is desired and avoiding what is undesirable. Even if the hymns or rituals are imperfect, may you both guard us by granting what is favored. Furthermore, together with our **bodies** <note>original: 'tanūbhiḥ'</note>—referring to our own limbs or our children—may we **overcome** <note>original: 'turyāma'</note> the **destroyers** <term>Dasyu: enemies or chaotic forces that disrupt the sacred order</term>. This means we might either slay them or cross over the danger they pose.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Mandala 2, Hymn 41 of the Rig Veda. It concludes the 8th section (Varga) with a prayer for independence and prosperity, then begins the 9th section, which introduces a three-verse sequence (triplet) dedicated to the dual deities Mitra and Varuna for use in the morning ritual.</meta>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

**May we not, O performers of wondrous deeds, enjoy the wealth of another with our own bodies, nor with our children, nor with our descendants. ॥ 4 ॥**
<note>Rig Veda 2.41.3. Note: The numbering here follows the manuscript's internal division.</note>

> May we | not | of anyone | O performers of wondrous deeds <note>original: 'adbhuta-kratū'</note> | wealth <note>original: 'yakṣam'</note> | enjoy | with our bodies | not | with children | not | with descendants. ॥ 4 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **performers of wondrous deeds** <note>original: 'adbhutakratū'</note>, performers of marvelous actions, may we **not enjoy** <note>original: 'mā bhujema'</note> the **wealth** <note>original: 'yakṣam'</note>—that is, the worshipful riches—of **anyone** else. May we not experience this **with our bodies** <note>original: 'tanūbhiḥ'</note>, meaning our physical limbs. The implication is: "Through your grace, may we be so prosperous that we never have to sustain our bodies using the wealth of others." Furthermore, may we not enjoy such [borrowed] wealth **with our children** <note>original: 'śeṣasā'</note>, nor **with our descendants** <note>original: 'tanasā'</note> such as grandsons. The meaning is: may no one in our entire lineage ever have to live off others.

-> ॥ Thus ends the eighth Varga of the fourth section of the fourth book ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

**The fifteenth hymn, beginning with "Come to us," consists of three verses. Its authorship is attributed to Bahuvrikta; it is composed in the Gayatri meter and addressed to Mitra and Varuna. The Index <term>Anukramanika: an ancient register of Vedic hymns</term> states: "Come to us is a triplet by Bahuvrikta." The ritual application of this hymn has been stated previously. In the Agnishtoma sacrifice, during the morning libation <term>Pratahsavana: the first of three daily offerings</term>, this triplet is used as the appropriate chant for the Maitra-Varuna priest. This is also indicated in the ritual manuals: "Come to us, O Mitra and Varuna, O destroyers of enemies..." <note>original: 'ā no mitrāvaruṇā no gantaṃ riśādasā'</note> as seen in Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 5.10.**

-> ॥ Therein, the First Verse ॥ <-

**Come to us, O destroyers of enemies, Varuna and Mitra, with crushing power, to this beautiful sacrifice. ॥ 1 ॥**
<note>Rig Veda 2.41.4</note>

> Come | to us | O you two | O destroyers of enemies <note>original: 'riśādasā'</note> | O Varuna | O Mitra | with crushing power <note>original: 'barhaṇā'</note> | near | this | beautiful | sacrifice <note>original: 'adhvaram'</note>. ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Varuna**, O **Mitra**, O **destroyers of enemies** <note>original: 'riśādasā'</note>—you who spur on or destroy foes—**come** <note>original: 'ā gantam'</note> **to our beautiful** <note>original: 'cārum'</note>, desirable **sacrifice** <note>original: 'adhvaram'</note>, which is non-violent in nature. In what manner do you come? With **crushing power** <note>original: 'barhaṇā'</note>, meaning with the greatness or the force that uproots and kills enemies.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

**For you two, O Varuna and Mitra, the wise ones, rule over everything; as our masters, increase our prayers. ॥ 2 ॥**
<note>Rig Veda 2.41.5</note>

> Of everything | for | O wise ones <note>original: 'pracetasā'</note> | O Varuna | O Mitra | you two rule | O masters | increase <note>original: 'pipyatam'</note> | prayers <note>original: 'dhiyaḥ'</note>. ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Mitra**, O **Varuna**, you two are the **wise ones** <note>original: 'pracetasā'</note>, possessing excellent knowledge. You **rule over everything** <note>original: 'viśvasya rājathaḥ'</note>; you are the lords of all. This is well known, as indicated by the word **for** <note>original: 'hi'</note>. O **masters** <note>original: 'īśānā'</note>, our rulers, may you **increase** <note>original: 'pipyatam'</note>—that is, cause to swell or overflow with rewards—our **prayers** <note>original: 'dhiyaḥ'</note>, meaning our ritual acts and meditations.

<vocab>
- performers of wondrous deeds (adbhutakratū): Deities (Mitra and Varuna) who act in marvelous ways.
- wealth (yakṣam): Here interpreted as external or worshipful riches.
- with our bodies (tanūbhiḥ): Referring to personal physical sustenance.
- destroyers of enemies (riśādasā): A common epithet for Mitra and Varuna.
- crushing power (barhaṇā): Immense strength used to overcome obstacles or foes.
- sacrifice (adhvaram): Literally "the uninjured," referring to the sacred fire ritual.
- wise ones (pracetasā): Those with heightened consciousness or foresight.
- masters (īśānā): Sovereign lords or rulers.
- increase (pipyatam): To nourish, fatten, or bring to full fruit.
</vocab>

## Hymn Text
**Come to us, O Varuna and Mitra, to the pressed [Soma] of the giver, for the drinking of this Soma. ॥ 3 ॥**

> Come | to us | pressed [Soma] | toward | come | O Varuna | O Mitra | of the giver | of this | Soma | for the drinking. ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Varuna**, O **Mitra**, both of you **come** toward our **pressed** <note>original: 'sutam'</note>—that is, the extracted—**Soma**. Come for the **drinking**—the consumption—of **this Soma** belonging to me, the **giver** <note>original: 'dāśuṣaḥ'</note> of the sacrificial oblation.

-> ॥ Thus ends the ninth Varga of the fourth section of the fourth book ॥ <-

The sixteenth hymn, beginning with "Toward Mitra and Varuna" <note>original: 'ā mitre varuṇe'</note>, consists of a triplet (three verses). Its authorship is attributed to the seer Bahuvrikta; it is composed in the <term>Ushnih: a Vedic meter consisting of 28 syllables</term> meter and is dedicated to **Mitra and Varuna** <note>original: 'maitrāvaruṇam'</note>. The Index <term>Anukramanika: an ancient register of the Rig Veda's contents</term> states: "The hymn 'Toward Mitra' is in the Ushnih meter." During the <term>Dasharatra: a ten-night sacrificial session</term>, on the third day, this triplet is used for the <term>Prauga Shastra: a specific recitation by the Hotri priest</term> dedicated to Mitra and Varuna. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "Toward Mitra and Varuna, we... O Ashvins, come here" <note>original: 'ā mitre varuṇe vayam aśvināveha gacchatam'</note> (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 7.10).

-> ॥ Herein the First Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Toward Mitra and Varuna we call with songs, shining like fire; sit down on the sacrificial grass for the Soma-drinking. ॥ 1 ॥**

> Toward | Mitra | Varuna | we | with songs | call | shining like fire | down | on the sacrificial grass | sit | for the Soma-drinking. ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**We**, the **descendants of Atri** <note>original: 'ātreyāḥ'</note>, **call upon** <note>original: 'ā juhumaḥ'</note> **Mitra and Varuna** for their sake with **songs**—meaning with sacred mantras. We call in a way that is **shining like fire** <note>original: 'arcivat'</note>, similar to Agni, the fire-god who stimulates our hymns. Therefore, O **Mitra and Varuna**, **sit down** <note>original: 'ni ṣadatam'</note> upon the **sacrificial grass** <note>original: 'barhiṣi'</note> for the **Soma-drinking**.

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**By the vow you are of firm security, by the law you set people in motion; sit down on the sacrificial grass for the Soma-drinking. ॥ 2 ॥**

> By the vow | you two are | of firm security | by the law | setting people in motion | down | on the sacrificial grass | sit | for the Soma-drinking. ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Mitra and Varuna**, through your **vow** <note>original: 'vratena'</note>—which means through your sacred actions or divine connection—and through the **law** <note>original: 'dharmaṇā'</note> that supports the world, **you are of firm security** <note>original: 'dhruvakṣemā sthaḥ'</note>. That is, you remain in an unwavering and stable position. You are **setting people in motion** <note>original: 'yātayajjjanā'</note>, meaning you incite and direct people toward their respective duties and works...

<summary>This page concludes Sukta 72 with an invitation to Mitra and Varuna to drink Soma, and begins Sukta 73, describing the deities as upholders of cosmic law (Dharma) who provide stability and motivate human action.</summary>

<meta>This page concludes the 72nd hymn of the fifth book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda and introduces the 73rd hymn. ## Commentary (Sayana)
The people are the priests, and those for whom these people are set in motion <note>original: 'yātayajjjanau'</note> are the two deities. Alternatively, the term refers to those whose people—their attendants—set the enemies in motion, meaning they destroy them. The rest of the explanation has already been provided.

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-
**May Mitra and Varuna be pleased with our sacrifice for its fulfillment. Sit down on the sacrificial grass for the drinking of the Soma. ॥ 3 ॥**

### Word-for-Word Breakdown
Mitra | and | our | Varuna | and | may they be pleased | sacrifice | for fulfillment | down | on the sacrificial grass | sit | for the drinking of Soma ॥ 3 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
May both **Mitra** and **Varuna** be pleased with **our sacrifice** for the sake of the **fulfillment** <note>original: 'iṣṭaye'</note> of our desires. Having arrived, **sit down** upon the **sacrificial grass** <note>original: 'barhiṣi'</note> to **drink the Soma**.

-> ॥ Thus ends the tenth group (Varga) of the fourth section of the fourth book ॥ <-
-> ॥ Thus ends the fifth lesson (Anuvaka) in the fifth book ॥ <-

In the sixth lesson, there are fifteen hymns. Among them, the first hymn, beginning with "Whether today you are..." <note>original: 'yad-vya-stha'</note>, consists of ten verses. Its authorship is attributed to the seer Paura of the Atri family <note>original: 'Atreyasya Paura'</note>. It is composed in the <term>Anushtubh: a Vedic meter consisting of four quarters of eight syllables each</term> and is dedicated to the **Ashvins**. The Index <term>Anukramanika: an ancient table of contents for the Rig Veda</term> states: "The hymn 'yad-vya' of ten verses by Paura is for the Ashvins, and it is in Anushtubh." Because it says "it," the six hymns beginning with this one are for the Ashvins. Because of the word "but" in the phrase "but in Anushtubh," this hymn and the one following it are both in the Anushtubh meter. In the <term>Prataranuvaka: the early morning litany</term> for the Ashvins, these two hymns are used in the section for the Ashvins in the Anushtubh meter. This is indicated in the ritual manuals <note>original: 'Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.15'</note>.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Therein the First Verse ॥ <-
**Whether you are today in a distant place or in a nearby place, O Ashvins; or whether you are in many places, O you of many protections, or in the atmosphere—come here! ॥ 1 ॥**

### Word-for-Word Breakdown
Whether | today | you both are | in a distant place | whether | in a nearby place | O Ashvins | whether | or | in many [places] | O you of many protections | whether | in the atmosphere | here | come ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **you of many protections** <note>original: 'purubhuja', meaning those who enjoy many sacrifices or provide much protection</note>, O **Ashvins** <note>The divine twin healers of the Vedas</note>, if **today**, at this time, you **are** in a **distant place**—that is, in the highest heaven—or if you are in a **nearby place** <note>original: 'arvavati', a place one can easily go to</note> close by; or if you are in **many** different regions, or if you are in the **atmosphere**, please **come** from all those places. Come to us.

<vocab>
- मित्र (Mitra): A deity of friendships and contracts, often associated with the morning sun.
- वरुण (Varuna): A deity of the cosmic law and the night sky.
- अश्विना (Ashvins): Twin horsemen who are the physicians of the gods and rescuers of those in distress.
- सोम (Soma): A sacred ritual drink prepared from a plant, central to Vedic sacrifice.
- बर्हिस् (Barhis): The sacred grass (Desmostachya bipinnata) strewn on the sacrificial altar as a seat for the gods.
- पुरूभुजा (Purubhuja): An epithet for the Ashvins, emphasizing their role as great enjoyers of offerings or great protectors.
</vocab>

<keywords>Mitra, Varuna, Ashvins, Soma, sacrifice, Paura Atreya, Anushtubh meter, Vedic ritual, Sayana's commentary</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the 73rd hymn of the fifth book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda. It contains the second, third, and fourth verses addressed to the Ashvins, the divine twin horsemen of the Vedic tradition. The commentary by Sayana continues to provide linguistic and ritualistic context.</meta>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

**I summon here those two who manifest for many, bearing many great deeds; I come to the most desirable ones of irresistible movement, the most powerful ones, for our protection and enjoyment. ॥ २ ॥**

### Word-for-Word Breakdown
Here | those two | who manifest for many <note>original: "puru-bhūtamā"</note> | many | deeds | bearing | most desirable | I come to | of irresistible movement <note>original: "adhrigū"</note> | I summon | most powerful | for protection/enjoyment ॥ २ ॥

---

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

**You have fixed one wheel of the chariot for its splendor in the sun; with the other, you traverse through the human ages and the worlds by your greatness. ॥ ३ ॥**

### Word-for-Word Breakdown
One [wheel] | the other | for beauty/splendor | the form/body | wheel | of the chariot | you two have held/fixed | around | the other | human <note>original: "nāhuṣā"</note> | ages/generations | by greatness | the worlds/spaces | you two traverse ॥ ३ ॥

---

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

**That deed of yours, O beautiful ones, is well done; everything you do is praised. Though born in different ways, you come together to us in sinless kinship. ॥ ४ ॥**

### Word-for-Word Breakdown
That | indeed | well | by you two | done | all | which | by you two | is praised | in different ways | born | sinless/pure | together | to us | kinship | you two have come ॥ ४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Here, in this** sacrifice, **those two** <note>original: "tyā"</note>, the **most manifest for many** <note>original: "purubhūtamā"</note>—meaning those who cause many sacrificers to prosper—who are **bearing** or maintaining **many** <note>original: "puru"</note> **deeds** <note>original: "daṃsāṃsi"</note> or rituals, I **approach** <note>original: "yāmi"</note> them. They are the **desirable ones** and possess **irresistible movement** <note>original: "adhrigū"</note>, meaning their movement is not held back by others. I **summon** <note>original: "huve"</note> these **most powerful ones** for our **enjoyment** or for our protection <note>original: "bhuje"</note>.

O Ashvins, **you have held** or fixed **one wheel** of **your chariot** in the **sun** <note>original: "īrmā... āditaye"</note>—the word *īrmā* is a form derived from the root meaning 'to go'—**for the splendor** or beauty of that sun. You fixed a **beautiful** and **radiant wheel** there. With **the other** wheel, you **traverse** or go around **the worlds** and the **human ages** <note>original: "nāhuṣā yugā"</note>—referring to the people descended from King Nahusha, or human beings in general—and the periods of time marked by them, such as the morning libations or the cycles of day and night, through your **greatness** or your own power. This is consistent with another verse: "You held one wheel of the chariot on the head of the other" <note>original: "Rig Veda 1.30.19"</note>.

<term>Ashvinau: The twin deities, often associated with the transition from darkness to light (dawn) and known as the physicians of the gods.</term>
<term>Damsāmsi: Refers to wonderful deeds or powerful ritual actions.</term>
<term>Adhrigū: A technical term often applied to the Ashvins or the sacrificial fire, meaning 'unrestrained' or 'irresistible in motion.'</term>
<term>Nāhushā yugā: Refers to the 'ages of man.' Nahusha was a legendary king, and his descendants represent humanity.</term>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary for Verse 4 of the 44th hymn in the fourth book (Mandala) and presents Verses 5 and 6 with their respective commentaries. ## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**When Sūryā has ever mounted that swift-moving chariot of yours, then your bright, heat-shedding steeds <note>The word 'vayah' can mean birds, horses, or moving rays.</note> encompass you with their glow. ॥ ५ ॥**

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**The sage Arci <note>Arci is the name of the seer (Rishi) of this verse, often identified as the father of the poet.</note> perceives your radiance, O Leaders, with a blissful and attentive mind, when for you two, O Nasatyas <note>An epithet of the Ashvins, meaning 'helpful' or 'not untruthful.'</note>, he makes the burning heat <note>original: "gharma"</note> harmless with the praise from his mouth. ॥ ६ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

<note>Concluding the commentary on Verse 4 from the previous page</note>
O all-pervasive ones <note>original: "viśvā vyāpnau"</note>, through this hymn I praise you both. Let this act, performed by the poet Paura, be well-accomplished for you. Though you are born separately <note>referring to the different times of the morning/evening associated with the twins</note>, you are both abundant and sinless; come to us together with food and wealth. This is the meaning.

> **When Sūryā has ever mounted that swift-moving chariot of yours, then your bright, heat-shedding steeds encompass you with their glow. ॥ ५ ॥**

O Ashwins, when **Sūryā** <note>The daughter of the Sun God, who is considered the wife of the Ashwins</note>, your wife, has mounted <note>original: "ātiṣṭhat"</note> your **swift-moving** and eternal **chariot**, then they surround you. Who? The **bright**, shining, and **heat-shedding** horses—who consume enemies—encompass you. Alternatively, "heat-shedding" <note>original: "ātapāḥ"</note> is an adjective for the horses/rays who travel and cause heat on all sides.

> **The sage Arci perceives your radiance, O Leaders, with a blissful and attentive mind, when for you two, O Nasatyas, he makes the burning heat harmless with the praise from his mouth. ॥ ६ ॥**

O **Leaders** <note>original: "narā"</note>, O Ashwins, our father, the sage **Arci**, **perceives**—meaning he knows or has praised—**your radiance** with a **mind** full of devotion and **bliss**, which resulted from the cooling of the fire's heat. Bliss is mentioned because it follows the removal of suffering. What was the occasion for this suffering? He explains: Because, O **Nasatyas**, through the hymn produced by **his mouth**, he **attained** <note>explained as the act of moving or reaching</note> the **Gharma**—the bright, burning fire thrown by demons to burn him—and rendered it **sinless** <note>original: "arepasam"</note>, meaning harmless and pleasant. 

The act of the Ashwins protecting someone from fire by using frost/snow is clearly shown in other verses, such as: *"You quenched the heat [Gharma] with frost for the sake of the sage"* (**Rig Veda 1.116.8**) and *"You two rescued Atri from the heated cavern"* (**Rig Veda 10.39.9**).

---

- The commentary links the term "Gharma" (which often refers to a sacrificial vessel or the milk within it) to a specific myth where the Ashwins cool a pit of fire to save the sage Atri.

## Hymn Text
**Your great and moving chariot is heard resourcing through the journeys, constant in its flight; when, O Ashvins, O Leaders, the sage Arci <note>The seer of this hymn, often identified as the poet's father.</note> turns you toward us by his wondrous deeds. ॥ ७ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
Of heightened strength, your **exalted**, great, **moving**, and **continuous** chariot is **heard** during its **journeys**, which refers to either its travel or its arrival at sacrifices. O **Ashvins**, O **Leaders**, **because** the sage **Arci**—our father—**turns** you toward us through his sacrificial **deeds**, your presence is felt.

## Hymn Text
**O Rudras <note>Here, an epithet for the Ashvins as fierce or mighty deities.</note>, mixers of the sweetness, our swelling praise serves you well; when you cross over the oceans <note>original: "samudrā"; here interpreted as the atmosphere or the celestial waters.</note>, the flanking worshipers bring you nourishment. ॥ ८ ॥**

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Madhvaḥ** <note>Of the honey/sweetness</note> । **Ūṃ** <note>particle: indeed</note> । **Su** <note>Well</note> । **Madhu-yuvā** <note>Mixers of honey</note> । **Rudrā** <note>O Rudras/Ashvins</note> । **Siṣakti** <note>Serves/Accompanies</note> । **Pipyūṣī** <note>Swelling/Overflowing</note> ।

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **mixers of honey**, you who blend the sweet Soma juice, O **Rudras** (so named because you are the sons of Rudra or are to be approached through praise), our swelling **praise**, filled with the **sweetness** of devotion, **serves** you well. **When** you **cross over** the **oceans**, meaning the mid-air regions which are the means of your travel, you reach the sacrifice. At that time, the **wings**—the worshipers positioned at the sides of the altar—**bring** for **you** the **nourishment** consisting of the sacrificial offerings.

## Hymn Text
**It is a truth indeed, O Ashvins, that the ancient seekers call you the bestowers of happiness; as such, be the most invoked at our sacrifice, and be the most merciful during our journey. ॥ ९ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Ashvins**, those who know the ancient ways **say** that **truly** you two are the **bestowers of happiness**. Therefore, being famous for your ability to grant bliss, you two, who are the **most invoked** in this **sacrifice**, and the **most merciful** in this **journey**— <note>Text continues on next page</note>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Tenth Verse ॥ <-

**May these sacred prayers, which bring increase, be most peaceful to the Ashvins; we have crafted them as one crafts a chariot, and we have spoken great homage. ॥ १० ॥**

-> ॥ Word-by-word Analysis ॥ <-

**imā** <note>These</note> । **brahmāṇi** <note>sacred prayers</note> । **vardhanā** <note>strengthening/increasing</note> । **aśvibhyām** <note>for the two Ashvins</note> । **santu** <note>may they be</note> । **śam-tamā** <note>most peaceful/blissful</note> ।

## Commentary (Sayana)

The sage now concludes the praise. May these **sacred prayers**—these grand hymns just now performed—be **strengthening** (invigorating) and **most peaceful** (giving the greatest happiness) for the **Ashvins**. Just as a craftsman fashions a chariot, we **have fashioned** or composed **these** hymns. We **have spoken** a **great** homage—an utterance of salutation that grants abundant rewards.

-> ॥ Thus ends the twelfth varga of the fourth adhyaya in the fourth book ॥ <-

The second hymn, beginning with "**Where are you?**", consists of ten verses and belongs to the Rishi Prastoka (of the lineage of Puru) <note>original: "paurastyārṣaṃ"</note>. According to the Index, it follows the previous pattern and is composed in the Anushtubh meter <note>A poetic meter of four quarters with eight syllables each</note>. As mentioned before, it is dedicated to the Ashvins. Its ritual use in the morning litany and the Ashvin-shastra ceremony is the same as described for the previous hymn.

-> ॥ Therein the First Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**O divine Ashvins, wealthy in thought, where are you today from heaven? Hear that [hymn], O showers of wealth; the sage Arci attends to you. ॥ १ ॥**

-> ॥ Word-by-word Analysis ॥ <-

**kū-sthaḥ** <note>Where are you two?</note> । **devau** <note>O divine ones</note> । **aśvinā** <note>O Ashvins</note> । **adya** <note>today</note> । **divaḥ** <note>from heaven</note> । **manā-vasū** <note>O wealthy in thought/praise</note> ।
**tat** <note>that</note> । **śruvathaḥ** <note>you two hear</note> । **vṛṣaṇvasū** <note>O showers of wealth</note> । **arciḥ** <note>the sage Arci</note> । **vām** <note>you two</note> । **ā** । **vivāsati** <note>attends/worships</note> ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **divine ones**, O **Ashvins** who are **wealthy in thought** (meaning your wealth consists of the praises offered to you), having come **from heaven** on this present day, **where are you?** <note>original: "kūṣṭhaḥ"; the commentator notes a grammatical variation where the dual "sthaḥ" (you two are) is joined with "kū" (where)</note>. Being present here on the earth, **hear that** hymn of praise. O **showers of wealth** (you whose riches rain down like blessings), the sage **Arci** <note>The son of Arbe, or a reference to the light of the prayer itself</note> **attends** to you or serves you from all sides.

Alternatively, the word **where** (kū) is joined with the verb **are** (sthaḥ) through a specific grammatical division. This usage is common in the Vedic tradition, similar to phrases like "like the spokes of a wheel" or "wherever he is born." The meaning is: In what place are you currently staying? The sage Arci is praising you; hear him.

Mandala 5. Adhyaya 6. Sukta 74. ] || Fourth Book (Ashtaka) || 525

## Hymn Text
**Where are those two? Where indeed are they renowned in heaven, the divine Nasatyas <note>A name for the Ashvins, often interpreted as "the ones in whom there is no untruth" or "the healers"</note>? To which person do you come? Who is in the company of your "rivers" of praise? ॥ २ ॥**

### Word-by-word Analysis

## Commentary (Sayana)
Where do **those two divine Nasatyas**, the **Ashvins**, stay? **Where indeed** today are they **renowned**? Do they dwell **in heaven**? This is the implied question. Now the poet addresses them directly: O **divine ones**, to **which person**—that is, to which sacrificer—do **you come**? Who is the singer of hymns who acts as a **companion** or helper to the **rivers** of your praises?

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**To whom do you travel? To whom indeed do you go? Toward whom do you yoke your wealth <note>Or chariot</note>? At whose sacred prayers do you rejoice? We desire you for our sacrifice. ॥ ३ ॥**

---

### Word-by-word Analysis
**kam** <note>to whom</note> । **yāthaḥ** <note>you two travel</note> । **kam** <note>to whom</note> । **ha** <note>indeed</note> । **gacchathaḥ** <note>you two go</note> । **kam** <note>whom</note> । **accha** <note>toward</note> । **yuñjāthe** <note>you two yoke</note> । **rayam** <note>wealth/chariot</note> ।
**kasya** <note>whose</note> । **brahmāṇi** <note>sacred prayers</note> । **raṇayathaḥ** <note>you two rejoice</note> । **vayam** <note>we</note> । **vām** <note>you two</note> । **uśmasi** <note>we desire</note> । **iṣṭaye** <note>for sacrifice/desire</note> ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Ashvins**, toward **which** sacrificer or sacrifice do **you travel**? Crossing the distance, toward **whom indeed** do **you go**? Having gone, with **whom** do you become **associated**? Toward **whom** do **you yoke** your chariot with horses? In **whose "brahmani"**—that is, their grand and lofty **prayers**—do **you rejoice** or take pleasure? **We**, for our part, **desire you** for our own **sacrifice** or petition. The implication is: "Therefore, do not go to anyone else's sacrifice."

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Indeed, you quicken Paura, even him who was bound in the water; you [act] for the sake of the sage Paura. Like a lion [freed] from a trap, or [held] in a pit of treachery. ॥ ४ ॥**

---

### Word-by-word Analysis
**pauram** <note>Paura (a devotee)</note> । **cit** <note>even/also</note> । **hi** <note>indeed</note> । **udru-mutam** <note>bound in the water</note> । **pauram** <note>Paura</note> । **paurāya** <note>for the sake of Paura</note> । **jinvathaḥ** <note>you two quicken/aid</note> ।
**yat** <note>when/since</note> । **īm** <note>him (particle)</note> । **gṛbhīta-tātaye** <note>for the sake of one who is seized/bound</note> । **siṃham-iva** <note>like a lion</note> । **druhaḥ** <note>of treachery/of the enemy</note> । **pade** <note>in the place/trap</note> ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Paura**! This is a direct address to the **Ashvins**. Because of their connection to the praise offered by the sage Paura, the **Ashvins** themselves are also addressed as **Paura**.

<term>Nāsatya (नासत्या): A common epithet for the Ashvins, the twin Vedic deities of the dawn and healing.</term>
<term>Ashvinau (अश्विनौ): The twin sons of the Sun, depicted as horsemen who bring light and rescue devotees in distress.</term>
<term>Sachā (सचा): A Vedic term meaning "along with" or "in the presence of."</term>
<term>Brahmāṇi (ब्रह्माणि): In this context, these are the sacred hymns or expansive prayers offered by the priest.</term>
<term>Raṇayathaḥ (रणयथः): To find delight or pleasure in something, specifically the joy the gods take in receiving a sincere hymn.</term>
<term>Uśmasi (उश्मसि): An archaic form of "we desire," expressing the longing of the devotee for the presence of the divine.</term>
<term>Paura (पौर): The name of a specific Vedic sage or king; here, Sayana explains it is also used as a name for the Ashvins themselves because they are the subject of Paura's hymns.</term>
<term>Jinvathaḥ (जिन्वथः): To stir into motion, to help, or to invigorate; used here to describe the Ashvins rescuing a devotee.</term>

It also introduces the legend of Paura, a devotee whom the Ashvins rescued from being bound in water, likening his plight to a lion caught in a snare.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the commentary for the 74th hymn (Sukta) of the fifth book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda. The previous page introduced the Ashvins and questioned their whereabouts. This page concludes the commentary on Verse 4 and provides the full text and explanation for Verses 5 and 6, transitioning from Varga 13 to Varga 14 of the fourth chapter of the fourth book (Ashtaka).</meta>

## Commentary (Sayana)
[Continuation of the commentary for Verse 4]

The use of the singular form here <note>original: "ekavacanaṃ"</note> for both of you is a poetic license of the Vedas. O **Ashvins**, who are associated with the sage **Paura**, you two [impel] **Paura**. The word *cid* <note>original: "cit"</note> is a filler word used to complete the meter. Because the **cloud** is also connected to the prosperity sought by Paura, the cloud itself is called **Paura**. You impel that **cloud**, the **shedder of water** <note>original: "udamṛtam"</note>, for the sake of the sage Paura—that is, for me. Or rather, you two go toward this cloud for the sake of Paura, who has maintained the continuity of the sacrifice. You impel it in the **place of harm** <note>original: "drohasya pade"</note>, such as a forest region, just as brave men forcibly drive away a **roaring, powerful lion**. ॥ ४ ॥

---

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**You released the covering from the aging Chyavana like a cloak. When you made him young again, he stirred the desire of his bride. ॥ ५ ॥**

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**pra** <note>prefix indicating forth/away</note> । **cyavānāt** <note>from the sage Chyavana</note> । **jujuruṣaḥ** <note>from the one who was aging</note> । **vavrim** <note>the covering/old body</note> । **atkam** <note>a cloak or armor</note> । **na** <note>like</note> । **muñcathah** <note>you two released</note> ।
**yuvā** <note>young</note> । **yadi** <note>when</note> । **kṛthaḥ** <note>you two made</note> । **punaḥ** <note>again</note> । **ā** <note>prefix indicating direction</note> । **kāmam** <note>desire/lovely form</note> । **ṛṇve** <note>he attained</note> । **vadhvaḥ** <note>of the bride</note> ॥ ५ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
From the sage **Chyavana**, who was **decaying with old age**, you two **released** the **covering**—his old, worn-out body—just **like a cloak** <note>original: "atkam na"</note> or a piece of armor. You cast it off him. This mirrors another mantra <note>Rig Veda 1.116.10</note> which says "you stripped the covering from Chyavana like a garment." **When** <note>original: "yadi"</note> you **made** him **young again**, he **attained** the **lovely form** <note>the "desire"</note> sought by his **bride**, a woman of great beauty.

-> ॥ Thus ends the thirteenth Varga of the fourth chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-
