## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Seventh Verse ॥ <-

**May those Rudras, the good sacrificers, like fires of great brilliance, protect [me], O Evayamarut! The earthly dwelling, long and wide, was spread out [by them]—they whose great powers [are seen] in their marches, they of wonderful deeds.** ॥ ७ ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown**
**Those | Rudras | good sacrificers | fires | like | of great brilliance | may they protect | O Evayamarut!**
**Long | wide | was spread out | dwelling | earthly | of whom | in marches | [unto] | great | powers | of wonderful deeds.** ॥ ७ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Maruts**, sons of **Rudra** <note>original: "rudrāsaḥ"</note>, you who are **good sacrificers** <note>original: "sumakhāḥ"</note>, like **fires** <note>original: "agnayo yathā"</note> you possess **great brilliance** <note>original: "tuvidyumnāḥ"</note> or abundant light. Alternatively, it means you are like fire in possessing abundant wealth. **Protect** <note>original: "avantu"</note> me, the Rishi <note>sage-poet</note> named **Evayamarut**. The **earthly** <note>original: "pārthivaṃ"</note>—referring to both the earth and the mid-air—**dwelling** <note>original: "sadma"</note> which is **long** and **wide** was **spread out** <note>original: "paprathe"</note>; it was made expansive by the Maruts. In the **marches** <note>original: "ajmeṣu"</note> or movements of these deities who are **of wonderful deeds** <note>original: "adbhutainasām," which Sayana also glosses as "without sin"</note>, **great powers** <note>original: "maho śardhāṃsi"</note> come forth.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Eighth Verse ॥ <-

**Without hatred, O Maruts, come to our path; hear the call of the singer, O Evayamarut! You who share the same wrath as the great Vishnu, drive away the haters with your skill, like chariot-fighters [driving away foes] to a distance.** ॥ ८ ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown**
**Without hatred | our | O Maruts | path | come | hear | call | of the singer | O Evayamarut!**
**Of Vishnu | great | having the same wrath | drive away | with | chariot-fighters | like | by skill | [away] | enmities | to a distance.** ॥ ८ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Maruts**, you who are **without hatred** <note>original: "adveṣo," glossed as "adveṣasaḥ"</note>, **come** <note>original: "ā itana"</note> toward **our path** <note>original: "no gātum"</note>, which refers to our hymn that is moving toward you. For that purpose, **hear** <note>original: "śrota"</note> the **call** <note>original: "havam"</note> of the **singer** <note>original: "jarituḥ"</note>, the divine **Evayamarut** (referring to myself). O you who possess the **same wrath** <note>original: "samanyavaḥ," glossed here as "same sacrifice"</note> as the **great** and all-pervading **Vishnu** <note>Sayana identifies Vishnu here with Indra, the king of gods</note>, you are like **praised chariot-fighters** <note>original: "rathyā na"</note> or warriors. Just as warriors drive away enemies, **drive away** <note>original: "apa yuyotana"</note> the **enmities** <note>original: "dveṣāṃsi"</note> or those who hate us, putting them **to a distance** <note>original: "sanutaḥ," a term for being hidden or set aside</note> through our **skill** <note>original: "daṃsanā," referring to sacrificial acts</note>.

## Critical Notes

This hymn is traditionally **prescribed for the ceremonies of opening and closing the Vedic study** <note>original: "adhyāyopākaraṇotsargayorviniyuktā"</note>. See the **Grihya Sutras** <note>manuals of domestic rituals</note> 3.5.

<vocab>
<term>Rudra</term>: The fierce father of the Maruts; here used as a name for the Maruts themselves as his progeny.
<term>Evayamarut</term>: A unique title used as a refrain in this hymn; Sayana identifies it as the name of the sage (Rishi) who composed the verses.
<term>Vishnu</term>: In this context, Sayana interprets the "Great Vishnu" as a reference to Indra's all-pervasive power.
<term>Damsana</term>: Refers to wondrous deeds or the effective power of ritual actions.
</vocab>

Mandala 5. Anuvaka 6. Sukta 87.] || Fourth Ashtaka || 569

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the Ninth Verse ॥<-

**O you who are worthy of sacrifice, come to our sacrifice; hear our call, O Evayamarut, so that the ritual may be well-performed and free from evil. Like the most ancient mountains in the sky, may you, the wise ones, be irresistible to the reviler.** ॥ ९ ॥

---

->**Word-by-Word Analysis**<-

**Come | to our | sacrifice | O you worthy of sacrifice | for well-performed ritual | hear | the call | O you without demons | Evayamarut |**
**The eldest | like | mountains | in the sky | you | of that | wise ones | may you be | difficult to restrain | for the reviler.** ॥ ९ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Maruts worthy of sacrifice** <note>original: "yajñiyāḥ"</note>, **come** <note>original: "gaṃta"</note> to our **sacrifice**. That is, arrive here. Do so **for the sake of a well-performed ritual** <note>original: "su-śami," meaning a beautiful or good action</note>; the sense is "for the sake of good performance." For that purpose, **hear our call** <note>original: "havam"</note>—listen to our invitation. You are **without demons** <note>original: "arakṣaḥ," meaning free from the interference of Rakshasas or evil spirits</note>. <note>Note: Sayana remarks here on a "liṅga-vacanayoḥ vyatyayaḥ," an exchange of gender and number common in Vedic grammar.</note>

Like the **eldest** <note>original: "jyeṣṭhāso"</note> or most prominent, like the **mountains** <note>original: "parvatāsaḥ"</note> such as the **Vindhyas** and others, you are exceedingly great and exist in the **sky** <note>original: "vyomani"</note> or mid-air. You who are **wise** <note>original: "pracetasaḥ"</note>, may you be **difficult to restrain** <note>original: "durdhartavaḥ"</note> or irresistible for **that reviler** <note>original: "nidaḥ"</note>—one who speaks ill of the sacrifice. May you **be** <note>original: "syāta"</note> so.

<meta>This page marks the transition from the end of the Fifth Mandala to the beginning of the Sixth Mandala of the Rig Veda. The previous page concluded the hymns attributed to the Atri family; this page introduces the hymns of the Bharadvaja family. The translation continues with the traditional scholarly commentary by Sayana, which provides context for the ritual use and grammatical structure of the verses.</meta>

-># Now Begins the Sixth Mandala #<-

In the Sixth Mandala, seen by the seer Bharadvaja, there are six sections <term>Anuvākas; subdivisions of a Mandala</term>. In the first section, there are fifteen hymns. The first hymn, beginning with "You, indeed, O Agni," consists of thirteen verses. Since the traditional index <note>the Anukramani</note> states, "Bharadvaja, the son of Brihaspati, saw the sixth Mandala," he is the designated Seer <term>Ṛṣi; the sage to whom the hymn was revealed</term> for this entire book. By the general rule of silence, the meter is **Trishtubh** <note>a Vedic meter of 11 syllables per line</note>. By the general rule for the start of a Mandala, the deity is **Agni** <note>the god of Fire</note>. This is known as the *Manota* hymn, to be recited by the Maitravaruna priest when the offerings of the animal sacrifice are being prepared. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "He recites, 'You, indeed, O Agni, were the first...'" <note>original: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 3.6</note>. In the morning litany <term>Prātaranuvāka</term>, during the ritual for Agni in the Trishtubh meter, this is the first of a group of six hymns (excluding the second). This is also noted: "Of the six beginning with 'You, indeed, O Agni, the first,' one should set aside the second" <note>original: Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.13</note>. Its use in the initial ritual preparations was mentioned in the previous section.

---

->## Regarding the First Verse ##<-

## Hymn Text

**You, indeed, O Agni, were the first weaver of thoughts for this prayer; you became the wondrous priest.**
**You, O Showerer of benefits, created an irresistible power for the sake of overcoming every powerful foe.** ॥ १ ॥

**Word-by-Word Analysis (Pada-patha):**
**You | indeed | O Agni | first | weaver of thoughts | of this | prayer | became | wondrous | priest |**
**You | [particle] | O Showerer | created | difficult to overcome | power | for every | power | for the sake of overcoming.** ॥ १ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, among the gods you are the **first**, the foremost, or the most excellent. You are indeed the **weaver of thoughts** <term>Manotā; the one in whom the minds (manas) of the gods are woven or connected</term>. The word "indeed" <note>original: "hi"</note> is used to highlight a well-known fact from the Brahmanas <note>ancient prose commentaries on the Vedas</note>: "Agni is all the Manotas; all Manotas come together in him" <note>original: Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 2.10</note>. O **wondrous one** <note>original: "dasma," meaning beautiful to behold</note>, you **became** the **priest** <term>Hotṛ; the invoker who calls the gods</term> **of this prayer** <note>original: "dhiyo," referring to this ritual action</note>. O **Showerer** <note>original: "vṛṣan," one who rains down the fulfillment of desires</note>, you **created** <note>original: "akṛṇoḥ"</note> an **irresistible** and indestructible **power** <note>original: "saho"</note> everywhere. For what purpose? **For the sake of overcoming** <note>original: "sahadhyai," for the defeat</note> **every powerful** enemy.

---

->## Now the Second Verse ##<-

## Hymn Text

**Then you, the priest, sat down, the most worshipful, in the place of libation, desiring offerings and being worthy of praise.**
**You, whom men, seeking the gods and contemplating great wealth, followed as the first.** ॥ २ ॥

<vocab>
- **Mandala**: One of the ten "books" or major sections of the Rig Veda.
- **Manotā**: A technical term for Agni as the focus of the gods' thoughts during a sacrifice; literally "the weaver."
- **Hotṛ**: The primary priest responsible for reciting the Rig Vedic verses to invite the gods to the ritual.
- **Pada-patha**: The "word-path," a method of reciting the Veda where every word is separated and analyzed in its basic form.
- **Bharadvaja**: One of the great hereditary seers (Rishis) of ancient India, to whom the 6th Mandala is attributed.
</vocab>

## Hymn Text

**[RV 6.1.2 Word-for-word Breakdown]**
Then. The invoking priest. Down. He sat. More worshipful. Of the libation-place. In the spot. Desiring. Worthy of praise. Being.
Him. You. Men. First. Seeking the gods. Great. For wealth. Conscious/Revealing. After. They went. || 2 ||

Going as if by a path with many treasures, they followed after the wealth, being wakeful in you.

**[RV 6.1.3 Word-for-word Breakdown]**

Shining. Agni. Visible. Great. Possessing strength. Always. Shining. || 3 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**[On Verse 2]**
"Then" <note>original: adha</note>, at this time, O Agni, you who are the "more worshipful" <note>original: yajīyān; the most excellent sacrificer</note> became the "invoking priest" <note>original: hotā; the priest who carries out the oblation</note> and "sat down" <note>original: nyasīdaḥ</note> in the "place of libation" <note>original: iḷo pade</note>, which refers to the location of the sacrificial altar on the earth. Doing what? "Desiring" <note>original: iṣayan</note> food in the form of sacrificial animals and cakes, while being "worthy of praise" <note>original: īḍyaḥ</note> or worship. The "men" <note>original: naraḥ</note>—referring to the leaders, the priests, and the patrons—"seeking the gods" <note>original: devayantaḥ</note> or desiring you as their god, "followed after" <note>original: anugman</note> you, who are that very same Agni. They did this "first" <note>original: prathamam</note>, even before the other deities, "perceiving" <note>original: citayantaḥ</note> or revealing through their praises that you are the source of "great wealth" <note>original: maho rāye</note>.

**[On Verse 3]**
"As if by a path" <note>original: vṛteva; mārgeṇa</note>. Here, the word "as if" <note>original: iva</note> is used in the sense of "now" or "truly." The sacrificers follow you as you are "going" <note>original: yantam</note> along the path between the two worlds <term>Earth and Heaven</term> together with "many treasures" <note>original: bahubhir vasavyaiḥ</note>—riches that are suitable for the dwellings of the worshippers. The sacrificers "follow" or serve you. What kind of worshippers? Those who are "wakeful in you" <note>original: tve rayiṃ jāgṛvāṃsaḥ</note>, meaning they are alert in bestowing wealth upon you through offerings. What kind of Agni is described? One who is "shining" <note>original: ruśantam</note> with a bright complexion, possessing qualities such as movement; "visible" <note>original: darśatam</note> or beautiful to behold; "great" <note>original: bṛhantam</note>; "possessing strength" <note>original: vapāvantam; literally possessing marrow or fat, referring to the richness of the sacrificial fire</note>; and "shining" <note>original: dīdivāṃsam</note> through "all time" <note>original: viśvahā</note>.

**[On Verse 4]**
The former sacrificers, "approaching" <note>original: vyantaḥ</note> the "place of the god" <note>original: devasya padam</note>—referring to the location of the *Ahavaniya* fire <term>the consecrated fire for offerings</term>—with "reverence" <note>original: namasā</note>, meaning with oblations or hymns of praise. These sacrificers were "desiring fame" <note>original: śravasyavaḥ</note> or desiring food, and they "attained fame" <note>original: śrava āpan</note> that is "unassailable" <note>original: amṛktam</note> or heard of everywhere.

<summary>This page contains the Vedic text and Sayana's commentary for verses 2-4 of Hymn 6.1, describing Agni's role as the primary priest and the sacrificers' devotion to him for wealth and fame.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Bharadvaja, Rig Veda, Sayana's Commentary, Hotar, sacrificial altar, Vedic wealth, Ahavaniya fire</keywords>

## Commentary (Sayana)
...that which is unassailable <note>original: mṛktam; meaning it cannot be obstructed or harmed by others</note>, they attained. O **Agni**, in the presence of your auspicious and praiseworthy sight, they find delight. They have held your **names which are worthy of sacrifice**—names that should be celebrated, such as **Vaishvanara** <note>The Fire belonging to all men</note> and **Jatavedas** <note>The Knower of all created beings</note>. Alternatively, this means they have maintained hymns as the means of offering their reverence.

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

The peoples upon the earth increase you; the wealth of both kinds of men increases you.
You, O Savior, have become the one to be known, the protector, the father and mother ever-present for humanity. || 5 ||

You. They increase. The peoples. Upon the earth. You. Wealth. Of both kinds. Of the people.
You. Protector. O Savior. To be known. You have become. Father. Mother. Ever-present. Indeed. Of humans. || 5 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, the **peoples** <note>kṣitayaḥ; here referring to the officiating priests</note> **increase** you <note>strengthen you through offerings</note> upon the **earth**, which is characterized here as the sacrificial **altar**. The **wealth** <note>rāyaḥ</note> consisting of **both types** <note>referring to the five kinds of sacrificial animals</note> belonging to the **people** <note>the patrons or sacrificers</note> is directed toward you by the priests to increase your strength. Alternatively, it means that both types of wealth, such as cattle and riches, increase your glory so that the patrons may obtain sons and other blessings. O **Savior** <note>taraṇe; one who carries us across the sea of suffering</note>, you have **become** the **protector** who is **to be known** <note>ceatyaḥ; worthy of being known through praise</note>. Furthermore, you **are** the **father and mother** for us, the **human** praisers; you are **always** <note>sadmit</note> in the position of our parents.

-> ॥ This ends the twenty-fifth Varga of the fourth Adhyaya in the fourth Ashtaka ॥ <-

Worthy of worship, dear among the clans, Agni, the delightful priest, the excellent sacrificer, has sat down.

Worthy of worship. He. Dear. Among the clans. Agni. The priest. Delightful. Down. He sat. More excellent sacrificer.
That. You. We. In the house. Shining. Toward. Bowing with knees bent. With reverence. May we sit. || 6 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)
**That Agni is worthy of worship** <note>saparyaṇyaḥ</note>; he is **dear** because he fulfills all desires. He is the **priest** <note>hotā; the one who performs the manual act of sacrifice</note> among the **clans** or subjects. He is **delightful** and is the **excellent sacrificer** <note>yajīyān; one who sacrifices much better than other deities</note>. **Agni, possessing such great majesty, has sat down** at the sacrifice. Now the poet addresses him directly: **That you**, O Agni, **we** the sacrificers, in our **home** <note>dame; the place of the domestic fire</note>, approach you while you are **shining**. We **approach** you by **bending** <note>jubādhaḥ</note> our knees in a gesture of humi—

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥ <-

O Agni, we who are of good intellect, desiring happiness and seeking the gods, approach you, the newly-praised one. You, O Agni, shining with great brilliance, have led the people to the heavens through the radiant light. || 7 ||

That. You. We. Of good intellect. The newly-praised. O Agni. Desiring happiness. We approach. Seeking the gods.
You. The people. You led. Shining. Of heaven. O Agni. With great. With radiance. || 7 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, we **approach** <note>original: īmahe; meaning we request or we praise</note> **you**, such a magnificent one, who are **newly-praised** <note>original: navyaṃ; meaning worthy of new or constant praise</note>. We are described as having **good intellect** <note>original: sudhyaḥ; beautiful or refined minds</note>, **desiring happiness** <note>original: sumnāyavaḥ</note>, and **seeking the God** that is you <note>original: devayantaḥ</note>. O **Agni**, while you are **shining** <note>original: dīdyānaḥ</note>—by what means? By your **great** and **radiant brilliance** <note>original: bṛhatā rocanena</note>—you **led** <note>original: anayaḥ; guided or caused to reach</note> the **people** <note>original: viśaḥ; here referring to the subjects or the singers</note> to **heaven**. The connection may also be: "Lead us to heaven by means of the radiant sun" <note>original: āditvena</note>; that is to say, via the solar path.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Eighth Verse ॥ <-

[We praise] Agni: the Sage of the people, the Lord of the perpetual tribes, the destroyer of enemies, the bestower of desires for men, the one who initiates movement, who provides nourishment, the Purifier, the Radiant One, who is worthy of sacrifice for the attainment of wealth. || 8 ||

Of the people. The Sage. The Lord of the people. Of the perpetual. The destroyer. The bestower. Of the men.
Initiating movement. Providing food. The Purifier. The Radiant. Agni. Worthy of sacrifice. Of wealth. || 8 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)

We praise Agni <note>the phrase "we praise" is added to complete the grammatical sense</note>, who is the **Lord of the people** <note>original: viśpatiṃ; master or protector</note>, meaning the eternal **people** consisting of the officiating priests and the patrons of the sacrifice. He is the **Sage** <note>original: kaviṃ; one with far-reaching vision</note>, the **destroyer** of enemies <note>original: nitośanaṃ</note>, and the **bestower** <note>original: vṛṣabhaṃ; literally 'the bull', symbolizing the pourer of rewards</note> of desires for the **men** who sing his praises. He is the one who **initiates movement** <note>original: pretīṣaṇiṃ</note>, who **provides food** <note>original: iṣayantam</note>, and the **Purifier** <note>original: pāvakaṃ</note>. He is either **Radiant** <note>original: rājantaṃ</note> himself or the one who makes others shine. He is **worthy of sacrifice** <note>original: yajataṃ</note> for the sake of obtaining **wealth**.

...O **Agni**, that mortal, that **sacrificer** <note>original: yajamana</note> has worshipped. He offers worship and he **praises** <note>original: śashame</note>. Since the word "shashamana" is recorded in the lists of words for praising, this term also refers to the act of praise. That sacrificer who, along with the **fuel** <note>original: samidha</note>, performs the **offering of oblations** <note>original: havyadatim</note>, the giving of sacrificial food. Furthermore, that sacrificer who thoroughly **knows** <note>original: pari veda</note>—meaning he gives—the **offering** <note>original: ahutim</note> consisting of clarified butter and other materials accompanied by **homage** <note>original: namobhih</note> or hymns of praise. That sacrificer, **protected by you** <note>original: tvotah</note>, **holds** <note>original: dadhate</note> all **desirable** <note>original: vamani</note> **riches** <note>original: dhanani</note>.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Tenth Verse ॥ <-

**Asmai u te mahi mahe vidhema namobhiragne samidhotahavyaih ।**
**Vedi suno sahaso girbhirukthaira te bhadrayam sumatau yatema ॥ 10 ॥**

**To this. Indeed. To you. Great. To the great one. Let us worship. With homages. O Agni. With fuel. And also. With oblations.**
**At the altar. O Son. Of strength. With songs. With hymns. Towards. Your. In the auspicious. In benevolence. Let us strive. ॥ 10 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, to **this** one—to **you**, the **great** one—may we **worship** <note>original: vidhema; meaning to serve or honor</note> **greatly** and excessively. The means are stated: **with homages** <note>reverent bows</note>, with **fuel**, and **also with oblations** <note>sacrificial food</note>. O **Son of Strength** <note>original: sahaso suno; a common title for Agni because fire is produced by the physical strength of rubbing two sticks together</note>, the connection is that we worship you **at the altar** with **songs** <note>original: girbhih; praises</note> and **hymns** <note>original: ukthaih; specifically the recited portions of the ritual</note>. Furthermore, may we **strive for** <note>meaning, let us reach</note> your **auspicious** and praiseworthy **benevolence** <note>original: sumatau; your beautiful, graceful mind or favor</note>. May we come to it; this is the meaning.

**A yastatantha rodasi vi bhasa sravobhisca sravasyastarutrah ।**

**Completely. Who. Has stretched. The two worlds. Outwardly. With brilliance. With fames (foods). And. Desiring fame. The deliverer.**
**With great. With foods/strengths. With firm ones. For us. With wealthy ones. O Agni. More widely. Shine. Forth. ॥ 11 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, you **who** have **stretched across** <note>original: vyatatantha; spread over</note> the **two worlds** <note>original: rodasi; Heaven and Earth</note> with your **brilliance** <note>light</note>. Moreover, you are the **deliverer** <note>original: tarutrah; one who carries us across difficulties</note> and you become **desirous of fame** <note>original: sravasyah; seeking or deserving of renown</note> through the **fames** <note>original: sravobhih; here meaning praises or the sacrificial foods that bring renown</note> offered to you. O Agni of such a nature, **shine forth** <note>original: vi bhahi</note> **even more specifically** <note>original: vitaram</note> **for our sake** <note>original: asme</note>. Do so with **great** and massive **foods**, and with **firm**, thick, and **wealthy** riches.

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Dweller** <note>original: vaso; Agni is called 'Vasu' because he dwells in all things or provides a dwelling/wealth</note>, O Agni who possesses wealth, **grant** or establish **always** and **indeed in us** wealth **associated with men** <note>original: nṛvat; meaning wealth accompanied by heroic sons or servants</note>. Furthermore, grant **abundant cattle**. For what purpose? For our **offspring** <note>original: tokāya; referring to a son</note> and for our **son** <note>original: tanayāya; referring to a grandson</note>. Moreover, may there **be in us** those types of **nourishment** <note>original: iṣah; food or offerings</note> that are **many**—meaning they fulfill many desires—and **great**, as well as **far from evil** <note>original: āre-aghāḥ; those from which sins or calamities are kept at a distance</note>. May there also be **auspicious** states of **glory** <note>original: sauśravasāni; high renown or fame</note> for us.

The verse beginning with **Pururayapri** is the invitatory verse <note>original: anuvākyā</note> for the deity Agni Kshetravan during the ritual of gathering the clay for the sacrificial pot <note>original: ukhā-saṃbharaṇīya</note>. It is also indicated in the ritual manuals: *“Pururāyagne purudhā tvāyā sa citra citraṃ citayantam-asme...”* (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.1). The text of that verse follows:

## Hymn Text

**[Verse 13]**
**O satisfy-er of many with wealth, through your help in many ways, O King, may I attain your wealth through the state of a wealthy one.**
**For many are your riches, O much-desired Agni, for the worshipper, in you, the King.** || 13 ||

**[Verse 13 - Word-by-word Analysis]**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, **O King**, may I **attain**—meaning may I pervade or enjoy—**your many** and **various** types of **riches** <note>original: vasūni; wealth in the form of cattle, horses, etc.</note> through **wealthiness** <note>original: vasutā; the state of being a possessor of wealth</note>. Regarding this, the scholar **Bharatasvami** interprets the word "vasutā" as being in the locative case <note>meaning "in the state of wealth"</note>, while **Bhatta Bhaskara Mishra** also considers it as a single word in the vocative case <note>addressing Agni as the personification of wealth</note>.

O **much-desired one** <note>original: puruvāra; one who is chosen or sought by many</note>, O Agni, in **you**, the **shining** King, there **are many** forms of **wealth** to be given to **me**, the one who **serves** <note>original: vidhate</note> you.

-> ॥ This concludes the thirty-sixth section (Varga) of the fourth chapter of the fourth volume (Ashtaka) ॥ <-

May the Great Lord, the Teacher of Wisdom <note>original: Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara</note>, who dispels the darkness of the heart by the light of the Veda’s meaning, grant the four goals of human life <note>original: puruṣārthas; righteousness, wealth, desire, and liberation</note>.

Thus ends the fourth chapter of the fourth volume in the *Madhaviya Vedartha Prakasha* <note>The Elucidation of the Meaning of the Veda</note>, the commentary on the Rig Veda Samhita composed by the great teacher **Sayana**, the minister of the empire of the illustrious King **Vira Bukka**, the sovereign king of kings and the promoter of the Vedic path.

# Book 4. Chapter 5. Section 1.

I bow to the Great Lord who is the Holy Place of Knowledge <note>original: Vidya-Tirtha-Maheshvara</note>, whose breath is the Vedas and who created the entire universe from those Vedas.

Now begins the fifth chapter. In the first section of the Sixth Book—which contains six sections in total—there are fifteen hymns. Among these, the second hymn beginning with the words "You indeed" (tvam hi) consists of eleven verses. The seer (rishi) is Bharadvaja, and the deity addressed is Agni (the Fire). The first ten verses are in the Anushtubh meter <note>a meter consisting of four quarters of eight syllables each</note>, and the final verse is in the fifty-six-syllable Shakvari meter. The Index <note>original: Anukramani; the ancient catalog of Vedic hymns</note> states: "The hymn 'Tvam hi' has eleven verses, ending in Shakvari, while the rest are Anushtubh." 

Regarding its ritual application: In the Morning Recitation <note>original: Pratar-anuvaka</note> dedicated to Agni, this hymn (excluding the final verse) is utilized within the Anushtubh section of the ceremony. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "You indeed, toward the home, O Agni, where the priest was born..." <note>Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.13</note>. This hymn is also to be recited during the Ashvina-shastra ritual, following the same rules as the Morning Recitation. Furthermore, on the second day of the "Two-Night Rite of the Angirasas," this very hymn serves as the libation-praise. It is noted: "The verse 'You indeed, toward the home' serves as the libation-praise" <note>Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 10.2</note>.

---

-> ॥ First Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**You indeed proceed toward the home-like glory, O Agni, as a friend.**
**You, O All-seeing Dweller, nourish our fame and prosperity.** ॥ १ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**You** | **Indeed** | **Associated with the home** | **Glory** | **O Agni** | **Friend** | **Like** | **You proceed/master** |
**You** | **O All-seeing** | **Fame/Food** | **O Dweller** | **Prosperity** | **And/Like** | **You nourish** ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, **you indeed** <note>original: tvam hi</note> truly **proceed toward** <note>original: patyase; literally 'to go' or 'to master'</note> the **glory** <note>original: yashas</note>, which here refers to the food characterized by the sacrificial offerings. This glory is **associated with the home** <note>original: kshaitavat</note>. The word 'kshiti' refers to a dwelling or sometimes to decay/depletion; thus 'kshaita' refers to the dry wood fuel or the residential offerings. An illustration is provided: **like a friend** <note>original: mitro na</note>. Just as the deity Mitra (who presides over the day) approaches the world, you approach the sacrifice. Alternatively, "glory" can mean the house itself; in this sense, you approach the sacrificer’s home, which contains the offerings, just as a friendly person visits a home. 

Alternatively, the verb "patyase" can imply lordship; thus, you are the master of such food. For this reason, O **All-seeing** one <note>original: vicharshane; one who sees everything specifically</note> and O **Dweller** <note>original: vaso; an epithet of Agni meaning one who provides a dwelling or is the essence of all beings</note>, you **nourish** <note>original: pushyasi</note> or increase the **fame** <note>original: shravas; often used to mean food that brings renown</note> found in the sacrificer's house, and (here the word **na** functions as "and") you also nourish our **prosperity**. You cause both the food and the resulting strength to grow.

<vocab>
- **Agni**: The sacred fire and messenger between gods and humans.
- **Bharadvaja**: A famous ancient seer and the traditional author of the Sixth Book of the Rig Veda.
- **Anushtubh**: A standard Vedic meter of 32 syllables.
- **Shakvari**: A long, complex meter of 56 syllables.
- **Sayana**: The 14th-century scholar whose commentary is the standard guide for understanding the Vedas.
- **Pratar-anuvaka**: A foundational morning litany in the Soma sacrifice.
- **Vicharshani**: "All-seeing" or "distinguishing"; an epithet highlighting Agni's wisdom.
- **Vasu**: "The Abode" or "The Radiant"; a class of deities or an epithet for Agni as the provider of stability.
</vocab>

The commentary explains the first verse, which praises Agni as a friendly deity who masters the sacrificial offerings and brings prosperity to the worshiper's home.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Bharadvaja, Sayana commentary, Vedic ritual, Anushtubh meter, prosperity, sacrificial food</keywords>

## Hymn Text
For you, indeed, the peoples honor with sacrifices and with songs;
Toward you the swift one goes, the un-harmer, the crosser of the regions, the observer of all. ॥ 2 ॥

### Padapatha
You. | Indeed. | [Particle] | The peoples. | With sacrifices. | With songs. | They honor.
You. | The swift one. | Goes. | The un-harmer. | The region-crosser. | The all-observer. ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, it is **you indeed** that the **peoples**, meaning human beings, **honor**—that is, they praise—with **sacrifices**, referring to the offering-materials used in worship, and **with songs**, meaning hymns of praise. Furthermore, the **swift one** <term>vājī: literally "possessing speed" or "strong," usually referring to a horse, but here interpreted as the Sun</term> **goes** toward you; he enters you, in fact. For so it is heard in the scriptures: "The Sun enters the Fire in the evening, therefore the fire is seen from a distance at night." <note>original: Aitareya Brahmana 8.28</note>. The word "swift" is also used in various places to refer to the Sun, as in: "Agni, Vayu, and Surya—these are indeed the swift ones." 

What is the nature of this "swift" Sun? He is an **un-harmer**, meaning he is free from those who would do violence. He is the **crosser of regions**. The word "regions" <note>original: rajas</note> can also mean "water," making him the impeller of rain; alternatively, it means he is the crosser or traveler through the various worlds or regions of space. Finally, he is the **observer of all**, the one who witnesses everything.

-> || Now the Third Verse || <-

## Hymn Text
With one accord, the leaders of heaven kindle you, the banner of the sacrifice,
When the human person, seeking happiness, calls you in the sacred rite. ॥ 3 ॥

### Padapatha
With one accord. | You. | Of heaven. | The leaders. | Of the sacrifice. | The banner. | They kindle.
When. | Indeed. | That. | Human. | Person. | Desiring happiness. | Calls. | In the sacrifice. ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, with **one accord**—meaning acting together with pleasure—the **leaders of heaven** (the priests who lead the chants) **kindle you**, who are the **banner of the sacrifice**, the one who makes the ritual known. If you ask when they do this, it is explained: **When indeed that human person**—the worshiper or the priest who is a descendant of Manu—**desiring happiness** for himself, **calls** upon you in the **sacrifice** <term>adhvare: a term for sacrifice literally meaning "that which is free from violence or harm"</term>.

-> || Now the Fourth Verse || <-

## Hymn Text
The mortal who today, for you the Bountiful, strives with prayer,
Through the protection of the great heaven, he crosses over enemies and distress... ॥ 4 ॥

<vocab>
**Peoples** (carṣaṇayaḥ: human beings), **Swift one** (vājī: usually a horse, but here the Sun), **Region-crosser** (rajastūr: one who travels through space or brings rain), **All-observer** (viśvacarṣaṇiḥ: the witness of all), **With one accord** (sajoṣaḥ: in harmony), **Banner** (ketum: a sign or light that reveals), **Seeking happiness** (sumnāyuḥ: one desiring well-being), **Sacrifice** (adhvare: a rite without injury).
</vocab>

...may he prosper. That sacrificer should prosper, O **Agni**, for you, the one who gives excellent gifts. <note>The commentator notes a grammatical shift: a dative case is used where a genitive "of you" would be expected.</note> Through the ritual action <term>dhiyā: a term implying both prayer and the physical work of the sacrifice</term> associated with you, whatever mortal—one subject to the law of death—exerts himself. Alternatively, the root word for "exertion" here refers to the act of praising; he praises you while being engaged in the ritual work for your sake. That sacrificer, through your protection <note>original: ūtyā</note> which comes from the great and shining heavens, crosses over his enemies and over sin <note>original: aṃhaḥ</note>, which is like a destructive blow. He overcomes them entirely. ॥ 4 ॥

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
The mortal who, with fuel, reaches your sharpened offering, O Agni,
He prospers in an abode full of branches and lasting a hundred years. ॥ 5 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
With fuel. | Who. | Your. | Offering. | Sharpened. | Mortal. | Reaches.
Possessing branches. | He. | Prospers. | Abode. | O Agni. | A hundred-year life. ॥ 5 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, consider the **mortal** man who **reaches**—meaning he fully attains or completes—your **sharpened offering**. This refers to an oblation that has been "sharpened" or refined through the power of the sacred mantras, and it is offered along **with fuel** <term>samidh: the sticks used to kindle the sacred fire</term>. That man, the sacrificer, **prospers** in his **abode** <term>kshaya: a dwelling or home</term>. What kind of home? One that is **full of branches**. Here, "branches" <note>original: vayāḥ</note> is a metaphor for a flourishing family tree, specifically meaning sons, grandsons, and further descendants. Furthermore, he prospers with a **life of a hundred years**, which represents either many various forms of wealth or simply a very long and healthy life. The meaning is that his prosperity and his lineage will endure for a long time.

-> ॥ Thus ends the first section (Varga) of the fifth chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Your brilliant smoke rises to the heavens; pure and spread out, it reaches upward.
Like the sun with its light, you shine with beauty, O Purifier. ॥ 6 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
Brilliant. | Your. | Smoke. | Rises. | In the heavens. | Being. | Pure. | Spread out.
The Sun. | Like. | Indeed. | With light. | You. | With beauty. | O Purifier. | You shine. ॥ 6 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, your **smoke**, which is **brilliant** and **pure**—meaning it is either stainless or white in color—**rises** into the **heavens** or the mid-space. As it is **spread out** extensively, it is transformed into the nature of clouds. Furthermore, O...

<vocab>
- अग्नि (Agni): The deity of fire, the mediator between gods and humans.
- यजमान (Yajamana): The person who sponsors and benefits from the sacrifice.
- समिध् (Samidh): Sacred fuel sticks, usually from specific trees, used to feed the ritual fire.
- आहुति (Ahuti): An offering made into the fire, such as clarified butter (ghee) or grains.
- वया (Vaya): Literally "branches," used here metaphorically to mean a family lineage or progeny.
- क्षय (Kshaya): A place of residence; a home or dwelling.
- शतायुष (Shatayusha): "Possessing a hundred years," the traditional Vedic ideal for a full human lifespan.
</vocab>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary for the second hymn of the Sixth Mandala of the Rig Veda. The previous page discussed Agni's role in rewarding the sacrificer with longevity and protection. This page continues the praise of Agni, likening him to a guest, a wise elder, and a swift horse, while explaining his manifestation through the ritual churning of wood.</meta>

O purifier, Agni the cleanser, **like the sun in the sky**, being praised by a hymn capable of attracting your grace, you truly shine with radiance. Indeed, you blaze forth. ॥ 6 ॥

->॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
Now indeed you are to be praised among the people, our dear guest;
Joyful like an elder in a city, like a son to be honored. ॥ 7 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
Now. | Indeed. | Among the people. | Praiseworthy. | You are. | Dear. | Our. | Guest.
Joyful. | Like in a city. | Aging/Elderly. | Son. | Like. | To be honored. ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
And furthermore, **among the people** <note>original: vikṣu</note>, O Agni, you **are to be praised** <note>original: īḍyaḥ</note>. The word **indeed** <note>original: hi</note> expresses the reason for this. Because you are such, you are our **guest** <note>original: atithiḥ</note>. This is an implied simile; you are dear to us like a guest. Or, having become one who travels constantly to carry the sacrificial offerings, you are dear to us. 

Also, **like in a city** <note>original: purīva</note>, where an **elder** <note>original: jūryo</note>—meaning an aged and wise king who advises for our welfare—resides, you are **joyful** <note>original: ranvo</note>, meaning pleasant or one who should be approached. 

Similarly, **like a son** <note>original: sūnurna</note>, you are **to be honored** <note>original: cayayāyyaḥ</note>, meaning you are to be cared for and protected by the sacrificers. <note>The word "cayayāyya" is a specialized grammatical form of the root "cay," meaning to honor or observe.</note> 

Alternatively, that word "to be honored" is a description of the son. One is "honored" because he attains a collection <note>original: caya</note> of knowledge, austerity, and ritual works. <note>The commentator explains the grammatical suffix "āyya" here is similar to that found in the word "desirable."</note> 

Or, "honored" refers to one who has obtained a "collection of births." Tradition records a collection of three births: first, the physical birth from the mother; second, from the tying of the sacred grass belt <term>maunjibandhana: the initiation ritual for a student</term>; and third, from the consecration for a sacrifice. Such a son is **joyful** and pleasant.

->॥ Now the Eighth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
By the rite, Agni, you are revealed in the wood, like a strong horse performing a task;
Like the wandering wind, you are food and home, like a swift horse, a child to be led. ॥ 8 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
By the rite. | Indeed. | In the wood. | You are revealed/anointed. | O Agni. | Horse. | Like. | Capable of action.
Like the wandering wind. | Food/Offering. | House/Wealth. | Steed. | Like. | To be led. | Child. ॥ 8 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, **by the rite** <note>original: kratvā</note> of churning the fire-sticks, you who exist **in the wood** <note>original: droṇe</note>—meaning the wooden materials or the fire-drills—**are revealed** <note>original: ajyase</note>. You are indeed made manifest. 

Also, **like a horse** <note>original: vājī na</note>, you are **capable of action** <note>original: kṛtvyaḥ</note>. The term *kṛtvi* is a name for action; you are the performer of actions such as carrying the sacrificial offerings. Just as a horse carries a man, Agni's likeness to a horse lies in his carrying the oblation to the gods. 

Furthermore, **like the wandering one** <note>original: parijmeva</note>—meaning like the wind that moves everywhere—you, who travel everywhere in forms such as the forest fire, are **sacrificial food** <note>original: svadhā</note>. This is a name for food. You are both food and the **house** <note>original: gayo</note> (or wealth). This means you are the giver of both.

<vocab>
Agni (Fire/The Divine Priest), Idya (praiseworthy), Atithi (guest), Sunu (son), Chayayayya (honorable/twice-born), Kratu (ritual action), Drona (wooden vessel/fire-stick), Vaji (strong horse), Parijman (all-pervading/wind), Swadha (ritual food/nourishment), Gaya (home/wealth).
</vocab>

The commentary also explains Agni's physical manifestation through the ritual churning of wood and his all-pervading nature as both the provider of food and the home.</summary>

## Commentary (Sayana) — Continued
Furthermore, even as a **newborn child** <note>original: śiśurjātamātro</note>, you are like a thoroughbred horse that does not always travel in a straight line; you move **crookedly** <note>original: hvāryaḥ</note>, flickering here and there. <note>The commentator notes that the word "hvaryah" is derived from the verbal root "hvṛ," meaning "to be crooked" or "to bend."</note> 

In the *Kariri* sacrifice <note>a ritual performed to bring rain</note>, specifically for the "Ammedha-chada" offering, the verse beginning with "Tvam tya" may be used as an optional invitatory prayer. This is indicated in the ancient ritual manuals: "You [consume] even those unshakeable things... all the worlds rest upon your foundation" <note>referencing the Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.13</note>.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Now the Ninth Verse ॥ <-

**You consume even those unshakeable things, O Agni, like a beast in a pasture.**
**When your splendors, O Ageless One, cut through the forests, you are the powerful one. ॥ 9 ॥**

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
You. | Those. | Indeed. | Unshakeable [things]. | O Agni. | Beast. | Like. | In pasture.
Splendors. | Indeed. | Which. | Your. | O Ageless One. | Forests. | They cut. | Powerful/Shining ones. ॥ 9 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, you consume **those** <note>original: tyā</note> pieces of wood. The word **indeed** <note>original: cit</note> here emphasizes that you consume **even** those things which are **unshakeable** <note>original: achyutā</note>—meaning logs so large and heavy they are impossible to move easily. 

A comparison is provided: you are **like a beast** <note>original: paśur na</note> such as a cow or goat released into a **pasture** <note>original: yavase</note> of grass. Just as the animal eats everything in its path, you burn through even the thickest wood in a mere moment. 

O **Ageless One** <note>original: ajara</note>—you who are free from decay—your **splendors** <note>original: dhāma</note>, which are your radiant flames, **cut through** <note>original: vṛścanti</note> or carve up the **forests** <note>original: vanā</note> that are meant to be enjoyed. The word **powerful** <note>original: śikvasaḥ</note> describes your blazing light. The word *ha* in the verse serves merely to complete the poetic meter.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Now the Tenth Verse ॥ <-

**For you desire the offerings of those performing the sacrifice, O Agni; you are the invoker in the house of the people.**
**O Lord of the People, make us prosperous; enjoy our oblation, O Angiras. ॥ 10 ॥**

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
You desire. | For. | Of those desiring sacrifice. | O Agni. | Invoker. | In the house. | Of the people.
Prosperous. | O Lord of the People. | Make [us]. | Enjoy. | Oblation. | O Angiras. ॥ 10 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, in the **house** <note>original: dame</note> of the **people** <note>original: viśām</note>—meaning the sacrificers who desire the performance of the sacred rite—you are the **Invoker** <note>original: hotā</note> who calls the gods. Because you **desire** <note>original: veṣi</note> our hymns and our offerings, O **Lord of the People** <note>original: viśpate</note> and protector of the community, **make** <note>original: kṛṇu</note> us **prosperous** <note>original: samṛdhaḥ</note>. 

Having done so, O **Angiras** <note>original: aṅgiraḥ</note>—you who possess the quality of swift movement or who appear in the form of glowing coals—**enjoy** <note>original: juṣasva</note> and accept our **oblation** <note>original: havyam</note>.

## Hymn Text

**O God of friendly light, speak of our good intentions to the gods between the two worlds;**
**Lead us to well-being and a secure dwelling, O leader of the men of heaven. May we cross over our haters, our sins, and our difficulties; may we cross them, may we cross them through your protection. ॥ 11 ॥**

**अच्छ॑ । नः॒ । मि॒त्र॒ऽम॒हः॒ । दे॒व॒ । दे॒वान् । अ॒ग्ने॒ । वो॒चः॒ । सु॒ऽम॒तिम् । रोद॑स्योः ।**
**वी॒हि । स्व॒स्तिम् । सु॒ऽक्षि॒तिम् । दि॒वः । नॄन् । द्वि॒षः । अंहो॑सि । दुः॒ऽइ॒ता । त॒रे॒म॒ । ता । त॒रे॒म॒ । तव॑ । अ॒वसा॑ । त॒रे॒म॒ ॥ ११ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **God of friendly light** <note>original: mitramaho; one whose radiance is beneficial or friendly</note>, O Agni, you who possess the qualities of generosity and light, you exist within the **two worlds** <note>original: rodasyoḥ; Heaven and Earth</note>. Please **speak** <note>original: vocaḥ; announce or proclaim</note> of our **good intentions** <note>original: sumatim; our prayer or hymn of praise</note> to the **gods** <note>original: devān</note> such as Indra and others. **Lead** <note>original: vīhi</note> us, who are the leaders of this praise to **heaven** <note>original: divaḥ</note>, toward **well-being** <note>original: svastim; non-destruction</note> and a **secure dwelling** <note>original: sukṣitim; a beautiful or stable place to live</note>. <note>The commentator notes that the verb 'vīhi' here implies a causative sense—'make us go' or 'lead us'.</note>

Furthermore, may we **cross over** <note>original: tarema</note> our **haters** <note>original: dviṣaḥ; enemies</note>, our **sins** <note>original: aṃhāṃsi</note>, and the **difficulties** <note>original: duritā</note> that arise as the results of those sins. May we also **cross over** **those** <note>original: tā</note> sins committed in previous lives which are now distant. This meaning is repeated for emphasis: O Agni, through **your protection** <note>original: tavāvasā</note>, may we completely cross over our enemies and all obstacles.

-> ॥ This concludes the second section of the fifth chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-

**The third hymn <note>referring to the third in this specific sequence, though it is the 4th Sukta of the Mandala</note>, beginning with "Agne sa kṣeṣad," consists of eight verses. It was revealed to the seer Bharadvāja, is set in the Triṣṭubh meter, and is addressed to Agni. It is listed in the index with the opening words "Agneṣṭau." Its ritual use is prescribed for the morning litany and the Ashvina ceremony.**

-> ॥ Here is the first verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**O Agni, he dwells in peace, the protector of the Order, born of the Order; he attains the wide light in your service, O God,**
**The mortal whom you, alongside Mitra and Varuna, protect from harm and distress. ॥ 1 ॥**

**अग्ने॑ । सः । क्षे॒षत् । ऋ॒त॒ऽपाः । ऋ॒ते॒ऽजाः । उ॒रु । ज्योतिः॑ । न॒श॒ते॒ । दे॒व॒ऽयुः । ते॒ ।**
**यम् । त्वम् । मि॒त्रेण॑ । वरु॑णः । स॒जोषाः॑ । दे॒व॒ । पा॒सि । त्यज॑सा । मर्त्त॑म् । अंहः॑ ॥ १ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni, he**—the patron of the sacrifice—**dwells in peace** <note>original: kṣeṣat; he lives or resides securely</note>. The meaning is that he shall live for a long time. What kind of worshiper is he? He is a **protector of the Order** <note>original: ṛtapā; protector of the cosmic truth or the sacrifice</note> and **born of the Order** <note>original: ṛtejā; born for the sake of the sacrifice</note>. By dwelling in this state and being **devoted to the gods** <note>original: devayuḥ; one who desires the gods for himself</note> in **your** <note>original: te</note> service, that worshiper **attains** <note>original: naśate</note> the **wide** <note>original: uru</note> and extensive **light**...

---
<vocab>
<term>Mitramahas</term> (Friendly light): An epithet of Agni emphasizing his benevolent aspect toward humans.
<term>Rodasi</term> (The two worlds): A common Vedic term referring to the duality of Heaven and Earth.
<term>Amhas</term> (Sin/Distress): Often carries the physical connotation of being "narrow" or "constricted," which Agni helps the worshiper "cross over" into "wide light."
<term>Rta</term> (Order): The cosmic, moral, and ritual truth that governs the universe.
</vocab>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the fourth Mandala of the Rigveda, specifically Hymn 5. It concludes the explanation for the first verse and provides the full text and commentary for the second and third verses. The text focuses on the spiritual and material rewards granted by Agni to the faithful sacrificer and describes the fearsome yet beautiful nature of the divine fire.</meta>

...attains the one named the Sun. He reaches him. O glowing Agni, that **mortal** <note>original: martam</note> man, the **sacrificer** <note>original: yajamanam</note>, whom you—being of one mind with **Mitra** and **Varuna** <note>original: varuṇaḥ; here the first case is used for the third case, meaning "with Varuna"</note>—protect from **sin** <note>original: aṃhasaḥ; also translated as distress or evil</note> by means of your weapon which drives away evil—that man is connected to the previous statement.

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**He has sacrificed with sacrifices, he has labored with ritual works; he has given to Agni, the bestower of abundant wealth. Thus, neither the lack of glorious sons, nor sin, nor misfortune ever overtakes that mortal man. ॥ 2 ॥**

**ई॒जे । य॒ज्ञेभिः॑ । शश॒मे । शमी॑भिः । ऋ॒ध॒ऽवारा॑य । अ॒ग्नये॑ । द॒दाश॒ ।**
**ए॒व । च॒न । तम् । य॒शसा॑म् । अ॒जु॒ष्टिः । न । अंहः॑ । म॒र्तम् । न॒श॒ते॒ । न । प्र॒ऽह॒प्तिः ॥ २ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
That sacrificer who **gives** <note>original: dadāśa</note> oblations to Agni—who is the **possessor of prosperous and desirable wealth** <note>term: ṛdhavārāya; from 'ṛdhat' (prospering) and 'vāra' (desirable treasure)</note>—has truly **sacrificed** <note>original: īje</note> with all possible sacrifices. Likewise, through his **ritual works** <note>original: śamībhiḥ</note> such as the difficult "Moon-penance" <note>A reference to the Cāndrāyaṇa fast, which follows the phases of the moon</note>, he has become **stilled and purified** <note>original: śaśame</note>. The meaning is that through the sacrifice to Agni, he obtains every possible fruit of his labor.

Furthermore, the **lack of attainment** <note>original: ajuṣṭiḥ; or disfavor</note> of **glorious** <note>original: yaśasām</note> sons never **overtakes** <note>original: naśate; reaches or touches</note> that sacrificer. In other words, he certainly becomes the father of sons. Likewise, **sin** <note>original: aṃhaḥ; evil</note> does not reach that mortal man, nor does **misfortune** <note>original: prahaptiḥ; interpreted here as the "excessive pride" which leads to ruin</note> reach him.

---

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**His appearance is pure like that of the Sun, when your fearsome flame goes forth from you, the glowing one. Like a neighing horse, like a stopper of grief, this forest-born dweller is beautiful in every place, even in the darkness. ॥ 3 ॥**

**सू॒रः । न । यस्य॑ । दृश॒तिः । अ॒रे॒पाः । भी॒मा । यत् । एति॑ । शुच॒तः । ते॒ । आ । धीः ।**
**हेष॑स्वतः । शु॒रुधः॑ । न । अ॒यम् । अ॒क्तोः । कुच॑ । चि॒त् । रु॒खः । व॒स॒तिः । वने॑ऽजाः ॥ ३ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **appearance** <note>original: dṛśatiḥ</note> of Agni is **pure** <note>original: arepāḥ; literally "without stain" or "sinless"</note>, just **like the Sun** <note>original: sūro na</note>. O Agni, when your **flame** <note>original: dhīḥ; interpreted here as the 'supporter' or the tongue of fire</note>, which is **fearsome** <note>original: bhīmā</note>, goes forth in all directions from you as you **glow** <note>original: śucataḥ</note>.

This Agni is like a **neighing horse** <note>original: heṣasvataḥ; making a loud sound like a stallion</note> and is the **stopper of grief** <note>original: śurudhaḥ; one who checks or halts sorrow</note>. During the **night** <note>term: aktu; literally 'night,' but often used to imply the demons or rakshasas who move in the dark</note>, he grants the "cows" <note>The commentator implies Agni provides light or wealth that counters the darkness of the night-demons</note>. He is the **dweller** <note>original: vasatiḥ; the abode or refuge for all</note> and is **born in the forest** <note>original: vanejāḥ; fire produced by the friction of wood</note>. He is **beautiful** <note>original: rukhaḥ; likely a scribal variant for 'rucaḥ' meaning radiant or lovely</note> even in certain places like mountain peaks.

<vocab>
- **Agni**: The Vedic god of fire, the mediator between gods and men.
- **Yajamana**: The patron or person who pays for the Vedic sacrifice.
- **Anhas**: A Sanskrit term for sin, but more specifically the "constriction" or "distress" caused by wrong action.
- **Vanejāḥ**: "Forest-born," a common epithet for fire because it is birthed from wooden fire-sticks (aranis).
- **Aktu**: Night or darkness; in a Vedic context, it often represents the chaotic forces that Agni's light keeps at bay.
</vocab>

<summary>This page describes the spiritual and physical protection Agni provides to the sacrificer, ensuring the birth of sons and freedom from sin. It also uses vivid imagery, comparing Agni's radiance to the sun and a neighing horse, highlighting his role as a "forest-born" protector who dispels the terrors of the night.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, sacrifice, protection from sin, descendants, forest-born fire, Vedic imagery, Sayana commentary, Rigveda 4.5.2-3</keywords>

This page moves into verses 4 and 5, which use vivid natural and technical metaphors—such as horses, axes, goldsmiths, and archers—to describe the physical and transformative power of the ritual fire.</meta>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

**His path is sharp and his form is great; he shines like a horse consuming grass with its mouth. Moving to and fro like an axe, he casts his tongue; like a smelter, he melts the wood while burning it. ॥ 4 ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
**Sharp. even. movement. great. form. his. shines. horse. like. consuming. with the mouth.
moving to and fro. axe. like. tongue. smelter. like. melts. wood. burning. ॥ 4 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **movement** <note>original: ema</note> or path of this Agni is **sharp** <note>original: tigmam</note> because it is impossible to touch. And the **form** <note>original: varpas</note> of this Agni is **great** <note>original: mahi</note> and **shines** <note>original: bhasat</note>. <note>The commentator notes: the root *bhas* is used in the sense of both threatening and shining</note>. What is this Agni like? He is **like a horse** <note>original: aśvo na</note> who, with his mouth, **consumes** <note>original: yamasānaḥ</note> grass and similar things. Furthermore, he is **like an axe** <note>original: paraśur na</note>. Just as an axe casts its sharp edge into wood, Agni casts his **tongue** <note>original: jihvām</note>—meaning his flame—into the shrubs and thickets while **moving to and fro** <note>original: vijehamānaḥ</note>. Also, while **burning** <note>original: dhakṣat</note> the **timber** <note>original: dāru</note>, he is **like a smelter** <note>original: druvir na</note>. A **smelter** <note>term: druviḥ; literally one who causes to flow, referring here to a goldsmith</note> is one who melts metals; just as a goldsmith melts gold and other metals, Agni "melts" the entire forest. This means he reduces everything with a solid form to ashes.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**Like an archer aiming, he fixes his flame; he sharpens his brilliance like the edge of an iron tool. He of the variegated path, the messenger of the night, who like a bird settles on trees, having quick-moving feet. ॥ 5 ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
**He. indeed. archer-like. toward. fixes. desiring to shoot. sharpens. brilliance. iron. like. edge.
wonderful-motioned. messenger/mover. who. of the night. bird. like. tree-settling. quick-moving-feet. ॥ 5 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Indeed, he** <note>original: sa it</note>—that Agni—fixes his flame **like an archer** <note>original: asteva</note> or a shooter of arrows. Just as a bowman aims an arrow toward a target, Agni aims his flame. Having aimed and **desiring to cast** <note>original: asiṣyan</note> his flame, he **sharpens** <note>original: śiśīta</note> his own **brilliance** <note>original: tejaḥ</note>. A comparison is given: **like the edge of an iron tool** <note>original: ayaso na dhārām</note>. Just as one who wishes to strike sharpens the edge of an iron axe or tool, so does Agni. Having sharpened it, he is of **wonderful or variegated motion** <note>original: citradhrajatiḥ</note>, and is the **one who moves toward** <note>original: aratiḥ</note> the **night** <note>original: aktoḥ</note>. He is **like a bird** <note>original: ver na</note> **settling upon trees** <note>original: duṣadvā</note>, and possesses **feet capable of rapid movement** <note>term: raghupatmajanhā; from 'raghu' (fast), 'patman' (flight/falling), and 'janghā' (legs/feet)</note>. The one who behaves in this manner is the one described in the previous verses.

-> ॥ Thus ends the third section (varga) of the fifth lesson (adhyaya) of the fourth book (astaka) ॥ <-

It highlights the "sharp" and "wonderful" nature of the ritual fire as it consumes wood and moves through the night.</summary>

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**Like a chanting singer, he clothes himself in the rays of light; with his brilliance he roars, possessing friendly glory. He who is bright by night and by day—the immortal who impels men by day; he who is bright and impels men by day. ॥ 6 ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
**He. indeed. singer. like. towards. clothes. rays of light. with brilliance. roars. friendly-glory.
By night. who. indeed. bright. who. by day. men. immortal. bright. who. by day. men. ॥ 6 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

This very Agni, **like a singer** <note>original: rebhaḥ; referring here to the sun as one worthy of praise</note>, clothes himself in **rays of light** <note>original: usrāḥ; bright flames</note>. Likewise, being a **light friendly to all** <note>original: mitramahāḥ</note>, he **roars** <note>original: rarapīti</note> loudly with his radiance. This Agni, **shining** <note>original: aruṣaḥ</note> by night, impels **men** <note>original: nṝn</note> to their respective tasks during the day, just as he does during the light of day. <note>The commentator notes the word "who" is repeated for grammatical completion</note>. Furthermore, the **immortal** <note>original: amartyaḥ</note> Agni, who is either bright or free from anger, impels his own rays—the "leaders"—with his shining light during the day. Alternatively, this can be understood as: Agni, shining by night and immortal by day, joins the leading gods with the sacrificial offerings. The repetition of the phrase **who by day [impels] men** is for the sake of emphasis and respect.

---

-> ॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**Whose roar sounded forth like that of the shining heaven; the showering bull, the bright one, roared among the plants. He who moves with a speeding flight like a glowing heat, filling the two worlds, who have a good lord, with wealth. ॥ 7 ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
**Of heaven. like. whose. performing. roared. showerer. bright. among plants. roared.
Glowing heat. like. who. with speed. with flight. going. towards. two worlds. with wealth. subduing. having a good lord. ॥ 7 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **roar** <note>original: navīnot</note> of this Agni was loud, **like that of the shining heaven** <note>original: divo na</note> or the sun that creates the rays. The text explains this further: the **showering bull** <note>original: vṛṣā; he who showers desires</note>, the **bright** <note>original: rukṣaḥ</note> Agni, **roared** <note>original: nūnot</note> as the **plants** <note>original: oṣadhīṣu</note> were being burned. He who exists **going** <note>original: yan</note> with a **flight** <note>original: patmanā</note> and a **speeding** <note>original: dhrajasā</note> radiance like **glowing heat** <note>original: ghṛṇā na</note>, that Agni **subdues** <note>original: dam</note> enemies and fills the **two worlds** <note>term: rodasī; Heaven and Earth</note>—which have Agni as a **good lord** <note>original: su-patnī</note>—with **wealth** <note>original: vasunā</note>.

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the Eighth Verse ॥<-

With sustaining foods or with the chants to be joined, may he flash like lightning with his own blazing strengths. He who fashioned the strength of the Maruts, like a far-shining Sun, the brilliant one has shone forth impetuously today. ॥ 8 ॥

**With sustaining foods. Or. He who. With the chants to be joined. With chants. Lightning. Like. May he flash. With his own. With blazing strengths.**
**The strength. Or. He who. Of the Maruts. He fashioned. The far-shining Sun. Like. Brilliant. Impetuous. He has shone. ॥ 8 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

That Agni who moves with **sustaining foods** <note>original: dhāyobhiḥ; literally "nourishments"</note> or with **chants** <note>original: arkaiḥ; songs of praise</note> that are **to be joined** <note>original: yujyebhiḥ; meaning they are naturally fitting or ready to be employed</note>, may that Agni **flash forth** <note>original: devidyot; shine repeatedly</note> like **lightning** <note>original: vidyut</note> with his own **blazing strengths** <note>original: śuṣmaiḥ; powers that dry up or consume</note>. And he who **fashioned** <note>original: tatakṣa; meaning he thins out, sharpens, or makes everything keen</note> the **strength** <note>original: śardhaḥ; the host or power</note> of the **Maruts** <note>original: marutām; the storm gods</note>, as if to say he dries up all things—that very Agni, like a **far-shining Sun** <note>original: ṛbhuḥ; here glossed as the sun that shines extensively</note>, being **brilliant** <note>original: tveṣaḥ</note> and **impetuous** <note>original: rabhasānaḥ; moving with great speed</note>, **shone forth** <note>original: adyaut; shines or illuminates</note> today.

->॥ Thus ends the fourth group in the fifth section of the fourth book ॥<-

---

## Hymn Text

The fourth hymn <note>The manuscript labels this as the fourth within this specific sub-section, though it is the fifth hymn of the sixth book</note> beginning with "As the Priest" contains eight verses. The seer is **Bharadvaja**, the meter is **Trishtubh**, and the deity is **Agni**. As recorded in the index: "As the Priest." Its application (use in ritual) is prescribed for the morning litany and the Ashvin libation.

->॥ Herein the First Verse ॥<-

As, O Priest, you sacrifice for the man at the god-appointed rite with sacrifices, O Son of Strength; so today, with one mind, sacrifice to the gods who desire the offerings, O Agni, you who also desire them. ॥ 1 ॥

**As. O Priest. Of the man. At the god-appointed rite. With sacrifices. O Son. Of strength. You sacrifice.**
**So. Our. Today. With one mind. Those of equal mind. Desiring. O Agni. The desiring ones. Sacrifice. To the gods. ॥ 1 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Priest** <note>original: hotar; the one who calls the gods</note>, the invoker of the gods, O **Son of Strength** <note>original: sahasaḥ sūno; fire is called the "son of strength" because it is produced by the vigorous friction of wooden sticks</note>, O Agni! In whatever way you **sacrifice** <note>original: yajāsi</note> to the gods for the sake of **man** <note>original: manuṣaḥ; referring to Manu, the ancestral progenitor, or the current human patron of the sacrifice</note> at the **god-appointed rite** <note>original: devatātā; a term for the sacrifice itself</note> using the **sacrifices** <note>original: yajñebhiḥ; the oblations which are the means of the rite</note>—so also, O Agni, sacrifice **quickly** <note>original: samanā</note> to the **gods** <note>original: devān</note> at our rite **today** <note>original: adya</note>. Sacrifice to those who **desire** <note>original: uśataḥ</note> the offerings, while you yourself **desire** <note>original: uśan</note> them too. Alternatively, **with one mind** <term>samana</term> <note>original: samana; a place where minds are united</note> refers to the sacrifice where all gods are thought of together; the verse should be understood as occurring in that context.

<meta>This page continues the fifth hymn (Sukta) of the fourth book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda. ## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

May that radiant Agni, who is like an observer of the day, the adorable one who is to be known, grant us food. He who is the life of all, the immortal among mortals, waking at dawn, the wonderful guest, the knower of all beings. ॥ 2 ॥

**He. Our. Radiant. Observer. Like. Of the day. Agni. Adorable. To be known. Food. May he grant. The life of all. Who. Immortal. Among mortals. Waking at dawn. Wonderful. Guest. Knower of all beings. ॥ 2 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Like the sun who is the **observer** <note>original: cakṣaṇiḥ; the one who makes things visible</note> of the **day** <note>original: vostoḥ</note>, the **radiant** <note>original: vibhāvā; shining intensely</note> Agni, who is **to be known** <note>original: vedyaḥ; someone everyone should recognize or attain</note>, may he **grant** <note>original: dhāt</note> us **food** <note>original: canaḥ</note> that is **praiseworthy** <note>original: vandāru</note>. 

He is the **life of all** <note>original: viśvāyuḥ; the cause of life for everyone</note>, **immortal** <note>original: amṛtaḥ; deathless</note> among **mortals** <note>original: martyeṣu; human beings</note>. He is the **guest** <note>original: atithiḥ; one who travels constantly to carry offerings to the gods</note> and the **knower of all beings** <note>original: jātavedāḥ; one who knows all that is born or possesses all wealth</note>. Such is Agni, who among **mortals** (the human worshippers) becomes **awake at dawn** <note>original: uṣarbhut; one who is awakened for the morning Agnihotra sacrifice</note>. This connects back to the previous description.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

The heavens praise his greatness as if they were singers; he clothes himself in light like the brilliant Sun. He who, unaging and purifying, pervades all with his flame, has loosened the ancient strengths even of the firm enemy. ॥ 3 ॥

**The heavens. Like. Whose. They praise. Greatness. Lights. He clothes. Sun. Like. Brilliant. Pervades. Who. Unaging. Purifier. Of the firm. Even. He has loosened. Ancient. ॥ 3 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The word **like** <note>original: na</note> is used here in the sense of "now." As it is said in the **Nirukta** <note>A famous ancient treatise on etymology and semantics by Yaska (9.31)</note>: "There is a use of the comparative particle in the sense of 'now'." 

The **heavens** <note>original: dyāvaḥ; here interpreted by Sayana as the praisers or priests</note> **now** praise the **greatness** <note>original: abhvam; a great work or majesty</note> of Agni. That Agni, being **brilliant** <note>original: śukraḥ; white or shining</note> like the **Sun**, **clothes** <note>original: vaste; covers or envelopes</note> himself in **lights** <note>original: bhāsāṃsi; rays of splendor</note>. This Agni is **unaging** <note>original: ajaraḥ</note> and the **purifier** <note>original: pāvakaḥ; the one who cleanses everything</note>. He **pervades** <note>original: inoti</note> everything with his light. He **has loosened** <note>original: śiśrathat; destroys or strikes down</note> the **ancient** <note>original: pūrvyāṇi</note> powers even of the **firm** <note>original: aghnasya; the unyielding enemy or demons</note>. The root *śrath* is used in the sense of "to strike" or "to kill."

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

From the head the ants have come forth... Agni by his birth made the path of food... O giver of strength, grant us strength, like a King... you dwell in a safe place... ॥ 4 ॥

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the fourth verse and provides the complete fifth verse of the fourth hymn (Sukta) in the sixth book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda. The previous page discussed Agni’s role as a guest and a knower of all beings. ## Hymn Text

**To be spoken of.** Indeed. **O Son.** Thus. **Agni.** **Sitting at the food.** **He made.** **Agni.** **By birth.** **A home.** **Food.** He. **You.** **Us.** **In the giving of strength.** **Strength.** **Grant.** **Like a king.** **Conquer.** **In a place free from wolves.** **You dwell.** **Within.** Thus. ॥ 4 ॥

---

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

He who sharpens his warding radiance, who eats the food; like the wind, the ruler, he passes beyond the nights. May we overcome those who do not give to you; like a swift horse, may you, the overcomer, strike down those who fall upon us. ॥ 5 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
**Sharpens. He. Warding. Food. Eats. Wind. Like. Ruler. Beyond. Goes. Nights. May we overcome. Who. Your. Of the commands. Non-givers. Swift horse. Like. Challenged. Falling. Overcomer.** ॥ 5 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Son** <note>original: sūno; referring to the "Son of Strength," a common title for Agni because he is produced by the forceful rubbing of wood</note> of might! Or, O Agni, the impeller of all! Truly, you are **to be spoken of** <note>original: vahvā; meaning praiseworthy</note>. The next part of the verse is spoken in the third person. **Sitting at the food**, Agni sits among the delicious oblations to accept them. **By birth**, or by his very nature, he has **made** for the sacrificers a **home** <note>original: ajjma; a term identified in the Nighantu as a synonym for "house" or "food"</note>. O **giver of strength**, O Agni who grants food, as such, may you **grant strength** and food to **us**. Furthermore, **conquer** our enemies **like a king**. Dwell **within** our fire-chamber, which is **free from wolves** <note>original: avṛke; meaning a place free from robbers, demons, or those who cause harm</note>.

**He who**, namely Agni, **sharpens** <note>original: nitikti; from the root 'tij' meaning to whet or sharpen</note> his own radiance which is the **warder** of darkness. And he **eats** the food in the form of oblations offered by the sacrificers. As it is said in the sacred texts: "Fire is indeed the eater of food and the lord of food." That Agni is the **ruler** <note>original: rāṣṭrī; a term for a sovereign or lord</note> **like the wind** <note>original: vāyur na</note>. Just as the wind rules everything by its own greatness, so too is Agni the lord of all. Being such, he **passes beyond** the **nights** <note>original: aktūn</note>; he dispels the darkness inherent in them. 

By your grace, may we **overcome** or strike down the person who is a **non-giver** <note>original: arātiḥ; one who does not offer oblations to the gods</note> toward you. Alternatively, may we strike down the person who opposes us when we announce our offerings. And you, **like a swift horse** <note>original: atyo na</note> of noble breed, be the **overcomer** <note>original: parihut; one who strikes down or bypasses</note> who destroys the **falling** enemies who come toward us in challenge.

-> ॥ Thus ends the fifth Varga of the fifth Anuvaka in the fourth Ashtaka ॥ <-

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Mandala 4, Sukta 7 of the Rig Veda. The previous page concluded with verse 5, discussing Agni as a protector against those who do not offer sacrifices. ## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

Like the Sun with its luminous rays, O Agni, you have extended across the two worlds <note>original: rodasi; refers to the pair of Heaven and Earth</note> with your light. Wonderful and enveloped in radiance, he leads away the darkness as he moves on his path, like the Sun, the son of the Desirous One <note>original: aushija; an epithet for the Sun or a specific radiant being</note>. ॥ 6 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
**Indeed. Sun. Like. Luminous. With rays. Agni. You have extended. Two worlds. Thus. Through light. Wonderful. Leads. Around. Darkness. Enveloped. With radiance. On the path. Son of the Desirous. Like. Moving.** ॥ 6 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, you have **extended** across the **two worlds**—meaning Heaven and Earth—with your **light**. You cover them completely. An illustration is provided: **Like the Sun** <note>original: suryo na</note> with its **luminous**, worshipful, and powerful rays. Just as the Sun spreads its light, so do you. The second half of the verse is spoken in the third person. **On the path** <note>original: patman; meaning the way or track upon which one falls/travels</note>, Agni moves **like the Son of the Desirous One** <note>original: aushijo na</note>. "The Desirous" <note>original: ushijah</note> refers to the worshippers; the "Son of the Desirous" is the Sun, who is related to them through their praise. Like the sun, **moving** and **enveloped** or joined **with radiance**, the **wonderful** and perceivable Agni **leads away** the **darkness** of the night. He makes it pass away. The meaning is that he removes it from every direction. ॥

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥ <-

Indeed, we choose you, the most delightful one, with the radiance of our prayers. O Agni, hear our great praise. The priests, the best of leaders, satisfy you with wealth in the form of offerings, as they would satisfy Indra with power or Vayu the traveler. ॥ 7 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
**You. Indeed. Most delightful. With the radiance of prayers. We choose. Great. Our. Hear. Agni. Indra. Like. You. With power. Deity. Vayu. They satisfy. With wealth. Best of leaders.** ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, because we **choose** <note>original: vṛṇīmahe; meaning to serve or honor</note> **you**, who are **the most delightful** <note>original: mandratamam; the most praiseworthy or pleasing</note> and who are endowed **with the radiance of prayers** <note>original: arka-shokaiḥ; meaning worshipful and beautiful lights or hymns</note>, therefore **hear our great** hymn. O Agni, the **best of leaders** <note>original: nṛtamāḥ</note>—referring to the priests who lead the chants—**satisfy** <note>original: pṛṇanti</note> **you**, who are a **divine being** <note>original: devatā</note>, **with wealth** consisting of the oblations. They do this just as they would satisfy **Indra** with **power** or as they would satisfy **Vayu** the traveler. <note>The commentator notes a grammatical variation here where the word "deity" (devatā) is used in place of the direct object "you".</note> ॥

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Eighth Verse ॥ <-

Now, O Agni, lead us to welfare by paths free from wolves <note>original: avṛkebhiḥ; paths where there are no robbers or wild beasts</note>. Through those paths, help us cross over distress. Grant that happiness to the patrons and to the one who sings your praise. May we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with brave sons. ॥ 8 ॥

<vocab>
**Agni:** The god of fire and the mediator of sacrifices.
**Rodasi:** The dual entity of Heaven and Earth.
**Surya:** The Sun.
**Bhanumat:** Possessing light or splendor.
**Shoka:** Radiance, heat, or the "burn" of a prayer.
**Ritvij:** A priest who performs the sacrifice at the proper time.
**Radhas:** Wealth, specifically the ritual wealth of the oblation.
**Sumna:** Benevolence, favor, or the happiness resulting from divine grace.
</vocab>
