## Hymn Text (RV 6.4.8 - Word-for-Word Breakdown)

Now. Us. O Agni. Through safe [paths]. Well-being. Lead. Wealth. Through paths. Lead across. Sin.
Those. For the wise ones. To the singer. Grant. Happiness. May we rejoice. A hundred winters. With brave sons. ॥ 8 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni, through safe [paths]** <note>original: avrkebhih</note>—the word "wolves" <note>original: vrka</note> here refers to thieves—so, through paths free from them, **now** quickly **lead** us to **wealth** with **well-being** <note>original: svasti</note> or safety. **Lead us across** from **sin** <note>original: amhas</note> or evil. Through the paths described, guide us to the other side. Those **happinesses** <note>original: sumnam</note> which are to be given by you to the **wise ones** <note>original: suribhyah</note> or the praisers—**grant** those to me, the **singer** who praises you. And may we **rejoice**, being **with brave sons** <note>original: suvira</note>—meaning sons and grandsons who are born with heroic strength—for **a hundred winters** <note>original: shatahima</note>, which refers to a hundred autumns or years. ॥

-> || This concludes the sixth section (varga) of the fifth chapter (adhyaya) of the fourth book (ashtaka) || <-

**"I call you..."** <note>original: huve vah</note> is the fifth hymn, consisting of seven verses. The seer is Bharadvaja, the meter is Trishtubh, and the deity is Agni. It is also indexed in the Catalog: **"I call you, seven"** <note>original: huve vah sapta</note>. Its ritual use is mentioned in the morning recitation <note>original: prataranuvaka</note> and the liturgy for the Ashvins <note>original: ashvinashastra</note>.

-> || Within this, the first verse || <-

## Hymn Text (RV 6.5.1)

I call upon the son of strength, the youthful one, the one of truthful speech, with prayers, the youngest;
He who impels all-desirable riches, the wise one, much-desired, and not deceitful. ॥ 1 ॥

**[Word-for-Word Breakdown]**
I call. You. Son. Of strength. Youthful. Of truthful speech. With prayers. Youngest.
Who. Impels. Riches. Wise. All-desirable. Much-desired. Not deceitful. ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, I **call** <note>original: huve</note> upon **you**—the plural "you" <note>original: vah</note> is used here by way of grammatical substitution for the singular—with **prayers** <note>original: matibhih</note> or hymns that are to be meditated upon. Of what kind is he? He is the **son of strength** <note>original: sahaso sunum</note>, for Agni is produced when he is churned with strength. He is **youthful**, meaning eternally young or the distributor of rewards. He is **of truthful speech** <note>original: adroghavacam</note>, meaning one in whom speech that is non-deceitful, praiseworthy, and in the form of hymns is employed. He is the **youngest** <note>original: yavishtham</note> or most youthful. He is **wise** <note>original: pracetah</note> or possessor of excellent knowledge; he is **much-desired** <note>original: puruvarah</note> or worthy of being chosen by many; and he is **not deceitful** <note>original: adhruk</note> toward the sacrificers. Such is **this Agni who impels** or sends **all-desirable** and praiseworthy **riches** <note>original: dravinani</note>—that is to say, he gives them to the singers. To you, I **call**—this connects back to the beginning of the verse. ॥

-> || Now the second verse || <-

## Hymn Text (RV 6.5.2)

In you, O Priest of many forms, the sacrificial ones have placed riches day and night;
In you, the Purifier, all beings and fortunes are held as if in the earth. ॥ 2 ॥

<vocab>
Agni: The fire god and divine messenger.
Bharadvaja: The traditional seer/author of the 6th Mandala.
Trishtubh: A Vedic meter consisting of four lines of eleven syllables each.
Sumna: Comfort, favor, or happiness.
Rasi: To grant or bestow.
Madema: "May we rejoice," a common concluding prayer in the Rig Veda.
Shatahima: "A hundred winters," a traditional idiom for a full human lifespan.
Sunu: Son; often used for Agni as the "Son of Strength" (Sahasas-punutra) because fire is produced by the vigorous friction of wood.
Sahas: Force, strength, or power.
Adroghavach: One whose speech is not injurious; truthful or reliable in his word.
Vishvavara: Containing or granting all desirable things.
Dravina: Wealth, property, or liquid assets (often used for sacrificial offerings or rewards).
</vocab>

## Hymn Text

<note>Analyzed word-for-word form (Padapatha) for Rig Veda 6.5.2</note>
They. [Particle]. Wealth. O Many-flamed. O Invoker. At night. In the morning. [Particle]. They moved. Worthy of sacrifice. Like the earth. All. Worlds. In whom. Together. Good fortunes. They placed. O Purifier. ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **many-flamed** <note>original: puruanika</note>—you who possess many tongues of fire—O **invoker** <note>original: hotar</note>—the caller of the gods—O Agni, in **thee**, at **night** <note>original: dosa</note> and during the **day** <note>original: vastoh</note>, those **worthy of sacrifice** <note>original: yajniyasah</note>—the sacrificers—**moved** <note>original: erire</note> **wealth** <note>original: vasuni</note> consisting of offerings. They impel them forward; that is, they offer them into the fire. Just as **all worlds** <note>original: vishva bhuvanani</note> or living beings [rest] **upon the earth** <note>original: kshama-iva</note>, so in this **purifier** <note>original: pavake</note>—Agni the cleanser—the gods **placed** <note>original: samdadhire</note> or firmly deposited **good fortunes** <note>original: saubhaghani</note> or riches. There is a scriptural text that says: <term>“In Agni, they deposited the lovely wealth”</term> <note>original: agnau vamam vasu samnyadadhata</note>. This [phrase regarding the gods] should be connected to the previous statement about the worshiper.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now, the Third Verse ॥ <-
Thou among the people from of old sittest; among these, through wisdom, thou becamest the leader of desirable things.
Thou drivest the Truth to the worshiper, O Wise One; continuously, O Knower of Beings, thou distributest riches. ॥ 3 ॥

<note>Analyzed word-for-word form (Padapatha) for Rig Veda 6.5.3</note>
Thou. Among the people. From of old. Sittest. Among these. Through wisdom. The leader/charioteer. Thou becamest. Of desirable things. Truth. Thou drivest. To the worshiper. O Wise One. [Particle]. Continuously. O Knower of Beings. Riches. ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, **thou** among **ancient** <note>original: pradivah; a term for antiquity</note> **people** <note>original: vikshu</note>—those of former times and those seen now—**sittest** <note>original: sidah</note>. You dwell as the inner soul of all. Likewise, through thy **wisdom** <note>original: kratva</note> or thy own sacred action, thou **becamest the leader** <note>original: rathir-abhavah</note>—the one who brings or conveys to the sacrificers—of **desirable** <note>original: varyanam</note> riches. For this reason, O **wise one** <note>original: cikitvo</note>, O **knower of beings** <note>original: jatavedo</note>—the one who knows all created things—to the **worshiper** <note>original: vidhate</note> who serves you, thou **drivest** <note>original: inoshi</note> **riches** <note>original: vasuni</note> **continuously** <note>original: anushak</note> or in an unbroken line. Thou impellest them in various ways.

---

## Hymn Text

<note>Ritual Context for Rig Veda 6.5.4</note>
In the <term>Pravargya</term> <note>a ritual where a clay pot of milk and ghee is heated to glowing</note> and the <term>Abhishava</term> <note>the pressing of the Soma stalks</note>, a pair of verses beginning with **“He who, secret from us”** is used. It is stated in the ritual manuals: “He who, secret from us, would harm us, O Agni; Be thou to us, O Agni, well-disposed when approached—these are the two verses.” (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.6).
-> ॥ The first of those two, and the fourth in the hymn ॥ <-

He who, secret from us, would harm us, O Agni, or he who, being internal, O thou of friend-like greatness, would attack us;
Him with thy undecaying, powerful flames, do thou burn, O hottest one, burning with thy heat. ॥ 4 ॥

<note>Analyzed word-for-word form (Padapatha) for Rig Veda 6.5.4</note>
He who. Us. Secretly. Would harm. O Agni. He who. Internal. O thou of friend-like greatness. Would attack. Him. With undecaying. Powerful [flames]. Thou. Thine own. Burn. O Hottest. With heat. Possessing heat. ॥ 4 ॥

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the fifth hymn (Sukta) of the sixth book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda. It completes the explanation for verse 4 regarding the destruction of hidden enemies and provides the full text and commentary for verses 5 and 6, focusing on the rewards of worship and the crushing of rivals.</meta>

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, the enemy who is **hidden** <note>original: sanutyah; sanutar is a name for that which is concealed</note>—remaining in a hidden place—who **harms** <note>original: abhidhasat</note> or weakens and oppresses us; and he who is an **insider** <note>original: antarah</note>—acting from within—O **you of friendly light** <note>original: mitramaho; one whose radiance is favorable or who honors his friends</note>, who would **harm** <note>original: vanusyat</note> us: O **most burning one** <note>original: tapistha</note>, most heated Agni, you who are **full of heat** <note>original: tapasvan</note> and possessor of splendor, **burn** <note>original: tapa</note> or consume them both. Do so with your own extraordinary **unaging** <note>original: ajarebhih; free from decay</note> and **showering** <note>original: vrsabhih; those that cause rain or grant desires</note> rays of light.

---

## Hymn Text

-> || Now, the Fifth Verse || <-

He who to thee with **sacrifice**, with **fuel**, he who with **recitations**, with **chants**, O **Son of Strength**, gives offerings; 
He among **mortals** becomes **immortal** and **wise**; through **wealth**, **splendor**, and **fame**, he **shines forth**. ॥ 5 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Padapatha):**
He | to thee | with sacrifice | with fuel | he | with recitations | with chants | O Son | [particle] | of Strength | gives offerings |
He | among mortals | immortal | wise | with wealth | with splendor | with fame | [prefix] | shines ॥ 5 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Son of Strength** <note>original: sahasas suno; Agni is called the "Son of Strength" because he is produced by the vigorous friction of the two fire-sticks</note>, O Agni, son of power! That sacrificer who **gives offerings** <note>original: dadasat</note> or serves you with **sacrifice** <note>original: yajnena</note>—by performing the rite; and he who serves with **fuel** <note>original: samidha</note>—the wood used as the means of kindling; and he who serves with **recitations** <note>original: ukthaih; hymns recited by the Hotar priest</note> and **chants** <note>original: arkaibhih; prayers or songs of praise worthy of being honored</note>: O **immortal one**—O Agni who is free from the nature of death—that worshiper, being **wise** <note>original: pracetah; possessing excellent knowledge</note> among **mortals** <note>original: martyesu</note> or human beings, **shines forth** <note>original: vi bhati</note> or is especially distinguished. He does so through **wealth** <note>original: raya</note>, through **splendor** <note>original: dyumnena</note> or shining riches, and through **fame** <note>original: sravasa</note>—which means either food that is "heard of" or glorious renown.

---

## Hymn Text

-> || Now, the Sixth Verse || <-

Do thou, then, being **impelled**, do that **quickly**, O Agni; strike down **rivals** with **strength**, O **Strong One**. 
As thou art **extolled** by the **lights**, **anointed** by our **words**, so **accept** the **loud prayer** of the **worshiper**. ॥ 6 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Padapatha):**
He | that | do | impelled | quickly | O Agni | rivals | strike down | with strength | O Strong One |
As | thou art extolled | with lights | anointed | with words | that | accept | of the worshiper | loud | prayer ॥ 6 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, may you, being **impelled** <note>original: isitah; sent or urged by us</note>, **do that** <note>original: tat krdhi</note> **quickly** <note>original: turyam</note>. If one asks "What is that?", it is said: You, being the **Strong One** <note>original: sahasvan; the powerful one</note>, **strike down** <note>original: badhasva</note> or destroy the **rivals** <note>original: sprdhah; those who compete or contend against us</note> with your **strength** <note>original: sahasa</note>—your power or splendor capable of overwhelming others. You who are **anointed** <note>original: aktah; sprinkled or saturated</note> by **shining lights** <note>original: dyubhih</note>—your own radiant flames—and who **are extolled** <note>original: sasyase</note> or praised with **words** <note>original: vacobhih</note>—meaning sentences in the form of hymns of praise—which are offered by the praisers for your sake: **accept** <note>original: jusasva</note> or enjoy that **loud** <note>original: ghosi</note> and **worthy of meditation** <note>original: manma</note> **prayer** <note>original: stotram</note> of the **worshiper** <note>original: jarituh</note>.

# 592 || Rig Veda || [Book 4. Chapter 5. Group 8.]

Regarding the offering of an eight-pot-sherd cake to **Agni of Desire** <note>original: Agni Kama</note>, the verse beginning with "May we attain" serves as the offering prayer <note>original: yajya</note>. It is also indicated in the ritual manuals: "May we attain that desire, O Agni, by your protection," for the sake of fulfilling a wish. (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2. 10.)

-> ॥ This is the Seventh Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
<note>RV 6.6.7</note>
May we **attain** that **desire**, O **Agni**, through your **protection**; may we **attain wealth**, O **Lord of Wealth**, that includes **heroic sons**.
May we **attain strength**, while **desiring strength**; may we **attain** your **unaging** and **decayless splendor**. ॥ 7 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Padapatha):**
May we attain | that | desire | O Agni | your | with protection | may we attain | wealth | O Lord of Wealth | with heroic sons |
May we attain | strength | [prefix] | desiring strength | may we attain | splendor | unaging | unaging | your ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, through your **protection** <note>original: utya</note>, which belongs to you, may we **attain** <note>original: ashyama</note> that **desire**. The commentator explains that very desire: O **Lord of Wealth** <note>original: rayivo</note>, O Agni, may we attain **wealth** <note>original: rayim</note> that is accompanied by **excellent sons** <note>original: suviram</note> and other descendants. Likewise, **desiring strength** <note>original: vajayanto; those wishing for food for themselves</note>, may we **attain the strength** <note>original: vajam; the food/sustenance</note> given by you. O **unaging one** <note>original: ajara; Agni who is free from decay</note>, may we attain your **unaging** and **radiant splendor** <note>original: dyumnam; shining fame and glory</note>.

-> ॥ Thus ends the seventh group in the fifth chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-

---

The sixth hymn <note>of this section; Sukta 7 of Mandala 6</note> beginning with "Toward the newest" consists of seven verses. Its seer <note>Rishi</note> is **Bharadvaja**, the meter is **Trishtubh**, and it is addressed to **Agni**. The application of this hymn in the **Morning Litany** <note>original: Prataranuvaka</note> and the **recitation for the Ashvin gods** <note>original: Ashvinashastra</note> has already been mentioned.

-> ॥ Therein, the first verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
<note>RV 6.7.1</note>
Toward the **newest** **Son of Strength**, seeking a **path** and **protection** through **sacrifice**, the worshiper **goes forward**.
To the one who **burns the forest**, whose **path is black**, who is **shining white**, the **divine Priest** of the sacrifice. ॥ 1 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Padapatha):**
[Prefix] | with newest | of strength | the son | toward | with sacrifice | path | protection | desiring |
one who burns the forest | one whose path is black | one who is shining white | with the sacrifice | the priest | divine | goes forth ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The worshiper, **desiring** <note>original: icchan</note> **protection** <note>original: avah; which can mean food or safety</note> and a **path** <note>original: gatum; a way to be approached or praised</note> from the **Son of Strength** <note>original: sahasas sunum; Agni is called the "Son of Strength" because he is generated by the vigorous friction of the fire-sticks</note>, and joined with a **newer sacrifice** <note>original: navyasa yajnena</note>, **goes forward** <note>original: pra jigati</note> directly **toward him** <note>original: achha</note>. What kind of Agni? He who **burns the forest** <note>original: vrshvadvnam; literally "forest-cutter," referring to Agni's power to consume and clear timber</note>, whose **path is black** <note>original: krishnayamam; the charred trail left behind by fire</note>, who is **shining white** <note>original: rushantam; the bright color of the flame</note>, and who is the **divine Priest** <note>original: hotaram; the one who calls the gods to the offering</note> existing in heaven.

# 593 || Rig Veda || [Book 4. Chapter 1. Hymn 6.]

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
<note>RV 6.6.2</note>
**He, the shining white one, the thundering one, abiding in the radiant realm, the most youthful, [comes] with the unaging and loudly-sounding [Maruts].**
**He who is the purifier, most abundant, Agni, follows after, consuming many broad [forests].** ॥ २ ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Padapatha):**
He | shining white | thundering | standing in the radiant realm | with the unaging | with the loudly-sounding | most youthful |
He who | purifier | most abundant | many | broad | Agni | follows | consuming ॥ २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
That **Agni** <note>the god of fire</note> is **shining white** <note>original: shvitanah; being of a white color</note>. He is the **thundering one** <note>original: tanyatuh; making sound</note> and **abides in the radiant realm**. The "radiant realm" <note>original: rochanam</note> refers to the atmosphere, as it is there that the planets, stars, and other celestial bodies shine. Existing there, he is joined by the **unaging** <note>original: ajarebhih; free from decay</note> and **loudly-sounding** <note>original: nanadadbhih; making a great noise</note> **Maruts** <note>storm deities</note>—or perhaps his own rays of light. He is the **most youthful** <note>original: yavishtho; most vigorous</note>. This **Agni**, who is the **purifier** <note>original: pavakah</note>, being **most abundant** <note>highly prevalent</note>, **follows after** and moves along **consuming** <note>original: bharvan; eating</note> **many** and **broad** <note>original: prithuni; thick</note> pieces of wood. The connection to the previous verse is that he exists in this specific manner.

<note>Ritual Note:</note> When the various sacrificial fires like the **Garhapatya** <note>term: Garhapatya; the domestic fire inherited by the householder</note> accidentally mix together, an offering <note>original: ishti</note> must be performed to **Agni the Separator** <note>original: Agni Vivichi</note>. For that ritual, the verse beginning with "Your [lights] move..." <note>verse 3 below</note> is used as the invitatory prayer <note>original: anuvakya</note>. (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 3. 13.)

---

-> ॥ This is the Third Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
<note>RV 6.6.3</note>
**Your pure lustres, O Agni, driven by the wind, travel everywhere, O Pure One.**
**The celestial, newly-moving ones, touching many [woods], consume the forests, breaking them down with bold power.** ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Padapatha):**
Away | your | in all directions | wind-driven | O Agni | lustres | O Pure One | pure | they travel |
touching many | celestial | newly-moving | forests | they consume | with bold power | breaking ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Pure One** <note>original: shuche; O clean or brilliant one</note>, O Agni, **your lustres** <note>original: bhamasah; lights/flames</note>, which are **pure** <note>stainless</note> and **driven by the wind**, **travel** and move **everywhere** in various directions. These rays, which are **celestial** <note>existing in the shining Agni</note> and **newly-moving** <note>original: navagva; moving with a fresh motion</note>, **touch many** <note>original: tuvimrakshaso</note> pieces of wood and **consume the forests**. This means they burn them. How do they do this? By **breaking** the forests down with **bold power** <note>original: dhrushata; with overwhelming brilliance</note>.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
<note>RV 6.6.4</note>
**Your bright, pure [rays], O Pure-rayed one, like loosened horses, scatter over the earth.**
**Then your wandering flame shines afar, spreading over the back of the dappled [earth]...**

<margin>VOL. III. 7 M</margin>

<vocab>
**Agni**: The deity of fire, central to Vedic ritual.
**Yavishtha**: "Youngest," a title for Agni because he is renewed every time the fire is lit.
**Pavaka**: "The Purifier," a common epithet for fire.
**Shvitana**: Shining white or bright.
**Tanyatu**: Thundering or making a loud roar, comparing fire's sound to a storm.
**Rochanastha**: Standing in the "Rochana," which usually refers to the luminous middle-space or heavens.
**Bhamas**: Radiant lights, flames, or manifestations of heat.
**Navagva**: A term often applied to a group of mythical ancestors, but here interpreted by the commentator as "newly-moving" rays.
**Garhapatya**: One of the three main ritual fires, maintained by the head of a household.
</vocab>

# 594 || Rig Veda || [Book 4. Chapter 5. Verse 8.]

## Hymn Text

**RV 4.4.4 (Word-for-word analysis)**
> Those | your | white | shining | O radiant one | the earth | shave | released | horses |
> then | whirling | your | broadly | shines | moving | upon | the ridge | of the variegated [earth] ॥ ४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **radiant one** <note>original: shuchishmah; possessed of brilliant light</note>, Agni, **those** white and **shining** rays of **yours** **shave** <note>original: vapanti; literally "to shear" or "to mow"</note> the **earth** <note>original: ksham</note>. This means they burn the plants and trees, which are like the hair of the earth. As another scripture states: **"Agni indeed shaves the hair of the earth"** <note>original Latin/Sanskrit reference: Rig Veda 1.65.4; अग्निह्रै दाति रोमा पृथिव्याः</note>. **Your** rays are like **released horses** <note>original: vishitaso ashvah</note> that gallop here and there. **Then**, at that time, **your** **whirling** <note>original: bhramah</note> mass of flames **shines** <note>original: vi bhati</note> **broadly** and intensely, **moving** <note>original: yatayamanah</note> its activity across the high **ridges** <note>original: sanu</note> of the **variegated** <note>original: prishneh; many-colored</note> earth or the mountain peaks.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**RV 4.4.5**
Now your tongue falls repeatedly, like the thunderbolt released by the warrior who fights for the cattle. Like the snare of a hero is the consuming heat of Agni; hard to resist and fearsome, he consumes the forests. ॥ ५ ॥

**RV 4.4.5 (Word-for-word analysis)**
Now | tongue | falls repeatedly | forth | of the vigorous | for the cattle-fighting [Indra] | like | thunderbolt | released |
of a hero-like | snare | consuming heat | of Agni | hard to resist | fearsome | consumes | the forests ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Now** also, the **tongue** <note>the flame</note> of the **vigorous** <note>original: vrishnah; the showerer of benefits</note> Agni **falls repeatedly** <note>original: papatiti</note>, meaning it moves forward again and again. An illustration is given: **like the thunderbolt released by the warrior who fights for the cattle**. This refers to Indra, who fights to recover the cows stolen by demons; Agni's flame is like the thunderbolt <note>original: ashanih; the vajra</note> cast by him. Furthermore, **like the snare** <note>original: prasitih; a binding net</note> **of a hero**, which is impossible for others to endure, the **consuming heat** <note>original: kshatih</note> of **Agni** is impossible to withstand. <note>Grammatical note: "Kshatih" is used here in the sense of a place where things are destroyed or burnt, namely the plants and trees.</note> Additionally, being **hard to resist** <note>original: durvartuh; difficult to stop</note> and **fearsome**, Agni **consumes** the **forests**. <note>The word "dayate" is used here specifically in the sense of burning.</note>

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**RV 4.4.6**
With your light, you have stretched across the earthly spaces with the boldness of a great driver. Drive away our fears with your powers; longing for the attackers, strike down the enemies. ॥ ६ ॥

**RV 4.4.6 (Word-for-word analysis)**
Across | with light | earthly | spaces | of the great | of the driver | with boldness | you have stretched |
He | drive away | off | fears | with powers | longing for the attackers | the enemies | down | strike ॥ ६ ॥

# 595 || Rig Veda || [Book 6. Chapter 1. Hymn 7.]

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, with your **radiance** <note>original: bhānu; light</note>, you have covered the places on earth that are to be reached <note>original: jayāṃsi; from the root 'ji', meaning places to be attained or traversed</note> along with your **daring rays** <note>original: dhṛṣatā raśminā; bold or overpowering beams</note>. You, being such, ward off those things that cause fear. Likewise, with your **overpowering forces** <note>original: sahobhiḥ; powers or splendors capable of defeating others</note>, destroy the **competitors** <note>original: spṛdhaḥ</note> and the **harmful enemies** <note>original: vanuṣaḥ; those who seek to injure</note>.

In the ritual of preparing the ceremonial pot <note>original: ukhā-saṃbharaṇīya-iṣṭi</note>, this verse beginning with **"He, the wonderful one..."** <note>original: sa citratayaiṣā</note> is used as the offering prayer <note>original: yājyā</note>. As it is stated in the ritual manuals: **"He who is bright, reminding us of what is bright... Agni rules over the great sovereign power."** <note>original Sanskrit: sa citra citraṃ citayantam-asme agnirīśe bṛhataḥ kṣatriyasya; Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.1</note>.

->॥ This is the Seventh Verse ॥<-

---

## Hymn Text

**RV 6.7.7**
O bright one, with bright and wonderful [acts], you make yourself known to us. O you of wonderful power, grant us that most wonderful wealth which bestows vigor, which is delightful, abundant in heroes, and great; O radiant one, join such wealth to the one who praises you with delightful songs. ॥ ७ ॥

### Word-for-Word Analysis (Pada-patha)
He | Bright one | Bright [wealth] | Making known | To us | O one of wonderful power | Most wonderful | Bestower of vigor |
Delightful | Wealth | Abounding in heroes | Great | Radiant one | With delightful [hymns] | To the praiser | Bestow/Join ॥ ७ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **bright one** <term>Chitra</term> <note>one who is worthy of being looked upon or admired</note>, O you of **wonderful power** <term>Chitrakshatra</term> <note>possessing extraordinary strength or wonderful wealth</note>, or O Agni who **gladdens** <note>original: chandra</note>, being such a person, grant wealth to us who praise you with gladdening hymns. <note>Note: There is a shift in grammatical number here from singular to plural</note>. Separate that wealth for us. What kind of wealth? **Bright** <note>admirable</note>, **making us known** <note>original: citayantam; wealth makes a man famous or recognized in society</note>, **most wonderful** <note>extraordinary</note>, **bestowing vigor** <term>Vayodha</term> <note>the giver of food or life-force</note>, **delightful** <note>original: chandram</note>, **full of heroes** <term>Puruvira</term> <note>accompanied by many sons, grandsons, and followers</note>, and **great** <note>vast</note>. The meaning is: "Please grant such wealth to us."

->॥ Thus ends the eighth section of the fifth chapter of the fourth book ॥<-

---

## Commentary (Introductory)

The seventh hymn, beginning with **"The Head..."** <note>original: mūrdhānam</note>, consists of seven verses and belongs to the seer **Bharadvaja**. Its deity is **Agni Vaishvanara**. The sixth and seventh verses are in the **Jagati** meter <note>12 syllables per line</note>, and the remaining five are in **Trishtubh** <note>11 syllables per line</note>. As the Index states: **"The hymn to Vaishvanara, 'The Head', ends with two Jagatis."** The ritual use of the hymn has been explained previously. In the Agnimaruta ritual of the Vishuvat day, the first three verses are an optional triplet for the chant. As noted: **"The Head of Heaven, the Charioteer of Earth... or The Head of Heaven, the Navel of Earth..."** <note>original Sanskrit: mūrdhānaṃ divo aratiṃ pṛthivyā mūrdhā divo nābhiragniḥ pṛthivyā; Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 8.6</note>.

->॥ This is the First Verse ॥<-

---

## Hymn Text

**RV 6.8.1**
The gods generated Agni—the head of heaven, the messenger of earth, the one common to all men <term>Vaishvanara</term>, born in the eternal law, the sage, the sovereign ruler, the guest of all people, and the vessel for our offerings. ॥ १ ॥

---

<vocab>
Chitra (चित्र) - Bright, wonderful, or worthy of being seen.
Chitrakshatra (चित्रक्षत्र) - Possessing wonderful dominion or extraordinary strength.
Vayodha (वयोधा) - One who bestows food, strength, or the span of life.
Puruvira (पुरुवीर) - Rich in followers or heroic sons/descendants.
Vaishvanara (वैश्वानर) - A name for Agni meaning "belonging to all men" or the universal fire.
Bharadvaja (भरद्वाज) - The traditional Vedic sage (Rishi) to whom this book is revealed.
</vocab>

596 || Rig Veda || [Book 4. Chapter 5. Varga 9.]

## Hymn Text (Word-for-Word Analysis)

The head | of heaven | the governor | of earth | the universal fire <note>original: vaiśvānara; the fire belonging to all men</note> | in the Truth <note>original: ṛte; referring to the cosmic order or the sacrifice</note> | toward | born | Agni | the wise | the sovereign | the guest | of the people | in the mouth | toward | the vessel <note>original: pātra; also meaning protector</note> | generated | the gods. ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**The head:** This means he who has become the head or the chief. **Of heaven:** Of the celestial world. **The governor of the earth:** He who is the traveler or mover upon the well-known earth. Alternatively, it means the Lord <note>original: svāmin</note> who is to be approached. **The universal fire:** He who relates to all men <note>original: viśveṣāṃ narāṇām</note>. **In the Truth:** "Truth" <note>original: ṛtam</note> is a name for either truth itself or the sacrifice. This word is in the locative case indicating the cause. **Born toward:** Produced at the beginning of creation for the sake of the sacrifice. **The wise:** One who sees beyond <note>original: krāntadarśin</note>. **The sovereign:** One who sacrifices perfectly. **The guest of the people:** The guest of the sacrificers, as he constantly goes to them to carry away the offerings <note>original: haviḥ</note>. Alternatively, he is to be honored like a guest. **In the mouth:** (The Sanskrit text uses a locative case here in place of an accusative). He has become the "mouth" of the gods, for the deities eat the offerings through the mouth that is characterized as Agni. **The vessel:** One who drinks or protects. Alternatively, one who holds the offerings with his mouth. The gods—meaning either the singers, the priests, or the deities themselves—**generated** such a universal Agni, endowed with these qualities. They produced him facing the sacrifice, bringing him forth from the two fire-sticks <note>original: araṇyoḥ; the wooden sticks used to churn fire</note>.

---

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**Samhita:**
The gods generated the universal fire, the center of sacrifices, the home of riches, the great reservoir of offerings; they praise him who is the charioteer of the rites and the banner of the sacrifice. ॥ २ ॥

**Word-for-Word Analysis:**
The navel/center | of sacrifices | the abode | of riches | the great | the reservoir | toward | together | they praise | the universal fire | the charioteer | of the rites | of the sacrifice | the banner/sign | generated | the gods. ॥ २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

He is the **navel of sacrifices**, meaning the binder or central point of rites like the *Jyotishtoma*. Likewise, he is the **abode of riches**, the single dwelling place where wealth resides. He is the **great reservoir** <note>original: āhāvam; a trough or place where things are called together</note>. It is called a reservoir because offerings are "called into" it. Alternatively, he is like a watering trough that holds the rain-water. The praisers **praise** <note>original: abhi saṃ navanta</note> such an Agni from all sides. Furthermore, the gods (priests or deities) **generate** the **universal fire**, who is the **charioteer of the rites**. Just as a charioteer leads his chariot, Agni is the leader or the one who causes the sacrifice to be grasped and conveyed to the gods. He is the **banner of the sacrifice**, the one who makes the ritual known. They produce him by the act of churning the fire-sticks.

---

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**Samhita:**
From you, O Agni, the inspired singers are born; from you come the heroes who overcome enemies. O universal fire, grant us riches that are desirable and sovereign, O King... ॥ ३ ॥

<term>Vaishvanara (Universal Fire): A form of Agni representing the fire that exists in all humans, or the sun in the sky and the digestive fire in the body.</term>
<term>Rita (Truth/Order): The cosmic law that governs the universe and the precise performance of rituals.</term>
<term>Ketu (Banner): A sign, signal, or manifestation that makes something known.</term>

## Hymn Text

<note>Rig Veda 6.7.3 — Word-for-Word Analysis</note>

From you | the sage | is born | the strong one | O Agni | from you | the heroes | the conquerors of enemies | Universal Fire | You | in us | place | riches | O King | desirable. ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni, possessor of strength** <note>original: vājī; meaning one who possesses sacrificial food</note>, a **sage** <note>original: vipraḥ; a wise or learned man</note> is **born** from you. That is to say, by giving offerings to you, a person becomes wise. Likewise, **heroes** <note>original: vīrāso</note> are born from you who are **conquerors of enemies** <note>original: abhimātiṣāhaḥ</note>, those who overpower their attackers. Because this is so, O **Universal Fire** <note>original: Vaiśvānara</note>, O **shining King** Agni, **place in us**, your devotees, **desirable** <note>original: spṛhayayyāṇi</note> **riches** <note>original: vasūni</note>. Bestow them upon us. ॥ ३ ॥

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fourth ॥ <-

All the gods, O Immortal One, praise you as you are born, like a newborn child; through your sacred powers they attained immortality, O Universal Fire, when you shone between the two parents. ॥ ४ ॥

<note>Word-for-Word Analysis</note>
Toward you | all | O Immortal | being born | a child | like | the gods | toward | together | praise | through your | sacred powers | immortality | they attained | O Universal Fire | when | of the parents | you shone. ॥ ४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Immortal** one <note>original: amṛta; Agni who is free from the nature of death</note>, **all the gods** <note>original: viśve devāḥ</note>—meaning the chanters and priests—**praise** you as you are **being born** from the friction-sticks, as if you were a **child** <note>original: śiśuṃ na</note> or a beloved son. Alternatively, "gods" may refer to the rays of light <note>original: raśmayaḥ</note>. They all gather toward you as you are born, just as parents go toward a son. Furthermore, O **Universal Fire**, **when** you **shone** between the two **parents** <note>original: pitroḥ; referring to the protectors, Heaven and Earth</note>, then the sacrificers **attained immortality** <note>original: amṛtatvam</note> or divinity through **your sacred powers** <note>original: kratubhiḥ</note>, which are the sacrificial acts such as the Jyotishtoma ritual. ॥ ४ ॥

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fifth ॥ <-

O Universal Fire, those great laws of yours, O Agni, no one has ever defied; when you were born in the lap of the parents, you found the banner of light among the paths of the days. ॥ ५ ॥

<note>Word-for-Word Analysis</note>
O Universal Fire | your | those | laws | great | O Agni | no one | [particle of emphasis] | has defied | when | being born | of the parents | in the lap | you found | the banner | among the paths | of the days. ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Universal Fire** <note>original: Vaiśvānara; he who relates to all men</note>, O Agni, **those** famous **laws** <note>original: vratāni; sacred works or ordinances</note> of yours are **great**. **No one** else **has defied** or obstructed them. **When** you were **being born** in the **lap of the parents** <note>original: pitrorupasthe; in the middle space or atmosphere between Heaven and Earth</note>, you found the **banner** <note>original: ketum; the sign or manifest light</note> among the **paths** <note>original: vayuneṣu</note> that must be traveled <unclear>...</unclear>

---

This Sukta is dedicated to Agni in his form as Vaiśvānara (the Universal Fire). The previous page likely discussed Agni's role in restoring light and establishing cosmic order.</meta>

Being born, you found the sun—the indicator of the days—which had been covered by <term>Svarbhānu</term> <note>A demonic figure in Vedic mythology responsible for eclipses; later associated with Rahu.</note>. By dispelling the demon who took the form of darkness with your own brilliance, you established the sun. At that time, those sacred laws <note>original: vratāni</note> were established... [this connects to the previous sentence].

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth ॥ <-

The peaks of heaven were fashioned by the light of the Universal Fire, by the banner of the immortal one. All beings have ascended upon his head like branches, as have the seven flowing streams. ॥ ६ ॥

**Word-for-Word Analysis**
Of the Universal Fire | fashioned | by the light | the peaks | of heaven | of the immortal | by the banner | of him | indeed | [filler] | all | beings | upon | the head | like branches | they ascended | seven | flowing streams. ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

By the light or brilliance of **the Universal Fire** <note>original: Vaiśvānara; Agni as the fire that belongs to all men</note>, who is the benefactor of all humanity, and by the **banner** <note>the indicator or sign</note> of the **immortal** water, the **peaks**—meaning the highly elevated places of **heaven** in the form of the stars—were **fashioned** or created.

Alternatively, the "peaks of heaven" refers to the elevated regions of the atmosphere where the clouds reside, which were fashioned by him. This is because clouds are considered a transformation of smoke <note>In Vedic thought, the smoke from sacrificial fires rises to form clouds and eventually rain.</note>. **Upon the head** of that same Universal Fire—meaning upon the smoke situated above him which has transformed into clouds—**all beings** (the pervasive waters) dwell.

Or, from another perspective, all living beings dwell upon the "head" or the highest region of the Supreme Brahman in the form of the Universal Fire. Likewise, the **seven** gliding **flowing streams**, such as the Ganges and other rivers, **ascended**—meaning they rise or manifest from this very Universal Fire. The intended meaning is that the entire world is produced from Agni through the mechanism of the sacrificial offering <note>The classic Vedic cycle: offerings into the fire reach the sun, the sun produces rain, rain produces food, and food produces living beings.</note>. ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Seventh ॥ <-

He of wise will, the Universal Fire, measured out the regions; the Seer measured out the bright spaces of heaven. He who has spread across all beings, the unbeguiled guardian, the protector of immortality. ॥ ७ ॥

**Word-for-Word Analysis**
Measured out | who | the regions | measured out | of wise will | the Universal Fire | [filler] | of heaven | the bright spaces | the Seer | around | who | all | beings | spread | unbeguiled | the guardian | of immortality | the protector. ॥ ७ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**The Universal Fire**, who is **of wise will** <note>original: sukratuḥ; one who performs good actions or possesses great wisdom</note> and is beneficial to all men, is the **one who measured out** the **regions**—meaning either the waters or the various worlds. Likewise, that Agni, being a **Seer** <note>original: kaviḥ; one who sees beyond the surface, a visionary</note> who perceives that which is beyond the senses, measured out the **bright spaces** belonging to **heaven**, such as the stars and other celestial lights. Furthermore, he has **spread across** all **beings**—referring to all created things or the pervasive waters...

<vocab>
- <term>Vaiśvānara</term> (Universal Fire): A cosmic form of Agni representing the fire found in all humans, the sun, and the digestive hearth.
- <term>Sukratu</term> (Wise Will): A term implying both high intelligence and the effective power to perform sacred rites.
- <term>Sānu</term> (Peak/Surface): Used here to describe the "heights" of the sky or the atmospheric layers.
- <term>Visruh</term> (Flowing Streams): Can refer to rivers, or metaphorically to plants growing like branches.
- <term>Kavi</term> (Seer): A poet-prophet; someone with divine insight into the cosmic order.
- <term>Amṛta</term> (Immortality/Nectar): Often refers to the divine drink (Soma) or water, which sustains eternal life.
- <term>Rajāṃsi</term> (Regions): The various layers of the universe (earth, atmosphere, and heaven).
</vocab>

He is depicted as the wise guardian of immortality who spans across all three worlds (earth, atmosphere, and heaven).</summary>

...expanded [the light] in all directions. He, the un-deceived and un-injured guardian, remains as the protector of all and the preserver of the water—which is the cause of immortality.

-> ॥ Thus ends the ninth group (varga) of the fifth chapter in the fourth book (ashtaka). ॥ <-

---

The eighth hymn, beginning with the words "Of the nourishing" (*Pṛkṣasya*), consists of seven verses composed by the seer **Bharadvāja**. Its deity is **Vaiśvānara Agni** <note>Agni as the 'Universal Fire' or 'Fire of All Men'.</note>. The first six verses are in the **Jagati** meter <note>A Vedic meter with 12 syllables per line.</note>, and the seventh is in the **Trishtubh** meter <note>A Vedic meter with 11 syllables per line.</note>. This is confirmed by the Index (*Anukramaṇī*), which states: "Of the nourishing... the last is Triṣṭubh."

In the ritual of the twenty-fourth day, this hymn is used as the foundational text for the Vaiśvānara litany within the *Āgnimāruta* offering. This is indicated in the *Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* (7.4): "Of the nourishing, the showerer, for the showering host." It is also used on the fifth day of the *Pṛṣṭhya* and *Abhilava* six-day sacrifices. Furthermore, the first two triplets (trichas) of this hymn serve as the *Stotriya* and *Anurūpa* <note>Technical terms for specific types of chants used in the Vedic liturgy.</note> during the *Viṣuvat* (equinox) day.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here follows the first verse ॥ <-
I proclaim now the power of the nourishing, showering, ruddy Knower of all Beings (*Jātavedas*) in the assembly. For the Universal Fire (*Vaiśvānara*), a praise that is newer, pure, and beautiful flows forth—just as the Soma juice is purified. ॥ १ ॥

**Word-for-word Breakdown (Pada-pāṭha):**
Of the nourishing | of the showerer | of the ruddy | now | the power | [prefix] | now | I spoke | in the assembly | of the Knower of all Beings.
For the Universal Fire | the prayer | newer | pure | like Soma | flows | beautiful | for Agni. ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Of the nourishing** (*pṛkṣasya*): Meaning pervasive or associated with, or alternatively, one who possesses sacrificial food (*havis*). **Of the showerer** (*vṛṣṇo*): One who pours down blessings. **Of the ruddy** (*aruṣasya*): One who is shining. **Of the Knower of all Beings** (*jātavedaso*): The one who knows all created things, namely Vaiśvānara Agni. I proclaim—meaning I speak or praise excellently—his **power** (*sahaḥ*), which is capable of overcoming enemies, quickly in the **assembly** (*vidatha*) or sacrifice.

A **prayer** (*matiḥ*)—a hymn to be meditated upon—which is **newer** (*navyasi*) or more recent, **pure** (*śuciḥ*)—either stainless or a purifier of the chanters—and **beautiful** (*cāruḥ*), **flows** (*pavate*) toward this Universal Fire, Agni. It flows from me; it emerges of its own accord. **Like Soma**: just as the Soma juice flows through the woollen filter, so does this prayer.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-
Being born in the highest heaven, Agni, the guardian of sacred laws, protected those laws. The wise one measured the atmosphere; the Universal Fire touched the sky with his greatness. ॥ २ ॥

## Hymn Text

-> **(Rig Veda 4.5.2 - Word-by-Word Analysis)** <-

He. Being born. In the highest. In the sky. Vows. Agni. Protector of vows. He protected. The atmosphere. He measured out. Of good intent. The Universal Fire (*Vaiśvānara*). By greatness. The firmament. He touched. ॥ २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

That Universal Fire (*Vaiśvānara*) Agni is the protector of vows <term>vratapa: one who guards sacred rites</term>. Being born in the highest sky <note>original: *vyomani*</note>—appearing in the form of the Sun—he has protected the "vows," meaning both worldly duties and Vedic rituals. He also measured out the atmosphere; that is, he created the three worlds represented by it. Similarly, the wise-acting Universal Fire, through his own greatness and brilliance, touched the firmament <note>original: *nākam*</note>, the realm of heaven.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here follows the third verse ॥ <-

The wonderful Friend propped up heaven and earth; he drove the darkness deep within with his light. Like two skins, he spread out the two supporting worlds; the Universal Fire held all virile power. ॥ ३ ॥

-> **(Word-by-Word Analysis)** <-

Propped up. Heaven and earth. Friend. Wonderful. Vanishing within. He made. With light. Darkness. Like. Two skins. The two supporters. He caused to spread. The Universal Fire. Everything. He held. Virile power. ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Being a friend <note>original: *mitra*</note> to all, or being a great and marvelous <note>original: *adbhuta*</note> being, the Universal Fire (*Vaiśvānara*) Agni propped up heaven and earth <note>original: *rodasī*</note>. He specifically supported them so they would not fall, establishing them in their proper places. Furthermore, with his brilliance, he made the darkness vanish <note>original: *antarvavat*</note>. <note>The commentator notes that 'vavat' is a grammatical form derived from a root meaning movement, indicating the dispersal of shadows.</note> Moreover, he spread out the two supporting worlds, heaven and earth, like two skins—just as a dresser of animal hides spreads out two skins to dry them. He made them wide and expansive. In short, this Universal Fire holds or maintains all virile power <note>original: *vṛṣṇyam*</note> and strength throughout the universe.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here follows the fourth verse ॥ <-

In the lap of the waters, the mighty ones seized him; the tribes stood near the king who is worthy of praise. Matariśvan brought Agni, the Universal Fire, from Vivasvat, from the far distance. ॥ ४ ॥

-> **(Word-by-Word Analysis)** <-

Of the waters. In the lap. The mighty ones. They seized. The tribes. The king. Near. They stood. Worthy of praise. Matariśvan. Brought. Agni. From Vivasvat <note>A solar deity or the first sacrificer</note>. The Universal Fire. From the far distance. ॥ ४ ॥

<vocab>
**Universal Fire** (*Vaiśvānara*) - An epithet of Agni representing fire as a cosmic force common to all humanity.
**Heaven and Earth** (*Rodasī*) - The dual world-halves.
**Sky/Space** (*Vyoman*) - The highest ethereal realm where the sun resides.
**Protector of vows** (*Vratapā*) - A title for Agni as the guardian of the integrity of rituals and natural laws.
**The Two Supporters** (*Dhiṣaṇe*) - A poetic term for heaven and earth, often envisioned as two bowls or supporting structures.
**Matariśvan** - A divine messenger or wind-deity who, like Prometheus, is credited with bringing fire from the heavens to mankind.
**Virile power** (*Vṛṣṇyam*) - Potent, masculine strength or the generative power of the bull.
</vocab>

### म० ६. अ० १. सू० ८.] ॥ Fourth Book ॥ ६०१

## Commentary (Sayana)
[Conclusion of commentary for Verse 4]

The word "Waters" <note>original: *āpaḥ*</note> is a name for the atmosphere. In the lap <note>original: *upasthe*</note>—meaning in the middle—of the waters or the atmosphere, the Mighty Ones—"Mighty" is the meaning of this word—the great Maruts <term>Maruts: storm deities who accompany Indra</term> seized him. This means they recognized this Universal Fire <note>original: *vaiśvānara*</note> as he existed in the form of lightning. Having taken hold of him, the subjects or the people <note>original: *viśaḥ*</note> stood near the King, their master, who is worthy of praise <note>original: *ṛgmiyam*</note>. That is, they praised him. Furthermore, Matariśvan <term>Matariśvan: a messenger of the gods, often identified with the Wind</term>, the swift messenger of the gods or the Wind itself, brought this Universal Fire, Agni, from a great distance—from the Sun-god Vivasvat—near whom he was previously located. He brought him back to this world.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
In every age, O Agni, bestow upon us who chant the newest praise, worthy of the assembly, wealth and glorious progeny. O King, O undecaying one, like a path-clearing bolt, cut down with your brilliance the speaker of evil, as one cuts down a tree. ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-by-Word Analysis:**
In every age. Worthy of the assembly. To those who chant. O Agni. Wealth. Glorious. Bestow. Newest. Like a path-clearing [bolt]. O King. The speaker of evil. O undecaying one. Downwards. Down. Cut. A tree. Like. With brilliance. ॥ ५ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, in every age <note>original: *yuge yuge*</note>—meaning time after time—bestow wealth and a glorious son upon us who utter the newest or freshest praise directed toward you, who are worthy of the assembly <note>original: *vidathyam*</note>. The assembly here refers to the sacrifice; thus, you are worthy of the sacrifice. Grant this to us. Furthermore, O King—radiant and undecaying Agni—with your own brilliance, which acts like a thunderbolt <note>original: *pathyeva*</note>, cut down the enemy who speaks evil or intends misfortune <note>original: *agha-śaṃsam*</note>. Cut him down so that he is brought low, just as one fells a tree.

---

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O Agni, maintain among us and our wealthy patrons an unbending power, undecaying and full of heroic might. May we, O Universal Fire, win through your protections food and strength in the hundreds and thousands, O Agni. ॥ ६ ॥

**Word-by-Word Analysis:**
Our. O Agni. Among the wealthy patrons. Maintain. Unbending. Power. Undecaying. Full of heroic might. We. May win. Consisting of hundreds. Consisting of thousands. O Universal Fire. Food/Strength. O Agni. With your protections. ॥ ६ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, in us—the word "our" is used here in the sense of "among us"—who are wealthy patrons <note>original: *maghavatsu*</note> because we possess wealth in the form of sacrificial offerings, establish power or wealth. What kind of power? It should be unbending <note>original: *anāmi*</note>—meaning it cannot be bowed or snatched away—undecaying or imperishable, and endowed with excellent heroic strength <note>original: *suvīryam*</note>. Furthermore, O Universal Fire <note>original: *vaiśvānara*</note>, through your protections, may we obtain food or strength <note>original: *vājam*</note> that is numbered in the hundreds and thousands, or perhaps consisting of hundreds and thousands of men.

---

<vocab>
Agni: The Fire-god, central to Vedic ritual.
Vaiśvānara: The "Universal Fire" or "Fire common to all men."
Marut: Storm deities, sons of Rudra.
Matariśvan: The divine being or wind that brought fire to humanity.
Yuge-yuge: From age to age; perpetually.
Maghavat: The "generous one," referring to the patron who pays for the sacrifice.
Vidathya: Worthy of the *vidatha*, a communal gathering for religious or social purposes.
Rayi: Wealth, often including cattle and progeny.
Kṣatra: Temporal power, dominion, or the wealth that supports it.
Suvīrya: Heroic might or a lineage of brave sons.
</vocab>

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Worshipped One <note>original: *iṣṭe* — one who is to be worshipped or is desirable</note>, O Dweller of the three regions <note>original: *triṣadhastha* — one who resides together in the three worlds, or one who stays in the three ritual sacrificial fires like the Āhavanīya with the gods to be worshipped</note>, O Agni! Guard them. The ninth hymn, beginning with "The day and...", consists of seven verses. It was seen by the seer Bharadvāja <term>Bharadvāja: a famous Vedic sage and the primary seer of the sixth book of the Rig Veda</term> and is dedicated to the Universal Fire (Vaiśvānara). It is noted in the ritual index <note>original: *Anukramaṇī*</note>: "The day and..." In the ritual of the "Shifted Ten-Nights" <term>Vyūḷha Daśarātra: a specific ten-day Soma sacrifice</term>, on the sixth day, during the litany to Agni and the Maruts, this hymn is used for the recitation to the Universal Fire. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "The day is black, the name of the honey/mead..." <note>Aśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 8. 8.</note>

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Within this hymn, the First Verse ॥ <-
The black day and the bright day revolve through the two regions by known paths. Like a king being born, Agni, the Universal Fire, has overcome the darknesses with his light. ॥ १ ॥
---
**Word-by-Word Analysis:**
The day. And. Black. The day. Bright. And. Revolve. The two regions. By known [paths]. The Universal Fire. Being born. Like. A king. Down. Overcame. With light. Agni. The darknesses. ॥ १ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
A "Day" <note>original: *ahas*</note> is so called because a man brings or performs his works within it. The "black" <note>original: *kṛṣṇam*</note> day—because it is grouped with the word for day—refers here to the Night, which is black in color due to darkness. The "bright" <note>original: *arjunam*</note> day is the white-colored day of sunlight. These two regions <note>original: *rajasī*</note>—coloring the whole world with their respective brilliance—revolve or turn around repeatedly <note>original: *vi vartete*</note> by paths that are "to be known" <note>original: *vedyābhiḥ* — known or understood as favorable movements</note>. Alternatively, "two regions" refers to the Heaven and Earth, which represent the three worlds by implication; they revolve by the command of the Universal Fire. For He is the deity being described here. And that Agni, the Universal Fire, being born—

<page-num>603</page-num>
<header>Mandala 6. Sukta 9. Verse 2.] ॥ Fourth Book (Ashtaka) ॥ 603</header>

## Hymn Text

Like a king appearing, he grows great; like a king with light and splendor, he strikes down the darkness.
The word *avatirati* <note>original: "अ॒व॒ति॒रति॑"</note> is an action of destruction. It means "he destroys" or "he vanishes [the darkness]."

->॥ Now the Second Verse ॥<-

I do not know the warp <term>tantu: the longitudinal threads in a loom</term>, nor do I know the woof <term>otu: the crosswise threads in a loom</term>, nor that [cloth] which they weave, striving together in the assembly. Whose son here shall speak the words that must be said, [even if] he were told by the higher one [the Sun] or the lower father [Agni]? ॥ २ ॥

---

I. Do not. I. Warp. Not. Distinctly. I know. Woof. Not. Which. They weave. Together-striving. Moving/Exerting.
Of whose. Indeed. Son. Here. Words to be spoken. Higher. He says. By the lower. By the father. ॥ २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Wishing to describe the greatness of the Universal Fire <term>Vaiśvānara</term>, the Seer <note>the Ṛṣi Bharadvāja</note> represents the sacrifice in the form of a cloth. The performers of the sacrifice <note>the Yajnikas</note> believe this verse expresses how difficult the sacrifice is to fully understand. 

**The warp** <note>original: *tantuṃ*</note>: These are the long threads of a cloth. In the "cloth" of the sacrifice, these are the meters like the Gāyatrī and the various hymns of praise. I do not fully know these. 
Similarly, **the woof** <note>original: *otuṃ*</note>: These are the threads that run crosswise. In this context, they are the Yajus formulas and the ritual actions performed by the Adhvaryu priest. These also I do not know. 
Furthermore, I do not know that finished cloth characterized as the sacrifice, which is achieved by both of these. **Which** cloth of the sacrifice, **in the assembly** <note>original: *samare* — the gathering place for the gods' sacrifice</note>, the priests **striving** <note>original: *atamānāḥ* — constantly exerting themselves</note> **weave** <note>original: *vayanti*</note>, meaning they stretch out the warp and woof to complete the sacrifice in the form of a garment. 

In this world, **whose son** <note>the word *svit* is used to express a doubt or a deep question</note>—meaning what human—**shall speak** the things that ought to be said? Even if he were **instructed by the father**, the Universal Fire <note>Agni</note> who exists **below** in this world, or by the **higher** one, the Sun who exists in that world above. The meaning is that no one is truly capable of explaining it fully. This is also stated by those who know the tradition:

> This Sun who stands above in heaven is the son of the Universal Fire. 
> The meters are the warp-threads of the sacrifice-garment.
> The Yajus formulas and rituals are the woof-threads; the sacrifice itself is the cloth to be woven.
> The Sun is the father situated high above, and Agni is considered the father on earth.

Those who know the Self <note>the Vedantins or philosophers</note> believe this verse expresses how difficult it is to understand the Creator of the world through this metaphor. 

**The warp**: I do not know the warp-like subtle elements <note>original: *tan-mātras*</note> such as space <note>Akasha</note> which are not yet combined <note>original: *apañcīkṛtāni* — refers to the five elements before they mix to form solid matter</note>. 
**The woof**: I do not know the gross elements like space which, having been combined <note>original: *pañcīkṛtāni*</note>, act as the cross-threads. 
Nor do I know the finished "cloth," which is the expanded universe <note>original: *prapañca*</note>, which worldly beings **weave** (produce) by constantly striving in the **assembly** (the meeting of warp and woof elements). It is said they "weave" it because the Lord creates the world for their enjoyment. In this matter, the things to be spoken of, which exist beyond the reach of the intellect... <note>Text continues to next page</note>

<vocab>
तन्तु (tantu): warp threads (symbolizing Rig/Sama verses or subtle elements)
ओतु (otu): woof/weft threads (symbolizing Yajus rituals or gross elements)
वैश्वानर (Vaishvanara): Agni as the cosmic fire or "Fire of all men"
यज्ञ (yajna): sacrifice/ritual
समरे (samare): place of meeting (the sacrificial ground or the point of creation)
अतमानाः (atamānāḥ): performing/exerting oneself
ऋत्विज (ritvij): priest
</vocab>

<page-num>604</page-num>
<header>॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Book 4. Chapter 5. Group 11.]</header>

## Commentary (Sayana) - Continued from previous page
Whose son indeed can speak <note>original: *vadāti*</note> these matters that are to be spoken, even if he were instructed by a lower, more recent father who was born in this mortal time? The sense is that no one, being ignorant of the events that occurred before their own birth, could possibly speak of them.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

He indeed knows the warp, He knows the woof; He speaks the words that must be said in due season. He who knows this is the protector of immortality; moving below, yet seeing from beyond through another [form]. ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown**
He | indeed | the warp | He | [distinctly] | knows | the woof | He | words to be spoken | seasonably | speaks |
Who | these [things] | knows | of immortality | the protector | below | moving | beyond | through another | seeing ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Although these matters are difficult to understand in the manner described, the **Universal Fire** <term>Vaishvanara-Agni</term> **knows** them and speaks them, expressing them through his consciousness. **He indeed** <note>original: *sa it*</note>, that very Universal Fire, **distinctly knows the warp** <term>tantu: the longitudinal threads of a loom</term>, which represents the meters such as the Gayatri and the hymns of praise. Likewise, He alone **knows the woof** <term>otu: the crosswise threads</term>, representing the Yajus-mantras and the ritual actions of the Adhvaryu priest. **Seasonably** <note>original: *ṛtutha*</note>, meaning at the proper time for each specific ritual performance, **He speaks** <note>original: *vadāti*</note> those words that are to be spoken. **He** who thus **knows these** <note>original: *īṃ ciketat*</note> things is the **protector of immortality** <note>original: *amṛtasya gopā*</note>, meaning the guardian of the waters <note>In Vedic Sanskrit, *amrita* often refers to the life-giving waters or rain</note>. **Moving below** <note>original: *avaścaran*</note> in the lower world, moving about in the form of the earthly fire, and **seeing from beyond** <note>original: *paraḥ... paśyan*</note> through his celestial form as the Sun, He illuminates the entire world and knows all beings; this connects to the previous statement.

Alternatively <note>Sayana now provides a philosophical/Vedantic interpretation</note>, **He indeed** knows the **warp**, meaning the subtle elements <term>tanmatras</term>, and no one else. Likewise, He alone knows the **woof**, meaning the gross elements. He alone **speaks** those **words to be spoken** or teachings **seasonably**, meaning at the various times when the tradition of knowledge is interrupted. Who is this who knows and speaks? The text says: He who is the **Universal Man** <term>Vaishvanara</term>, the Supreme Self, the **protector of immortality** <note>original: *amṛtasya gopā*</note>, meaning the protector of liberation. **Moving below** in the state of worldly existence <term>samsara</term>, He moves about as the individual soul <term>Jivatma</term> endowed with an internal organ (mind); yet **seeing from beyond** through **another** <note>original: *anyena*</note> form—the unconditioned form characterized by Being, Consciousness, and Bliss <term>Sat-Chit-Ananda</term> which is distinct from the previously mentioned individual soul—He illuminates the entire world and **knows these** things. Regarding this Supreme Self, the scripture says:
> When He shines, everything shines after Him; by His light, all this is illuminated. <note>original: *tamevabhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhātīti* — A famous quote from the Mundaka and Katha Upanishads</note>

<vocab>Vaishvanara (Universal Fire/Self), Agni (Fire), Tantu (warp/subtle elements), Otu (woof/gross elements), Amrita (immortality/water/liberation), Gopa (protector), Ritutha (seasonably/in due time)</vocab>

<summary>This page interprets Rig Veda 6.9.3, presenting Agni-Vaishvanara as the divine "weaver" who understands the complex structure of both the sacrifice (ritual level) and the universe itself (philosophical level).</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Vaishvanara, weaving metaphor, warp and woof, ritual vs. philosophy, Supreme Self, Jivatma, Paramatma, Upanishadic quote</keywords>

<header>Mandala 6. Hymn 1. Sukta 9.] || Fourth Book || 605</header>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

This one is the first Invoker <note>original: *hota*</note>; behold Him! This immortal light is within mortals. He, the firm one, is born and seated [at the sacrifice]; He is the immortal one, growing through His [human] body. ॥ ४ ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
This | Invoker | first | behold | this | this | light | immortal | among mortals |
This | He | was born | firm | [all around] | seated | immortal | through the body | growing ॥ ४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

This **Universal Fire** <term>Vaishvanara-Agni: the fire that exists in all things</term> is the **first**—the original—**Invoker**. The human invoker is merely secondary. O humans, **behold Him**, which means you should worship Him. The meaning is that **this light**, called the Universal Fire, exists **among mortals**—within bodies that are subject to death—in the form of the **digestive fire** <note>original: *jatharagni*</note>, which is itself **immortal** and free from death. Furthermore, this Fire is **firm**, meaning unshakeable, and is **seated** or established everywhere, being all-pervasive. For this reason, even though He is **immortal** and free from death, He is said to be **born** <note>original: *jajne*</note> because of His connection to a physical **body**, and He is figuratively described as **growing**.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

A firm light is established for the sake of seeing; the mind is the swiftest of all things that fly. All the gods, of one mind and one purpose, move rightly toward that one single Will. ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
firm | light | established | for seeing | [for the sake of] | mind | swiftest | among things that fly | within |
all | gods | of one mind | of one purpose | one | Will | toward | [variously] | move | rightly ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The light called the **Universal Fire** <term>Vaishvanara</term> is **firm** (unchanging) and is **established within** all moving living beings. It is swifter even than the **mind**, which is the **swiftest** of all things. It was **established** there by the **Creator** <term>Prajapati: the Lord of Progeny</term>. For what purpose? **For the sake of seeing**—that is, for the purpose of perception or knowledge. Furthermore, **all the gods** are **of one mind** and **one purpose** (meaning they possess equal wisdom); they **move rightly toward** and serve the **one** primary **Will** <term>kratu: often meaning a ritual act or the intelligence behind it</term>, the performer of all actions.

Alternatively, the meaning is that within all moving living beings, in the center of the heart, there is a **firm**, unchanging, and unwavering **light** which is **swifter than the mind**. This is the **Light of Brahman-Consciousness** <note>original: *brahma-chaitanya*</note>. It is not "established" by anyone else, for the scripture says, "He who knows that which is hidden in the secret cave [of the heart] in the highest ether." For what purpose? For the sake of seeing; for it is through this light of knowledge that all beings know. Furthermore, the **gods** <note>original: *deva*</note> here refer to the **senses**, as they are "shining" or illuminating powers. **All the gods**, meaning all the sense organs such as the eyes and others, act **with the mind** and possess the same illumination...

<summary>This page contains verses 4 and 5 of Rig Veda 6.9, where Agni is described as the immortal light within mortals and the swift consciousness that directs both the senses and the universe.</summary>
<keywords>Vaishvanara, Agni, Light, Immortality, Mind, Prajapati, Brahman-consciousness, Senses, Rig Veda commentary</keywords>

<page-num>६०६</page-num>
<header>॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Book 4, Adhyaya 5, Varga 11]</header>

...they go toward the One, the one without a second, the performer of the acts of creation and such, the Supreme Self <note>original: *paramatman*</note> who is the soul of all men, correctly and well. They go in various ways. Indeed, the gods themselves approach Him. They approach from all sides in various ways. This means they worship Him. As it is heard in scripture: "That which the gods worship as the light of lights, as life, and as immortality." <note>This quote is from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 4.4.16.</note>

---

->॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

My ears fly apart; my eyes fly apart; and this light, which is placed in my heart, also flies apart. My mind, with its thoughts fixed on the distant, wanders. What indeed shall I say? What, indeed, shall I now think? ॥ ६ ॥

**Padapatha:**
Apart । my । ears । fly । apart । eye । apart । this । light । in the heart । placed । which ।
Apart । my । mind । wanders । thoughts-fixed-on-the-distant । what । indeed । shall I say । what । indeed । now । shall I think ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Desiring to hear the **Universal Fire** <term>Vaishvanara: Agni as the cosmic fire that dwells in all people</term>, my **ears fly apart**—they move in various directions—because the qualities of His that must be heard are many. Likewise, my organ of **sight**, desiring to see the Universal Fire, **flies apart**. It moves in various directions because the forms of His that must be seen are many. So too, the **light** that illuminates, which is **placed** or deposited in the **heart**—specifically the lotus of the heart—which is the principle known as the **intellect** <note>original: *buddhi*</note>, also **flies apart**. It moves in various ways in order to know the nature of the Universal Fire. 

Furthermore, he is one **whose thoughts are fixed on the distant** <term>duradhih</term>; that is, one whose contemplation <note>original: *adhyana*</note> is on distant or remote objects. <note>The commentator notes a Vedic grammatical variation (Chandasa) regarding the gender of the word here.</note> My **mind wanders**; it proceeds in various directions. Thus, with all my senses racing against one another as if in a competition, what indeed shall I **say** is the form of the Universal Fire? What indeed shall I **think** or understand with my mind? The meaning is: because the qualities of the Universal Fire are infinite, they cannot be known by someone like me who has dull intellect.

---

->॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

All the gods, being afraid, bowed to You, O Agni, when You stood in the darkness. May the Universal Fire protect us for our welfare; may the Immortal One protect us for our welfare. ॥ ७ ॥

**Padapatha:**
All । gods । bowed । being afraid । You । O Agni । in darkness । standing ।
Universal Fire । may He protect । for welfare । us । immortal । may He protect । for welfare । us ॥ ७ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Universal Fire, all the gods **bowed** to You as You **stood** in the **darkness**—the blinding gloom. Why did they do so? Because they were **afraid**; they feared the darkness. Such an **immortal** one...

<summary>The Rishi Bharadvaja describes a mystical experience where his senses and mind are overwhelmed by the infinite qualities of Agni Vaishvanara. The page concludes by describing how even the gods sought Agni's light out of fear of the darkness.</summary>

<page-num>607</page-num>
<header>Mandala 6. Sukta 10. Verse 1.] || Fourth Book || 607</header>

May the deathless Universal Fire <term>Vaishvanara: Agni as the fire that dwells in all beings</term> protect us with his protection for our well-being. May he protect us. The repetition is for the sake of emphasis <note>original: *adarartha*</note>.

->॥ Thus ends the eleventh section of the fifth chapter of the fourth book ॥<-

The tenth hymn, beginning with "Before you" <note>original: *puro vah*</note>, consists of seven verses and is seen by the sage Bharadvaja and addressed to the Fire-god, Agni. The seventh verse consists of twenty syllables and is in the "Two-footed Viraj" <note>original: *dvipada virat*</note> meter; the remaining verses are in the "Trishtubh" <note>original: *trishtup*</note> meter. Thus it is recorded in the Index: "Before you, ending with the two-footed." In the morning litany <term>Prataranuvaka: A series of recitations performed before sunrise in certain Vedic rituals</term>, during the fire-offering ritual, these four hymns starting with this one are used for the Trishtubh meter section. It is indicated in the ritual manuals: "The four hymns beginning with 'Before you the delightful' and the six starting with 'Him of the beautiful appearance'." (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.13).

->॥ Here is the first verse ॥<-
## Hymn Text
Place the delightful, divine Agni, who is well-purified, before you at the proceeding sacrifice, at the un-injured rite. With many hymns [place him], for he, the radiant Knower of All Beings <term>Jatavedas: A title for Agni meaning the one who knows all created things</term>, makes our sacrifices successful. ॥ १ ॥

**Pada-patha:**
Before । you । delightful । divine । well-purified । proceeding । sacrifice । Agni । un-injured-rite । place-ye ।
Many । with-hymns । he । for । our । radiant । well-performed-sacrifices । makes । Knower-of-All-Beings ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O priests and sacrificers, you should place before you <note>original: *puro dadhidhvam*</note>—that is, establish in the front as the sacred offering-fire <term>Ahavaniya: The primary fire used for pouring oblations</term>—this Agni who is delightful <note>causing joy or worthy of praise</note>, divine <note>born in heaven</note>, and well-purified <note>either completely free from faults or easily approached</note>. Place him at this sacrifice <note>yajna</note> or un-injured rite <note>adhvara: a ritual free from violence or the interference of demons</note> which is now proceeding. Alternatively, "place him before you" means to appoint him as your lead priest <note>purodhasam</note>. Also, place him before you with many hymns and songs of praise. Since he, the radiant Knower of All Beings <note>Jatavedas: the one who knows all that are born</note>, makes our sacrifices successful <note>well-performed</note>, the sage urges the listeners to establish him in the front.

---

->॥ Now the second verse ॥<-
## Hymn Text
O radiant one of many faces, O invoker, O Agni, kindled by humans along with your other fires—to him [the priests'] thoughts purify a hymn of power, like Mamata, as clear as clarified butter. ॥ २ ॥

**Pada-patha:**
Him । indeed । radiant । many-faced । invoker । Agni । fires-with । human । kindled ।
Hymn । which । for-him । like-Mamata । power । clarified-butter । like । pure । thoughts । purify ॥ २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O radiant one <note>shining</note>, O one of many faces <note>possessing many flames</note>, O invoker <note>the caller of the gods</note>, O Agni, being kindled and made bright by humans along with your other fires which are parts of yourself...

<page-num>६०८</page-num>
<header>॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Book 4. Chapter 5. Section 12.]</header>

...the praisers, that hymn should be pure—this is the remaining sense. The word "u" is used to fill the meter <note>original: *padapuranam*</note>. Which hymn? A song of praise that is pleasing and purified like clarified butter <term>Ghrita: Purified butter used in Vedic rituals</term> is cleansed by two strainers—pure and clean. For this Agni, the thinkers—the praisers—act like Mamata. Mamata was a woman who spoke of the Divine <term>Brahmavadini: A female scholar or seer of Vedic wisdom</term> and the mother of the sage Dirghatamas. Just as she purifies, they also purify and refine the hymn, pronouncing it free from any faults. This is the grammatical connection of "that hymn."

-> ॥ Now the third verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

That mortal thrives with fame among men, the wise one who serves Agni with hymns. Agni of varied radiance, with wondrous protections, establishes him in the gain of a cattle-filled enclosure. ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
Thrives; he; with fame; among mortals; who; to Agni; gave/served; the wise; with hymns; with wondrous; protections; of varied radiance; of the enclosure; in the gain; cattle-filled; establishes. ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

That sacrificer thrives among **mortals** (human beings) with **fame** <note>Sayana glosses *shravasa* as "with food"</note>. The **wise** or intelligent sacrificer **who** **serves** or provides oblations along with **hymns** of praise—to that sacrificer, Agni, who possesses **varied radiance**, **establishes** him in the **attainment** or possession of a **cowshed** (enclosure) filled with **cattle**, through his **wondrous** or amazing **protections**.

---

-> ॥ Now the fourth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

He who, being born, filled the two wide worlds with far-reaching light, he of the black path. Then, the Purifier was seen piercing even the thick darkness of the night with his brilliance. ॥ ४ ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
Filled; who; being born; the two wide ones; with far-seen; light; black-pathed; then; thick; even; darkness; of the night; piercing; with brilliance; was seen; the Purifier. ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

The one whose **path is black** <note>original: *krishnadhva*—this refers to the trail of smoke left by fire</note>, namely Agni, as he **is born** or becomes manifest, **fills** the **two wide** worlds (heaven and earth) with his **light** that is **seen from afar**. After **then**, that **Purifier** (Agni) is **seen** casting aside or piercing the **thick darkness** belonging to the **night** <note>original: *urmyayah*—a Vedic term for night</note> with his **brilliance**.

---

-> ॥ Now the fifth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

O Agni, now grant stable wealth and protection to our patrons, those who, through their generosity and fame, and through their heroic power, surpass other men. ॥ ५ ॥

## Hymn Text
(Verse 5 Word-for-word breakdown conclusion)
Now. To us. Wonderful. With many strengths/foods. With protection. O Agni. Wealth. To the generous patrons. And. Bestow.
Who. With wealth. With fame/food. And. Beyond. Others. With good hero-sons/valor. And. Surpass. People. ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, to the **generous patrons** <term>Maghavans: The wealthy sponsors of the sacrifice</term> who possess wealth in the form of oblations, and to **us**, along **with protections** and **many strengths** <note>original: *puru-vajabhih*, meaning either abundant food or many powers</note>, **bestow**—that is, give or grant—**wonderful** and desirable **wealth** **now** (quickly). The word **"and"** is used to connect this with what follows. Grant us also such sons **who**, through **wealth**, **fame** <note>Sayana glosses *shravasa* here as food</note>, and **good hero-sons** (or valorous deeds), **surpass**—greatly excel over—**other people** (other men). This is the meaning. ॥ ५ ॥
