-> ॥ Now the sixth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O Agni, desiring this sacrifice, place food within yourself; the sacrificer, sitting down with oblations, offers it to you. Among the Bharadvajas, you have maintained pure praise; protect them in the winning of attainable strength. ॥ ६ ॥

(Word-for-word breakdown)
This. Sacrifice. Food. Place. O Agni. Desiring. Which. To you. Sitting. Offers. Possessing oblations.
Among the Bharadvajas. You have maintained. Pure praise. Protect. Of strength/food. Attainable. In the winning. ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, you who are **desiring** [the offering], **place**—that is, hold within yourself—this **food** <term>Chanas: Food, specifically referring to the sacrificial offerings</term> which is the means of **this sacrifice** taking place before us. And **which** cake or other offering the **sacrificer**, **possessing oblations** and **sitting** down (seated), **offers to you**—the connection is to that very offering. **Furthermore**, **among the Bharadvaja** seers <term>Bharadvajas: The priestly clan to whom this Book of the Rig Veda is attributed</term>, you **maintain pure praise**—that is, a hymn of praise beautifully devoid of any faults. **Protect** those seers **in the winning** (the obtaining or sharing) of **attainable strength** <note>original: *vajasya gadhyasya*, referring to wealth or food that is to be mixed or acquired</note> or food. ॥ ६ ॥

-> ॥ Now the seventh verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Drive away the haters; increase the nourishment; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with good hero-sons. ॥ ७ ॥

(Word-for-word breakdown)
Away. Haters/Enemies. Drive. Increase. Nourishment. May we rejoice. Hundred-winters. With good hero-sons. ॥ ७ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, **drive away**—send in various directions—the **haters**, who are our enemies. And **increase our nourishment** <term>Ila: A goddess or personification of sacrificial food and refreshment</term>. And **may we**, being **blessed with good hero-sons** (endowed with excellent sons, grandsons, and so on), **rejoice**—be satisfied and happy—for **a hundred winters**, which means for a hundred full years. ॥ ७ ॥

<meta>This page transitions from the end of Hymn 10 to the beginning of Hymn 11 in the sixth book of the Rig Veda. While Hymn 10 focused on general praise and a plea for protection for the Bharadvaja clan, Hymn 11 shifts toward a more technical invocation of Agni as the supreme ritual priest (Hotar) who must invite the other gods to the sacrificial ground.</meta>

६१० || Rig Veda || [Book 6. Hymn 11. Verses 1-2.]

The eleventh hymn, beginning with "Sacrifice, O Priest," consists of six verses. It is attributed to the seer **Bharadvaja**; the meter is **Trishtubh** <note>A Vedic meter consisting of four lines of eleven syllables each</note>; and the deity is **Agni**. The traditional index <note>original: *Anukramani*</note> states: "Sacrifice, [hymn of] six [verses]." It is traditionally used in the **Morning Litany** <term>Pratar-anuvaka: A series of recitations performed at dawn</term> and the **Ashvina Shastra** <term>A specific recitation dedicated to the twin gods, the Ashvins</term>.

---

## Hymn Text

->|| Herein the first verse ||<-

**Sacrifice, O Priest, you who are incited, the most excellent sacrificer; O Agni, like the power of the Maruts, subduing [enemies]! To our sacrifice, may you bring Mitra and Varuna, the Nasatyas, and Heaven and Earth.** ॥ १ ॥

**Sacrifice. O Priest. Incited. Most excellent sacrificer. O Agni. Subduer. Of the Maruts. Like. Power/Force.**
**To. Us. Mitra-Varuna. Nasatyas. Heaven. For the sacrifice. And Earth. May you bring/turn toward.** ॥ १ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Priest** <note>original: *Hotar*, the invoker of the gods</note>, O Agni, you who are the **most excellent sacrificer** <note>original: *yajiyan*</note>, being **incited**—that is, requested or prayed to by us. The word **"like"** <note>original: *na*</note> here functions as an intensive or means "truly." In the **power** <note>original: *prayukti*</note> of the sacrifice currently being performed, **sacrifice** to the **Maruts** <note>The storm-gods</note>, who are the **subduers** of enemies. 

Alternatively, there are two separate thoughts here:
1. O Priest Agni, sacrifice to the gods!
2. Like the strength or **power** of the **Maruts**, you should **subdue**—that is, crush the enemies. 

Furthermore, may you **bring** <note>original: *avavrityah*, meaning turn toward or cause to arrive</note> to **our sacrifice** the following deities: **Mitra and Varuna** (Mitra who presides over the day and Varuna who presides over the night); the two **Nasatyas** <note>An epithet for the Ashvins, the twin physicians of the gods</note>, who are either the leaders of truth, truthful by nature, or born from the nose; and **Heaven and Earth**. ॥ १ ॥

---

## Hymn Text

->|| Now the second verse ||<-

**You are the most joyous priest for us, harmless, the divine one among mortals in the sacrificial assembly. O Agni, with the purifying ladle, as the carrier [of oblations] through your mouth, sacrifice to your own body.** ॥ २ ॥

**You. Priest. Most joyous. For us. Harmless. Within. Divine. Fit for the assembly. Among mortals.**
**With the purifying. Ladle/Flame. Carrier. With the mouth. O Agni. Sacrifice. Body. Your. Own.** ॥ २ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, among **mortals** (human beings), you exist **within** the **sacrificial assembly** <term>Vidatha: A gathering for religious or scholarly purposes</term> as the **Priest** who invites the gods. What kind of priest are you? You are **most joyous** <note>original: *mandratamah*, also meaning most praiseworthy</note> and **harmless** to **us**—that is, you are free from malice toward us, meaning you are always our friend. You are the **divine one** <note>original: *devah*</note>, endowed with the qualities of giving and light. 

Furthermore, O Agni, with the **ladle** <note>original: *juhu*</note>—so called because offerings are poured into it, referring here to the sacrificial **flame**—which is **purifying**, and through your **mouth** (since the fire is the mouth of the gods), you are the **carrier** <note>original: *vahni*</note> of the oblations. As such, **sacrifice** to **your own body** <note>original: *tanvam*</note>, which is known by the name **Svishtakrit** <term>Agni Svishtakrit: The aspect of the fire that "makes the sacrifice well-offered," usually receiving a concluding portion of the offering</term>. ॥ २ ॥

<vocab>
Bharadvaja: The primary seer of the sixth book of the Rig Veda.
Agni: The god of fire and mediator between gods and men.
Maruts: Vedic storm deities, companions of Indra.
Mitra-Varuna: A dual deity representing cosmic order, day, and night.
Nasatyas: Another name for the Ashvins, the twin gods of healing.
Juhu: A wooden ladle used for pouring clarified butter into the fire; often used metaphorically for the fire's tongue or flame.
Svishtakrit: A specific form of Agni honored at the end of a ritual to correct any errors made during the ceremony.
</vocab>

<keywords>Agni, Bharadvaja, Priest (Hotar), Maruts, Ashvins (Nasatyas), Mitra-Varuna, Sacrifice (Yajna), Svishtakrit, Trishtubh meter</keywords>

६११ || Mandala 6. Anuvaka 1. Hymn 11. || Fourth Octave || ६११

->|| Herein the third verse ||<-

## Hymn Text

**Indeed, the prayer for wealth desires you, [O Agni], to praise the birth of the gods so they may be sacrificed to. For the most vibrant singer among the Angirases, the wise poet, brings the honey-sweet hymn in the sacrifice.** ॥ ३ ॥

---

**Wealth-desiring. Indeed. For. In you. Prayer/Hymn. Desires. Forth. The gods. Birth. For the one who praises. To sacrifice.**
**Most vibrant. Among the Angirases. When. Indeed. Wise/Sage. Honey. Meter/Hymn. Brings. Singer. In the sacrifice.** ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **prayer** <note>original: *dhishana*, interpreted here as a hymn of praise</note>, which is **wealth-desiring** <note>original: *dhanya*, seeking wealth or being the cause of wealth</note>, O Agni, **desires** <note>original: *vashti*, loves or seeks</note> you. The word **"indeed"** <note>original: *chit*</note> is used here as a metrical filler. For what purpose? For the worshiper who **praises** <note>original: *grinate*</note> the **birth**—that is, the manifestation—of you [Agni], in order **to sacrifice** <note>original: *pra yajadhyai*, to sacrifice intensely</note> to the gods like Indra and others. **When** indeed, among the **Angirases** <term>A group of semi-divine ancestral seers</term>, the most **vibrant** <note>original: *vepishthah*, the most intense inspirer of praise</note>, **wise** <note>original: *viprah*</note> poet and **singer** <note>original: *rebhah*</note> **Bharadvaja** <note>The specific seer of this hymn</note> **brings**—meaning utters—the **honey-sweet** <note>original: *madhu*</note> **hymn** <note>original: *chandas*</note> in the **sacrifice** <note>original: *ishtau*</note>, then the prayer is said to desire Agni. This is the grammatical connection.

---

->|| Herein the fourth verse ||<-

## Hymn Text

**The wise and radiant one has shone brightly; O Agni, worship the wide-reaching Heaven and Earth. As the five classes of men, having offered oblations, honor a guest with reverence, so they anoint the well-fed [Agni].** ॥ ४ ॥

---

**Has shone. Wise. Radiant. O Agni. Worship. Heaven and Earth. Wide-reaching.**
**Mortal/Guest. Like. Whom. With reverence. Those who have offered oblations. Anoint/Satisfy. Well-fed/Having good food. Five. Men/Classes.** ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

This Agni **shone** <note>original: *adidyutat*, he glows or shines brightly</note>. Of what nature is he? He is **wise** <note>original: *svapakah*; Sayana explains that *paka* means an "unripe" or foolish mind, so *a-paka* means one who is the opposite: exceptionally wise</note> and **radiant** <note>original: *vibhava*, full of light</note>. The rest of the verse is addressed directly to him. O Agni, you who are such, **worship** <note>original: *yajasva*, honor with offerings</note> the **wide-reaching** <note>original: *uruchi*</note> **Heaven and Earth** <note>original: *rodasi*</note>. Just **as** <note>original: *na*</note> a mortal **guest** <note>original: *ayum*, here interpreted as a human guest who must be honored</note> is treated, so the **five classes of men** <note>original: *pancha janah*, referring to the four castes and the forest-dwellers, or specifically the priests and the patron of the sacrifice</note>, being **offered-oblation-givers** <note>original: *rata-havyah*</note>, **anoint** <note>original: *anjanti*, smear with butter or satisfy with offerings</note> with **reverence** <note>original: *namasa*, meaning food in the form of an oblation</note> the Agni who is **well-fed** <note>original: *suprayasam*, possessing excellent sacrificial food</note>. The connection is: "You, being so anointed, should perform the sacrifice."

---

->|| Herein the fifth verse ||<-

## Hymn Text

**I prepare the sacred grass with reverence when, O Agni, the perfect praise is offered; the sacrifice has been established today in the seat of the Earth, as the eye is fixed upon the Sun.** ॥ ५ ॥

---

**I prepare. Indeed. When. With reverence. Sacred grass. O Agni. I bring/extend. Possessing perfect praise. Perfect praise.**
**It has been beheld/established. Today. In the seat. Of the Earth. It has been supported. Sacrifice. In the Sun. As if. The eye.** ॥ ५ ॥

६१२ || Mandala 6. Hymn 4 (cont.) and Hymn 5. || Fourth Octave || Adhyaya 5 || Varga 14.

## Hymn Text

**I pluck. Indeed. When. With homage. Sacrificial grass. In the fire. Is offered. Ladle. Filled with clarified butter. Well-purified.**
**Attained. Altar. In the place. Of the earth. Was supported. Sacrifice. In the sun. Like. Eye.** ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

When indeed, with **homage**—that is, together with the oblation—near the fire, the **sacrificial grass** <term>Barhis; sacred grass strewn on the altar for the gods to sit upon</term> is **plucked** <note>original: *vṛñje*, from the root for cutting; here meaning it is harvested and brought</note>. It is cut; the meaning is that it is brought. The **ladle** <note>original: *sruk*, a wooden tool used to pour offerings</note>, which is **well-purified** <note>original: *suvṛktiḥ*, meaning it is well-cleansed of any defects</note> and **filled with clarified butter** <note>original: *ghṛtavatī*</note>, is offered and held steady as it is placed upon the grass. Likewise, in the **place of the earth**—meaning on the ground—the **altar** <note>original: *sadma*, the ritual seat or dwelling</note> for the placing of oblations is **attained** <note>original: *amyakṣi*, derived from a root meaning to go or move; here meaning it is reached and occupied</note>. It is surrounded and taken possession of. At that time, the **sacrifice was supported** <note>original: *yajño'śrāyi*</note>; that is, the sacrificer becomes supported by it. A comparison is given: **Like the eye in the sun.** Just as the illuminating light is inherent in the **sun** <note>original: *sūrye*, referring to the Aditya who impels all things</note>, so too does the light of the sacrifice reside in the ritual.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Herein the sixth verse ॥ <-

**Grant us wealth, O Agni of many manifestations, O Invoker, kindled along with the divine fires. O Son of Strength, as we clothe ourselves [in your protection], may we cross over distress as we would an enemy.** ॥ ६ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
**Grant. Us. Of many manifestations. O Invoker. With the gods. O Agni. With fires. Being kindled.**
**Of wealth. O Son. Of strength. Clothed/Abiding. Over. May we cross. Trouble. Like. Sin.** ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni of many manifestations** <note>original: *purvanīka*, meaning he who has many flames</note>, O **Invoker** <note>original: *hotar*, the priest who calls the gods</note>, as you are **being kindled** <note>original: *idhānaḥ*</note> along with the other **divine fires**—which are your own manifestations—**grant** <note>original: *daśasya*, meaning to give or bestow</note> to us **wealth** <note>original: *rāyaḥ*</note>. O **Son of Strength** <note>original: *sahasaḥ sūno*, an epithet for Agni because he is produced by the forceful friction of wood</note>, we who **clothe** <note>original: *vāvasānāḥ*</note> ourselves with you by offering oblations, **may we cross over** <note>original: *ati sasema*, meaning to go beyond or transcend</note> **sin** <note>original: *aṃhaḥ*</note> just as one might overcome a **trouble** or an **enemy** <note>original: *vṛjanam*</note>.

-> ॥ Thus ends the thirteenth varga of the fifth chapter of the fourth octave ॥ <-

---

## Sukta Introduction

The twelfth hymn, beginning with "In the middle, the priest," consists of six verses. The seer is Bharadvaja, the meter is Trishtubh, and the deity is Agni. Its application is mentioned in the rituals of the Morning Litany and the Ashvin Shastra.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Herein the first verse ॥ <-

**The priest in the middle of the house, the ruler of the sacrificial grass, Agni [incites] the worshiper to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth. This son of strength, the observer of truth, has spread out with his radiance from afar like the sun.** ॥ १ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
**In the middle. Priest. In the house. Of the sacrificial grass. Ruler. Agni. Of the inciter. Heaven and Earth. To sacrifice.**
**This. He. Son. Of strength. Observer of truth. From afar. Sun. Like. With radiance. Has spread out.** ॥ १ ॥

<vocab>
- पुर्वणीक (purvanika): Of many manifestations or many flames; describing Agni's diverse forms.
- सहसः सूनो (sahasah suno): Son of strength; a common title for Agni, referring to the physical effort required to ignite him.
- वृजनं (vrijanam): Enemy, trouble, or a difficult situation.
- अंहः (amhah): Sin, distress, or narrowness that restricts the soul.
- भरद्वाज (Bharadvaja): The historical seer (Rishi) of this family of hymns in the Rig Veda.
- त्रैष्टुभ (Traistubha): A poetic meter consisting of four lines of eleven syllables each.
- आग्नेय (Agneya): Relating to or dedicated to Agni, the fire god.
- रोदसी (Rodasi): A dual term referring to Heaven and Earth together as a pair.
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes the fourth hymn of Mandala 6, asking Agni to grant wealth and protection from sin, and begins the fifth hymn by describing Agni as the divine priest who radiates light like the sun.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Bharadvaja, Son of Strength, sacrificial grass, altar, wealth, protection from sin, Heaven and Earth, Trishtubh meter</keywords>

६१३ || Mandala 6. Hymn 1. Sukta 12. ] || Fourth Octave || ६१३

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Second Verse ॥ <-

**In whom—in you—O wise one, O worshipful King, the sacrifice is offered; like the all-encompassing heaven, may you indeed be. Existing in three abodes, like the speed of the one who crosses the sky, for the sacrificing of human offerings and riches.** ॥ २ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis (Pada-patha):**
**In. In whom. In you. [End-marker]. O wise one. O worshipful one. May he sacrifice. O King. Like the all-encompassing sacrifice. Indeed. Heaven.
Existing in three abodes. Of the one who crosses. Like. Speed. Offerings. Riches. Belonging to humans. For sacrificing.** ॥ २ ॥

-> ॥ The Third Verse ॥ <-

**Whose flame is most sharp, ruling in the forest; like a goader on the path, the one increasing has shone. Not deceiving, like a runner, he perceives by himself—the immortal one—among the plants that lack brilliance.** ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis (Pada-patha):**
**Most sharp. Whose. Flame. Ruling in the forest. Goad. On the path. The one increasing. Has shone.
Not deceiving. Like. A runner. He perceives. By himself. The immortal one. Lacking brilliance. Among the plants.** ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

<note>Conclusion of commentary on RV 6.12.1</note>
The **invoker** <term>Hotar; the priest who calls the gods</term> of the gods, the **king** <note>original: *rāt*</note> of the **sacrificial grass** <term>Barhis</term> and the sacrifice, is the fire. The **sacrificer** <note>original: *todo*</note> is so called because he is "goaded" or distressed by the heat of his penance. [The Fire] sits in the middle of his **house** <note>original: *durone*</note>. For what purpose? To **sacrifice** <note>original: *yajadhyai*</note> to **Heaven and Earth** <note>original: *rodasī*</note>. Such is this **Son of Strength** <term>Sahasaḥ sūnu; a common title for Agni because fire is produced by the strength of rubbing sticks</term>, the possessor of truth or the possessor of sacrifice. This Agni, like the **sun** <note>original: *sūryo na*</note>, has extended his **brilliance** <note>original: *śociṣā*</note> or heat from afar. He spreads it out. The meaning is that even while remaining at a distance, he illuminates the whole world just like the sun.

<note>Commentary on RV 6.12.2</note>
**Heaven** <note>original: *dyauḥ*</note> refers to the praiser. The phrase **like the all-encompassing** <note>original: *sarvatātaiva*</note> uses the word "iva" (like) as a filler. This is a name for a sacrifice. It refers to a sacrifice being extended by all. Alternatively, the suffix *-tāti* is added to the word "all" (*sarva*) without changing the meaning. Every praiser, O **worshipful** <note>original: *yajatra*</note>—O Agni who is worthy of being worshipped—O **King**—O shining one—O **wise one** <note>original: *apāke*</note>, in **you** <note>original: *tve*</note>, who are very **quickly** <note>original: *nu*</note> reached, he offers the oblations. You, **existing in three abodes** <note>original: *triṣadhasthaḥ*</note>, stay together in the three worlds. Or, it means you exist in three forms as the Gārhapatya fire and others. Being such, may you have **speed** <note>original: *jaṃhaḥ*</note> like **the one who crosses** <note>original: *tataruṣo na*</note>, meaning the sun. The word *jaṃhaḥ* is a form derived from the root meaning "to go." Alternatively, it comes from the root *tṛ* (to cross or float). The form *tataruṣaḥ* is the genitive case of "one who has crossed." The meaning is: let your speed be like that of the crossing sun. For what purpose? To **sacrifice** <note>original: *yajadhyai*</note>—that is, to give to the gods—the **offerings** <note>original: *havyā*</note> and **riches** <note>original: *maghāni*</note> which are desirable, praiseworthy, and **belonging to humans** <note>original: *mānuṣā*</note>.

<note>Commentary on RV 6.12.3 (Beginning)</note>
Of which Agni the **flame** <note>original: *aratiḥ*</note>—the moving flash—being **most sharp** <note>original: *tejiṣṭhā*</note> and extremely brilliant, exists **ruling in the forest** <note>original: *vanerāt*</note> in the form of a forest fire. That Agni, **the one increasing** <note>original: *vṛdhasānaḥ*</note>, [shone] like a **goad** <note>original: *todaḥ*</note> on the **path** <note>original: *adhvan*</note>. A goad...

<vocab>
Agni (Fire god), Yajamana (Sacrificer), Yajatra (Worshipful), Havi (Oblation), Surya (Sun), Oshadhi (Plants/Herbs), Sahasa Sunu (Son of Strength), Sarvatati (All-encompassing sacrifice)
</vocab>

<summary>This page discusses Agni's dual nature: his presence in the three ritual fires and his cosmic power compared to the sun. The text emphasizes his speed in conveying human offerings to the gods and his sharp brilliance when burning through forests.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, solar imagery, sacrificial fires, speed of the sun, forest fire, Son of Strength, Sayana, Rig Veda 6.12</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the twelfth hymn of the sixth Mandala of the Rig Veda (though the header marks it by the Ashtaka system as Ashtaka 4, Adhyaya 5, Varga 14). It completes the explanation of verse 3, provides the full text and word-for-word breakdown for verse 4, and begins the explanation of verse 5. The focus remains on Agni's destructive yet vital power in the forests and his role in the sacrificial home.</meta>

६१४ || Rig Veda || Ashtaka 4. Adhyaya 5. Varga 14.

The sun is the **inspirer** of all. Like the sun, Agni has **shone** in his own path within the atmosphere. Furthermore, he is "not deceiving" <note>original: *adrogho*</note>, meaning he is not to be deceived; or perhaps, like the wind which, as the life-breath of all, does not deceive, such is the **immortal** <term>Amartya; deathless</term> Agni dwelling among the **plants**. They are called *oshadhi* because ripening heat <note>original: *osha*</note> is placed <note>original: *dhiyate*</note> within them—namely, the forests. Moving swiftly through them and being **unrestrained** by anyone, he **perceives** <note>original: *cetati*</note> or makes things known by his own light. He causes the whole world to be known.

---

->॥ The Fourth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
With our pleasing hymns, Agni—the knower of all beings—is praised in the house; consuming the wood with his power like a swift traveler, he is honored with sacrifices like a fatherly bull. ॥ ४ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis (Pada-patha):**
**He. With ours. Like a traveler. Not [particle of comparison]. With pleasing hymns. Agni. Is praised. In the house. [Towards]. Knower of all beings.
One whose food is difficult wood. Consuming. By his power/action. Like. A swift one. A bull. Like a father. Is praised. With sacrifices.** ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Jatavedas** <term>A title for Agni meaning "knower of all births" or "possessor of innate wisdom"</term> is that Agni who is praised by our chanters. Just as the hymns found in a **traveler** <note>original: *etari*; one who approaches to ask or supplicate</note> are extremely pleasing, so is he praised with pleasing hymns in our **sacrificial home** <term>Dame</term>. Furthermore, he is "one whose food is difficult" <note>original: *durvannaḥ*</note>, meaning that "difficult wood" <note>original: *durdrumaḥ*</note> is his food. Therefore, **consuming** the forests and by his own **action** <note>original: *kratvā*</note>, he becomes a beautiful mover. To this, an illustration is given: **like a fatherly bull** <note>original: *usraḥ piteva*</note>. As a bull, the protector <note>original: *pitā*</note> or father of calves, moves quickly for mating, so too is Agni **praised** <note>original: *jārayāyi*</note> by the sacrificing worshippers. <note>The word *jārayāyi* is a form derived from the root *jṛ*, meaning to praise.</note>

---

->॥ The Fifth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
Indeed, they praise his rays when he effortlessly carves his way along the broad earth; he is the swift runner, set free and moving fast, like a thief over the desert, a shining ruler. ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis (Pada-patha):**
**Indeed. [Filler particle]. His. They praise. The rays. Effortlessly. When. Carving. Follows along. The broad earth.
Immediately. Who. The runner. Set free. Moving very fast. Like a thief. [Particle of comparison]. A thief. Across. The desert/firmament. The shining ruler.** ॥ ५ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
Now <note>original: *adha*</note> in this world—the word *sma* is a filler—the chanters **praise** <note>original: *panayanti*</note> the rays of this Agni. When he **effortlessly** <note>original: *vṛthā*</note>, without any exertion, **carves** <note>original: *takṣat*</note> or thins the forests by burning them completely, and **follows** along the wide forest-land, then they praise him. That Agni who is the **runner**...

<meta>This page continues the commentary of Sayana on the 6th Mandala of the Rig Veda. It concludes the explanation for the 5th verse of Hymn 12, provides the full text and commentary for the 6th verse of Hymn 13, and begins the 14th Hymn. ६१५ || Rig Veda || Ashtaka 4. Adhyaya 5. Varga 14.

...moving quickly, released, and free from obstruction; for this reason, he is immediately the swiftest of travelers. Like what? Like a thief <note>original: *tāyuḥ*</note>. Just as a thief is a swift traveler, so this Agni, having crossed the desert <note>original: *dhanva*</note>, shines. Alternatively, "the atmosphere" is called *dhanva* because waters flow from it; having pervaded the atmosphere extensively, he shines.

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ The Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**O runner, Agni, kindled by all the fires, protect us from reproach. Bring us wealth, drive away our sorrows; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with noble sons.** ॥ ६ ॥

-> Word-by-word Analysis <-
**He. You. Us. O runner. From reproach. With all. O Agni. With fires. Being kindled.**
**Bring. Wealth. Away. You go. Sorrows. May we rejoice. A hundred winters. With noble sons.** ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **runner** <term>Arvan; an epithet for Agni meaning "the swifter" or "the horse"</term>, Agni who moves, **you**, being such a one, protect us from **reproach** <note>original: *nidāyā*</note>—meaning either from people who deserve blame or from the act of censure itself. In what manner? **Being kindled** <note>original: *idhānaḥ*</note> **by all** the other **fires** which are like your own branches. **Bring** us **wealth**; or alternatively, "bring" means you desire the wealth characterized by sacrificial offerings. **And you go away** from—meaning you drive away—the **sorrows** or the painful armies of our enemies. And may we, being **blessed with noble sons** <note>original: *suvīrāḥ*; literally "having good heroes" or "strong sons"</note>, **rejoice** <note>original: *madema*</note> for **a hundred winters** <term>Śatahimāḥ; a standard Vedic expression for a full lifespan of one hundred years</term>.

## Introduction to Sukta 14
The **thirteenth hymn** <note>traditionally numbered as Sukta 14 of the 6th Mandala</note>, beginning with "From you, all..." <note>original: *tvad viśvā*</note>, contains six verses. Its Seer is **Bharadvaja** <term>Bharadvāja; the prominent sage of the 6th Mandala</term>, its meter is **Trishtubh** <term>Triṣṭubh; a meter consisting of four lines of eleven syllables each</term>, and its deity is **Agni**. The application of this hymn has been stated in the context of the "Morning Litany" and the "Aswina Weapon" ceremonies.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ The First Verse ॥ <-

**From you, O fortunate Agni, all blessings spread out like branches from a tree. Prosperity, food, the overcoming of enemies in battle, the rain from heaven, and the flowing of the waters are all to be praised from you.** ॥ १ ॥

-> Word-by-word Analysis <-
**From you. All. O fortunate one. Blessings. O Agni. Away. They go. Trees. Like. Branches.**
**Quickly. Wealth. Food. In the overcoming of enemies. From heaven. Rain. To be praised. Flow. Of waters.** ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **fortunate one** <note>original: *subhaga*</note>—you who possess beautiful wealth—O Agni, **all blessings** or riches **spread out from you** in various directions. This is because gold is the root of all wealth, and gold was produced from Agni; for the Scripture <term>Śruti; the revealed Vedic texts</term> says: "His seed fell and became gold." Regarding this spreading out...

<vocab>
अर्वन् (arvan) - runner/horse, epithet for Agni
निदा (nidā) - blame/contempt
अग्नि (agni) - fire deity
भरद्वाज (bharadvāja) - the Rishi of this Sukta
त्रैष्टुभ (traiṣṭubha) - Trishtubh meter
आग्नेय (āgneya) - relating to Agni
सुभग (subhaga) - fortunate/blessed
शतहिमाः (śatahimāḥ) - living for a hundred winters
</vocab>

<meta>This page continues the commentary of Sayana on the 6th Mandala of the Rig Veda, Sukta 13. It concludes the explanation for Verse 1, provides the full text and commentary for Verse 2, and begins the commentary for Verse 3. The page numbering is 616, and the header indicates this falls within the 4th Ashtaka, 5th Adhyaya, and 15th Varga.</meta>

६१६ || Rig Veda || Ashtaka 4. Adhyaya 5. Varga 15.

An illustration: *Like the branches of a tree* <note>original: vanino na vayāḥ</note>. Just as branches emerge in various ways from a tree, in the same manner, wealth and herds of cattle go forth quickly from you. The Taittiriya scripture says: "Cattle are indeed wealth; one attains cattle [through him]." In the slaying of Vritra <note>the "encloser" or obstacle-demon</note>, in the battle to conquer enemies, strength and power go forth from you. That rain which comes from the sky and atmosphere also goes forth from you alone. The oblation cast into the fire reaches the Sun perfectly. From the Sun, rain is born; from rain, food; from food, progeny—as the traditional law <note>Smriti</note> remembers. Therefore, being worthy of praise by all, you are the guide of the flow of the waters.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Second [Verse] ॥ <-

**O Agni, you are like Bhaga to us; bring us delightful wealth. Like a traveler through the world, you dwell everywhere, possessing visible splendor. O God, like a friend, you are the dispenser of the great Law and of abundant treasures.** ॥ २ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**

**You. Bhaga. Like. Unto. Indeed. Jewel/Wealth. For strength/food. Like a traveler. You dwell. Possessing visible splendor. O Agni. Friend. Like. Of the great. Of the Law/Sacrifice. You are. Dispenser. Of the desirable. O God. Of the abundant.** ॥ २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, you are **Bhaga**, the one to be shared or worshipped; for us, to the **jewel**—meaning delightful wealth—bring it <note>original: ā hī</note>; grant it. The word *ishe* <note>for strength/food</note> comes from the root meaning "to go." The particle *hi* is a filler. You possess **visible splendor** <note>original: dasmavarcāḥ</note> and you dwell everywhere like the **traveler** <note>original: parijman</note> or the wind which goes all around. Alternatively, the root *kshi* <note>to dwell</note> implies lordship; you rule over all. O Agni, like a **friend** <note>original: mitro na</note>, the protector from decay, you are the **dispenser** <note>original: kṣattā</note> of the **great Law** <term>Rita: the cosmic order, often identified here with the sacrifice or the waters</term>. Here, the word "dispenser" <note>original: kṣadatih</note> implies the act of giving; you are the giver. Likewise, O shining Agni, it follows that you are the giver of **abundant** and desirable wealth.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Third [Verse] ॥ <-

**That protector of the good, through power, slays the enemy. O Agni, the wise man seizes the food of the Pani. You, O wise one born of the Law, O Son of Waters, speed him forward with wealth.** ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**

**He. Protector of the good. With power. Slays. Vritra. O Agni. The wise man. [Separately]. Of the Pani. He carries/takes. The food/strength. Whom. You. O wise one. Born of the Law. With wealth. Being in harmony. Son. Of the waters. You speed forward.** ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, that man who is a **protector of the good** <note>original: satpatiḥ</note> slays the **enemy** <note>Vritra, the "encloser"</note> through his power. And he, being a **wise man** <note>original: vipraḥ</note>, seizes the **food** or strength of the merchant-demon named **Pani**. He takes it away. <note>The verb *bharti* is used here in the sense of taking away</note>. O you of excellent knowledge <note>original: pracetāḥ</note>, **born of the Law**—*Rita* is a name for the sacrifice; Agni is born for the sake of that—O **Son of Waters** <term>Apam Napat: a title for Agni meaning "the descendant of the waters," referring to fire's origin in the lightning or the moisture of wood</term>, [one who does not let fall...]

<vocab>
Agni: Fire, the mediator deity.
Bhaga: The dispenser of fortune.
Ratna: Literally "jewel," but signifies delightful wealth.
Dasmavarcha: Having wonderful or visible light.
Rita: Cosmic order, truth, or the sacrificial rite.
Satpati: Lord of the virtuous or the true.
Vritra: The personification of obstruction or drought.
Vipra: An inspired poet or wise priest.
Pani: A class of demons who withhold wealth or cows.
Vaja: Strength, booty, or sacrificial food.
Apam Napat: The "Grandson of Waters," a solar or fiery deity of the deep.
</vocab>

## Hymn Text
O **Son of Strength**, whatever mortal reaches your **sharpening** on the sacrificial altar through hymns, chants, and sacrifices; he, O God Agni, holds every desirable grain and rules over all riches. ॥ ४ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Whoever. Your. O Son. Of Strength. By hymns. By chants. By sacrifices. Mortal. Sharpening. On the altar. Reached. All. He. O God. Every. Desirable. O Agni. Holds. Grains. Rules. Over riches. ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Son of Strength** <note>Sahasah suno: Agni is so called because he is generated by the forceful friction of fire-sticks</note>, O Agni! Whatever mortal sacrificer brings your **intensity** <note>original: niśitim; sharpness or power</note> to the sacrificial ground <term>Vedi</term> through hymns of praise, chants <note>specifically "ukthas" or recited verses</note>, and the sacrificial means such as oblations; that mortal, O shining Agni, sustains all that is sufficient. And he also holds grain. He becomes possessed of **riches** <note>original: vasavyaiḥ</note>. ॥ ४ ॥

## Hymn Text
O Agni, **Son of Strength**, bring to the leaders those items of **high renown** and good progeny for our nourishment. By your power, you create abundant food from cattle even for the **wolf**, the enemy, and the consumer. ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Those. To the leaders. [Bring] near. Of high renown. With good sons. O Agni. O Son. Of Strength. For nourishment. Place [among us]. You create. Which. By power. Abundant. Of cattle. Food. For the wolf. For the enemy. For the consumer. ॥ ५ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Son of Strength, O Agni! Bring those **high renowns** <note>original: sauśravasā; also interpreted as "excellent foods"</note> which are accompanied by excellent sons from the enemy folk and place them <note>original: dhāḥ</note> among us. For what purpose? For **nourishment**. Alternatively, place them among us, the leaders of these hymns. Grant them to us directly. You, who are endowed with might, produce the abundant food consisting of curds and other cattle-products even for the **wolf** <note>original: vṛkāya; here meaning the "taker" or "consumer"</note>, for the one who stints <note>the enemy</note>, or for the consumer. The meaning is: take that food and grant it to us. ॥ ५ ॥

## Hymn Text (RV 6.13.6 - Word-by-word Analysis)

Speaker. O Son <note>original: "sūno"</note>. Of Strength <note>original: "sahasah"</note>. To us. All-pervading <note>original: "vihāyāḥ"</note>. O Agni. Progeny. Grand-progeny. Full of food. Give. With all. Songs of praise. Over. Fulfillment. May I attain. May we rejoice. Living a hundred years. Having brave sons. ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Son of Strength** <note>original: "sahasah sūno"</note>, son of power, O Agni, you are **all-pervading** <note>original: "vihāyāḥ"</note>. This is a name for one who is "great." May you be our **speaker** <note>original: "vaktā"</note>, one who speaks and advises what is beneficial for us. Furthermore, **give** to us **progeny** <note>original: "tokam"</note>—meaning a son—and **grand-progeny** <note>original: "tanayam"</note>—meaning the son's son—who are **full of food** <note>original: "vājinaḥ"</note>. I, the singer of praise, **may I attain** <note>original: "abhyasyām"</note> the **fulfillment** of my desires through **all** the **songs of praise** directed toward you. The rest of the verse has been explained previously <note>referring to the standard prayer for a long life of a hundred years with heroic descendants</note>.

-> ॥ Thus ends the fifteenth group <term>Varga</term> of the fifth chapter in the fourth [Ashtaka] ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text (RV 6.14.1-2)

**The fourteenth hymn, beginning with "Agna ya," consists of six verses and is attributed to the Seer <term>Rishi</term> Bharadvaja, dedicated to Agni. The sixth verse is in the Shakkari meter, and the remaining five are in the Anushtubh meter. As stated in the Index <note>Anukramani</note>: "Agna ya is in Anushtubh, ending in Shakkari." This hymn is used in the morning litany <term>Prataranuvaka</term> and the ceremony for the Ashvins <term>Ashvinashastra</term> dedicated to Agni. It is indicated by the reference: "Agna yo hota-janishta" (Asvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.13). In the four-day sacrifice known as Chaturvira, on the third day of the multi-day sacrifice <term>Ahina</term>, this hymn is used for the ritual recitation <term>Ajyashastra</term>. It is indicated: "Agna yo martyo duva on the third day" (Asvalayana Shrauta Sutra 10.2).**

-> ॥ Here is the first [verse] ॥ <-

O Agni, whatever mortal serves you with worship, ritual acts, and songs of praise; may he quickly shine forth as the foremost among men, and may he choose food for his protection. ॥ १ ॥

**॥ Word-by-word Analysis ॥**

O Agni. Who. Mortal. Worship. Ritual act. Served. With songs of praise. Shine. Indeed. He. Forth. Foremost. Food. May he choose. For protection. ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Whatever mortal** man **serves** <note>original: "jujoṣa"</note>—meaning performs—**worship** <note>original: "duvaḥ"</note> or service **in Agni** <note>directed toward Agni</note> and the **ritual act** <note>original: "dhiyam"</note> such as the sacrifice, along **with songs of praise**, that **mortal** being **foremost** <note>original: "pūrvyaḥ"</note> or chief among his predecessors, may he **indeed** quickly **shine forth**. That is, may he become possessor of great light. **For protection** of his sons and others, may he **choose** <note>original: "vurīta"</note> or obtain **food**, and may he take it from his enemies. ॥ १ ॥

---

## Hymn Text (RV 6.14.2)

-> ॥ Now the second [verse] ॥ <-

Agni is indeed the wise one; Agni is the most skilled creator and the Seer. Human tribes praise Agni as the priest in their sacrifices. ॥ २ ॥

**॥ Word-by-word Analysis ॥**

Agni. Indeed. For. Wise. Agni. Most skilled creator. Seer. Agni. The priest. They praise. In sacrifices. Human. Tribes. ॥ २ ॥

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Rig Veda, Mandala 6, Hymn 14. It concludes the explanation of verse 2 and provides the text and scholarly commentary for verses 3, 4, and the beginning of verse 5. The focus remains on Agni as the supreme knower and the provider of strength and wealth to his worshippers.</meta>

## Commentary (Sayana) - Verse 2 [Continued]

Agni alone is this—Agni is the **wise one** <note>original: "pracetāḥ"</note>, the one possessing excellent knowledge, and no one else. Because this is so, he is the **supreme performer** <note>original: "vidhātṛtamaḥ"</note>, the one who preeminently carries out the acts of conveying the oblation and other duties; he is the **seer** <term>Rishi</term> and the witness of everything. The **subjects** <note>original: "viśaḥ"</note> of the human sacrificer—meaning the officiating priests—**praise** <note>original: "īḷate"</note> such an Agni, the **invoker** <term>Hotar</term> who calls the gods, in the various sacrifices.

---

## Hymn Text - Verse 3

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

**In various ways, O Agni, for protection, the riches of the enemy strive; humans, overcoming the destroyer, seek to overpower the lawless with sacred rites.** ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
In various ways | indeed | O Agni | for protection | they strive | riches | of the enemy | overcoming | the destroyer <term>Dasyu</term> | humans | through sacred rites | seeking to overcome | the lawless. ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, the **riches** <note>original: "rāyaḥ"</note> of the **enemy** <note>original: "aryaḥ"</note>—the foe—strive in **various ways** <note>original: "nānā"</note>, becoming separated from the enemy for the **protection** <note>original: "avase"</note> of those who praise you. They engage in a sort of competition, as if saying, "I shall protect them! I shall protect them!" The **humans** <note>original: "āyavaḥ"</note>, who are the praisers, are those who **strike down** <note>original: "tūrvaṇtaḥ"</note> and destroy the **enemy** <term>Dasyu</term>. Through **sacred rites** <note>original: "vrataih"</note> dedicated to you, they desire to **withstand and overcome** <note>original: "sīṣantaḥ"</note> the person who is **lawless** <note>original: "avratam"</note> or opposed to such sacred vows.

---

## Hymn Text - Verse 4

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

**Agni gives a hero, a winner of waters, an overcomer of hostilities, a lord of the virtuous; at the sight of whom, enemies tremble with fear from his strength.** ॥ ४ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Agni | winner of waters | overcomer of hostilities | a hero | gives | a lord of the virtuous | of whom | they tremble | from strength | at the sight | enemies | with fear. ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

This Agni **gives a hero** <note>original: "vīram"</note>—meaning a son. He bestows him upon the praisers. What kind of son? One who is a **winner of waters** <note>original: "apsām"</note>, meaning he obtains or enjoys the works and rewards to be reached; an **overcomer of hostilities** <note>original: "ṛtīṣaham"</note>, one who endures and subdues enemies or injuries; and a **lord of the virtuous** <note>original: "satpatim"</note>, a protector of good and true deeds. The connection is that **at the sight** <note>original: "saṃcakṣi"</note> of this hero, the **enemies tremble** and are agitated with **fear** <note>original: "bhiyā"</note> because of his **strength** <note>original: "śavasaḥ"</note>.

---

## Hymn Text - Verse 5

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**For Agni, the god, protects the mortal from the censurers and the obstacles; he is the conqueror, whose wealth is unassailable and unhindered in battles.** ॥ ५ ॥

<vocab>
**Agni** (अग्नि) - The Fire god, primary deity of the Vedic sacrifice.
**Dasyu** (दस्यु) - A destroyer or enemy; often interpreted as those who do not perform the Vedic rites.
**Humans** (आयवः - Ayavah) - Mortals or descendants of the ancestor Ayu; specifically the praisers in this context.
**Overcomer of hostilities** (ऋतीषहम् - Rtisaham) - One who is capable of defeating enemies or enduring attacks.
**Lord of the virtuous** (सत्पतिम् - Satpatim) - A guardian of those who perform the correct rituals or follow the truth.
</vocab>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on Hymn 14 of the 6th Book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda and introduces Hymn 15. It marks the transition from the 16th to the 17th Section (Varga) within the 5th Chapter (Adhyaya) of the 4th Volume (Ashtaka).</meta>

## Hymn Text

<note>Rig Veda 6.14.5 (Word-by-word Analysis)</note>
Agni | indeed | through knowledge | from the reviler | the God | the mortal | protects | the powerful | whose | of the courser | wealth | in battles | is unhindered. ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**The powerful one.** <note>original: "sahāsvā"</note> Power <note>original: "sahas"</note> means strength. The God Agni, who possesses that strength and is endowed with qualities such as generosity, uses his **knowledge** <note>original: "vidmanā"</note> to **protect** <note>original: "uruṣyati"</note> the **mortal** <note>original: "marttaṃ"</note>—the human sacrificer—from the **reviler** <note>original: "nidaḥ"</note> or the one who speaks ill. The word "indeed" <note>original: "hi"</note> serves as an emphatic filler. The connection of the verse is as follows: Agni protects that sacrificer who possesses offerings, whose **wealth** <note>original: "rayiḥ"</note> (consisting of the sacrificial oblation) is **unhindered** <note>original: "avṛtaḥ"</note>—meaning it is not obscured by demons or similar entities—and which, in **battles** <term>vāja</term> <note>here referring to the sacrificial rites</note>, is not intercepted or shared by other rival sacrificers.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**O God Agni, whose greatness is like a friend, speak of our good intent to the gods of Heaven and Earth. Lead us to well-being and a secure dwelling. May we cross over our enemies, sins, and difficulties; may we cross over them; through your protection, may we cross over them completely.** ॥ ६ ॥

<note>Rig Veda 6.14.6 (Word-by-word Analysis)</note>
Towards | our | O you of friendly greatness | God | to the gods | O Agni | speak | good intent | of the two worlds (Heaven and Earth) | lead | well-being | secure dwelling | of heaven | the leaders | enemies | sins | difficulties | may we cross over | those | may we cross over | your | with protection | may we cross over. ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
This verse has been explained previously. The literal meaning of the words is: O Agni, you who possess friendly radiance and qualities like generosity, having reached the two worlds of Heaven and Earth, **speak** <note>original: "vocaḥ"</note> or proclaim our excellent praise to the gods who are to be worshipped. **Lead** <note>original: "vīhi"</note> us, the leaders of this praise, to a secure dwelling and to a state that is free from destruction. By your grace, may we **cross over** <note>original: "tarema"</note> those who hate us, as well as our sins, the fruits of those sins, and the difficult paths we must walk. May we also cross over those hidden sins committed in other births. Through your protection, may we cross over them entirely.

-> ॥ Thus ends the sixteenth section of the fifth chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-

## Introductory Notes (Sukta 6.15)
The fifteenth hymn, beginning with "Imam u shu va," consists of nineteen verses. The **seer** <term>Rishi</term> is Vitahavya, the son of Varshamatri, who belongs to the lineage of Angiras and Bharadvaja. Regarding the **meters** <term>Chhandas</term>: the first nine verses are in the **Jagati** <note>a meter with 48 syllables</note> meter. However, the third and fifteenth verses are **Shakvari** <note>56 syllables</note>, the sixth is **Atishakvari** <note>60 syllables</note>, the seventeenth is **Anushtubh** <note>32 syllables</note>, and the eighteenth is **Brihati** <note>36 syllables</note>. Seven verses—specifically the tenth through the fourteenth, the sixteenth, and the nineteenth—are in the **Trishtubh** <note>44 syllables</note> meter.

This is confirmed by the **Index of Hymns** <term>Anukramani</term>: **"The hymn 'Imam u shu' has nineteen verses; Vitahavya is the seer; the meter is Jagati before the tenth verse, but the third and fifteenth are Shakvari, the sixth is Atishakvari, and Anushtubh and Brihati are the penultimate ones."**

In the ritual of the **Morning Libation** <term>Prataranuvaka</term>, specifically in the Agni-related portion of the **Ashvina Litany** <term>Ashvina-shastra</term>, the first nine verses of this hymn are recited. This is indicated by the liturgical manuals: **"Imam u shu vo atithimusharbudham..."**

<vocab>
अग्नि (Agni): The god of fire and mediator between gods and humans.
वीतहव्य (Vitahavya): The name of the sage or seer who "heard" this hymn.
भरद्वाज (Bharadvaja): A famous sage and the primary seer of the 6th Book of the Rig Veda.
जगती (Jagati): A classical Vedic meter.
शक्वरी (Shakvari): An elongated Vedic meter.
त्रिष्टुप् (Trishtubh): The most common Vedic meter, consisting of four lines of eleven syllables.
वर्ग (Varga): A small sectional division of the text.
सूक्त (Sukta): A Vedic hymn.
मन्त्र (Mantra): A sacred verse or chant.
भाष्य (Bhashya): A scholarly commentary, here by the 14th-century scholar Sayana.
</vocab>

--- Page 689 ---
<meta>Mandala 6, Anuvaka 1, Sukta 15, Verses 1-2. This page begins the 15th Hymn of the 6th Mandala. This hymn is historically attributed to the seer Bharadvaja or a king-seer named Vitahavya. The previous page concluded the 14th Hymn of this Mandala.</meta>

In the ritual prescriptions <note>original: "Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.23"</note>, it is stated: "On the fifth day of the Ten-night sacrifice, the recitation for the clarified butter <term>Ajyashastra</term> <note>A specific liturgical recitation performed by the Hotri priest</note> consists of nine verses." It is further indicated <note>original: "Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 7.12"</note>: "The new butter recitation begins with 'To this your guest, who wakes at dawn' <note>original: "imam u ṣu vo atithim"</note>."

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The First Verse ॥ <-

To this your guest, who wakes at dawn, the lord of all the people, [approach] with a straightforward song. Truly, by his very birth from heaven, the pure one comes; the child [of the wood] long consumes that which is unshakeable. ॥ १ ॥

**To this | indeed | well | your | guest | waking at dawn | of all | of the people | lord | straightforwardly | with a song |
He approaches | indeed | from heaven | by birth | somehow | even | hither | the pure one | for a long time | even | consumes | the child |
which | is unshakeable. ॥ १ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Sage **Vitahavya** or **Bharadvaja**, you yourself [worship]. <note>Note on grammar: There is an exchange of grammatical case and number in the original Sanskrit here.</note> **To this indeed**—to this very Agni—**with a song**, meaning with a hymn of praise, **straightforwardly** <note>original: "swañjase"</note> provide adornment or worship. **Yaska says: "Añjati" refers to the act of adorning or preparing.** <note>Yaska was an ancient grammarian who wrote the Nirukta.</note> What kind of Agni? He is the **guest** <note>original: "atithim"</note>, the one who travels constantly; or, he who is to be honored like a guest. He is **waking at dawn**, meaning he is awakened at the break of day. He is the **lord** or protector of **all the people** (the subjects). By his **birth**—by his very nature—the **pure**, stainless, and bright Agni **somehow** (at some time during the performance of the sacrifice) **from heaven** <note>original: "divaḥ"</note> **approaches**. The connection is: "at that time, provide the adornment." Thus adorned, Agni is the **child** <note>original: "garbhaḥ"</note>—existing like an embryo within the two friction-sticks <term>arani</term> <note>The wooden blocks used to churn fire</note>. Alternatively, he is the child of Heaven and Earth. **That which is unshakeable** <note>original: "achyutam"</note>, meaning the eternal substances like milk used for the daily fire-offering, he **consumes** or eats **for a long time**.

---

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

Whom the Bhrigus placed in the wood like a well-settled friend, the worshipful one with upward-tending flames—you, O wonderful one, well-pleased by the offerings of Vitahavya, are magnified day by day with excellent praises. ॥ २ ॥

**A friend | like | whom | well-placed | the Bhrigus | have set | in the wood | to be worshipped | whose radiance is upward |
He | you | well-pleased | in the one who has offered the oblation (Vitahavya) | O wonderful one | with praises | are magnified | day by day. ॥ २ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Whom the **Bhrigus**—the great ancient seers—**have set** or established in their homes, like a **friend** or a companion; that Agni who is **well-placed** within the **wood** (the friction-sticks), who is **to be worshipped** or praised, and who possesses **upward-tending flames** (lofty brilliance). O **wonderful** and great Agni, **he**—that very you—be **well-pleased** with the sage named **Vitahavya**. Because **day by day** (every day), you **are magnified** or honored with **praises**, that is, with excellent hymns. Since Vitahavya is among the Bharadvaja seers, the name "Vitahavya" can be understood here as "Bharadvaja, who has given the oblations."

--- Page 690 ---
<meta>This page continues the 15th Hymn of the 6th Mandala, focusing on Agni, the Fire God. The previous page introduced the hymn with its ritual context and the first two verses. This page contains verses 3, 4, and the start of 5, along with the traditional commentary by the 14th-century scholar Sayana.</meta>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Third Verse ॥ <-

**May you, a harmless protector, be the increaser of our ritual skill, the overcomer of the distant and the nearby enemy.**
**O Son of Strength, grant wealth and extensive shelter to Vitahavya among mortals, and to Bharadvaja wide-spread protection. ॥ ३ ॥**

**He | You | of ritual skill | harmless protector | increaser | be | of the enemy | of the distant | of the nearby | overcomer |**
**Wealth | O Son | of strength | among mortals | hither | shelter | grant | to Vitahavya | wide-spread | to Bharadvaja | wide-spread ॥ ३ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, you are such a one—a **harmless protector** <note>original: "avṛkaḥ," meaning one who does not injure or a protector who acts unlike a predatory wolf</note>. May you be the **increaser** <note>original: "vṛdhaḥ"</note> of the one who is **skilled in ritual** <note>original: "dakṣasya"</note>. You are also the **overcomer** <note>original: "taruṣaḥ," a conqueror or savior</note> of the **distant enemy** <note>original: "parasya aryaḥ"</note> and the **nearer enemy** who is close by. For this reason, O **Son of Strength** <note>original: "sahasaḥ sūno," a title for Agni because he is produced by the forceful friction of wooden sticks</note>, you who are **wide-spread** in all directions, grant **wealth** and **shelter** <note>original: "chardiḥ," meaning a house or protection</note> among human beings to **Bharadvaja**, who possesses food in the form of prepared oblations. This is also addressed to **Vitahavya** <note>original: "vītahavyāya," meaning 'he whose oblations have been offered' or referring to the king-seer of that name</note>. The repetition of the word **wide-spread** <note>original: "saprathaḥ"</note> is intended to show great respect.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Fourth Verse ॥ <-

**I glorify the shining one, your guest, the leader of heaven, Agni the invoker of Manu, the master of the good sacrifice.**
**Like a sage of brilliant words, I approach the carrier of oblations with excellent hymns, the immortal lord and god. ॥ ४ ॥**

**Shining | your | guest | leader of heaven | Agni | invoker | of Manu | of the good sacrifice |**
**Sage | like | of brilliant words | with excellent hymns | carrier of oblations | lord | god | I glorify. ॥ ४ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Vitahavya, with **excellent hymns** of praise, you should **glorify** <note>original: "ṛñjase," meaning to adorn, prepare, or gratify</note> the god Agni, the **carrier of oblations** to the heavens. What is Agni like? He is **shining** with light; he is your **guest**, worthy of honor like a visitor in one's home; he is the **leader of heaven** <note>original: "svarṇaram"</note>; the **invoker** <note>original: "hotāram," the priest who calls the gods</note> at the sacrifice of **Manu** <note>the ancestral father of humanity</note>; and the master of the **good sacrifice**. He is like a **wise sage** <note>original: "vipram"</note> whose speech is the very dwelling place of light (**brilliant-worded**). He is the **lord** <note>original: "aratim," an eternal manager or master</note> and the ageless god.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**With a purifying and conscious grace, like the dawn with its light, shining extensively on the earth...**
**Like the horse Etasha in his course, the ageless one who is never thirsty in the heat... ॥ ५ ॥**

<vocab>
Agni: The Vedic god of fire and transformation.
Bharadvaja: A famous ancient seer and the traditional author of the 6th book of the Rig Veda.
Vitahavya: A king or seer mentioned as the patron or composer of this hymn.
Daksha: Spiritual skill, willpower, or ritual ability.
Rayi: Material and spiritual wealth.
Chardis: A protective cover, specifically a house or secure shelter.
Atithi: A guest; Agni is often called the 'guest in every house' because of the domestic hearth.
Hotr: The primary invoking priest who recites the verses of the Rig Veda.
Dyukshavachas: One whose words are heavenly or filled with light.
</vocab>

<summary>This page contains verses 3-5 of Hymn 15, praising Agni as a protector, a guest, and a wise priest. The commentary identifies Agni's role in granting wealth and shelter to the seers Bharadvaja and Vitahavya.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Bharadvaja, Vitahavya, ritual skill, divine guest, wealth, protection, Vedic sacrifice, Son of Strength</keywords>

--- Page 691 ---
<meta>This page continues the commentary on the 15th Hymn of the 6th Mandala of the Rig Veda. It concludes the explanation for Verse 5 and provides the full text and commentary for Verse 6. The focus remains on Agni's dual nature as a cosmic light and a ritual fire.</meta>

## Hymn Text

**By the purifying [light], by the awakening light, he has shone upon the earth like the Dawn with her radiance; as if overcoming [enemies] in a march, [he helps] in the battle of Etasha; he who shines quickly, as if thirsty, the ageless one. ॥ ५ ॥**

**Purifying | who | awakening | by light | on the earth | has shone | of the dawn | like | with radiance |**
**Overcoming | like | in a march | of Etasha | quickly | in battle | hither | who | in heat/shining | like | thirsty | ageless ॥ ५ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

That Agni, with his **purifying** <note>original: "pāvakayā," meaning cleansing or sanctifying</note> and **awakening** <note>original: "citayantyā," that which makes one conscious or bestows wisdom</note> **light** <note>original: "kṛpā," beauty or luster</note>, **has shone** <note>original: "ruruce"</note> upon the **earth** <note>original: "kṣāman"</note>. **Like the Dawn with her radiance**—just as the Dawn shines with her own light, so does he. Furthermore, in a **march** <note>original: "yāman"</note> or a conflict, like a man **overcoming** <note>original: "tūrvan"</note> or striking down his enemies, Agni **quickly** <note>original: "nu"</note> **shines** <note>original: "āghṛṇe"</note> to assist in the **battle** <note>original: "raṇe"</note> of the sage named **Etasha** <note>original: "etaśasya"</note> against the Sun. *“And Etasha contended with the Sun”* <note>original: "praitaśaṃ sūrye paspṛdhānaṃ," quoting Rig Veda 1.61.15</note>—this is another Vedic citation for the same story. Surely all the gods provided him assistance there. And he who is **thirsty** <note>original: "tatṛṣāṇaḥ," meaning one who by his power tends to consume everything</note> and **ageless** <note>original: "ajaraḥ," free from decay</note>—this refers to that god described in the previous verse.

-> ॥ Thus ends the seventeenth section of the fifth chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**Serve Agni after Agni with fuel; [serve] your very dear guest, who is to be praised. Approach the immortal one with your songs; for he, the god among gods, accepts the precious gift; for he, the god among gods, accepts our service. ॥ ६ ॥**

**Pada-patha:**
**Agni | Agni | your | with fuel | serve | dear | dear | your | guest | who is to be praised |**
**Towards | your | with songs | the immortal | approach/serve | the god | among the gods | accepts | indeed | the precious | the god |**
**among the gods | accepts | indeed | our | service ॥ ६ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O our singers/praisers, **your** <note>original: "vaḥ"</note>—that is, you all—**serve** <note>original: "duvasyata," worship or attend to</note> **Agni after Agni** <note>original: "agnimagnim," indicating each individual fire or every ritual occasion</note>, and no other god. He is **your** very **dear** <note>original: "priyam priyam"</note> **guest** <note>original: "atithim," to be honored like a guest in the home</note> and **to be praised** <note>original: "gṛṇīṣaṇim," worthy of hymns</note>. Serve him **with fuel** <note>original: "samidhā," the act of kindling or with the sacrificial wood sticks</note>. Alternatively, "to be praised" could be interpreted as being the subject of the song itself. Furthermore, you all **approach and serve** <note>original: "vivāsata"</note> the **immortal** <note>original: "amṛtam"</note> Agni **with your songs** <note>original: "gīrbhiḥ"</note> or hymns. **For** <note>original: "hi"</note> among the **gods**, the **god** Agni, who possesses the quality of giving, **accepts** <note>original: "vanate," enjoys or partakes in</note> the **precious gift** <note>original: "vāryam," the desirable offerings like fuel and clarified butter</note>. **For** among the **gods**, the **god** Agni **accepts** <note>original: "vanate"</note> **our service** <note>original: "duvaḥ," our worshipful attendance</note>; therefore, the instruction is to "serve" him.

Regarding the ritual for the tenth day of the *Agni-maruta* ceremony, the triplet of verses beginning with **"Kindled"** <note>original: "samiddham"</note> serves as the invitation for the *Jatavedas* offering. As it is stated: *"The triplet 'Kindled is Agni, praise him with fuel and song'..."* <note>original: quoting the Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 8.12</note>.

<vocab>
**Agni**: The Fire God. | **Samidh**: Fuel or sacrificial wood. | **Atithi**: Guest (Agni is the guest of the house). | **Varya**: Desirable or precious offering. | **Duvasyata**: Worship or serve. | **Etasha**: A mythical horse or sage involved in a race with the Sun. | **Ushas**: The Goddess of Dawn. | **Jatavedas**: A common title for Agni meaning "knower of all births/beings."
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes verse 5, describing Agni's brilliance compared to the dawn and his aid in the myth of Etasha, and presents verse 6, which exhorts worshippers to serve Agni as a dear guest with fuel and hymns.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Etasha, Dawn, sacrifice, ritual fuel, hospitality, immortality, Sayana's commentary</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the text of the Rig Veda, specifically Mandala 4, Sukta 7. The previous page concluded with verse 6, describing Agni’s swift movement. This page contains verses 7, 8, and the beginning of 9, focusing on Agni's role as a divine priest, a protector of the people, and a messenger between the human and divine realms.</meta>

# Rig Veda: Book 4, Hymn 7, Verses 7–9

-> ## The seventh verse of the first hymn ## <-

I praise the well-kindled Agni with fuel and with song—the pure, the purifier, the steadfast one who stands at the front of the sacrifice. We approach the wise invoker, the much-desired, the harmless sage, the Knower of All Beings, with hymns of joy. ॥ ७ ॥

**Well-kindled | Agni | with fuel | with song | I praise | the pure | the purifier | in the front | at the sacrifice | the steadfast |**
**The wise | the invoker | the much-desired | the harmless | the sage | with joys/hymns | we approach | the Knower of All Beings ॥ ७ ॥**

---

## Commentary by Sayana

I praise (**grṇe**) the **well-kindled** <note>original: "samiddhaṃ," meaning thoroughly ignited or blazing</note> Agni with a **song** <note>original: "girā"</note> of praise that serves as the cause for his kindling. Alternatively, I praise him who is **well-kindled** by the **fuel** <note>original: "samidhā," referring to the wooden logs</note> of the altar. Furthermore, I place in front of me at the **sacrifice** <note>original: "adhvare"</note> that Agni who is **pure** in himself, the **purifier** <note>original: "pāvakaṃ," the one who cleanses all things</note>, and **steadfast** or unwavering. 

In this same way, we **approach** <note>original: "īmahe," meaning we worship or seek out</note> Agni, the **wise** <note>original: "vipraṃ," the inspired sage</note>, the **invoker** <note>original: "hotāraṃ," the priest who calls the gods</note>, the **much-desired** <note>original: "puruvāram," one who should be chosen by many</note>, the **harmless** <note>original: "aduham," one who does not betray or harm, being favorable to all</note>, the **sage** <note>original: "kaviṃ," the seer who looks beyond</note>, and the **Knower of All Beings** <note>original: "jātavedasam," he who knows everything that is born</note>. We do this with **joys** <note>original: "sumnaiḥ"</note>, meaning with hymns that produce happiness. Alternatively, using the third case in place of the second, it means: we ask for "joys," meaning we pray for wealth.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ## Now the eighth ## <-

O Agni, gods and mortals alike have established you as the immortal messenger in every age, the bearer of oblations, the protector, and the one worthy of praise. They have approached with reverence the ever-wakeful, all-pervading Lord of the People. ॥ ८ ॥

**You | messenger | O Agni | immortal | in age after age | bearer of oblations | they have established | protector | worthy of praise |**
**The gods | and | mortals | and | the ever-wakeful | the all-pervading | the Lord of the People | with reverence | they | have approached ॥ ८ ॥**

---

## Commentary by Sayana

O Agni, both **gods** <note>original: "devāso"</note> and **mortals** <note>original: "martāso," meaning human beings</note> have **established** <note>original: "dadhire"</note> you as their **messenger**. What kind of messenger? You are the **immortal** one, and **in age after age** <note>original: "yuge yuge," at every time of performing the sacrifice</note>, you are the **bearer of oblations** <note>original: "havyavāhaṃ," the one who carries the sacrificial offerings to the gods</note>, the **protector** <note>original: "pāyuṃ," the guardian</note>, and the one **worthy of praise**. 

Furthermore, both groups have **approached** <note>original: "niṣedire," sat down near or attended upon</note> that Agni who is **ever-wakeful** <note>original: "jāgrviṃ," meaning ever-vigilant</note>, **all-pervading** <note>original: "vibhuṃ," present everywhere</note>, and the **Lord of the People** <note>original: "viśvapatim," the protector of all subjects</note>. They approach you with **reverence** <note>original: "namasā," either through bowing or by offering food in the form of oblations</note>.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ## Now the ninth ## <-

Adorning both realms, O Agni, according to the sacred laws, you travel as the messenger of the gods between the two worlds. Since we choose your prayer and your favor, then be a triple-shelter and a source of bliss for us. ॥ ९ ॥

<note>The commentary for this verse is not present on this page, but the vocabulary and mantra text are provided.</note>

<term>Jatavedas (जातेवेदस्): A common name for Agni. It literally means "he who knows all that is born" or "he in whom all wisdom is found," emphasizing the fire-god's role as a witness to all human actions and a source of divine knowledge.</term>

<summary>This page translates verses 7 and 8 of Hymn 7 in the 4th Book, where Agni is praised as a wise, immortal messenger and priest who serves both gods and humans. It highlights his dual role as a consumer of fuel and a source of spiritual wisdom for the sacrificer.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Vedic sacrifice, Jatavedas, messenger, immortal, priest, ritual fuel, protector, Lord of the People</keywords>

# [Mandala 6. Hymn 15. Verse 15.] || Fourth Book || 625

## Hymn Text

**[Rig Veda 6.15.9 Word-by-Word Analysis]**
> Adorning | O Agni | both | the cosmic order | the laws | messenger | of the gods | the two regions | together | you traverse |
> Since | your | sacred work | good favor | we choose | then | indeed | for us | triple-sheltering | auspicious | become ॥ ९ ॥

---

## Commentary by Sayana

O Agni, **adorning** <note>original: "vibhūṣan," meaning especially decorating or honoring</note> **both** types—that is, both gods and men—you **traverse** <note>original: "samīyase," you move through</note> the **two regions** <note>the earth and the sky</note> as the **messenger of the gods** during the **laws** <note>original: "vratā," referring here to the sacred works or sacrifices</note>. You go to the heavenly world to bring the gods here, and you move in this world to carry the offerings to them. Furthermore, **since** <note>original: "yat"</note> we **choose** or participate in the **sacred work** <note>original: "dhītim," here interpreted as the ritual action</note> and the **good favor** <note>original: "sumatim," meaning a beautiful song of praise</note> intended for you, for that reason, may you, who are **triple-sheltering** <note>original: "trivarūthaḥ," meaning one who exists in three places or provides three-fold protection</note>, **become auspicious** <note>original: "śivaḥ," the bringer of happiness</note> to us. The word "sma" in the text is a <term>particle (pada-pūraṇa)</term> used to complete the meter of the verse.

In the ritual context of the <term>Prātaranuvāka</term> <note>the morning litany</note> and the <term>Āśvina-śastra</term> <note>the recitation for the twin gods, the Ashvins</note>, within the Agni-related portion of the rite performed in the <term>Triṣṭubh</term> meter, these six verses beginning with "Him of beautiful form" are used. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "Him of beautiful form, these six" (Aśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.13).

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here begins the tenth verse of the hymn ॥ <-

**[Rig Veda 6.15.10 Original Verse]**
Him of beautiful form, fair to look upon, moving gracefully, though we are ignorant, we serve him who is most wise. May he, Agni, knowing all the ways, offer the sacrifice; may he announce our oblation among the immortals. ॥ १० ॥

**[Rig Veda 6.15.10 Word-by-Word Analysis]**
Him | beautiful-formed | fair-to-look-upon | moving-gracefully | the ignorant | the-most-wise | we serve |
He | may sacrifice | all | ways/wisdoms | knowing | forth | the offering | Agni | among the immortals | may speak ॥ १० ॥

---

## Commentary by Sayana

We, who are **ignorant** <note>original: "avidvāṃsaḥ," lacking deep knowledge or of small intellect</note>, **serve** <note>original: "sapema," we worship or attend to</note> that Agni who is **most wise** <note>original: "viduṣṭaram," the most all-knowing</note>. What is he like? He is of **beautiful form** <note>original: "supratīkam," having handsome limbs</note>, **fair to look upon**, and **moving gracefully** <note>original: "svañcam," one who travels well</note>. Furthermore, may such an Agni **sacrifice** to the gods. **Knowing** all **ways** <note>original: "vuyunāni," usually meaning wisdom, but here referring to the "things to be known"</note>, may **Agni announce** our **offering** among the **immortals** <note>original: "amṛteṣu," the gods who do not die</note>. Let him say: "The oblation is prepared for your sake, therefore come."

-> ॥ This ends the eighteenth section (varga) of the fifth chapter (adhyāya) of the fourth book (aṣṭaka) ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the eleventh verse ॥ <-

**[Rig Veda 6.15.11 Original Verse]**
O Agni, you protect and you also bring across the one who offers prayer to you, O Hero, for the sake of the singer. Whether it be the sharpening of the sacrifice or its rising, you join him with strength and with wealth. ॥ ११ ॥

---

<keywords>Agni, Sayana, Rig Veda, sacrifice, messenger, immortals, Prātaranuvāka, ritual commentary</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Rig Veda, Mandala 6, Hymn 15. The previous page (625) concluded the commentary on Verse 10 and began the word-by-word analysis of Verse 11. This page completes the explanation of Verse 11, provides the full text and commentary for Verse 12, and introduces Verse 13 with its specific ritual applications (Viniyoga).</meta>

# [Rig Veda] || [Ashtaka 4, Adhyaya 5, Varga 19] 626

## Hymn Text

<note>Rig Veda 6.15.11 Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha)</note>
Him | O Agni | you protect | and | him | you deliver | who | to you | has reached | for the wise one | O Hero | prayer | of sacrifice | or | refinement | or | rising | or | him | indeed | you fill | with strength | and | with wealth ॥ ११ ॥

---

->|| Now the Twelfth Verse ||<-

You, O Agni, protect us from the attacker; you, O Mighty One, protect us from blame. May the food-offering, free from all defects, reach you; may wealth, consisting of thousands and greatly desired, come to us ॥ १२ ॥

<note>Rig Veda 6.15.12 Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha)</note>
You | O Agni | from the attacker | thoroughly | protect | you | indeed | us | O Mighty One | from blame | together | you | possessing destruction | towards | may it go | the food-offering | together | wealth | desirable | consisting of thousands ॥ १२ ॥

---

->|| This is the Thirteenth Verse in the Hymn ||<-

Agni is the Priest, the Master of the house, he is the King; he, the Knower of All Births, knows all generations. He who is the most skilled sacrificer among both gods and mortals, may he, the observer of Truth, perform the sacrifice ॥ १३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, you **protect** <note>original: "pāsi"</note> that man. Moreover, you **fill** <note>original: "piparṣi," meaning to satisfy or fulfill with desires</note> him. That man who, O **Hero** <note>original: "śūra," meaning one possessing valor</note> Agni, performs for you—who are the **wise one** <note>original: "kavaye," the one with transcendent vision</note>—the **prayer** <note>original: "dhītiṃ," meaning the ritual work or song of praise</note> and thereby **reaches** <note>original: "ānaṭ," attains or approaches</note> you. Alternatively, the commentator notes a grammatical variation where the fourth case <term>dative</term> is used for the agent: "The one who possesses prayer makes it reach you, the wise one." You protect him; this is the connection. Furthermore, whether it is the **refinement** <note>original: "niśitiṃ," the preparation or consecration</note> of the **sacrifice** <note>original: "yajñasya"</note> or of the oblation which is the means of that sacrifice, or the **rising** <note>original: "uditim," the upward progress of the ritual</note> that he makes reach you, you **fill** <note>original: "pṛṇakṣi," satisfy</note> that very person with **strength** <note>original: "śavasā," power</note>. And you also fill him with **wealth** <note>original: "rāyā," riches</note>.

---

O Agni, do you **thoroughly protect** <note>original: "ni rakṣa"</note> us from the **attacker** <note>original: "vanuṣyataḥ," the injurious enemy</note>. O **Mighty One** <note>original: "sahasāvan," O powerful Agni</note>, you alone protect us from **blame** <note>original: "avadyāt," from sin or reproach</note>. May the **food-offering** <note>original: "pāthaḥ," specifically the sacrificial oblation</note> given by us, which is **free from defects** <note>original: "dhvasmanvat," literally 'possessing destruction' of flaws, meaning purified</note>, **reach** <note>original: "samabhyetu," go well toward</note> you. And may **wealth** <note>original: "rayiḥ"</note> that is **desirable** <note>original: "spṛhayāyyaḥ"</note> and **consisting of thousands** <note>original: "sahasrī," meaning a great quantity</note>, given by you, come to us perfectly.

In the **Ten-Night Sacrifice** <note>original: "Vyūḷha Daśarātra," a complex Vedic ritual lasting ten days</note>, on the fifth day, during the litany for Agni and the Maruts, the triplet of verses beginning with "Agni is the Priest" (6.15.13) is used as the portion for <term>Jatavedas</term>. This is indicated in the **Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra** (8.8): "Agni is the Priest, the Master of the house, he is the King—these three verses." Also, in the **Offerings to the Wives of the Gods** <note>original: "Patnī-saṃyāja"</note>, the first verse of this triplet is used for the 'Master of the House' invocation. This is indicated in the Sutras (1.10): "Agni is the Priest, the Master of the house... these are the offerings for the wives." It is also the beginning of the **Litany to the Ashvins** <note>original: "Āśvina-śastra"</note>. This is indicated (6.5): "Agni is the Priest... is the starting verse, recited foot by foot."

<vocab>Agni: the sacred fire and mediator between gods and humans</vocab>
<vocab>Yajna: the Vedic sacrificial ritual</vocab>
<vocab>Hotar: the primary priest who recites the Rig Veda</vocab>
<vocab>Grihapati: 'Lord of the House,' a title for Agni as the protector of the domestic hearth</vocab>
<vocab>Jatavedas: 'Knower of all births,' an epithet of Agni signifying his omniscience</vocab>
<vocab>Rayi: wealth or prosperity, often sought through ritual</vocab>
<vocab>Shavas: heroic strength or vital force</vocab>
<vocab>Nishiti: the sharpening, refinement, or preparation of a ritual element</vocab>
<vocab>Patnisamyaja: specific offerings made to the wives of the gods at the end of a sacrifice</vocab>
<vocab>Ashvinashastra: a long recitation dedicated to the twin Ashvin deities during the pre-dawn ritual</vocab>
<vocab>Vyulha: a specific 'shifted' arrangement of meters and deities in a multi-day sacrifice</vocab>
