# Rig Veda || Book 4. Chapter 4. Verse-group 1. || 782

## Commentary (Sayana)
<note>Continued from previous page - Commentary on Rig Veda 4.2.1</note>

The word "you" <note>original: "vaḥ"</note> is to be understood as following this. You all perform the praise. We too shall praise that Agni. The repetition of the word "forth" <note>original: "pra"</note> in the phrase "greatly delighted" is for the purpose of completing the meter <note>term: "pādapūraṇa" — a common Vedic technique where syllables or words are added or repeated to satisfy the rhythmic requirements of the verse</note>. There is a shift in number to the singular here. It uses the Vedic past tense <note>original: "luṅ"</note>. We praise him. Of what kind? Him who is immortal <note>original: "amṛtaṃ"</note>, meaning free from death; the "Knower of Beings" <note>term: "jātavedas" — a title for Agni implying he knows all created things, possesses innate wisdom, or is the possessor of wealth</note>; and like a friend <note>original: "mitraṃ na"</note>, who is dear and favorable. 

Alternatively, by grammatical substitution, the word "you" <note>original: "tvam"</note> stands in place of "to you." The word "to Agni" is in the dative case to indicate the object of the action. The word "and" <note>original: "ca"</note> and the particle "if" <note>original: "cet"</note> are used in the sense of a condition. The word "you prosper" <note>original: "dakṣase"</note> is a verbal form from the root "dakṣ," meaning to grow or increase, used here in the sense of causing someone else to increase. Because of the connection with the particle "if," the usual loss of accent is prohibited. 

The meaning is this: O Singer of praises! If you, in sacrifice after sacrifice, increase this Agni with your song of praise, then we too shall praise him who possesses qualities such as immortality.

---

-> || Now the Second Verse || <-

## Hymn Text
<note>RV 4.2.2</note>

O **Son of Strength**! Truly, this one who desires us—him we serve for the **giving of oblations**. May he be the **protector** in battles; may he be our **increaser**, and also the **savior** of our **bodies**. ॥ 2 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Son of Strength** <note>original: "ūrjo napātam"</note>; **He** <note>original: "saḥ"</note>; **Truly** <note>original: "hina"</note>; **This one** <note>original: "ayam"</note>; **Desiring us** <note>original: "asmayuḥ"</note>; **May we serve** <note>original: "dāśema"</note>; **For the giving of oblations** <note>original: "havya-dātaye"</note>; **May he be** <note>original: "bhuvat"</note>; **In battles** <note>original: "vājeṣu"</note>; **Protector** <note>original: "avitā"</note>; **May he be** <note>original: "bhuvat"</note>; **Increaser** <note>original: "vṛdhaḥ"</note>; **And** <note>original: "uta"</note>; **Savior** <note>original: "trātā"</note>; **Of bodies/descendants** <note>original: "tanūnām"</note>. ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

We should praise the "Son of Strength"—either the son of food or the son of physical power <note>note: Agni is called the Son of Strength because fire is generated by the forceful friction of wooden sticks</note>. The two particles "hi" and "na" combined here carry the meaning of "truly." This Agni indeed becomes one who desires us. And we shall serve that Agni, the giver of offerings to the gods, for the purpose of the "giving of oblations." We should offer the sacrificial materials. And may that Agni be a protector in "plenitudes," meaning in battles, and may he be our increaser. Furthermore, may he be the savior of our "bodies," meaning our children and our descendants.

---

-> || Now the Third Verse || <-

## Hymn Text
<note>RV 4.2.3</note>

For you, O **Agni**, are the **showerer**, **ageless**, and **great**; you **shine** with your **flame**. Glowing with **perpetual light**, O **pure one**, **shine brightly** with your **beautiful rays**. ॥ 3 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Showerer** <note>original: "vṛṣā"</note>; **For** <note>original: "hi"</note>; **O Agni** <note>original: "agne"</note>; **Ageless** <note>original: "ajaraḥ"</note>; **Great** <note>original: "mahān"</note>; **You shine** <note>original: "vi-bhāsi"</note>; **With flame** <note>original: "arciṣā"</note>; **With perpetual** <note>original: "ajasreṇa"</note>; **With light** <note>original: "śociṣā"</note>; **Glowing** <note>original: "śośucat"</note>; **O pure one** <note>original: "śuce"</note>; **With beautiful rays** <note>original: "su-dītibhiḥ"</note>; **Well** <note>original: "su"</note>; **Shine** <note>original: "dīdihi"</note>. ॥ 3 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni! You are the "Showerer," the one who rains down the fulfillment of desires, or the one who causes rain. You are ageless, free from decay, and great in your many qualities. Being such as you are, you truly shine with your light. You illuminate in a special way. O pure one...

<note>interpretive: The vocabulary list below defines the key technical terms used in the Sanskrit original.</note>
**Agni**: The Fire-God and mediator between gods and humans.
**Son of Strength** <note>original: "Urjo napat"</note>: A common epithet for Agni, referring to his birth from friction.
**Showerer/Strong** <note>original: "Vṛṣan"</note>: An epithet meaning one who possesses virile power or showers blessings like rain.
**Knower of Beings** <note>original: "Jatavedas"</note>: A title for Agni as the all-knowing witness.
**Giving of oblations** <note>original: "Havyadati"</note>: The ritual act of offering food or clarified butter into the fire.
**Battle/Plenitude** <note>original: "Vaja"</note>: A term that can mean physical battle or the prize/food won in such a struggle.
**Sayana's Commentary** <note>original: "Sayana Bhashya"</note>: The 14th-century authoritative interpretation of the Vedas.

It emphasizes Agni's role as a protective, immortal force produced through ritual effort ("Son of Strength") who guards the family and descendants of the worshiper.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Rig-Veda-Sanhita commentary. The previous page concluded the explanation of the third verse of Hymn 48 in the sixth Mandala. This page presents verses 4 and 5, focusing on Agni’s role as the divine priest who brings other gods to the ritual and his physical manifestation through the elements and human effort.</meta>

# Book 6. Chapter 4. Hymn 48. || The Fourth Book (Ashtaka) || 743

O Agni, shine brilliantly and beautifully with your unfailing and continuous light. Illuminate us well; bring us light.

-> || Now the fourth [verse] || <-

## Hymn Text
You worship the great gods in succession through your wisdom and your wondrous deed. O Agni, bring them here to us for our protection; bestow riches upon them and take your share of the offerings. || 4 ||

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
Great. Gods. You worship. Worship. In succession. Your. Through wisdom. And. Wondrous deed.
Hither-turning. [Particle of emphasis]. Make. O Agni. For protection. Bestow. Riches. And. Enjoy/Accept. || 4 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, you **worship the great gods** <note>original: "maho devānyajasi"</note>. You honor them with oblations at the sacrifice of the patrons. Therefore, at our sacrifice as well, **worship** <note>original: "yakṣi"</note> them in a way that is **continuous** <note>term: "ānuṣak" — meaning uninterrupted or in proper sequence</note>. Worship those gods! To achieve that, use **your wisdom** <note>original: "kratvā"</note> and also your **wondrous deed** <note>original: "daṃsanā"</note> or ritual action. The word **"seem"** <note>original: "sīm"</note> is used here as a particle to encompass all. **Make** <note>original: "kṛṇuhi"</note> all those gods **face toward us** <note>original: "arvācaḥ"</note> for **our protection**. Furthermore, **bestow** <note>original: "rāsva"</note> **riches** <note>original: "vājān"</note>—specifically the food characterized by sacrificial offerings—upon them. And you, too, **accept** <note>original: "vaṃsva"</note>; enjoy the offerings that have been presented to you.

-> || Now the fifth [verse] || <-

## Hymn Text
Whom the waters, the stones, and the woods nourish as the womb of the sacred order; who is born from the earth's summit when rubbed with strength by the priests. || 5 ||

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
Whom. Waters. Stones. Woods. Embryo/Womb. Of the sacred order/Truth. Nourish.
With strength. Who. Rubbed/Churned. Is born. By men. Of the earth. Upon. The summit. || 5 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **waters** <note>term: "vasativarī" — specifically the waters collected on the previous day and kept overnight for the Soma ritual</note>, the **stones** <note>original: "adrayaḥ" — the stones used to press the Soma juice</note>, and the **woods** <note>original: "vanā" — the wooden sticks used for fuel</note> **nourish** or fill that Agni who resides within them like an **embryo** <note>original: "garbham"</note> of the sacrifice <note>original: "ṛtasya"</note> or of the water itself. 

Alternatively, the waters of the ocean, the clouds <note>original: "adrayaḥ"</note>, and the forests nourish Agni as he exists in the form of the submarine fire, the lightning, and the forest fire. This Agni is **born** or manifested **upon the summit** <note>original: "sānau"</note> of the **earth**, meaning the elevated and excellent place of sacrifice, when he is **rubbed** <note>note: This refers to the ancient practice of generating fire by vigorously rubbing two wooden sticks (aranis) together</note> with **strength** by the **men**—that is, the guiding priests. The instruction is that you, Agni, should then enjoy the offerings. Or, this verse connects back to the previous request to "bestow and enjoy."

-> || Thus ends the first Varga of the eighth Adhyaya of the fourth Ashtaka || <-

<summary>This page contains verses 4 and 5 of Rig Veda 6.48, where Agni is praised as the mediator who brings gods to the sacrifice and is described as the "embryo" of nature (water, stones, wood) brought forth by the priests' labor.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, sacrifice, Vasativari waters, fire-churning, Sayana, Vedic ritual, priesthood</keywords>

# Book 4. Chapter 8. || The Fourth Book (Ashtaka) || 794
### || Rig Veda ||

-> **|| Now the Sixth [Verse] ||** <-

## Hymn Text

He who has filled both portions of the world <note>original: "rodasī", referring to Heaven and Earth</note> with his radiance, now rushes through the sky with his smoke. He is seen through the darkness in the dusky nights—the bright, strong showerer of benefits; the bright, strong showerer of benefits. || 6 ||

**He. Who. Filled. With radiance. Both worlds. Both. With smoke. Rushes. In the sky.**
**Through. Darkness. Is seen. In the nights. [Particle of emphasis]. In the dusky [nights]. The bright one. The showerer. [Particle of emphasis]. The dusky [ones]. The bright one. The showerer. || 6 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

This Agni fills **both worlds** <note>original: "rodasī"</note>, meaning Heaven and Earth, with his **radiance** <note>original: "bhānunā"</note> or light. He **rushes** <note>original: "dhāvate"</note> or travels through the **sky** <note>original: "divi"</note>—the atmosphere—by means of his smoke. Indeed, smoke is seen to travel through the atmosphere, having been transformed into the nature of clouds. Because the cause (fire) and the effect (smoke/clouds) are considered non-different in this poetic context, this movement is attributed to Agni himself.

Furthermore, this **bright one** <note>original: "aruṣaḥ"</note>, who shines brilliantly, is a **showerer** <note>original: "vṛṣā"</note>, meaning one who rains down or fulfills all desires. Agni, possessing such qualities, is **seen** <note>original: "dadṛśe"</note> everywhere after having **pushed aside** <note>original: "tiraskṛtya"</note> the **darkness** <note>original: "tamo"</note> in the **dusky** <note>original: "śyāvāsu"</note> or dark-colored **nights** <note>term: "ūrmyāsu" — an ancient word for night</note>. He remains present during these dark nights. The repetition of the phrase "the bright showerer" is intended either to show great **respect** <note>original: "ādarārthā"</note> or simply to complete the rhythmic structure of the verse.

---

-> **|| Now the Seventh [Verse] ||** <-

## Hymn Text

O Agni, with your great flames and your bright, holy glow, O God, being kindled for the protector of riches <note>original: "bharadvāje"</note>, O youngest one, shine wealthily upon us; O bright one, shine brilliantly; O purifier, shine! || 7 ||

**With great. O Agni. With flames. With bright. O God. With glow.**
**In the protector of riches / For Bharadvaja. Being kindled. O youngest one. Wealthily. For us. O bright one. Shine. Brilliantly. O purifier. Shine. || 7 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **God** <note>original: "deva"</note>, you who are endowed with the qualities of giving, O **youngest one** <note>term: "yaviṣṭhya" — literally 'most youthful,' referring to fire being reborn fresh each time it is lit</note>, O **bright one** <note>original: "śukra"</note> whose tip is radiant! You are **being kindled** <note>original: "samidhānaḥ"</note> for **Bharadvaja** <note>note: Sayana interprets this as "our brother/kinsman" or the patron of the sacrifice</note>. With your **flawless glow** <note>original: "śociṣā"</note> and your **great flames** <note>original: "bṛhadbhirarcibhiḥ"</note>, please **shine** <note>original: "dīdihi"</note> for our sake in a way that is **wealthy** <note>original: "revat"</note> or full of riches. Likewise, O **purifier** <note>original: "pāvaka"</note>, O Agni who cleanses, shine in a way that is joined with **brilliance** <note>original: "dyumat"</note> or light.

<summary>These verses describe Agni's physical manifestation as smoke rising to the sky and light piercing the dark of night, while requesting that he bring wealth and purity to the patron of the sacrifice.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, light and smoke, night, darkness, Bharadvaja, ritual fire, wealth, purification</keywords>

# Mandala 6. Chapter 4. Hymn 48. || The Fourth Book (Ashtaka) || 715

## Hymn Text (Verse 8)

->॥ Now the Eighth [Verse] ॥<-

O Agni, you are the lord of the house <term>Grhapati: the master of the household and the guardian of the domestic fire</term> for all the human tribes. O youngest one <note>original: "yaviṣṭha," an epithet for Agni as the fire is newly kindled each time</note>, protect the one who kindles the fire from sin with a hundred forts <note>meaning a hundredfold protection</note> for a hundred winters <note>original: "śataṃ himāḥ," a traditional Vedic wish for a long life of 100 years</note>, and protect those who give wealth to the chanters. || 8 ||

**Pada-patha (Word-for-word breakdown):**
**Of all. Lord of the house. Of the tribes. You are. You. O Agni. Of humans.**
**A hundred. With forts. O youngest one. Protect. From sin. The kindler. A hundred. Winters. For the chanters.**
**Who. And. They give. || 8 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, you **are the lord of the house** <note>original: "gṛhapatiḥ"</note>; you are the master of the home for **all** the **human** <note>original: "mānuṣīṇām"</note> tribes, who are the descendants of the first man, Manu. O **youngest one** <note>original: "yaviṣṭha"</note>, ever-youthful Agni, therefore **protect** <note>original: "pāhi"</note> me—the **kindler** <note>original: "samiddhāram"</note> who has properly ignited you—for **a hundred winters** <note>original: "śataṃ himāḥ"</note>, meaning a hundred years, with a **hundred** <note>original: "śatam"</note> **forts** <note>original: "pūrbhiḥ"</note> or various means of protection, from **sin** <note>original: "aṃhasaḥ"</note>, which may refer to moral failing or a destructive enemy. **And** also protect those **who give** wealth **to the chanters** <note>original: "stotṛbhyaḥ"</note>, providing the means for those who perform your kindling and praise.

---

## Hymn Text (Verse 9)

->॥ Now the Ninth [Verse] ॥<-

You, O wonderful one, with your protection, O Vasu <note>Agni as the "Dweller" or "Giver of Habitation"</note>, impel riches toward us. O Agni, you are the leader <note>original: "rathīḥ," literally a charioteer</note> of this wealth; quickly find a firm foundation for our offspring. || 9 ||

**Pada-patha (Word-for-word breakdown):**
**You. Us. Wonderful. With protection. O Vasu. Riches. Impel.**
**Of this. Of wealth. You. O Agni. The leader. You are. Find. A firm foundation. For the offspring. Indeed. Us. || 9 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Vasu** <note>original: "vaso"</note>, Agni who causes all to dwell, you are **wonderful** <note>original: "citra"</note> or beautiful to behold; with your **protection** <note>original: "ūtyā"</note>, **impel** <note>original: "codaya"</note> or send **riches** <note>original: "rādhāṃsi"</note> **to us**. **You are the leader** <note>original: "rathīr-asi"</note>, the one who guides and directs **this wealth** <note>original: "asya rāyaḥ"</note> that is seen throughout the world. Therefore, the meaning is: "bestow riches upon us." Furthermore, for **our offspring** <note>original: "tuce"</note>—this is a term for children and descendants—for those sons and progeny who prevent the decline of our lineage, **find** <note>original: "vidāḥ"</note> or establish a **firm foundation** <note>original: "gādham"</note> **quickly** <note>original: "tu"</note>.

---

## Hymn Text (Verse 10)

->॥ Now the Tenth [Verse] ॥<-

Deliver our children and descendants, you, with protectors that are undeceivable and unwearied. O Agni, ward off from us the divine wraths and the ungodly harms. || 10 ||

**Pada-patha (Word-for-word breakdown):**
**Deliver. Child. Descendant. With protectors. You. With undeceivable [ones]. With unwearied [ones].**
**O Agni. Wraths. Divine. Ward off. From us. Ungodly. Harms. And. || 10 ||**

This hymn is dedicated to various deities; these specific verses transition from Agni (the Fire) to the Maruts (the Storm Gods) and the symbolic "Cow" of ritual and speech.</meta>

<header>॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Book 4. Chapter 8. Varga 3.]</header>

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, with your **unassailable** <note>original: "adabdhaiḥ," meaning not harmed by anyone</note> and **non-negligent** <note>original: "aprayutvabhiḥ"</note> protections—the word "yauti" here is used in the sense of "separation," so these are "not separated" or "joined" means of protection—**protect** <note>original: "parṣi"</note> our **son** <note>original: "tokam"</note> and our **grandson** <note>original: "tanayam"</note>. **Separate** <note>original: "yuyodhi," drive away</note> from us the **divine** <note>original: "daivyā"</note> **wraths** <note>original: "heḷāṃsi"</note> or angers, and also separate from us the **non-divine** <note>original: "adevāni"</note> or human-related **injuries** <note>original: "hvarāṃsi"</note> and harms.

->॥ This ends the second Varga of the eighth Adhyaya in the fourth Ashtaka ॥<-

---

->॥ Now the Eleventh [Verse] ॥<-

## Hymn Text

O friends, drive the milk-yielding cow [toward us] with a newer song; release her, the unyielding one. || 11 ||

**Padapatha:**
**Hither. O friends. The nectar-yielder. The cow. Drive. Toward. With a newer. Word.**
**Release. The un-strikable. || 11 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **friends** <note>original: "sakhāyaḥ," referring to the Adhvaryu priests of equal status</note>, **drive** <note>original: "ājadhvam," bring toward us or obtain</note> the **milk-yielding** <note>original: "sabardughāṃ"</note> cow. The word "Sabar" is a name for milk; she is the milker of the milk that is the cause of immortality. By what means? With a **newer** <note>original: "navyasa"</note> **word** <note>original: "vacaḥ," a song or sound in the form of an invitation</note>. After that, **release** <note>original: "upasṛjadhvam"</note>—meaning bring the calf to—that **un-strikable** <note>original: "anapasphurām"</note> cow. The root "sphurati" refers to the act of killing or striking; thus, she is not to be struck away. The implied meaning is that the milk is being drawn for a sacrifice to the Maruts.

Alternatively, the "Cow" is the mother of the Maruts named **Prishni** <note>the speckled cloud-cow of Vedic mythology</note>, or the Voice of the intermediate realm. O friends, you chanters, approach Prishni, the cow who milks the moisture that brings the Maruts into being, with a newer song of praise. Release her from her bonds. If such is the great cow, the mother of the Maruts, what then can be said of their own greatness? Thus, this is a praise of the **Maruts** <term>Maruts: Storm deities who are the sons of the cow-goddess Prishni and Rudra</term>.

---

->॥ Now the Twelfth [Verse] ॥<-

## Hymn Text

She who milked the immortal food for the self-shining Marut host; she who is in the favor of the rushing Maruts; she who comes with blessings. || 12 ||

<note>Note: The Samhita text above follows the printed version with accentuation.</note>

**Padapatha:**
**She who. For the host. Of the Maruts. Self-shining. Food. Immortal. Milked.**
**She who. In the favor. Of the Maruts. Of the rushing. She who. With blessings. Coming. || 12 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**She who**—the cow—**milked** <note>original: "adhukṣat"</note> the **immortal** <note>original: "amṛtyu"</note> **food** <note>original: "arvaḥ," characterized by milk</note> for the **Marut host** <note>original: "mārutāya śardhāya"</note>. What kind of host? One that is **powerful** <note>original: "śardhāya," possessing the nature of overcoming</note> and **self-shining** <note>original: "svabhānave," possessing self-dependent light</note>. And she who...

<vocab>
- **Agni**: The Fire deity, primary mediator between gods and humans.
- **Marut**: The Storm deities, known for their collective power and brilliance.
- **Sabardugha**: Yielding "Sabar" (nectar or milk); a term for a cow that provides the substance of immortality.
- **Dhenu**: A cow, frequently used in the Vedas as a symbol for Earth, Speech, or Ritual Plenty.
- **Vacas**: A word, hymn, or ritual sound.
- **Prishni**: The mythological mother of the Maruts, often envisioned as a brindled or speckled cow representing the rain-cloud.
</vocab>

<header>Mandala 6. Adhyaya 4. Sukta 48. | ॥ Fourth Ashtaka ॥</header>

## Commentary (Sayana) - Continued

She <note>the symbolic cow, representing rain or ritual speech</note> remains intent on the **grace** <note>original: "mṛḷīke," meaning happiness or favor</note> of the **quick-acting** <note>original: "turāṇām"</note> **Maruts** <note>the storm-gods</note>. She who travels with the **fast-moving** <note>original: "evayāvarbiḥ"</note> horses, or perhaps with the waters of the middle region, arrives with **rain-waters** <note>original: "vṛṣṭijalaiḥ"</note> for the sake of others' happiness. The previous instruction to "drive that cow hither" applies here as well. This should be understood as a further praise of the Maruts.

---

-> ॥ Now the Thirteenth [Verse] ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
For Bharadvaja, you have milked twice hither the cow that yields all and the food that nourishes all. || 13 ||

**Padapatha:**
**For Bharadvaja. Hither. Milked. Twice.**
**The cow. And. The all-yielding. The food. And. The all-nourishing. || 13 ||**

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Maruts**, for our **seer** <note>original: "ṛṣaye"</note> **Bharadvaja**, you have **milked** <note>original: "avadhukṣata"</note> a **duality** <note>original: "dvitā," referring to two specific boons</note>. What is this duality? It is the **cow** <note>original: "धेनुं"</note> and the **food** <note>original: "इषं"</note>. What kind of cow? One that is **all-yielding** <note>original: "viśvadohasam," milking everything that is pervasive and abundant</note>. What kind of food? That which is **all-nourishing** <note>original: "viśvabhojasam," sufficient for the enjoyment of all</note>.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fourteenth [Verse] ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
I praise that [host] of yours for the assignment [of wealth], like Indra of good deeds, like Varuna the wise, like Aryaman the delightful, and like Vishnu the great provider. || 14 ||

**Padapatha:**
**That. Your. Indra. Like. Of good deeds. Varuna. Like. The wise.**
**Aryaman. Like. Delightful. The great provider. Vishnu. Like. I praise. For assignment. || 14 ||**

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **host of Maruts** <note>original: "marudgaṇa"</note>, I **praise** <note>original: "stuṣe"</note> you. For what purpose? For **assignment** <note>original: "ādiśe," meaning the granting or bestowing of wealth</note>. How do I describe you? You are **like Indra** <note>the king of the gods</note> in being **one of good deeds** <note>original: "sukratuṃ," performing pious or effective actions</note>. You are **like Varuna** <note>the god of cosmic order</note> in being **wise** <note>original: "māyinaṃ," possessing occult wisdom or extraordinary power</note>. You are **like Aryaman** in being **delightful** <note>original: "mandraṃ," praiseworthy or joyous</note>. You are **like Vishnu** in being a **great provider** <note>original: "suprabhojasam," possessing or giving abundant wealth</note>. <note>Sayana adds a grammatical note: if these names refer to the specific deities themselves rather than comparisons to the Maruts, the words for "like" should be understood as "and."</note>

---

-> ॥ Now the Fifteenth [Verse] ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
The brilliant host, like the Maruts, loud-sounding and unobstructed, like Pushan... who shall provide hundreds and thousands for the people; may he bring to light the hidden riches, may he make the riches easy for us to find. || 15 ||

**Padapatha:**
**Brilliant. Host. Like. Of the Maruts. Loud-sounding. Unobstructed. Pushan. Together. As. Hundreds.**
**Together. Thousands. May he provide. For the people. Hither. Manifest. Hidden. Riches. May he make. Easy to find. For us. Riches. May he make. || 15 ||**

<summary>This page contains hymns 13-15 of Rig Veda 6.48, where the Maruts (storm gods) are praised for providing the "duality" of cows and food to the seer Bharadvaja, and are compared to other major Vedic deities like Indra, Varuna, and Vishnu.</summary>
<keywords>Maruts, Bharadvaja, Indra, Varuna, Vishnu, Pushan, wealth, cow, Vedic sacrifice, Sayana commentary</keywords>

<header>॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Book 4. Chapter 8. Section 4.]</header>

## Hymn Text

**[Mandala 6 | Hymn 48 | Verse 15]**

The **brilliant** host, like that of the **Maruts**, **loud-sounding**, **unrivaled**, I praise **Pushan**. In such a way that he may **bestow** **hundreds** and **thousands** [of riches] upon the **people**, may he **reveal** the **hidden** **wealth**; may he make **wealth** **easy to find** for **us**. || 15 ||

**[Word-by-word Analysis]**
**Brilliant. Host. Like. Of the Maruts. Loud-sounding. Unrivaled. Pushan. Together. In which way. Hundreds. Together. Thousands. May he make. For the people. Hither. Visible. Hidden. Wealth. May he make. Easy to find. For us. Wealth. May he make. || 15 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The word **like** <note>original: "na"</note> here signifies "now" <note>original: "sampratyarthe"</note>. **Now**, at this time, I praise the **brilliant** <note>original: "tveṣam"</note>, **loud-sounding** <note>original: "tuvisvanam"</note>, **unrivaled** <note>original: "anarvāṇam," meaning not reached or countered by enemies</note> **Pushan** <note>the Nourisher</note>, who possesses the **strength** <note>original: "śardho"</note> or power of the Marut host. And in **which way** <note>original: "yathā"</note> that Marut host might **bestow** <note>original: "kāriṣat"</note> **hundreds** <note>original: "śatā"</note> of riches **together** <note>original: "sam"</note> upon the **people** <note>original: "carṣaṇibhyo"</note>—that is, us—so do I praise them. The syllable "ā" is used here for emphasis or collection. Or, in the same way that he might **bestow** **thousands** <note>original: "sahasrā"</note> of riches **together**, so do I praise him—this connects back to the earlier part of the verse. Furthermore, may that Marut host **make visible** <note>original: "āviṣkarat"</note> the **hidden** <note>original: "gūḷhā"</note> or concealed **wealth** <note>original: "vasūni"</note>. Let them reveal it to us. Likewise, may he make **wealth** **easy to find** <note>original: "suvedā"</note> for **us** <note>original: "no"</note>. If, however, this verse is taken to be addressed specifically to Pushan based on the divine characteristics, then the construction should be: "I praise the deity named Pushan, the nourisher, who is brilliant like the host of the Maruts."

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixteenth [Verse] ॥ <-

Hasten toward me, O **Pushan**; I will now **praise** you **in your ear**, O **Glowing One**; and now, let the **hostilities** of the **enemy** [be driven away]. || 16 ||

**[Word-by-word Analysis]**

**Hither. Me. Pushan. Toward. Hasten. I will praise. Now. Your. In the ear. O Glowing One. And now. Of the enemy. Hostilities. || 16 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Pushan**, **hasten** <note>original: "mādraba"</note> toward **me** <note>original: "mā"</note>. Come for the sake of protection. O **Glowing One** <note>original: "āghṛṇe," meaning one who has attained radiance</note>, **now** <note>original: "adhā"</note> **attack** <note>original: "upadrava"</note> the **hostile** <note>original: "arātayaḥ"</note> people who are our **enemies** <note>original: "araryo"</note>. Subdue them. The verb "to run" with the prefix "near" <note>original: "upapūrvo dravatiḥ"</note> is used here in the sense of "to afflict" or "to hinder," just as one might drive away or afflict the cattle of a sacrificer's enemy. And I, being situated in the **vicinity of your ear** <note>original: "apikarṇe"</note>, **quickly** <note>original: "nu"</note> **praise** <note>original: "śaṃsiṣam"</note> you.

-> ॥ Thus ends the third Varga in the eighth Adhyaya of the fourth Ashtaka ॥ <-

<page-num>719</page-num>
<header>Mandala 6. Adhyaya 4. Sukta 48.] || Fourth Ashtaka || 719</header>

## Hymn Text

**[Verse 17]**
Do **not** **uproot** the **Kakambira** <note>original: "kākambīraṃ," a tree-name used here as a metaphor for the family protector</note>, the **Lord of the Forest**. **Destroy** the **wicked** <note>original: "aśastīḥ," those who speak ill or cause sorrow</note> enemies. **May** the **tyrant** **not** **seize** us; for they **set** **snares** <note>original: "grīvāḥ," literally "necks," interpreted here as traps</note> as if for a **bird**. || 17 ||

---

-> || Now the Eighteenth || <-

**[Verse 18]**
May your **friendship** <note>original: "sakhyam"</note> be **unharming** <note>original: "avṛkam," literally "without a wolf," meaning safe or unbreakable</note> toward us, **like** a **skin-bag** <note>original: "hateriva"</note>—
One that is **leakless**, **containing curds**, **well-filled**, and **containing curds**. || 18 ||

**[Word-by-word Analysis]**
**Like a skin-bag. Your. Unharming. Let there be. Friendship. Leakless. Containing curds. Well-filled. Containing curds.** || 18 ||

---

-> || Now the Nineteenth || <-

**[Verse 19]**
For you are **beyond** **mortals**, and **equal** to the **gods** in **glory** <note>original: "śriyā"</note>.
**Look upon** us, O **Pushan**, in our **battles**; **protect** us **now** just **as** you did **of old**. || 19 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)

**[Regarding Verse 17]**
The Sage, representing himself and his descendants as a great tree that provides shelter to many birds, prays for that tree not to be uprooted. O **Pushan**, do not **uproot** <note>original: "udvṛhaḥ"</note> the **Kakambira**—the tree that supports the crows <note>original: "kākānāṃ bhartāraṃ"</note>. Do not strike it down. The meaning is: "Do not harm me, who am accompanied by friends like sons and grandsons and who provides refuge to many others." The word "hi" functions here as "and." **And destroy** <note>original: "vinīnaśo hi"</note> the **wicked** <note>original: "aśastīr," those who are unworthy of praise</note> subjects or enemies who proclaim misery. **And may not** <note>original: "mota"</note> the **tyrant** <note>original: "sūraḥ," the instigator or enemy</note> seize us. Because the verb is accented and connected to the word "evam" <note>in this way</note>, the word "yathā" <note>just as</note> is understood here even if not explicitly heard. **Snares** <note>original: "grīvāḥ," those which swallow or bind the neck</note>. Just as hunters <note>original: "vyādhā"</note> **set** snares or net-like bonds upon the ground to catch a **bird** <note>original: "veḥ"</note>, and by those means they take the birds, so too may the enemy not take us by means of traps.

---

**[Regarding Verse 18]**
O **Pushan**, may **your** **friendship** be **unharming** <note>original: "avṛkaṃ," free from obstacles</note> and remain always in one form for us. Let it be **always**. **Like a skin-bag** <note>original: "hateriva"</note>. Just as your friendship with the skin-bag is uninterrupted, let ours be the same. What kind of **skin-bag**? One that is **leakless** <note>original: "acchidrasya," without holes and well-joined</note>, **containing curds** <note>original: "dadhanvato"</note>, and **well-filled** with curds. The word **containing curds** is repeated to emphasize the great abundance of the curds. Such a skin-bag is always present on Pushan's chariot. The Sage prays that we, too, may be your friends just like that bag.

---

<note>Translator's Note: The imagery of the skin-bag (hṛti) is specific to Pushan, who is often depicted as a pastoral deity carrying a bag of curds (karambha) on his travels.</note>

<summary>This page contains prayers to Pushan for the protection of the family line (metaphorized as a tree) and a plea for a sturdy, abundant friendship compared to a well-filled leather skin-bag.</summary>
<keywords>Pushan, Kakambira tree, family protection, curds, skin-bag (hṛti), snares, friendship (sakhyam), Bharadvaja</keywords>

## Hymn Text

-> 19 <-
**For | indeed | beyond | mortals | you are | equal | with the gods | and | in glory.**
**Look | upon | O Pushan | in battles | us | you | protect | now | just as | before. || 19 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Pushan** <note>original: "pūṣan," the protector of paths and flocks</note>, you stand **beyond** <note>original: "paraḥ," above or superior to</note> **mortals** <note>original: "martyebhyaḥ," human beings</note>. In **glory** <note>original: "śriyā," prosperity or splendor</note> and wealth, you are **equal** to **all the gods**. Therefore, **look upon** us in **battles** <note>original: "pṛtanāsu," in struggles or wars</note> with a merciful gaze. Just **as** you **protected** the people of **ancient times**, **now**—in this very moment—**protect** us. ||

---

## Hymn Text

-> || Now the Twentieth || <-

**May the pleasant and true speech of the Shakers be the leader to wealth;**
**The praise of the great god or the sacrificing mortal, O worshipful ones. || 20 ||**

**Excellent | of the desirable | O Shakers | leadership | let there be | pleasant and true |**
**of the god | or | of the great | of the mortal | or | of the sacrificer | O worshipful ones. || 20 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Shakers** <note>original: "dhūtayaḥ," a title for the Maruts who shake the world with storms</note>, O **worshipful ones** <note>original: "prayajyavaḥ," those who deserve great offerings</note>, may that **pleasant and true** <note>original: "sūnṛtā," speech that is both kind and factual</note> speech of yours—which is the voice of the middle realm—be the **leader** <note>original: "praṇītiḥ," the guide or bringer</note> of wealth for us. Whether it belongs to a **god** or to a **great mortal** who has performed the sacrifice, may that **excellent** <note>original: "vāmī," praiseworthy</note> speech lead us to **desirable** <note>original: "vāmasya," that which is to be sought after</note> wealth. May this guidance be for our benefit. ||

---

## Hymn Text

-> || Now the Twenty-First || <-

**Whose action immediately encompasses the heaven, like the divine sun;**
**The Maruts have held a blazing, worshipful, Vritra-slaying power; the highest Vritra-slaying power. || 21 ||**

**Immediately | indeed | whose | action | around | heaven | god | like | moves | Sun |**
**Blazing | power | they held | name | worshipful | Maruts | Vritra-slayer | power | highest | Vritra-slayer | power. || 21 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Whose**—meaning the host of the **Maruts**—**action** <note>original: "carkṛtiḥ," work or celebration</note> **immediately** moves **around the heaven** and the atmosphere. Just **as** the shining **Sun** <note>original: "sūryaḥ"</note> encompasses the sky, so too does their influence. These **Maruts** have **held** <note>original: "dadhire," possessed</note> a **blazing** <note>original: "tveṣam," bright or fierce</note> **power** <note>original: "śavaḥ," strength</note> that is **worshipful** <note>original: "yajñiyam," worthy of sacrifice</note> and causes enemies to **bow down** <note>original: "nāma," here interpreted as making others bend</note>. That power is a **Vritra-slayer** <note>original: "vṛtrahaṃ," the killer of the demon of drought or obstruction</note>. And that Vritra-slaying power is the **highest** <note>original: "jyeṣṭham," most excellent or eldest</note> among all forms of strength. ||

<summary>This page concludes the praises for Pushan and transitions to the Maruts, highlighting their celestial power and their role in guiding the worshiper to wealth. It emphasizes the Maruts' strength as being equal to the sun and capable of overcoming the forces of obstruction (Vritra).</summary>

<page-num>७९१</page-num>
<header>Mandala 6. Adhyaya 4. Sukta 49.] ॥ Fourth Ashtaka ॥ 791</header>

## Hymn Text

**Mandala 6. Adhyaya 4. Sukta 48. (Conclusion)**

Once indeed the Heaven was born; once the Earth was born.
From the Dappled Cow, once the milk was milked; after that, nothing else is born in like manner. || 22 ||

**Word-by-word Analysis (Padapatha):**
Once | indeed | Heaven | was born | Once | Earth | was born |
From the Dappled Cow | the milked | once | milk | that | other | not | after | is born. || 22 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Once indeed** <note>original: "sakṛddha"</note>—only once—the **Heaven was born**. It arose. Once it was produced, it remains established. It does not happen that when that heaven is destroyed, another similar heaven is born. Similarly, the **Earth was born** only **once**. From the **Dappled Cow** <note>original: "pṛśnyā," referring to the mother of the storm-gods</note>, who is the mother of the **Maruts** <note>storm deities</note>, the **milk** was **milked** only **once**, and from that milk, the Maruts were born. There is a scriptural passage from the <term>Taittiriya</term> <note>a branch of the Yajur Veda</note> that says: "Indeed, from the milk of the Dappled Cow, the Maruts were born." Just as Heaven and Earth are produced only once, so too did the Dappled Cow give birth to the Maruts with that milk just once. After that, **nothing else** <note>no other substance or entity</note> **is born in like manner**; nothing similar to that is produced again.

-> ॥ Thus ends the fourth section (varga) of the eighth chapter (adhyaya) in the fourth book (ashtaka). ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

**Mandala 6. Adhyaya 4. Sukta 49.**

**The sixth hymn, beginning with "I praise the people," consists of fifteen verses. The seer is Rijishvan, the son of Bharadvaja. The deities are the Universal Gods (Visvedevas). The final verse is in the <term>Shakkari</term> meter (fifty-six syllables), while the remaining verses are in the <term>Trishtubh</term> meter. As stated in the <term>Anukramani</term> <note>the ancient index of the Rig Veda</note>: "I praise... five less than twenty... Rijishvan... to the Universal Gods... ending in Shakkari." In the ritual of the <term>Vyulha Dasharatra</term> <note>a ten-day sacrifice</note>, on the fifth day, this hymn is used for the <term>Vaishvadeva-Nivid</term> <note>an invocation to the Universal Gods</note>. It is also indicated in the <term>Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra</term> (7.8): "The hymn to the Universal Gods is 'The Ribhus, Vibhvan, I praise the people'." The first verse is to be recited during the <term>Mahanimni</term> vow.**

-> ॥ This is the first verse ॥ <-

I praise the divine host of good deeds with newest songs, and Mitra and Varuna, who grant happiness.
May they come here, may they hear us here—those of noble power: Varuna, Mitra, and Agni. || 1 ||

**Word-by-word Analysis (Padapatha):**
I praise | the people | of good deeds | with newest | songs | Mitra and Varuna | granting happiness |
they | let | come | they | here | let | hear | of noble power | Varuna | Mitra | Agni. || 1 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

I **praise** <note>original: "stuṣe"</note> the **divine host** <note>original: "daivyaṃ janam," literally "divine people"</note> of **good deeds** <note>original: "suvratam"</note> with **newest songs** or hymns. Likewise, I praise **Mitra and Varuna**. **Mitra** is the protector from decay/death, and **Varuna** is the one who averts sins. What is their nature? They are **granting happiness** <note>original: "sumnyantā"</note>, desiring joy for those who offer praise. May all those gods, including Varuna and the others who possess **noble power** <note>original: "sukṣatrāsaḥ," meaning great strength or dominion</note>, **come here** to this sacrifice.

<summary>This page concludes Hymn 48 with a verse on the unique, singular nature of the creation of Heaven, Earth, and the Maruts, and begins Hymn 49, an invocation to the Universal Gods (Visvedevas) for protection and presence at the sacrifice.</summary>
<keywords>Maruts, Prishni (Dappled Cow), creation, Visvedevas (Universal Gods), Mitra, Varuna, Agni, Rijishvan, Bharadvaja, sacrifice</keywords>

<page-num>792</page-num>
<header>|| Rig Veda || [Book 4. Chapter 8. Section 5.]</header>

...may they come. May such ones hear. And may they hear our praises. Here, the enumeration of deities like Mitra and others is illustrative <note>original: "upalakṣaṇam"</note> because the entire hymn is intended to propound all the deities. Therefore, the earlier reference to "the people" <note>original: "janam"</note> was a general indication.

-> || Now the second verse || <-

## Hymn Text
To him who is to be praised in every community, the one of un-confused wisdom at the sacrifices, the master of the two young ones <note>Heaven and Earth</note>; 
The child of Heaven, the son of strength, Agni, the banner of the sacrifice, the bright one—to him I sacrifice. || 2 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**In every community.** **Worthy of praise.** **In the sacrifices.** **Of un-confused wisdom.** **The master.** **Of the two young ones.**
**Of Heaven.** **The child.** **Of strength.** **The son.** **Agni.** **Of the sacrifice.** **The banner.** **The bright one.** **To sacrifice.** || 2 ||

**In every community** <note>original: "viśo viśaḥ"</note> means among all people. **Worthy of praise** <note>original: "īḍyam"</note> refers to Agni being invoked by the priests in the **sacrifices** <note>original: "adhvareṣu"</note>. He is described as **of un-confused wisdom** <note>original: "ahra-kratum"</note>, meaning one whose actions are devoid of pride or one who possesses undeluded intelligence. He is the **master** <note>original: "aratim," interpreted here as a lord or one who moves toward an end</note> of the **two young ones**, which refers to Heaven and Earth. He is the **child of Heaven** <note>original: "divo śiśum"</note>, for as the scripture says:
> "Agni was first born from Heaven." <note>original: "divaspari prathamaṃ jajñe agniḥ," Rig Veda 10.45.1</note>
Alternatively, he is like a son to the one who praises Heaven; as the scripture also says:
> "You become the son of him who serves you." <note>original: "tvaṃ putro bhavasi yaste vidhat," Rig Veda 2.1.9</note>
He is the **son of strength** <note>original: "sahasaḥ sūnum"</note> <note>Agni is "born of strength" because the sacrificial fire is produced by the forceful rubbing of wood</note>. He is the **banner of the sacrifice** <note>original: "yajñasya ketum"</note>, the one who makes the ritual known, and he is **bright** <note>original: "aruṣam"</note> or shining. To such an Agni, the word **to sacrifice** <note>original: "yajadhyai"</note> is used; we should append the thought "I praise" or "I worship."

---

-> || Now the third verse || <-

## Hymn Text
The two daughters of the Bright One take on different forms; the one is adorned with stars, the other by the Sun.
Moving past one another, though crossing paths, these two pure ones reach our well-known prayer when the hymn is recited. || 3 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Of the Bright One.** **The two daughters.** **Of different forms.** **With stars.** **The one.** **Is adorned.** **The Sun.** **The other.**
**Moving past each other.** **Moving through.** **Pure.** **Prayer.** **Well-known.** **They reach.**
**When the hymn is recited.** || 3 ||

This is a praise of Day and Night. They are the **two daughters** of the **Bright One** <note>original: "aruṣasya"</note>, who is the shining Sun. Since the Sun divides the day and the night, and their existence depends on him, they are called his "daughters." They are **of different forms** <note>original: "virūpe"</note> because of their white and black colors. Among them, **the one** (Night) **is adorned** with **stars** <note>original: "stṛbhiḥ"</note> <note>The root "piś" implies forming or adorning</note>. **The other** daughter, representing the Day, is adorned by the **Sun** <note>original: "sūraḥ"</note>. Thus, they are both decorated by the stars and the Sun respectively...

---

<vocab>
- Agni: The Vedic fire god, central to all sacrifices.
- Adhvara: A term for sacrifice, literally meaning "that which is not injurious."
- Arusha: Meaning red or bright; here it refers to the Sun as the progenitor of time.
- Ketu: A banner or sign; Agni is the 'banner' because his smoke and light signal the sacrifice.
- Virupa: "Diverse-formed," describing the contrast between the light of day and the dark of night.
</vocab>

<keywords>Agni, Sun, Day and Night, ritual sacrifice, Sayana, Rig Veda, cosmology</keywords>

<page-num>793</page-num>
<header>Mandala 6. Anuvaka 4. Sukta 49.] || Fourth Book || 793</header>

...this is the meaning. **Mutually opposing** <note>original: "mithusturā"</note> means they obstruct each other. Day is set aside by Night, and Night is set aside by Day—this is their mutual obstruction. For this very reason, they are **wandering in various ways** <note>original: "vicaratī"</note>, moving separately and extensively. They are **purifiers** <note>original: "pāvake"</note>, as they cleanse or clarify everything. Being such as they are, and being **praised** <note>original: "ṛcyamāne"</note> by us, may they **reach** <note>original: "nakṣataḥ"</note> or pervade the **prayer** <note>original: "manma"</note> that is to be heard and meditated upon, which we have composed.

-> ॥ Now the fourth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

> Let the great prayer go forth towards Vayu, who possesses great wealth, who is desired by all, and who fills the chariot.
> O you who are worthy of great sacrifice, you travel with a shining path, governing your harnessed mares; as a seer, you seek the wise worshipper. ॥ 4 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Forth.** **Towards Vayu.** **Great.** **Prayer.** **Great.** **Wealth.** **All-desirable.** **Chariot-filling.**
**Shining-pathed.** **Harnessed [mares].** **Governing.** **Seer.** **The seer [worshipper].** **You seek/honor.** **O you who are worthy of great sacrifice.** ॥ 4 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

May our **great** or mighty **prayer** <note>original: "manīṣā"</note>, which is our hymn of praise, **go forth** toward and face the deity **Vayu**. Since a preposition is used <note>original: "pra," meaning "forth"</note>, the appropriate action "to go" is understood. What is Vayu like? He is one who possesses **great wealth**, is **all-desirable** (meaning he is to be sought or enjoyed by everyone), and is **chariot-filling**, meaning he protects or fills his own chariot. Alternatively, it means he fills the chariots of those who praise him with riches.

Now follows the direct praise: **O you who are worthy of great sacrifice** <note>original: "prayajyo"</note>, O Vayu, you possess a **shining path**. You are **governing**—that is, approaching or controlling—your **harnessed mares** <note>original: "niyutaḥ"</note>, which are the horses to be yoked to your own chariot. Alternatively, the word for governing <note>original: "patyamānaḥ"</note> implies lordship; he is the lord of those mares. You are a **seer** <note>original: "kaviḥ"</note>, one who sees beyond or possesses far-reaching vision. Being such a one, you **seek** or honor with wealth the **seer**, the wise singer of hymns.

---

-> ॥ Now the fifth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

> May that chariot of the Ashvins cover my body—the chariot that is radiant and yoked by the power of thought.
> O leaders, O truthful ones, with that chariot come to our home for the sake of the son and for ourselves. ॥ 5 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**That.** **My.** **Body.** **May it cover.** **Of the two Ashvins.** **Which.** **Chariot.** **Radiant.** **With thought.** **Yoked.**
**By which.** **O leaders.** **O truthful ones.** **To move towards.** **The home.** **You two go.** **For the son.** **For the self.** **And.** ॥ 5 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

May **that chariot** belonging to the **Ashvins** **cover** <note>original: "chadayatu"</note> or protect **my body**. That is, may it envelope it with its splendor. This is the **chariot** which is **radiant** <note>original: "virukmān"</note>, meaning it shines exceptionally, and which is **yoked** to its horses by the mere activity of the **thought** or mind. 

**O leaders** <note>original: "narā"</note>, O guides; **O truthful ones** <note>original: "nāsatyā"</note>, you who are truthful by nature, or leaders of truth, or—according to another tradition—those born from the nose <note>original: "nāsikā-prabhavau"</note>, referring to the two Ashvins. With that chariot, **you two go** to the **home** <note>original: "vartiḥ"</note> of the worshipper for the sake of the **son** and for the **self** as well.

### Vocabulary Glossary
- **Vayu** <note>term: vāyu</note>: The Vedic deity of the wind.
- **Ashvin** <note>term: aśvin</note>: The twin deities of the dawn and physicians to the gods, often traveling in a three-wheeled chariot.
- **Manisha** <note>term: manīṣā</note>: A prayer, hymn, or inspired thought.
- **Ratha** <note>term: ratha</note>: Chariot, the primary vehicle of the Vedic gods.
- **Kavi** <note>term: kavi</note>: A seer, poet, or sage; someone with extraordinary insight.
- **Prayajyu** <note>term: prayajya</note>: One who is preeminently worthy of sacrifice or worship.
- **Nasatya** <note>term: nāsatya</note>: A common title for the Ashvins; literally meaning "not untrue" (truthful), though scholars also link it to "healing" or an ancient Indo-European root for "returning home."

->॥ Now the sixth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

O Parjanya and Vata, you two bulls of the earth, nourish the replenishing waters.
O seers who hear the truth, you who are wise, by the songs of the singer, make all that moves and all that stands still come toward us. ॥ 6 ॥

---

### Pada-patha
Parjanya-Vata. Bulls. Of the earth. Waters. Nourish. Honorable.
Seers of truth. Wise ones. Whose. By songs. Of the world. Of the standing. The world. Toward. Make. ॥ 6 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Parjanya-Vata** <note>the deities of Rain and Wind</note>, you who are **bulls** <note>original: "vṛṣabhā," meaning showerers or fertilizers</note> of the **earth**—here "earth" <note>original: "pṛthivyāḥ"</note> is a name for the atmosphere—nourish the **waters** <note>original: "purīṣāṇi"</note> which are the "fillers" that must be given by the atmosphere. Send them forth.

The second half of the verse refers to the Maruts <note>the Storm Gods</note>. O **seers of truth** <note>original: "satya-śrutaḥ"</note>, you who are listeners to true praise, and O **wise ones** <note>original: "kavayo"</note>, the intelligent Maruts: by the **songs** or hymns of **that** worshipper by whom you are praised, **make** the entire **world**—consisting of both the moving and the stationary—come **toward** him. O **stander of the world** <note>original: "jagataḥ sthāḥ"</note>: though the word is singular, it refers to the entire host. It should be applied as: "O Marut host, you who establish the world of moving and stationary things."

In the introductory sacrifice <note>original: "Anvārambhaṇīyā"</note>, the verse beginning with "**She of the spear**" <note>original: "pāvīravī"</note> is the offering-verse <note>term: yājyā - the verse recited when the oblation is cast into the fire</note> for the Sarasvata oblation. It is indicated in the scriptures: "She of the spear, the maiden of wonderful life... the swelling [milk] of Sarasvat" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.8). In the animal sacrifice dedicated to Sarasvati, this same verse is the offering-verse for the sacrificial cake <note>term: puroḍāśa - a cake made of ground grain offered in fire</note>. It is indicated: "She of the spear, the maiden of wonderful life... that breast of yours which is exhausted, which is the source of joy" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 3.9). This verse also appears in the Litany to Agni and the Maruts <note>original: "Āgnimāruta śastra"</note>. It is indicated: "I [invoke] Raka—these two verses; and 'She of the spear, the maiden of wonderful life'" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 5.20).

->॥ This is the seventh verse in the hymn ॥<-

## Hymn Text

May the purifying maiden, of wonderful life, Sarasvati, wife of the hero, grant us wisdom.
In harmony with the divine women, may she grant the singer protection that is flawless, a refuge that is difficult to overpower. ॥ 7 ॥

---

### Pada-patha
She of the spear. Maiden. Of wonderful life. Sarasvati. Wife of the hero. Wisdom. May she grant.
With the divine women. Flawless. Refuge. Harmonious. Difficult to overpower. To the singer. Protection. May she grant. ॥ 7 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

**She of the spear** <note>original: "pāvīravī"</note> means the purifier. **Maiden** <note>original: "kanyā"</note> means one who is lovely or desirable. **Of wonderful life** <note>original: "citrāyuḥ"</note> means she who has wonderful motion or possesses wonderful food. **Wife of the hero** <note>original: "vīrapatnī"</note>: the "hero" is Prajapati <note>the Lord of Progeny</note>, and she is his wife. Or, it means she who protects heroes. In this manner—

पुरीष (Purisha): In Vedic Sanskrit, often refers to "fillings" or the waters of the atmosphere.

...the manifest **Sarasvati** <note>the goddess of speech and wisdom</note> should support our **prayer** <note>original: "dhiyam"</note>, which is our action called sacrifice. May she place it, sustain it, or give it. Indeed, the object signified by the word is what is performed. Furthermore, may she, **together with the Gnas** <note>the wives of the gods</note>, being equally pleased—or **Gnas** may refer to the meters such as the Gayatri, based on the scripture <note>original: "Shruti"</note> "The meters are indeed the Gnas"—being pleased with them, grant to me, the singer, a **refuge** <note>original: "sharanam"</note> that is **without holes** <note>original: "achidram," meaning perfect or continuous</note> and **unassailable**—impossible for enemies or even cold winds to attack—and grant us **happiness** <note>original: "sharma"</note>. ॥

In the animal sacrifice dedicated to Pushan among the eleven victims, the verse **"Of path after path"** <note>original: "pathaspatha"</note> is the offering prayer for the oblation. This is indicated in the *Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra* (3.7): "Of path after path, the protector of the surrounding, with speech... O Brihaspati, that which is the highest distance"—these two. ॥

-> || This is the eighth verse of the hymn || <-

## Hymn Text

Of path after path the protector, won over by the desire of the singer with hymns; may he, **Pushan**, grant us riches with gold at their tips, and may he further every one of our prayers. ॥ 8 ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown (Pada-patha):**
Of path. Of path. Around. Protector. By speech. By desire. Made. Toward. He reached. By hymns.
He. Us. May he give. Riches. Gold-tipped. Prayer-prayer. May he further. Forth. Pushan. ॥ 8 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Of path after path** <note>original: "pathaspatha"</note> means the lord or protector of every road. The singer, having won over the worshipful **Pushan** <note>the solar deity of journeys and nourishment</note> with the **desire** for the intended fruit/result, **reaches** him or attains him through **speech**, that is, through praise. And may that Pushan **give** to us **riches** <note>original: "shurudhah," interpreted here as cattle</note> which stop our sorrows and have **gold at their tips** <note>original: "chandra-agraah"</note>—"Chandra" is a name for gold—meaning they have gold at their faces or gold-tipped horns. The word **"rasat"** <note>may he give</note> comes from the root *ra* (to give). Likewise, may Pushan **further** or bring to success every **prayer** or action of ours. ॥

In the animal sacrifice dedicated to Tvashtr, the verse **"The one who shares first"** <note>original: "prathamabhajam"</note> is the offering prayer for the oblation. This is indicated in the *Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra* (3.8): "The one who shares first, the glorious, the bestower of strength, Soma and Pushan, the begetters of wealth..." ॥

-> || This is the ninth verse of the hymn || <-

## Hymn Text

May the priest <note>original: "Hotar"</note> worship the one who **shares first**, the glorious, the bestower of strength, the fair-handed god, the one with skillful fingers, the skillful one; may Agni worship **Tvashtr**, the adorable one of the dwellings, who is easily invoked and radiant. ॥ 9 ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown (Pada-patha):**
First-sharing. Glorious. Strength-bestowing. Fair-handed. God. Skillful-fingered. Skillful.
The priest. May he worship. The adorable. Of the dwellings. Agni. Tvashtr. Easily-invoked. Radiant. ॥ 9 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**The one who shares first** <note>original: "prathamabhajam"</note> refers to the one who is the distributor of portions to living beings at the very time of their birth/origin. As the scripture <note>original: "Shruti"</note> says: "In whatever way the semen is poured, Tvashtr transforms the forms; in that way is it born." The **glorious** one...

...the **glorious one** <note>original: "yashasvinam"</note>, the **bestower of vitality** <note>original: "vayodham"</note>, the supporter or holder of food in the form of the oblation; or alternatively, the one who grants food to the chanters. He is **skilful-handed** <note>original: "supanim"</note>; here, "pani" refers to the region of the hand above the wrist. He is **easily invoked** <note>original: "suhavam"</note>, meaning he can be easily called upon. May the **Invoker** <note>the Hotr priest</note>, the radiant Agni who calls the gods, worship such a **Tvashtr** <note>the divine artisan</note>. ## Hymn Text

With these songs, magnify the **Father of the world** <note>original: "bhuvanasya pitaram"</note>, **Rudra**, by day; magnify **Rudra** by night. The great, the radiant, the ageless, the **very gracious** <note>original: "susumnam"</note>—may we, impelled by the **Sage** <note>original: "kavina"</note>, invoke him uniquely. ॥ 10 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
Of the world । the Father । with songs । these । by these । Rudra । by day । magnify । Rudra । in the night ।
The great । the radiant । the ageless । the very gracious । uniquely । may we invoke । by the Sage । those who are impelled ॥ 10 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O chanter, magnify **Rudra**, the protector <note>original: "pitaram"</note> of the **world** <note>original: "bhuvanasya"</note>—that is, the collection of all created beings—with these songs or praises by day. Likewise, magnify the same Rudra with praises in the night <note>original: "aktau"</note>. **Rudra** is the Lord <note>Ishvara</note> who drives away <note>original: "dravayitaram"</note> suffering <note>original: "rut"</note>. And may we, being **impelled** <note>original: "ishitasah"</note> or inspired by the wise Rudra, the **Sage** <note>original: "kavina"</note>, invoke him in a way that is **prosperous** <note>original: "ridhak"</note> or abundant. We praise him who is endowed with such qualities as being **great** <note>original: "brihantam"</note>, **radiant** or beautiful to look upon <note>original: "rishvam"</note>, **ageless** <note>original: "ajaram"</note>, and **very gracious** <note>original: "susumnam"</note>, meaning one who grants excellent happiness. ॥

## Hymn Text

Come, O youthful, wise, and **sacrificial** <note>original: "yajniyaso"</note> **Maruts**, to the desirable praise of the singer. Even the **dull-witted** <note>original: "achitram"</note> you indeed inspire; O **leaders** <note>original: "narah"</note>, as you increase, reaching [everywhere] in this manner like the **Angirasas**. ॥ 11 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
Come । O youthful ones । O wise ones । O sacrificial ones । O Maruts । come । of the singer । to the desirable [praise] ।
The dull-witted । even । indeed । you inspire । increasing । thus । reaching । O leaders । like the Angirasas ॥ 11 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **youthful ones** <note>original: "yuvana"</note>, who are eternally young; O **wise ones** <note>original: "kavayah"</note>, the learned; O **sacrificial ones** <note>original: "yajniyaso"</note>, worthy of sacrifice—O Maruts of such nature, come to the **desirable** <note>original: "varasyam"</note> praise of the singer. Come near. Furthermore, O **leaders** <note>original: "narah"</note>, the guiding Maruts, increasing in this very manner; or alternatively, **reaching** <note>original: "nakshantah"</note> or pervading the atmosphere in this way **like the Angirasas** <note>original: "angirasvat"</note>. The Angirasas here are the moving rays of light. Just as they quickly...

<page-num>797</page-num>
<header>Mandala 6, Anuvaka 4, Sukta 49] || Fourth Ashtaka || 797</header>

...they pervade the firmament like that. Alternatively, the sages themselves are the Angirases <note>a group of celestial seers</note>. They are similarly swift-moving. Being such, you [the Maruts] nourish even the **unconscious** <note>original: "acit"</note>—meaning a region thick with herbs and trees. You also gladden <note>original: "jinvatha"</note> a place distinct from that, even one devoid of herbs and vegetation. You satisfy it with rain. The word "hi" is used here as a filler particle.

->॥ Now the Twelfth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
Drive the song to the **hero** <note>original: "vīrāya"</note>, to the **mighty** <note>original: "tavase"</note>, the **swift** <note>original: "turāya"</note>, as a **herdsman** <note>original: "paśurakṣiḥ"</note> drives his **flock** <note>original: "yūtheva"</note> **home** <note>original: "astam"</note>. May he make the inspired word of the singer **touch** <note>original: "pispṛśati"</note> the **body** <note>original: "tanvi"</note> of the **famed** <note>original: "śrutasya"</note> deity, as the **stars** <note>original: "stṛbhiḥ"</note> touch the **firmament** <note>original: "nākam"</note>. ॥ १२ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Drive | to the hero | drive | to the mighty | to the swift | drive | like a flock | the herdsman | to the home |
He | touches | in the body | of the famed | with the stars | like | the firmament | of the speech | the inspired singer ॥ १२ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Drive forward** <note>original: "prāja"</note>—O chanter, make your praise reach—the troop of Maruts, who are the **hero** <note>original: "vīrāya"</note>, meaning the valiant ones or those who scatter their enemies in various ways. Likewise, drive it to that troop which is **mighty** <note>original: "tavase"</note> and **swift-moving** <note>original: "turāya"</note>.

A comparison is given here: like a **herdsman** <note>original: "paśurakṣiḥ"</note> and **flocks** <note>original: "yūtheva"</note>. Just as a protector of cattle drives the herds of cows quickly to their **home** <note>original: "astam"</note> in the evening, so too should you impel the praise. And may that troop of Maruts make the **famed** <note>original: "śrutasya"</note> hymn—which is to be heard—**touch** <note>original: "pispṛśati"</note> or unite with their own **bodies** <note>original: "tanvi"</note>. <note>Sayana notes a grammatical shift where the possessive case is used for the dative 'for the body'.</note> This means: let the hymn of the **inspired singer** <note>original: "vipaḥ"</note>, the wise chanter of **speech** <note>original: "vacanasya"</note>, reach their hearts.

A comparison for this touching is provided: **as the stars touch the firmament** <note>original: "stṛbhira na nākaṃ"</note>. Just as the stars are joined to the sky, so may the hymn be joined to the gods.

---

->॥ Now the Thirteenth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
He who **measured out** <note>original: "vimame"</note> the **earthly** <note>original: "pārthivāni"</note> **spaces** <note>original: "rajāṃsi"</note> **thrice** <note>original: "triḥ"</note>, even **Vishnu**, for **Manu** <note>the progenitor of humanity</note> when he was **distressed** <note>original: "bādhitāya"</note>. In his **shelter** <note>original: "śarman"</note>, which is being approached, may we rejoice with wealth, in person and with progeny. ॥ १३ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Who | spaces | measured out | earthly | thrice | indeed | Vishnu | for Manu | for the distressed |
of him | of you | in the shelter | in that which is being approached | with wealth | may we rejoice | with the body | with progeny | and ॥ १३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
That **Vishnu** who, for the sake of **Manu** <note>Prajapati, the lord of creatures</note> when he was harassed by demons, **measured out** <note>original: "vimame"</note> the **earthly** <note>original: "pārthivāni"</note> **spaces** <note>original: "rajāṃsi"</note> or worlds. This refers to the three worlds. He measured them **thrice** <note>original: "triḥ"</note>. The word "cit" is used for emphasis. With only three strides, he measured them all. O Vishnu, of such a one as you... <note>Sayana notes the use of the possessive 'of you' for the instrumental 'by you'.</note> ...in the **shelter** <note>original: "śarman"</note>, meaning the house or the state of bliss, being granted to us by you...

<vocab>
- Marudgaṇa: The troop of Maruts, storm deities known for their speed and power.
- Viṣṇu: A solar deity in the Rig Veda, famous for crossing the universe in three strides.
- Manu: The archetypal human/progenitor who receives divine aid.
- Paśurakṣi: A cattle-protector or herdsman; a common metaphor for a guide or priest.
- Rajāṃsi: Translated here as "spaces" or "worlds," referring to the divisions of the universe.
- Śarman: A word meaning shelter, protection, house, or the happiness derived from safety.
</vocab>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary for Verse 13 of Mandala 6, Sukta 49, and presents the full text and commentary for Verses 14 and 15. The previous page discussed the Maruts and Vishnu; here, the focus shifts to a collective invocation of deities including the Serpent of the Deep, Savitar, and Bhaga, concluding the hymn with a prayer for enduring wealth and victory.</meta>

...being present in this state, may we rejoice with wealth, with a body free from diseases and other ailments, and with offspring <note>original: "tanayena," referring to sons/descendants</note>. May we be gladdened. May we be joyful.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fourteenth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
May the **Serpent of the Deep** <note>original: "Ahirbudhnya"</note> grant us that, with **waters** and **hymns**; may the **Mountain** <note>original: "Parvata"</note> and **Savitar** <note>original: "Savitar"</note> grant that **food** <note>original: "canas"</note>. May the **All-Gods**, the **bestowers of gifts** <note>original: "rātishācaḥ"</note>, grant that along with **herbs**; may **Bhaga** <note>the dispenser of fortune</note>, the **goddess of abundance** <note>original: "Purandhi"</note>, impel us toward **wealth** <note>original: "rāye"</note>. ॥ १४ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
That | for us | Serpent | of the Deep | with waters | with hymns | that | Mountain | that | Savitar | food | grant |
That | with herbs | toward | bestowers of gifts | Bhaga | goddess of abundance | impel | forward | for wealth ॥ १४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Serpent of the Deep:** The word "deep" <note>original: "budhna"</note> refers to the atmosphere. The "Serpent" <note>original: "ahi"</note> is the one who exists there. He is called a serpent because he moves through the atmosphere. It has been said: "He is the serpent because of his movement in the atmosphere." This deity, signified by these two words, being praised by **hymns** <note>original: "arkaiḥ"</note>—which are mantras used as means of worship—may he **grant us that** well-known **food** <note>original: "canaḥ"</note> in the world, along with **waters**. May he bestow it. **The Mountain:** One who fills <note><term>the root "pṛ" means to fill</term></note>. Alternatively, "Mountain" refers to the one who possesses the mountain-like thunderbolt <note>Indra</note>. Or "Mountain" may mean the enemy of the mountain <note>the clouds</note>. May he also grant that food. Likewise, **Savitar**, the inspiring god, may he also grant that food. Furthermore, the **bestowers of gifts**: those who accompany or serve the act of giving; these are the All-Gods <note>Visvedevas</note>. May they grant that food along with **herbs**. Herbs <note>original: "oshadhi"</note> are things like sesame and beans, in which "ripening" <note>original: "osha"</note> is placed. Finally, may **Bhaga**, who is to be worshipped, and the **goddess of abundance** <note>original: "Purandhi"</note>—meaning one with great wisdom, great intelligence, or one of many deeds—**impel** us for the sake of **wealth**. May they inspire us.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fifteenth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Now grant us **wealth** <note>original: "rayi"</note> associated with **chariots**, **satisfying men**, rich in **heroes**, the guardian of the **Great Truth** <note>original: "Ṛta"</note>. Grant us an **unaging home**, by which we may **overcome godless rivals** and prevail over **godless people**. ॥ १५ ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
Now | for us | wealth | with chariots | satisfying men | rich in heroes | of the Great | of the Truth | guardian |
Home | grant | unaging | by which | people | rivals | godless | over | and | may we overcome | people | godless | over | may we prevail ॥ १५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O all you Gods, **grant us wealth** and a **home**. Bestow them upon us. What kind of wealth? **Associated with chariots**, meaning possessed of chariots. **Satisfying men**: "Men" <note>original: "charshani"</note> are human beings; it is the filler or satisfier of them. **Rich in heroes**: "Heroes" are sons and others who are born from one's own strength; wealth accompanied by many such heroes. **Great**...

<summary>This page concludes the 49th hymn of the 6th Mandala with prayers to a variety of atmospheric and celestial deities for food, water, and abundance. The final verse is a petition for enduring wealth, a stable home, and the power to overcome godless enemies.</summary>
<keywords>Ahirbudhnya, Savitar, Bhaga, Purandhi, wealth, cosmic order, Rita, protective deities, victory over enemies</keywords>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on the final verse of Rig Veda Mandala 6, Sukta 50, and introduces the first two verses of Sukta 51. The previous page ended with an invocation for protection; here, the commentator Sayana explains the necessity of the sacrificial fee (dakshina) and lists the various deities to be invoked in the new hymn.</meta>

## Commentary (Sayana)

Guardian of the **Cosmic Order** <note>original: "Rta," referring here to the sacrifice</note>, meaning the protector of the sacrifice. For the sacrifice is protected by wealth in the form of the **sacrificial fee** <note>original: "dakshina"</note>; according to the saying, "A sacrifice without a fee is a dead sacrifice." What kind of dwelling? One that is **undecaying** <note>original: "ajaram"</note>, free from old age. With such wealth and such a dwelling, may we overcome the **rivals** <note>original: "sprdhaḥ"</note>, the enemies, and the **godless** <note>original: "adeviḥ"</note> or demonic armies of the **Asuras**. Likewise, may we reach the **godly people** <note>original: "adevyaḥ vishaḥ"</note>—the subjects in whom the gods have entered to accept the oblations—and through such wealth and housing, may we fully obtain them. The meaning is that the Lord is the giver of such prosperity.

->॥ This concludes the seventh section (Varga) of the eighth chapter of the fourth book (Ashtaka) ॥<-
->॥ This concludes the fourth lesson (Anuvaka) of the sixth circle (Mandala) ॥<-

In the fifth lesson, there are twelve hymns. Among them, the first hymn, beginning with **"I invoke you"** <note>original: "huve vaḥ"</note>, consists of fifteen verses. The seer is **Rijishvan**, a descendant of Bharadvaja; the hymn is addressed to multiple deities and is composed in the **Trishtubh** metre. The application of the hymn has already been mentioned in the general rules.

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Here is the first verse ॥<-

I invoke with **reverence** for our **bliss** the divine **Aditi**, and **Varuna**, **Mitra**, and **Agni**;
And **Aryaman**, the destroyer of enemies, the very gracious one, the **Saviours**, the **All-Gods**, **Savitar**, and **Bhaga**. ॥ १ ॥

**Padapatha:**
I-invoke | you | divine | Aditi | with-reverence | for-bliss | Varuna | Mitra | Agni |
the-destroyer-of-enemies | Aryaman | very-gracious | Saviours | Gods | Savitar | Bhaga | and ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Gods, I invoke your mother, the **divine** or shining **Aditi** <note>literally "the indivisible" or "boundless"</note>, the deity of that name, for the sake of **bliss** <note>original: "mrulīkāya," meaning happiness or mercy</note> with **reverential acts** or songs of praise. I invoke, I praise. Likewise, I invoke **Varuna**, the withholder; **Mitra**, the god who saves from decay; and **Agni**—all these gods I invoke with reverence. Likewise, **Aryaman**, who is the **destroyer of enemies** <note>original: "abhikṣadām," where 'kṣad' means to strike or destroy</note> and is **very gracious** or the source of great happiness, I invoke with reverence. I invoke **Savitar and Bhaga** with reverence. Why say more? I invoke and praise all the **Saviours** or protectors, all the **Gods**, with hymns of reverence.

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the second verse ॥<-

O **Sun**, you of beautiful light, go to the gods, the **fathers of wisdom**, for our **sinlessness**, O you of great glory;
They who are **twice-born**, who are the **protectors of immortality**, who are **truthful**, **dwellers in light**, **holy**, and **fire-tongued**. ॥ २ ॥

**Padapatha:**
Of-beautiful-light | Sun | Wisdom-fathers | in-sinlessness | of-great-glory | go-to | Gods |
Twice-born | who | immortality-protectors | truthful | light-possessors | holy | fire-tongued ॥ २ ॥

<vocab>
<term>Aditi<gloss>The boundless mother of the gods, representing the infinite.</gloss></term>
<term>Aryaman<gloss>One of the Adityas, often associated with customs, marriage, and social order; here described as a destroyer of enemies.</gloss></term>
<term>Dakshina<gloss>The fee or gift given to priests, considered essential to complete a sacrifice.</gloss></term>
<term>Agni-jihva<gloss>Literally "fire-tongued," describing how gods "eat" the sacrificial offerings through the medium of the ritual fire.</gloss></term>
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes the previous hymn with a focus on the protective power of sacrificial fees and transitions into a new hymn (Sukta 51) that collectively invokes the Vedic pantheon—including Aditi, Varuna, and the Sun—to grant bliss and witness the worshippers' sinlessness.</summary>
<keywords>Sayana, Rig Veda, Aditi, Varuna, Aryaman, Dakshina, Yajna, Sinlessness, Twice-born</keywords>
