<meta>This page continues the commentary on the second verse of Rig Veda, Mandala 6, Sukta 50, and provides the full text and commentary for verses 3 and 4. The previous page introduced the hymn by the seer Rijishvan, addressed to the All-Gods (Vishvedevas).</meta>

# Rig Veda — Page 800
### Ashtaka 4, Adhyaya 8, Varga 9

O **Great Stimulator** <note>original: "sumahaḥ"</note>, the beautiful and radiant Sun, the impeller of all! Toward the **descendants of Daksha** <note>original: "dakṣapitr‌̥n," referring to the gods who have the progenitor Daksha as their ancestor</note>. The term "Ancestors" <note>original: "pitr‌̥"</note> generally refers to one's forefathers. As it is said: "I have found the ancestors who know the right path" <note>original: "pitr‌̥nsuvidatrām̐ avitsi"; Rig Veda 10.15.3</note>. That these gods are the descendants of Daksha is known from the mantra: "For Aditi was born [from Daksha]" <note>original: "aditirhyajaniṣṭeti"; Rig Veda 10.72.5</note>. To such gods who possess **beautiful light** <note>original: "sujyotiṣaḥ"</note>, lead us toward **sinlessness** <note>original: "anāgāstve"</note>, meaning freedom from fault. Grant this request <note>original: "vīhi"</note>; the sense is: "Act in such a way that they do not find fault in us." These gods are **twice-born** <note>original: "dvijanmāno"</note> as they manifest in two worlds; they are **adherents of the Cosmic Order** <note>original: "r‌̥tasāpa"</note> because they touch or attend the sacrifice; they are **truthful** and do not fail; they are **possessors of wealth** <note>original: "svarvanto"</note>; they are **worthy of sacrifice** <note>original: "yajatā"</note>; and they are **those whose tongue is fire** <note>original: "agnijihvāḥ"</note>, meaning Agni serves as the tongue through which they receive offerings. The instruction is to approach these gods who possess such qualities.

---

-> ॥ Verse 3 ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
And may **Heaven and Earth** grant us wide **sovereignty**; may the **two worlds**, great and providing good refuge, grant us a **shelter** that is full of happiness.
May you both create great **wealth** for us, so that it may be ours; O **Two Supporters**, grant us a **sinless** dwelling. ॥ ३ ॥

**Pada-patha:**
And | Heaven and Earth | sovereignty | wide | great | the two worlds | refuge | full of happiness | full of happiness |
great | may you create | wealth | so that | for us | for us | for a dwelling | O Two Supporters | sinless. ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
Furthermore, O **Heaven and Earth** <note>original: "dyāvāpr‌̥thivī"</note>, may you both create <note>original: "karathaḥ"</note>—meaning produce—a wide and extensive **sovereignty** or strength <note>original: "kṣatram"</note>. Likewise, O **Two Worlds** <note>original: "rodasī"</note>, may you both, being full of happiness, create a great and vast **refuge** or house <note>original: "śaraṇam"</note>. The meaning is: produce for us great **wealth** <note>original: "varivo"</note> so that it may be ours. Moreover, O **Two Supporters** <note>original: "dhiṣaṇe," referring to Heaven and Earth as the sustainers of all</note>, create for our **dwelling** <note>original: "kṣayāya"</note> a place that is **sinless** <note>original: "anehaḥ"</note> or free from evil.

---

-> ॥ Verse 4 ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
May the **sons of Rudra** <note>the Maruts</note> incline toward us today, they who are invoked, the **bringers of wealth**, the **unassailable**.
Whether in a **small** matter or a **great** one, the **Maruts** are placed for our protection in the **struggle** of the days of the gods. ॥ ४ ॥

**Pada-patha:**
Toward | us | of Rudra | sons | may they incline | today | invoked | bringers of wealth | unassailable |
Whether | them | in small | in great | or | placed | in struggle | Maruts | of days | gods. ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
May the **Maruts**, who are the sons of Rudra, having been **invoked** <note>original: "āhūtāsaḥ"</note> at this time, **incline** <note>original: "ānamantām"</note> toward us. That is, may they be well-disposed and come to us. What are they like? They are **bringers of wealth** <note>original: "vasavo"</note>, those who cause us to dwell in prosperity, and they are **unassailable**...

# Rig Veda — Page 901
### Mandala 6, Hymn 50, Verse 5

[They are] unharmed by others. Whenever these **Maruts** <note>original: "maruto"</note>, the gods, are placed or established in a battle, whether it be small <note>original: "arbhe"</note> or great and powerful <note>original: "mahati"</note>, we call upon them today on the path. This is the connection of the words.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Among whom the divine **Rodasi** <note>original: "rodasī"</note> indeed joins quickly; **Pushan** <note>original: "pūṣā"</note>, who honors the sacrificers with prosperity, [joins them too]. Having heard our call, O **Maruts**, when you truly go forth, all beings tremble on the cleared path. ॥ 5 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
Among whom | Rodasi | indeed | the goddess | joins | Pushan | the prosperity-bestowing-sacrificer | having heard | the call | O Maruts | when | indeed | you go | the beings | tremble | on the path | cleared. ॥ 5 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
Among these Maruts, the goddess **Rodasi** <note>original: "rodasī"</note>—who is the wife of Rudra or perhaps the "Middle Speech" <note>original: "mādhyamikā vāk," referring to a level of sound associated with the atmospheric realm</note>—quickly unites <note>original: "mimyakṣa"</note>. Likewise, the god **Pushan** <note>original: "pūṣā"</note>, the nourisher, who is a **bestower of prosperity through sacrifice** <note>original: "abhyardhayajvā"</note>—meaning one who makes the singers prosperous and honors them with wealth—attends to or serves these Maruts. The sage Yaska explains: "He who honors by making them prosperous" <note>original: "abhyardhayanjayati"; Nirukta 6.6</note>.

O **Maruts**, when you truly go forth <note>original: "yaddha yātha"</note> after having heard our **call** <note>original: "havam"</note> or invitation, then all **beings** <note>original: "bhūmā"</note>—the multitude of living creatures existing there—**tremble** <note>original: "rejante"</note> because the **path** <note>original: "adhvani"</note> has been cleared or set apart for your passage. As it is said in another mantra:

> "They cause the mountains to tremble; they rend the forest trees asunder." <note>original: "pra vepayanti parvatānvi viñcanti vanaspatīn"; Rig Veda 1.39.5</note>

-> ॥ This ends the seventh Varga in the eighth Adhyaya of the fourth Ashtaka ॥ <-

---

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Worship that **Hero** <note>original: "vīram"</note>, the lover of songs, **Indra**, with a new prayer from the singer. May he surely hear the call while being praised; may he, being celebrated, grant great strengths and riches. ॥ 6 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
Toward | that | Hero | the lover of songs | worship | Indra | with prayer | O singer | with a new | heard | surely | the call | near | and | being praised | may he grant | strengths | near | great | being celebrated. ॥ 6 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **singer** <note>original: "jaritaḥ"</note>, worship <note>original: "abhyarca"</note>—that is, praise—that well-known and powerful **Hero** <note>original: "vīram"</note>, who is the driver away of enemies, the **lover of songs** <note>original: "girvaṇasam"</note> who enjoys our hymns, even **Indra**. Do this with a **new** <note>original: "navena"</note>, beautiful, and fresh **prayer** <note>original: "brahmaṇā"</note> or hymn.

While being **praised** <note>original: "stavānaḥ"</note>, may he surely **hear** <note>original: "upavadit"</note> our call and hymn. Furthermore, may Indra, while being **celebrated** <note>original: "gṛṇānaḥ"</note>, **grant** <note>original: "rāsat"</note> us **great** <note>original: "mahaḥ"</note> and abundant **strengths** <note>original: "vājān"</note> or food. The meaning is: because he is such a giver, you should praise him.

---
<vocab>
**Maruts** (Storm-gods), **Pushan** (Nourishing deity), **Rodasi** (Goddess associated with Rudra/Maruts), **Indra** (King of gods), **Jaritr** (The singer/chanter), **Brahmana** (Prayer/sacred word), **Vajan** (Strengths/provisions/wealth), **Abhyardhayajva** (One who increases prosperity through worship), **Pravikte** (A path cleared or set apart)
</vocab>

This page (902) contains the text and commentary for verses 7, 8, and 9, shifting focus to the Waters, the Sun-god Savitar, and the Fire-god Agni.</meta>

# Rig Veda — Page 902
### Mandala 6, Hymn 50, Verse 7

-> ॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

O Waters <note>original: "āpaḥ"</note>, who are friendly to humanity, grant us uninjured protection <note>original: "omānam"</note>, and for our children and descendants, peace and health <note>original: "śaṃ yoḥ"</note>. For you are truly the most motherly healers, the progenitors of all that is stationary and all that moves. ॥ 7 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
Protection | Waters | human-friendly | uninjured | grant | for offspring | for descendants | peace | health | you | indeed | are | healers | most motherly | of all | stationary | moving | progenitors. ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Waters, who are beneficial to humanity** <note>original: "āpo mānuṣīḥ"</note>, grant us **uninjured** <note>original: "amṛktam"</note>—meaning unharmed—**protection** <note>original: "omānam"</note>. The word *omā* refers to food or protection that sustains <note>original: "avanti rakṣatītyomā"</note>. Grant this to our **offspring** <note>original: "tokāya"</note>, meaning our sons, and to our **descendants** <note>original: "tanayāya"</note>, meaning our grandsons. Likewise, grant us **peace** <note>original: "śam"</note>, which is the calming of miseries, and **health** <note>original: "yoḥ"</note>, which is the separation or removal of that which should be avoided. 

Why should you do this? The text says: **For** <note>original: "hi"</note> you **are the most motherly** <note>original: "mātṛtamā"</note>—meaning even greater than biological mothers—**healers** <note>original: "bhiṣajaḥ"</note>. The connection is that since you are such, you must grant these things. How is your healing power greater than a mother’s? It is because you are the **progenitors** <note>original: "janitrīḥ"</note> of **all** <note>original: "viśvasya"</note> things, both the **stationary** <note>original: "sthātuḥ"</note>, like plants and stones, and the **moving** <note>original: "jagataḥ"</note>, like animals and humans. Therefore, you are the ultimate healers.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Eighth Verse ॥ <-

May the divine **Savitar** <note>the Sun-god as the "Impeller" of life</note>, the protector, he of the golden hands and worthy of worship, come to us. He who, being wealthy, reveals desirable things for the giver of oblations, just as the face of the Dawn [reveals the world]. ॥ 8 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
Towards | us | divine | Savitar | protector | golden-handed | worthy-of-worship | may-he-come | who | wealthy | of-dawn | like | the-face | reveals | for-the-giver | desirable-things. ॥ 8 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

May the **protector** <note>original: "cāyamāṇo"</note>—he who guards—the **golden-handed** <note>original: "hiraṇyapāṇiḥ"</note>—referring either to hands of gold or hands that are beneficial and beautiful—the **worthy of worship** <note>original: "yajato"</note>—he who is fit to be honored with sacrifice—the divine **Savitar, the impeller** <note>original: "savitā prerakaḥ"</note>, **come to us** <note>original: "no'smānājagamyāt"</note>. 

The text continues: **He who** is **wealthy** <note>original: "dattavān"</note> **reveals** <note>original: "vyūrṇute"</note>—meaning displays or makes manifest—**desirable wealth** <note>original: "vāryāṇi"</note> to the **sacrificer** <note>original: "dāśuṣe"</note> who has given oblations. He does this **like the face of the Dawn** <note>original: "uṣaso na pratīkam"</note>; just as the appearance of the dawn light reveals all things that were hidden in the dark, so too does Savitar reveal and bestow wealth.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Ninth Verse ॥ <-

And you, O **Son of Strength** <note>an epithet for Agni, the Fire-god</note>, bring the gods to this sacrifice today. May I always remain in your auspicious favor; may we, O Agni, be blessed with heroes through your protection. ॥ 9 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
And | you | Son | of Strength | us | today | [bring] | the gods | in this | sacrifice | may-you-turn-them-towards | may-we-be | I | your | always | indeed | in-auspicious-giving | your | may-we-be | O Agni | with-protection | having-good-heroes. ॥ 9 ॥

<vocab>
**Waters** (Āpaḥ), **Savitar** (Sun-god/Impeller), **Agni** (Fire-god), **Son of Strength** (Sūno sahasaḥ - Agni is "born" from the physical strength used to rub fire-sticks together), **Healers** (Bhiṣajaḥ), **Mothers/Progenitors** (Janitrīḥ), **Golden-handed** (Hiraṇyapāṇiḥ), **Desirable wealth** (Vāryāṇi), **Sacrifice** (Adhvare).
</vocab>

<summary>This page contains prayers to the Waters (Apah), the Sun (Savitar), and Fire (Agni), seeking protection, health for descendants, and the bestowal of wealth and divine presence at the ritual.</summary>
<keywords>Waters, Savitar, Agni, healing, protection, golden-handed, sacrifice, prosperity, Son of Strength</keywords>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary for Rig Veda, Mandala 6, Hymn 50, Verse 9, and provides the full text and commentary for Verses 10 and 11. It maintains continuity from the previous discussion regarding Agni's role in the sacrifice and moves toward an invocation of the Ashvins and the broader pantheon of deities (the Vishvedevas).</meta>

# Rig Veda — Page 803
### Mandala 6, Hymn 50, Verse 9 (Continued)

## Commentary (Sayana) - Continued
[Concluding the commentary for Verse 9]

Moreover, O **son of strength** <note>original: "sahasaḥ sūno"</note>, O Agni, child of power, at this time in this **sacrifice** <note>original: "adhvare"</note> of ours, bring the **gods** <note>original: "devān"</note> who are to be worshipped, such as Indra and others, by turning them toward us. Furthermore, may I **always** <note>original: "sadmit"</note> remain within your **gift** <note>original: "rātau"</note> of wealth. Likewise, O Agni, through your **protection** <note>original: "avasā"</note>, may I be **endowed with good heroes** <note>original: "suvīraḥ"</note>—meaning sons, grandsons, and so on.

---

->॥ Now the Tenth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
[Verse 10]

And may those two **Truthful Ones** <note>original: "nāsatyā"</note> come to my **invocation** <note>original: "havam"</note> through our **prayers** <note>original: "dhībhiḥ"</note>, O wise ones. Just as you **freed** <note>original: "amumuktam"</note> the sage **Atri** from the great **darkness** <note>original: "tamasaḥ"</note>, O leaders, **save** <note>original: "tūrvatam"</note> us from **distress** <note>original: "duritāt"</note> in the face of conflict. ॥ 10 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
And | those two | my | invocation | to | come | Truthful ones | by prayers | you two | quickly | wise ones | Atri | like | great | from darkness | freed | save | O leaders | from distress | in the face of [conflict]. ॥ 10 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

Furthermore, O **wise ones** <note>original: "viprā"</note> of intelligent nature, O **Truthful ones** <note>original: "nāsatyā"</note>—meaning those whose nature is truth or who lead us to truth—O Ashvins, may you two come quickly to **my invocation** <note>original: "me havam"</note>, which is this hymn of praise, accompanied by these **prayers** <note>original: "dhībhiḥ"</note> or ritual acts of service. And having come, just as you **freed** <note>original: "amumuktam"</note> the sage **Atri** from the **great darkness** <note>original: "mahas tamasaḥ"</note> created by the demons, so too, O **leaders** <note>original: "narā"</note>, you two Ashvins, **save** <note>original: "tūrvatam"</note> us; cross us over from the **distress** <note>original: "duritāt"</note> or sorrow caused by enemies when **conflict** <note>original: "abhīke"</note> has arrived.

->॥ This concludes the ninth varga of the eighth adhyaya of the fourth ashtaka ॥<-

---

->॥ Now the Eleventh Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
[Verse 11]

O Gods, be the **givers** <note>original: "dātāraḥ"</note> to us of **wealth** <note>original: "rāyaḥ"</note> that is **splendid** <note>original: "dyumataḥ"</note>, **powerful** <note>original: "vājavataḥ"</note>, **accompanied by sons** <note>original: "nṛvataḥ"</note>, and **abundant** <note>original: "purukṣoḥ"</note>. O celestial ones, O earthly ones, O those born of the cow, and O those of the waters—be gracious to us. ॥ 11 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
Those | to us | wealth | splendid | powerful | givers | be | accompanied by men | abundant | revealing [desires] | celestial | earthly | born of the cow | of the waters | be gracious | and | O Gods. ॥ 11 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **gods** <note>original: "devāḥ"</note>, may you **be the givers** <note>original: "dātāro bhūta"</note> to us of **wealth** <note>original: "rāyaḥ"</note> that is **splendid** <note>original: "dyumataḥ"</note> or shining, **powerful** <note>original: "vājavataḥ"</note>, **accompanied by men** <note>original: "nṛvataḥ"</note> such as sons and followers, and **abundantly praised** <note>original: "purukṣoḥ"</note> by many. Furthermore, may you who **reveal** <note>original: "dṛśayantaḥ"</note> or grant our desires—the **celestial** <note>original: "divyāḥ"</note> ones (the Adityas existing in heaven), the **earthly** <note>original: "pārthivāsaḥ"</note> ones (the Vasus existing on earth), the **born of the cow** <note>original: "gojātāḥ"</note> (the Maruts, born from Prishni or from the middle-realm speech), and the **water-dwelling** <note>original: "apyāḥ"</note> ones (the Rudras existing in the waters of the atmosphere)—may all of you **make us happy** <note>original: "mṛḷata"</note> or grant us prosperity.

# Rig Veda — Page 804
### [Book 6, Hymn 50, Verses 12–14]

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Twelfth Verse ॥ <-

May **Rudra** and **Sarasvati**, acting in harmony, and the bountiful **Vishnu** and **Vayu** be gracious to us. May **Ribhuksha**, **Vaja**, the divine **Ordainer** <note>original: vidhātā</note>, and **Parjanya** and **Vata** increase our nourishment. ॥ 12 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
They | our | Rudra | Sarasvati | acting in harmony | the bountiful ones | Vishnu | may [they] be gracious | Vayu |
Ribhuksha | Vaja | divine | Ordainer | Parjanya and Vata | may [they] increase | nourishment | our ॥ 12 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **bountiful ones** <note>original: mīḷhuṣmantaḥ</note>, or those who grant the rain, may those gods be gracious to us; that is, may they make us happy. If one asks, "Who are they?", it is explained: **Rudra** <note>the storm god</note>, **Sarasvati** <note>the goddess of speech and rivers</note> acting in harmony, **Vishnu**, and **Vayu** <note>the wind</note>. 

**Ribhuksha** and **Vaja** refer to the three brothers known as the **Ribhus** <note>divine artisans, sons of Sudhanvan</note>. Ribhuksha is the eldest and Vaja is the youngest. This mention is an **allusion** <note>term: upalakṣaṇam - a figure of speech where a part represents the whole</note> that includes the middle brother, **Vibhvan**, as well. 

Furthermore, the divine **Ordainer** <note>vidhātā</note>, who is **Prajapati** <note>the Lord of Creatures</note>, and **Parjanya and Vata** <note>the rain-cloud and the wind</note>—may they both increase or swell our **nourishment** <note>original: iṣam</note>, which is to say, our food.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Thirteenth Verse ॥ <-

And may that divine **Savita** and **Bhaga** protect us; and may the **Son of the Waters** <note>original: apāṃ napāt</note>, the filler of gifts, protect us. May **Tvashtri** in harmony with the **wives of the gods**, and **Heaven** with the gods, and **Earth** with the **oceans**, be gracious. ॥ 13 ॥

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
And | that | divine | Savita | Bhaga | our | of the waters | Son | may [he] protect | gift | the filler |
Tvashtri | with the gods | with the wives | acting in harmony | Heaven | with the gods | Earth | with the oceans ॥ 13 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

And also, "that" <note>original: sya</note> well-known divine **Savita** <note>the solar stimulator</note>, who is famous everywhere as the impeller, and **Bhaga** <note>the distributor of wealth</note>, and the **Son of the Waters** <note>original: apāṃ napāt</note>—who is the son of the waters residing in the clouds, the **fire of the middle region** <note>lightning</note>—may he protect us. 

What is the nature of this Son of the Waters? He is the **filler** <note>original: papriḥ</note> or the protector of the **wealth that is to be given** <note>original: dānu</note>. <note>Sayana provides a technical grammatical justification here: the word "papriḥ" is derived from the root "pṛ" (to fill), and despite certain rules of grammar, it maintains its relationship with the objective case here.</note> 

Likewise, may **Tvashtri** <note>the divine architect</note>, who shares affection with the **gods** and their **wives** <note>original: janibhiḥ</note>, and **Heaven** <note>Dyaus</note> rejoicing with the gods, and **Earth** <note>Prithivi</note> rejoicing with the **oceans**—may all these deities protect us.

The verse "And may the Serpent of the Deep..." <note>RV 6.50.14</note> is indicated here. It is noted in the liturgical texts: *And may the Serpent of the Deep hear us, may the longing wives of the gods protect us* (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 5.20).

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ This is the Fourteenth Verse of the Hymn ॥ <-

And may the **Serpent of the Deep** <note>original: ahirbudhnyaḥ</note> hear us, and the **One-footed Goat** <note>original: aja ekapāt</note>, the **Earth**, and the **Ocean**. May all the **gods** who increase the **Sacred Law** <note>original: ṛta</note>, being invoked and praised with **mantras** uttered by **sages**, protect us. ॥ 14 ॥

# Rig Veda — Page 905
### [Mandala 6, Hymn 51, Verse 14 to Hymn 52, Verse 1]

## Hymn Text

**Rig Veda 6.51.14 (Word-by-word analysis)**
And | our | the Serpent of the Deep <note>original: ahiḥ budhnyaḥ</note> | may he hear | the Unborn One-Footed One <note>original: ajaḥ ekapāt</note> | Earth | Ocean |
All | Gods | the Increasers of Truth <note>original: ṛta-vṛdhaḥ</note> | being invoked | praised | to be counseled <note>original: maṃvāḥ</note> | lauded by sages | may [they] protect [us] ॥ 14 ॥

---

**Rig Veda 6.51.15**
->॥ Now the fifteenth verse ॥<-

Thus do the descendants of my lineage, the **Bharadvajas**, worship with prayers and songs of praise. O **Vasus** <note>the 'Bright Ones' or benevolent deities</note>, O All-Gods, you who are invincible and worthy of sacrifice, having been praised and offered oblations, and you, O **Gnas** <note>the wives of the gods</note>, be present at our sacrifice! ॥ 15 ॥

**(Word-by-word analysis)**
Thus | descendants | my | of that [one] | with prayers | the Bharadvajas | [they] worship | with songs of praise |
The wives of the gods | offered oblations | the Vasus | invincible | All | praised | be [you all] | worthy of sacrifice ॥ 15 ॥

---

**Rig Veda 6.52.1**
->॥ The first verse thereof ॥<-

That great and beloved eye of **Mitra** and **Varuna** rises, unerring and pure; it is the bright countenance of the Eternal Order <note>original: ṛta</note>, visible to all. Like a golden gem of the sky, it has shone forth upon its rising. ॥ 1 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

**On Verse 14:**
And also may the **Serpent of the Deep** <note>original: ahirbudhnyaḥ; a deity associated with the celestial depths or the atmospheric waters</note> hear our hymn. The **Unborn** <note>original: ajaḥ</note> refers to one who is without birth. The **One-Footed One** <note>original: ekapāt</note> is he who moves or arrives with a single support. May the deity signified by these two words, as well as the **Earth** and the **Ocean**, hear our hymn. Furthermore, may the **All-Gods** protect us. These gods are described as **Increasers of Truth** <note>original: ṛtāvṛdhaḥ</note>, meaning those who increase the sacrifice or the truth; they are **Invoked** <note>original: huvānāḥ</note> by us; they were **Praised** by the ancient seers; they are **To be counseled** <note>original: maṃvāḥ; meaning those to be addressed in secret or those who are the subject of sacred mantras</note>; and they are **Lauded by sages** <note>original: kaviśastāḥ</note>, meaning they are celebrated through the recitations of wise poets. May they protect us.

**On Verse 15:**
In this manner, I have praised the gods. The **descendants** <note>original: napātaḥ; literally 'grandsons' or 'offspring'</note> of my lineage—namely the Bharadvajas like Suhotra and others—worship and glorify the gods with **prayers** <note>original: dhībhiḥ</note> and with **songs of praise** <note>original: arkaiḥ</note> which are the means of worship. O **Worthy of Sacrifice** <note>original: yajatrāḥ</note>, O gods who are the **Vasus** <note>the dwellers or those who cause others to dwell</note>, you are **Invincible** <note>original: adhṛṣṭāḥ</note>, for you are harmed by none. You have been **Offered oblations** <note>original: hutāsaḥ</note> such as the sacrificial cakes. May all of you, along with the **Gnas** <note>the wives of the gods</note>, be praised by these worshipers.

->॥ This concludes the tenth section (varga) of the eighth chapter (adhyaya) of the fourth book (ashtaka) ॥<-

**Introduction to Hymn 52:**
The second hymn, beginning with "That [eye] rises" <note>original: udu tyat</note>, consists of sixteen verses. The seer is **Rijishvan**, and the deity is the **All-Gods** (Vishvedevas). The three verses starting from the thirteenth are in the **Ushnih** meter; the sixteenth is in **Anushtubh**; and the remaining verses are in **Trishtubh**. Thus it is stated in the Index <note>original: Anukramani</note>: "The eye rises... sixteen verses, Ushnih and Anushtubh at the end." The ritual application of the hymn follows.

## Critical Notes
- The commentary identifies the poet (Rishi) of Sukta 52 as **Rijishvan**.
- Verse 15 mention of **Gnā** is explained as the **wives of the gods** <gloss>original: devapatnyaścha</gloss>.
- The term **Māmvā** in verse 14 is interpreted as **to be counseled** <gloss>original: mantraṇīyā</gloss>, suggesting a deity who is the recipient of secret or sacred counsel.
- The meter for Sukta 52 shifts at the end, moving from the standard eleven-syllable Trishtubh to shorter meters for the concluding verses.

# Rig Veda — Page 906
### [Ashtaka 5, Adhyaya 4, Varga 11]

## Hymn Text
**Rig Veda 7.61.1 (Word-by-word analysis)**

Up | indeed | that | eye | great | of the two Mitras <note>The dual form here refers to the pair Mitra and Varuna</note> | comes forth | beloved | of the two Varunas | unassailable | of the Eternal Order <note>original: ṛtasya</note> | pure | beautiful countenance | golden ornament | like | of the sky | having risen | has shone forth ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

That famous eye, the illuminator, great and vast, is dear to Mitra and Varuna. The names "Mitra" and "Varuna" are used here in the dual sense to encompass both deities together. This eye is most beloved to them, unassailable <note>original: adabdham; meaning it cannot be harmed or deceived by demons</note>, pure, stainless, and beautiful to behold. Such is the countenance or the radiant power of the Sun, which belongs to the **Eternal Order** <note>original: ṛta; here referring to the cosmic truth or the sun itself</note>, and it rises facing all beings. When the Sun rises, that light shines forth like a **golden ornament** <note>original: rukma; a piece of jewelry or a bright disc</note> of the sky or the atmosphere.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

The wise one who knows the three sacred places of these gods, and their hidden births; the Sun, looking upon the upright and the crooked among mortals, watches over the ways of the noble. ॥ 2 ॥

**(Word-by-word analysis)**
Knows | who | three | sacred places | of these | of the gods | birth | hidden | indeed | and | the wise one |
Upright | among mortals | crooked | and | seeing | looks upon | the Sun | of the lord | ways ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The Sun <note>Surya</note> knows the three—meaning the three worlds—which are the **sacred places** <note>original: vidathyāni; places of knowledge or assembly</note> to be known. He, the wise and sagacious Sun, also knows the hidden <note>original: sanutaḥ; a term for that which is concealed or not easily perceived</note> birth of these gods who dwell in the three worlds in the forms of the **Vasus** <note>deities of light and elements</note>, **Rudras** <note>deities of storm and might</note>, and **Adityas** <note>solar deities</note>. That Sun, seeing as a witness the upright <note>good</note> deeds and the crooked <note>wicked</note> deeds existing among human beings, looks upon them all. He illuminates the entire world from every side. Thus, acting as the Lord <note>original: aryaḥ</note>, he reveals to humans the desires or goals that are to be attained.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the third verse ॥ <-

I praise you, the guardians of the great Order, and Aditi, Mitra, Varuna, the well-born, Aryaman, and Bhaga; those of unassailable intent, I address the purifiers with a wealth of song. ॥ 3 ॥

**(Word-by-word analysis)**
I praise | indeed | you | of the great | of the Order | guardians | Aditi | Mitra | Varuna | well-born |
Aryaman | Bhaga | of unassailable intent | toward | I speak | with wealth | the purifiers ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Gods, I praise <note>original: stuṣe</note> you who are the protectors of the great **Order** <note>original: ṛta; here interpreted as the sacred sacrifice</note>...

# Rig Veda — Page 807
### [Mandala 6, Hymn 51, Verse 3 cont.]

The word "u" <note>original: u; a particle often used for emphasis or to fill the meter</note> is a filler. The poet speaks of those same gods: **Aditi**, the mother of the gods who is never diminished; **Mitra** and **Varuna**; those of noble birth <note>original: sujātān</note>; **Aryaman** and **Bhaga**, whose holy works are unassailable <note>original: adabdhadhītīn; meaning their rituals or intentions cannot be harmed</note>; along with wealth; and the purifiers <note>original: pāvakān</note> who cleanse the entire universe. I declare my praise toward all such gods.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
The destroyers of enemies, the protectors of the virtuous, the unassailable, the great kings, the givers of fine dwellings; the youthful, the mighty, the rulers of heaven, the leaders, the sons of Aditi—I approach them, and Aditi, who desires our devotion. ॥ 4 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Destroyers of enemies | Protectors of the virtuous | Unassailable | Great | Kings | Of fine dwellings | Givers | Youthful | Mighty | Rulers | Of heaven | Leaders | Sons of Aditi <note>original: Ādityān</note> | I approach | Aditi | Desiring devotion ॥ 4 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Destroyers of enemies** <note>original: riśādasaḥ</note> refers to those who consume or cast down those who seek to harm. Alternatively, it means the eaters of those who injure. **Protectors of the virtuous** <note>original: satpatīn</note> are the guardians of good people. They are **unassailable** <note>original: adabdhān</note>, meaning they are not harmed by anyone. They are the **great kings**, the shining lords who are **givers of fine dwellings** <note>original: suvasanasya dātṄn</note> or beautiful places to live. They are **youthful**, eternally young, and possess **great might** <note>original: sukṣatrān</note>, which can mean either excellent wealth or great strength. They **rule** or dwell everywhere. The term "ruling" <note>original: kṣayataḥ</note> implies lordship. They are the **leaders** <note>original: nṄn</note> of the heavenly realm and the **sons of Aditi** <note>the solar deities</note>. I approach all such gods, as well as **Aditi**, the mother of the gods, who is **desirous of our devotion** <note>original: duvoyu; an archaic form meaning one who seeks our service or worship</note>. I reach out to them, or rather, I petition them.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O Father Heaven, O Mother Earth, O guileless Brother Agni, O Vasus, be gracious to us! All you sons of Aditi, and Aditi, being of one mind, grant us abundant protection and wide-reaching happiness. ॥ 5 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Heaven | Father | Earth | Mother | Guileless <note>original: adhruk; free from malice or treachery</note> | Agni | Brother | Vasus <note>a class of deities representing the elements</note> | Be gracious | To us | All | Sons of Aditi | Aditi | Of one mind | To us | Protection/Happiness | Abundant | Wide-reaching | Grant ॥ 5 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Heaven**, who takes the place of a father; O **Earth**, who takes the place of a mother and is **guileless** <note>original: adhruk; non-harming</note>; O **Agni**, who is like a brother; O **Vasus** <note>original: vasavaḥ; the indwellers or those who provide habitation</note>, you gods—all of you make us happy <note>original: mṄlata</note>. O all you **Adityas**, sons of Aditi, and O **Aditi** herself; you all, being **of one mind** <note>original: sajoṣāḥ; in unanimous agreement</note>, grant us **abundant protection** <note>original: śarma; can mean either happiness or a spacious house/shelter</note> and bestow it widely upon us.

# Rig Veda — Page 908
### [Mandala 6, Hymn 51, Verses 6–8]

->॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
> O Holy Ones, deliver us not to the wolf, nor to the she-wolf; deliver us not to anyone who seeks to harm us. For you are the guides of our bodies; you have become the masters of our strength and our splendor. ॥ 6 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Not | Us | To the wolf | To the she-wolf | To any such | Desiring to harm | Deliver | O Holy Ones <note>original: yajatrāḥ; those worthy of being worshipped through sacrifice</note> | You | Indeed | Are | Guides <note>original: rathyaḥ; literally "charioteers," meaning those who direct or lead</note> | Our | Of bodies | You | Of strength | Of splendor | Have become ॥ 6 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Holy Ones**, gods worthy of sacrifice, do **not deliver us**—do not bring us under the control—of the **wolf**, the injurious thief, nor to the **she-wolf**, his female counterpart. Alternatively, the **wolf** refers to the wild dog of the forest, and the **she-wolf** is its mate. Furthermore, do not hand us over to **any such** person who **seeks to harm** us, meaning any enemy who desires misfortune or disaster for us. For **you indeed** are the **guides** <note>original: rathyaḥ; leaders or drivers</note> of our **bodies**. You have also **become** the leaders of our **strength** <note>original: kṣayasya; interpreted here as power or dwellings</note> and our **splendor** <note>original: varcasas; refers to the power of our speech or radiance</note>. Therefore, the connection is: because you are our leaders, do not deliver us to our enemies.

---

->॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
> O Vasus, may we not suffer for the sin committed by another. May we not perform that act for which you take vengeance. O All-Gods, you truly rule over the whole world; let the enemy harm his own body. ॥ 7 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis:**
Not | Your <note>referring to the gods' subjects</note> | Sin | Committed by another | May we enjoy <note>original: bhujema; here meaning "to suffer the consequences of"</note> | Not | That | Action | O Vasus <note>the "Bright Ones" or "Dwellers"</note> | Which | You punish <note>original: cayadhve</note> | Of the whole | Indeed | You rule | O All-Gods | Himself | The enemy | Body | May he harm ॥ 7 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Gods, we who belong to **you** should **not suffer** <note>original: mā bhujema; let us not experience the fruit of</note> the **sin committed by another**, produced by our enemies. O **Vasus**, gods who cause the world to dwell, do not **punish** us <note>original: cayadhve; Sayana notes that the root 'ci' here means to injure or take vengeance</note> for the sin of a ritual performed incorrectly. May we **not perform that** sinful **action**. O **All-Gods**, **you indeed rule** over <note>original: kṣayatha</note> the entire world. Therefore, let our **enemy harm his own body** by himself. The intent is: "May you act in such a way that the enemy's malice recoils upon him."

---

->॥ Now the Eighth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
> Homage indeed is powerful; I seek homage. Homage supports the Earth and the Heaven. Homage is for the Gods; Homage rules over them. Even a sin already committed, I wash away with homage. ॥ 8 ॥

# Rig Veda — Page 909
### [Mandala 6, Hymn 51, Verses 8–10]

## Hymn Text

**Reverence | indeed | is formidable. | Reverence | [I] seek | to perform. | Reverence | sustained | the earth | and | the heaven. |**
**Reverence | to the gods. | Reverence | rules | over them. | Even | a committed | sin | through reverence | [I] seek | to drive away. ॥ 8 ॥** <note>This is the Padapatha or "word-path," which breaks down the Sanskrit compounds into their individual roots for clarity.</note>

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Leaving aside the inherent greatness of the gods for a moment, the poet declares that even the act of bowing to them is itself so glorious. He praises the gods using the logic of "how much more" <note>original: kaimutika-nyāya; a logical inference that if a lesser thing (reverence) is powerful, then the greater thing (the gods) must be even more so</note>.

**Reverence indeed** <note>original: nama it</note>—the act of salutation alone—is the most excellent strength or power. Indeed, everything is obtained through it. Therefore, **I seek to perform** <note>original: ā-vivāse</note> or practice that **reverence**. It is **reverence** alone that **sustained the earth and the heaven**. When the Earth and Heaven are honored by living beings, they remain for a long time to provide enjoyment to those beings. Therefore, I offer such **reverence to the gods**.

The **reverence** shown to **these** gods **rules** <note>original: īśe</note> or has power over them, because they are won over by it. Even an **already committed sin** <note>original: enaḥ</note> **I seek to drive away**—meaning I avoid or destroy it—**through reverence** and salutation.

---

-> ॥ Now the Ninth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**O you who are the charioteers of the Cosmic Order, of purified will, who sit in the home of the Cosmic Order, who are undeceived—**
**To those far-seeing leaders, to all of you who are great and worthy of worship, I bow down with my reverences. ॥ 9 ॥**

**Of the Cosmic Order | your | charioteers | of purified will | of the Cosmic Order | sitting in the home | undeceived |**
**To them | [I] bow | with reverences | far-seeing | leaders | to all | you | [I] bow | great | worthy of worship ॥ 9 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **worthy of worship** <note>original: yajatrāḥ; those to be honored with sacrifice</note> gods! You are the **charioteers** <note>original: rathyaḥ; the drivers or leaders</note> of **your Cosmic Order** <note>original: ṛtasya; here interpreted as the sacrifice or Yajña</note>. You are **of purified will** <note>original: pūta-dakṣān; possessing pure strength or skill</note>. You are **sitting in the home** <note>original: pastya-sadaḥ</note> belonging to the **Cosmic Order**, which refers to the house where the sacrifice is performed. You are **undeceived** <note>original: adabdhān; unharmed or unfooled</note> by demons and such. You are **far-seeing** <note>original: uru-cakṣasaḥ; literally "wide-eyed" or all-seeing</note> **leaders** of men. To all of **you**, who are **great**, I **bow down** <note>original: ā-name</note> in your presence with **reverences** or salutations. I am humbled before you.

-> ॥ Now the Tenth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**For they possess the most excellent splendor; they lead us across all difficulties.**
**The powerful ones: Varuna, Mitra, and Agni, whose thoughts are of the Truth, whose speech is truly governed. ॥ 10 ॥**

**They | for | of the most excellent splendor | they | indeed | us | across | all | difficulties | lead |**
**Powerful ones | Varuna | Mitra | Agni | whose thoughts are of the Truth | whose speech is truly governed ॥ 10 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

Those gods who possess the qualities that are about to be described **indeed** are **of the most excellent splendor** <note>original: śreṣṭha-varcasaḥ</note>; that is, they possess the most praiseworthy radiance.

<vocab>
- **Reverence (Namah):** A physical or mental act of bowing; in this context, it is treated as a potent force that can influence the divine and erase mistakes.
- **Cosmic Order (Rta):** The fundamental principle of truth and harmony in the universe, often identified with the ritual of sacrifice.
- **Charioteers (Rathyah):** A metaphor for the gods as the skilled drivers or directors of the world and the sacrifice.
- **Home (Pastya):** A dwelling-place; specifically the consecrated space where the sacred fire is kept.
</vocab>

Therefore, they indeed lead all our **sins** <note>original: duritā pāpāni</note> to be hidden or removed. That is to say: may they destroy them. They are truthful and unfailing toward those who praise them. This is how the sentence connects.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Verse 11 ॥ <-

**May Indra, the Earth, the Ground, Pushan, Bhaga, Aditi, and the Five Tribes increase [our prosperity].**
**May they be of good shelter, providers of good food, good leaders, good protectors, and good guardians for us. ॥ 11 ॥**

**Padapatha:**
They | for us | Indra | Earth | the ground | increasing | Pushan | Bhaga | Aditi | five | peoples | 
of good shelter | providers of good food | good leaders | may they be | for us | good protectors | good guardians ॥ 11 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

May those gods increase our **ground** <note>original: kṣāma</note>, meaning our place of residence. Who are they? Indra, the Earth, Pushan, Bhaga, and Aditi (the mother of the gods who is never diminished). Also the **five tribes** <note>original: pañca janāḥ</note>—this refers to the classes of beings mentioned in the sacred texts, such as gods, humans, Gandharvas, Apsaras, and others. May they all, for our sake, be **of good shelter** <note>original: su-śarmāṇaḥ</note> or bringing great happiness, **well-providing** <note>original: svavasaḥ</note> with excellent food, and **good leaders** <note>original: su-nīthāḥ</note> who bring us to our goals. The intent is: may they grant us excellent happiness and other blessings.

Likewise, let them be **good protectors** <note>original: su-cācāsaḥ</note> and **excellent guardians** <note>original: su-gopāḥ</note>. "Protection" <note>original: trāṇam</note> refers to saving us from enemies who are already present. "Guarding" <note>original: gopanam</note> refers to protection by preventing those enemies from even arising or being born.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Verse 12 ॥ <-

**Now may the Invoker of the Bharadvaja clan reach the divine dwelling, O Gods; he seeks your benevolence.**
**The sacrificer, along with those who sit at the ritual and offer wisdom, has praised the birth of the gods, desiring wealth. ॥ 12 ॥**

**Padapatha:**
Now | dwelling | divine | reach | Gods | Bharadvaja | benevolence | seeks | Invoker |
with those who sit | the sacrificer | with the wise | of the gods | birth | desiring wealth | has praised ॥ 12 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

In this verse, the seer speaks of himself in the third person. O **Gods**, may this **Invoker** <note>original: hotā</note>, this praiser-seer born of the **Bharadvaja** lineage, quickly **reach** <note>original: naṃśi</note> the **dwelling** <note>original: sadmānam</note> that exists in heaven. Furthermore, he **seeks** <note>original: yāti</note> your **benevolence** <note>original: sumatim</note>, which is your gracious and favoring mind. The word *yāti* here is used in the sense of "to ask" or "request." To that end, along with other **sacrificers** <note>original: yajamānaiḥ</note> who are **seated** <note>original: āsānebhiḥ</note> at the ritual and who are **wise** <note>original: miyadhaiḥ</note> or possessors of sacred knowledge...

Indra, Earth, Pushan, Bhaga, Aditi, Five Tribes (Pancha Janah), Bharadvaja, Invoker (Hota), Sacrificer (Yajamana), Ground (Kshama), Benevolence (Sumati)
</vocab>

The sacrificer <note>original: yajamāno</note>, while performing the sacrifice, and the sage <note>original: rishi</note>, desiring wealth <note>original: vasuyuḥ; literally "seeking riches for himself"</note>, has praised the birth <note>original: janma</note> or the assembly <note>original: saṃgham</note> of the gods. He praises them or hymns them.

On the fourth day of the **Ten-Night rite** <note>original: Daśarātra</note>, during the **Prauga-shastra** recitation <note>a specific series of hymns recited for various deities</note>, the verse "Away that crooked one" is used. It belongs to a triplet <note>original: tṛca</note> dedicated to the All-Gods <note>original: Vaiśvadeva</note>. This is also indicated in the ritual manuals: "Away that crooked enemy, the river, the most river-like" is the triplet in the Anushtubh meter for the Prauga-shastra (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 7.11).

## Hymn Text

**O Agni, drive away that crooked enemy, the thief who is evil-minded.**
**O Lord of the Good, make our path easy and far-reaching. ॥ 13 ॥**

**Pada-patha:**
Away | that | crooked | enemy | thief | O Agni | evil-minded |
farthest | of this | Lord of the Good | make | easy-going ॥ 13 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, cast away <note>original: apasya; from the root 'as' meaning to throw</note> to the **farthest** distance that well-known **crooked** <note>original: vṛjinam</note> or wicked **enemy** who commits sins, and the **thief** who is a harmer and **evil-minded** <note>original: durādhyam; one who contemplates harm or has wicked intentions</note>. O **Lord of the Good** <note>original: satpate; protector of the righteous</note>, O Agni, **make** for us a **path that is easy to travel** <note>original: sugam</note> and pleasant. In this context, because Agni is being praised as the embodiment of all the gods, the verse is classified as being dedicated to the All-Gods <note>original: Vaiśvadeva</note>.

->॥ Now the fourteenth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

**O Soma, these pressing-stones have indeed increased for our friendship.**
**Slay the devourer, the stingy merchant, for he is a wolf. ॥ 14 ॥**

**Pada-patha:**
The pressing-stones | O Soma | our | indeed | [filler] | for friendship | have increased |
slay | [down] | the devourer | the stingy merchant | a wolf | indeed | he ॥ 14 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Soma**, these **pressing-stones** <note>original: grāvāṇo; stones used to extract the sacred juice</note> of ours **have increased**—that is, they desire—your **friendship**. The word **kam** is a filler used to complete the verse, and **hi** expresses the reason. Because this is so, you must **utterly slay** the **stingy merchant** <note>original: paṇim; the Panis were a class of demons or misers who hoarded wealth and cattle</note> and the **devourer** <note>original: atriṇam; a demon or creature that swallows or eats greedily</note>. This merchant is truly a **wolf** <note>original: vṛkaḥ</note> because he is intent on taking away from others and is always stealing from us. Therefore, the meaning is that you should destroy him. The root of the word for wolf <note>original: vṛka</note> comes from a root meaning "to take or seize."

->॥ Now the fifteenth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

**For you are bounteous givers, O gods, with Indra as your chief, looking upon the heavens.**
**Protect our homes and make our paths easy for us. ॥ 15 ॥**

---

<vocab>
- <term>vṛjina</term>: "crooked" or "wicked," referring to moral or physical obstacles.
- <term>stena</term>: "thief" or "robber," often used for those who steal sacrificial offerings or cattle.
- <term>satpati</term>: "Lord of the Good," a title for a protector of the righteous.
- <term>grāvan</term>: "pressing-stone," the sacred stones used to crush the Soma plant.
- <term>paṇi</term>: a "miserly merchant" or demon who withholds wealth from the gods and humans.
- <term>atrin</term>: "devourer," a type of demon associated with consumption and destruction.
- <term>sudānu</term>: "bounteous givers," an epithet for the gods who grant rain or gifts.
- <term>praüga-śastra</term>: a specific ritual recitation during the morning libation of the Soma sacrifice.
</vocab>

## Hymn Text

-> **[RV 6.51.15 Padapatha]** <-

You | indeed | are | O bounteous ones | with Indra as your chief | heavenly-radiant |
make | for us | on the path | hither | easy-going | protectors | at home ॥ 15 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **bounteous ones** <note>original: su-dānavaḥ; those who give excellent gifts</note>, you gods **are** <note>original: stha</note> indeed present. You are certainly capable and prosperous. **With Indra as your chief** <note>original: indra-jyeṣṭhāḥ</note> means those for whom Indra is the eldest or principal leader. You are **heavenly-radiant** <note>original: abhidyavaḥ</note>, meaning your light reaches toward the heavens. Being our **protectors** <note>original: gopāḥ</note> along every **path** <note>original: adhvani</note>, and being with us **at home** <note>original: amā</note> or in our company, **make** <note>original: kartṛ; used here for the imperative 'kuru'</note> the way **easy to travel** <note>original: su-gam</note> and pleasant. The particle 'ā' is used for emphasis. Make it truly easy.

<note>Ritual Note:</note> This verse beginning "We have reached the path" is to be muttered by the **sacrificer** <note>original: yajamāna</note> when returning from a journey. This is indicated in the *Asvalayana Shrauta Sutra* (2.5): "Having returned, holding a piece of fuel in hand, he says: 'We have reached the path that leads to well-being...'"

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ This is the sixteenth verse of the hymn ॥ <-
-> **[RV 6.51.16]** <-

**We have reached the path that leads to well-being, which is without harm,**
**by which one avoids all enemies and finds wealth. ॥ 16 ॥**

-> **[RV 6.51.16 Padapatha]** <-

Hither | the path | we have reached | leading to well-being | without harm |
by which | all | around | enemies | he avoids | he finds | wealth ॥ 16 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

We have **reached** <note>original: aganmahi</note> or arrived at the **path** <note>original: panthām</note>. What kind of path? One that is **safe to travel** <note>original: svasti-gām; easy to traverse with comfort</note> and **without harm** <note>original: anehasam; free from sin or obstruction</note>. By this path, a traveler **avoids** <note>original: pari-vṛṇakti; wards off or bypasses</note> all **enemies** <note>original: dviṣo; hostile people</note> and **finds** <note>original: vindate</note> **wealth** <note>original: vasu</note>. Such is the nature of the path we have attained.

-> ॥ Thus ends the thirteenth varga of the eighth chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-

## Sukta Introduction (RV 6.52)

The third hymn, beginning with **"Not that indeed"** <note>original: na tad-viva</note>, contains seventeen verses. The **Rishi** <note>the sage to whom the hymn was revealed</note> is **Rijishvan**. It is dedicated to the **All-Gods** <note>original: Vaiśvadevam</note>. The first six verses are in the **Trishtubh** meter; from the seventh verse onwards, six verses (7-12) are in the **Gayatri** meter; the thirteenth is **Trishtubh**; the fourteenth is **Jagati**; and the remaining three are **Trishtubh**. This is as described in the *Anukramani* <note>the Vedic index</note>: "Not that... is one verse short of the full count <note>referring to a specific meter variation</note>, then seven following are Gayatri, the fourteenth is Jagati." The ritual application <note>original: viniyoga</note> has been stated previously.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the first verse ॥ <-
-> **[RV 6.52.1]** <-

**I do not think it can be done by the sky, nor by the earth, nor by the sacrifice, nor by these ritual acts.**
**May the well-formed mountains crush him; may the performer of an excessive sacrifice be cast down. ॥ 1 ॥**

-> **[RV 6.52.1 Padapatha]** <-

Not | that | by the sky | not | by the earth | along | I think | not | by the sacrifice | not | and | by ritual acts | these |
let them crush | him | the well-formed | mountains | down | let him be cast | of the excessive sacrifice | the performer ॥ 1 ॥

<vocab>
- **bounteous ones** <term>sudānavaḥ</term>: gods who are generous givers.
- **with Indra as chief** <term>indrajyeṣṭhāḥ</term>: the group of gods led by Indra.
- **heavenly-radiant** <term>abhidyavaḥ</term>: reaching toward or shining from the heavens.
- **All-Gods** <term>vaiśvadevam</term>: a collective invocation of the Vedic pantheon.
- **Rijishvan** <term>ṛjiṣvan</term>: the seer (Rishi) of this particular hymn.
- **Trishtubh/Gayatri/Jagati**: standard rhythmic patterns (meters) used in Vedic chanting.
- **ritual application** <term>viniyogaḥ</term>: the specific time or ceremony when a verse is recited.
- **performer of sacrifice** <term>yaṣṭā</term>: the one who offers the oblation.
</vocab>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on the first verse of Rig Veda, Mandala 6, Sukta 52, and contains the full text and explanation for verses 2 and 3. The previous page discussed the arrival at a safe path; this page shifts to a polemic against a rival sacrificer (Atiyaja) and a plea for divine protection against those who despise the sacred hymns.</meta>

### Page 813

## Commentary (Sayana)
**[Continued from previous page for Mantra 1]**

A certain sage named **Atiyaja** <note>literally: "The Over-Sacrificer"</note>, thinking, "I shall be superior among those who possess the soma-dregs <note>original: rjiṣvatsu</note>," sacrificed to the gods. The Rishi <note>Rijishvan, the seer of this hymn</note> rejects that sacrifice of his in this first verse. I do not agree that the sacrifice of this Atiyaja is accompanied by the **heavenly** <note>original: divā</note> host of gods. I do not grant it my approval. Nor do I agree that it is accompanied by the earthly host of gods. Nor do I agree that it is equal to the **sacrifice** <note>original: yajñena</note> performed by me. Furthermore, I do not agree that it is equal to these ritual **labors** <note>original: śamībhiḥ</note> and other actions performed by me. The sense is: the gods, having been won over by me, do not accept his sacrifice, and he, due to his ignorance, is unable to sacrifice correctly. Moreover, may the **mountains** <note>original: parvatāsaḥ</note>, well-disposed and sent by Indra, strike down and destroy that sage. The word *ujjh* implies the act of killing or abandoning. Likewise, let the priest of that Atiyaja—who is possessed by the prideful thought, "I sacrifice to the gods more than Rijishvan does"—be utterly **degraded** <note>original: nī hīyatām</note> and brought low.

---

-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O **Maruts**, whoever thinks himself superior to us, or whoever seeks to revile the **prayer** <note>original: brahma</note> being performed; let **burning heats** <note>original: tapūṃṣi</note> be obstacles for him. Let **Heaven** <note>original: dyauḥ; here meaning the Sun</note> blaze against that hater of prayer. ॥ 2 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Beyond | or | who | O Maruts | thinks | us | prayer | or | who | being performed | wishes to revile |
burning-heats | for him | obstacles | let they be | hater-of-prayer | against | him | let blaze | Heaven ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Maruts** <note>storm deities and companions of Indra</note>, whatever person **thinks beyond** <note>original: ati-manyate</note> us—that is, considers his own superiority and thinks himself greater than us—or whoever desires to **revile** <note>original: ninitsāt</note> the **prayer** <note>original: brahma</note> or hymn of praise being performed by us, for that person, let **burning heats** <note>original: tapūṃṣi</note> or fiery energies become **obstacles** <note>original: vṛjināni</note> or sources of pain. Let them be so. Let **Heaven** <note>original: dyauḥ</note>, in the form of the Sun, **blaze against** <note>original: abhi-śocatu</note> that enemy who is a hater of prayer. Let it scorch him; let it burn him up.

---

-> ॥ Now the third verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Why indeed, **Soma**, do they call you the **guardian** <note>original: gopām</note> of prayer? Why indeed do they call you our **protector from insults**? Why indeed do you look at us while we are being **reviled**? Hurl your burning weapon at the hater of prayer. ॥ 3 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Why | indeed | you | of prayer | Soma | guardian | why | indeed | you | they call | protector-from-insults | our |
why | indeed | us | do you see | being reviled | hater-of-prayer | burning | weapon | hurl ॥ 3 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
The words **why indeed** <note>original: kim aṅga</note> are two particles used to express a well-known fact. O **Soma** <note>the deity of the sacred ritual drink</note>, the ancient knowers call **you** the **guardian** <note>original: gopām</note> or protector of the **prayer** <note>original: brahmaṇaḥ</note>, meaning the sacred mantra, the ritual act, or the priestly class. They say this. Likewise...

<vocab>
मरुतः (Marutas - storm deities), सोम (Soma - ritual drink/deity), ब्रह्म (Brahma - prayer/hymn), गोपा (Gopa - protector/guardian), निद्यमानान् (Nidyamanan - those being reviled/blamed), तपूंषि (Tapumshi - burning heat/power), वृजिनानि (Vrijinani - obstacles/evils)
</vocab>

<summary>This page describes a rivalry between the sage Rijishvan and a pretender named Atiyaja, followed by a prayer to the Maruts and Soma to protect the sanctity of the hymns and punish those who despise them with "burning weapons."</summary>

## Commentary (Sayana)
**[Continued from previous page for Verse 3]**

Indeed, they call you the **protector from curses** <note>original: abhiśastipām</note>—the one who guards us from those who would revile us. Alternatively, the word *anga* is used to address you directly. O **Soma**, for what reason do they call you the guardian of the **sacred prayer** <note>original: brahmaṇo gopām; here "brahman" refers to the Vedic hymn or the ritual prayer</note>? Or for what reason do they call you our protector from insults? O Soma, why do you look on with indifference while we are being insulted and tormented by others? Everyone proclaims you alone to be the protector of the prayer and the guardian against enemies; therefore, your apathy while we are being slandered by others is improper. Therefore, hurl your **burning weapon** <note>original: tapuṣiṃ heti; a glowing or heat-emitting missile</note> at the hater of prayer—at the one who hates the priest. Cast it; send it forth against him.

---

->॥ Now the fourth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
May the **Dawns** <note>original: uṣaso</note> as they arise protect me; may the flowing **Rivers** <note>original: sindhavaḥ</note> as they swell protect me; may the firm **Mountains** <note>original: parvatāso</note> protect me; may the **Fathers** <note>original: pitaro; the ancestral spirits</note> protect me at the **invocation of the gods** <note>original: devahūtau</note>. ॥ 4 ॥

> **Word-by-word Analysis:**
> May they protect; me; the Dawns; arising; may they protect; me; the Rivers; swelling; may they protect; me; the Mountains; firm; may they protect; me; the Fathers; at the invocation of the gods. ॥ 4 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
May the Dawns, as they manifest and appear, protect me. Likewise, may the Rivers, characterized by their flowing motion and increasing in volume, protect me. Similarly, may the firm and immovable Mountains protect me. Also, at the "invocation of the gods"—which refers to the **sacrifice** <note>original: yāgaḥ</note> where the gods are called upon—may the Fathers, the ancestral deities present there, protect me.

---

->॥ Now the fifth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
May we always be of **good mind** <note>original: sumanasaḥ</note>; may we truly behold the **Sun** <note>original: sūryam</note> as it rises. May the **Lord of Riches** <note>original: vasupatiḥ</note>, the swiftest to come with aid, who brings the gods, do so for us. ॥ 5 ॥

> **Word-by-word Analysis:**
> At all times; good-minded; may we be; may we behold; truly; the Sun; rising; so; may he do; the Lord of Riches; of riches; the gods; bringing; with aid; the swiftest to come. ॥ 5 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Gods, may we at all times be of "good mind"—meaning may we possess noble and auspicious thoughts. The word *nu* is used here for emphasis or conjunction. May we also always behold the Sun as it rises in the sky. May **Agni** <note>Sayana identifies the "Lord of Riches" here as the fire-god Agni</note>, who is the supreme master of all wealth and who "brings" <note>original: ohānaḥ</note> or carries the gods to our sacrifice by means of our offerings, and who is the most frequent visitor among those who come to help—may he, being endowed with these qualities, "do so." That is, may he make us such as we have described—prosperous and possessed of noble minds.

->॥ Thus ends the fourteenth section (varga) of the eighth chapter (adhyaya) in the fourth book (ashtaka) ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the sixth verse ॥ <-

May **Indra** come most closely with his protection; may **Sarasvati** come, swelling with her rivers; may **Parjanya**, the source of happiness, come to us with the medicinal plants; and may **Agni**, who is well-praised and easy to invoke, come to us like a father. ॥ 6 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Indra**; most closely; with protection; come; **Sarasvati**; with rivers; swelling; **Parjanya**; to us; with plants; source of happiness; **Agni**; well-praised; easy to invoke; like a father. ॥ 6 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

May this Indra come most closely—meaning as near as possible—together with his protection or guardianship. May the goddess Sarasvati, in the form of a river, also come, swelling and increasing with her flowing waters. May Parjanya <note>The Vedic deity of rain and thunder, often associated with the fertility of the earth.</note>, along with the medicinal plants, be the bringer of happiness to us. And may Agni <note>The god of fire and the mediator of sacrifices.</note> be like a father—just as a father is the progenitor and protector of his son—one who is easily praised with happiness and easily called upon.

**Ritual Application:**
In the **Agrayana** <term>Āgrayaṇa: The Vedic sacrifice of the "first-fruits" of the harvest</term> ceremony, the verse beginning "All you gods, come..." serves as the invitatory prayer for the offering to the **Universal Gods** <note>original: Viśve Devāḥ</note>. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "All you gods, come hither, you who are of the earth, of great might, and skilled in wonders" (Asvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.9).

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ This is the seventh verse of the hymn ॥ <-

O **Universal Gods**, come here! Hear this, my invocation! Sit down upon this **sacred grass**. ॥ 7 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
All; **Gods**; come; hear; my; this; invocation; [come] to; this; **sacred grass**; sit down. ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Universal Gods, all you deities, come here! Having arrived, hear this, my call or invitation. Having heard it, sit down upon this strewn **sacred grass** <term>Barhis: The sacrificial grass (usually Kusha grass) spread out on the altar as a seat for the gods</term>. Be seated upon the grass that has been prepared for you.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the eighth verse ॥ <-

O Gods, to that man who honors you with an offering dripping with **clarified butter**, all of you, go unto him. ॥ 8 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
He who; for you; O **Gods**; with **ghee**-dripping; offering; honors/serves; him; all; go near. ॥ 8 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Gods, whatever person honors and serves you with a sacrificial offering <note>original: havya</note> that is dripping with **ghee** <note>original: ghṛta; clarified butter, the primary substance used in Vedic fire rituals</note>, all of you should go near to that person. Be present with him.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the ninth verse ॥ <-

May the **sons of the Immortal One** hear our songs; may they be most gracious to us. ॥ 9 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
To [us]; our; **sons**; songs/prayers; let them hear; of the **Immortal**; who [are]; most gracious/merciful; let them be; to us. ॥ 9 ॥

<note>The commentary for Verse 9 likely continues on the following page. The "sons of the Immortal" refers to the gods, who are born of the eternal cosmic order.</note>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on Verse 9 of Rig Veda, Mandala 6, Hymn 52, and provides the text and commentary for Verses 10, 11, and 12. These verses continue the invocation of the "Universal Gods" (Viśve Devāḥ), Indra, and Agni.</meta>

May the sons of the deathless <note>original: "amṛtasya"</note> Lord of Creatures <note>original: "prajāpateḥ"</note>—those gods—listen to our words of praise. May they be very kind to us and grant us happiness.

-> ॥ Now the tenth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
May the **Universal Gods**, who increase the Sacrifice <note>original: "ṛtāvṛdhaḥ"; those who foster the eternal order or the ritual</note>, hearing our call at the proper seasons, enjoy the fitting milk-offering. ॥ 10 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
Universal; Gods; increasers-of-Sacrifice; with-seasons; hearing-the-call; may-they-enjoy; fitting; milk. ॥ 10 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
"Increasers of the Sacrifice" <note>original: "ṛtāvṛdhaḥ"</note> means those who cause the sacrifice to grow. "Hearing our call at the proper seasons" refers to those who hear the calls of praise at specific times and are praised during those various appointed hours. May these Universal Gods enjoy the fitting milk, which is in the form of **Amiksha** <term>Āmiksā: A ritual offering made of curdled milk</term>. Indeed, the scripture says: "He brings curds into that milk; that is the Amiksha for the Universal Gods."

---

-> ॥ Thus ends the fifteenth varga of the eighth adhyaya of the fourth ashtaka ॥ <-

---

-> ॥ Now the eleventh verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
I praise **Indra** with his host of **Maruts**, accompanied by **Tvashtar**, **Mitra**, and **Aryaman**; may they enjoy these our offerings. ॥ 11 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
I-praise; Indra; Marut-host; accompanied-by-Tvashtar; Mitra; Aryaman; these; offerings; may-they-enjoy; us. ॥ 11 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
May Indra—whose attendants or followers are the host of Maruts <note>The storm deities who accompany Indra in battle</note>—along with Tvashtar <note>The celestial smith or architect of the gods</note>, and Mitra and Aryaman, enjoy our praise and these ritual offerings.

---

-> ॥ Now the twelfth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O **Agni**, Invoker, worship the divine host at this our sacrifice in the proper order of knowledge, for you are the wise one. ॥ 12 ॥

**Pada-patha:**
This; our; Agni; sacrifice; O-Invoker; in-order-of-knowledge; worship; wise-one; divine; people. ॥ 12 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Invoker <note>original: "hotar"</note> Agni, who calls the gods! You, being wise and knowing the divine host <note>original: "daivyaṃ janam"</note>—the assembly of gods worthy of worship—worship them at this our non-violent sacrifice <note>original: "adhvaram"</note>. Do so in the proper order of knowledge <note>original: "vayunaśaḥ"</note>, according to the sequence in which the gods are mentally arranged for the ritual.

Regarding the **Vaishvadeva Shastra** <term>Vaiśvadeva Śastra: A specific recitation addressed to all the gods during the Soma sacrifice</term>, the verse "All you gods..." is used as the concluding prayer <note>original: "yājyā"</note>. It is also indicated in the ritual texts: "Having recited the verse 'For the hearing...', he should whisper the prayer 'All you gods, hear this my call...'" (Asvalayana Shrauta Sutra 5.18). This same verse is also the concluding prayer for the animal sacrifice dedicated to the Universal Gods. It is indicated: "**All you gods, hear this my call, you who are of the earth, of great might, and skilled in wonders**" (Asvalayana Shrauta Sutra 3.7).

<meta>This page continues the transcription and commentary of Rig Veda, Mandala 6, Hymn 52. The previous page (816) covered verses 10 through 12, focusing on the Universal Gods and Indra. This page provides the text and commentary for verses 13 and 14, emphasizing the invitation of the gods to the ritual and the poet's desire for pure speech.</meta>

-> ॥ This is the thirteenth verse in the hymn ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O **Universal Gods**, hear this my call, you who are in the atmosphere and you who are near the sky.
You who are **Agni-tongued** <note>original: "agnijihvā"; those who use fire as their tongue to consume offerings</note> and worthy of worship, sitting on this sacrificial grass, delight yourselves. ॥ 13 ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown (Pada-patha):**
Universal; Gods; hear; this; call; my; who; in the atmosphere; who; near; the sky; are.
Who; Agni-tongued; and; or; worthy-of-worship; having-sat; on-this; sacrificial-grass; delight-yourselves. ॥ 13 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Universal Gods** <note>original: "viśve devāḥ"</note>, hear this **call** or invitation of mine. You who **are** <note>original: "stha"</note> present in the atmosphere; and you who are in the vicinity of the earth; and you who are in **heaven** <note>original: "dyavi"</note>. And you who are **Agni-tongued**—this means those for whom Agni (Fire) holds the place of a tongue. Alternatively, it means the "tongue of Agni," because the gods are nourished by that tongue; thus they are called "Agni-tongued." Moreover, all you who are **worthy of worship** <note>original: "yajatrā"</note>, having sat down on this strewn **sacrifical grass** <term>Barhis: A layer of sacred grass (kusha) spread on the sacrificial ground as a seat for the deities</term>, **delight yourselves** <note>original: "mādayadhvam"</note>; that is, gratify yourselves with the Soma juice.

---

-> ॥ Now the fourteenth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
May the worshipful **Universal Gods** hear my prayer; may both **Heaven and Earth** and the **Son of the Waters** hear my hymn.
May I not speak words that are blameworthy; being very close to you, may we delight in your blessings. ॥ 14 ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown (Pada-patha):**
Universal; Gods; my; may-they-hear; worshipful; both; Heaven-and-Earth; of-the-waters; Son; and; hymn.
May-not; your; words; blameworthy; I-speak; in-blessings; indeed; your; nearest; may-we-delight. ॥ 14 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
May the **Universal Gods** who are **worthy of worship** <note>original: "yajñiyā"</note> **hear my hymn** <note>original: "manma"</note>, which is a song of praise to be meditated upon. Let them hold it in their minds. Likewise, may both **Heaven and Earth** <note>original: "rodasī"</note> and the **Son of the Waters** <note>original: "apām napāt"</note>—referring to the Fire of the middle region <note>lightning</note>—hear our hymn.

Now the poet addresses the gods directly: O Gods, **may I not speak** <note>original: "mā vocam"</note> **blameworthy** <note>original: "paricakṣyāṇi"</note> **words** or hymns to you. This means I should not utter songs that are to be avoided or rejected, but rather those that are proper. Therefore, being **nearest** <note>original: "antamāḥ"</note> to you, may we **delight** <note>original: "madema"</note> or rejoice only in the **blessings** <note>original: "sumneṣu"</note> or happiness granted by you.

In the *Agrayana* ritual <term>Āgrayaṇa: An offering of the first fruits of the harvest</term>, this verse "May the gods of the earth..." is used as the consecrating verse (yajya). This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "Universal Gods, come hither, those who are on the earth, the great ones, the masters of mystic power" (Aśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 2.9). This same verse is used as the consecrating verse for the cake-offering (purodasha) to the Universal Gods. The ritual rule has been cited accordingly.

<summary>This page contains verses 13 and 14 of Hymn 52, where the poet invites the gods from all realms (earth, atmosphere, and heaven) to sit on the sacred grass and listen to a pure, blameless hymn of praise.</summary>
<keywords>Universal Gods, Agni-tongued, Son of the Waters, Heaven and Earth, Sacrificial Grass, Agrayana ritual, Pure Speech, Sayanacharya</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the translation of Rig Veda, Mandala 6, Hymn 52. The previous page (817) concluded with verse 14, where the poet called upon the Universal Gods and the Earth to protect the ritual and ensure pure speech. # Rig Veda [Book 4, Chapter 8, Section 16.]

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ This is the fifteenth verse in the hymn ॥ <-

Whatever mighty ones, with profound wisdom <note>original: "ahimāyāḥ"; literally meaning those whose wisdom is unfailing or as vast as the sky</note>, were born on the **earth** <note>original: "jmā"</note>, in the **sky**, or in the **gathering place of the waters** <note>original: "apāṃ sadhasthe"; a reference to the mid-air or atmosphere where clouds form</note>.
May those gods provide for us all through our **life**, throughout the **nights** and the **days**, for the sake of our desired nourishment. ॥ 15 ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown (Pada-patha):**
Those; whichever; and; earth; mighty; profound-wisdom; sky; were-born; waters; gathering-place.
They; for-us; for-desire; all; life; nights; days; let-them-provide; gods. ॥ 15 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **mighty ones** <note>original: "mahinā"</note> are the great ones who possess **profound wisdom** <note>original: "ahimāyāḥ"</note>. Wisdom <note>original: "māyā"</note> here refers to knowledge; thus, they possess knowledge that is unfailing. Whichever such **gods** appeared or **were born** <note>original: "jajñire"</note> on the **earth** <term>Jmā: An ancient Vedic term for the Earth</term>; and whichever were born from the **sky** <note>original: "divo"</note> or heaven; and whichever were born in the **gathering place of the waters** <note>original: "apāṃ sadhasthe"</note>, meaning together in the atmosphere—may all **those gods provide** <note>original: "varivasyantu"</note> or grant to **us**, for our **desire** <note>original: "iṣaye"</note> (which refers to that which is desired, such as sons and grandsons), **all life** <note>original: "viśvam āyur"</note>, meaning food or longevity. May they do so during all **nights** <note>original: "kṣapaḥ"</note> and all **days** <note>original: "usrāḥ"</note>, providing for us constantly and without interruption.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the sixteenth verse ॥ <-

O **Agni and Parjanya** <note>The Fire God and the Rain God</note>, protect my **prayer** in this **invocation**, you who are easy to call; protect our beautiful **hymn of praise**.
One of you **generates nourishment**, the other **generates the embryo**; grant us **food** that is accompanied by **offspring**. ॥ 16 ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown (Pada-patha):**
Agni-and-Parjanya; protect; prayer; my; in-this; invocation; easy-to-call; beautiful-praise; our.
Food; one; generates; embryo; the-other; offspring-possessing; food; grant; to-us. ॥ 16 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni and Parjanya**, **protect** <note>original: "avataṃ"</note> or guard **my prayer** <note>original: "dhiyaṃ"</note>, which is the ritual act of this sacrifice. Come to it, or protect it. O you two who are **easy to call** <note>original: "suhavā"</note>, protect our **beautiful praise** <note>original: "suṣṭutiṃ"</note> in **this invocation** or sacrifice. Alternatively, the word "protect" is understood in the sense of hearing; thus, "Hear our praise." Between the two of you, **one** (Parjanya, the Rain God) **generates nourishment** <note>original: "iḷām"</note> or food. Indeed, through rain, herbs and trees are born, and from them, food is produced. The **other** (Agni, the Fire God) **generates the embryo** <note>original: "garbhaṃ"</note>. This refers to the idea that food eaten by a person is cooked by the **internal digestive fire** <term>Jāṭharāgni: The "belly-fire" or metabolic heat believed in Vedic science to transform food into vital fluids and reproductive energy</term>, which then turns into semen, and that becomes the embryo in women. Therefore, you two **grant** or establish in **us** such **food** <note>original: "iṣo"</note> that is **joined with offspring** <note>original: "prajāvatīḥ"</note>.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the seventeenth verse ॥ <-

With the **sacrificial grass** <term>Barhis: The sacred kusha grass spread as a seat for the gods</term> strewn and the **fire kindled**, I worship with a **hymn** and with great **reverence**.
O worshipful ones, **Universal Gods**, rejoice in the **oblation** at this sacrifice today. ॥ 17 ॥

<summary>This page concludes the 52nd hymn of Mandala 6, invoking all gods from the three realms and specifically praising Agni and Parjanya for their roles in producing food and life. It highlights the Vedic belief in the connection between natural elements (rain/fire) and human biological processes (digestion/procreation).</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Parjanya, Universal Gods, sacrifice, nourishment, embryo, digestive fire, ritual prayer, Barhis</keywords>
