<meta>This page continues the transition from the hymns to Ushas (Dawn) into the hymns dedicated to the Maruts (the Storm-Gods). Specifically, this page covers the ritual instructions and the first two verses of Mandala 6, Hymn 66 of the Rig Veda.</meta>

[Page 862]

# 862 || Rig Veda || [5th Ashtaka, 1st Adhyaya, 7th Varga]

<note>This introductory section details the ritual usage (viniyoga) of the hymn in Vedic sacrifices.</note>

It is chanted as the eleventh hymn to the Maruts. During the "Shifted" Ten-Night sacrifice <note term="vyūḷha-daśarātra">A specific ten-day ritual sequence where the meters of the hymns are rearranged</note>, on the sixth day, during the litany for Agni and the Maruts, this hymn is used as the insertion for the Maruts. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "The nourisher of the oblation" (6.65) and "Now let that wonder" (6.66) (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 8.8). Furthermore, in the seasonal sacrifice to all gods (*Vaishvadeva*), for the offering of a seven-layered cake to the Maruts, the verse beginning with "Proclaim the wondrous light" is used as the sacrificial chant. It is also the sacrificial chant for the animal sacrifice to the eleven Maruts, as noted: "Proclaim the wondrous light to the swift one, who like spokes is never last" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 3.7).

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the First Verse ॥ <-

Now let that wonder be manifest to the one who knows; it possesses a common name, being the nourisher. One of its forms swells in the mortal world to be milked, while Prishni <note term="prishni">The mother of the Maruts, often envisioned as a dappled cow representing the starry sky or the rain-clouds</note> once milked the bright udder. ॥ १ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
The wonder | indeed | that | to the one who knows | even | let [it] be | common | name | nourisher | moving |
among mortals | another | for milking | it swells | once | the bright [fluid] | she milked | Prishni | the udder ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**That** refers to the famous and **common** or uniform form. The Maruts are always of equal form, as another sacred text says: "Among them, none is eldest and none is youngest" (Rig Veda 5.60.6). **Name** refers to the namer of even the stable things. **Nourisher** means the one who pleases. Let this great, ever-**moving** form **indeed** quickly appear to the **wise** praiser. (The word "even" is a filler for the meter). Furthermore, that form **among mortals** (in the human world) causes **another** thing—such as herbs and trees—to **swell** in order to **milk** <note>In the sense of fulfilling or yielding</note> desires. Moreover, in direct reference to the Maruts, **Prishni** (the atmosphere) **milked** the **bright** white-colored water from her **udder** **once** a year during the rainy season.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

They who, like kindled fires, shine brightly; when the Maruts have grown twofold or threefold according to their will. Dustless and golden, may they appear together with their riches and their manly powers. ॥ २ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
They who | fires | like | shine brightly | being kindled | twice | when | thrice | the Maruts | have grown |
dustless | golden | of them | together | with riches | with manly powers | and | may they be [present] ॥ २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**They who**, the Maruts, **shine brightly** like **kindled fires**. Because the Maruts **grow** **twofold** or **threefold** according to their own desire. <note>Sayana notes: In the rhythmic chant, the vowel is lengthened according to Vedic grammatical rules.</note> The chariots **of them**, the great ones, are **dustless** (free of dust) and **golden** (decorated with gold). May those Maruts **appear** or become present **together** with **riches** and with **manly powers** (strength). As another text states: "They who come with dappled deer as mounts and with spears" (Rig Veda 1.37.2).

<summary>This page contains the ritual introduction and the first two verses of Rig Veda 6.66, focusing on the Maruts' dual nature as divine fire-like beings and as the source of seasonal rain and earthly growth.</summary>
<keywords>Maruts, Prishni, ritual application, rain-myth, golden chariots, Vedic sacrifice, Sayana's commentary</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the translation of Mandala 6, Hymn 66 of the Rig Veda, dedicated to the Maruts (the Storm-Gods). # 863 || Rig Veda || Mandala 6, Anuvaka 6, Hymn 66

-> ### Now the Third Verse ### <-

Who are the sons of the bounteous Rudra <note>Rudra is the fierce father of the Maruts, associated here with the power of procreation and storms</note>, whom the enduring Prishni was able to bear? For the great Mother knows them; she, the Great One, even Prishni, conceived the seed for the well-being of humanity. ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Of Rudra | who | of the bounteous [one] | are | sons | whom | and | indeed | the enduring [mother] | to bear [was able] |
knows | for | the mother | of the great [ones] | the great | she | she | indeed | Prishni | for the well-being | the seed | [she] | held ॥ ३ ॥

---

-> ### Now the Fourth Verse ### <-

They do not flee from birth <note>This implies they are omnipresent or that they do not abandon those to whom they are born as protectors</note>; being within all, they purify sins. When the pure ones milk the clouds according to their pleasure, they moisten their bodies with glory. ॥ ४ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Not | who | flee | from birth | by this [path] | indeed | within | being | sins | purifying |
out | when | they milk | the pure ones | according to | pleasure | according to | glory | the body | moistening ॥ ४ ॥

---

-> ### Now the Fifth Verse ### <-

Quickly, among those for whom the milk is drawn... <note>This verse is continued on the following page</note> ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary by Sayana

**On Verse 3:**
The sons of the pourer [of rain], Rudra <note>original: "mīḷhuṣaḥ" — meaning one who pours or sprinkles</note>, are the Maruts. The "enduring" one is Prishni, here meaning the atmosphere, who is capable of bearing these Maruts. The Mother of these great ones knows them all; she is Prishni, the Great One. Furthermore, this Prishni held the "seed"—which refers to the rain-water—for the proper well-being of men.

---

**On Verse 4:**
These well-known Maruts do not "flee" or move away from people (the praisers) by any means of travel. Is it because they do not need to protect them? No, that is not the case. They are "within," meaning they exist in the hearts of everyone, and from there they purify and wash away sins. 

This is supported by another Vedic text <note>original: "nigamāntaram"</note> which states: "The Maruts are indeed the vital breaths <note term="prana">The life-force or breath of living beings</note>." Therefore, because they dwell as the life-force in the hearts of all living creatures, they do not "go away." This demonstrates their spiritual existence as the breath of life, while their famous swift movement should be understood as their divine form in the heavens. 

When these pure, shining Maruts "milk" <note>An ancient metaphor for causing rain to fall from the clouds</note> the water according to the desires of the worshippers, they follow that glory by revealing their own bodies and moistening the earth. Alternatively, it means they moisten the earth so that it becomes vast and expansive.

<summary>This page describes the divine parentage of the Maruts as sons of Rudra and Prishni, and explains their dual nature as both atmospheric storm-gods and the internal life-breath (Prana) that purifies the soul.</summary>
<keywords>Maruts, Rudra, Prishni, Storm-Gods, purification, rain metaphor, life-breath, Prana, Sayana, Rig Veda</keywords>

# 864 || Rig Veda || [Book 5, Chapter 1, Section 8]

## Hymn Text
<note>RV 6.66.5 (Word-by-word breakdown)</note>

Quickly | as | among whom | for the milking | even | moving | [towards] | name | bold | of the Maruts | assuming |
not | who | thieves | moving | with greatness | now | even | the generous giver | [away] | may he go | approaching ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Among those well-known Maruts, the praisers who approach while uttering the bold <term>Marut-name</term> <note>original: "mārutaṃ nāma" — referring to the specific power invoked by speaking their name</note>—which acts like a weapon—quickly become capable of "milking" or fulfilling their desires. The word "not" <note>original: "na"</note> is used here in the sense of "now" or "indeed." Even those who are "thieves" <note>original: "staināḥ"</note>—those who are hidden or who might take away the wealth of the praisers—move with greatness; yet, may the sacrificer, who possesses excellent offerings, appease them and lead them away <note>original: "avayajate" — to appease or remove anger through sacrifice</note>. The word "not" is again used in the sense of "indeed."

->॥ Now the sixth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
<note>RV 6.66.6</note>

They indeed are the mighty ones, with strength and a bold army; they have yoked both the well-fashioned worlds <note>Heaven and Earth</note>. And among these powerful ones, Rodasi, self-shining, stood like a light. ॥ ६ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
They | indeed | mighty | with strength | with a bold army | both | yoked | the two worlds [Heaven and Earth] |
well-fashioned |
And | indeed | among these | Rodasi | self-shining | [towards] | among the powerful | stood | like | light ॥ ६ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

Those Maruts, endowed with strength and speed and possessing a bold army, yoke both the well-fashioned <note>original: "sumeke" — well-formed or beautiful</note> worlds, Heaven and Earth. The intention is that they satisfy the Earth with rain. Furthermore, among these Maruts, <term>Rodasi</term> <note>Sayana identifies her as either the wife of Rudra or the personification of "Speech" in the middle realm of the atmosphere</note> abides with her own innate brilliance. Among those powerful ones, no hindering light or obstruction stands in their way; it does not issue forth to stop them.

without fodder | without reins | crossing the atmosphere | through | the two worlds [Heaven and Earth] | path | goes | accomplishing ॥ ७ ॥

# 965 || Rig Veda || [Book 5, Chapter 6, Section 6]

May it be so. May it appear. Furthermore, that chariot which the **non-charioteer** <note>original: "arathīḥ" — here referring to the singer or priest who is not a professional driver</note> drives or impels. Even though he is not a professional charioteer, the chariot [of the Maruts], which is **without horses** <note>original: "anashvaḥ"</note>, **without provisions** <note>original: "apanavasaḥ" — lacking food for the journey</note>, and **without reins** <note>original: "anabhīṃshuḥ" — without ropes</note>, is the **impeller of water** <note>original: "rajastūḥ"</note>. Accomplishing the desires of the praisers, it travels through the **two worlds** <note>Heaven and Earth</note> and along the **atmospheric paths** <note>original: "pathyāḥ"</note>. It goes in various ways.

---

-> ॥ Now the eighth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
There is no restrainer for him, nor an overcomer, O Maruts, whom you protect in the acquisition of wealth. Whether it be for a son, for cattle, for a grandson, or for water—he whom you protect becomes the breaker of the cow-pen in the final battle, even against a shining foe. ॥ ८ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Not | of him | restrainer | not | overcomer | indeed | is | O Maruts | whom | you protect | in the acquisition of wealth |
in the son | or | in cattle | in the grandson | whom | in waters | he | cow-pen | breaker | in the final battle | even | of the shining one ॥ ८ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Maruts! In the **acquisition of wealth** <note>original: "vāja-sātau" — referring to battle or the winning of spoils</note>, there is no **restrainer** <note>impeller or obstructer</note> of this person whom you protect. There is also no **overcomer** <note>original: "tarutā" — injurer or conqueror</note> of him. Furthermore, for the sake of a **son** <note>original: "toke"</note>, a **grandson** <note>original: "tanaye"</note>, wealth, cattle, or water—whomever you protect, he becomes the **breaker** <note>shatterer</note> of the **cow-pen** <note>the enclosure/assemblage of cows</note> of the enemy in the **final battle** <note>original: "pārye"</note>, even if that enemy is **shining** <note>original: "dyoḥ" — light-filled or illustrious</note> and desirous of victory.

---

-> ॥ Now the ninth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Bring forth the wonderful song for the one who praises, for the swift and self-strong Marut-host. They overcome strengths with their own strength; O Agni, the earth trembles before these worshipful ones. ॥ ९ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Forth | wonderful | song | for the one who praises | for the swift | for the Marut-host | for the self-strong | bring ye forth |
who | strengths | with strength | overcome | trembles | O Agni | the earth | before the worshipful ones ॥ ९ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni! For the **one who praises** <note>the one making sound or the one being praised</note>, for the **swift** <note>original: "turāya"</note>, and for the **self-strong** <note>possessing inherent power</note> Marut-host, bring forth the **wonderful** <note>beautiful to look at</note> **song** <note>original: "arkam" — which can also mean food or an offering</note>. This is supported by the fact that the word *arka* is included in the lists of names for "food." **Bring forth** <note>original: "pra-bharadhvam"</note>: the priests who are your helpers and you yourself, all of you should bring it forth. <note>In common worldly usage, one might address a chief among many people working toward one goal and say "you all do this." Similarly, here Agni alone is addressed as the chief, but the plural verb "bring ye forth" is used to include his assistants.</note> These Maruts **overcome** the **strengths** <note>the powers of enemies</note> with their own **strength**. Out of fear for these **worshipful** <note>original: "makhebhyaḥ" — the great or adorable ones</note> Maruts, the earth **trembles** <note>shakes</note>. Regarding the word "for the Marut-host" <note>original: "mārutāya"</note>, even though the individual Maruts are included within the collective term...

The relative pronoun **"who"** <note>original: "ya"</note> refers back to the subject because of the logical division. This is seen in the **Great Commentary** <note>original: "Mahabhashya" — the foundational work on Sanskrit grammar by Patanjali</note>: "Now begins the instruction of words." To which it is asked, "Of which words?" Or as in common speech, when one says "The King’s man," the question follows: "Of which King?"

-> ॥ Now the tenth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Brilliant as the lightning of the sacrifice, moving swiftly like the tongues of fire,**
**The Maruts, the shakers, like heroes, of shining birth, are unassailable, offering praise. ॥ १० ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Brilliant | of the sacrifice-like | lightning | moving swiftly | tongues | like | of fire |
praising | shakers | like | heroes | of shining birth | Maruts | unassailable ॥ १० ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **Maruts** <note>storm deities</note> are like the lightning of the **sacrifice** <note>original: "yajna"</note>, flashing; they are **swift-moving** <note>original: "trishucyavasah"</note>; they are **brilliant** like the **tongues** <note>or flames</note> of fire; they are **praiseworthy**; they are like **shakers** because they make their enemies tremble; they are brave **heroes**; they possess **shining bodies**; and they are **unassailable**, meaning they cannot be overcome by others.

---

-> ॥ Now the eleventh verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**That increasing host of Maruts, with shining spears, the son of Rudra, I worship with a call;**
**For the strength of heaven, pure thoughts and powerful songs have striven, like waters from the clouds. ॥ ११ ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Him | increasing | relating to the Maruts | having shining spears | of Rudra | son | with a call | [I] worship |
of heaven | for the host | pure | thoughts | mountains | like | waters | powerful | striven ॥ ११ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
I **worship** <note>original: "avivase" — I serve or honor</note> with a **call** <note>a song of praise</note> that well-known, **increasing** host of Maruts, the **son of Rudra**, who possess **shining spears**. Furthermore, the **pure** and stainless **thoughts** <note>original: "manishah" — devotional hymns</note> of the singer are raised for the **strength** of the Maruts. We know "Shardha" refers to **strength** <note>original: "balanamasu pathat" — from its inclusion in ancient lexicons of strength</note>. These songs have **striven** or competed like **waters** flowing from **clouds** <note>original: "girayah" — while often meaning mountains, the commentator notes its use here as a name for clouds</note>.

-> ॥ Thus ends the eighth section (Varga) of the first chapter of the fifth book ॥ <-

---

The sixth hymn [of this section], beginning with **"To all of you"** <note>original: "vishvesham vah"</note>, has eleven verses. The seer is **Bharadvaja**; the meter is **Trishtubh** <note>a rhythmic pattern of 11 syllables per line</note>; the deities are **Mitra and Varuna**. Thus the index <note>Anukramani</note> states: **"To all, the hymn to Mitra and Varuna."** The ritual application of the hymn is determined by its indicative marks. In the **animal sacrifice** <note>Pashu-yajna</note> dedicated to Mitra and Varuna, the verse "Come, O Mitra and Varuna" is used as the invitatory prayer for the **sacrificial cake** <note>original: "pashu-purodasha"</note>. This is indicated in the **Sutras** <note>specifically the Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 3.8</note>: **"Come, O Mitra and Varuna, with good praise; O Mitra and Varuna, for our enjoyment of the offering."** In the modified ritual...

<vocab>
- Maruts: Storm deities, sons of the god Rudra, known for their brilliance and power.
- Sacrifice (Adhvara/Yajna): The central ritual act of the Vedic period involving offerings into a sacred fire.
- Spear (Rishti): The characteristic weapon of the Maruts, often associated with lightning bolts.
- Devotional thought (Manisha): Inspired poetic wisdom or hymns directed toward the gods.
- Mitra and Varuna: Two major Vedic deities; Mitra governs friendship and contracts, while Varuna governs cosmic order and the waters.
- Bharadvaja: A famous sage (Rishi) to whom the hymns of the sixth book of the Rig Veda are attributed.
- Sacrificial cake (Purodasha): A cake made of ground grain, usually offered in the fire during rituals.
</vocab>

[Mundala 6. Adhyaya 6. Hymn 67.] || Fifth Book || 867

On the seventh day of the ten-day rite <note>original: "Dasharatra," a major Vedic sacrificial session</note>, during the recitation of the *Prauga* <note>a specific litany of seven triplets of verses recited by the Hotri priest</note>, the third triplet beginning with "When towards you two..." <note>original: "pra yad vam"</note> is dedicated to Mitra and Varuna. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "When towards you two, O Mitra and Varuna, the contenders with the wagon-possessing Ashvins..." <note>quoting Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 8.9</note>.

-> || There, the first verse || <-

## Hymn Text
**O Mitra and Varuna, most senior among all existing beings, may you be magnified by our songs. Like a most skillful driver with a rein, you two—though unequal—restrain the people with your arms. ॥ १ ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
Of all | your | existing beings | most senior | with songs | Mitra-Varuna | for magnifying |
completely | who | rein-like | restrained | most skillful at restraining | two | people | unequal | with arms | their own ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Among all existing beings, you are the **most senior** <note>original: "jyeshthatama" — meaning the most excellent or eldest in status</note>. O **Mitra and Varuna**, I have proceeded **to magnify** <note>to increase or strengthen through praise</note> you with **songs** <note>original: "girbhih" — hymns of praise</note>. These **two** <note>the deities</note> are **unequal** <note>original: "asama" — referring to their distinct roles, such as Mitra ruling the day and Varuna the night</note>. 
> The fierce four-edged one strikes the three-edged one. <note>original: "cirashri hanti caturashrirugrah" — a quote from Rig Veda 1.152.2 illustrating their distinct power</note>
As the **most skillful restrainers**, you **restrain** <note>control or guide</note> the **people** with your own **arms**, just as a driver guides horses with a **rein**. The use of the plural for "arms" is a mark of **honor** <note>original: "pujartham" — a grammatical plural used to show respect to the deity's power</note>.

---

-> || Now the second verse || <-

## Hymn Text
**This prayer of mine spreads out towards you both; with reverence, the beloved sacrificial grass is spread. O Mitra and Varuna, grant us an unassailable shelter; O bounteous givers, let your protection be our shield. ॥ २ ॥**

**Word-by-word breakdown:**
This | from me | you two | spreads out | prayer | near | beloved | with reverence | sacrificial grass | towards |
giving | to us | Mitra-Varuna | unassailable | shelter | which | yours | protecting | O good givers || २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Mitra and Varuna**, this **prayer** <note>intellectual praise</note> of **mine** <note>from me</note> **spreads out** <note>covers or reaches</note> **towards you**. O **beloved** ones, it approaches you along with the **reverence** <note>original: "namasa" — here interpreted as the food or sacrificial oblation</note>. It also reaches the **sacrificial grass** <note>original: "barhih" — the sacred grass where deities are invited to sit</note> of your sacrifice. O Mitra and Varuna, **grant** <note>bestow</note> to **us** a **shelter** <note>a home or protection</note> that is **unassailable** <note>not overcome by enemies</note>. O **good givers**, the **shelter** which belongs to you and is given by you is **protecting**—it wards off cold, wind, and heat.

---

-> || Now the third verse || <-

## Hymn Text
**Come hither, Mitra and Varuna, you who are well-praised, being called with beloved reverence; you who, like a diligent worker, guide the people, you lead them by your greatness... ॥ ३ ॥**

|| Rigveda || [Mandala 5. Adhyaya 1. Varga 9.] 868

## Hymn Text (RV 5.62.3)

### Word-by-word Breakdown
Come | hither | O Mitra and Varuna | with beautiful praise | near | dear ones | with reverence | being invoked | 
together | who | like a diligent workman | with action | people | desiring to hear | indeed | you regulate | with greatness ॥ ३ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Mitra and Varuna**, you who are **invoked** <note>original: "huyamanau" — being called or praised</note> with **beautiful praise** <note>original: "sushasti" — excellent recitation</note> and with **reverence** <note>original: "namasa" — either food offerings (havis) or hymns of praise</note>, you who are **dear** to the whole world: **come hither**. Approach us. You **two**, who are possessed of **greatness**, just as a **diligent workman** <note>original: "aprahsthah" — one established in his task or work</note> regulates his **work**, so do you **regulate** <note>original: "samyatathah" — govern or control</note> the **people** who **desire to hear** <note>original: "shrudhiyatah" — those seeking to hear the truth or seeking fame</note>.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text (RV 5.62.4)

### Verse Text
Like two powerful steeds, with purified bonds, when Aditi bore you as an embryo for the sake of the Eternal Law. As you were being born great and mighty, you were held as formidable ones against the mortal enemy. ॥ ४ ॥

### Word-by-word Breakdown
Horses | like | who | powerful | purified-bonds | Law/Truth | when | embryo | Aditi | for bearing | 
forth | who | great | mighty | being born | formidable | for the mortal | for the enemy | down | held ॥ ४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Who**, like two **horses** or two powerful **steeds** <note>original: "vajina" — strong or spirited</note>, have **purified bonds** <note>original: "putabandhu" — whose connections or praises are pure</note> and are **Truth** <note>original: "rita" — adhering to the cosmic order</note>. When the goddess **Aditi** <note>The infinite mother of the gods</note> **bore** <note>original: "bharadhyai" — to carry or sustain</note> you both as an **embryo** in her womb. Furthermore, you two, **Mitra and Varuna**, who even while **being born** were **great** and **mighty** <note>extremely powerful</note>, Aditi held you in her womb as **formidable** ones, the slayers of the **mortal enemy** <note>original: "ripave" — the harmer or sinner</note>.

---

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text (RV 5.62.5)

### Verse Text
When all the gods, of one mind, bestowed dominion upon you both while rejoicing in your greatness. When you encompass the two wide worlds, there are your spies, undeceived and wise. ॥ ५ ॥

### Word-by-word Breakdown
All | when | your | greatness | rejoicing | dominion | the gods | bestowed | of one mind | 
around | when | you are | Heaven and Earth | indeed | wide | they are | spies | undeceived | wise ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**All** the **gods**, being **of one mind** <note>original: "sajoshas" — united in heart and purpose</note> and **rejoicing** in your **greatness**, **bestowed** <note>original: "adadhuh" — gave or established</note> upon you both **dominion** <note>original: "kshatram" — royal power or sovereignty</note>. Furthermore, when you **encompass** <note>original: "paribhuthah" — pervade or surround</note> the two **wide** worlds of **Heaven and Earth** <note>original: "rodasi"</note>, your **spies** <note>original: "spashah" — in Vedic thought, these are the unblinking observers of human conduct, often identified with the rays of the sun</note> are present there; they are **undeceived** <note>unharmed or impossible to trick</note> and **wise** <note>not ignorant</note>.

-> ॥ Thus ends the ninth Varga of the first Adhyaya of the fifth Mandala ॥ <-

<vocab>
- <term>Mitra-Varuna</term>: A dual deity representing the complementary aspects of sovereignty—Mitra presiding over the day, contracts, and friendship; Varuna over the night, the vast sky, and moral law.
- <term>Aditi</term>: The primordial mother of the gods (Adityas), symbolizing infinity and liberation from sin.
- <term>Kshatram</term>: Sacred and temporal power; the authority to rule and protect.
- <term>Rodasi</term>: A dual term for Heaven and Earth, seen as the two halves of the world.
- <term>Spashah</term>: The "spies" or "watchmen" of the gods, particularly Varuna, who observe the deeds of mortals to ensure justice.
</vocab>

It details how the other gods collectively bestowed sovereignty upon them, and mentions their "spies" (rays of light) that watch over Heaven and Earth.</summary>

# Rigveda-Sanhita: Mandala 6, Hymn 67
### [Mandala 6, Chapter 6, Hymn 67] || Fifth Ashtaka || Page 769

->॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
You two indeed uphold **dominion** day after day; you strengthen the **summit** of the sky as if with a **supporting pillar**. The cloud, made firm by you, traverses the **atmosphere**, and the **all-divine** Sun, spreading across the earth and heaven, is nourished by the **mortal's food** <note>original: "dhasina" — referring to the sacrificial oblation</note>. ॥ ६ ॥

### Word-by-word Breakdown
**They two** (Mitra and Varuna) | **Indeed** | **Dominion** | **Uphold** | **According to** | **Days** | **Strengthen** | **Summit** | **From a measure** (pillar) | **Like** | **Of heaven** | 
**Firm** | **Atmosphere-traversing** (cloud) | **And** | **All-divine** (Sun) | **Earth** | **Spreading** | **Heaven** | **By food** | **Of the mortal** ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Those two, **Mitra and Varuna**, you uphold **dominion** <note>original: "kshatram" — strength or sovereign power</note> day by day. You strengthen the **summit**—the highly elevated region of the atmosphere, or the cloud, or the sun. You make it firm. **As if with a supporting pillar** <note>original: "upamat" — interpreted here as a post or pillar (sthuna)</note>; just as a pillar holds a calf, so do you hold the heavens. The cloud, **made firm** by you two, is **traversing the atmosphere** <note>original: "nakshatrah" — pervading the mid-air</note>, and also the **all-divine** Sun <note>original: "vishwadevah" — here referring to Surya</note> spreads over the **earth** and the **heavens**. Being nourished by the **food** <note>original: "dhasina" — the sacrificial butter or oblation</note> of the **mortal** <note>original: "ayoh" — the human sacrificer; referenced from ancient word-lists as a name for man</note>, he is extended or strengthened by you.

---

->॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
You two support the **wise priest** so that his **belly** may be filled; when the **attendant priests** together fill the **place of sacrifice**. The **youthful ones**, never-drying, are not overwhelmed, when they bear the **water** that invigorates all. ॥ ७ ॥

### Word-by-word Breakdown
**They two** | **The wise one** | **Support** | **The belly** | **For the sake of filling** | **When** | **The place of sacrifice** | **The attendant priests** | **Fill** | 
**Not** | **They are overwhelmed** | **The youthful ones** (rivers/directions) | **Never-drying** | **Apart** | **When** | **Water/Vigor** | **All-invigorating** | **They bear** ॥ ७ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Those two, **Mitra and Varuna**, you support the **wise** <note>original: "vipram" — the learned sacrificer</note> to fill his **belly** <note>original: "jatharam" — metaphorically the sacrificial vessel or the priest's stomach</note> with Soma juice. This happens when the **attendant priests** <note>original: "sabhritayah" — the officiating priests who gather together</note> fill the **place of sacrifice** <note>original: "sahyam" — the sacrificial assembly or hall</note>. O **invigorators of all**, when the **water** sent by you is carried, then the **youthful ones** <note>original: "yuvatayah" — the rivers or the cardinal directions</note> are **not overwhelmed** <note>original: "na mrishyante" — they are not overcome by dust or decay</note>. They remain **never-drying** <note>original: "avatah" — not withered or dry</note> and they **bear** or sustain their great power and abundance.

---

->॥ Now the Eighth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
You two, with your **tongue**, always [provide] this, O **wise ones**; when your **true messenger** has become active. May that **greatness** of yours be accompanied by **food of clarified butter**; do you two drive away **sin** from the giver. ॥ ८ ॥

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Rigveda, specifically focusing on Mandala 5, Hymn 67. # Rigveda-Sanhita: Mandala 5, Hymn 67
### [Mandala 5, Chapter 1, Varga 10]

## Hymn Text

**[Verse 5.67.8 — Word-by-word analysis]**
Those two | with the tongue | always | here | this | the wise one | when | of you two | true | the messenger | in the rite | has become |
That | of you two | greatness | O you whose food is ghee | let it be | you two | for the giver | away | destroy | sin. ॥ ८ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Regarding those two, **Mitra and Varuna**, the **wise one** <note>original: "sumedhāḥ" — a person of great intelligence or wisdom</note> always asks for **this** water with his **tongue** <note>original: "jihvayā" — meaning through the power of speech or recitation</note>. Since the prefix "ā" is observed, we supply the verb "asks" to complete the sense. Because water was the subject of the previous verse, the word "this" <note>original: "idam"</note> refers back to the water present in the mind of the speaker. Alternatively, the **true messenger** <note>original: "aratiḥ" — one who approaches or a servant of the ritual</note>, free from illusion, has become present for you two in the **rite** <note>original: "ṛte" — the sacrifice or cosmic order</note>. **O you whose food is ghee** <note>original: "ghṛtānnau"</note>, let that **greatness**—characterized by the granting of desired fruits—belong to you two. Furthermore, may you two **destroy** <note>original: "vicayiṣṭham" — to clear away or annihilate</note> the **sin** <note>original: "aṃhaḥ" — evil or spiritual obstruction</note> of the **giver** <note>original: "dāśuṣe" — the sacrificer. Note: Sayanacharya points out that the Dative case is used here in the sense of the Genitive "of the giver"</note>. ॥ ८ ॥

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the Ninth Verse ॥<-

When those who challenge your **dear abodes**, O **Mitra and Varuna**, diminish the works ordained by you;
Neither the **Gods** by their praise, nor **mortals**, nor those **connected to water** who do not sacrifice, nor those who are **not sons**. ॥ ९ ॥

**[Word-by-word analysis]**
Toward | when | of you two | Mitra and Varuna | challenging | dear | abodes | ordained by you | they diminish |
Not | those | Gods | by praise | not | mortals | not associated with sacrifice | connected to water | not | sons. ॥ ९ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Mitra and Varuna**, when people who do not perform sacrifice, **challenging** <note>original: "spūrdhan" — competing or struggling against</note> you, **diminish** or harm your **dear abodes** <note>original: "priyā dhāma" — here interpreted as "sacred acts" or "ordained duties"</note> that were **ordained by you** <note>original: "yuvadhitā"</note>. These include **Gods** who are not joined by **praise** <note>original: "ohasā" — the means of carrying the sacrifice, i.e., the hymn</note>, and **mortals** who are not joined by praise. Also, those **connected to water** <note>original: "apyaḥ" — those whose works involve water, or perhaps common worldly people</note> who are **not associated with sacrifice**—meaning those who perform useless acts. And those who are **not sons**. <note>Note: Sayana derives "putra" (son) from the root "pṛ" meaning to fill or satisfy. Thus, "not sons" refers to those who "do not satisfy" the gods with offerings.</note> The command to "destroy" from the previous verse is applied to all of these people as well. ॥ ९ ॥

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ Now the Tenth Verse ॥<-

When the **singers** bear the **speech**, and some recite the **Nivids**, meditating [on you];
Then let us speak **true hymns** to you; for no one else strives with the **Gods** in **greatness** as you do. ॥ १० ॥

**[Word-by-word analysis]**
Away | when | speech | the singers | bear | they recite | some | certain | liturgical calls | meditating |
Then | to you two | let us speak | true | hymns | no one | with the gods | you two strive | in greatness. ॥ १० ॥

<vocab>
- <term>ghṛtānnau</term>: "Ghee-eaters"; a title for deities who receive clarified butter in the fire.
- <term>aratiḥ</term>: A messenger or a devoted servant of the ritual who "moves" between worlds.
- <term>dhāma</term>: Can mean a physical "abode," but in the Vedas, it often refers to "sacred laws" or "customary rites."
- <term>nivid</term>: A specific type of ancient Vedic liturgical formula or short invocation inserted into the hymns.
- <term>kīstāsaḥ</term>: An archaic term for praisers, poets, or singers of the sacred hymns.
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes the hymn to Mitra and Varuna, asking the deities to destroy the sins of the faithful while rebuking those who neglect the sacrifice. It emphasizes the importance of the "true hymns" and the unique, unmatched greatness of these two gods among the divine host.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from the end of Mandala 6, Hymn 67 to the beginning of Mandala 6, Hymn 68. When the **wise chanters** <note>original: "kīstāso" — referring to the Udgatars or singers of the Sama Veda</note> who are **desirous** <note>original: "uśijaḥ"</note> of divine favor perform their task—as the list of names for "wise" includes these terms—they **bring forth** <note>original: "vi bharante"</note> their speech or praise, pronouncing it distinctly. At that time, some of the Rigvedic priests <note>original: "bahvṛcā"</note>, meditating on Agni and other gods, recite the sacrificial invocations <note>term: Nivids|Short, ancient prose formulas used to invite the gods to the sacrifice</note>. This being the case, we speak **true hymns** <note>original: "satyānyukthāni"</note> of praise to **you two** (Mitra and Varuna). In your **greatness** <note>original: "mahitvā"</note>, along with the **other gods**, you are **unrivaled** <note>original: "nakiryatayaḥ" — literally "none go against you" or "none can reach your level"</note>.

-> ॥ Now follows the eleventh verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

Indeed, may we receive your protection and an unfailing house, O Mitra and Varuna. When the praises ring out like cows, and when they yoke the powerful, desire-showering Soma at the sacrifice, may we find your favor. ॥ 11 ॥

**[Word-by-word analysis]**

Protection | Indeed | Of you two | House/Shelter | Approaching | Of you two | O Mitra and Varuna | Unfailing |
Following | When | Praises/Cows | Resound | The straight-going | The powerful/subduer | When | In the sacrifice | The showerer (Soma) | They yoke. ॥ 11 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Mitra and Varuna**, in **approaching you** <note>original: "avoravatrorvāṃ"</note> for protection, may the **house** <note>original: "chardiṣo" — can also mean comfort or shelter</note> that is to be given by you to the singers who approach you be **unfailing** <note>original: "askṛdhoyu" — meaning uninterrupted or not shortened</note>. <margin>The word "house" (chardiṣo) is in the genitive case used here in the sense of the dative, "for the house."</margin> In this regard, the grammarian Yaska states: "Askṛdhoyu means 'not shortened' (akṛdhrayu); 'Kṛdhvi' is a name for something short or cut off." (Nirukta 6.3). This is **indeed** <note>original: "itthyā"</note> true.

When does this approach to Mitra and Varuna happen? He says: **When** <note>original: "yad-yadā"</note> the **praises** <note>original: "gāvaḥ" — literally "cows," often used as a metaphor for voices or rays of light</note> **resound** <note>original: "anu-sphurān"</note> in succession. And when the sacrificers **yoke** the **Soma** <note>term: Soma|A sacred ritual drink offered to the gods, personified as a deity</note> at the **sacrifice** <note>original: "raṇe" — a place of delight or ritual</note>. This Soma is described as **straight-going** <note>original: "ṛñjapyam"</note>, **powerful** <note>original: "dhṛṣṇum" — the overcomer of enemies</note>, and a **showerer** <note>original: "vṛṣaṇam"</note> of desires.

-> ॥ Thus ends the tenth Varga of the first Adhyaya of the fifth Ashtaka ॥ <-

---

The seventh hymn [of this section], beginning with **"Listen to us,"** <note>original: "śruṣṭī vām"</note> consists of eleven verses. The seer is Bharadvaja; the meter is Trishtubh; the deities are Indra and Varuna. As noted in the Index <note>term: Anukramani|A systematic index of the Vedic hymns providing the seer, meter, and deity</note>: **"The hymn 'Listen to us' is addressed to Indra-Varuna; the penultimate two verses are in the Jagati meter."** The two verses starting with **"To the assembly, O Indra and Varuna, drinkers of the pressed juice"** are Jagati; the remaining are Trishtubh. The deities are **Indra and Varuna**.

In the *Abhijit* sacrifices, specifically during the hymns of the Third Libation <note>term: Tritiya-savana|The third and final daily offering of Soma, usually performed in the evening</note>, this hymn is used by the Maitravaruna priest for insertions when the chants are extended. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: **"Listen to us, the sacrifice is yours, O heroes"** (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 7.9). During the Third Libation, the verse **"O Indra and Varuna, drinkers of the pressed juice, this pressed Soma"** is the offering verse for the Prashastri priest. It is indicated: **"O Indra and Varuna, drinkers of the pressed juice, this pressed Soma, and Indra, drink the Soma, O Brihaspati"** (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 5.5). In the *Ukthya* sacrifice, at the Third Libation, the verse **"O Indra and Varuna, of the sweetest..."** is the offering verse for the Maitravaruna priest's recitation. It is indicated: **"The offering verse is: O Indra and Varuna, of the sweetest..."** (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 6.1).

# || Rig Veda || [Ashtaka 5, Adhyaya 1, Varga 11]

->॥ Here begins the first verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
May the sacrifice, offered with one accord, reach you **quickly**—as it did for Manu—when the sacrificial grass is strewn for the worship. Today, for the sake of nourishment and for great happiness, may that [Soma] bring you here, O Indra and Varuna. ॥ 1 ॥

**[Word-by-word analysis]**

Quickly | To you two | The sacrifice | Offered/Ready | With one accord | Like Manu | One who has prepared the sacrificial grass | To worship | Toward | Which | O Indra and Varuna | For food/nourishment | Today | For great | For happiness | For great | May it bring. ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O O venerable Indra and Varuna, for the sake of you both, the sacrifice—that is, the Soma—is **quickly** <note>original: "śruṣṭī"</note> offered today, joined with the priests. Indeed, Yaska <note>An ancient commentator on Vedic etymology</note> states that the word *śruṣṭī* means "quickly," derived from the root meaning to hear or listen. This Soma, as it did for **Manu** <note>The legendary first man and archetypal sacrificer</note>, now brings you both here for the sake of the **nourisher** <note>original: "vṛktabarhiṣo" — referring to the sacrificer who has cut and strewn the sacred grass</note> to provide food and great happiness.

---

->॥ Now follows the second ॥<-

## Hymn Text
For those two are the best at the sacrifice, the impellers [of wealth], the strongest among heroes; they have become the most liberal among the wealthy donors. They are of mighty power, overcomers of enemies through Truth, and possessors of all armies. ॥ 2 ॥

**[Word-by-word analysis]**

Those two | Indeed | Best | At the sacrifice | Impellers/Givers | Among heroes | Strongest | Those two | Indeed | Have become | Of the wealthy donors | Most liberal/giving | Of mighty power | By Truth | Slayers of the enemy | With all armies. ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Indra and Varuna, **those** <note>original: "tā"</note> two of you are well-known and **best** <note>original: "śreṣṭhā"</note> at the **sacrifice** <note>original: "devatātā"</note>. This is supported by the lists of names for a sacrifice which include *devatāti*. You both are the **impellers** or givers of wealth. Furthermore, you two are the **strongest** <note>original: "śaviṣṭhā"</note> among all heroes. You have become the **most liberal** <note>original: "maṃhiṣṭhā"</note> among the wealthy donors, possessing **mighty power** <note>original: "tuviśuṣmā"</note>. Through **Truth** <note>term: Rta|The cosmic and moral order that governs the universe</note> you are the **overcomers of enemies** <note>original: "vṛtratutā" — specifically referring to the destruction of Vritra or obstacles</note>, and you both act with your **entire army** <note>original: "sarvasenā"</note>.

---

## Hymn Text
Praise those two with respectful songs and powerful hymns that bring happiness, O Indra and Varuna, for they desire them. With his **thunderbolt** and his strength, the one [Indra] slays the enemy; the other [Varuna], the wise one, remains among the people in their struggles. ॥ 3 ॥

**[Word-by-word analysis]**

Those two | Praise | With respectful [songs] | With powerful [hymns] | With hymns of happiness | O Indra and Varuna | Desiring | With the thunderbolt | The one | With strength | Slashes/Slays | The enemy | Abides | The other | In the struggles/assemblies | The wise one. ॥ 3 ॥

# Mandala 6, Chapter 6, Hymn 68 | Fifth Ashtaka

O Bharadvaja, with worshipful <note>original: "namasyebhiḥ"</note>, praise-worthy, and heroic strengths—"Heroic" <note>original: "nṛṣam"</note> is a name for strength—and with all joys, they have desired praise. The word "kayati" refers to the act of sounding or praising; this is its form in the perfect tense. Sing to those two, Indra and Varuna; that is, praise them. Among them, one—Indra—strikes the demon <margin>the demon Vritra</margin> <note>Reconstructed from "vṛ-makamasuraṃ" as "vṛtram akamasuraṃ"</note> with his thunderbolt. The other—Varuna—who is a wise sage, joins with power and strength to protect <margin>to protect from calamities</margin> <note>Reconstructed from "upadra- rakṣituṃ" as "upadravebhyo rakṣituṃ"</note> the worshipers in their battles.

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

**When the goddesses and the men have increased [in strength], and all the gods who are self-guided by the leaders; O Indra and Varuna, through your greatness, and O Heaven and Earth, become vast for these [sacrificers]. ॥ 4 ॥**

**Goddesses | and | when | men | and | they have increased | all | gods | of the leaders | self-guided | toward | these | Indra-Varuna | through greatness | Heaven | and | Earth | become | the two vast ones. ॥ 4 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Among the leaders or men, there are the **goddesses** <note>original: "gnāśca"</note>—as the ancient etymologist Yaska says, "Mena and Gna are names for women/celestial females"—and the **men**, and **all the gods**. Regarding the word **gods** <note>original: "devāsaḥ"</note>, it is a grammatical usage where the masculine form represents both the masculine and feminine; thus, "gods" refers to both goddesses and gods. When these, being **self-guided** or naturally inclined, **increase** or are magnified by praises, then, O **Indra and Varuna**, you who are endowed with **greatness**, provide abundantly <note>original: "prabhūtaṃ"</note> for these singers. O **Heaven and Earth**, you two who are **vast** and wide, may you also provide abundantly for them.

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**He indeed is bounteous, wealthy, and observant of Truth, O Indra and Varuna, whoever offers to you personally. With nourishment, that giver overcomes enemies, dwelling among riches and wealthy people. ॥ 5 ॥**

**He | indeed | bounteous | wealthy | observant of Truth | O Indra | who | to you two | O Varuna | gives | personally | with food/nourishment | he | enemies | may he cross/overcome | the giver | dwelling | wealth | the wealthy | and | people. ॥ 5 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra** and O **Varuna** <note>Note: The commentary explains that the dual form is used for both names due to their pairing in the hymn</note>. For you two, whichever sacrificer **personally** <note>original: "tman"</note> or by his own self **gives** oblations, **he indeed** becomes **bounteous** <note>original: "sudānuḥ"</note>—one whose giving is excellent. He becomes **wealthy** and **observant of Truth** <note>original: "ṛtāvān"</note>, meaning a possessor of the sacrifice. Furthermore, that **giver**, by means of **nourishment** or sacrificial food, crosses over or overcomes his **enemies**...

<vocab>
<term>Indra-Varuna (इन्द्रावरुणौ)</term>: A dual deity representing the combined power of the warrior-king (Indra) and the guardian of cosmic and moral law (Varuna).
<term>Gna (ग्ना)</term>: Celestial women or goddesses often associated with the divine power of speech or the wives of the gods.
<term>Sudānu (सुदानु)</term>: "Bounteous" or "giving well," describing both a generous god and a generous sacrificer.
<term>Ṛtāvā (ऋतावा)</term>: One who acts according to *Ṛta*, the cosmic order or truth; often refers to the regular performance of sacrifices.
</vocab>

<summary>This page describes the dual nature of Indra and Varuna, where Indra destroys the demonic Vritra while Varuna protects the righteous. It emphasizes that a sincere sacrificer gains wealth, divine favor, and the strength to overcome enemies through the grace of these two deities and the vastness of Heaven and Earth.</summary>
<keywords>Indra, Varuna, Vritra, Sayana's Commentary, Rig Veda, sacrifice, goddesses, Heaven and Earth, prosperity, cosmic order</keywords>

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O Gods, what wealth, rich in possessions and abundant in food, you bestow upon the one who offers the sacrifice—O Indra and Varuna, may that wealth also be ours, which shatters the ill-repute of our enemies. ॥ 6 ॥

**What | you two | for the one who gives the sacrifice | O Gods | wealth | bestow | rich in possessions | abundant in food | among us | that | Indra-Varuna | also | may it be | which | shatters | of the assailants | the ill-repute. ॥ 6 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Indra and Varuna**, you two gods who are being praised, what kind of **wealth** <note>original: "rayiṃ"</note> do you **bestow** <note>original: "dhatthaḥ"</note> or provide **for the one who gives the sacrifice** <note>original: "dāśvadhvarāya"</note>, that is, the one who has offered the oblation? This wealth is **rich in possessions** <note>original: "vasumantaṃ"</note>, meaning it is connected to riches, and **abundant in food** <note>original: "purukṣuṃ"</note>, meaning it contains much nourishment or is filled with glory. And that wealth which **shatters** or breaks the **ill-repute** <note>original: "aśastīḥ"</note>—meaning the infamy or the disgraceful reputation belonging to the enemies—of the **assailants** <note>original: "vanuṣām"</note> or those who wish to harm us; may such wealth **be** <note>original: "syāt"</note> among us.

---

-> ॥ Now the Seventh [Verse] ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
And, O Indra and Varuna, may there be wealth for us, for the patrons, which is well-protecting and guarded by the gods; [the wealth of those] whose strength, overcoming in battles and conquering, immediately promotes our glories. ॥ 7 ॥

**And | for us | well-protecting | guarded by the gods | for the patrons | Indra-Varuna | wealth | may it be | of whom | strength | in battles | overcoming | forward | immediately | glories | promotes | conquering. ॥ 7 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
And also, O **Indra and Varuna**, may there **be wealth** for **us**, and for the **patrons** <note>original: "sūribhyaḥ"</note>, who are the singers of the hymns. This wealth is **well-protecting** <note>original: "sutrācaḥ"</note> and **guarded by the gods** <note>original: "devagopāḥ"</note>—that is, it is of such a kind that the gods themselves are its protectors. Furthermore, may our **strength** <note>original: "śuṣmaḥ"</note> or power, being an **overcomer** <note>original: "sāhvān"</note> of enemies **in battles** <note>original: "pṛtanāsu"</note> and a **conqueror** <note>original: "tarturiḥ"</note> or destroyer [of foes], immediately **promote** <note>original: "pratirate"</note> or fully establish our **glories** <note>original: "dyumnā"</note>, which are our fame.

---

-> ॥ Now the Eighth [Verse] ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Now, O Indra and Varuna, being praised, O Gods, provide us with wealth for the sake of good renown. Thus praising the host of the Great One, may we cross over difficulties like crossing waters with a boat. ॥ 8 ॥

<note>This verse introduces the classic Vedic metaphor of the "boat" of prayer or sacrifice used to cross the "ocean" of worldly suffering or sin.</note>

<term>Indra-Varuna (Indrāvaruṇau)</term>: A dual deity representing the combined powers of the king of the gods (Indra) and the guardian of cosmic law (Varuna).
<term>Wealth (Rayi)</term>: In the Vedic context, this refers not just to money but to cattle, food, healthy progeny, and social prestige.
<term>Patrons (Sūri)</term>: The wealthy leaders who sponsored the sacrifices and supported the poets/priests.

## Hymn Text

<note>Rig Veda 6.68.8 (Word-for-word analysis continued)</note>
Now . for us . O Indra-Varuna . being praised . provide . wealth . for high reputation . O Gods .
thus . praising . of the mighty [pair] . the strength . difficulties . like . with a boat . over waters . may we cross . ॥ 8 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra and Varuna** <note>original: "indrāvaruṇā"</note>, being **praised** <note>original: "gṛṇānā"</note> by us, may you two **quickly** <note>original: "nu"</note> **provide** <note>original: "pṛktaṃ"</note> **wealth** <note>original: "rayiṃ"</note> **for us, for the sake of high reputation** <note>original: "sauśravasāya"</note>. The state of having "good fame" is high reputation; provide wealth for that purpose. Furthermore, O **Gods** <note>original: "devā"</note>, while we are **praising** <note>original: "gṛṇantaḥ"</note> in **this way** <note>original: "itthā"</note> the **strength** <note>original: "śardhaḥ"</note> or power of the **mighty** <note>original: "mahinasya"</note> duo (you two), **may we cross** <note>original: "tarema"</note> over our **difficulties** <note>original: "duritā"</note> **like** <note>original: "na"</note> crossing over **waters** <note>original: "apaḥ"</note> **with a boat** <note>original: "nāvā"</note>.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Ninth Verse ॥ <-

Sing now a dear, extensive hymn to the great sovereign, the shining Varuna;
He who, of great deeds and possessing greatness, shines through wisdom like an ageless flame over the wide worlds. ॥ 9 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis —**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O praiser, **now** <note>original: "nu"</note> **sing** <note>original: "pra arca"</note>—meaning chant or proclaim—a **dear** <note>original: "priyaṃ"</note> or heart-pleasing **hymn** <note>original: "manma"</note> that is **extensive** <note>original: "saprathaḥ"</note> (wide in all directions). Regarding this, the ancient etymologist Yaska says: "Saprathaḥ means wide in all directions." This hymn is for **Varuna**, the **shining god** <note>original: "devāya"</note>, the **great** <note>original: "bṛhate"</note> or all-encompassing one, and the **sovereign** <note>original: "samrājñe"</note> who rules over kings by his command. **This** <note>original: "ayaṃ"</note> very Varuna, who is endowed with **greatness** <note>original: "mahinā"</note>, who is **of great deeds** <note>original: "mahivrataḥ"</note>, and who possesses **wisdom** <note>original: "kratvā"</note> and **brilliance** <note>original: "śociṣā"</note>, **shines upon** <note>original: "vibhāti"</note> and illuminates the **wide** <note>original: "urvī"</note> or vast heaven and earth, appearing **like one ageless** <note>original: "ajaro na"</note> or free from decay.

## Hymn Text

## Commentary (Sayana)

**O Indra and Varuna** <note>original: "indrāvaruṇā"</note>, you two are the **drinkers of the pressed juice** <note>original: "sutapau"</note>. May you **drink** <note>original: "pibataṃ"</note> **this pressed** <note>original: "sutam"</note> (extracted) **Soma** juice which is **exhilarating** <note>original: "madyaṃ"</note>. ## Hymn Text

O Indra and Varuna, O bestowers of blessings, may you two drink of the most sweet, showering Soma. This food is poured out for you among us; sitting down on this sacrificial grass, may you rejoice. ॥ 11 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis:**
O Indra-Varuna . of the most sweet . the showering . of Soma . O bestowers . [prefix] . may you two drink .
This . for you both . food . poured out . among us . sitting down . on this . sacrificial grass . may you two rejoice ॥ 11 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra and Varuna** <note>original: "indrāvaruṇā"</note>, you two who are **bestowers** <note>original: "vṛṣaṇā"</note> of desires, may you **drink** <note>original: "āvṛṣethām"</note> the **Soma** <note>original: "somasya"</note> which is **most sweet** <note>original: "madhumattamasya"</note>, or exceedingly full of nectar and flavor, and which is **showering** <note>original: "vṛṣṇaḥ"</note> or granting. On this point, the *Shatapatha Brahmana* says: "Eat according to your portions; thus he says 'drink/consume' according to your portions" <note>original: "2.4.2.20"</note>. For **you both** <note>original: "vām"</note>, **this food** <note>original: "idam andhaḥ"</note> in the form of Soma has been **poured out** <note>original: "pariṣiktaṃ"</note> into the ritual vessels **among us** <note>original: "asme"</note> or by us. Therefore, **having sat down** <note>original: "āsadya"</note> **on this sacrificial grass** <note>original: "asmin barhiṣi"</note> in the sacrifice, **may you rejoice** <note>original: "mādayethām"</note> in the drinking of the Soma.

-> ॥ Thus ends the twelfth section of the first chapter of the fifth book ॥ <-

---

The eighth hymn, beginning **"With your action"** <note>original: "saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā"</note>, consists of eight verses seen by the sage <term>Bharadvaja</term> <note>a prominent Vedic seer</note>. It is in the <term>Trishtubh</term> meter <note>a rhythmic structure of 11 syllables per line</note> and is dedicated to the dual deity Indra-Vishnu. The index states: **"With your action is an eight-verse hymn to Indra-Vishnu"** <note>original: "saṃ vām aṣṭāvaindrāvaiṣṇavam iti"</note>. In the <term>Ukthya</term> <note>a specific type of Soma sacrifice</note> during the <term>Third Libation</term> <note>the evening offering</note>, this hymn belongs to the priest called the <term>Achhavaka</term>. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: **"The offering-verse is 'With your action, O Indra-Vishnu, masters of exhilaration'"** <note>original: "Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 6. 9."</note>. If there is an excess of Soma during the <term>Morning Libation</term>, in the rite performed under certain circumstances, according to the opinion of the teacher Ganagari, **"With your action"** is the offering-verse for that rite. It is noted: **"Because the deity is primary, Ganagari says it is for Indra-Vishnu: 'With your action I urge you with nourishment'"** <note>original: "Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 6. 7."</note>. For an excess of Soma at the <term>Midday Libation</term>, the verse **"She who is of all"** <note>original: "yā viśvāsām"</note> is the offering-verse, as noted: **"The offering-verse is 'She who is the generator of all prayers'"** <note>original: "Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 6. 9."</note>. At the Third Libation of the Ukthya, the priest's offering-verse is "O Indra-Vishnu, masters of exhilaration," as already cited. At the Third Libation, "O Indra-Vishnu, drink the honey" is the verse for the set offerings. It is noted: **"O Indra-Vishnu, drink of the sweet Soma... this hymn for the worthy Jatavedas"** <note>original: "Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 5. 5."</note>.

-> ॥ There, the First Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

I urge you both with action and with nourishment, O Indra and Vishnu, at the completion of this work. Accept the sacrifice and grant us wealth, leading us across with safe paths. ॥ 1 ॥

Indra-Varuna: dual deity representing power and cosmic order.
Indra-Vishnu: dual deity representing power and pervasive space.
Soma: the sacred ritual beverage.
Barhis: the layer of sacred grass on which gods are invited to sit.
Bharadvaja: the traditional author/seer of this hymn.
Trishtubh: a classic 44-syllable Vedic meter.
Shrauta Sutra: ancient manuals describing the performance of Vedic rituals.
</vocab>

## Hymn Text

### Verse 6.69.1 (Word-for-word Analysis)

Together | for you both | with [devotional] work | together | with food | I impel | O Indra and Vishnu | of the work | at the end | of this | may you both enjoy | the sacrifice | and wealth | bestow | by paths | for us | bringing [us] across ॥ 1 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra and Vishnu** <note>original: "indrāviṣṇū"</note>, **I impel** <note>original: "sam hinomi"</note> or urge you both **together** with **prayer** <note>original: "karmaṇā"</note> and with **oblation** <note>original: "haviṣā"</note>. I encourage you well. At the **end** <note>original: "pāre"</note> or the conclusion **of this** <note>original: "asya"</note> ritual **work** <note>original: "apasaḥ"</note> or recitation, **may you both enjoy** <note>original: "juṣethāṃ"</note> or partake in the **sacrifice**. Furthermore, you two who are **bringing us across** <note>original: "pārayantā"</note> or leading us to the opposite shore by **paths** <note>original: "pathibhiḥ"</note> that are **without injury** <note>original: "ariṣṭaiḥ"</note> or safe, **bestow** <note>original: "dhattaṃ"</note> or give **wealth** <note>original: "draviṇam"</note> to us ॥

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

Those two who are the progenitors of all prayers, O Indra and Vishnu, who are the jars for holding the Soma; may the hymns being recited reach you, may the songs being sung with the chants [reach you]. ॥ 2 ॥

### Verse 6.69.2 (Word-for-word Analysis)

Who | of all | the progenitors | of prayers | O Indra and Vishnu | jars | for holding Soma | [prefix] | for you both | the hymns | being recited | may they reach | [prefix] | the songs | being sung | by the singers ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Those two** <note>original: "yā"</note> who are the famous Indra and Vishnu are the **progenitors** <note>original: "janitārā"</note> or the generators **of all** <note>original: "viśvāsām"</note> **prayers** <note>original: "matīnām"</note> or praises. <note>The word "janitārā" is a form derived from the root "jan," meaning to give birth or generate. Alternatively, it comes from the root "janī," meaning manifestation; in this case, a specific grammatical rule allows for the elision of certain sounds.</note> May they also be like the **jars** <note>original: "kalaśā"</note> or vessels that are **holders of Soma** <note>original: "somadhānā"</note>, the containers for the sacred drink.

Now follows the direct praise: O Indra and Vishnu, may the **hymns** <note>original: "giraḥ"</note> or spoken words in the form of specialized recitations, which are **being recited** <note>original: "śasyamānā"</note> or uttered, **reach** <note>original: "pra avantu"</note> or come to **you both** <note>original: "vām" </note>. May the **songs** <note>original: "stomāsaḥ"</note> or praises **being sung** <note>original: "gīyamānāsaḥ"</note> by the **singers** <note>original: "arkaiḥ"</note> or reciters also reach you ॥

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

O Indra and Vishnu, lords of exhilaration, come to the Soma, bearing wealth. May the prayers anoint you both with the rays of light, and may the songs [anoint you] when being recited with the hymns. ॥ 3 ॥

### Verse 6.69.3 (Word-for-word Analysis)

O Indra and Vishnu | lords of exhilaration | of the exhilarations | [prefix] | the Soma | may you two come | wealth | bearing | together | you both | may they anoint | with rays of light | of prayers | together | the songs | being recited | with hymns ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra and Vishnu**, you are the **lords of exhilaration** <note>original: "madapatī"</note>, the masters of the **Somas** <note>original: "madānām"</note>. In this phrase "lords of exhilaration," the word "exhilaration" is used as a descriptive repetition. You are also bearing **wealth** <note>original: "draviṇo"</note> or riches. <note>The word "draviṇo" is formed by the merging of the two words "draviṇā" and "u"...</note>

- Indra-Vishnu: A dual deity representing the combined power of the King of Gods and the All-Pervader.

## Commentary (Sayana) — Continued from previous page
The word **wealth** <note>original: "draviṇo"</note> is thus derived. **Bestowing** <note>original: "dadhānā"</note> or giving, may you both come toward the Soma. May the **hymns** <note>original: "stomāsaḥ"</note> of the **thinkers** <note>original: "matīnām"</note>—the praise-singers—which are being **recited** <note>original: "shasyamānāsaḥ"</note> or uttered along with the **invocatory prayers** <note>original: "ukthyaiḥ shastraiḥ"</note>, **anoint** <note>original: "samañjantu"</note> or enrich you both with **rays of light** <note>original: "aktubhiḥ"</note> or splendor. That is, may they make you prosperous. The repetition of the word "together" <note>original: "sam sam"</note> is intended to show respect or emphasis.

---

->॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
May the horses that overcome enemies, O Indra and Vishnu, who rejoice together, bring you both here. May you both enjoy all the invocations of the thinkers; listen to my sacred prayers and my songs of praise. ॥ 4 ॥

**Padapatha (Word-for-word Analysis):**
Bring | you both | horses | overcoming enemies | O Indra and Vishnu | rejoicing together | may they carry |
may you both enjoy | all | invocations | of the thinkers | [prefix] | sacred prayers | listen | songs | my ॥ 4 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Indra and Vishnu** <note>original: "indrāviṣṇū"</note>, may the **horses** <note>original: "ashvāsaḥ"</note> who are **overcomers of enemies** <note>original: "abhimātiṣāhaḥ"</note>—meaning those who strike down or defeat attackers—and who **rejoice together** <note>original: "sadhamādaḥ"</note>, bring you both here. May you both **enjoy** <note>original: "juṣethām"</note> or accept **all** <note>original: "vishvā"</note> the **invocations** <note>original: "havanā"</note> or hymns of the thinkers. For that purpose, **listen** <note>original: "upashṛṇutam"</note> to my **sacred prayers** <note>original: "brahmāṇi"</note> and my **songs** <note>original: "giraḥ"</note> in the form of recited chants.

---

->॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
O Indra and Vishnu, that deed of yours is praiseworthy; in the exhilaration of Soma, you both stepped out widely. You made the atmosphere wider and you expanded the worlds for our living. ॥ 5 ॥

**Padapatha (Word-for-word Analysis):**
O Indra and Vishnu | that | praiseworthy | for you both | of the Soma | in the exhilaration | wide | you both stepped out |
you both made | the atmosphere | wider | you expanded | for living | our | the worlds ॥ 5 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Indra and Vishnu**, that deed of yours is **praiseworthy** <note>original: "panayāyyam"</note> or worthy of being celebrated. What is that deed? He explains: when there was **exhilaration from the Soma** <note>original: "somasya made"</note>, you both **stepped out** <note>original: "cakramāthe"</note> or strode across **widely** <note>original: "uru"</note>. Although the act of wide-stepping <term>Vikrama: The famous three steps of Vishnu that encompass the universe</term> usually belongs to Vishnu alone, it is spoken of here as belonging to both because they are united in a single purpose. Furthermore, you **made** <note>original: "akṛṇutam"</note> the **atmosphere** <note>original: "antarikṣam"</note> **wider** <note>original: "varīyaḥ"</note> or more spacious. And also, the **worlds** <note>original: "rajāṃsi"</note>—all the regions. **Yaska** <note>An ancient etymologist and author of the Nirukta, the oldest surviving Sanskrit glossary</note> says that the word 'rajāṃsi' refers to the worlds. You **expanded** <note>original: "aprathatam"</note> them for **our living** <note>original: "no jīvase"</note> or for our continued survival.

---

->॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

## Hymn Text

<note>RV 6.69.6 — Word-for-word Analysis (Concluding Verse 6)</note>

Indra-Vishnu | by the **oblation** <note>original: "havisā"</note> | increasing | of the noble | eating | with **homage** <note>original: "namasā"</note> | having given oblations | **pouring ghee** <note>original: "ghrtāsutī"</note> | **wealth** <note>original: "dravinam"</note> | bestow | upon us | **ocean** <note>original: "samudrah"</note> | you two are | **vessel** <note>original: "kalashah"</note> | Soma-containing ॥ 6 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Indra and Vishnu, who consume **ghee** <note>clarified butter used in sacrifices</note> as your food <note>original: "ghrtāsutī"</note>, growing strong by the oblation or by the Soma, you who are the eaters of the first-pressed Soma: bestow **wealth** <note>original: "dravinam"</note> or riches upon us, the sacrificers who have offered oblations with **homage** <note>original: "namasā"</note> or reverential bowing. Furthermore, you two are like the **ocean** <note>original: "samudrah"</note>—the great reservoir of water—because you are the **vessel** <note>original: "kalashah"</note> in which the Soma is contained <note>original: "somadhānah"</note>.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥<-

<note>RV 6.69.7 — Original Verse</note>

O Indra and Vishnu, drink of this sweet Soma; O **achievers** <note>original: "dastrā"</note>, fill your **bellies** <note>original: "jatharam"</note>. May the exhilarating offerings reach you both; listen to my **sacred prayers** <note>original: "brahmāni"</note> and my call. ॥ 7 ॥

<note>RV 6.69.7 — Word-for-word Analysis</note>

Indra-Vishnu | drink | of the sweet | this | Soma | O achievers | belly | fill | [prefix] | to you both | foods | exhilarating | have reached | [prefix] | sacred prayers | listen | call | my ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **achievers** <note>original: "dastrā"; those who are beautiful or doers of great deeds</note>, Indra and Vishnu, drink this intoxicating Soma. Moreover, may you **fill your bellies** <note>original: "jatharam prnethām"</note> with the Soma juice. O Indra and Vishnu, may the exhilarating foods—consisting of the Soma—reach you both. Listen to my **sacred prayers** <note>original: "brahmāni"</note>, which are my songs of praise, and listen to my **call** <note>original: "havam"</note>, which is my invitation to the sacrifice.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Eighth Verse ॥<-

<note>RV 6.69.8 — Original Verse</note>

Both of you have conquered; you are never defeated. Not one of these two has ever been conquered. O Vishnu, when you and Indra strove together, you distributed the **thousand-fold** <note>original: "sahasram"</note> in **three ways** <note>original: "tredhā"</note>. ॥ 8 ॥

<note>RV 6.69.8 — Word-for-word Analysis</note>

Both | have conquered | not | [prefix] | you are defeated | not | [prefix] | was conquered | whichever | [particle] | of these two | Indra | and | O Vishnu | when | you strove | in three ways | thousand-fold | [prefix] | that | you distributed ॥ 8 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Indra and Vishnu, you **both** <note>original: "ubhā"</note> have conquered; you have triumphed over your enemies. You are never defeated; that is, you are never overcome at any time. Between the two of you, **neither one** <note>original: "katarashcana"</note> has ever been conquered. O Vishnu, when you and Indra **strove** <note>original: "apaspṛdhethām"</note> or contended against the demons <note>the Asuras</note>, you **distributed** <note>original: "vaitairayethām"; or stepped across</note> that which is **thousand-fold** <note>meaning infinite or immeasurable</note> and situated in **three ways** <note>original: "tredhā"</note>—in the form of the worlds, the Vedas, and speech. As the **Brahmana** <note>the ritualistic explanations of the Vedas</note> says: "Regarding 'Both of you have conquered,' both of them indeed conquered..." <note>The text here begins to quote a scriptural justification for this shared victory.</note>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on Sukta 69 (dedicated to the dual deity Indra-Vishnu) and begins Sukta 70 (dedicated to Heaven and Earth). It bridges the 13th and 14th sections (Vargas) of the first chapter of the fifth book (Ashtaka).</meta>

"Neither of you has been conquered, nor has either been defeated" <note>This refers to the equal power of Indra and Vishnu</note>. For neither of them was ever defeated. When you two, Indra and Vishnu, strove together, you distributed the thousand-fold power into three parts. Indeed, Vishnu and Indra fought against the **Asuras** <note>a class of powerful beings often opposed to the gods</note>. Having conquered them, they said, "Let us make a settlement." The Asuras agreed. Then Indra said, "As much as this Vishnu can stride over in three steps, that shall be ours, and the rest shall be yours." He <note>Vishnu</note> then strode over these worlds, the Vedas, and Speech itself. That is what they call "the thousand"—namely, these worlds, the Vedas, and Speech. Thus, the text says "you two distributed it." **Aitareya Brahmana 6.15.** Or alternatively, "that thousand" refers to a thousand cows, which they divided into three parts.

-> ॥ Thus ends the thirteenth section (varga) of the first chapter in the fifth book. ॥ <-

**The ninth hymn, beginning "Ghee-laden" <note>original: "ghrtavatī"</note>, consists of six verses. It was seen by the sage Bharadvaja, is composed in the Jagati meter, and is dedicated to the deity Heaven and Earth <note>original: "dyāvāprthivī"</note>. Thus the index states: "The six verses starting with 'Ghee-laden' are dedicated to Heaven and Earth in the Jagati meter." During the fifth day of the Abhiplava ritual, in the litany to the All-Gods, the first three verses are used to introduce the section for Heaven and Earth. This is indicated in the ritual manual: "The two triplets 'Ghee-laden for the beauty of beings' and 'Indra with the gift-bearing Ribhus'..." (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 7.6). It is also used in the Brihaspatisava sacrifice (Ashvalayana 9.5). On the third day of the Abhiplava ritual, the three verses beginning with "With Ghee, Heaven and Earth" are used for the same purpose (Ashvalayana 7.9).**

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the first verse ॥ <-

Rich with **ghee** <note>clarified butter used in offerings; also symbolizes rain or light</note>, the refuge of all beings, wide, expansive, milking sweetness, beautifully formed.
Heaven and Earth are held apart by the law of **Varuna** <note>the god of cosmic order</note>; they are ageless and possess abundant life-force. ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Rich with ghee | for the beings | as a refuge | wide | expansive | milking sweetness | beautifully formed.**
**Heaven and Earth | of Varuna | by the law | held apart | ageless | with abundant life-force. ॥ 1 ॥**

O Heaven and Earth, you are **rich with ghee** <note>original: "ghrtavatī"</note>, meaning you are either full of radiance or full of water. (This is based on "ghee" being listed as a name for water in the ancient lexicons). The word "become" should be supplied to complete the sense. You are the **refuge of beings** <note>original: "bhuvanānām abhishriyā"</note>, meaning you are to be resorted to by all living creatures; this quality should be understood throughout. You are **wide** <note>original: "urvī"</note> or extensive, and **expansive** <note>original: "prthvī"</note> because you have spread out into many forms and functions. You are **milking sweetness** <note>original: "madhudughe"</note>, meaning you yield the "honey" of rain-water. You are **beautifully formed** <note>original: "supeshasā"</note>, having a lovely appearance. By the **law** <note>original: "dharmanā"</note> or command of Varuna, who is the...

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the 70th hymn of the 6th book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda, dedicated to the dual deity Heaven and Earth (Dyavaprithivi). # Mandala 6, Section 6, Hymn 70 | Fifth Book | Page 881

...held apart and separately supported by the law <note>original: *dharma*</note> of the regulator, these two are unaging <note>eternal</note> and possess abundant seed <note>original: *bhūri-retasā*; meaning they possess great creative power or produce many effects</note>. Here, because the context is a direct praise of Heaven and Earth, the mention of "the ruddy one" <note>original: *aruṇasya*</note> should be understood as referring to their shared radiance.

---

-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Never-clashing, of many streams, full of moisture, they yield ghee for the one who acts well, they of pure vows. Ruling over this world, O Heaven and Earth, pour into us that seed which is beneficial for mankind. ॥ 2 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis (Padapatha):**
Never-clashing. Of many streams. Full of moisture. Ghee. They yield.
For the well-doer. Of pure vows.
Ruling. Of this. Of the world. O Heaven and Earth. In us. Seed.
Pour. Which. Beneficial for mankind. ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Never-clashing** <note>original: *asam-yantī*</note> means not sticking together, or perhaps pushing away the darkness. **Of many streams** <note>original: *bhūri-dhāre*</note> refers to the many flows; from the Heaven come streams of rain, and from the Earth come streams of juice/essence produced from sacrificial offerings. Thus, both are "of many streams." **Full of moisture** <note>original: *payasvatī*</note> means possessing water. On this, the ancient etymologist Yaska says: "Either not sticking together or pushing away, of many streams, possessing water" <note>Nirukta 5.2</note>. **Of pure vows** <note>original: *śuci-vrate*</note> means Heaven and Earth are of pure actions. For the **well-doer** <note>original: *su-kṛte*</note>, the sacrificer who performs good deeds, they **yield** <note>original: *duhāte* - literally "milk"</note> **ghee** <note>original: *ghṛtam*</note>, which here refers to the water that is the cause of the prosperity of crops and other things.

Now follows the direct praise: **O Heaven and Earth** <note>original: *rodasī*</note>, you two are **ruling** <note>original: *rājan-tī*</note> or acting as the masters of **this world** <note>meaning the collection of all living beings</note>. You two, **pour into us** <note>original: *asme... siñcatam*</note> that **seed** <note>original: *retaḥ*</note> which is the power capable of procreation. **Which seed is beneficial for mankind** <note>original: *manur-hitam*</note>, meaning it is helpful for all human beings.

---

-> ॥ Now the third verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
That mortal, O Heaven and Earth, O supporting ones, who offers to you for an upright path, he succeeds. He increases with progeny according to the law; from you are poured [seeds] of various forms but of common purpose. ॥ 3 ॥

**Word-by-word Analysis (Padapatha):**
Who. To you two. For the upright. For the path. O Heaven and Earth. Mortal. Has offered. O supporting ones. He. Succeeds.
Forward. With progeny. He is born/increases. From the law. Beyond. Of you two. Poured. Of various forms. Having common purpose. ॥ 3 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
**O supporting ones** <note>original: *dhiṣaṇe*</note>, you who are brave or who serve as the dwelling place for the entire world, **O Heaven and Earth**, that **mortal** <note>human</note> **who offers** oblations to you **for an upright path** <note>meaning for your easy and smooth movement</note>, that mortal **succeeds**. He accomplishes his desires. Furthermore, he **increases** <note>original: *pra-jāyate*</note> or prospers **with progeny** <note>sons, grandsons, etc.</note>. He becomes greatly expanded...

...comes to be. By the law <note>original: *dharmaṇā*</note>, by the ritual act <note>original: *karmaṇā*</note>, and over and above you two, the seeds <note>original: *retāṃsi*; here referring to the rain or creative life-force</note> are poured.
