# Rig Veda
### [Book 5. Chapter 1. Section 23.]

-> ॥ Here is the first verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Men generate the praiseworthy **Agni** <note>the god of fire</note> with their **fingers** from the two **friction sticks** by the movement of their hands—him who is visible from afar, the lord of the house, and the one who moves toward the gods. ॥ 1 ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
That. Agni. Our. With fingers. From the two friction sticks. By the movement of hands. They generate. Praiseworthy. Seen from afar. Lord of the house. Moving toward the gods. ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**Men** refers to the leaders or the officiating priests. They **generate Agni**, who is present within the **two friction sticks** <note>original: *araṇyoḥ*; the wooden sticks used to churn fire</note>, by the **movement of their hands** and with their **fingers**. He is **praiseworthy**, meaning highly extolled, and **visible from afar**, meaning he can be seen from a distance or he watches from a distance. He is the **lord of the house**, the protector of dwellings, and is **moving toward the gods** <note>original: *atharyum*; interpreted as one who goes toward the sacrifice or is active</note>. The word for **fingers** <note>original: *dīdhitiḥ*</note> is used because they are employed in sacred acts. The fire is said to be born from the friction sticks because it is "fittingly born" from their union. Thus, they generated the one who is fair to behold and the master of the home. (Reference: Nirukta 5.10).

---

-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
The **Vasus** <note>the "dwellers" or the Vasishtha clan</note> have established that Agni in the **home** for protection against any danger—him who is beautiful to behold, who is **worthy of honor**, and who has been the **eternal** resident in the dwelling. ॥ 2 ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
That. Agni. In the home. The Vasus. Down. They established. Beautiful to behold. For protection. From anywhere. Even. Worthy of honor. Who. In the house. Was. Eternal. ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The Agni who **was eternal** <note>original: *ajasra*; unceasing</note> and who is **worthy of honor** in the house—meaning he is to be worshipped or enriched with oblations—him, the **Vasus** have established. The Vasus are the "dwellers," specifically the family of **Vasishtha**. They placed Agni, who is **beautiful to behold**, within the **home** for **protection** from **any** cause of fear whatsoever. They "established" <note>original: *nyṛkhan*; literally "dug in" or "fixed firmly"</note> him there.

---

-> ॥ Now the third verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O **youngest** Agni, being greatly kindled, shine before us with an **unceasing**, bright **flame**; to you, all **strengths** continually come. ॥ 3 ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
Greatly kindled. O Agni. Shine. In front. Our. With unceasing. With a bright flame. O youngest. To you. Continual. Toward. They go. Strengths/Spoils. ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **youngest** <note>original: *yaviṣṭha*; fire is called youngest because it is freshly kindled every day</note> Agni, you who are **greatly kindled**, shine before us with an **unceasing**, moving **bright flame**...

<vocab>
- **Agni**: The fire deity, central focus of this hymn.
- **Narah**: Men, specifically referring to the officiating priests (<term>ritvijas<gloss>priests who perform sacrifices according to the seasons</gloss></term>).
- **Didhiti**: Fingers; explained by the commentator as being "placed" in ritual work.
- **Arani**: Friction sticks; the traditional Vedic method of producing fire by churning wood.
- **Grihapati**: Lord or protector of the household.
- **Dakshayya**: Worthy of worship or being honored with offerings.
- **Yavishtha**: Most youthful; a common epithet for Agni as he is "reborn" each time the fire is lit.
- **Surmya**: A bright, flowing flame or a beautiful metal image.
</vocab>

# Rig Veda
### [Book 7. Chapter 1. Section 1.]
**Fifth Book of Eight (Ashtaka 5). Page 903.**

With your flame, shine before us <note>for our sake</note> in the place of the **Ahavaniya** fire <note>the consecrated fire used for offerings</note>. Shine brightly! Many **foods** and **oblations** <note>original: *vājāḥ*; representing strength-giving offerings</note> approach you. They come toward you.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the fourth verse ॥ <-

Your **fires**, O Agni, shine forth most excellently <note>superior to all others</note>, radiant and providing **noble sons**, there where **noble men** sit together in assembly. ॥ 4 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Forth. Your. Fires. Than [other] fires. Better. Out. Having noble heroes. Shine intensely. Radiant. Where. Men. Sit together. Well-born. ॥ 4 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

These fires of yours shine intensely and preeminently. They are superior to ordinary worldly fires, they are exceedingly radiant, and they grant the blessing of excellent sons and grandsons. These fires are present where **well-born men**—the leaders of the ritual acts, who may be the **sacrificers** <note>the patrons who pay for the ritual</note> or the **priests**—sit together in harmony.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the fifth verse ॥ <-

Grant us, O Agni, through our **prayer**, wealth that is full of **noble sons** and **excellent descendants**, O Conqueror! Provide us that **praiseworthy** wealth which no **attacker** <note>one who comes with ill intent</note> or practitioner of **malice** can overcome. ॥ 5 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Give. To us. O Agni. By prayer. Wealth. Having noble heroes. Having good descendants. O Conqueror. Praised. Not. Which. The attacker. Overcomes. Possessed of magic or violence. ॥ 5 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, you who are skilled in overcoming enemies! Grant to us, through our **hymn of praise**, **wealth** <note>original: *rayim*</note> that is accompanied by noble sons and grandsons, and is highly esteemed. Give us this prosperity. This wealth is such that no **approaching enemy** <note>original: *yāvā*</note> who comes with the intent to harm <note>The commentator notes a grammatical variation here regarding the word for 'attacker' specific to the Vedic dialect</note> can overcome or obstruct it. In other words, this wealth is secure from all violence.

-> ॥ This concludes the twenty-third section (varga) of the first chapter of the fifth book ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the sixth verse ॥ <-

The **young woman** <note>likely the sacrificial ladle</note>, bearing oblations and **shining with ghee** <note>clarified butter</note>, approaches him who is highly skilled, by **night** and by **day**. **Devotion**, seeking wealth, approaches him as her own. ॥ 6 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Toward. Whom. Goes. The young woman. Highly skilled. By night. By day. Bearing oblations. Shining with ghee. Toward. Own. Him. Devotion. Seeking wealth. ॥ 6 ॥

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the 36th hymn of the first Mandala of the Rig Veda, attributed to the Sage Kanva Ghaura. # Rig Veda
### [Ashtaka 1. Adhyaya 5. Varga 24.]
**Page 904**

## Commentary (Sayana)
[Continuation of the commentary on verse 6]

The **sacrificial ladle** <note>original: *ghṛtācī*; literally "the one that moves with clarified butter"</note>, which is full of offerings, approaches that Agni who is very capable and strong. This ladle is like a **young woman** <note>original: *yuvatiḥ*</note> who is eternally united with the fire; she approaches him by night and by day. Similarly, the devotee’s own **radiant devotion** <note>original: *arama-tiḥ*; meaning a restless or intense light of praise</note>, seeking wealth for those who sing the hymns, approaches the fire.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Here is the seventh verse ॥ <-

O Agni, burn away all **enemies** <note>original: *arātīḥ*; those who do not give offerings or act with hostility</note> with those scorching heats with which you burned the demon **Jarutha**. Drive away **disease** <note>original: *amīvām*</note> until it is silenced! ॥ 7 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
All. O Agni. Away. Burn. Enemies. With those. With heats. You burned. Jarutha. 
Forth. Silently <note>original: *ni-svaram*; literally "making the sound go down" or "utterly"</note>. Drive away. Disease. ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, burn away all enemies with your intense splendors. Use those same heats with which you once burned **Jarutha**, a demon <note>original: *rākṣasam*</note> who makes harsh or terrifying sounds. The word *Jarutha* is derived from the root meaning "to sound" <note>original: *gṛṇāteḥ*</note>. You burned him; likewise, burn these enemies. Furthermore, drive away **disease** or sickness so that its torment is utterly subdued and silenced. The term **silently** <note>original: *ni-svaram*</note> comes from the root *svṛ*, meaning both sound and heat/torment. Drive it away thoroughly <note>The commentator Bhattabhaskara Mishra suggests the word *chata* means "to go," implying the disease should be made to go away</note>.

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Here is the eighth verse ॥ <-

O **most excellent**, bright, **shining**, and purifying Agni! For the one who kindles your **splendor** <note>original: *anīkam*; literally "face" or "front flame"</note>, may you be present here at our sacrifice with these our praises! ॥ 8 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Hither. Who. Your. O Agni. Kindles. Splendor. O Most Excellent. O Bright one. O Shining one. O Purifier. 
And also. Our. With these. With praises. Here. Be. ॥ 8 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, you are the **most excellent** <note>original: *vasiṣṭha*</note>, the pure white or **bright** one <note>original: *śukra*</note>, the **ever-shining** <note>original: *dīdivaḥ*</note>, and the **purifier** <note>original: *pāvaka*</note>. For the person who kindles your flame and increases your splendor, you are present. In that same way, for us as well, may you be present at this sacrifice through these hymns of praise that we offer.

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Here is the ninth verse ॥ <-

The **mortals** and **leaders** who have attained your **splendor**, O Agni, have flourished in many places. May you also be **well-disposed** toward us here! ॥ 9 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Apart. Who. Your. O Agni. Have attained/shared. Splendor. Mortals. Men. Flourishing/Swelling. In many places. 
And also. Our. With these. Well-disposed. Here. Be. ॥ 9 ॥

# Mandala 7. Anuvaka 1. Hymn 1.
### [Book 5. Page 905]

## Commentary (Sayana) — Continued (Verse 9)
O Agni, those **men** <note>original: *narah*; leaders of the rites or sacrificers</note> who are the patrons of the sacrifice, desiring to satisfy your **radiant form** <note>original: *anīkam*; literally "face" or "army/splendor"</note>, have distributed it in many places for the benefit of the ancestors or the noble ones. This is to say, they have **established** <note>original: *ādadhur-iti yāvat*</note> you. Like them, may you be well-disposed toward us and these singers of the hymns, and be present here at this sacrifice.

---

## Hymn Text — Verse 10
-> ॥ Here is the tenth verse ॥ <-

May these **heroic men** <note>original: *naro... śūrā*</note> in the **battles against the enemy** <note>original: *vṛtrahatyeṣu*; literally "the slaying of Vrtra," referring to any conflict with obstructive forces</note> overcome all **demonic illusions** <note>original: *adevīr... māyāḥ*; ungodly or deceptive powers</note>—those men who praise my excellent **devotion** <note>original: *dhiyaṃ*</note>. ॥ 10 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Pada-Patha):**
These. Men. In the slaying of the enemy (battles). Heroes. All. Ungodly. Overcome (may they be). Illusions.
Who. My. Devotion (or ritual action). Praise. Excellent. ॥ 10 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
Those men who praise or speak of my excellent **devotion** <note>original: *dhiyaṃ*; meaning either the ritual act or the hymn of praise</note>, those men who are affectionate toward me, may they be heroic in **battles** <note>original: *vṛtrahatyeṣu*; literally "slaying of Vrtra"</note> and overcome all **demonic illusions** <note>original: *adevīḥ... māyāḥ*; the powers of the Asuras</note>. Let them be victorious.

-> ॥ This marks the end of the twenty-fourth section (Varga) of the first chapter of the fifth book ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text — Verse 11
-> ॥ Here is the eleventh verse ॥ <-

O Agni, may we not sit in an **empty house** <note>original: *śūnye*; a house without children or life</note>, nor may we, O **Lord of the Home** <note>original: *durya*</note>, sit in the houses of others. May we not be without **descendants** <note>original: *aśeṣasaḥ*</note> or **heroic strength** <note>original: *avīratā*</note> while attending to you; let us dwell in houses full of **offspring** <note>original: *prajāvatīṣu*</note>. ॥ 11 ॥

**Word-for-word analysis (Pada-Patha):**
Not. In emptiness. O Agni. Down. May we sit. Of men. Not. Without descendants. Lack of heroes (sons). Around. You.
In [houses] possessing offspring. In houses. O Lord of the Home. ॥ 11 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, let us not sit—that is, let us not dwell—in an **empty house** <note>original: *śūnye*; a home lacking sons and other family members</note>. Nor may we dwell in the houses of other men. O Agni, you who are **beneficial to the home** <note>original: *durya*</note>, may we not be **without sons** <note>original: *aśeṣasaḥ*; the term 'śeṣa' is listed in ancient lexicons as a synonym for 'son'</note>. May we not be characterized by a **lack of heroic sons** <note>original: *avīratā*</note> while we serve you. Instead, let us dwell only in houses that possess **offspring** <note>original: *prajāvatīṣu*</note>.

To our house, which the **twin Aswins** <note>original: *aśvinī*</note> always visit, the house of sacrifice, rich in offspring and good children, growing with **descendants** <note>original: *śeṣasā*</note> born of the light... ॥ 12 ॥

## Hymn Text

<note>Word-for-word breakdown (Padapatha) for Verse 12</note>
Whom. O Agni. Constantly. Approaches. The sacrifice. Having offspring. Having good descendants. The home. To us. By his own nature. Through a son. Increasing. ॥ 12 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The sacrifice, which is the refuge of the ritual, and which Agni—who possesses speed and horses—constantly approaches; give to us, O Agni, that **home** <note>original: *kshayam*</note> which is full of offspring, including servants and followers, and blessed with excellent descendants. May this home be **increasing** <note>original: *vavṛdhānam*</note> through a son born of our own blood. This is the intended meaning.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here begins the thirteenth verse ॥ <-

<note>Rig Veda 5.4.13</note>
Protect us, O Agni, from the unpleasing **demon** <note>original: *rakshas*</note>; protect us from the malice of the stingy and the sinful. With you as my ally, may I overcome those who bring war against us. ॥ 13 ॥

<note>Word-for-word breakdown (Padapatha) for Verse 13</note>
Protect. Us. O Agni. From the demon. Unpleasing. Protect. From the malice. Of the non-giver (stingy). Of the one who desires sin. You. As an ally. Those who desire battle. Overcome. May I. ॥ 13 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, protect us from the **demon** <note>original: *rakshas*</note> who is an object of dislike and displeasure. Furthermore, protect us from the **malice** <note>original: *dhūrteḥ*; meaning the injury or harm</note> of the one who does not give (the stingy) and who desires sin. Also, with **you as my ally** <note>original: *tvā yujā*; with you as a helper</note>, may I **overcome** <note>original: *abhi syām*; meaning to defeat or surpass</note> those who desire battle against us.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here begins the fourteenth verse ॥ <-

<note>Rig Veda 5.4.14</note>
May this Agni excel all other fires, where the vigorous son, with firm-gripping hands and a thousand paths, approaches with the imperishable hymn. ॥ 14 ॥

<note>Word-for-word breakdown (Padapatha) for Verse 14</note>
He. Indeed. Agni. Fires. Excel (surpass). May he be. Other. Where. Vigorous. Son. Firm-handed. Of a thousand paths. The imperishable [hymn]. Approaches. ॥ 14 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

"He indeed"—that is, our very own Agni (the sacrificial fires such as the Ahavaniya)—may he **excel** <note>original: *atyastu*; surpass or be superior to</note> the other fires belonging to other people. "Where"—meaning in which Agni—our **son** <note>original: *tanayaḥ*</note>, who is vigorous (possessing strength or food) and **firm-handed** <note>original: *vīḷupāṇiḥ*; having a strong grip</note>, approaches. The word **Vilu** <note>original: *vīḷu*</note> is cited in ancient lexicons as a synonym for "strength." This son, who has "a thousand paths" (meaning much food, many locations, or abundant water), approaches while perfectly performing the service with an **imperishable** <note>original: *akṣarā*; a praise or song that never decays</note> hymn. The underlying sentiment is that the Agni of a person who possesses such capable sons will always triumph over the fires of others. ॥ 14 ॥

# Mandala 7, Chapter 1, Hymn 1 — Fifth Ashtaka — Page 907

-> ॥ Verse 15 ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
He is Agni, who protects the one who kindles the fire from the **attacker** <note>original: *vanuṣyataḥ*</note>; may he deliver the worshiper from **sin** <note>original: *aṃhasaḥ*</note>. Noble-born heroes surround him. ॥ 15 ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
He. Verily. Agni. Who. From the attacker. Protects. The one who kindles. From sin. May deliver. Noble-born. Around. Move. Heroes. ॥ 15 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
He who protects the kindler—the one who awakens the fire—from the **attacker** <note>original: *vanuṣyataḥ*; the ancient etymologist Yaska defines this as one who kills or harms</note>. May he deliver or guard him completely from excessive sin or distress. This Agni is the one whom noble-born heroes—meaning virtuous praisers or perhaps worthy sons—surround and serve.

-> ॥ Thus ends the twenty-fifth group (Varga) of the first chapter of the fifth [Ashtaka] ॥ <-

-> ॥ Now the sixteenth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
This is that Agni, to whom oblations are poured, whom the **lord** <note>original: *īśānaḥ*</note>, possessing offerings, kindles with fuel. The **invoker** <note>original: *hotā*</note> goes around him during the rituals. ॥ 16 ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
This. That. Agni. Poured-with-oblations. In many places. Whom. The lord. Completely. Verily. Kindles. Possessing-offerings. Around. Whom. Goes. In rituals. The invoker. ॥ 16 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Whom the **lord** <note>original: *īśānaḥ*; meaning one who is wealthy or one who desires prosperity</note>, the sacrificer possessing offerings, kindles or lights perfectly. He whom the **invoker** <note>original: *hotā*; the priest who calls the gods</note> walks around during the **rituals** <note>original: *adhvareṣu*; sacrifices characterized as being free from violence or interruption</note>. This is that Agni, who is invoked with oblations in many places or across many sacrifices.

-> ॥ Now the seventeenth verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O Agni, may we, as masters of wealth, offer many eternal oblations to you; performing both **tasks** <note>original: *vahatū*</note> at the sacrifice. ॥ 17 ॥

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
To you. O Agni. Oblations. Many. Masters. May we offer. Eternal. Both. Performing. Tasks. At the sacrifice. ॥ 17 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, while we are **masters** <note>original: *īśānāso*; lords of riches</note>, may we offer many eternal oblations, such as the daily fire-offerings. In the **sacrifice** <note>original: *miyedhe*</note>, we perform both **tasks** <note>original: *vahatū*; literally 'the two vehicles', referring here to the hymns of praise and the ritual recitations</note> that carry the ritual forward.

<note>Technical Terms Summary:</note>
**Agni**: The deity of Fire and the mediator between gods and humans.
**Attacker** <note>original: *vanuṣyat*</note>: An enemy or one who seeks to cause harm.
**Sin** <note>original: *aṃhas*</note>: Moral or physical distress; often refers to the obstruction of the ritual.
**Yaska**: An ancient scholar famous for the Nirukta, the earliest treatise on Sanskrit etymology.
**Invoker** <note>original: *hotā*</note>: One of the primary priests in a Vedic sacrifice responsible for reciting the Rig Veda.
**Ritual** <note>original: *adhvara*</note>: A sacrifice; the word specifically implies a process that is "not-injured" or continuous.
**Sacrifice** <note>original: *miyedha*</note>: A sacred ritual or offering.

<keywords>Agni, Sayana Commentary, Vedic Sacrifice, Hotar priest, Mandala 7, Sanskrit Etymology, Yaska, Varga 25</keywords>

# 909 ॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Mandala 7. Lesson 1. Hymn 1.] ॥ Fifth Ashtaka ॥ 909

->॥ Now the twenty-first [verse] ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**O Agni, you who are easily invoked, beautiful to behold, and possessor of bright light—O Son of Strength—shine forth! Being with us, do not burn our eternal, own son; may the heroic man, who is beneficial to people, not perish from us. ॥ 21 ॥**

**Pada-patha:**
You. Agni. Well-invoked. Pleasant-to-behold. With-bright-light. O Son. Of strength. Shine.
Not. Your. With. In the son. In the eternal. Burn. Not. The hero. From us. Beneficial to men.
Perish. ॥ 21 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Son of Strength** <note>original: *sahasaḥ sūno*; a common title for Agni because fire is produced by the "strength" of rubbing sticks together</note>, O Agni, you who are **well-invoked** <note>original: *suhavaḥ*; easily called to the sacrifice</note> and **pleasant to behold** <note>original: *raṇvasandṛk*; of beautiful appearance</note>, **shine forth** with **bright light**! Furthermore, being a companion **with** us, **do not burn** <note>original: *mā dhak*</note> our **eternal**, legitimate **son**. Additionally, let the **heroic** son, who is **beneficial to men**, not **perish** <note>original: *vi dāsīt*; be exhausted or pass away</note> or be separated **from us**. <note>The grammar here uses the fifth case (ablative) to function as the sixth case (genitive).</note>

->॥ Now the twenty-second [verse] ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**O Agni, do not report us for difficult maintenance among these fires kindled by the gods; O Son of Strength, let not the ill-wills of you, the god, reach us even through error. ॥ 22 ॥**

**Pada-patha:**
Not. Us. Agni. For difficult-maintenance. With. In these. Kindled-by-gods. In the fires. Proclaim.
Not. Your. Us. Ill-wills. From error. Even. Of the god. O Son. Of strength. Reach. ॥ 22 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, as our companion, **do not proclaim** <note>original: *mā pravochaḥ*; do not speak of or report</note> **us** for **difficult maintenance** <note>original: *durmṛtaye*; interpreted here as the hardship of poverty or "unhappy death"</note> among **these fires** which are **kindled by the gods** <note>original: *deveddheṣu*; lit. "ignited by the priests/gods"</note>. The meaning is: speak of us in such a way that the fires, who are your helpers, may support us without hardship. Furthermore, **O Son of Strength**, child of power, O Agni, let the **ill-wills** <note>original: *durmatayaḥ*; wicked thoughts or intentions to punish</note> of **you**, the shining **god**, not **reach** us, even **from error** <note>original: *bhṛmāt*; due to confusion or a slip</note>. <note>In this context, the commentator notes a grammatical vowel change in the word "bhṛmāt."</note>

-> ।। Now the twenty-fourth [verse] ।। <-

**O Agni, you who are the knower of our great prosperity, bring great wealth to our wise patrons. O Mighty One, through that wealth may we rejoice, remaining undiminished throughout our lifespan and blessed with heroic sons. ॥ 24 ॥**

**Pada-patha:**
Great. Our. Agni. Of-prosperity. Knower. Wealth. To-wise-patrons. Bring. Great.
By-which. We. O-Mighty-One. May-rejoice. Undiminished. By-lifespan. With-heroic-sons. ॥ 24 ॥

-> ।। Now the twenty-fifth [verse] ।। <-

**Now, O Agni, exalt my sacred prayers. O Divine One, satisfy the generous patrons. May we be under the favor of both groups. Protect us always with your blessings. ॥ 25 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni of **fair countenance** <note>original: "svanīka"; meaning one with beautiful light</note>, you who are **immortal** <note>original: "amartye"</note> and have a divine nature—**that mortal** <note>original: "sa marto"</note> man who **offers** <note>original: "ājuhoti"</note> a **sacrificial oblation** <note>original: "havyaṃ"</note> to you becomes **wealthy** <note>original: "revān"</note>. To **whom** <note>meaning that mortal</note> the **wise patron** <note>original: "sūriḥ"; a learned person</note>, **seeking a goal** <note>original: "arthī"; desiring wealth etc.</note>, **comes asking** <note>original: "pṛcchamāno"; inquiring if the man is generous</note>, that man himself **gives** <note>original: "dadāti"</note> or holds the **bestowal of wealth** <note>original: "vasuvaniṃ"</note> for the **deities**. Alternatively, the interpretation is: that **deity** Agni **holds** or supports the **bestower of wealth** <note>meaning the sacrificer</note>. To **that Agni**, the **wise** <note>the singer of praises</note> who has a **need** comes **asking**, "Who is this Agni?"

---

O **Agni**, you who are the **knower** <note>original: "vidvān"</note> of **our** <note>original: "no"</note> **great prosperity** <note>original: "maho suvitasya"; meaning our auspicious ritual work</note>—this means you know our good deeds—bring **great wealth** <note>original: "bṛhantaṃ rayiṃ"</note> to us, the **wise patrons** <note>the singers of praise</note>. He further describes this wealth: O **Mighty One** <note>original: "sahasāvan"; powerful Agni</note>, through **which** wealth **we**, the singers, being **undiminished** <note>original: "avikṣitāso"</note>, having a **full lifespan** <note>original: "āyuṣā"</note>, and **blessed with heroic sons** <note>original: "suvīrāḥ"; having excellent sons and grandsons</note>, **may rejoice** <note>original: "madema"; be happy</note>.

---

<vocab>
- **Agni**: The deity of fire, often called "of fair countenance" due to the beauty of the flames.
- **Mortal (Martah)**: Refers to the human sacrificer in contrast to the immortal gods.
- **Wise patron (Sūri)**: The noble or learned person who sponsors the sacrifice.
- **Rayi**: A general term for wealth, often encompassing cattle, sons, and long life in the Vedic context.
- **Suvīra**: Literally "good heroes," referring to the blessing of strong, capable sons to carry on the lineage.
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes the first hymn of the fourth Mandala of the Rig Veda, focusing on Agni's role as a mediator who bestows wealth and longevity upon mortal sacrificers and wise patrons. The commentary by Sayana provides two interpretations for how wealth is circulated between the deity, the patron, and the singer.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Rig Veda 4.1.23-25, Sayana's Bhashya, sacrificial oblation, prosperity, immortality vs mortality, wealth (Rayi), heroic sons (Suvira)</keywords>

<meta>This page concludes the first chapter (Adhyaya) of the fifth section (Ashtaka) of the Rigveda commentary and begins the second hymn of the seventh Book (Mandala). It provides the final verse of Hymn 1, followed by formal closing prayers and the introduction to Hymn 2, which is an Apri—a special type of propitiatory hymn used in rituals.</meta>

## Hymn Text

**O Agni, quickly exalt my sacred prayers. O Divine One, grant happiness to our generous patrons. May both we and they be under your favor. Protect us always with your blessings. ॥ 25 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

This verse has already been explained. <note>This verse serves as a recurring refrain for many hymns in the seventh Mandala.</note>

-> ॥ This concludes the twenty-seventh section of the first chapter of the fifth [Ashtaka] ॥ <-

**By the light of the meaning of the Veda, may Vidyatirtha-Maheshvara—who dispels the darkness in the heart—grant the four goals of human life.** <note>The four goals, or Purusharthas, are Virtue (Dharma), Prosperity (Artha), Pleasure (Kama), and Liberation (Moksha).</note>

Thus ends the **first chapter of the fifth section** in the "Light of the Vedic Meaning," a commentary on the Rigveda collection composed by Sayanacharya, the minister of the empire of King Virabukka, the supreme ruler and promoter of the Vedic path.

**I salute that Vidyatirtha-Maheshvara, whose breath is the Vedas and who created the entire world from the Vedas.**

The second hymn, beginning with **"Accept ours"** <note>original: "juṣasva naḥ"</note>, consists of eleven verses. The Seer <note>Rishi</note> is Vasishtha, and the meter is Trishtubh <note>a Vedic meter with eleven syllables per line</note>. Because it is categorized as an *Apra* <note>original: "āpra"</note> hymn, this is an *Apri* hymn—a specific ritual litany—that omits the deity Tanunapat <note>a form of Agni often invoked in other families' rituals</note>. In each verse, specific forms of Agni, starting with the "Kindled One" <note>original: "Samiddha"</note>, are mentioned as the deities. The index of the Veda <note>Anukramani</note> states: "The eleven verses starting with *juṣasva* are *Apri* verses." This hymn is used in animal sacrifices. It is also noted in the ritual manuals: "For the Vasishtha family, the *Apri* begins with 'Accept our fuel'" <note>original: "juṣasva naḥ samidham"; referencing Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 3.2</note>. As mentioned previously, this serves as the offering prayer <note>original: "yājyā"</note> for the sacrifice to the deity Tvashtri during the "Offerings to the Wives" <note>original: "patnī-saṃyāja"</note> and as the invitatory prayer <note>original: "anuvākyā"</note> for the sacrificial cake in animal sacrifices dedicated to Tvashtri <note>the divine architect/artisan</note>.

-> ॥ The first verse of that hymn follows ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**O Agni, accept our fuel today; with your great and worshipful smoke, O exalted one, shine forth. Reach the heavenly peak with your smoke-columns; spread out and join with the rays of the sun. ॥ 1 ॥**

**Word-for-word breakdown:**
Accept. Ours. Fuel. O Agni. Today. Shine. Great. Worshipful. Smoke. O Exalted One.
Reach. Heavenly. Peak. With smoke-columns. Fully. With rays. Spread out. Of the sun. ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, **accept** <note>original: "juṣasva"</note> or partake in **our fuel** <note>original: "samidham"</note> **today**. **Worshipful** <note>original: "yajataṃ"</note>, meaning deserving of worship or excellent...

<term>Agni</term> The Vedic deity of fire, acting as the mediator between humans and gods.
<term>Vasishtha</term> One of the most famous Vedic Seers (Rishis) to whom the seventh Book of the Rigveda is attributed.
<term>Apri</term> A specific group of hymns used to "propitiate" or "please" the deities before the main animal sacrifice.
<term>Samidh</term> The wood or kindling used to sustain the sacrificial fire.
<term>Trishtubh</term> A rhythmic meter consisting of four lines of eleven syllables each.
<term>Sayanacharya</term> The 14th-century scholar and minister in the Vijayanagara Empire who wrote the definitive commentary on the Vedas.
<term>Virabukka</term> King Bukka Raya I, a founding ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire and patron of Vedic scholarship.

<keywords>Agni, Vasishtha, Apri hymns, Sayanacharya, King Virabukka, Vedic ritual, Trishtubh meter, animal sacrifice, Vidyatirtha</keywords>

...releasing and impelling smoke, shine exceedingly. And also, touch the divine summit—the firmament—with your heated, brilliant rays. Furthermore, become one in essence with the rays and light of the Sun. Join with them.

-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
We shall praise the greatness of **Narashamsa** <note>original: "narāśaṃsasya"</note> among these gods, of the worshipful one with sacrifices; those gods who are wise, pure, and sustainers of prayer, who enjoy both types of offerings. ॥ 2 ॥

The word-by-word analysis <note>Pada-patha</note>:
Narāśaṃsasya । mahimānam । eṣām । upa । stoṣāma । yajatasya । yajñaiḥ ।
ye । su-kratavaḥ । śucayaḥ । dhiyam-dhāḥ । svadanti । devāḥ । ubhayāni । havyā ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
Those gods who are <term>Sukratu</term> <note>wise or performers of good deeds</note>, <term>Shuci</term> <note>brilliant</note>, and <term>Dhiyamdha</term> <note>the sustainers or holders of ritual actions</note>, who <term>Svadanti</term> <note>taste or enjoy</note> both types of offerings—the Soma-based offerings and the butter-based offerings—among them, through sacrifices (with oblations or hymns), we shall praise the greatness of the worshipful **Narashamsa**. Narashamsa is a specific form of Agni who is "to be praised by men" <note>original: "naraiḥ praśaṃsanyasya"</note>.

In this regard, the ancient etymologist Yaska says: "Men, sitting down, praise him." The sage Shakapuni says: "He is Agni, for he is praised by men." Regarding this verse, it is said:
> We shall praise the greatness of Narashamsa among these gods, of the worshipful one with sacrifices; those who perform good deeds, are pure, and the sustainers of prayer—let the gods enjoy both offerings, the Soma and the others. <note>Nirukta 8.6</note>

---

-> ॥ Now the third verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O priests, let us always honor Agni for the sacrifice—he who is worthy of praise, the powerful, the wise, the messenger between the two worlds <note>Heaven and Earth</note>, the speaker of truth; kindled by **Manu** <note>the first man</note> as he is by men today. ॥ 3 ॥

The word-by-word analysis:
Iḷenyam । vaḥ । asuram । su-dakṣam । antaḥ । dūtam । rodasī iti । satya-vācam ।
manu-ṣvat । agnim । manunā । sam-iddham । sam । adhvarāya । sadam । it । mahema ॥ 3 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O officiating priests, for your sake, we should always honor—that is, fully worship—Agni for the sacrifice. He is <term>Ilenya</term> <note>worthy of praise</note>, <term>Asura</term> <note>powerful</note>, and <term>Sudaksha</term> <note>very wise</note>. He acts as a <term>Duta</term> <note>messenger</note> traveling between the two worlds of Heaven and Earth to carry oblations to the gods. He is <term>Satyavacha</term> <note>a speaker of truth</note>. He is kindled <term>Manushvat</term> <note>in the manner of men</note>; just as humans kindle the fire now, he was kindled in ancient times by **Manu**, the Lord of Progeny. <note>The commentator notes a grammatical variation here where the verb form suggests 'we honor' though the context implies an exhortation to the priests.</note>

<summary>This page contains the second and third verses of an Apri hymn, focusing on Agni's roles as Narashamsa (the one praised by men) and as the divine messenger kindled by the ancestral figure Manu.</summary>

<header>Mandala 7, Adhyaya 1, Sukta 2 || Fifth Ashtaka || 913</header>

->॥ Now the fourth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
Desirous of worshiping, bringing the offerings on bended knees, they spread the sacrificial grass <note>original: "barhis"</note> with reverence before the fire. O **Adhvaryu** priests, as you invoke the gods, adorn the grass that is glistening with ghee and yields abundance. ॥ 4 ॥

**The word-by-word analysis <note>Pada-patha</note>:**
saparyavaḥ । bharamāṇāḥ । abhi-jñu । pra । vṛñjate । namasā । barhiḥ । agnau ।
ā-juhvānāḥ । ghṛta-pṛṣṭham । pṛṣat-vat । adhvaryavaḥ । haviṣā । marjayadhvam ॥ 4 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Those who are **saparyavaḥ** <note>desiring to perform service or worship</note>, being **abhijñu** <note>with knees bent or approaching on the knees</note>, and **bharamāṇāḥ** <note>bearing or bringing the materials with their steps</note>, spread the **barhis** <note>sacrificial grass</note> in the fire along with the **namasā** <note>reverence or the oblation</note>. They "spread it forth" <note>original: "pra-vṛñjate"</note>. The sage explains further: O **Adhvaryu priests**, you who are **ājuhvānāḥ** <note>invoking or offering</note>, must **marjayadhvam** <note>cleanse, adorn, or serve</note> the fire and the grass which is **ghṛtapṛṣṭham** <note>sprinkled with ghee on its surface</note> and **pṛṣadvat** <note>marked with large drops of butter</note>, along with the **haviṣā** <note>sacrificial oblation</note>. Perform the service for the Fire.

---

->॥ Now the fifth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
The pious performers of the rite, seeking the gods, have opened wide the Divine Doors <note>original: "dvāraḥ"</note>, desiring chariots in the sacrifice. Like two mother cows licking their young calf, the two ancient ones <note>the Ladles</note> are anointed in the assemblies, just as rivers join together. ॥ 5 ॥

**The word-by-word analysis <note>Pada-patha</note>:**
su-ādhyāḥ । vi । duraḥ । deva-yantaḥ । aśiśrayuḥ । rathi-yuḥ । deva-tātā ।
pūrvī iti । śiśum । na । mātarā । rihāṇe iti । sam-yayuvaḥ । na । samaneṣu । añjan ॥ 5 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **svādhyaḥ** <note>those who perform good works</note> and **devayantaḥ** <note>sacrificers who desire the presence of the gods</note>, as well as those who are **rathayu** <note>desiring chariots/wealth</note>, have **vyaśiśrayuḥ** <note>resorted to or opened wide</note> the **duraḥ** <note>the doors of the sacrificial hall</note> during the **devatātā** <note>in the sacrifice or among the assembly of gods</note>. Furthermore, in the **samaneṣu** <note>the sacrificial assemblies</note>, the **pūrvī** <note>the two ancient ladles, the Juhu and Upabhrit, placed with their tips facing east</note> are like **mātarā** <note>two mother cows</note> who are **rihāṇe** <note>licking</note> their **śiśum na** <note>like a calf</note>—in this case, Agni. They are **añjan** <note>anointing him with ghee</note>, just as **ayuvo na** <note>like rivers</note> join together to moisten a field with water. The Adhvaryu priests anoint the fire with clarified butter.

->॥ Thus ends the first section <note>varga</note> of the second chapter <note>adhyaya</note> of the fifth book <note>ashtaka</note> ॥<-

---

->॥ Now the sixth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
And may the two divine maidens, the great Dawn and Night, yielders of abundance like a cow that is easily milked, sit upon the sacrificial grass. Worshipful and wealthy ones, may they rest here for our prosperity. ॥ 6 ॥

**The word-by-word analysis <note>Pada-patha</note>:**
uta । yoṣaṇe iti । divye iti । mahī iti । naḥ । uṣāsānaktā । su-dughā-iva । dhenuḥ ।
barhiḥ-sadā । puru-hūte iti । maghonī iti । ā । yajñiye iti । su-vitāya । śrayetām ॥ 6 ॥

<vocab>
Adhvaryu: The priest responsible for the physical ritual actions and measurements.
Barhis: A bed of sacred kusha grass spread for the gods to sit upon during the sacrifice.
Ghee-backed: A poetic description for ritual items or the fire itself when glistening with clarified butter.
Seeking the gods: A translation of 'Devayanta,' referring to the intent of the ritual patron.
Dawn and Night: Deified as a pair (Ushasanakta) who jointly preside over the passage of ritual time.
Adorn/Service: The verb 'marjayadhvam' implies both physical cleaning/polishing and ritual honoring.
Sacrifice: The 'Yajna,' the central Vedic ritual of offering.
</vocab>

Sayana's commentary clarifies the metaphors of mother cows and flowing rivers used to describe the anointing of the fire with butter.</summary>

<page-num>914</page-num>
<header>॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Ashtaka 5, Adhyaya 2, Varga 2]</header>

And furthermore, may the two **young women** <note>original: "yoṣaṇe"</note>, who are of feminine form and exist in the **divine** heavens, who are **great** <note>original: "mahī"</note> and **seated upon the sacrificial grass** <note>original: "barhiṣadā"</note>, who are **invoked by many** <note>original: "puruhūte"</note> in praise, who are **wealthy** <note>original: "maghonī"</note> and **worthy of sacrifice** <note>original: "yajñiye"</note>—namely **Dawn and Night** <note>original: "uṣāsānaktā"</note>—favor us for our **welfare** <note>original: "suvitāya"</note>, just as a **cow that yields milk easily** <note>original: "sudugheva dhenuḥ"</note>—a wish-fulfilling cow—provides for us.

->॥ Now the seventh verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
O wise ones, I consider you two, the knowers of all beings, as the performers of the rites in the sacrifices of men. Make our sacrifice ascend during the invocations; you two possess desirable things among the gods. ॥ 7 ॥

**The word-by-word analysis <note>Pada-patha</note>:**
viprā । yajñeṣu । mānuṣeṣu । kārū iti । manye । vām । jāta-vedasā । yajadhyai ।
ūrdhvam । naḥ । adhvaram । kṛtam । haveṣu । tā । deveṣu । vanathaḥ । vāryāṇi ॥ 7 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O divine invokers <note>The "Divine Hotars," two celestial priests associated with Agni</note>, you who are **wise** <note>original: "viprā"</note> and **possessors of wealth from birth** <note>original: "jātavedasā"</note>, I **consider** <note>original: "manye"</note> you to be the **performers** <note>original: "kārū"</note> of the ritual acts in the **sacrifices** <note>original: "yajñeṣu"</note> performed by **humanity** <note>original: "mānuṣeṣu"</note>. I praise you so that I may worship. Furthermore, when the **invocations** <note>original: "haveṣu"</note> and hymns are underway, **make** <note>original: "kṛtam"</note> our **undeviating sacrifice** <note>original: "adhvaram"</note> **ascend** <note>original: "ūrdhvaṃ"</note> toward the gods. Moreover, you two **possess** <note>original: "vanathaḥ"</note> the **desirable** <note>original: "vāryāṇi"</note> riches that exist among the **gods** <note>original: "deveṣu"</note>; the meaning is that you should bestow those riches upon us.

---

->॥ Now the eighth verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
May **Bharati** come here in harmony with the Bharatis; **Ila** with the gods and humans, and **Agni**. May **Sarasvati** come with the Sarasvatas. May these **three goddesses** sit upon this **sacrificial grass**. ॥ 8 ॥

**The word-by-word analysis <note>Pada-patha</note>:**
ā । bhāratī । bhāratībhiḥ । sa-joṣāḥ । iḷā । devaiḥ । manuṣyebhiḥ । agniḥ ।
sarasvatī । sārasvatebhiḥ । arvāk । tisraḥ । devyaḥ । barhiḥ । ā । idam । sadantu ॥ 8 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
These four verses starting from this one are also found in the eighth chapter of the second book <note>Mandala 3, Sukta 4, Verse 8</note>. Although they have been explained there, they are briefly explained here again due to the distance between the texts. May **Bharati** <note>The goddess of speech/revelation</note>, the wife of the sun <note>original: "bharatasya-ādityasya patnī"</note>, come together **in harmony with the Bharatis** <note>her attendant powers</note>. May **Ila** <note>The goddess of nourishment and the sacrificial earth</note> come along with **Agni** and the **gods** born of the human world. May **Sarasvati** <note>The goddess of the celestial waters and wisdom</note> come **towards us** <note>original: "arvāk"</note> along with the **Sarasvata** deities of the middle region <note>the atmosphere</note>. Having arrived, may these **three goddesses** <note>original: "tisro devyaḥ"</note> <note>Note: The commentator notes a grammatical substitution where the accusative form is used for the nominative plural</note> **sit upon this sacrificial grass** <note>original: "barhiḥ ā-sadantu"</note>.

## Hymn Text

->|| Now the ninth verse ||<-

O Tvaṣṭṛ, being well-pleased, grant us that seminal fluid which is quick and nourishing. From which is born a heroic son, skilled in action, of great ability, a presser of the sacred stones, and a seeker of the gods. ॥ 9 ॥

**That (tat) । to us (naḥ) । seminal fluid (turīpam) । then (adha) । nourishing (poṣayitnu) । divine (devam) । of Tvaṣṭṛ (tvaṣṭuḥ) । [prefix] (vi) । being well-pleased (rarāṇaḥ) । grant/release (syasva) ॥**
**From which (yataḥ) । a hero (vīraḥ) । skilled in action (karmaṇyaḥ) । of great ability (su-dakṣaḥ) । who has joined the pressing-stones (yukta-grāvā) । is born (jāyate) । a seeker of the gods (deva-kāmaḥ) ॥ 9 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O shining **Tvaṣṭṛ** <note>the divine artisan and shaper of forms</note>, you who are delighting, **release** <note>original: "vi syasva"; specifically meaning to let go or bestow</note> to **us** <note>original: "naḥ"</note> that **seminal fluid** <note>original: "turīpam"</note> which quickly reaches and **nourishes** <note>original: "poṣayitnu"</note>. From **which** <note>original: "yataḥ"</note> fluid a **heroic son** <note>original: "vīraḥ"</note> is **born** <note>original: "jāyate"</note>—one who is **skilled** <note>original: "karmanyaḥ"</note> in performing rituals, **possesses great strength** <note>original: "sudakṣaḥ"</note>, is a **presser of Soma** <note>original: "yuktagrāva"; literally "one who has joined the pressing stones"</note>, and is a **seeker of the gods** <note>original: "devakāmaḥ"</note>.

---

## Hymn Text

->|| Now the tenth verse ||<-

O Lord of the Forest, release the offerings to the gods. Let Agni, as the preparer, season the oblation. Let him, the most truthful Invoker, perform the sacrifice, as he knows the births of the gods. ॥ 10 ॥

**O Lord of the Forest (vanaspate) । [prefix] (ava) । release (sṛja) । near to (upa) । the gods (devān) । Agni (agniḥ) । the oblation (haviḥ) । the preparer (śamitā) । seasons/refines (sūdayati) ॥**
**He (saḥ) । indeed (it) । [particle] (ūṃ) । the Invoker (hotā) । most truthful (satya-taraḥ) । let him sacrifice (yajāti) । just as (yathā) । of the gods (devānām) । the births (janimāni) । he knows (veda) ॥ 10 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Lord of the Forest** <note>original: "vanaspate"; refers to the sacrificial post or Agni in that form</note>, **release** the offerings **towards the gods**. Now follows a praise in the third person: **Agni**, being the **Lord of the Forest** and the **preparer** <note>original: "śamitā"; the one who prepares the sacrificial animal</note>, **refines** <note>original: "sūdayati"</note> or prepares the **oblation**. May he do so. **He** <note>original: "sa it"</note> himself, the Lord of the Forest, though he is the **Invoker** <note>original: "hotā"</note> of the gods and **most truthful**, let him **sacrifice**. Just **as** he himself **knows** the **births** <note>original: "janimāni"</note> of the **gods**, so may he perform the rite.

---

## Hymn Text

->|| Now the eleventh verse ||<-

Come, O Agni, when kindled, turning towards us in the same chariot with Indra and the swift gods. May Aditi, the mother of noble sons, sit upon our sacred grass; may the immortal gods delight in the "Svāhā" call. ॥ 11 ॥

**[prefix] (ā) । come (yāhi) । O Agni (agne) । being kindled (sam-idhānaḥ) । towards us (arvāṅ) । with Indra (indreṇa) । with the gods (devaiḥ) । in the same chariot (sa-ratham) । with the swift ones (turebhiḥ) ॥**
**The sacred grass (barhiḥ) । for us (naḥ) । let her sit (āstām) । Aditi (aditiḥ) । having noble sons (su-putrā) । Hail! (svāhā) । the gods (devāḥ) । the immortals (amṛtāḥ) । let them delight (mādayantām) ॥ 11 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **kindled Agni**, come **towards us** <note>original: "arvāṅ"</note> and face us. Come in the **same chariot** <note>original: "saratham"</note> with **Indra** and with the **swift** <note>original: "turebhiḥ"</note> **gods**... <note>Commentary continues on the next page.</note>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary for the second Varga (section) of the second Adhyaya (chapter) within the fifth Ashtaka (octave) and begins Sukta 3 of the seventh Mandala. It includes the ritual context (Anukramanika) and the first two verses dedicated to Agni.</meta>

<header>|| Rigveda || [Chapter 5, Lesson 2, Section 3]</header>

Come in such a way that you are on the same chariot. Approach! May Aditi, she of the noble sons <note>original: "suputra"</note>, sit upon our sacred grass <note>original: "barhis"</note>. May all the immortal gods, being satisfied by the "Svaha" offering, rejoice.

---

**The third hymn, beginning with "Agniṃ vo devam" (To Agni, your god), consists of ten verses. It was seen by the seer Vasistha, composed in the Trishtubh meter, and is addressed to the fire-god Agni.** Here is the ritual index <note>original: "Anukramanika"</note>: The ten hymns starting with "Agniṃ vo..." (excluding the third and fourth) are assigned to the morning recitation <note>original: "Prataranuvaka"</note> in the Agneya ritual, specifically in the Trishtubh section of the Ashvina-shastra invocation. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "Of the ten starting with 'Agniṃ vo...', one should omit the third and fourth" <note>reference: Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.13</note>. In the "Vyudha" ten-night ritual, on the eighth day, this hymn serves as the Ajya-shastra invocation. As stated: "The Ajya-shastra of the second is 'Agniṃ vo devam'" <note>reference: Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 8.10</note>.

->|| The First Verse ||<-

## Hymn Text
**Bring near for yourselves the divine Agni, together with other fires, he who is the most skilled sacrificer, the messenger at the sacrifice; he who, among mortals, is firmly established, the guardian of the Cosmic Order, the burning-headed, the ghee-fed, the Purifier. ॥ 1 ॥**

**Agni (Agniṃ) । for you (vaḥ) । divine (devam) । with fires (agnibhiḥ) । together (sajoṣam) । most skilled sacrificer (yajiṣṭham) । messenger (dūtam) । at the sacrifice (adhvare) । make/establish (kṛṇudhvam) ॥**
**Who (yaḥ) । among mortals (martyeṣu) । firmly established (ni-dhruviḥ) । possessor of Truth (ṛta-vā) । burning-headed (tapuḥ-mūrddhā) । ghee-fed (ghṛta-annaḥ) । the Purifier (pāvakaḥ) ॥ 1 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **priests** <note>original: "devāḥ"; here interpreted by the commentator as the officiating priests</note>, establish for **yourselves** <note>original: "vaḥ"</note> the **divine** and shining **Agni**—together with **other fires**—as the **best sacrificer** and the **messenger** in the **sacrifice** <note>original: "adhvare"; literally "a rite without crookedness/violence"</note>. Even though he is a god, **who** <note>Agni</note> remains **firmly established** <note>original: "nidhruviḥ"</note> among **mortals**. He is the **possessor of the sacrifice** <note>original: "ṛtāvā"; also meaning one who holds the Truth</note>, having **burning luster for a head** <note>original: "tapumūrddhā"</note>, **fed by ghee** <note>original: "ghṛtānnaḥ"</note>, and is the **Purifier** <note>original: "pāvakaḥ"</note> who cleanses all things.

---

->|| The Second Verse ||<-

## Hymn Text
**Like a horse neighing when seeking grass, he has stood forth from the great enclosure; then the wind blows after his flame, and then indeed your path is black. ॥ 2 ॥**

**Neighing (prothat) । a horse (aśvaḥ) । like (na) । in the grass (yavase) । seeking to eat (aviṣyan) । when (yadā) । from the great (mahaḥ) । enclosure (saṃ-varaṇāt) । [prefix] (vi) । stood (asthāt) ॥**
**Then (āt) । his (asya) । the wind (vātaḥ) । after (anu) । blows (vāti) । flame (śociḥ) । then (adha) । indeed (sma) । your (te) । path (vrajanam) । black (kṛṣṇam) । is (asti) ॥ 2 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Like **a horse** <note>original: "aśvaḥ na"</note> that is **seeking to eat** grass and makes a **neighing sound** while moving about, **when** the **great** forest fire **stands forth** from its **enclosure** <note>original: "saṃvaraṇāt"; meaning the confinement of the wood or the thicket</note>, it spreads out among the standing trees...

The text provides ritual instructions for its use in Vedic ceremonies and presents the first two verses describing Agni's role as a divine messenger and his horse-like power when burning through the forest.</summary>

## Commentary (Sayana)
[Conclusion of commentary for Verse 2]

The wind blows along with the flame and light of this Agni. Now follows the direct praise. After that, O Agni, your path is black <note>original: "krishnam-asti"</note>. It becomes so. The particle "sma" is used here to complete the meter.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Verse 3 ॥<-

**When you are newly born, O showerer of benefits, your unaging flames rise up and are kindled, O Agni. The ruddy smoke reaches toward the sky; as the messenger, O Agni, you indeed go to the gods. ॥ 3 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Up. Whose. Your. Newly-born. Of the showerer. O Agni. Move. Unaging. Kindled.
Toward. Heaven. Ruddy. Smoke. Goes. Together. Messenger. O Agni. You go. Indeed. To the gods. ॥ 3 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, you who have newly appeared, who are the showerer of benefits <term>Vrishan: literally "the bull," an epithet for a powerful deity who showers blessings</term>, your unaging and decay-less flames rise upward and are kindled. The ruddy and shining smoke of such a one reaches toward the heavens. O Agni, being the messenger <note>original: "duta"</note>, you truly reach and approach the gods.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Verse 4 ॥<-

**Whose light has spread across the earth, when you have quickly consumed the food with your jaws; your onset goes forth like a released army, O wonderful one, you consume the wood with your tongue as if it were barley. ॥ 4 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Apart. Whose. Your. On the earth. Power/Light. Spread. Quickly. When. Foods. Consumed. With jaws.
Like an army. Released. Onset. Your. Goes. Barley. Like. O wonderful one. With the tongue. You consume/pervade. ॥ 4 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, your light and strength <note>original: "pajah"</note>, which belongs to you in your form as the consumer of wood, has spread across the earth. When you quickly consume the "foods"—referring to the wood and fuel—with your "jaws"—meaning your flames—your onset <note>original: "prasitih"</note> or flame goes forth like a prepared army. O wonderful and beautiful Agni <note>original: "dasma"</note>, you consume or pervade the wood with your tongue <note>original: "juhva"</note> just as one might consume barley.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Verse 5 ॥<-

**Him, indeed, at night and at dawn, the most youthful Agni, men groom like a swift horse; sharpening him, the guest in his own dwelling, the light of the showered-upon and powerful one shines forth. ॥ 5 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Him. Indeed. At night. Him. At dawn. The most youthful. Agni. A horse. Like. They groom. Men.
Sharpening. The guest. His. In the place. Shines. Light. Of the showered-upon. Of the powerful. ॥ 5 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
[Conclusion of commentary for Verse 5]

...the most youthful <term>yaviṣṭha: the youngest or most vigorous, an epithet for the fire that is newly kindled every day</term>, the most youthful guest <note>original: "atithim"</note>, who is to be honored like a guest—this very Agni, during the night and also during the day, men kindle him in the "womb" or seat of Agni, which is the location of the *Ahavaniya* altar or the sacrificial hearth. They groom him <note>original: "marjayanta"</note> as one would a horse that is constantly moving and capable of carrying a load. The flame of that Agni, the showerer <term>Vrishan: the 'bull' who rains down or fulfills desires</term> to whom offerings have been made, shines brightly.

-> ॥ Thus ends the third Varga in the second Adhyaya of the fifth [Ashtaka] ॥ <-

---

-> ॥ Now the Sixth [Verse] ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**O Agni of beautiful countenance, your appearance is fair to see when you shine like a golden ornament or the sun in close proximity. Your strength goes forth like the thunder of heaven; like the wonderful sun, you display your brilliance. ॥ 6 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada Patha):**
Fair-to-look-upon. Your. O-one-of-beautiful-countenance. Appearance. Out. When. Gold/Sun. Like. You-shine. In-proximity.
Of-heaven. Like. Your. Of-the-thunderer. Goes. Strength. Wonderful. Like. Sun. Toward. You-display. Brilliance. ॥ 6 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni of good brilliance <term>svanika: having beautiful flames or a fair face</term>, whenever you shine particularly <note>original: "vi rochase"</note> like a golden ornament <note>original: "rukmo na"</note> or like the sun when it is nearby, then your appearance—your form or your limbs—becomes fair to look upon <term>susandṛk: pleasing to the sight</term>. Moreover, your strength <term>śuṣma: vital energy or force</term> goes forth like the thunderbolt of the sky. Like the visible sun, you display your own brilliance.

---

-> ॥ Now the Seventh [Verse] ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Just as we may offer to you, Agni, with the "Svaha" call, with milk-offerings, with clarified butter, and with sacrificial foods; with those unmeasured powers of yours, O Agni, protect us with a hundred iron-strong forts. ॥ 7 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada Patha):**
As. To-you. Well-spoken/Hail. To-Agni. We-may-offer. Around. With-offerings. With-clarified-butter. And. With-sacrificial-foods.
With-those. Us. O-Agni. With-unmeasured. With-great-powers. A-hundred. With-forts. Made-of-iron. Down. Protect. ॥ 7 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, leader! For you, let there be this well-offered oblation <note>original: "svāhā"</note>. Furthermore, just as we serve you with cows or cow-products <note>original: "iḷābhiḥ"</note> such as milk, with oblations accompanied by clarified butter <term>ghṛta: sacrificial melted butter</term>, and with sacrificial cakes and foods, so may you also protect us completely. Protect us with those famous, immeasurable powers of yours, through a hundred cities or forts that are as strong as iron <note>The commentator notes that in some contexts "iron" or "ayas" can also refer to gold/brightness</note>.

<page-num>919</page-num>
<header>Mandala 1. Anuvaka 9. Sukta 3.]  ॥ Fifth Ashtaka ॥  919</header>

-> ॥ Now the Eighth [Verse] ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Whatever [flames] of yours exist for the giver, O unassailable ones, or whatever words by which you protect men; with those, O Son of Strength, protect us along with our noble patrons and singers, O Knower of all Beings. ॥ 8 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Whatever. Or. Your. Are. For-the-giver. Unassailable. Words. Or. By-which. Protecting-men. Protect.
With-those. Us. O-Son! (of). Strength. Down. Protect. Together-with. Noble-patrons. Singers. O-Knower-of-Beings. ॥ 8 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**O Son of Strength** <note>original: "sahasaḥ sūno"</note>, O child of power! **O Agni, Knower of Beings** <note>original: "jātavedas"</note>, for the **giver** <note>original: "dāśuṣe"</note>—that is, the one who bestows offerings—whatever flames of yours **exist**, or whatever **words** <note>original: "giraḥ"</note> there are that remain **unassailable** <note>original: "adhṛṣṭā"</note> (unconquered by demons), and **by which** words you **protect** <note>original: "uruṣyāḥ"</note> the people who possess many sons—with **both of those**, protect **us**. The word **together-with** <note>original: "smat"</note> is a word of praise. **Protect** <note>original: "ni pāhi"</note>—that is, guard thoroughly—our praised **noble patrons** <term>sūrin: the wealthy leaders who sponsor the sacrifice and urge the offerings forward</term> and the **singers** <note>original: "jaritṝn"</note> who chant the hymns.

---

-> ॥ Now the Ninth [Verse] ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
When he goes forth like a polished axe, shining with his own light and his own body; he who is desirable, of good intent, and a purifier, was born from his mother for the sacrifice to the gods. ॥ 9 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Out. When. Purified-like. Axe. Pure. Went. With-own. Light. With-body. Shining.
Toward. Who. Of-the-mother. Desirable. Was-born. For-the-sacrifice-to-gods. Of-good-intent. Purifier. ॥ 9 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**When** the **pure** Agni, **shining** with his **own light** and his extended **body**, **goes forth** from the wood like a **purified axe** <term>svadhiti: a sacrificial knife or axe that has been sharpened or polished</term>, he then becomes ready for the **sacrifice to the gods**. He [the poet] clarifies this further: **He who** is **desirable** <note>original: "uśenyaḥ"</note>, of **good intent** <note>original: "sukratuḥ"</note> (performing good works), and the **purifier** <note>original: "pāvakaḥ"</note>, was **born from his mother**—that is, from the fire-sticks <note>original: "araṇyāḥ"</note>. Such an Agni becomes fit for the sacrifice to the gods.

---

-> ॥ Now the Tenth [Verse] ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O Agni, shine these fortunes upon us; may we also attain a wise understanding. May all these [blessings] be for the singers and the one who praises. May you all protect us always with blessings. ॥ 10 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
These. Our. O-Agni. Fortunes. Shine. Also. Intent/Sacrifice. Of-good-consciousness. May-we-attain.
All. For-the-singers. For-the-one-who-praises. And. May-they-be. You. Protect. With-blessings. Always. Us. ॥ 10 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, **shine** upon **us these** visible **fortunes** <note>original: "saubhagā"</note>—that is, beautiful riches. Illumine them, or rather, grant them. **And also**, may we **attain** a **wise understanding** <note>original: "sucetasam"</note> or a sacrificial act <note>original: "kratum"</note>—that is, may we be the performers of sacrifices. <note>The text continues on the next page.</note>

<header>॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Book 5. Chapter 2. Section 5.]</header>

...or we might attain a **wise** <note>original: "sucetasaṃ"</note> son, one endowed with excellent knowledge and intelligence. Let us **enjoy** <note>original: "vane ma"</note> this together. Regarding the verb "to enjoy" <note>original: "vanateḥ"</note>, when used in the sense of shared enjoyment, the form changes to include the suffix. May **all** <note>original: "viśvā"</note>—that is, all forms of wealth—be granted to the **chanters** <note>original: "stotṛbhya"</note> and the **singers** <note>original: "gṛṇate"</note> who praise the gods. You, along with all your followers, **protect** <note>original: "pāta"</note> **us** <note>original: "naḥ"</note> always and at all times with your **blessings** <note>original: "svastibhiḥ"</note> and security.

The fourth hymn, beginning with "To your bright..." <note>original: "pra vaḥ śukrāya"</note>, consists of ten verses. It was revealed to the seer **Vasishtha** <term>Vasishtha: one of the most celebrated Vedic sages, progenitor of the Vasishtha clan</term>. The meter is **Trishtubh** <term>Trishtubh: a Vedic meter consisting of four lines of eleven syllables each</term> and the deity is **Agni**. This is specified in the ancient index <note>original: "anukrāntaṃ"</note>. Regarding its ritual use: it is cited as the second hymn among the thirteen hymns of the **Early Morning Litany** <note>original: "prātaranuvāka"</note> and the **Ashvina-shastra** <note>original: "āśvina-śastrayoḥ"</note> <note>See: Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.13</note>. Furthermore, in the animal sacrifice dedicated to Agni, this verse starting with "To your bright..." is used as the **offering prayer** <term>yājyā: the specific verse recited as the offering is poured into the fire</term> for the **omentum** <term>vapā: a part of the sacrificial animal offered to the gods</term>. This is also indicated in the ritual texts: "Bring forward to the bright radiance, just as through the offerings of the wise man..." <note>See: Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 3.7</note>.

-> ॥ Therein, the first verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

Bring forward the **oblation** <note>original: "havyaṃ"</note> and the **prayer** <note>original: "matiṃ"</note>, well-purified, for your **bright** radiant **Agni**, he who with **wisdom** moves between all **divine** and **human** generations. ॥ 1 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
Forward. Your. For-the-bright. For-the-radiant. Bring-forward. Oblation. Prayer. And. For-Agni. Well-purified.
Who. Divine. Human. Generations. Within. All. With-wisdom. Moves. ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O you who carry the oblations! You should **bring forward** <note>original: "prabharadhvaṃ"</note> the **well-purified** <note>original: "supūtaṃ"</note>—that is, the very clean—**oblation** <note>original: "havyaṃ"</note> and **prayer** <note>original: "matiṃ"</note> or praise for **Agni**, who is **bright** <note>original: "śukrāya"</note> and **radiant** <note>original: "bhānave"</note>. Which Agni is this? He **who** <note>original: "yaḥ"</note> moves between all **divine** <note>original: "daivyāni"</note> and **human** <note>original: "mānuṣāṇi"</note> **generations** <note>original: "janūṃṣi"</note> or created beings. He **moves** <note>original: "jigāti"</note> through the path of **wisdom** <note>original: "vidmanā"</note>. The meaning is that he exists to carry the oblations between the gods and the humans.

-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

May that wise Agni be **vigorous** <note>original: "taruṇaḥ"</note>, he who as the **youngest** was born from his **mother**. Being pure, he **consumes** the forests; and devouring them, he suddenly **eats** even much food. ॥ 2 ॥

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada-patha):**
He. Wise. Agni. Vigorous. Indeed. Let-him-be. From-whom. Youngest. Was-born. Mother.
Together. Who. Forests. Joins/Consumes. Pure. Devouring. Much. Indeed. Foods. Completely. Indeed. Eats. Suddenly. ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

He is **wise** <note>original: "gṛtsaḥ"</note>, meaning highly intelligent. As the ancient etymologist Yaska says: "Gritsa is a name for the wise." **Agni** is **vigorous** <note>original: "taruṇaḥ"</note>, meaning he is a rescuer or a youth. At that time, when he, as the **youngest** <term>yaviṣṭha: a frequent title for Agni because he is "born anew" every time the sacrificial fire is lit</term>, was born from his **mother**, the fire-stick...

<vocab>
**Śukra**: bright or pure.
**Bhānu**: light, radiance, or the sun-like glow of fire.
**Vasiṣṭha**: 'The Best' or 'Most Wealthy', the name of a prominent Vedic Rishi.
**Āgneya**: relating to or dedicated to Agni, the god of fire.
**Traiṣṭubha**: a poetic meter of 44 syllables.
**Vapā**: the fatty membrane (omentum) of a sacrificial animal.
**Yājyā**: a consecrating verse used at the moment of sacrifice.
**Gṛtsa**: clever, wise, or adroit.
**Taruṇa**: young, fresh, or one who helps across (a savior).
**Yaviṣṭha**: the youngest; Agni is called this because he is freshly generated by friction.
</vocab>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the fourth hymn (Sukta) of the seventh book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda. The previous page ended with a discussion on the ritual placement of this hymn in the Morning Litany and the characteristics of Agni as he consumes the forest.</meta>

<page-num>921</page-num>
<header>Mandala 7. Sukta 4. Verse 4.] || The Fifth Book || 921</header>

...was born. That Agni, who has **bright teeth** <note>original: "śucidant"</note>—meaning shining or burning teeth—**unites with** <note>original: "saṃyuvate"</note> the various forests, joining them to himself as fuel. Furthermore, he **entirely consumes** <note>original: "samatti"</note> **even many** <note>original: "bhūri cit"</note> foods—that is, his own consumable fuels—**immediately** <note>original: "sadya it"</note> or right away.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

**अ॒स्य दे॒वस्य॑ सं॒सदनी॑के॒ यं मर्ता॑सः श्ये॒तं जगृ॒भ्रे ।**
**नि यो गृ॒भं पौ॑रुषे॒यीमु॒वोच॑ दुरो॒कम॑ग्निरा॒यवे॑ शुशोच ॥ ३ ॥**

**Word-for-word analysis:**
अ॒स्य (Of this) । दे॒वस्य॑ (of the god) । स॒म्ऽसद॑ि (in the assembly) । अनी॑के (in the presence/face) । यम् (whom) । मर्ता॑सः (mortals) । श्ये॒तम् (white/shining) । जगृ॒भ्रे (have grasped) ।
नि (down/certainly) । यः (who) । गृ॒भम् (grasp/seizure) । पौ॑रुषे॒यीम् (human-made) । उ॒वोच॑ (accepted/served) । दुः॒ऽओक॑म् (difficult to approach) । अ॒ग्निः (Agni) । आ॒यवे॑ (for man) । शु॒शोच॑ (shone) ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

In the **presence** <note>original: "anīke"</note> or face of this divine Agni, and in the **assembly** <note>original: "saṃsadi"</note> where he is stationed, the **mortals** <note>original: "martāsaḥ"</note>—meaning human beings—have grasped the **white** <note>original: "śyetaṃ"</note> or bright and pure Agni. This Agni has **accepted** <note>original: "nyuvoca"</note> the **human grasp** <note>original: "pauruṣeyīṃ gṛbhaṃ"</note>—the act of being seized or served by men. <gloss>The root "uc" or "vac" is used here in the sense of serving or frequenting.</gloss> This means he dwells among them. That Agni **shone** <note>original: "śuśoca"</note>—meaning he glows brightly—for the sake of **man** <note>original: "āyave"</note>. <note>The word "āyave" refers to man, as "āyava" is listed among the synonyms for "human" in ancient lexicons.</note> He shines in such a way that he is **difficult to approach** <note>original: "durokam"</note> or hard to withstand for his enemies.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-

**अ॒यं क॒विरक॑विषु प्रचे॑ता॒ मर्ते॑ष्व॒ग्निर॒मृतो॑ नि धा॑यि ।**
**स मा नो॒ अर्व॑ग् जुहुरः सहस्वः॒ सदा॑ ते सु॒मन॑सः स्याम ॥ ४ ॥**

**Word-for-word analysis:**
अ॒यम् (This) । क॒विः (wise/seer) । अ॒क॑वि॒ऽषु (among the unwise) । प्र॒ऽचे॑ताः (conscious/illuminator) । मर्तेषु (among mortals) । अ॒ग्निः (Agni) । अ॒मृतः॑ (immortal) । नि (down) । धा॒यि (placed) ।
सः (that one) । मा (not) । नः॒ (us) । अर्व॑क् (here/downwards) । जु॒हु॒रः॒ (harm/abandon) । स॒ह॒स्वः॒ (O powerful one) । सदा॑ (always) । ते (your) । सु॒ऽम॑नसः (well-disposed) । स्या॒म (may we be) ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

This Agni is a **seer** <term>Kavi: one with "krāntadṛk" or far-reaching vision who sees beyond the ordinary</term>, the **illuminator** <note>original: "pracetāḥ"</note> who reveals all things, and is **immortal** <note>original: "amṛtaḥ"</note>—free from the nature of death. He has been **placed** <note>original: "nidhāyi"</note> or established among **mortals** <note>original: "marteṣu"</note> who are subject to death and who lack that far-reaching vision <note>original: "akaviṣu"</note>. Now follows a direct praise: O **mighty** <note>original: "sahasvo"</note> and powerful Agni, in whose presence **we** <note>original: "vayam"</note> may **always** be **well-disposed** <note>original: "sumanasaḥ"</note> or of good intent; you, being such a god, do **not harm** <note>original: "mā juhuraḥ"</note> or abandon **us** in **this world** <note>original: "arvāk"</note>.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**आ यो योनिं॑ देव॒कृतं॑ स॒साद् ऋ॒त्वा ह्य॒ग्निर॒मृताँ॑ अतारीत् ।**
**तमोष॑दीषु वनि॒नश्च॒ गर्भे॑ भूमि॑श्च वि॒श्वधा॑यसं बिभर्ति ॥ ५ ॥**

<vocab>
अग्नि (Agni) - The Vedic fire deity, messenger between gods and humans.
मर्तासः (Martas) - Mortals; humans who are subject to death.
कवि (Kavi) - A wise seer; in the Vedas, this refers to someone with divine poetic insight.
अमृत (Amrita) - Immortal; the deathless state of the gods.
सहस्वः (Sahasvah) - Mighty; an epithet for Agni emphasizing his overwhelming strength.
</vocab>

<summary>This page contains the commentary on Rig Veda 7.4.3-4, describing Agni as an immortal seer established among mortals and a prayer for his protection. It highlights Agni's role as a "Kavi" (wise seer) who accepts the service of humans and shines for their benefit.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the fourth hymn (Sukta) of the seventh book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda. It covers the final verses of the hymn, focusing on Agni’s role as the preserver of the gods, a source of wealth, and the importance of true lineage.</meta>

<page-num>922</page-num>
<header>|| Rig Veda || [Book 5. Chapter 2. Group 6.]</header>

## Hymn Text

**He who has sat in the source made by the gods; indeed, Agni has surpassed the immortals by his wisdom. The plants and the trees and the earth carry him, the supporter of all, like an embryo.** ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-for-word analysis:**
आ (Toward/at) । यः (who) । योनिं॑ (source/place) । दे॒वऽकृ॑तं (god-made) । ससा॑द (has sat) । ऋ॒त्वा (by wisdom/intelligence) । हि (indeed) । अ॒ग्निः (Agni) । अ॒मृता॑न् (the immortals) । अ॒तारी॑त् (has crossed/surpassed) ।
तं (him) । ओष॑धीः (plants) । च॒ (and) । व॒निन॑: (trees) । च॒ (and) । गर्भं॑ (embryo) । भूमिः॑ (earth) । च॒ (and) । वि॒श्वऽधा॑यसं (all-supporting) । बिभ॑र्ति (carries) ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

That Agni who **has sat in** <note>original: "āsasāda"</note>—meaning occupies—the **source** <note>original: "yoniṃ"</note> or place **made by the gods** <note>original: "devakṛtaṃ"</note> or arranged by them. Why do the gods arrange a place for Agni? To this, the text says: **Indeed** <note>original: "hi"</note> because Agni **surpassed** <note>original: "atārīt"</note> the **immortal** <note>original: "amṛtān"</note> gods through his **wisdom** <note>original: "kratvā"</note> or intelligence. The **plants** <note>original: "oṣadhayaḥ"</note> and the **trees** <note>original: "vaninaśca"</note> carry him, the **supporter of all** <note>original: "viśvadhāyasaṃ"</note>, while he is an **embryo** <note>original: "garbhaṃ"</note>. The **earth** <note>original: "bhūmiśca"</note> also carries him. <note>Grammatical note: The word "carries" (bibharti) is seen here as being transformed into a plural sense to connect with the many subjects: plants and trees.</note>

-> ॥ This concludes the fifth group in the second chapter of the fifth book ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**For Agni is the lord of much immortality; he is the lord of giving wealth and good hero-strength. O mighty one, may we not sit around you without sons, without form, or without service.** ॥ ६ ॥

**Word-for-word analysis:**
ईशे॑ (Rules/is lord) । हि (for) । अ॒ग्निः (Agni) । अ॒मृत॑स्य (of immortality) । भूरे॑: (of much) । ईशे॑ (rules) । रा॒यः (of wealth) । सु॒ऽवीर्य॑स्य (of good hero-strength) । दा॒तोः (of the giver) ।
मा (not) । त्वा॒ (you) । व॒यम् (we) । सह॑साऽवन् (O mighty one) । अ॒वीरा॑: (without sons/heroes) । मा (not) । अ॒प्सवः॑ (without form/beauty) । परि॑ (around) । स॒दाम॒ (may we sit) । मा (not) । अ॒दुवः॑ (without service) ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Agni **rules** <note>original: "īṣṭe"</note> over **much** <note>original: "bhūreḥ"</note> **immortality** <note>original: "amṛtasya"</note>, which refers here to sacrificial food or water. <note>Grammatical note: The genitive case is used here in the sense of the objective case.</note> He is the lord and the **giver** <note>original: "dātoḥ"</note> of **wealth** <note>original: "rāyaḥ"</note> consisting of **excellent hero-strength** <note>original: "suvīryasya"</note> or power. Now follows a direct praise: **O mighty one** <note>original: "sahasāvan"</note>, O powerful Agni, may we, the clan of Vasistha, **not sit around** <note>original: "mā pariṣadāma"</note> you being **without sons** <note>original: "avīrāḥ"</note>—that is, lacking children and descendants. May we not sit around you **without form** <note>original: "apsavaḥ"</note>, meaning being devoid of beauty or status. As the ancient etymologist Yaska says: <gloss>The word "apsas" is a name for "form" (rūpa).</gloss> Also, may we not sit around you being **without service** <note>original: "aduvaḥ"</note>—meaning lacking in the performance of ritual service.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥ <-

**The wealth of a stranger is indeed to be avoided; let us be the masters of our own eternal wealth. O Agni, an offspring born of another is no offspring; do not lead us away from the path of one who is wise.** ॥ ७ ॥

**Word-for-word analysis:**
परि॑ऽसद्यं (To be avoided/surrounded) । हि (for) । अ॒र॒णस्य॑ (of a stranger/other) । रे॒क्णः॑ (wealth/inheritance) । नित्य॑स्य (of the eternal/own) । रा॒यः (of wealth) । पत॑यः (masters) । स्याम (may we be) ।
न (not) । शेषः॑ (offspring/remainder) । अ॒ग्ने॒ (O Agni) । अ॒न्यऽजा॑तं (born of another) । अ॒स्ति (is) । अ॒चे॒तानस्य (of the ignorant/unwise) । मा (not) । प॒थः (from the path) । वि (away) । दुक्षः (lead/milk) ॥ ७ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **wealth** <note>original: "rekṇaḥ"</note> of a **stranger** <note>original: "araṇasya"</note>—meaning someone else—is **to be avoided** <note>original: "pariṣadyaṃ"</note> or is merely something that surrounds us but isn't truly ours. Therefore, **may we be the masters** <note>original: "patayaḥ syāma"</note> of **eternal** <note>original: "nityasya"</note> **wealth** <note>original: "rāyaḥ"</note>—that which does not have to be given back. Alternatively, the wealth of a stranger is something to be shunned...

<vocab>
<term>Agni</term> : The Vedic deity of fire, seen as the priest of the gods and the mediator between heaven and earth.
<term>Kratu</term> : A complex term meaning intelligence, will, or the sacrificial power/wisdom that guides ritual action.
<term>Amrita</term> : Literally "not-death"; refers to the drink of the gods, immortality, or in a ritual context, the sustaining waters or sacrificial offerings.
<term>Oshadhi</term> : Herbs or plants, frequently described in the Vedas as the "womb" where Agni (as heat or life force) resides.
<term>Sahasavan</term> : "Possessing power"; a frequent title for Agni, referring to his birth from the "force" or "strength" of rubbing fire-sticks together.
<term>Avira</term> : One who lacks "Viras" (heroes/sons); in Vedic society, having sons was essential for continuing the lineage and the ritual fire.
<term>Reknas</term> : Property, inheritance, or wealth, often specifically referring to what is handed down through a family line.
<term>Nitya</term> : Eternal, perpetual, or one's own; here used to distinguish indigenous/family wealth from that of a stranger.
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes Sukta 4 of Mandala 7, where the sage prays to Agni for legitimate offspring and independent wealth. Sayana's commentary clarifies that Agni is the source of both immortality for the gods and material prosperity for humans, emphasizing the avoidance of relying on "strangers" for lineage or riches.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Sayana, Rig Veda, Mandala 7, Vedic ritual, immortality, wealth, lineage, sons, Yaska, Sanskrit commentary</keywords>
