<meta>This page continues the commentary on the fourth hymn (Sukta) of the seventh book (Mandala) of the Rig Veda. It concludes the discussion on the importance of biological lineage versus adoption (verse 8) and Agni's role as a protector (verse 9).</meta>

<page-num>923</page-num>
<header>Mandala 7. Section 1. Hymn 4.] || Fifth Volume || 923</header>

## Commentary (continued from previous page)
...it becomes. Therefore, may we be the masters of eternal, legitimate wealth <note>original: rayiḥ</note> in the form of a biological son. O Agni, a child born of another—one not of one's own blood—is not truly offspring. It is not. May he [Agni] not lead us, who are unseeing and ignorant, toward the paths primarily concerned with producing such [unnatural] sons. "Do not let us be ignorant" <note>The root "dush" here implies a perversion or corruption of the natural order</note>.

The ancient etymologist Yaska explains this as follows: "That which is to be avoided and not approached is the wealth of a stranger <note>original: araṇa</note>. The word 'araṇa' means 'distant' or 'removed.' 'Reknas' is a name for wealth that is left behind. May we be masters of our own eternal wealth. There is no offspring, O Agni, that is born of another. 'Shesha' is a name for offspring, meaning that which 'remains' or continues the line; it belongs to the unthinking or the negligent. Do not lead us onto the paths of the unseeing." <note>Nirukta 3.2</note>.

---

-> ॥ Verse 8 ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
A stranger, even if very kind, who is born of another’s womb, is not to be accepted as a son, nor is he even to be considered so in the mind. For indeed, such a one returns to his own home again. Therefore, let a powerful son, a conqueror of enemies, newly born, come to us. ॥ ८ ॥

**Word-for-word analysis:**
**न॒हि** (Indeed not) । **ग्रभाय॑** (To be grasped/accepted) । **अर॒णः** (A stranger) । **सु॒ऽशेवः॑** (Very kind/bringing happiness) । **अ॒न्यऽउ॑दर्यः** (Born of another's womb) । **मन॑सा** (By the mind) । **मन्त॑वै** (To be thought of) । **ऊँ॒ इति॑** (Indeed) ।
**अध॑** (Then) । **चि॒त्** (Even) । **ओकः॒** (Home/abode) । **पुन॑: (Again)** । **इत्** (Indeed) । **सः** (He) । **ए॒ति॒** (Goes/returns) । **आ** (Toward) । **नः॒** (Us) । **वा॒जी** (Powerful/swift) । **अ॒भि॒ऽषाट्** (Overpowering/conquering) । **ए॒तु॒** (Let him come) । **नव्य॑: (New/freshly born)** ॥ ८ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
The meaning stated in the previous verse is elaborated here. A stranger <note>original: araṇaḥ</note>, meaning one who provides no delight, born of another's womb <note>original: anyodaryaḥ</note>, even if he is very kind <note>original: suśevaḥ</note> or extremely pleasant, is not to be grasped <note>original: grabhāya</note> as a son, nor even considered <note>original: mantavai</note> as such in one's heart. For even then, that child born of another returns only to his own place or original home <note>original: okaḥ</note>. Therefore, let a powerful son <note>original: vājī</note>—one who possesses strength and sustenance—who is a subduer <note>original: abhiṣāṭ</note> of enemies and newly born <note>original: navyaḥ</note> to us, come into our family.

---

-> ॥ Verse 9 ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O Agni, protect us from those who wish us harm; and you, O powerful one, protect us from blame. May pure food reach you, and may desirable wealth in the thousands reach us. ॥ ९ ॥

**Word-for-word analysis:**
**त्वम्** (You) । **अ॒ग्ने॒** (O Agni) । **व॒नु॒ष्य॒तः** (From those who harm) । **नि** (Down/entirely) । **पा॑हि॒** (Protect) । **त्वम्** (You) । **ऊँ॒ इति॑** (Indeed) । **नः॒** (Us) । **स॒ह॒सा॒ऽवन्** (O Powerful One) । **अ॒व॒ऽद्यात्** (From blame/sin) ।
**सं** (Together) । **त्वा॒** (You) । **ध्व॒स्मन्॒ऽवत्** (Pure/faultless) । **अ॒भि** (Toward) । **ए॒तु॒** (Let it go/reach) । **पाथः॑** (Food/oblation) । **सं** (Together) । **र॒यिः** (Wealth) । **स्पृ॒ह॒याय्य॑:** (Desirable) । **सह॒स्री** (In the thousands) ॥ ९ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, protect us from those who wish to harm <note>original: vanuṣyataḥ</note> or destroy us. You alone protect us from blame <note>original: avadyāt</note> or the stain of sin. May the food <note>original: pāthaḥ</note> or sacrificial oblation <note>original: haviḥ</note>, which is pure <note>original: dhvasmanvat</note> and free from defects, reach you properly. Furthermore, let desirable <note>original: spṛhayāyyaḥ</note> wealth <note>original: rayiḥ</note> in the thousands <note>original: sahasrī</note> come to us.

<summary>This page concludes the hymn by emphasizing the Vedic preference for biological sons over adoption, arguing that an adopted son eventually returns to his original lineage. It ends with a prayer to Agni for protection against enemies and for the arrival of great wealth.</summary>

<keywords>Agni, adoption, lineage, biological son, protection, wealth, Yaska, Nirukta, Vedic sacrifice</keywords>

<header>|| Rig Veda || [Book 5. Chapter 2. Section 7.]</header>

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ The Tenth Verse ॥ <-

**O Agni, shine these fortunes upon us; may we obtain a wisdom that is full of good consciousness.**
**May all blessings be for the chanters and for the one who praises; and you, O gods, protect us always with your blessings! ॥ 10 ॥**

**These . upon us . O Agni . fortunes . shine . also . wisdom . good-consciousness . may-we-obtain .**
**All . for-the-chanters . for-the-one-who-praises . and . let-them-be . you . protect . with-blessings . always . us ॥ 10 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
This verse has already been explained <note>Sayana frequently refers back to earlier occurrences of common closing refrains, as the second half of this verse "May all blessings..." is a standard closing for the hymns of the Vasishtha family</note>.

-> ॥ Thus ends the sixth section of the second chapter of the fifth volume ॥ <-

The fifth hymn, beginning with "To the powerful Agni," consists of nine verses. It was seen <note>The term 'arsham' suggests the sage did not 'compose' the hymn but 'saw' it through divine inspiration</note> by the sage Vasishtha, is set in the Trishtubh meter <note>A Vedic meter consisting of four lines of eleven syllables each</note>, and is dedicated to Agni in his form as Vaishvanara <note>term: Vaishvanara; literally 'belonging to all men' or 'the universal fire'</note>. The Index of Hymns states: "The nine verses beginning with 'To Agni' are dedicated to Vaishvanara." The ritual application is determined by the specific markers in the text.

-> ॥ There, the first verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Bring forward your song for the powerful Agni, the messenger of heaven and earth,**
**Vaishvanara, who, in the lap of all the immortals, has grown through the wakeful ones. ॥ 1 ॥**

**Forward . for-Agni . for-the-powerful . bring-forth . the-song . of-heaven . for-the-messenger . of-earth .**
**Who . of-all . of-the-immortals . in-the-lap . the-universal-fire . has-grown . with-the-wakeful-ones ॥ 1 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O chanters, bring forth your song—your praise—to the powerful, highly-developed Agni, the one known as Vaishvanara, who is the messenger <note>original: arataye; literally 'one who moves' or 'reaches' between two points</note> going between heaven (the mid-air) and the earth. He is Vaishvanara, the fire who benefits all human beings <note>original: viśva-nara-hita</note>. He is the one who, in the lap—meaning the presence or the place of the sacrifice—of all the immortal gods, has grown. He grows through the songs of praise and the oblations offered by the "wakeful ones," meaning the gods who are ever-conscious and alert.

-> ॥ Now the second verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**Agni was placed as the one sought in heaven and on earth; the leader of the rivers, the bull among the standing waters.**
**He, Vaishvanara, increases in excellence and shines upon the human tribes. ॥ 2 ॥**

**Sought . in-heaven . placed . Agni . on-earth . leader . of-the-rivers . bull . of-the-standing-waters .**
**He . human . toward . tribes . shines-forth . the-universal-fire . increasing . with-excellence ॥ 2 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
He is the leader of the rivers <note>original: sindhūnām</note> and the "bull" or bestower of rain for the "standing waters." According to the words of the ancient etymologist Yaska: "The standing waters <note>original: sthiyā</note> are called so because they stay or remain in place" <note>Nirukta 6.17</note>. He is the bull (the rainer) who is "sought"—meaning worshipped or joined with brilliance.

<header>Mandala 7, Chapter 1, Hymn 5 || Fifth Volume || 925</header>

## Hymn Text

<note>Conclusion of the commentary for Rig Veda 7.5.2</note>
That fire which was placed in the heavens, in the mid-air, and on the earth—that <term>Vaishvanara</term><note>The universal fire, or fire belonging to all men</note>, who is beneficial to all people, increasing through the most excellent oblation or through his own brilliance, shines upon the human tribes and all human subjects.

---

->**॥ The Third Verse ॥**<-

**Through fear of you, the dark-hued tribes fled, scattered and abandoning their possessions, O Vaishvanara, when you, Agni, shining for the sake of King Puru, didst burn and shatter their forts. ॥ 3 ॥**

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
**Through fear | of you | the tribes | fled | the dark-hued | scattered | abandoning | possessions |**
**O Vaishvanara | for Puru | shining | the forts | when | O Agni | shattering | you didst shine ॥ 3 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Vaishvanara**, Agni who is the leader of all men, through **fear** of **you**, the **dark-hued** <note>original: "asiknīḥ"; literally 'the black ones,' referring here to the dark-skinned indigenous enemies of the Vedic people or metaphorically to the nights</note> **tribes** of the enemies, becoming **scattered** <note>original: "asamanāḥ"; not together, disorganized</note> and **abandoning** their **possessions** and wealth, they **fled**. When did this happen? **When** you, **shining** with great light **for Puru** <note>A famous king and ancestor of the Puru tribe</note>, didst **shatter** the **forts** of his enemies and **shined** with brilliance. This is supported by another Vedic passage: 
> **"O King, you provided wide space and light for Puru." (Rig Veda 1.63.7)** <note>original: "aṃho rājanvarivaḥ pūrave kaḥ"</note>

---

## Hymn Text

->**॥ The Fourth Verse ॥**<-

**The Earth and also the Heavens followed your threefold law, O Agni Vaishvanara; you have extended through the two worlds with your brilliance, shining with unwearied light. ॥ 4 ॥**

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
**Your | threefold | Earth | and | Heaven | O Vaishvanara | law | O Agni | followed |**
**You | with brilliance | the two worlds | have extended | with unwearied | light | shining ॥ 4 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Vaishvanara**, leader of all men. Regarding this, the ancient etymologist **Yaska** says: 
> **"Why is he called Vaishvanara? Because he leads all men (vishwa-nara), or because all men lead/carry him."** <note>A citation from the Nirukta, the ancient Sanskrit treatise on etymology</note>

**Your law**, meaning the sacrificial work that is pleasing to you, is **followed** by the **threefold** world—the mid-air, the earth, and also the heavens. This means the people dwelling in these three worlds perform sacred rites for your sake. Furthermore, **you**, **shining** with **unwearied light** <note>original: "ajasreṇa śociṣā"; light that is never extinguished</note> and with your own **brilliance**, **have extended** through and pervaded the **two worlds**, namely Heaven and Earth.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**Toward you, O Agni, the neighing tawny horses and the resounding, ghee-bearing voices of praise proceed; you are the lord of the people, the charioteer of riches, the universal leader <term>Vaishvanara</term><note>An epithet of Agni meaning "belonging to all men"</note>, the herald of the dawns and the days. ॥ 5 ॥**

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
**Toward you | O Agni | the tawny horses | neighing / longing | voices of praise | proceed | resounding | bearing ghee / clarity |**
**The lord | of the people | the charioteer | of riches | the universal leader | of the dawns | the herald | of the days ॥ 5 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, you are the **lord** or master of the **people** <note>original: "kṛṣṭīnām"; Sayana notes that according to the Nighantu, 'kṣitayaḥ' and 'kṛṣṭayaḥ' are synonyms for human beings</note> and the **leader** of **riches** and wealth. You are the **great herald** or indicator of the **dawns** and the **days**, and you are **Vaishvanara**, the one who is beneficial to all humanity. To you, the **tawny horses** <note>original: "haritaḥ"; the horses of the sun or fire</note>, **longing** for you, **proceed** or serve you. Likewise, the **voices** of praise from men, which are **resounding**—meaning they wash away or **shake off sin**—and **bearing ghee**—meaning they are accompanied by **sacrificial offerings**—also **proceed** toward you.

-> ॥ Thus ends the seventh section (Varga) of the second hymn in the fifth book ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**In you, O Agni, the <term>Vasus</term><note>A class of elemental deities associated with light and nature</note> placed divine power, for they favored your wisdom, O honorer of friends. You, O Agni, drove the <term>Dasyus</term><note>Those who do not perform Vedic rituals; often interpreted as enemies of the Vedic people</note> from their homes, creating wide light for the <term>Arya</term><note>The noble ones who follow the Vedic path</note>. ॥ 6 ॥**

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
**In you | divine power | the Vasus | placed | wisdom / ritual | for | your | O honorer of friends | they favored |**
**You | the Dasyus | from the home | O Agni | drove out | wide | light | generating | for the Arya ॥ 6 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, **honorer of friends**, the **Vasus**—the indwelling gods—**placed** or established **divine power** and strength **in you**. They indeed **favored** or took pleasure in your **wisdom**, which refers to the **ritual acts** that please you. Furthermore, O Agni, while **generating wide light** or great radiance for the **Arya**—the person who performs the sacred rituals—you **drove out** the **Dasyus**, those who are devoid of ritual action, from their **homes** or dwelling places.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Seventh Verse ॥ <-

**Being born in the highest heaven, you, like the wind, immediately protect the path. You, O <term>Jatavedas</term><note>An epithet of Agni meaning "knower of all births" or "knower of all beings"</note>, creating the worlds, roared aloud, bestowing gifts for the sake of offspring. ॥ 7 ॥**

**Word-by-Word Breakdown:**
**He | being born | in the highest | heaven | the wind | like | the path | around | you protect | immediately |**
**You | the worlds | creating | aloud | roared | for offspring | O Jatavedas | bestowing gifts ॥ 7 ॥**

---

<vocab>
Agni: The Vedic deity of fire, messenger between gods and men.
Vaishvanara: The aspect of Agni that resides in all humans; "The Universal Fire."
Krishthinam: A term for human tribes or subjects.
Dasyu: Those who do not observe the Vedic law; often used for enemies or the lawless.
Arya: Those who follow the Vedic rites and culture.
Jatavedas: A common name for Agni, signifying his all-knowing nature regarding created beings.
Mitramahas: One who honors or treats friends with great respect; here, a title for Agni.
</vocab>

<header>M. 7. A. 1. S. 5. ] || The Fifth Octave || 927</header>

O <term>Vaishvanara</term><note>An epithet of Agni meaning "Belonging to All Men"</note>, you are that famous one appearing in the highest, most distant sky, manifesting in the form of the sun. Just as the wind <note>Vayu</note> drinks the first <term>Soma</term> at non-sacrifices, you immediately drink the Soma-juice. Or rather, like the wind, you drink up the waters; that is to say, you dry them. Furthermore, O <term>Jatavedas</term><note>Agni as "Knower of Created Beings" or "He from whom wealth is born"</note>, you create the worlds or the waters—for "bhuvana" is listed among the names for water—and being kind to the sacrificer who is to be protected like an offspring, and granting his desires, you roar or thunder through your form as lightning.

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ The Eighth Verse ॥<-

**O Agni, send us that shining nourishment, O Vaishvanara, O Jatavedas; through which you nourish wealth, O you who are chosen by all, and grant wide fame to the mortal who gives offerings. ॥ 8 ॥**

> **That | O Agni | to us | nourishment | toward | impel | O Vaishvanara | shining | O Jatavedas | by which | wealth | you nourish | O you chosen by all | wide | fame | to the giver | to the mortal ॥ 8 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Jatavedas**—you of innate wisdom—O **Vaishvanara**—Agni who is beneficial to all men—impel or send to us that desired **nourishment** <note>original: "iṣam"</note> or rain which is **shining** <note>original: "dyumatīm"</note> or full of light. Indeed, the three worlds shine because of rain. Alternatively, send that shining nourishment in the form of food. Regarding this, it is heard in the scriptures: **"Therefore, he who has the most food here, indeed shines most in the world."** <note>original: "tasmād yasyaiveha bhūyiṣṭham annam bhavati sa eva bhūyiṣṭhaṃ loke virājati"</note>. Or again, impel that desired, brilliant, and radiant light. With this nourishment, you protect or nourish **wealth** <note>original: "rādhaḥ"</note>. Moreover, O **Chosen by All** <note>original: "viśvavāra"</note>—O Agni who is desired by everyone—you nourish or bestow **wide** or extensive **fame** <note>original: "śravaḥ"</note> upon the **mortal** who is a **giver**—the sacrificer.

---

## Hymn Text

->॥ The Ninth Verse ॥<-

**O Agni, for our wealthy patrons, join to us that wealth consisting of many foods and that strength which is worthy of being heard; O Vaishvanara, grant us great protection, O Agni, being in harmony with the Rudras and the Vasus. ॥ 9 ॥**

> **That | our | O Agni | for the wealthy patrons | possessing many foods | wealth | down | strength | worthy of hearing | join | O Vaishvanara | great | to us | protection | grant | with the Rudras | O Agni | with the Vasus | being in harmony ॥ 9 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, for the **wealthy patrons**—meaning those who possess the sacrificial offerings—bestow upon **us** that famous **wealth** <note>original: "rayim"</note> which is **possessing many foods** <note>original: "purukṣum"</note> or which brings much fame, and also join to us **strength** <note>original: "vāja"</note> which is **worthy of hearing** <note>original: "śrutyam"</note>. Entirely...

---

The hymn beginning with **"Forth to the Sovereign"** <note>original: "pra samrāja"</note> consists of seven verses and is the sixth hymn seen by the seer <term>Vasishtha</term>. The ritual index <note>Anukramani</note> states: **"The seven verses to the Sovereign are addressed to Vaishvanara."** Because of this statement, <term>Agni Vaishvanara</term> is the deity of this hymn. Its ritual application is determined by the inherent meaning of the verses.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ First Verse ॥ <-

**Forth I praise the renown of the Sovereign, the Divine Power, the Hero of the tribes, who is to be celebrated; like the deeds of the mighty Indra, I, praising him, speak of the ancient acts of the powerful one who breaks the strongholds. ॥ 1 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Padapatha):**
**Forth | of the Sovereign | of the Divine Power (Asura) | renown | of the Hero | of the tribes | who is to be celebrated | like Indra | forth | of the mighty | deeds | I praise | the powerful | praising | I speak ॥ 1 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

I praise the **powerful one** <note>original: "dādham"</note>, the breaker of enemy strongholds. While offering praise, I speak of the **renown** <note>the hymns of glory</note> and the **deeds** <note>the heroic actions</note> of that **Vaishvanara**, who is the **Sovereign** <note>the lord of the entire world</note>, the **Divine Power** <note>the strong one; original: "asurasya"</note>, and the **Hero** <note>the brave one; "pums" refers to virility or heroism</note>. Regarding this, the ancient etymologist <term>Yaska</term> says: "A hero (pumān) is one who possesses a great mind or one who exerts power." He is the one who is **to be celebrated** <note>worthy of praise</note> by the **tribes** <note>the people</note>, and his power is **like that of the mighty Indra**. I proclaim these things.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Second Verse ॥ <-

**The gods impel the Sage, the Banner of the world, the Supporter, the Radiance of the mountain, the Bliss, the Sovereignty of Heaven and Earth; with my songs, I worship the ancient, great laws of Agni, the destroyer of cities. ॥ 2 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Padapatha):**
**The Sage | the Banner | the Supporter | the Radiance | of the mountain | they impel | Bliss | Sovereignty | of the two worlds | of the destroyer of cities | with songs | toward | I worship | of Agni | the laws | ancient | great ॥ 2 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The gods **impel** <note>they please or urge forward</note> Agni Vaishvanara, who is the **Sage** <note>the wise one</note>, the **Banner** <note>the one who makes all things known</note>, the **Supporter** <note>one who sustains the singer or the mountain</note>, and the **Radiance** <note>the light-giver</note>. He is **Bliss** <note>the bringer of happiness</note> and holds **Sovereignty** over the **two worlds** <note>Heaven and Earth; original: "rodasyoh"</note>. And I, with my **songs**, **worship** <note>serve or attend to</note> the **ancient** and **great laws** <note>the divine actions or duties</note> of **Agni**, the **destroyer of cities** <note>original: "purandara," an epithet meaning he who breaks through fortifications</note>.

-> ॥ Third Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**He drove away those without ritual, the talkative ones of corrupt speech, the <term>Panis</term><note>original: "paṇīn"; a group often described as stingy, faithless traders or hoarders who do not offer sacrifices.</note> who lack faith, who do not prosper, and who do not sacrifice. Agni, being the foremost, drove those <term>Dasyus</term><note>original: "dasyūn"; a term for enemies of the Vedic order or those who do not follow the sacred rites.</note> far away and made the non-sacrificers the lowest of all. ॥ 3 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Padapatha):**
**Down | those without ritual | the talkative | of corrupt speech | the Panis | the faithless | the non-prospering | the non-sacrificing | far, far | those | the Dasyus | Agni | drove away | the foremost | made | the lowest | the non-sacrificers ॥ 3 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Agni drove far away those **Dasyus**—those who waste their time in vain—who are **without ritual** (lacking the capacity for sacrifice), **talkative** (mere babblers), **of corrupt speech** (those whose speech is injurious), the **Panis** (known as usurers or stingy ones), **faithless** (lacking belief in sacrifices and other rites), **non-prospering** (those who do not increase Agni’s strength through their praises), and **non-sacrificing** (bereft of the sacred fire-ritual). To explain further: Agni, being **foremost** (the chief), made the **non-sacrificers** (those who do not perform the Yajna) **the lowest** (the most degraded).

---

-> ॥ Fourth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**He, the supreme leader, who through his powers made the folk who were rejoicing in the backward-turning darkness move forward; I praise that Agni, the lord of wealth, who remains unbent and subdues those who assail him. ॥ 4 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Padapatha):**
**Who | in the backward-turning | darkness | rejoicing | forward-moving | made | the supreme leader | by his powers | Him | the Sovereign | of wealth | Agni | I praise | the unbent | subduing | the assailants ॥ 4 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Agni, the **supreme leader** (the best of guides), made the subjects who were submerged in **backward-turning darkness** (unilluminated gloom), but were nonetheless **rejoicing** (praising him), move **forward** (on the straight or righteous path) by means of the **powers** (the wisdom or skills) he granted them. Alternatively: the supreme leader Agni, through his wisdom, made the **Dawns**—which were delighting in the backward darkness of night—move forward (into the day). I **praise** that Agni, who is the master of **wealth**, who is **unbent** (never bowing to enemies), and who **subdues** those who are **assailants** (those desiring battle).

---

-> ॥ Fifth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**He who brought down the strongholds with his weapons, he who made the Dawns have a noble master; that Great Agni, having subdued the people of <term>Nahusha</term><note>A specific tribe or lineage of men mentioned frequently in the Rigveda.</note>, made them bringers of tribute through his might. ॥ 5 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Padapatha):**
**Who | the strongholds | brought down | with weapons | Who | having a noble master | the Dawns | made | He | having subdued | of Nahusha | the Great | Agni | the tribes | made | bringers of tribute | by his might ॥ 5 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana) - Conclusion of Verse 5
This Agni, the divine one, diminished the <term>Asuric</term><note>original: "āsurīḥ"; referring to the powers of the Asuras, often depicted as rivals to the gods in Vedic literature.</note> powers that were fortified in bodies, using his weapons or missiles. He also created the Dawns, whose husband is the Sun. That great Agni, having restrained the people by his strength, made the subjects of King <term>Nahusha</term><note>original: "nahuṣo"; a legendary king; his "subjects" here likely refer to all of humanity or specific neighboring tribes.</note> into tribute-bearers and givers of taxes.

---

-> ॥ The Sixth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**In whose shelter all people have stood with their sacred acts, seeking his good favor. <term>Vaishvanara</term><note>original: "vaiśvānaraḥ"; Agni as the 'Common to all Men' or the Universal Fire.</note> Agni has sat in the excellent lap of the parents, the two worlds of Heaven and Earth. ॥ 6 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada Patha):**
**Whose | in shelter | near | all | people | by sacred acts | have stood | good favor | seeking | Vaishvanara | the excellent | [unto] | the two worlds | [unto] | Agni | has sat | of the parents | in the lap ॥ 6 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
All people have stood near for the sake of <term>sharma</term><note>original: "śarman"; meaning bliss, protection, or happiness.</note>, seeking the good favor of this <term>Vaishvanara</term>, either through their sacred acts or their sacrificial offerings. That same <term>Vaishvanara</term>—who is Agni as the Sun, the benefactor of all men—reached the excellent <term>upasttha</term><note>original: "upastham"; literally 'lap', referring here to the middle space or atmosphere.</note> of the two parents, namely Heaven and Earth. That is to say, he arrived there.

---

-> ॥ The Seventh Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
**The shining God has taken the treasures of the depths; <term>Vaishvanara</term> [has taken them] at the rising of the sun. From the lower ocean and from the upper, Agni has taken from heaven and from earth. ॥ 7 ॥**

**Word-by-word analysis (Pada Patha):**
**[Unto] | the God | has taken | of the depths | treasures | Vaishvanara | in the rising | of the Sun | [unto] | from the ocean | the lower | [unto] | from the further | [unto] | Agni | has taken | from heaven | [unto] | from the earth ॥ 7 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
<term>Vaishvanara</term>, the shining God Agni, takes those things belonging to the depths—that is, the atmospheric regions. <note>The word for depth/foundation is "budhna".</note> The <term>Nirukta</term><note>The ancient Vedic treatise on etymology by Yaska.</note> states: "The atmosphere is called the foundation (<term>budhna</term>) because the waters are bound or held within it." <note>original: "Nirukta 10.44"</note>. He takes the "treasures" (<term>vasuni</term>), which here refer to the "coverings" of darkness. <note>Sayana derives "vasu" from the root "vas", meaning 'to cover'.</note>

This occurs at the rising of the sun. He takes the darkness from the "lower ocean," which refers to the earth <note>The atmosphere is called "samudra" or ocean in Vedic lists of synonyms.</note>. He also takes the darkness from the "further ocean," meaning the heavens. The text demonstrates this by saying: Agni took the darkness of heaven and he took the darkness of the earth.

-> ॥ Thus ends the ninth group in the second chapter of the fifth book ॥ <-

<vocab>
- Vaishvanara (Vaiśvānara): The Universal Fire; Agni in his cosmic form as the sun or the digestive fire.
- Sharma (śarman): Peace, protection, or the bliss resulting from divine shelter.
- Upastha (upastha): Literally 'lap' or 'womb'; used metaphorically for the atmosphere between Heaven and Earth.
- Budhnya (budhnya): Related to the foundation or depth; interpreted by commentators as the atmosphere.
- Samudra (samudra): Usually 'ocean', but in the Veda, it frequently refers to the 'ocean' of the sky or the atmospheric waters.
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes Sukta 59, praising Agni Vaishvanara as the sun who occupies the atmosphere between Heaven and Earth and dispels darkness from both realms. It highlights Agni's role as a protector to whom all people bring offerings and tribute.</summary>
<keywords>Agni Vaishvanara, Heaven and Earth, Nahusha, Sun, atmospheric treasures, darkness, Yaska Nirukta, Vedic sacrifice</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Rig Veda commentary by Sayana. The previous page concluded Sukta 59 of the 1st Anuvaka. We now begin the 7th Sukta of the 1st Anuvaka of the 7th Mandala. The focus remains on Agni, the fire deity, now through the eyes of the seer Vasishtha.</meta>

Mandala 7. Anuvaka 1. Sukta 7.] ॥ Fifth Ashtaka ॥ 931

The seventh hymn, beginning with "To you, the divine" (<note>original: "pra vo devam"</note>), consists of seven verses, is authored by the seer <term>Vasishtha</term><note>one of the most revered Vedic sages</note>, is composed in the <term>Trishtubh</term><note>a meter consisting of four lines of eleven syllables each</note> metre, and is dedicated to <term>Agni</term>. This is stated in the <term>Anukramani</term><note>the ancient index of the Rig Veda</note>. Its ritual use is prescribed for the "Morning Recitation" (<note>original: "prātar-anuvāka"</note>) and the "Ashvina-shastra" ritual, as mentioned in the section covering thirteen hymns.

->॥ Here is the first verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

**I urge forward for you the divine Agni, the powerful one, like a swift horse, with salutations. Be our messenger of the sacrifice, knowing it; he is found among the gods by himself, moving swiftly. ॥ 1 ॥**

---

**I urge | for you | the divine | indeed | the powerful | Agni | a horse | like | swift | I send | with salutations |**
**Be | our | messenger | of the sacrifice | knowing | by himself | among the gods | he is found | moving swiftly ॥ 1 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, I **urge forward** (<note>original: "prahiṣe"</note>) **you**, the **divine** one endowed with qualities like radiance, the **powerful** one who overpowers demons or possesses great strength. You are the leader of the sacrifice, like a **horse**—**like** a **swift** and strong horse—I urge you with **salutations**, which are either hymns of praise or sacrificial offerings. O Agni, I indeed send you forward. Furthermore, O Agni, **knowing** the ritual, **be** **our** **messenger** of the **sacrifice**. Now follows praise in the third person: **By himself**, of his own accord, he **is found** **among the gods**, **moving swiftly** (<note>original: "mitadruḥ"</note>) like the fire that consumes trees. He is well-known.

---

->॥ Now the second verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

**Come, O Agni, along your own paths, delightful one, enjoying friendship with the gods. Making the ridge of the earth resound with your power, consuming all forests with your jaws as you desire them. ॥ 2 ॥**

---

**Come | [near] | Agni | paths | following | your own | delightful | of the gods | friendship | enjoying |**
**[on] the ridge | with power | making resound | of the earth | with jaws | all | desiring to burn | forests ॥ 2 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, you are the **delightful** one who gladdens others, or the one worthy of praise. **Enjoying** the **friendship** of **the gods**—meaning an alliance with the gods—**making** the **ridge** (<note>original: "sānu"</note>), the high places of the **earth** such as grass and shrubs, **resound** (<note>original: "nadayan"</note>) or crackle with your **powers** which dry and burn. Indeed, that which is being burnt makes a sound. With your **jaws**, meaning your flames, **desiring to burn** and consuming **all** the **forests**, **come** following **your own** **paths**. The word **come** (<note>original: "āyāhi"</note>) is repeated in the analysis to show respect and urgency.

---

->॥ Now the third verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

**The sacrifice is directed eastward; the sacrificial grass is well-placed; Agni, being praised like a Hotar priest, is pleased. Being invoked into the two mother-worlds who possess all wealth, O youngest one, you were born most blissful. ॥ 3 ॥**

<vocab>
- Agni: The fire deity and the divine priest of the gods.
- Vasishtha: The Rishi or seer of this specific hymn.
- Trishtubh: A standard Vedic metre of 44 syllables.
- Sacrifice (<note>original: "adhvara"</note>): A religious ritual or offering.
- Messenger (<note>original: "duta"</note>): Agni's role in carrying offerings from humans to gods.
- Friendship (<note>original: "sakhya"</note>): The bond or alliance between the worshiper, Agni, and the gods.
- Sacrificial grass (<note>original: "barhis"</note>): The sacred grass (Kusha) spread on the altar for gods to sit upon.
- Hotar: The specific priest responsible for reciting the Rig Vedic hymns.
- Youngest (<note>original: "yavishtha"</note>): A common title for Agni, as he is "reborn" every time a new fire is lit.
</vocab>

<summary>This page introduces the 7th Sukta of Mandala 7, where the seer Vasishtha invokes Agni as a powerful, horse-like messenger who travels between the human sacrifice and the divine realm, consuming forests with his flame-jaws.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Vasishtha, Trishtubh, messenger, sacrifice, divine paths, Vedic ritual, fire deity</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the translation of Rig Veda, Mandala 7, Sukta 7. On the previous page, we saw the initial invocation where the sage Vasishtha urged Agni forward like a swift horse. This page continues with the word-by-word breakdown (Padapatha) and Sayana’s detailed commentary for verses 3, 4, and the beginning of 5, focusing on Agni's birth at the altar and his role as the divine priest.</meta>

## Hymn Text

<note>Padapatha for Verse 3 (continued from previous page)</note>

Forward | sacrifice | well-placed | indeed | grass | pleases | Agni | praised | like | invoker | 
both parents | all-bestowing | invoking | since | youngest | you were born |
very gracious ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

This **sacrifice** (<note>original: "yajñaḥ"</note>) is **forward-moving** (<note>original: "prācīnaḥ"</note>), meaning it is being performed correctly. Alternatively, it means the invoker of the sacrifice is moving forward. Or, it suggests the sacrificial oblation is moving forward, facing the east and approaching the altar. **Indeed** (<note>original: "hi"</note>), the **sacrificial grass** (<note>original: "barhiḥ"</note>) is **well-placed** (<note>original: "sudhitaṃ"</note>) or properly prepared. **Agni**, when **praised** (<note>original: "īḷitaḥ"</note>), **pleases** (<note>original: "prīṇīte"</note>) the gods and becomes satisfied. He is **like** (<note>original: "na"</note>) an **invoker** (<note>original: "hotā"</note>); the word "na" here also functions as "and." He is **invoking** (<note>original: "huvāno"</note>) the **two parents** (<note>original: "mātarā"</note>), namely Heaven and Earth, who are **all-bestowing** (<note>original: "viśvavāre"</note>), into the sacrificial food. When does this happen? The text says: **Since** (<note>original: "yataḥ"</note>) or when, O **youngest** (<note>original: "yaviṣṭha"</note>) Agni—O ever-youthful one—you are **born** (<note>original: "jajñिṣe"</note>) as one who is **very gracious** (<note>original: "suśevaḥ"</note>), providing great comfort and happiness.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the fourth verse ॥ <-

<note>Rig Veda 7.7.4 Samhita</note>
**Instantly at the sacrifice, the wise men generate the chariot-like leader; he who is the Lord of the People has been placed in the home—Agni, the delightful, the sweet-spoken, the observer of Truth. ॥ 4 ॥**

<note>Rig Veda 7.7.4 Padapatha</note>
Instantly | at the sacrifice | chariot-like | they generate | men | wise | who | of these |
of the people | was placed | Lord of All | in the home | Agni | delightful | sweet-spoken | observer of Truth ॥ 4 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Wise** (<note>original: "vicetasaḥ"</note>) or possessing discerning intelligence, **men** (<note>original: "mānuṣāso"</note>) **instantly** (<note>original: "sadyaḥ"</note>) **generate** (<note>original: "jananta"</note>) or produce Agni—who is the **chariot-like** (<note>original: "rathiraṃ"</note>) leader—at the **sacrifice** (<note>original: "adhvare"</note>). He who carries their oblation, this very **Agni**, who is the **Lord of the People** (<note>original: "viśapatiḥ"</note>), the protector of the subjects or the lord of the universe, the **delightful** (<note>original: "mandraḥ"</note>) gladdener, the **sweet-spoken** (<note>original: "madhuvacāḥ"</note>) one whose voice brings joy, and the **observer of Truth** (<note>original: "ṛtāvā"</note>) who possesses the ritual, has been **placed** (<note>original: "adhāyi"</note>) or established in the **home** (<note>original: "duroṇe"</note>)—the house of the **men** (<note>original: "viśāṃ"</note>).

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the fifth verse ॥ <-

<note>Rig Veda 7.7.5 Samhita</note>
**The chosen carrier has sat down, having arrived; Agni the Great, the sustainer, in the seat of men. Both Heaven and Earth have strengthened him whom the invoker worships, the all-bestowing one. ॥ 5 ॥**

<note>Rig Veda 7.7.5 Padapatha</note>
Has sat down | chosen | carrier | having arrived | Agni | the Great | in the seat of men | sustainer |
Heaven | and | whom | Earth | they two have strengthened | whom | the invoker | worships | all-bestowing ॥ 5 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Chosen** (<note>original: "vṛtaḥ"</note>) for the role of the invoker, the **carrier** (<note>original: "vanhiḥ"</note>) who bears the oblations to the gods, **the Great** (<note>original: "brahmā"</note>) or the all-encompassing one, the **sustainer** (<note>original: "vidhartā"</note>) or supporter of the universe—**Agni**, **having arrived** (<note>original: "ājaganvān"</note>) from the celestial realm or being of a nature that constantly approaches the sacrifice, **has sat down** (<note>original: "asādi"</note>) in the **seat of men** (<note>original: "nṛṣadane"</note>), which is the designated place of the invoking priest.

<vocab>
**Agni** (<note>Sanskrit: अग्नि</note>) - The sacred fire deity who mediates between gods and humans.
**Sacrifice** (<note>Sanskrit: यज्ञ, yajña</note>) - The central Vedic ritual of offerings.
**Invoker** (<note>Sanskrit: होता, hotā</note>) - The specific priest who recites the Rig Vedic verses.
**Lord of the People** (<note>Sanskrit: विशपति, viśapati</note>) - A title for Agni as the protector of the human settlement.
**The Great** (<note>Sanskrit: ब्रह्मा, brahmā</note>) - In this context, an epithet for Agni's vastness or his role as the presiding priest.
**Youngest** (<note>Sanskrit: यविष्ठ, yaviṣṭha</note>) - An epithet for Agni because he is "born anew" each time the sacrificial fire is lit.
**In the home** (<note>Sanskrit: दुरोणे, duroṇe</note>) - Referring to the domestic or sacrificial hearth.
**Sweet-spoken** (<note>Sanskrit: मधुवचाः, madhuvacāḥ</note>) - Describing the pleasing sound of the crackling fire or the hymns.
</vocab>

<summary>This page details Agni’s installation at the sacrificial altar, describing him as a wise leader generated by men who sustains the universe and brings together Heaven and Earth. Sayana explains Agni's various roles as the carrier of oblations and the delightful, sweet-spoken guest in the homes of worshippers.</summary>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary on the fifth verse of Rig Veda, Mandala 7, Sukta 8, and provides the complete text and explanation for verses 6 and 7. [He who is] seated. The Agni whom both Heaven and Earth increase <note>original: "vavṛdhāte"</note>—that is, nourish. And whom the human invoker sacrifices to, he who is all-choice <note>original: "viśvavāram"</note>—meaning desirable to all.

->|| Now the Sixth [Verse] ||<-

## Hymn Text
These men have increased everything with riches; they who, being manly, have fashioned the hymn as a desirable thing.
They who, burning with zeal, increase the people; they who have kindled this light of my cosmic order. ॥ 6 ॥

**Padapatha**
These | with riches | everything | hither | they increased | zeal or hymn | who | desirable | manly | they fashioned |
forward | who | people | they increase | burning | hither | who | my | of this | they kindled | of cosmic order ॥ 6 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
**These** (<note>original: "ete"</note>) men of mine have **increased** (<note>original: "ātiranta"</note>) or nourished the **entire** (<note>original: "viśvam"</note>) group of those to be supported with **riches** (<note>original: "dyumnebhiḥ"</note>). Alternatively, it means they have pervaded the whole world with their glories. Who are they? The text says: those **manly** (<note>original: "naryā"</note>) men who **fashioned** (<note>original: "atakṣan"</note>) or prepared the **hymn** (<note>original: "manyum"</note>)—which is the object of praise—as something **desirable** (<note>original: "vāram"</note>) or sufficient. The word "va" indicates a conjunction ("and"). And those **people** (<note>original: "viśaḥ"</note>) who are **burning** (<note>original: "oṣamāṇāḥ"</note>) with zeal <note>Sayana notes a grammatical variation here: the rules for doubling the root in the desiderative form <term>śṛṇoteḥ sanyaṅoriti</term> and the markers for making the suffix <term>iko jhaliti sanaḥ</term> do not apply here as these rules are optional in Vedic Sanskrit <term>chandasi vikalpyanta</term></note>... they **increase** (<note>original: "atiranta"</note>) others. Furthermore, those who are mine have **kindled** (<note>original: "ādīdhayan"</note>) the **truth** (<note>original: "ṛtasya"</note>) of this, referring to this sacrificial Agni <note>The use of the genitive case "of the truth" functions here as the object of the verb, similar to the phrase "of the human fires"</note>.

---

->|| Now the Seventh [Verse] ||<-

## Hymn Text
Now, O Agni, we the Vasishthas pray to you, the lord of riches, O son of strength.
Bring food to the praisers and the wealthy patrons. Do you all protect us ever with blessings. ॥ 7 ॥

**Padapatha**
Now | you | O Agni | we pray | the Vasishthas | the lord | O son | of strength | of riches |
food | to the praisers | to the wealthy patrons | he reached | you | protect | with blessings | always | us ॥ 7 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **son of strength** (<note>original: "sahasaḥ sūno"</note>)—meaning Agni, who is produced by the force of friction—we, the **Vasishthas**, pray to **you**, the **lord** (<note>original: "īśānam"</note>) of all **riches** (<note>original: "vasūnām"</note>). **Bring** (<note>original: "ānaṭ"</note>) or cause **food** (<note>original: "iṣam"</note>) to reach **quickly** (<note>original: "nu"</note>) today our **praisers** (<note>original: "stotṛbhyaḥ"</note>) and our **wealthy patrons** (<note>original: "maghavadbhyaḥ"</note>) who provide the oblations <note>The verb "ānaṭ" comes from the root for "to pervade" or "to reach" and uses a specific Vedic tense marker</note>. May **you** and all your divine attendants **always protect us** with your **blessings** (<note>original: "svastibhiḥ"</note>). This is what we **pray** (<note>original: "īmahe"</note>) for or request.

The eighth hymn, beginning "The King is kindled," consists of seven verses composed by the seer Vasishtha in the Trishtubh meter, addressed to Agni. <note>This matches the entry in the <term>Anukramani</term>, the ancient index of the Vedas</note>.

<vocab>
- अग्नि (Agni): The divine fire, mediator between gods and humans.
- वसिष्ठ (Vasishtha): A famous Vedic sage; the "Vasishthas" refers to his family/clan.
- द्युम्न (Dyumna): Radiant wealth or glory.
- ऋत (Rita): The fundamental cosmic order or truth that governs the universe.
- सहसः सूनु (Sahasah Sunu): "Son of Strength," a title for Agni because fire is produced by the physical strength of rubbing sticks.
- इष् (Ish): Vitality, food, or refreshing draughts.
- मघवत् (Maghavat): "The Generous Ones," referring to the patrons who fund the sacrifice.
</vocab>

934 || Rig Veda || [Mandala 5, Anuvaka 2, Varga 11]

**Application for the Morning Prayer and the Recitation for the Ashvins:** In the <term>Atithyā</term><note>The 'Hospitality' rite performed for the arrival of the Soma plant at the sacrificial ground.</note> ceremony, the verse "Forward, forward this Agni..." is used as the <term>Yājyā</term><note>The consecration or offering verse recited by the priest.</note> for the <term>Sviṣṭakṛt</term><note>The "Maker of Good Sacrifice," an epithet of Agni during the final portion of an oblation.</note> offering. It is also indicated in the ritual manuals: "Forward, forward this Agni of Bharata, I hear," are the two verses for the joint offering. (Asvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4. 5.)

## Hymn Text

-> || Here is the First Verse || <-

The King, the Master, is kindled with salutations, he whose face is anointed with butter.
Men with offerings worship him, pressing forward; this Agni has shone forth at the dawning of the days. ॥ 1 ॥

**Word-for-Word Analysis**
Kindled | King | Master/Lord | with salutations | whose | face | anointed/offered | with butter |
Men | with offerings | they worship | pressing forward | hither | Agni | this | of the dawns | has shone forth ॥ 1 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
The radiant (<note>original: "rājā"</note>) Master (<note>original: "aryaḥ"</note>), who is either the lord or the stimulator of offerings, is thoroughly kindled by Agni with hymns of praise. That is, he is set ablaze. The face or form (<note>original: "pratīkam"</note>) of this Agni becomes anointed or offered into with butter (<note>original: "ghṛtena"</note>). Furthermore, our **men**—meaning the priests—who are **pressing forward** (<note>original: "sabādhaḥ"</note>), being either closely intent or experiencing the pressure of the rite, **worship** (<note>original: "īḷate"</note>) or praise him along with the offerings. This Agni **has shone forth** (<note>original: "āśoci"</note>) or blazes up at the arrival of the **dawns**.

## Hymn Text

-> || Now the Second Verse || <-

This Agni is known as very great, the delightful Invoker, the sacrifice of man.
He has spread his light, the bright one, manifesting himself upon the earth; with a black path, he has grown through the herbs. ॥ 2 ॥

**Word-for-Word Analysis**
This | [particle] | indeed | very great | is known | Invoker | delightful | of man | sacrifice | Agni |
broadly | light | the bright one | manifesting | upon the earth | black-pathed | with herbs | has grown ॥ 2 ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)
This very **Invoker** (<note>original: "hotā"</note>), the caller of the gods, the **delightful** (<note>original: "mandraḥ"</note>) or gladdening one, the great Agni who is the **sacrifice of man**, is **known as very great** (<note>original: "sumahān avedi"</note>). He is recognized for his immense greatness. Moreover, he, the **bright one** (<note>original: "arkaḥ"</note>), spreads his **lights** (<note>original: "bhāḥ"</note>) through the atmosphere. Furthermore, this **black-pathed** (<note>original: "kṛṣṇapaviḥ"</note>) Agni—so called because he leaves a black trail—while **manifesting** (<note>original: "sasṛjānaḥ"</note>) or being created upon the earth, **has grown** (<note>original: "vavakṣe"</note>) or increased by consuming the **herbs** <note>Meaning the wood and plants used as fuel.</note>.

With what [hymn], O Agni, will you clothe our prayer in beauty? What self-power will you bring, being praised?
When shall we become the masters of riches, the winners of wealth that is hard to surpass and brings success? ॥ 3 ॥

**Word-for-Word Analysis**

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the hymns of the Rig Veda, specifically Mandala 7, Sukta 8. [Mandala 7, Anuvaka 1, Hymn 8]      || Fifth Book (Ashtaka) ||      935

O Agni, by what food (<note>original: "svadhayā"</note>) or oblation do you reach (<note>original: "vivaḥ"</note>) our praise? That is, do you pervade or cover it? And what food do you attain when you are being lauded or praised? O Agni of beautiful gifts (<note>original: "sudatra"</note>)! Regarding this, the ancient etymologist Yaska says: <gloss>"Sudatra" means one who gives welfare.</gloss> When shall we become the masters (<note>original: "patayaḥ"</note>) of wealth that is difficult for enemies to overcome, and is beneficial? When shall we become the enjoyers and sharers of such riches?

->॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**Far and wide this Agni of the Bharata is heard, when he shines with great light like the Sun.**
**He who stood over the Puru in battles, the shining divine guest has blazed forth. ॥ 4 ॥**

**Far and wide | this | Agni | of the Bharata | is heard | out | when | Sun | like | shines | great | light |**
**over | who | Puru | in battles | stood | shining | divine | guest | has blazed ॥ 4 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
This famous Agni of the sacrificer (<note>original: "bharatasya"</note>), who is mine, is heard far and wide. He becomes renowned. If you ask "when?", the text answers: when he shines (<note>original: "virocate"</note>) with great light, appearing like the Sun. Furthermore, this Agni, who in battles overcame the demon named Puru (<note>original: "puru-namakam-asuram"</note>), now shines as the divine guest (<note>original: "daivyo atithiḥ"</note>). Being worthy of worship like a guest of the gods, he has blazed forth.

->॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**In you, Agni, are many sacrificial offerings; be well-disposed with all your forms.**
**O Agni, you are heard when praised; O well-born one, increase your own body. ॥ 5 ॥**

**Are | indeed | in you | offerings | many | be | with all | well-disposed | with forms |**
**praised | indeed | Agni | you are heard | being lauded | yourself | increase | body | well-born ॥ 5 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, in you (<note>original: "tve"</note>) there are many sacrificial offerings or oblations of clarified butter. This is certainly the case. And may you be well-disposed (<note>original: "sumanāḥ"</note>) along with all your forms (<note>original: "anīkaiḥ"</note>), which refers to your splendors, your manifestations, or the various sacrificial fires. O Agni, hear the hymn of the praiser (<note>original: "stutaḥ"</note>). The word "stut" refers to one who praises. O <term>Sujata</term><note>An epithet meaning "well-born" or "nobly manifested," referring to Agni's birth from the friction of the fire-sticks or his appearance at the sacrifice.</note>, O Agni of auspicious appearance, as you are being lauded, increase your own body—or perhaps increase my own body (<note>original: "tanvam"</note>) as the sacrificer.

**Vocabulary:**
- **Agni:** The deity of fire and mediator between gods and men.
- **Bharata:** A term for the sacrificer or a specific noble lineage.
- **Offerings (<note>original: "āhavanāni"</note>):** Ritual oblations poured into the fire.
- **Well-born (<note>original: "sujāta"</note>):** A title for Agni highlighting his pure and noble origin.
- **Heard/Renowned (<note>original: "śṛṇve"</note>):** To be famous or widely recognized.
- **Battles (<note>original: "pṛtanāsu"</note>):** Conflicts where the deity's protection is sought.
- **Guest (<note>original: "atithi"</note>):** Agni is viewed as the "divine guest" residing in the home of the sacrificer.

<summary>This page concludes the 8th hymn of Mandala 7, describing Agni as a powerful, sun-like force who overcomes enemies (like the demon Puru) and acts as a benevolent divine guest who receives many offerings.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Bharata, Puru, Sun imagery, divine guest, sacrifice, Sayanacharya commentary, Rig Veda Mandala 7</keywords>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**May this hymn, bestowing hundreds and thousands, be born for Agni, the one who is twice-mighty. May it be a source of happiness for the singers and their kin—a radiant prayer, dispelling disease and slaying the demons. ॥ 6 ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Bestowing hundreds** (<note>original: "śatasā"</note>) refers to one who grants a hundred cows; **with thousands** (<note>original: "saṃsahasram"</note>) means one who is also joined with a thousand cows. **Twice-mighty** (<note>original: "dvibarhā"</note>) refers to the seer Vasishtha, who is great through two things: knowledge and ritual action. Alternatively, it means one who is great in two places, namely the two worlds of heaven and earth. As the ancient etymologist Yaska says: <gloss>"Twice-mighty" means one who is exalted in two places.</gloss> May **this hymn** (<note>original: "idaṃ vaca"</note>), this song of praise, **be born** or generated for Agni. To explain what kind of hymn it is, the text says: that which is **radiant** (<note>original: "dyumat"</note>), meaning full of light or bringing glory. It is **dispelling disease** (<note>original: "amīvacātanam"</note>), meaning a remover of illnesses, and a **slayer of demons** (<note>original: "rakṣohā"</note>). May it **be** (<note>original: "bhavāti"</note>) a source of **happiness** (<note>original: "śam"</note>) or comfort for the singers and for their **kin** (<note>original: "āpaye"</note>), such as sons and other relatives.

## Sukta Introduction

The ninth hymn, beginning with the words **"The lover has awakened"** (<note>original: "abodhi jāra"</note>), consists of six verses. It was seen by the seer Vasishtha, is composed in the Trishtubh meter, and is addressed to Agni. The index of verses confirms "The lover has awakened" contains six verses. Its ritual application (<term>viniyoga: the specific time a hymn is recited in a sacrifice</term>) is mentioned as being among the thirteen hymns used for the morning prayer and the litany to the Ashvins.

[Mandala 7, Section 1, Hymn 9]      || Fifth Book (Ashtaka) ||      937

The consumer <note>original: "jāraḥ"</note> who causes all living beings to age, the invoker <note>original: "hotā"</note> of the gods, the delightful or praiseworthy one, the wisest seer, and the purifier—Agni—has been awakened in the midst of the dawns. Furthermore, he establishes wisdom <note>original: "ketum"</note> for both two-legged and four-legged creatures, whether divine or human. He places the offerings among the gods and bestows wealth upon the pious sacrificers.

---

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**He is the one of noble intent, who opened the doors of the Panis; he purifies for us the adorable herd of cows that provides much nourishment. The delightful invoker of the people, the friend of the house, he is seen dispelling the darkness of the nights. ॥ 2 ॥**

**Pada-patha (Word-for-Word):**
saḥ | su-kratuḥ | yaḥ | vi | duraḥ | paṇīnām | punānaḥ | arkam | puru-bhojasam | naḥ |
hotā | mandraḥ | viśām | damūnāḥ | tiraḥ | tamaḥ | dadṛśe | rāmyāṇām ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

That Agni is of noble intent <note>original: "sukratuḥ"</note>, meaning he possesses good actions or great wisdom. It is Agni who threw open the doors—the enclosures that hid the cows—of the Panis <note>the Panis were mythical demons or stingy beings who stole and hid the cattle of the gods, representing the hoarding of light or wealth</note>. He is purifying <note>original: "punānaḥ"</note>—meaning he is bringing or preparing—for our sake the adorable <note>original: "arkam"</note> herd of cows which provides much nourishment <note>original: "purubhojasam"</note> through their milk. He is the invoker <term>Hotā (an officiating priest who calls the gods)</term>, the delightful or praiseworthy one, the friend of the home <note>original: "damūnāḥ"</note> with a disciplined mind. He is seen <note>original: "dadṛśe"</note> dispelling <note>original: "tiraskurvan"</note> the darkness of the nights that cause people to rest, or of the people who are the sacrificers. Alternatively, it means he causes the darkness to disappear.

---

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**The wise, the seer, the boundless, the radiant, the one with a fair assembly, the friend, the guest, and our auspicious one; of wonderful luster, he shines before the dawns. As the child of the waters, he has entered the burgeoning plants. ॥ 3 ॥**

**Pada-patha (Word-for-Word):**
amūraḥ | kaviḥ | aditiḥ | vivasvān | su-saṃsat | mitraḥ | atithiḥ | śivaḥ | naḥ |
citra-bhānuḥ | uṣasām | bhāti | agre | apām | garbhaḥ | pra-svaḥ | ā | viveśa ॥ 3 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

This Agni is not confused <note>original: "amūraḥ"</note>, he is the wise seer <note>original: "kaviḥ"</note>, the boundless or not-wretched one <note>original: "aditiḥ"</note>, and the luminous one <note>original: "vivasvān"</note>. He possesses a beautiful assembly or place of sitting <note>original: "susaṃsat"</note>. He is Mitra <note>the god of friendship/contracts</note>, the protector from death, and he is the guest <note>original: "atithiḥ"</note> of all, to be honored like a visitor. He is our auspicious one <note>original: "śivaḥ"</note>, the doer of good for the world, and possesses wonderful luster <note>original: "citrabhānuḥ"</note>. He shines at the head or the face of the dawns. Being the child of the waters <note>original: "apām garbhaḥ"</note>, he has entered <note>original: "ā viveśa"</note> the plants <note>original: "pra-svaḥ"</note> as they are being born.

<note>Footnote: VOL. III. 11 F</note>

<vocab>
- **Agni**: The sacred fire, viewed here as a priest, a guest, and a cosmic force.
- **Pani**: A class of demonic beings in the Rig Veda known for withholding wealth (cows/light) from the righteous.
- **Sukratu**: A term implying both high intelligence and the power to act rightly.
- **Child of the Waters**: A common epithet for Agni (*Apām Napāt*), referring to lightning coming from rain clouds or the sap within plants.
</vocab>

<summary>These verses describe Agni as a wise and luminous deity who liberates light (symbolized by cows) from the demonic Panis and manifests within the natural world as the "child of the waters" dwelling in plants.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Panis, liberation of cows, dawn, solar fire, Mitra, Vedic sacrifice, Sayana commentary</keywords>

<meta>This page concludes the ninth hymn of the seventh Mandala of the Rig Veda. While the previous page discussed Agni’s role as the dispeller of darkness and the opener of the enclosures of the Panis, this page focuses on Agni’s role as the divine messenger (Duta) and the protector of the Vasistha lineage. It includes the final three verses (4, 5, and 6) of the hymn, along with the traditional commentary by the scholar Sayana.</meta>

938 || Rig Veda || Book 5, Chapter 2, Section 12.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥ <-
Worthy of praise among the generations of men, Jatavedas <note>original: "jātavedāḥ"; an epithet of Agni meaning "knower of all created beings" or "possessor of wealth"</note> shines, traveling through the assemblies. He who radiates with a beautiful appearance and a brilliant light; the praises <note>original: "gāvaḥ"; literally "cows," but here interpreted as hymns of praise</note> awaken him as he is kindled. ॥ 4 ॥

**Word-for-Word (Pada-patha):**
Worthy of praise | for you | of man | in the ages | traveling through assemblies | shines | knower of all beings | 
beautiful to behold | with brilliance | who | shines forth | towards | praises (cows) | being kindled | they awaken. ॥ 4 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, you are the one <note>original: "vastvam"; Sayana notes a grammatical shift in person/number here</note> who is worthy of praise <note>original: "īḷenyaḥ"</note> during all the days and times of sacrifice for **mankind**. From this point, the praise shifts to the third person. That Agni, who is the **knower of all beings** (or the possessor of wealth), travels through and is present in the sacrificial assemblies <note>original: "samanagā"</note> and **shines** <note>original: "aśrucat"</note> brightly. He **shines forth** with a **brilliance** that is **beautiful to behold**. The **praises**—compared here to cows—**awaken** that Agni as he is **being kindled**; that is, they rouse or honor him.

Regarding the ritual use: This verse (along with the following) is used as the concluding prayer <note>original: "yājyā"</note> for the offering of the marrow in the animal sacrifice dedicated to the All-Gods <note>original: "vaiśvadeve paśau"</note>. It is indicated in the ritual manuals: **"Agni, go upon your mission as messenger, do not fail us..." these three verses are used (Asvalayana Srauta Sutra 3. 7).**

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ And this is the Fifth Verse ॥ <-
O Agni, go upon your **mission as messenger**; do not fail us. Reach toward the **gods** with this **group** of **prayer-makers**. Worship **Sarasvati**, the **Maruts** <note>the storm gods</note>, the **Ashvins** <note>the twin divine physicians</note>, the **Waters**, and **all the gods**, so they may **bestow riches** upon us. ॥ 5 ॥

**Word-for-Word (Pada-patha):**
O Agni | go | messenger's office | do not | fail | the gods | towards | prayer-making | with the group |
Sarasvati | the Maruts | the two Ashvins | the Waters | worship | the gods | for the bestowal of riches | all. ॥ 5 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, perform the **mission of a messenger**, which consists of carrying the sacrificial offerings and similar tasks. **Go toward the gods**. Together with this **group** of **prayer-makers**—meaning us and our fellow singers—**do not fail** us; do not let us be harmed. **Worship** these deities: **Sarasvati, the Maruts, the Ashvins, and the Waters**, as well as **all the gods**, so that they may **bestow riches** <note>original: "ratnadheyāya"; literally "the placing of jewels"</note> upon us.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-
O Agni, the **most excellent Vasistha**, kindling you, has **slain the demon Jarutha**. Worship the gods for our **wealth** and for **wisdom**. O Knower of all beings, you who are **led by many**, be praised! And **may you all protect us always with blessings!** ॥ 6 ॥

**Word-for-Word (Pada-patha):**
You | O Agni | kindling | Vasistha | Jarutha | has slain | worship | for wealth | wisdom |
led by many | knower of all beings | be praised | you (all) | protect | with blessings | always | us. ॥ 6 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, the sage **Vasistha** <note>the chief seer of this Mandala</note>, while **kindling** you, **has slain Jarutha** <note>a demon or an enemy of the Vasisthas</note>. **Worship** the gods so that we may obtain **wealth** and **wisdom** <note>original: "puramdhim"</note>. O **Jatavedas**, you who are **led by many** in various sacrifices, **be praised** by us. The hymn ends with the traditional refrain of the Vasistha family: **"May you all"**—the gods mentioned before—**"protect us always with blessings."**

<vocab>
Agni (अग्नि) : The Vedic god of fire, the mediator between gods and humans.
Jatavedas (जातवेदस्) : An ancient title for Agni, meaning one who knows all things that are born.
Dutya (दूत्य) : The function or office of a messenger; Agni acts as the courier of the sacrifice.
Vasistha (वसिष्ठ) : "The most excellent"; the name of the prominent sage (Rishi) who authored this section of the Veda.
Ratnadheya (रत्नधेय) : The act of bestowing or granting precious wealth or "jewels."
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes Hymn 9 of the seventh Mandala, focusing on Agni's dual role as the divine messenger who carries offerings to the gods and a powerful protector who destroys demons like Jarutha. It emphasizes the relationship between the sage Vasistha and the sacred fire, ending with a collective prayer for eternal protection.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Vasistha, Jarutha, Vedic sacrifice, divine messenger, Jatavedas, Sarasvati, Maruts, Ashvins, blessings</keywords>

<meta>This page concludes the commentary for the ninth hymn of the seventh Mandala (book) of the Rig Veda and introduces the tenth hymn. The text follows the traditional structure of the Rig Veda: the Samhita (continuous) text, the Pada-patha (word-by-word) text, and the extensive commentary (Bhashya) by the 14th-century scholar Sayana. ## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, the Sage **Vasistha** is the one who is **kindling** you. **Destroy** <note>original: "han"</note> that **Jarutha**, the demon-multitude who is either a harsh speaker or one who deserves to be struck down. **Sacrifice** <note>original: "yakṣi"</note> to the **many-thoughted** <note>original: "purandhim"; meaning many-minded or abundant</note> assembly of gods for the sake of the **wealthy** patron. Furthermore, O **Jatavedas** <note>original: "jātavedas"; Agni as the knower of all births</note>, **praise** the gods <note>original: "jarasva"</note> with a **great hymn of many paths** <note>original: "puruṇīthā"</note>. Or alternatively, the phrase means: "make the many-pathed demons grow old and perish."

->॥ This concludes the twelfth section of the second chapter of the fifth book ॥<-

The tenth hymn, beginning with **"Like the lover of the Dawn,"** <note>original: "uṣo na jāra"</note> consists of five verses. It is attributed to the Sage Vasistha, set in the Trishtubh meter <note>a Vedic meter of 44 syllables</note>, and is addressed to the deity Agni. As stated in the Ancient Index: **"The five verses beginning 'Usho na'..."** Its ritual application <note>original: "viniyoga"</note> is prescribed for the Morning Litany and the Ashvina Shastra <note>a specific recitation for the Twin Gods of Dawn</note>.

->॥ Here begins the first verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
Like the lover of the Dawn, Agni has spread his broad light, flashing, glowing, and intensely brilliant. The showerer of benefits, the carrier of oblations, the pure one shines with light, impelling our prayers and awakening the longing ones. ॥ 1 ॥

**Word-for-Word (Pada-patha):**
Of the Dawn | like | the lover | broad | light | has spread | flashing | glowing | intensely brilliant |
The showerer | the golden-hued | the pure | shines | with light | prayers | impelling | the longing ones | he has awakened. ॥ 1 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Just as the **lover of the Dawn** is the Sun <note>original: "sūrya"</note>, even so Agni **has spread** <note>original: "aśvet"</note> his **broad**, extensive **light** or power. Furthermore, the three words **flashing**, **glowing**, and **intensely brilliant** <note>original: "davidyutat, dīdyat, śośucāna"</note> are all used to denote "shining"; however, they are used together not as a repetition, but to emphasize the extreme intensity of the radiance. It means he is "exceedingly brilliant." Agni, who is the **showerer** <note>original: "vṛṣā"</note> of desires, the **golden-hued** <note>original: "hariḥ"</note> impeller of oblations, and the **pure** purifier, **shines** with **light** while **impelling** or stimulating ritual **prayers**. Moreover, he **awakens** the **longing ones**—those who desire the gods—or he brings out the people who were hidden by the darkness of the night.

->॥ Now the second verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
Like the sun in the day, he has shone before the dawns, as those who desire the gods perform the sacrifice like a prayer. Agni, the divine, knowing all births, the swift messenger who goes to the gods, the best bestower. ॥ 2 ॥

**Word-for-Word (Pada-patha):**
The Sun | like | of the day | of the dawns | he has shone | the sacrifice | performing | those who desire (the gods) | like | prayer |
Agni | births | the divine | [prefix] | [prefix] | knowing | swiftly | messenger | who goes to the gods | the best bestower. ॥ 2 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Agni, in the **day** <note>original: "vastoḥ"; identified as a name for day in ancient lexicons</note>, at the start of the **dawns**, is **like the sun** <note>original: "svar-na"</note>... <note>Commentary continues on the next page</note>

<vocab>
- **Agni**: The deity of fire and the divine priest.
- **Vasistha**: One of the seven great Sages, traditional author of the 7th book of the Rig Veda.
- **Ushas**: The Goddess of Dawn.
- **Jatavedas**: A common title for Agni, meaning "he who knows all things born."
- **Purandhi**: A term for a goddess or a mental state associated with abundance and wisdom.
- **Jarutha**: Often interpreted as a specific demon or a general term for an adversary of the sacrifice.
- **Manma**: A prayer, thought, or meditation directed toward the divine.
- **Vanishtha**: The superlative form of "giving," meaning the most excellent bestower of wealth.
</vocab>

...as [the sun]. And so says Yaska <note>An ancient Sanskrit grammarian and etymologist</note>: "The word 'Svar' <note>original: "svar"</note> refers to the Sun, because it is easy to approach and easy to reach." **He shines** <note>original: "aroci"</note>. The eager priests <term>ushijo; those desiring to perform the ritual</term>, while extending and expanding the sacrifice, [recite] **thoughtful** [manmani] **hymns** <note>original: "stotrāṇi"</note>—this is the implied meaning. The word "na" here is used in the sense of "now." Furthermore, the wise one [vidvan], the **messenger** [duto] of the gods, who **goes toward the gods** [devayava] and is the **most excellent giver** [vanishtho], has **come forward in various ways** [abhyadhrat].

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Verse 3 ॥ <-

Towards Agni go our voices and our thoughts, seeking the gods and begging for wealth. He is fair to look upon, of beautiful appearance, moving gracefully, the carrier of oblations, and the master of mankind.

> **Towards** [achha] । **Voices** [girah] । **Thoughts** [matayah] । **Seeking the gods** [devayantyih] । **Agni** [agnim] । **They go** [yanti] । **Wealth** [dravinam] । **Begging** [bhikshamanah] ।
> **Fair to look upon** [susandresham] । **Beautifully formed** [supratikam] । **Moving gracefully** [svancham] । **Carrier of oblations** [havyavaham] । **Master** [aratim] । **Of mankind** [manushanam] ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Thoughts** [matayah] in the form of praise, **seeking the gods** [devayantir], and **begging** [bhikshamanah] for **wealth** [dravinam], [and our] **voices** [girah] **go towards** [achha yanti] **Agni**. He is described as **fair to look upon** [susandresham] (possessing a beautiful appearance), **beautifully formed** [supratikam] (having a handsome form or lovely limbs), **moving gracefully** [svancham] (going well toward the sacrifice), the **carrier of oblations** [havyavaham] (the one who carries the offerings to the gods), and the **master** [aratim] (lord) **of mankind** [manushanam].

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Verse 4 ॥ <-

O Agni, being in harmony with the Vasus, bring Indra to us. With the Rudras, bring the great Rudra. With the Adityas, bring Aditi, who is beneficial to all people. With the singers, bring Brihaspati, who possesses all boons.

> **Indra** [indram] । **To us** [nah] । **O Agni** [agne] । **With the Vasus** [vasubhih] । **In harmony** [sajosha] । **Rudra** [rudram] । **With the Rudras** [rudrebhih] । **Bring** [a vaha] । **The great** [brihantam] ।
> **With the Adityas** [adityebhih] । **Aditi** [aditim] । **Beneficial to all people** [vishvajanyam] । **Brihaspati** [brihaspatim] । **With the singers** [rikvabhih] । **Possessing all boons** [vishvavaram] ॥ ४ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, being **in harmony** [sajoshas] (associated) with the **Vasu** gods <term>Vasus; a group of eight elemental deities representing aspects of nature</term>, **bring Indra** for **us** [nah]. Associated with the **Rudra** gods <term>Rudras; eleven storm deities associated with the wilder aspects of nature</term>, **bring the great Rudra**. Associated with the **Aditya** gods <term>Adityas; twelve solar deities representing cosmic laws</term>, **bring Aditi**, who is **beneficial to all people** [vishvajanyam]. Associated with the **singers** [rikvabhih]—referring to the praiseworthy Angiras deities—**bring Brihaspati** <note>The lord of prayer and preceptor of the gods</note>, who is **to be chosen/honored by all** [vishvavaram].

---

## Hymn Text
-> ॥ Verse 5 ॥ <-

The eager worshippers praise Agni, the delightful invoker, the youngest, at the sacrifices. For he has become the lord of riches in the night, the tireless messenger for the worship of the gods...

### Mandala 7 | Chapter 1 | Hymn 11
### The Fifth Ashtaka | Page 941

## Hymn Text
<note>Rig Veda 7.10.5 — Word-by-word breakdown (Padapatha)</note>

**The pleasant** [mandraṃ] । **Invoker** [hotāraṃ] । **The eager ones** [uśijaḥ] । **The youngest** [yaviṣṭhaṃ] । **Agni** [agniṃ] । **The people** [viśaḥ] । **They worship** [īḷate] । **In sacrifices** [adhvareṣu] ।
**He** [saḥ] । **Indeed** [hi] । **Possessed of the night** [kṣapā-vān] । **Became** [abhavat] । **Of riches** [rayīṇām] । **Untiring** [atandraḥ] । **Messenger** [dūtaḥ] । **For the worship of the gods** [yajñiyāya devān] ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **eager ones** [uśijaḥ], meaning those who desire [the fruits of the ritual], the **people** [viśaḥ], meaning human beings, **worship** [īḷate]—that is, they praise—**Agni** in their **sacrifices** [adhvareṣu]. He is the **pleasant** [mandraṃ] one, worthy of praise, the **invoker** [hotāraṃ] who calls the gods, and the **youngest** [yaviṣṭhaṃ], most youthful. **Indeed** [hi], for this reason, Agni **became possessed of the night** [kṣapāvān]. <note>original: "kṣapāvān rātrimān"</note> This is because the Agnihotra <term>Agnihotra; a daily fire offering</term> is specifically performed for Agni during the night. He is the **untiring** [atandraḥ], or alert, **messenger** [dūtaḥ] for the **sacrificial worship of the gods** [devān yajathāya], acting on behalf of the **wealthy** [rayīṇām]—the patrons of the sacrifice who possess the "sun-like" wealth of oblations. As the sacred texts say: "Because he became the messenger, therefore the people worship him in the sacrifice."

-> ॥ This concludes the thirteenth section (Varga) of the second chapter of the fifth Book (Ashtaka) ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text
<note>Introduction to Hymn 11</note>

**"Great are you" is a five-verse hymn, the eleventh in this section. Its Seer is Vasishtha, its meter is Trishtubh, and its deity is Agni. This is noted in the Index (Anukramani) with the phrase "Great" [mahan]. Its ritual use is prescribed for the Morning Litany [Pratar-anuvaka] and the Ashvina Litany [Ashvina-shastra].**

-> ॥ Verse 1 ॥ <-
<note>Rig Veda 7.11.1</note>

**Great are you, the indicator of the sacrifice; without you, the immortals do not rejoice.**
**O Agni, come on the same chariot with all the gods; sit here as the first invoker.**

**Great** [mahān] । **You are** [asi] । **Of the sacrifice** [adhvarasya] । **Indicator** [pra-ketaḥ] । **Not** [na] । **Without** [ṛte] । **You** [tvat] । **The immortals** [amṛtāḥ] । **Do rejoice** [mādayante] ।
**Come** [ā] । **With all** [viśvebhiḥ] । **On the same chariot** [sa-rathaṃ] । **Travel** [yāhi] । **With the gods** [devaiḥ] । **Down** [ni] । **O Agni** [agne] । **Invoker** [hotā] । **First** [prathamaḥ] । **Sit** [sad] । **Here** [iha] ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, being the **indicator** [praketaḥ] or the one who makes the sacrifice known, **you are great** [mahān asi]. **Without you** [tvad ṛte]—that is, in your absence—the **immortals** [amṛtāḥ], the gods, **do not rejoice** [na mādayante]. Therefore, **come** [ā yāhi] **on the same chariot** [sarathaṃ] with **all the gods** [viśvebhiḥ devaiḥ]. And **sit down** [niṣada] **here** [iha] on the strewn sacred grass as the **first** [prathamaḥ] or chief **invoker** [hotā] who calls the gods.

In the Vajapeya sacrifice <term>Vajapeya; a high-ranking "Drink of Strength" ritual</term>, this verse serves as the invitation prayer [anuvakya] for the offering of rice pap [caru] to Brihaspati, specifically for the Agni Svishtakrit <note>The aspect of Agni that "makes the offering well-made."</note> portion. This is indicated in the ritual manuals [Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 9.9]: "They worship you, the swift messenger..."

---

-> ॥ Verse 2 ॥ <-
<note>Rig Veda 7.11.2</note>

**The humans, possessing oblations, worship you for your swift messengership, you who are the dweller of the hall.**
**O Agni, for the man on whose sacred grass you sit with the gods, the days become auspicious.**

**You** [tvāṃ] । **They worship** [īḷate] । **Swift** [ajiraṃ] । **For messengership** [dūtyāya] । **Possessing oblations** [haviṣmantaḥ] । **The dweller of the hall** [sadman] । **Indeed** [it] । **Humans** [mānuṣāsaḥ] ।
**Whose** [yasya] । **With the gods** [devaiḥ] । **Sit upon** [ā-asadaḥ] । **Sacred grass** [barhiḥ] । **O Agni** [agne] । **Days** [ahāni] । **For him** [asmai] । **Auspicious** [su-dinā] । **Become** [bhavanti] ॥ २ ॥

## Critical Notes
- The page includes volume markings at the bottom: **VOL. III.** and **11 G**, used by printers and bookbinders to organize the large volumes of the Rig Veda commentary.
- The term *Kshapavan* is interpreted by the commentator specifically through the lens of the Agnihotra ritual, connecting the cosmic "night" to the specific timing of human devotion.
- The *Anukramani* (the introductory sentence for Sukta 11) acts as a metadata summary for the hymn, ensuring the chanter uses the correct tone and tradition.
