## Page 942 || Rig-Veda || [Book 5, Chapter 2, Section 14]

## Commentary (Sayana)
**[Continued from previous page for Verse 2]**

O **Agni**, human beings <note>original: "mānuṣāso"</note>—the sacrificers who possess oblations—always praise you, the **swift-moving** one, for the **office of messenger** <note>original: "dūtyāya"</note>, which is the task of carrying the offerings to the gods. For what purpose? He explains: For whichever sacrificer you sit upon the **sacred grass** <term>barhis; the layer of grass where gods are invited to sit</term> along with the gods, for that giver of oblations, the days become **"good days"**—beautiful and auspicious days.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Now the Third Verse ॥<-

**Thrice a day, O Agni, they have made known the riches within you for the mortal giver. Like Manu, O Agni, sacrifice here to the gods; be our messenger and the protector against calumny.** ॥ ३ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown (Padapatha):**
**Thrice** [triḥ] । **Thrice** [triḥ] । **Of the day** [aktoḥ] । **Forward** [pra] । **They have made known** [cikituḥ] । **Riches** [vasūni] । **Your** [te] । **Inside** [antaḥ] । **For the giver** [dāśuṣe] । **For the mortal** [martyāya] ।
**Like Manu** [manuvat] । **O Agni** [agne] । **Here** [iha] । **Sacrifice** [yakṣi] । **To the gods** [devān] । **Be** [bhava] । **Our** [naḥ] । **Messenger** [dūtaḥ] । **Protector against calumny** [abhiśasti-pāvā] ॥ ३ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, the priests **make known** [pra-cikituḥ]—that is, they announce or prepare—the **riches** [vasūni], meaning the oblations, that are placed **within you** [te antar] during the **day** [aktoḥ]. <note>Sayana notes that although "aktu" usually means night, here it refers to the day because forms are "revealed" (añjyante) in the light.</note> This happens **thrice** [triḥ], corresponding to the three daily soma-pressings <term>savanas; the morning, midday, and evening offerings</term>. This is done for the **mortal** [martyāya] man who is the **giver** [dāśuṣe] of the sacrifice. 

Alternatively, it means that the priests have known the three fires (the domestic, sacrificial, and southern fires) that are placed within you during the day. Furthermore, **like Manu** [manuvat]—as was done in the time of the ancestral progenitor Manu—**sacrifice** [yakṣi] to the **gods** here in this ceremony of mine. Be our **messenger** [dūtaḥ] and our **protector against calumny** [abhiśastipāvā], guarding us from the accusations of enemies who wish us ill.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥<-

**Agni rules the great sacrifice; Agni rules every prepared oblation. For the Vasus enjoy his wisdom; then the gods established him as the carrier of offerings.** ॥ ४ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown (Padapatha):**
**Agni** [agniḥ] । **Rules** [īśe] । **Of the great** [bṛhataḥ] । **Of the sacrifice** [adhvarasya] । **Agni** [agniḥ] । **Of every** [viśvasya] । **Of the oblation** [haviṣaḥ] । **Of the prepared** [kṛtasya] ।
**Ritual wisdom** [kratum] । **Indeed** [hi] । **His** [asya] । **The Vasus** [vasavaḥ] । **Enjoy** [juṣanta] । **Then** [atha] । **The gods** [devāḥ] । **Established** [dadhire] । **The carrier of offerings** [havya-vāham] ॥ ४ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Agni rules** [īśe] the **great** [bṛhataḥ] **sacrifice** [adhvarasya]. <note>Sayana defines "adhvara" as a sacrifice free from "kautilya" or injury/crookedness.</note> Agni alone rules over **every** [viśvasya] **prepared** [kṛtasya] or consecrated **oblation** [haviṣaḥ]. **Indeed** [hi], because the **Vasu gods** [vasavaḥ] **enjoy** [juṣanta] and serve the **ritual wisdom** [kratum] or the sacred acts of this Agni. Moreover, the **gods** **established** [dadhire] Agni as the **carrier of offerings** [havyavāham], the one who conveys the sacrificial gifts to the heavens.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥<-

**O Agni, carry the oblation so that the gods may come; let those with Indra as their chief rejoice here. Place this sacrifice in heaven among the gods; protect us always with your blessings.** ॥ ५ ॥

<vocab>
**Agile/quick** [ajira]: describing Agni’s swift movement as a messenger.
**Human beings** [mānuṣāsa]: the mortal participants in the ritual.
**Office of messenger** [dūtyāya]: the specific role of Agni in connecting Earth and Heaven.
**Praise/implore** [īḷate]: the act of ritual invocation.
**Day** [aktu]: though usually "night," here interpreted as the light of day.
**Protector against curses** [abhiśastipāvā]: one who shields the sacrificer from verbal or spiritual attacks.
**Sacrifice** [adhvara]: literally "uninjured," a pure ritual.
**The Vasus** [vasavaḥ]: a group of elemental deities associated with Agni.
**Carrier of oblations** [havyavāha]: a standard epithet for the sacrificial fire.
**Well-being/prosperity** [svasti]: the ultimate goal of the blessings requested.
</vocab>

It highlights Agni's governance over all prepared offerings and his appointment by the gods as the official carrier of oblations.</summary>

## Page 943 || Mandala 7, Chapter 1, Sukta 12 || Fifth Book

## Hymn Text
<note>Rig Veda 7.12.4 — Word-by-word breakdown (Padapatha)</note>

Bring [ā] । O Agni [agne] । Carry [vaha] । For the eating of oblations [haviḥ-adyāya] । The gods [devān] । With Indra as the chief [indra-jyeṣṭhāsaḥ] । Here [iha] । Let them rejoice [mādayantām] ।
This [imam] । Sacrifice [yajñam] । In heaven [divi] । Among the gods [deveṣu] । Place [dhehi] । You all [yūyam] । Protect [pāta] । With blessings [svasti-bhiḥ] । Always [sadā] । Us [naḥ] ॥ 4 ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
<note>On Rig Veda 7.12.4</note>

O **Agni**, for the "eating of the oblation" <note>original: "haviradyāya"</note>—that is, for the consuming of the sacrificial offerings—bring the gods here. For what purpose? He explains: In this sacrifice, let the gods, who are "led by Indra" <note>original: "indrajyeṣṭhāsaḥ"</note> or have Indra as their chief, rejoice. **Place** <note>original: "dhehi"</note>—or deposit—this sacrifice, meaning this oblation which is to be offered, among the gods who reside in heaven. The underlying meaning is: either bring the gods here or carry this offering to the gods. The final line of the verse <note>the prayer for protection</note> has been explained previously.

->॥ This concludes the fourteenth group (varga) of the second chapter of the fifth book ॥<-

---

## Sukta Introduction
<note>Introduction to Hymn 13 (Rig Veda 7.13)</note>

The twelfth hymn in this sequence, beginning with "We have approached the great" <note>original: "aganma mahā"</note>, consists of three verses. Its seer is **Vasistha**, its meter is **Trishtubh** <term>a Vedic meter of 4 lines with 11 syllables each</term>, and its deity is **Agni**. This is also stated in the Index of Hymns <note>the Anukramani</note>: "We have approached, a triplet." Its ritual application is mentioned in the **Morning Litany** <note>original: "prātaranuvāka"</note> and the **Recitation for the Ashvins** <note>original: "āśvinaśastra"</note>. In the "arranged" ten-night ritual <note>original: "vyūḷhe daśarātre"</note>, on the ninth day, this hymn serves as the **Ghee Recitation** <note>original: "ājyaśastra"</note>. This is indicated in the liturgical texts: "The Ghee Recitation for the third session is 'We have approached the great'" <note>original: "tṛtiyasyāganma mahetyājyaṃ"</note> [Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 9.11].

---

## Hymn Text
<note>Rig Veda 7.13.1</note>

->॥ First Verse ॥<-

**We have approached the Youngest with great reverence, who shines kindled in his own dwelling; the bright-rayed one between the two wide worlds, well-invoked, facing all directions.** ॥ १ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown (Padapatha):**
We have approached [aganma] । With great [mahā] । Reverence [namasā] । The Youngest [yaviṣṭham] । Who [yaḥ] । Shines [dīdāya] । Kindled [sam-iddhaḥ] । In his own [sve] । Dwelling [duroṇe] ।
Bright-rayed [citra-bhānum] । The two worlds [rodasī] । Between [antaḥ] । Wide [urvī] । Well-invoked [su-āhutam] । From all sides [viśvataḥ] । Facing [pratyañcam] ॥ १ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
<note>On Rig Veda 7.13.1</note>

That **Agni** who shines while being kindled with wood in his own place—the **Ahavaniya** fire <term>the consecrated fire used for making offerings</term>—to him, the "Youngest" <note>original: "yaviṣṭham"</note> or the ever-youthful, who exists between the two wide "worlds" <note>original: "rodasī"</note> (heaven and earth) in the mid-region; to him who has "bright rays" <note>original: "citrabhānum"</note> or colorful flames, and who is "well-invoked" <note>original: "svāhutam"</note> with excellent offerings; to that Agni who "faces all directions" <note>original: "viśvataḥ pratyañcam"</note> or moves toward all, we have **approached** <note>original: "aganma"</note>—that is, we come near with great salutation and reverence.

---

## Hymn Text
<note>Rig Veda 7.13.2</note>

->॥ Second Verse ॥<-

**He, having overcome all difficulties by his greatness, I praise Agni, the Knower of Beings, in the house. May he protect us from difficulty and blame—us, the singers, and also our patrons.** ॥ २ ॥

**Word-by-word breakdown (Padapatha):**
He [saḥ] । By greatness [mahnā] । All [viśvā] । Difficulties [duḥ-itāni] । Having overcome [sahvān] । Agni [agniḥ] । I praise [stuve] । In the house [dame] । [Prefix] [ā] । Knower of Beings [jāta-vedāḥ] ।
He [saḥ] । Us [naḥ] । May protect [rakṣiṣat] । From difficulty [duḥ-itāt] । From blame [avadyāt] । Us [asmān] । The singers [gṛṇataḥ] । And [uta] । Our [naḥ] । Patrons [maghonaḥ] ॥ २ ॥

<meta>This page continues the 7th Mandala of the Rig Veda. It concludes the commentary on Hymn 12, focusing on Agni's identification with other major deities like Varuna and Mitra, and begins Hymn 13, which is dedicated to Agni in his "Vaishvanara" (Universal) aspect.</meta>

# Page 944 || Rig Veda || [Book 5, Chapter 2, Section 16]

## Commentary (Sayana)
That Agni, who through his greatness <note>original: "mahvā"</note> overcomes all misfortunes, who is the "knower of all births" <note>original: "jātavedas" — a common epithet for Agni implying omniscience or possessor of all wealth</note>, is praised by us in the sacrificial house <note>original: "dame"</note>. May that Agni protect us from misfortune, from sin, and from blameworthy actions. May he also protect us who sing his praises. Furthermore, may that Agni protect our patrons <note>the "Maghavans" or wealthy sponsors of the sacrifice</note> who provide the offerings.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Now the third verse ॥<-
**You, O Agni, are Varuna and Mitra; the Vasisthas increase you with their prayers.**
**May there be well-granted riches in you; protect us always with your blessings. || 3 ||**

**You | Varuna | and | Mitra | O Agni | You | they increase | with prayers | the Vasisthas |**
**In you | riches | well-granted | let them be | You all | protect | with blessings | always | us. || 3 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, you are **Varuna** <note>the deity of cosmic law</note>. And also you are **Mitra**, the protector of the world from decay. The **Vasisthas** <note>the family of the seer Vasistha</note> increase you—that is, they make you grow—with their prayers and hymns of praise. Let the riches [vasu] existing in you be "well-granted" <note>original: "susananāni"</note>, meaning easily shared or enjoyed. The rest of the verse is clear from previous explanations.

->॥ This concludes the fifteenth group (varga) of the second chapter of the fifth book ॥<-

The thirteenth hymn, beginning with "Toward Agni" <note>original: "pra agnaye"</note>, consists of three verses. Its seer is **Vasistha**, its meter is **Trishtubh** <note>a rhythmic cycle of 44 syllables</note>, and its deity is **Vaishvanara Agni**. Thus it is stated in the Index: "Toward Agni is dedicated to Vaishvanara." Its ritual application is determined by its specific characteristics.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Here is the first verse ॥<-
**Bring your thought and prayer to Agni, who shines for all, the sustainer of wisdom, the slayer of demons.**
**Like an offering on the sacred grass, I, rejoicing, bring praise to Vaishvanara, the director of our prayers. || 1 ||**

**Toward | Agni | who shines for all | the sustainer of wisdom | the slayer of demons | thought | prayer | bring |**
**I bring | offering | like | on the sacred grass | rejoicing | to Vaishvanara | the director | of prayers. || 1 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O companions, bring a mindful hymn [manma] and ritual action [dhītim] to Agni, to the one who <term>illuminates the universe</term> [viśvaśuce], to the <term>sustainer of wisdom</term> [dhiyaṃdhe] (the supporter of ritual acts), and to the <term>slayer of demons</term> [asuraghne]. To <term>Vaishvanara</term>—the specific form of Agni who belongs to or benefits all men—and who is the director or giver [yataye] of desired fruits, I, while being pleased, bring [bhare] a hymn of praise, just like an offering [havir na] placed upon the <term>sacred grass</term> [barhiṣi] at the sacrifice. Alternatively, it may mean: "I, pleasing Agni with an offering, gather the oblation upon the sacred grass." In this context, the word "na" is used in the sense of "now."

<vocab>
- Agni (अग्नि): Vedic deity of fire
- Varuna (वरुण): Vedic deity associated with cosmic order (Rita)
- Mitra (मित्र): Vedic deity associated with contracts and friendship
- Vasishtha (वसिष्ठ): Name of the Rishi (seer) to whom the hymn is attributed
- Vaishvanara (वैश्वानर): An aspect of Agni (fire belonging to all men)
- Asuraghne (असुरघ्ने): Slayer of demons/Asuras
- Barhishi (बर्हिषि): On the sacred grass (ritual context)
- Vishvashuche (विश्वशुचे): Illuminating the universe
- Dhiyandhe (धियंधे): Supporter of wisdom or ritual action
</vocab>

### [Mandala 7, Anuvaka 1, Sukta 14] || The Fifth Ashtaka || 945

->॥ Now the second verse [of Sukta 13] ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**O Agni, as you were being born, you filled the two worlds <note>Heaven and Earth; original: "rodasī"</note> with your shining light. You, O Vaishvanara <note>the Universal One</note>, Knower of all beings <note>original: "jātavedas"</note>, delivered the gods from reproach through your greatness. || 2 ||**

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**You | O Agni | with light | shining | [you] filled | Heaven and Earth | as you were being born |**
**You | the gods | from reproach | delivered | O Universal One | Knower of all beings | through greatness. || 2 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, you, while being born and shining with your brilliance <note>original: "shociṣā"</note>, filled the two worlds—meaning the Heaven and the Earth. Furthermore, O Knower of all beings <note>Sāyaṇa interprets this as "one with innate wisdom" or "possessor of wealth"</note>, O Universal One who is beneficial to all men <note>original: "vaiśvānara"</note>, you delivered the gods from the reproach of the accuser or the thief through your inherent majesty.

---

->॥ Now the third verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**When born, O Agni, you looked upon the worlds like a diligent shepherd <note>original: "gopā"</note> watching over his cattle, moving everywhere. O Universal One, find the path <note>original: "gātum"</note> for our prayer. Do you all protect us always with your blessings. || 3 ||**

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Born | when | O Agni | the worlds | you looked upon | cattle | like | a shepherd | diligent | moving around |**
**O Universal One | for the prayer | find | the path | You all | protect | with blessings | always | us. || 3 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, when you were born in the form of the Sun, being the master and mover who travels everywhere <note>original: "parijmā"</note>, you looked upon the living beings <note>original: "bhuvana"</note> to protect them, just as a guardian of cows <note>a shepherd</note> watches over his cattle. When you do so, find the path—meaning the way to the attainment of results—for the "Brahma" <note>this can mean either the sacred hymn of praise or the Brahmin priest</note>. Alternatively, find the way by which the offerings of the priest may go forth. The rest of the verse is clear.

->॥ This concludes the sixteenth group (varga) of the second chapter of the fifth book ॥<-

---

The fourteenth hymn, beginning with "With fuel, O Knower of all beings," consists of three verses. The seer is Vasistha and the deity is Agni. The first verse is in the **Brihati** metre <note>a Vedic metre of 36 syllables</note>, while the second and third are in the **Trishtubh** metre <note>a Vedic metre of 44 syllables</note>. This is noted in the Index: "With fuel, etc., starting with Brihati." The ritual application <note>original: "viniyoga"</note> follows the indications of the text itself.

**With fuel <note>original: "samidhā"</note> for the Knower of all beings, for the God with invitations to the deities, with oblations and with bright light—we, the worshipers, would offer service to Agni. || 1 ||**

## Commentary by Sayana

<note>Commentary on RV 7.14.1</note>
To the Knower of all beings <note>original: "jātavedase"</note>—meaning Agni who possesses innate wisdom—we, the clan of Vasishtha, offer with kindling. Let us serve him. To the god—the praiseworthy Agni—we offer with divine invocations <note>original: "devahūtibhiḥ"</note>, meaning songs of praise. To the one of bright radiance—Agni of pure light—we, possessing oblations, offer with our offerings. <note>Grammatical note: Sāyaṇa explains that here, due to the use of the verb "to offer/honor" (dāś), the dative case is used to indicate the object of the action, as is common in Vedic usage.</note>

<note>Commentary on RV 7.14.2</note>
O Agni, we of the Vasishtha family honor you <note>original: "te"</note> with kindling. Let us serve you. O one worthy of sacrifice <note>original: "yajatra"</note>, O Agni who is to be worshipped, we offer with fine praise, meaning beautiful hymns. We serve you. O invoker <note>original: "hotar"</note> of the ritual sacrifice, we offer to you with clarified butter <note>original: "ghṛtena"</note>. O god of auspicious light <note>original: "bhadraśoce"</note>, O shining Agni, we offer to you with oblations.

<note>Commentary on RV 7.14.3</note>
O Agni, come to our divine invocation <note>original: "devahūtim"</note>—meaning our hymn or sacrifice—along with the other gods. Come while enjoying the ritual "Vashat" call and the oblation. May we be "givers" <note>original: "dāśataḥ"</note>, meaning those who serve you, the shining god. The rest of the verse is as previously explained.

The fifteenth hymn, beginning with "Upasadya" (Approaching), consists of fifteen verses. Its seer <note>original: "rishi"</note> is Vasishtha, its meter is Gayatri, and its deity is Agni. As stated in the Index <note>original: "Anukramani"</note>:

<term>Jatavedas: An epithet of the fire-god Agni, interpreted as "he who knows all created beings" or "the one from whom wealth is born."</term>

### Mandala 7. Anuvaka 1. Sukta 15. || The Fifth Ashtaka || 947

**Introductory Ritual Commentary**

It has been stated: "The hymn beginning 'To the one who should be approached' <note>original: "upasadyāya"</note> consists of fifteen Gayatri verses." In the Morning Litany <note>term: prātaranuvāka; the first collection of hymns recited before dawn in the Soma sacrifice</note>, during the ritual for Agni in the Gayatri meter and in the litany for the Twin Gods <note>term: āśvinasastra</note>, this hymn is used. It is also indicated: "From the hymn 'To the one who should be approached,' and 'You, O Agni, of the sacrifices,' one should set aside the last three verses." (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.13).

In the morning <term>Upasad</term> rite <note>A preliminary ritual of the Soma sacrifice where the gods "besiege" the demons</note>, the three verses beginning with "To the one who should be approached" are used as the kindling verses <note>term: sāmidhenīs; verses recited while adding fuel to the sacred fire</note>. As it is said: "For the hymn 'To the one who should be approached, the bestower of rewards,' one should recite each of the three verses thrice." (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.8).

In the <term>Pavitreṣṭi</term> <note>A purification ritual</note>, the verse "O Agni, the demons..." is the first introductory verse for the clarified butter portion. It is indicated: "The two butter portions possess purifying power; Agni drives away the demons." (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.12). In the introductory rite <note>term: anvārambhaṇīyā</note>, there is a sacrificial verse for Agni's portion. It is indicated: "Just as the Sun-God Savitr brings all, may he bring us riches." (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.4). In the ritual for well-being <note>term: svastyayanī</note>, the verse "O Agni, protect us" is the first introductory verse for the butter portion. It is indicated: "In the ritual for well-being, the two verses possess protective power: 'O Agni, protect us from sin.'" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 2.10).

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Here is the First Verse ॥ <-

<note>Rig Veda 7.15.1</note>
**To the one who should be approached, the bestower of rewards, pour the oblation into his mouth; he who is our closest kinsman. || 1 ||**

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**To the one who should be approached | to the bestower of rewards | in the mouth | pour | the oblation | who | our | closest | kinsman. || 1 ||**

---

## Commentary of Sayana

O **priests** <note>original: "adhvaryava"</note>, for Agni, who is to be approached <note>original: "upasadanīyāya"</note> and who is the rainer of desires <note>original: "mīḷhuṣe"</note>, pour the sacrificial offering into his very mouth for his satisfaction. This Agni is our closest <note>original: "nediṣṭham"</note> or nearest relative. The word for **kinsman** <note>original: "āpyam"</note> here acts as a noun meaning a close friend or brother.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Second Verse ॥ <-

<note>Rig Veda 7.15.2</note>
**He who has settled before the five peoples in every house—the wise one, the lord of the house, the youth. || 2 ||**

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**Who | five | peoples | towards | has settled | in house after house | the wise | the lord of the house | the youth. || 2 ||**

---

## Commentary of Sayana

That Agni—who is **wise** <note>original: "kaviḥ"</note> or far-sighted, the **lord of the house** <note>original: "gṛhapatiḥ"</note> or protector of homes, and the **youth** <note>original: "yuvā"</note> meaning eternally young—**has settled** or sits in **every house** facing the **five peoples** <note>original: "pañca carṣaṇīḥ"</note>, meaning the five classes of human beings. The full meaning of this sentence concludes with the following verse.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Third Verse ॥ <-

<note>Rig Veda 7.15.3</note>
**May that Agni protect our wealth and our household from every side; and may he save us from sin. || 3 ||**

**Word-by-word Analysis:**
**He | our | wealth | household | Agni | may protect | from every side | and | us | may save | from sin. || 3 ||**

---

## Commentary of Sayana

May that Agni protect our **wealth** <note>original: "vedaḥ"</note> and our **household** <note>original: "amātyam"</note>—meaning those who stay near us or our kinsmen—from all obstructing forces **from every side**. Furthermore, may he save us, the family of Vasishtha, from **sin** <note>original: "aṃhasaḥ"</note> or evil. May he protect us.

## Hymn Text

-> || The Fourth Verse || <-

I have now produced a new song of praise for Agni, the hawk of heaven; may he surely bestow riches upon us. || 4 ||

Now . indeed . song of praise . for Agni . of heaven . hawk . I have produced . riches . surely . may he bestow . us . || 4 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

For Agni, who is like a hawk <note>original: "śyenāya"</note> of heaven because he moves swiftly, I produce <note>original: "jījanam"</note> a new <term>stoma</term> <note>A hymn or song of praise</note>. May that Agni surely bestow upon us—the worshipers—abundant riches <note>original: "vasvaḥ"; the commentator notes this is a grammatical variation where the possessive form is used to mean the object 'wealth'</note>. The sense is: "May he give us wealth."

---

## Hymn Text

-> || The Fifth Verse || <-

Whose desirable splendors are like the wealth of one who has heroic sons, beautiful to behold—the splendors of Agni as he shines at the sacrifice. || 5 ||

Desirable . whose . splendors . to behold . wealth . of one with heroes . like . Agni . of the sacrifice . of the shining one . || 5 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The splendors—the radiant lights—of Agni, who shines at the front of the sacrifice, are desirable to the eye or for the observer to behold, just as the wealth of a man with many heroic sons <note>original: "vīravataḥ"</note> is desirable. The phrase "I have produced a new song of praise" from the previous verse is understood to carry over here, or it connects to the following verse.

---

-> || Thus ends the eighteenth section of the second chapter of the fifth book || <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> || The Sixth Verse || <-

May he accept this ritual offering; may Agni delight in our hymns, he the most excellent sacrificer and carrier of oblations. || 6 ||

He . this . may he accept . the 'vashat' utterance . Agni . may he delight . our . hymns . most excellent sacrificer . carrier of oblations . || 6 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

May Agni—who is the most excellent sacrificer <note>original: "yajiṣṭhaḥ"</note> and the carrier of the sacrificial offerings <term>havyavāhana</term>—accept <note>original: "vetu"</note> this ritual offering <note>original: "vaṣaṭkṛtim"</note> given by us. That is, may he desire it or consume it. And may he delight in <note>original: "juṣata"</note> our hymns and songs of praise.

---

## Hymn Text

-> || The Seventh Verse || <-

We establish you, O Lord of the People, the radiant one, O Divine Agni, we have placed you who are well-invoked and surrounded by heroes. || 7 ||

Down . you . to be approached . O Lord of the People . radiant . O God . we have placed . O Agni . O well-invoked . || 7 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O Agni, you who are to be approached <note>original: "nakṣya"</note>, O Lord of the People <note>term: viśvapati; protector of the human settlements</note>, O radiant God, you who are well-invoked by all the sacrificers, we have established <note>original: "ni dhīmahi"</note> you. You are the one who possesses brilliance and the one who is accompanied by excellent heroic worshipers.

<note>The term 'nakṣya' is derived from a root meaning 'to pervade' or 'to reach,' signifying Agni is the goal of the ritual movement.</note>

<summary>This page contains verses 4-7 of Sukta 15, where the poet Vasishtha compares Agni's swiftness to a hawk and his brilliance to the coveted wealth of a large family. The text emphasizes Agni's role as the "Carrier of Oblations" who accepts the sacred ritual utterances.</summary>

-> ॥ The Eighth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Shine during the nights and the mornings; through you, may we be well-served with fire. You are a possessor of heroes, favoring us. || 8 ||

Nights . mornings . and . shine . well-served with fire . through you . we . possessor of heroes . you . favoring us . || 8 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, shine through the nights <note>original: "kṣapaḥ"</note> and the days or mornings <note>original: "usraḥ"</note>; that is to say, shine always. Through you, the radiant one, we—the family of Vashishtha—become "well-served with fire" <note>original: "svagnayaḥ"</note>, meaning those who possess a beautiful and well-tended fire. You are "favoring us" <note>original: "asmayuḥ"; the commentator explains this as 'one who desires or loves us'</note>. <note>Grammatical note: Sayana explains the linguistic derivation from the Paninian rules regarding the suffix 'kyac' and the Vedic loss of the letter 'd'</note>. The ancient lexicographer Yaska also confirms that "asmayu" means "one who desires us." May you be a "possessor of heroes" <note>original: "suvīraḥ"</note>, meaning one followed by excellent worshipers or praisers.

-> ॥ The Ninth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
To you, for the acquisition of wealth, the leaders and wise men approach with prayers; our thousand-fold, imperishable speech also approaches you. || 9 ||

Toward . you . for acquisition . leaders . wise men . go . with prayers . toward . imperishable . thousand-fold . || 9 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, the leaders <note>original: "naro"; the patrons of the sacrifice</note> and the wise, intelligent men <note>original: "viprāso"</note> approach you through their ritual acts and prayers <note>original: "dhītibhiḥ"</note> for the sake of acquiring wealth or for the attainment of their desires. Furthermore, our speech, which consists of praise and is "thousand-fold" <note>original: "sahasriṇī"; meaning abundant or multifaceted</note> and "imperishable" <note>original: "akṣarā"</note>, also comes toward you.

-> ॥ The Tenth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
Agni drives away the demons; he is of bright flame, immortal, pure, the purifier, and worthy of praise. || 10 ||

Agni . demons . drives away . bright-flamed . immortal . pure . purifier . to be praised . || 10 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Agni, who possesses a bright flame <note>original: "śukraśociḥ"</note>, who is immortal and divine by nature, who is personally pure <note>original: "śuciḥ"</note> and the purifier of others <note>original: "pāvakaḥ"</note>, and who is worthy of being praised, drives away—that is, destroys or wards off—the <term>Rakshasas</term> <note>Malevolent demons or night-stalkers</note>.

-> ॥ Thus ends the nineteenth section (Varga) of the second chapter of the fifth book ॥ <-

-> ॥ The Eleventh Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text
O Son of Strength, as the ruler of all, bring us riches. And may Bhaga grant us what is desirable. || 11 ||

He . us . riches . bring . ruler . of strength . son . Bhaga . and . may he give . desirable . || 11 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Son of Strength <note>original: "sahaso yaho"; an epithet for Agni, who is 'born' from the vigorous friction of wood</note>, you are the famous ruler <note>original: "īśānaḥ"</note> or lord of the entire world. As such, bring to us "riches" <note>original: "radhāṃsi"</note>. <note>Sayana notes that "rayo" and "radhas" are listed as synonyms for wealth in ancient Vedic lexicons</note>. Bring these to us.

<vocab>
- **Night** (Kṣapa): The period of darkness.
- **Day/Morning** (Usra): The period of light.
- **Desiring us** (Asmayu): One who looks with favor or affection upon the worshipers.
- **For acquisition** (Sātaye): For the purpose of obtaining (specifically wealth).
- **Demons** (Rakṣāṃsi): Chaotic or evil spirits (Rakshasas).
- **Son of Strength** (Sahaso Yaho): A title for Agni referring to his birth from fire-sticks.
- **Ruler/Lord** (Īśāna): One who has mastery over the world.
- **Riches/Wealth** (Rādhāṃsi): Material prosperity and spiritual gifts.
</vocab>

Bring [wealth]. May <term>Bhaga</term><note>The god of fortune and share-giving.</note>, the divine Bhaga, also give us choiceworthy wealth. May he give to us. This is a characteristic of the repetition in the meter. In this hymn, Bhaga is an incidentally mentioned deity <note>original: "nipatabhagini", a deity who is not the main subject of the hymn but receives a share of the praise</note>.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Twelfth Verse ॥ <-

**You, O Agni, [give us] fame accompanied by heroes; and may the divine Savitr, Bhaga, and Diti give us choiceworthy wealth. || 12 ||**

-> **Word-for-Word Analysis** <-
**You . Agni . hero-possessing . fame . God . and . Savitr . Bhaga . Diti . and . may give . choiceworthy wealth . || 12 ||**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, may **you** [give us] **fame**—the word here implies food or renown—which is **accompanied by heroes**, meaning a lineage of sons and grandsons. Furthermore, may the **divine Savitr**, the impeller of all, **give** <note>original: "dāti", a Vedic form of "dadātu"</note> us **choiceworthy** wealth. May the god **Bhaga** also give. May the goddess **Diti** also give. Savitr and the others are incidental deities in this hymn.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Thirteenth Verse ॥ <-

**Agni, protect us from distress; O God, against those who would harm us, burn them with your most intense heat, you who are ageless. || 13 ||**

-> **Word-for-Word Analysis** <-
**Agni . protect . us . from distress . against . (particle) . God . the harming one . with most intense heat . ageless . burn . || 13 ||**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni**, may **you protect us** from **distress** or sin. <note>original: "raksā"; the long vowel in the Samhita text is a Vedic grammatical variation.</note> Furthermore, O **God**, radiant Agni, you who are **ageless** and free from decay, **burn**—meaning reduce to ashes—those **harming** enemies with your **most intense heat**, the splendors that cause extreme torment to foes.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Fourteenth Verse ॥ <-

**Now, be for us a great, iron-like, unassailable fortress for the protection of men, possessing a hundred enclosures. || 14 ||**

-> **Word-for-Word Analysis** <-
**Now . great . our . iron-like . unassailable . for-the-protection-of-men . fortress . be . hundred-walled . || 14 ||**

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Now**, O Agni, you who are **unassailable** and cannot be overcome, **be** for **our** **protection of men** <note>original: "nṛpītaye", the guarding of the people</note> a **great**, **iron-like** <note>original: "āyasī", as if made of metal</note> **fortress** <note>original: "pūḥ"</note>. This "fortress" refers to a city or the ramparts that serve as a means of defense. May it be **hundred-walled**, meaning extremely wide or possessing a hundred-fold strength. Just as a city made of iron or its protective walls shield those who are afraid of enemies, so too should you protect us who are afraid of demons.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Fifteenth Verse ॥ <-

**You, protect us from distress, O Illuminator of the Dark, from the one who intends evil, by day and by night, O Undeceivable One. || 15 ||**

-> **Word-for-Word Analysis** <-
**You . us . protect . from distress . Illuminator-of-the-Dark . the-evil-intending . by day . by night . undeceivable . || 15 ||**

<vocab>
- Agni: The sacred fire, seen here as a protective barrier and provider.
- Savitr: A solar deity representing the impulsive power of the sun.
- Bhaga: An Aditya responsible for the distribution of wealth and luck.
- Diti: A goddess often mentioned alongside Aditi, here invoked for material boons.
- Distress (Anhas): A term covering sin, calamity, and the "narrowness" of misfortune.
- Hundred-walled (Shatabhuji): Literally "hundred-armed" or "hundred-bending," referring to a complex, powerful fortification.
- Protection of men (Nripiti): The act of guarding the human community.
- Iron-like (Ayasi): Metaphor for strength and impenetrability; can refer to bronze or copper in earlier periods.
- Illuminator of the Dark (Doshavastar): An epithet for Agni, who dispels the darkness of night.
- Undeceivable (Adabhya): One who cannot be tricked or harmed by enemies.
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes Sukta 15, with the poet Vashishtha requesting Agni's total protection against enemies and sin. Agni is metaphorically described as an iron fortress with a hundred walls, guarding the worshipers day and night alongside other deities like Savitr and Bhaga.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, protection, iron fortress, Bhaga, Savitr, Diti, security, defense against evil, Vedic prayer</keywords>

<page-num>951</page-num>
<header>Mandala 7. Adhyaya 1. Sukta 16.] || The Fifth Ashtaka || 951</header>

O **unassailable** <note>original: "adābhya"</note> one—you who cannot be harmed—O **Coverer of Darkness** <note>original: "doṣāvasta"</note>, you who clothe the night, meaning the one who wards off the darkness. O **Agni**, **protect** <note>original: "pāhi"</note> **us** from **sin** <note>original: "aṃhasaḥ"</note> and from the **enemy** who **desires evil** <note>original: "aghayataḥ"</note>, both by **day** and by **night**, at all times.

->|| Thus ends the Twentieth Section (Varga) of the Second Chapter in the Fifth Book ||<-

The sixteenth hymn, beginning with "**With this [praise] for you**" <note>original: "ena vaḥ"</note>, consists of twelve verses. The <term>Ṛṣi</term> (Seer) is **Vasiṣṭha**, and the deity is **Agni**. The odd-numbered verses are in the <term>Bṛhatī</term> meter, and the even-numbered verses are in the <term>Satobṛhatī</term> meter. This is confirmed by the Index <note>original: "Anukramani"</note>: "*With this for you, twelve verses in the Pragatha style.*" 

In the <term>Prātar-anuvāka</term> <note>the morning litany ritual</note>, this hymn is recited during the portion dedicated to Agni in the Brhati meter; it is also used in the <term>Āśvina Śastra</term> <note>the recitation for the Twin Gods</note>. This is indicated in the ritual manuals: "*With this for you, Agni, I call the great one...*" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 4.13). 

In the <term>Agnimāruta Śastra</term> <note>the litany to Agni and the Storm Gods</note>, the <term>Pragātha</term> <note>a strophic couplet</note> beginning with "**The divine Giver of Wealth for you**" <note>original: "devo vo draviṇodā"</note> is used as the corresponding response. This is also indicated: "*The two Pragathas beginning with 'The divine Giver of Wealth' are the corresponding responses to the chants.*" (Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 5.20).

---

## Hymn Text

->|| Here follows the First Verse ||<-

**With this [praise] I call Agni for you—the Son of Strength, the beloved, the most conscious, the Master, the one who brings a good sacrifice, the messenger of all, the immortal. || 1 ||**

**Pada-patha:**
**With this . for you . Agni . with praise . of Strength . the Son . (prefix) . I call . beloved . most conscious . the Master . good-sacrifice-bringing . of all . the messenger . the immortal || 1 ||**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Son of Strength** <note>original: "ūrjo napātam"</note>: The son of vigor. This is confirmed by its inclusion in the ancient lists of names for offspring. **Beloved**: Dear to us. **Most conscious** <note>original: "cetiṣṭham"</note>: One who knows or makes known most excellently. **Master** <note>original: "arati"</note>: One who moves, or the Lord. **Good-sacrifice-bringing**: One who facilitates a perfect sacrifice. **The messenger of all**: The divine courier for every sacrificer. **The immortal**: The eternal **Agni**. 

**With this praise** <note>original: "enena namasā"</note>: referring to the hymn of worship. Although the specific pronoun rule <note>original: "anvadesha"</note> isn't strictly applied here, the word "this" is substituted due to Vedic grammatical freedom. Alternatively, "this" could be an adjective modifying Agni. Since this hymn follows the previous ones by the same Seer, Vasistha refers back to him. **For you** <note>original: "vaḥ"</note>: For your sake. **I call** <note>original: "ā huve"</note>: I summon him.

---

## Hymn Text

->|| Now the Second Verse ||<-

**He yokes the two ruddy [steeds] that feed all; well-invoked, may he hasten [here]. He is the one with good prayers, the sacrifice, the good worker for the Vasus, the divine wealth of the people. || 2 ||**

**Pada-patha:**
**He . yokes . the two ruddy [steeds] . all-feeding . He . may hasten . well-invoked . with good prayers . the sacrifice . well-working . of the Vasus . the divine . wealth . of the people || 2 ||**

<vocab>
- Vasiṣṭha: A famous sage and the seer of this hymn.
- Agni: The god of fire and mediator between humans and gods.
- Urjo Napāta: "Son of Strength," a common title for Agni referring to fire produced by the friction of hands (strength).
- Namas: Reverence, obeisance, or a prayerful hymn.
- Dūta: A messenger or envoy.
- Amṛta: Immortal or deathless.
- Bṛhatī: A Vedic meter consisting of 36 syllables.
- Satobṛhatī: A Vedic meter consisting of 40 syllables.
- Pragātha: A combination of Brhati and Satobrhati verses.
</vocab>

It details the ritual uses and meters of the hymn and provides the text and commentary for the first two verses, emphasizing Agni's role as a divine messenger and master of sacrifice.</summary>

<header>|| Rig Veda || [Book 5. Chapter 2. Section 21.]</header>

That Agni joins the two shining ones <note>original: "uṣārocamānau"</note>, the all-sustaining <note>original: "viśvabhojasā"</note>—the protectors of the universe—the two horses. Let him yoke them to the chariot. Or rather, he joins with his all-sustaining radiance, which protects the universe. He was joined [to them]. Furthermore, let him run swiftly <note>original: "amṛdudravat"</note> to bring the gods, or he [already] runs. The sacrifice, well-offered with good oblations, accompanied by good prayers <note>original: "subrahmā"</note> and good rituals <note>original: "suśamī"</note>, is to be performed. May the oblation reach this shining god, the wealth of the most excellent people who dwell [there]. Or: Agni, distinguished in this way, is like the most beloved wealth among the treasures of the people, the most radiant god among the <term>Vasūs</term> <note>a class of benevolent deities associated with dwelling and prosperity</note>.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Now the Third Verse ॥<-

The **brilliance** of the **bestower**, who is being **invoked**, has **risen up**. The **reddish-shining smoke**, **touching the sky**, [has risen]; **men kindle** Agni. ||3||

**Word-by-word Breakdown (Padapatha):**
Up. His. Brilliance. Has risen. Of the one being invoked. Of the bestower.
Up. Smokes. Reddish-shining. Sky-touching. Thoroughly. Agni. They kindle. Men. ||3||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **brilliance** <note>original: "śociḥ"</note> or radiant energy of Agni—who is the **bestower** <note>original: "mīḷhuṣaḥ"</note> of desires and who is being **invoked** <note>original: "ājuhvānasya"</note> with oblations—**has risen up** <note>original: "udasthāt"</note>. It rises. The **reddish-shining** <note>original: "aruṣāsaḥ"</note> **columns of smoke** <note>original: "dhūmāso"</note>, **touching the sky** <note>original: "divispṛśo"</note> (meaning reaching the atmosphere), have also risen. The verb "arose" <note>original: "asthāt"</note>, though appearing in the singular in the text, is here interpreted in the plural sense to agree with the smoke. **Men** <note>original: "naraḥ"</note>—the leaders of the ritual, the priests—**kindle** <note>original: "samindhate"</note> this Agni; they ignite him thoroughly.

---

## Hymn Text
->॥ Now the Fourth Verse ॥<-

We **choose** you, the **most glorious** one, as our **messenger**. **Bring** the **gods** here for the **feast**. O **Son of Strength**, **grant** us **all** those **human enjoyments** that we **beg** of you. ||4||

**Word-by-word Breakdown (Padapatha):**
Him. You. Messenger. We choose. Most glorious. Gods. Toward. For the feast. Bring.
All. O Son. Of strength. Mortal-enjoyments. Grant. That. Which. You. We beg. ||4||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Son of Strength** <note>original: "sahasaḥ sūno"</note>—Agni, born of the powerful friction of the kindling sticks—we **choose** <note>original: "vṛṇīmahe"</note> or appoint **you**, the famous and **most glorious** <note>original: "yaśastamam"</note> one, as our **messenger** <note>original: "dūtam"</note>. As such, **bring** <note>original: "āvaha"</note> the **gods** here for the **feast** <note>original: "vītaye"</note>, that they may consume the oblations. Furthermore, whatever we **beg** <note>original: "īmahe"</note> of you, at that very time **grant** <note>original: "rāsva"</note> to us **all** <note>original: "viśvā"</note> those **human enjoyments** <note>original: "martyabhojanā"</note>—the auspicious wealth intended for the use of mortals. Give them to us.

<vocab>
- **Bestower of desires** <note>original: "mīḷhuṣaḥ"</note>: one who rains down or grants wishes.
- **Brilliance** <note>original: "śociḥ"</note>: the flame or light of the fire.
- **Son of Strength** <note>original: "sahasaḥ sūno"</note>: a common title for Agni, referring to the physical strength required to churn the fire-sticks to produce a spark.
- **Messenger** <note>original: "dūtam"</note>: Agni's role as the intermediary who carries oblations from earth to the gods in heaven.
- **Grant** <note>original: "rāsva"</note>: to give or bestow.
- **We beg** <note>original: "īmahe"</note>: our request or prayer.
</vocab>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Fifth Verse ॥ <-

**You, O Agni, are the master of the house; you are our invoker at the sacrifice.**
**You are the purifier, O bestower of all boons, the wise one; perform the sacrifice and accept the desirable [oblation].** || 5 ||

**Word-by-word Breakdown (Padapatha):**
You. Agni. Master-of-the-house. You. Invoker. Our. At the sacrifice.
You. Purifier. Bestower-of-all-boons. Wise-one. Sacrifice. Accept. And. Desirable. || 5 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **bestower of all boons** <note>original: "viśvavāra"</note>, O Agni who is to be chosen by all, you are the **master of the house** <note>original: "gṛhapatiḥ"</note> at our **sacrifice** <note>original: "adhvare"</note>. That is, you are the patron of the sacrifice <note>original: "yajamāna"</note>. You are the **invoker** <note>original: "hotā"</note>, the one who calls the gods. You, and only you, are the **purifier** <note>original: "potā"</note> <note>a specific type of priest who purifies the offerings</note>. Therefore, being the **wise one** <note>original: "pracetāḥ"</note> of excellent intellect, **perform the sacrifice** <note>original: "yakṣi"</note> with the **desirable** <note>original: "vāryam"</note> oblation. Sacrifice it. **And accept it** <note>original: "veṣi ca"</note>. Desire it, or rather, consume it.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**O you of noble deeds, provide wealth for the sacrificer, for you are the giver of treasures.**
**In our sacrifice, sharpen every priest, and him who praises well and grows strong.** || 6 ||

**Word-by-word Breakdown (Padapatha):**
Provide. Treasure. For the sacrificer. O-you-of-noble-deeds. You. Indeed. Giver-of-treasures. You are.
In. Our. Sacrifice. Sharpen. Every. Priest. Who-praises-well. Who. And. Grows-strong. || 6 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **performer of noble deeds** <note>original: "sukrato"</note>, O Agni of beautiful rituals, **provide** <note>original: "kṛdhi"</note> or grant **treasure** <note>original: "ratnam"</note>—meaning wealth—to the sacrificer, to me. <note>The commentator notes that "ratnam" is listed among the synonyms for wealth.</note> **Indeed** <note>original: "hi"</note>, because you are the **giver of treasures** <note>original: "ratnadhāḥ"</note>. In **our** <note>original: "naḥ"</note> **sacrifice** <note>original: "ṛte"</note>, **sharpen** <note>original: "śiśīhi"</note> or make keen **every priest** <note>original: "viśvam ṛtvijam"</note>. Furthermore, he **who praises well** <note>original: "suśaṃsaḥ"</note>, namely my son who offers good hymns and **grows strong** <note>original: "dakṣate"</note>, cause him to prosper. Alternatively, it means: cause the <term>Hotr</term> <note>the chief priest who recites the Rig Veda</note> who praises well and prospers to grow even more. The separate mention of the <term>Hotr</term> is intended to show special respect.

-> ॥ This concludes the twenty-first section (Varga) of the second chapter of the fifth book (Ashtaka) ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥ <-

**O Agni, well-invoked with oblations, may the wise patrons be dear to you;**
**those generous ones who are the leaders of the people and who distribute the stalls of cattle.** || 7 ||

**Word-by-word Breakdown (Padapatha):**
In you. Agni. Well-invoked. Dear. Let them be. The wise patrons.
The leaders. Those. Generous ones. Of the people. The stalls. They distribute. Of cattle. || 7 ||

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni, well-invoked** <note>original: "svāhuta"</note>, you who are well-called by the sacrificers with oblations; may the **wise patrons** <note>original: "sūrayaḥ"</note>—the instigators of the sacrifice or the chanters—be **dear** <note>original: "priyāsaḥ"</note> **to you** <note>original: "tve"</note>... <unclear>the text continues on the next page</unclear>

[The previous verse concluded with a wish for patrons to be dear to Agni.] ...let them be dear. May they become so. Furthermore, those **wealthy patrons** <note>original: "maghavāno"</note> who are the **distributors** <note>original: "yantāraḥ"</note> among our people, who bestow **great herds** <note>original: "ūrvān"</note> of **cattle** <note>original: "gavām"</note>—let them also be dear to you. This connects with the previous statement.

->॥ Now the Eighth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**In whose house Ila, with butter in her hands, sits down in abundance; protect them, O Powerful One, from the deceiver and the scorner. Grant us, O far-famed one, a refuge.** || 8 ||

**Word-by-word Breakdown (Pada-patha):**
In whose. **Ila** <note>Goddess of nourishment</note>. **With butter in her hands**. **In the house**. Sits. Indeed. **Abundant**. Sits down.
Them. **Protect**. **O Powerful One**. **From the deceiver**. **From the scorner**. **Grant**. To us. **Refuge**. **O far-famed one**. || 8 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
In whose **house** <note>original: "duroṇe"</note> the goddess **Ila**, who is **butter-handed** <note>original: "ghṛtahastā"</note>—meaning her hands are smeared with clarified butter, or rather, she is consecrated with butter—sits. **Ila** is the goddess in the form of food or the oblation <note>original: "havir-lakṣaṇā devī"</note>. This is supported by the ancient word-lists where "Ira" and "Ila" are listed as names for food. She **sits down** <note>original: "niṣīdati"</note> in **abundance** <note>original: "prātā"</note>, meaning fully. The word **api** <note>original: "api"</note> is used here as a filler for the verse.

O **Powerful One** <note>original: "sahasya"</note>—O Agni, who is beneficial to strength and born of force—**protect** <note>original: "trāyasva"</note> those sacrificers who possess the oblations. Protect them from the **deceiver** <note>original: "druhaḥ"</note> and from the **scorner** <note>original: "nidaḥ"</note> or the mocking enemy. And to us, **grant** <note>original: "yaccha"</note> a **refuge** <note>original: "śarma"</note>, meaning happiness or a secure home, that is **far-famed** <note>original: "dīrghaśrut"</note>—worthy of being heard about for a long time.

->॥ Now the Ninth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
**With a delightful tongue, a bearer through his mouth, and most wise; O Agni, bring wealth to our patrons and guide the giver of offerings.** || 9 ||

**Word-by-word Breakdown (Pada-patha):**
He. **With a delightful [tongue]**. And. **With a tongue**. **A bearer**. **Through the mouth**. **Most wise**.
O Agni. **Wealth**. **To the patrons**. To us. **Bring**. **The giver of offerings**. And. **Guide**. || 9 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O Agni, you are the one with a **delightful** <note>original: "mandrayā"</note> tongue—that which rejoices the gods. Your **tongue** <note>original: "jihvayā"</note> is your flame, which acts as your **mouth** <note>original: "āsā"</note>. You are the **bearer** <note>original: "vahniḥ"</note> who carries the oblations to the gods, and you are **most wise** <note>original: "viduṣṭaraḥ"</note>, possessing the greatest knowledge. Being that famous one, **bring** <note>original: "ā vaha"</note> **wealth** <note>original: "rayim"</note> to us and to our **wealthy patrons** <note>original: "maghavadbhyaḥ"</note> who offer the sacrifice. And as for the **giver of offerings** <note>original: "havyadātim"</note>—meaning the one who gives the oblations, the sacrificer—**guide** <note>original: "sūdaya"</note> or impel him in his sacred works. This definition of "havyadāti" as the sacrificer is also held by the followers of the Vajasaneyi school, who say: "The sacrificer is indeed the giver of offerings."

## Hymn Text
**Those who give gifts, mighty riches with desire for great protection; deliver them from distress, O Youngest One, with a hundred protective walls.** || 10 ||

## Hymn Text

**Those who give riches, gifts consisting of horses, with the desire for great protection;**
**protect them from distress, O Most Youthful One, with a hundred protecting forts.** || 10 ||

**Word-by-word Breakdown (Pada-patha):**
**Those.** **Riches.** **They give.** **Consisting of horses.** **Gifts.** **With desire.** **Of protection.** **Great.**
**Them.** **From distress.** **Protect.** **With protectors.** **You.** **A hundred.** **With forts.** **O Most Youthful One.** || 10 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Most Youthful One** <note>original: "yaviṣṭha"</note>, O Agni, those patrons who, with the **desire** <note>original: "kāmena"</note> for **great** <note>original: "maho"</note> **glory** <note>original: "avaso"</note>—meaning those who are desirous of fame—**give** <note>original: "dadati"</note> **gifts** <note>original: "maghāni"</note> of **riches** <note>original: "rādhāṃsi"</note> that accomplish their goals and consist of horses; **protect** <note>original: "pipṛhi"</note> those givers from **sin** <note>original: "aṃhasaḥ"</note> or distress. Do so with **protectors** <note>original: "partṛbhiḥ"</note>—those things which are the means of defense—and with **a hundred** <note>original: "śatam"</note> **forts** <note>original: "pūrbhiḥ"</note>, implying an infinite number of fortified cities.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Eleventh Verse ॥ <-

**The god, the giver of wealth, desires your full pouring-ladle.**
**Pour out or fill up, and then the god bears you onward.** || 11 ||

**The god.** **Of you.** **The giver of wealth.** **The full.** **Desires.** **The pouring-ladle.**
**Out.** **Or.** **Pour.** **Near.** **Or.** **Fill.** **Then.** **Indeed.** **Of you.** **The god.** **Bears.** || 11 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **giver of wealth** <note>original: "draviṇodā"</note>, the **god** Agni, **desires** <note>original: "vivaṣṭi"</note> your **full** <note>original: "pūrṇām"</note> **pouring-ladle** <note>original: "āsicam"</note>, which is the sacrificial spoon <note>term: sruc - a large wooden ladle used for pouring clarified butter or Soma</note> filled with the oblation. Therefore, either **pour out** <note>original: "utsiñcadhvam"</note> the Soma into the vessel, **or fill it up** <note>original: "upapṛṇadhvam"</note> with Soma. The word "or" <note>original: "vā"</note> is used here in a cumulative sense <note>original: "samuccayārthau"</note>, meaning "and." The meaning is: fill the Hotar’s cup using the **fixed vessel** <note>term: dhruva-graha - a specific ritual container for Soma</note> and offer the Soma to Agni. **Then** <note>original: "ād it"</note>, immediately afterward, the **god** Agni **bears** <note>original: "ohate"</note> you—he carries you across <note>to heaven or through the sacrifice</note>.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Twelfth Verse ॥ <-

**The gods made him the priest of the sacrifice, the wise one, the carrier.**
**Agni bestows a treasure of great heroism upon the person who serves and gives.** || 12 ||

**Him.** **The priest.** **Of the sacrifice.** **The wise one.** **The carrier.** **The gods.** **Made.**
**Bestows.** **Treasure.** **To the one who serves.** **Great heroism.** **Agni.** **To the person.** **To the giver.** || 12 ||

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **gods made** <note>original: "akṛṇvanta"</note> Agni, who possesses **excellent wisdom** <note>original: "pracetasam"</note>, to be the **carrier** <note>original: "vahnim"</note> of the sacrifice and the **priest** <note>original: "hotāram"</note> of the **sacrifice** <note>original: "adhvarasya"</note>. For what purpose? He explains: that Agni **bestows** <note>original: "dadhāti"</note> or gives a **treasure** <note>original: "ratnam"</note>, which is delightful wealth, and **great heroism** <note>original: "suvīryam"</note>—wealth accompanied by noble sons and strength—to the **person** <note>original: "janāya"</note> who **serves** <note>original: "vidhate"</note> him and to the **giver** <note>original: "dāśuṣe"</note> who provides the oblations.

९५६ ->॥ Rig Veda ॥<- [Book 5. Chapter 2. Group 23.]

These verses are in the two-footed Trishtubh meter. The index of the Veda states: "The seven verses beginning with 'O Agni, become' are in the two-footed Trishtubh meter." <note>A 'Dwipada Trishtubh' is a poetic meter consisting of two lines of eleven syllables each, rather than the standard four.</note> In the liturgical context of the Atiratra sacrifice <note>A major Soma sacrifice performed overnight</note>, on the sixth day during the third pressing of the Soma, in the recitation for the deities Mitra and Varuna, the triplet of verses beginning with 'O Agni, become' is used as the 'corresponding' set of verses <term>anurupa: a set of verses that follows and matches the meter of the preceding 'stotriya' or chant</term>. This is indicated in the Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra (8.2): "The two verses 'O Agni, you are our closest' and 'O Agni, become well-enkindled' serve as the chant and its corresponding recitation."

->॥ Here is the First Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
O Agni, become well-enkindled with good fuel, and let the sacred grass be spread widely. ॥ 1 ॥

**O Agni. Become. With-good-fuel. Well-enkindled. And. Sacred-grass. Widely. (Prefix). Let-be-spread. ॥ 1 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Agni**, become **well-enkindled** <note>original: "samiddhaḥ"</note> by means of **good fuel** <note>original: "su-samidhā"</note>. That is, become properly radiant. **And also** <note>original: "utāpi ca"</note>, let the priest spread the **sacred grass** <note>original: "barhiḥ"</note>—the grass upon which the gods sit—**widely** <note>original: "urviyā"</note>, meaning extensively.

---

->॥ Now the Second Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
And let the desiring doors swing open; and bring the desiring gods here. ॥ 2 ॥

**And. Doors. Desiring. (Prefix). Let-them-rest-open. And. Gods. Desiring. (Prefix). Bring. Here. ॥ 2 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
**And also** <note>original: "utāpi ca"</note>, let the **doors** <note>original: "dvāraḥ"</note> of the sacrificial hall, which are **desiring** <note>original: "uśatīḥ"</note> the gods, swing **open** <note>original: "viśrayantām"</note>. These may also refer to the "Goddesses of the Doors." Regarding this, the etymologist **Yaska** says: "The word for doors [dvarah] comes from the root meaning to speed, to run, or to restrain" <note>original: "Nirukta 8.9"</note>. **And also** <note>original: "utāpi ca"</note>, **bring** <note>original: "āvaha"</note> **here** to this sacrifice the **gods** <note>original: "devān"</note> who are **desiring** <note>original: "uśataḥ"</note> the ritual offerings.

## Commentary (Sayana)
O **Jatavedas** <note>original: "jātavedo"</note>—the Agni from whom wealth is born—**approach** <note>original: "vīhi"</note> or go toward the gods. **Worship** <note>original: "yakṣi"</note>—that is, sacrifice to—the **gods** <note>original: "devān"</note> **with the oblation** <note>original: "haviṣā"</note>. And **make** <note>original: "kṛṇuhi"</note> the **sacrifices successful** <note>original: "svadhvarā"</note>, meaning perform the rites beautifully.

## Commentary (Sayana)

And let him **please** <note>original: "piprayat"</note> them with songs of praise.

Therefore, O **Great One** <note>original: "maho"</note>, you who are being **entreated** <note>original: "iyānaḥ"</note> or approached with requests, **grant** <note>original: "vidhadhuḥ," interpreted here as "vidhatsva"</note> lovely **treasures** <note>original: "ratnā"</note> or wealth **to us**.

## Introductory Notes (Anuvaka 2, Sukta 18)

There are sixteen hymns in the second subdivision (Anuvaka). Among them, the first hymn, which begins with the phrase "In you, indeed, what our fathers" <note>original: "tve ha yat pitara"</note>, consists of twenty-five verses. It was revealed to the seer Vasishtha, is composed in the Trishtubh meter <note>A meter of 44 syllables</note>, and is dedicated to the deity Indra. The final four verses, starting from the twenty-second, are a praise of liberality <term>dānastuti: a specific type of Vedic hymn praising the generosity of a patron or king</term> regarding King Sudas, the son of Pijavana. Therefore, those specific verses are dedicated to him as the deity. The Index of the Veda states: "The hymn 'In you, indeed' is Indra-centric for five-and-a-half parts; the final four verses regarding Sudas, son of Paijavana, are a praise of gifts." In the Great Vow ritual <term>Mahāvrata: a highly symbolic soma sacrifice performed at the end of the year</term>, the first fifteen verses of this hymn are to be recited. This is indicated in the Fifth Aranyaka of the Aitareya school: "The fifteen verses beginning with 'In you, indeed, what our fathers' and 'Indra comes' are used." (Aitareya Aranyaka 5.8).

<summary>This page concludes Sukta 17 with prayers to Agni for wealth and success, marking the end of the first Anuvaka. It then introduces Sukta 18, a significant historical hymn praising King Sudas and his victory, noting its liturgical use in the Mahavrata ritual.</summary>

**In-you. Indeed. When. Fathers. Even. Our. Indra. All. Desirable-things. Singers. Obtained. In-you. Cows. Easy-to-milk. In-you. Indeed. Horses. You. Wealth. To-the-one-seeking-gods. Greatest-giver. ॥ १ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra**, **in you indeed** <note>original: "tve ha"</note>—in you alone—**our** <note>original: "naḥ"</note> **fathers also** <note>original: "pitaraścit"</note>, being **singers** <note>original: "jaritāraḥ"</note> or praisers, **when** <note>original: "yad"</note> for that reason they **obtained** <note>original: "asanvan"</note> **all** <note>original: "viśvā"</note> **desirable** <note>original: "vāmā"</note> wealth—that is, riches to be longed for. And so says the ancient etymologist Yaska: **"That which is desirable is to be longed for"** <note>original: "vāmaṃ vananīyaṃ bhavatīti"</note>. Since they obtained it, we too, desiring wealth, praise you. **That is appropriate** <note>original: "tadyuktaṃ"</note>. **Because** <note>original: "hi"</note> for this reason **in you** <note>original: "tve"</note> are **cows** <note>original: "gāvaḥ"</note> that are **easy to milk** <note>original: "sudughā"</note>, and **in you** are **horses** <note>original: "aśvāḥ"</note>. **You** are the **greatest giver** <note>original: "vaniṣṭhaḥ"</note> of **wealth** <note>original: "vasu"</note> to the **sacrificer who seeks the gods** <note>original: "devayate"</note>, that is, the one who desires you, the divine.

## Hymn Text
->॥ Now the Second Verse ॥<-

Like a king with his wives, you dwell with the days, being a wise seer. O Lord of Wealth, with a form, with cows and horses, sharpen us for the sake of riches, as we desire you. ॥ २ ॥

**Like-a-king. Indeed. With-wives. You-dwell. Thus. Down. With-days. Towards. They-know. Seer. Being. With-form. Voices/Praises. O-Lord-of-Wealth. With-cows. With-horses. For-you-desiring. Sharpen. For-wealth. Us. ॥ २ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra**, you, with your **wives** <note>original: "janibhiḥ"</note>, are **like a king** <note>original: "rājeva"</note>. Together with the **days** <note>original: "dyubhiḥ"</note> or your splendors, you **dwell** <note>original: "kṣeṣi"</note> as one who has taken up residence. The word "indeed" <note>original: "hi"</note> is used here as a filler for the meter. Furthermore, O **Lord of Wealth** <note>original: "maghavan"</note>, O wealthy Indra, **being** <note>original: "san"</note> a **wise** <note>original: "viduḥ"</note> and **sage-like seer** <note>original: "kaviḥ"</note>—meaning one whose actions or wisdom are transcendent—protect **us**, the **singers** <note>original: "giraḥ"</note>, on all sides **with a form** <note>original: "piśā"</note> such as gold, and with **cows** and **horses**. For **us who desire you** <note>original: "tvāyataḥ"</note>, **sharpen** <note>original: "śiśīhi"</note> us—that is, prepare or strengthen us—**for the sake of wealth** <note>original: "rāye"</note>.

९५९ ॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Book 7. Chapter 2. Section 24.]

O **Indra**, these **songs** <note>original: "giraḥ"</note> of praise have **approached** <note>original: "upasthuḥ"</note> you. The worshippers, whether **competing** <note>original: "paspṛdhānāsaḥ"</note> or **rejoicing** <note>original: "mandrā"</note> during the sacrifice, stand before you. ## Hymn Text

Like a cow in a lush pasture, desiring to milk you, Vasistha has released his sacred prayers. Indeed, everyone says to me that you are the Lord of Cattle; may Indra come toward our good prayer. ॥ ४ ॥

**Cow. Like. You. Lush-pasture. Desiring-to-milk. Near. Prayers. Released. Vasistha. You. Indeed. Me. Lord-of-Cattle. Everyone. Says. Toward. Us. Indra. Good-favor. To-go. Toward. ॥ ४ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Indra**, like a **cow** <note>original: "dhenuṃ na"</note> standing in a stall filled with **good grass** <note>original: "suyavase"</note>, [you stand] in the sacrificial hall with the priests. By the power of this comparison, we understand your accessibility and generosity. Desiring to **milk** <note>original: "dudukṣan"</note> his desires from you—<note>note: in the Samhita version of the word "dudukṣan," the letter 'd' is substituted by Vedic grammatical rules</note>—the sage **Vasistha** has **released** <note>original: "upasasṛje"</note> **sacred prayers** <note>original: "brahmāṇi"</note> which are like calves following the cow. **Everyone** <note>original: "viśvaḥ"</note> says to **me** <note>original: "me"</note> that you, Indra, are the **Lord of Cattle** <note>original: "gopati"</note>, the protector of all wealth. Now follows a prayer in the third person: May **Indra come toward** <note>original: "ā gantu achā"</note> **our** <note>original: "naḥ"</note> **good prayer** <note>original: "sumati"</note>.

## Hymn Text

The waters, even as they were spreading wide, Indra made shallow and easy to cross for King Sudas. For the singer of this new praise, he made the bold Shimyu and the curses of the rivers into harmless things. ॥ ५ ॥

**Waters. Even. Spreading. For-Sudas. Indra. Shallows. Made. Easy-to-cross. Bold. Shimyu. Praise. New. Curse. Rivers. Made. Harmless. ॥ ५ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **new** <note>original: "navyaḥ"</note> Indra, who is ever worthy of fresh praise, **made** <note>original: "akṛṇot"</note> the **waters** <note>original: "arṇāṃsi"</note> of the **Parushni** <note>term: the modern Ravi River</note>—which had been diverted or breached by enemies and were **spreading wide** <note>original: "paprathānā cit"</note>—into **shallows** <note>original: "gādhāni"</note> that were **easy to cross** <note>original: "supārā"</note> for King **Sudas**. 

Furthermore, for the sake of the **singer** <note>original: "uchathasya"</note> of this praise, Indra **overcame** <note>original: "akṛṇot"</note> the **bold** <note>original: "śardhataṃ"</note> and arrogant enemy **Shimyu**. He also turned the **curse** <note>original: "śāpaṃ"</note> of the **rivers** <note>original: "sindhūnām"</note> and their **ill-repute** <note>original: "aśastīḥ"</note>—referring to the dangerous floods or the obstacles they presented—into harmlessness.

९६० ॥ Rig Veda ॥ [Book 7. Chapter 2. Section 25.]

-> ॥ Here is the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

**Turvasha** was indeed the sacrificial cake, and the **Yakshu** was the one performing the sacrifice for the sake of wealth. The **Matsyas**, like fish caught in a net, were focused on their goal. The **Bhrigus** and the **Druhyus** showed their obedience; the Friend <note>Indra</note> helped his friend <note>King Sudas</note> cross over the two opposing sides. ॥ ६ ॥

**Sacrificial-cake. Indeed. Turvasha. Yakshu. Was. For-wealth. Matsyas. Focused. Caught-as-it-were. Obedience. They-showed. Bhrigus. Druhyus. And. Friend. Friend. Helped-across. Of-two-sides. ॥ ६ ॥**

---

-> ॥ Here is the Seventh Verse ॥ <-

The **Pakthas**, the **Bhalanas**, the **Alinas**, the **Vishanins**, and the **Shivas** shouted in praise. He <note>Indra</note> who led the companion of the noble performer of rituals, came with men for the sake of cattle through battle for the **Tritsus**. ॥ ७ ॥

**Indeed. Pakthas. Bhalanas. Shouted. Indeed. Alinas. Vishanins. Shivas. Indeed. Who. Led. Fellow-reveler. Of-the-noble-one. For-cattle. For-the-Tritsus. He-came. By-battle. Men. ॥ ७ ॥**

## Commentary (Sayana)

**Yakshu** refers to one skilled in sacrifice. <note>Etymologically derived from the root 'yaj' (to sacrifice) with the suffix 'san'.</note> **Purodash** <note>original: "puroḷāḥ"</note> means one who goes before or one who gives first. The particle **id** is used for emphasis. There was a king named **Turvasha**. This Turvasha went to King Sudas, the friend of Indra, for the sake of obtaining **wealth** <note>original: "rāye"</note>. Like **Matsyas** <note>fish</note> caught in water or focused on their aim, even the Bhrigus and the Druhyus—who were warriors—showed their **obedience** <note>original: "śruṣṭiṃ"</note>, meaning they quickly reached or assisted Sudas and Turvasha. In the midst of the **two opposing sides** <note>original: "viṣūcoḥ"</note> moving in different directions, the Friend, Indra, helped his friend, King Sudas, **cross over** <note>original: "atarat"</note>. This means Indra saved Sudas and struck down Turvasha.

Alternatively, the interpretation is: King Turvasha was the **Purodasha** <note>the giver of the first offering</note> and the **Yakshu** <note>the performer of sacrifice</note>. By him, the **Matsya** peoples were oppressed or bound. Furthermore, the Bhrigus and Druhyus acted for the happiness of Turvasha. In the midst of the two sides, Indra, acting as a friend to Turvasha, helped the king cross over safely.

---

**Pakthas** are the "cooks" of the sacrificial offerings. **Bhalanas** means those with auspicious or noble faces <note>from 'bhala' meaning auspicious</note>. **Alinas** refers to the Alinas <note>Sayana interprets this as "those not grown powerful through austerities"</note>. **Vishanins** means "those holding horns"; specifically, those who hold the horn of a black antelope for the purpose of scratching during a ritual. This indicates they are **consecrated** <note>term: Dikshita — one who has undergone the initiation ritual for a sacrifice</note>. **Shivas** means those who bring auspiciousness to all the world through their rituals, for sacrifice brings well-being to the world. They **shouted** <note>original: "abhananta"</note>, meaning they praised Indra. <note>The root 'bhan' refers to making a sound or praising.</note>

Indra is called the **companion in revelry** <note>original: "sadhamāḥ"</note> because he rejoices together with the worshippers while drinking the Soma juice. He brought [victory] for the **noble one** <note>original: "āryasya"</note>, the one who performs the sacred works.

<vocab>
Indra: The primary warrior deity and king of heaven in the Vedas.
Sudas: A historical king of the Tritsu tribe, famous for winning the "Battle of the Ten Kings."
Turvasha: One of the five major tribes (Panchajana) often mentioned in the Rig Veda.
Bhrigu: An ancient clan of priests and warriors associated with fire and rituals.
Druhyu: A tribe traditionally opposed to the Tritsus in Vedic accounts.
Paktha: A tribal group mentioned as participants in the great battle.
Tritsu: The tribe or clan of King Sudas, supported by the sage Vasistha.
Yakshu: A specific group or person, sometimes identified with the Yadu tribe.
Shrushti: Interpreted here as prompt assistance or obedience in a military/ritual context.
Sadhamada: A term for a companion at a feast, particularly a co-drinker of Soma.
</vocab>

[Book 7. Chapter 2. Hymn 18.] || The Fifth Book <note>This refers to the "Ashtaka" or eighth-part division of the Rig Veda</note> || 961

...Regarding the herds of cattle, he <note>Indra</note> brought them to the **Tritsus** <note>the tribe of King Sudas</note> from the attackers. He himself arrived and obtained the herds of cows. By means of battle, killing those enemies, he slew them—this is the implied meaning.

->॥ Here is the Eighth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
The evil-minded ones, the witless ones, making the boundless <note>original: "aditim"</note> river **Parushni** flow away, split its banks. Through his greatness, he <note>Sudas</note> pervaded the earth as its master; the poet-king **Kavi**, son of **Chayamana**, lay down like a sacrificial animal. ॥ ८ ॥

**Pada Patha:**
**Evil-minded. The boundless. Making-to-flow. Witless. Apart. They-seized. Parushni. By-greatness. He-pervaded. The-earth. Being-master. Animal. Poet. He-lay. Chayamana. ॥ ८ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
The **evil-minded ones** <note>original: "durādhyaḥ"</note>, those having wicked intentions, and the **witless ones** <note>original: "acetasaḥ"</note> of dull intellect—these enemies of **Sudas**—making the "undivided" or boundless river **Parushni** flow out of its channel, they **split** <note>original: "vijagṛbhre"</note> it. This "splitting" refers to the breaking of the riverbanks; the meaning is they breached the banks of the Parushni to cause a flood.

However, that King Sudas, through the greatness obtained by the grace of Great Indra, **pervaded the earth**. He covered it, as it were, and was not hindered or drowned by the water. Consequently, the enemy of Sudas—the son of **Chayamana** named **Kavi**, who was a king being protected by his own men—**lay down** like a sacrificial animal slaughtered in a ritual. He lies there still; the meaning is that he was slain by Sudas.

->॥ Here is the Ninth Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text
They went to their goal, but not to the pit of destruction; they went toward the **Parushni**, and even the swift horse reached the destination. For the sake of **Sudas**, **Indra** subdued the babbling enemies with their many offspring in the world of men—those whose speech was emasculated. ॥ ९ ॥

**Pada Patha:**
**They-went. Goal. Not. To-destruction. Parushni. Swift. Even. Indeed. To-the-destination. He-went. For-Sudas. Indra. Having-good-offspring. Enemies. He-subdued. In-the-human-world. Emasculated-speech. ॥ ९ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)
Then Indra joined the broken "joints" or sections of the riverbanks of the **Parushni**. Because of this, the waters of the Parushni, as before, **went toward their goal** <note>original: "artham"</note>—that is, they flowed toward the sloping ground where they were intended to go. They arrived there. 

<note>The commentator notes that the verb "iyuḥ" (they went) is derived from the root "i" meaning "to go," used here in a specific grammatical sense.</note> 

The waters did **not go toward destruction** <note>original: "nyartham"</note>, which refers to the unreachable low-lying ground situated on the sides of the Parushni where the enemies tried to divert the flood. Even the **swift** horse of King Sudas went safely to the intended destination. 

Furthermore, for King Sudas, in the world of men, **Indra** subdued the **enemies** who were mere babblers with **emasculated speech** <note>original: "vadhrivācaḥ"</note>—meaning their threats were hollow or ineffective—and who had many children <note>original: "sutukān," derived from "toka" meaning offspring</note>. He brought them all under his control.

<summary>This page describes the climax of the Battle of the Ten Kings, where King Sudas's enemies unsuccessfully attempted to drown his army by breaching the banks of the Parushni river, only for Indra to intervene and secure Sudas's victory.</summary>
<keywords>King Sudas, River Parushni, Battle of the Ten Kings, Indra, Tritsus, Kavi Chayamana, Vedic geography, ancient warfare</keywords>

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Tenth Verse ॥ <-
They went like cows toward pasture, without a herdsman, following a pre-arranged path toward a friend, as they were summoned. Dappled in hue, sent forth by the Dappled Mother <note>original: "Prishni", the mother of the Maruts</note>, the teams of horses and the playful ones made haste. ॥ १० ॥

**Padapatha:**
They-went. Cows. Like. From-pasture. Without-herdsman. As-arranged. Toward. Friend. Summoned.
Dappled-cows. Sent-by-the-Dappled-Mother. Speed. They-made. Teams-of-horses. Playful. And. ॥ १० ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

When Indra comes for the protection of King **Sudas**, then the **sent forth by the Dappled Mother** <note>original: "pṛśninipreṣitāsaḥ"</note>—those sent or directed by their mother, **Prishni**—being united and knowing their purpose, the **Dappled-cow ones** <note>original: "pṛśnigāvaḥ"</note>—the **Maruts** <note>storm gods who accompany Indra</note> whose horses have the color of dappled cows—approached. They did so **as arranged** <note>original: "yathākṛtam"</note>, meaning they did not violate the previous agreement to assist Indra. They approached their **friend** <note>original: "mitram"</note>, Indra, like **cows without a herdsman** <note>original: "gāvo na agopāḥ"</note> approaching **pasture** <note>original: "yavasāt"</note>—here the word for pasture is used in the sense of a motive or cause. The playful, rejoicing **teams of horses** <note>original: "niyutaḥ"</note> of the Maruts **made haste** <note>original: "śruṣṭiṃ cakruḥ"</note>, meaning they arrived quickly. The sense is that in that battle, the Maruts arrived to assist Indra.

-> ॥ Thus ends the twenty-fifth section of the second chapter of the fifth book ॥ <-

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Eleventh Verse ॥ <-
The King who, out of a desire for glory, struck down twenty-one men of the two **Vaikarna** tribes; like a skilled priest <note>original: "dasmo na"</note> in the assembly, he trims the sacred grass. The hero Indra made the charge of these <note>the Maruts</note> successful. ॥ ११ ॥

**Padapatha:**
One. And. Who. Twenty. And. By-desire-for-glory. Of-the-two-Vaikarnas. Of-the-peoples. King. Down. Struck.
Skilled. Like. Together. Down. He-trims. Sacred-grass. Hero. Charge. He-made. Indra. Of-them. ॥ ११ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

**He who**—King **Sudas**—out of **desire for glory** <note>original: "śravasyā"</note>, whether intentionally or unintentionally, **struck down** <note>original: "nyastaḥ"</note> by his own hand **twenty-one men** <note>original: "ekaṃ ca viṃśatiṃ ca janān"</note> belonging to the **two Vaikarna** territories located on the banks of the **Parushni** river. That King, **like a skilled** <note>original: "dasmo na"</note> or beautiful young **Adhvaryu** priest <note>the priest in charge of the physical rituals</note> in the **sacrificial house**, **trims** <note>original: "ni śiśāti"</note> the **sacred grass** <note>original: "barhiḥ"</note>; so too in that battle did he cut down his enemies. In that battle, the **hero Indra made the charge** <note>original: "sargam akṛṇot"</note> of these **Maruts** successful for the sake of helping Sudas.

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ The Twelfth Verse ॥ <-
The famous **Kavasha**, the elder, he threw into the waters; the **Druhyu** king was struck down by the wielder of the thunderbolt <note>Indra</note>. Those who, desiring friendship, sought your alliance, followed you while rejoicing... ॥ १२ ॥

<vocab>

</vocab>

## Hymn Text

-> [Rig Veda 7.18.12] <-

Then, the **thunder-armed** <note>original: "vajrabāhuḥ", an epithet of Indra</note> submerged the famous **Kavasha**, the elder **Shruta**, and **Vriddha** in the waters; and likewise, he cast down the **Druhyu**.
